English: Like the headquarters, the president’s house was a shabby building that hardly lived up to the title.

Japanese: リョウがインターフォンを鳴らすと、汐社長本人が玄関のドアを開く。
English: When Ryo rang the intercom, President Shio himself opened the front door.

Japanese: おれもそんなに親しいってわけでもないけれど、一応面識はある。
English: I was not especially close to him, but we did at least know one another.

Japanese: 「なんだお前ら。いつの間にかまたつるみ始めたのか？」
English: “What are you two doing? When did you start running around together again?”

Japanese: 汐さんは挨拶もしないで開口一番そう言った。
English: That was the first thing Mr. Shio said, without so much as a greeting.

Japanese: 彼はそんなに暑い時期でもないのに、ポロシャツにハーフパンツという、きわめてラフな格好をしている。この人では年間を通じてこの私服だ。おれはいくら思い出そうとしても、この服装と、作業時のつなぎ姿でしか汐健慈朗という人物を思い浮かべることが出来ないんだよね。
English: Though the weather was not particularly warm, he wore a polo shirt and shorts: an extremely casual outfit he wore at home throughout the year. Try as I might, I cannot picture Kenjiro Shio in anything but those clothes or the coveralls he wore for work.

Japanese: 身なり全般がいいかげんで、ぼさぼさの頭にはいつも寝癖がついているし、ヒゲは伸び放題で顔中を毛むくじゃらにしている。
English: His appearance in general was careless. His shaggy hair was always rumpled from sleep, and an untrimmed beard left his face thick with hair.

Japanese: ただ、不潔というわけではないんじゃないかな。むしろ髪も肌も艶がよく、近くに行くと良いにおいさえする。これは本人の性格か、一緒に暮らす一人娘の影響によるものなのか、ちょっとわからないけれども。
English: Yet I would not say he was unclean. His hair and skin had a healthy sheen, and when one drew near, he even smelled pleasant. Whether that was due to his own nature or the influence of the only daughter who lived with him, I could not quite say.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。名コンビの復活だ。よろしく頼むよ汐さん」
English: “That’s right. The celebrated duo has returned. I trust we can count on you, Mr. Shio.”

Japanese: と、おれが返事をする横で、
English: As I answered, beside me Ryo said,

Japanese: 「今日はたまたまだよ」
English: “Today was a coincidence.”

Japanese: リョウは仏頂面でそう言って、相手の許可も得ずに勝手に玄関を上がる。
English: He spoke with a sullen face, then stepped inside without waiting for permission.

Japanese: Y地区には靴のまま入っていくような家が多いけれど、ここは主人が日本人だけあって、玄関で靴を脱いで上がる構造になっている。
English: Many homes in Y District allowed visitors to enter in their shoes, but Mr. Shio was Japanese, and this entrance was designed for people to remove their footwear before stepping up.

Japanese: 「つれないねえ」
English: “How cold.”

Japanese: おれはそう言って、リョウのあとを続いた。
English: With that remark, I followed Ryo inside.

Japanese: 汐さんは別段何も言わず、くるりと背を向けて廊下を行く。
English: Mr. Shio said nothing in particular. He simply turned around and went down the hall.

Japanese: 「松坊は？」
English: “Is Matsu here?”

Japanese: おれがその背に尋ねても、返事もしない。
English: I called the question after him, but he did not answer.

Japanese: 悪意があるわけではないんだよね。この汐という人物は普段からこうで、非常に無口で扱いにくい人間だと知られている。ｋまあ、ゴミというものには人の秘密がつまっているもんだし、それを受け取って処分する仕事をする人間としては、それくらいの方が信頼出来るような気もするよ。
English: There was no malice in it. Shio was always like this and was known as an extremely taciturn, difficult man. Well, rubbish is full of people’s secrets. In a man whose work was to receive and dispose of it, such reserve almost seemed grounds for trust.

Japanese: 板張りの廊下も清掃が行き届いていて清潔だった。けれど、続くリビングルームは若干散らかっている。近くの総菜屋の包み紙がテーブルの上でくしゃくしゃになり、その脇には空になったポリケースに割り箸が突っ込まれている。朝食か何かを食べ終わったそのままに放置したのだろう。間違いなくこれは汐さんの無頓着さのせいに違いない。
English: The wooden hallway was spotless and thoroughly cleaned, but the living room beyond was somewhat untidy. A wrapper from a nearby delicatessen lay crumpled on the table, with disposable chopsticks thrust into an empty plastic container beside it. Someone had evidently finished breakfast or some other meal and abandoned everything where it was. This was unquestionably the result of Mr. Shio’s carelessness.

Japanese: 「電話で話したとおり、見せたいものがあるんです」
English: “As I said on the telephone, there is something I want to show you.”

Japanese: リョウは部屋に入ると、さっそくテーブルの上に上着で包んだ虎の肉塊をどさりと置き、そして次にポケットからハンカチを取り出した。
English: The moment he entered the room, Ryo dropped the jacket-wrapped lump of tiger flesh onto the table, then took the handkerchief from his pocket.

Japanese: 「こっちの小さいのがコア組織。でかいのがそれ以外の体組織です」
English: “The small piece here is core tissue. The larger one is the rest of the body tissue.”

Japanese: リョウにとっては、これを汐さんに見せるのがここに尋ねた本当の趣旨らしい。てっきりおれは車を拝借した説明をするためにここへやって来たものと思っていたので、なんだか意外だった。
English: Showing this to Mr. Shio appeared to be Ryo’s true reason for coming. I had assumed we were here so that he could explain borrowing the truck, and found the revelation rather surprising.

Japanese: 「虎が再生するのを見た時はまさかと思ったけど、やっぱりビンゴでした」
English: “When I saw the tiger regenerate, I thought it couldn’t be—but it turns out I was right.”

Japanese: いいながらハンカチを開くと、先ほど虎の死骸からつまみ出した肉片があらわれる。……いや、これってもう肉片とは呼べないんじゃないか？
English: He opened the handkerchief as he spoke, revealing the scrap of flesh he had plucked from the tiger’s carcass. ...No. Could this still be called a scrap of flesh?
“This...”

Japanese: おれはリョウの方を見るけれど、彼の視線は汐さんの表情に注がれている。そして汐さんも、眉間にしわを寄せて難しい顔をしている。
English: I looked at Ryo, but his eyes were fixed on Mr. Shio’s face. Mr. Shio, in turn, wore a troubled frown.

Japanese: その物体は、赤色こそさきほどの肉片のままなんだけれど、その質感は肉と呼べるようなものではなく、幾分透明感を持っていて、ゲル状というのか？　クラゲみたいなゼリーみたいな、よくわからんものに変化していた。
English: The object was still as red as the flesh had been, but its texture was no longer anything one could call meat. It had become partly translucent and—gelatinous, perhaps? It was some incomprehensible substance resembling a jellyfish or a piece of jelly.

Japanese: しかもそれはグニャグニャと動き、ハンカチの上から逃れようとしている。
English: It was also squirming and struggling to escape the handkerchief.

Japanese: 「おい。なんだこれ。本当に、ただタイプＢが濃いだけなのかねえ？　こんなもの見たことがない」
English: “Listen. What is this? Is it truly nothing more than an unusually strong Type B? I have never seen such a thing.”

Japanese: リョウはおれの言葉には反応せず、真剣な顔で汐さんの方を見ながら、
English: Ryo did not respond to me. His expression serious, he kept looking at Mr. Shio and said,

Japanese: 「汐さん、見てくださいよこれ。虎から採取したんです。『虎』ですよ？」
English: “Mr. Shio, look at this. I collected it from a tiger. A ‘tiger,’ of all things.”

Japanese: そして、彼は先ほど滑走路で起きた出来事を話した。
English: Then he related what had happened on Runway Street.

Japanese: 汐さんは一言も口をきかずに静かに話を聞いた。そして聞き終わると、大きく溜息をつく。
English: Mr. Shio listened quietly without speaking once. When the account was over, he released a great sigh.

Japanese: 「まったく一緒ですよね。そして、虎ってのはそういうことなんじゃないですか？」
English: “It’s exactly the same, isn’t it? And doesn’t that account for the tiger?”

Japanese: リョウが勢い込んでいうと、
English: Ryo pressed him eagerly.

Japanese: 「そう考えたいが、まだなんとも言えんな」
English: “I would like to think so, but we still cannot say.”

Japanese: そして二人とも黙り込んでしまう。
English: Then both men fell silent.

Japanese: 二人の頭のなかには、これについて考えるだけの材料があるかもしれないけれど、おれはただただ驚くばっかりだ。黙っていれば二人がおれにもわかるような話をしてくれるかと思って待ってみたけれど、いつまでも沈黙している。
English: They might have possessed enough information to think about the matter, but I could only be astonished. I waited, supposing that if I remained quiet, they would eventually explain it in terms I could understand. Their silence continued without end.

Japanese: 「なあ、こいつ、まだ生きてるのかねえ？」
English: “Say, is this thing still alive?”

Japanese: 耐えられなくなっておれはそう尋ねた。リョウは顔を上げる。
English: Unable to endure it any longer, I asked. Ryo raised his head.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。といっても、生物の細胞は生体から切り裂かれてもある程度は生きるものだけどね。ただ、こいつは、それとは全く別のレベルで『生きている』。……見なよ、さっきと形ちがうでしょ？　切り離された途端、単体で生存出来るかたちに自分から変化したんだよ。これって結構すごいことなんだよ。詳しくわかりやすく説明するのはちょっと難しいけど……」
English: “It is. Of course, the cells of a living organism remain alive for a certain time even after they are cut away from the body. But this is ‘alive’ on an entirely different level. ...Look. It isn’t the same shape it was before, is it? The moment it was separated, it transformed itself into a form capable of surviving on its own. That is rather extraordinary. Explaining the details in simple terms would be difficult...”

Japanese: 「ありがとう。細かいことはいいんよ。どうせわからんのだし。それより、もう一つ質問に答えてくれるかなあ？　なんで虎がこんな風になるんだろう。やっぱりタイプBなのかい？　再生しているときはなんとなくそう思ったけど……でも、タイプBだからってこんなにならないだろうし……それとも、濃ければなるのか？」
English: “Thank you. I need no details. I wouldn’t understand them in any case. More importantly, might you answer one other question? Why does a tiger turn into this? Is it a Type B after all? While it was regenerating, that somehow seemed likely... But being a Type B should not make anything like this... Or does it, when the blood is strong enough?”

Japanese: 「まあ、それは、何と言ったらいいか……」
English: “Well, that is... How should I put it?”

Japanese: リョウは言葉を濁しながら、
English: Ryo equivocated, then said,

Japanese: 「とりあえず、タイプBではあると思う」
English: “For the moment, I think it is a Type B.”

Japanese: 「そうか。タイプBってのは謎の多い存在だなあ！　まあ、タイプBの上にAまでくっついてるおれが言うことでもないんだけどさ。でも、そういう話を聞くと自分というものがますます分からなくなるね。まったく、世界は不思議だなあ」
English: “I see. Type Bs are mysterious creatures indeed! Though perhaps that is no observation for me to make, when I have A fastened on top of B myself. Still, hearing such things only makes me understand myself less and less. The world is altogether marvelous.”

Japanese: おれはまじまじと、元は虎の一部であった物体を見つめた。
English: I stared fixedly at the object that had once been part of a tiger.

Japanese: 「地下室へ行くか……」
English: “Shall we go to the basement?”

Japanese: 汐さんが重い口を開く。
English: Mr. Shio finally broke his heavy silence.

Japanese: 「それがいいと思う」
English: “I think that would be best.”

Japanese: リョウは笑顔で頷き、テーブルにぽとりと落ちたゲルをつまみ上げ、またハンカチのなかに包み込む。
English: Ryo nodded with a smile, picked up the gel that had dropped onto the table, and wrapped it in the handkerchief once more.

Japanese: 汐健慈朗の自宅の地下にこんな部屋があるとは知らなかった。
English: I had not known that such a room existed beneath Kenjiro Shio’s home.

Japanese: いや、おれだけでなく、Y地区中の誰もが想像もしなかったろう。ゴミ処理会社社長宅の地下に、こんなに不思議な機材に満ちあふれたSFチックな部屋があるだなんて。
English: No—not only I. No one in Y District could have imagined that the basement of a waste-company president’s house contained an extraordinary room straight out of science fiction, overflowing with strange equipment.

Japanese: 何かの実験室？　あるいは研究室というやつなのだろうか？　そういう場所に足を踏み入れたことがないからちょっと断定は出来ないけれど、なんだかそんな気がする。
English: Was it some kind of laboratory? Or what they call a research room? I had never set foot in such a place before and could not say for certain, but that was the impression it gave me.

Japanese: 棚には薬品の入った瓶が並び、スポイトやビーカーの姿も目に付く。そして何を測定するのかはわからないけれども何かを測定するらしい、メーターのついた機械があり、さらに用途を想像することも出来ない様々な機械が所狭しと並んでいる。
English: The shelves held rows of chemical bottles, and pipettes and beakers caught the eye. There were machines fitted with gauges, apparently intended to measure something—though I could not imagine what—and still more devices of utterly unknowable purpose crowded every available space.

Japanese: そこは全体的にひどく雑然としていて、最小限の機能性をたもつ整理整頓しかなされていない。ガラス製の機具や、ノートが散乱している。ここばかりは確実に一人娘の手が入っていないのだろうなあと、おれにも断言出来る。
English: The entire room was in terrible disorder, organized only so far as necessary to remain minimally functional. Glass implements and notebooks lay scattered about. Here, at least, even I could say with certainty that his daughter had never done the tidying.

Japanese: こんなわけのわからない施設を、どうして自宅に持っているのか？　何に使っているのか？　彼は何者なのか？
English: Why did he keep such an incomprehensible facility in his home? What did he use it for? Who was this man?

Japanese: おれはなんだか妙な目眩がしそうだった。
English: A strange dizziness threatened to overtake me.

Japanese: その一方、リョウは勝手知ったる人の家とばかりに部屋の奥へ進んでゆく。そして、まず冷蔵庫らしき装置に上着で包んだままの肉塊を無造作に入れると、次に部屋の中央にあるテーブルの上の紙くずを手で払って、どこからか取り出したシャーレを置き、その中に件のゲルを入れた。
English: Ryo, meanwhile, proceeded into the room with the ease of a man who knew another’s home as well as his own. First he carelessly placed the jacket-wrapped lump of flesh inside a device resembling a refrigerator. Then he swept the scraps of paper from the table in the center of the room with one hand, produced a petri dish from somewhere, and put the gel inside it.

Japanese: リョウと汐さんはよほど通じ合っているらしく、お互い短い単語を口にし、アイコンタクトをとり、それで充分コミュニケーションがとれているようだがおれにはちっともわからん。
English: Ryo and Mr. Shio seemed to understand one another extraordinarily well. A few brief words and exchanges of glances appeared sufficient for them to communicate, but I understood none of it.

Japanese: ゲルはシャーレの中で伸びたり縮んだりを繰り返し、時々突起のようなものを作って中空にさしのべては、また本体に吸収させている。
English: Inside the petri dish, the gel repeatedly stretched and contracted. From time to time it formed something like a projection, extended it into the air, and then absorbed it back into the main body.

Japanese: 確かにこれは生きている。おれもへんてこな生き物は沢山見てきたからそこまでは驚きはしないけれど、それでも、見たことがない現象ではある。
English: There could be no doubt that it was alive. I had seen many strange creatures and was not so easily astonished, but even I had never seen this phenomenon before.

Japanese: グレートホールの近くでは、タイプAやタイプBといったミュータントが生まれやすいと言う話がある。それと関係してか、このY地区では小動物や植物にも突然変異をした奇妙な形状や能力を持つ生き物が多い。子供達はよくそういった珍しい生き物を見つけるとおもちゃにして遊び、大抵その結果殺してしまう。
English: People say that mutants such as Type As and Type Bs are more likely to be born near the Great Hole. Perhaps for that reason, Y District also abounds in small animals and plants with strange mutant forms and abilities. When children discover one of these rare creatures, they often make a toy of it and, in most cases, kill it in the process.

Japanese: リョウはちょっと違って、生きたまま持ち帰ることを重要視して、ポケットやらカゴやらに片っ端から突っ込んでいたが、当時からこんな風に汐さんのところに持ち込んで二人で話していたんだろうか？
English: Ryo was a little different. He considered it important to bring them home alive and stuffed every creature he found into a pocket or basket. Had he been bringing them to Mr. Shio even then, so that the two of them could discuss them like this?

Japanese: 二人の口ぶりから察するに、どうもそんな気がする。
English: Judging from the way they spoke, I rather thought he had.

Japanese: おれはずっとリョウとは親友だと思っていたけれど、ちっとも知らなかったなあ。
English: I had always considered Ryo my closest friend, yet I had known nothing about it.

Japanese: 驚きつつ感心していると、汐さんはいつの間にか透明なプラスチックの容器を手にしていて、そこから赤っぽい液体をゲルの入ったシャーレに注ぎ込む。
English: While I stood there astonished and impressed, I noticed that Mr. Shio was holding a transparent plastic container. He poured a reddish liquid from it into the petri dish holding the gel.

Japanese: 「これは何ですか？」
English: “What is that?”

Japanese: 「細胞の培養に使う基礎培地だよ」
English: “Basal medium. It’s used to culture cells.”

Japanese: 汐さんのかわりにリョウが答える。
English: Ryo answered in Mr. Shio’s place.

Japanese: 「キソバイチ？」
English: “Bay-sull meedyum?”

Japanese: 「水に、ちょっとした栄養が混ざっているんだ」
English: “Water with a few nutrients mixed into it.”

Japanese: 「つまり、こいつに餌を与えているわけか？」
English: “In other words, you are feeding the thing?”

Japanese: 「まあそうだね」
English: “More or less.”

Japanese: ゲルが浸る程度に液体が行き渡ると、汐さんはガラスのふたをシャーレに被せて、上に重しのつもりか、何冊かの本を上に置いた。一番上になった本には、アルファベットでタイトルが書かれている。
English: Once there was enough liquid to immerse the gel, Mr. Shio placed a glass lid over the petri dish, then stacked several books on top, apparently to weigh it down. The title of the uppermost book was written in the Roman alphabet.

Japanese: 「これ何語だ？　ら……るみえれ……そーたんと……」
English: “What language is this? La... loo-mee-air... soh-tant...”

Japanese: おれが首をひねっていると、汐さんは立ち上がる。
English: As I puzzled over it, Mr. Shio stood.

Japanese: 「こいつはあとで洗浄して無菌室に保管しておく。今日はもうしまいにしよう。もうすぐ松が帰って来る」
English: “I’ll clean this later and keep it in the sterile room. We are finished for today. Matsu will be home soon.”

Japanese: 彼は一方的にそう言い放ち、返事も待たずに地下室を出る階段へ向う。おれとリョウはその背中を追う格好になる。
English: He made the announcement unilaterally and headed for the stairs without waiting for a response. Ryo and I had little choice but to follow.

Japanese: 「なあ、アレを飼うのか？」
English: “Are you going to keep that thing?”

Japanese: おれが小声で尋ねるが、リョウはそれには答えず、
English: I asked quietly. Ryo did not answer the question.

Japanese: 「このことは、松子には内緒にしてよ」
English: “Do not tell Matsuko about this.”

Japanese: とだけ言った。
English: That was all he said.

Japanese: どういう事情があるのかよくわからないが、おれはとにかく頷いた。
English: I did not understand the circumstances, but nodded all the same.

Japanese: リビングに戻ると、今さっきのことなどなかったかのようにリョウと汐さんは世間話を始めた。
English: Back in the living room, Ryo and Mr. Shio began making small talk as though nothing had happened.

Japanese: リョウの大学生活についてや、師事している教授のこと。話の内容を聞いていると、汐さんは一人暮らしになってからのリョウの状況をそれほど詳しく知っているわけではないようだった。そしてもう一つ意外なのは、汐さんが大学やら学問やらの世界に詳しいような物言いをしているところ。
English: They discussed Ryo’s university life and the professor under whom he studied. From their conversation, Mr. Shio did not seem to know much about Ryo’s circumstances since he began living alone. Another surprise was the familiarity with which Mr. Shio spoke about universities and the academic world.

Japanese: 「汐さんって、昔そういう関係の仕事か何かしていたの？　学者か何か。どう見てもそういう人間の風貌じゃないが」
English: “Mr. Shio, did you once have some kind of work in that field? Were you a scholar? You certainly do not look like one.”

Japanese: やたらと人の素性を尋ねるのは失礼だとは承知の上だけれど、おれはたまらなくなって地下の施設を見た時からの疑問を素直にぶつけてみた。しかし、汐さんは自分のことは話したくないらしく、「ああ」と、肯定とも否定ともつかない声をあげるだけだった。
English: I knew it was rude to pry into a man’s history, but I could restrain myself no longer and put to him the question that had troubled me ever since I saw the underground facility. Mr. Shio apparently had no wish to discuss himself. He merely grunted, “Ah,” in a way that conveyed neither assent nor denial.

Japanese: おれはなるべく黙って二人の話を聞いたのだけれど、話しているのはほとんどリョウで、汐さんは黙って頷きながら、時々質問をするだけだった。
English: I tried to remain silent and listen to the two of them. Ryo, however, did almost all the talking. Mr. Shio nodded without speaking and only occasionally asked a question.

Japanese: リョウは学校での生活に充実感を持っているというようなことを語る。生物系の勉強をしているらしいが、よほど性にあっているらしい。一方、最近Y地区では話題となっている父のクリス・ツェーの病気の話などはまず口にしなかった。
English: Ryo spoke of finding his life at university fulfilling. He was studying some branch of biology, which appeared to suit him exceedingly well. On the other hand, he said virtually nothing about the illness of his father, Chris Tse, though the matter had lately become the talk of Y District.

Japanese: おれからすると、わざと話題を避けているように見える。
English: To me, it looked as though he were deliberately avoiding the subject.

Japanese: ということはつまり、意識はしてるってことだ。案外、こいつは本当にこの街に帰ってくるのかもしれないな。
English: That would mean it was on his mind. Perhaps, against all expectation, he truly would return to this city.

Japanese: そんなことを考えているうちに、汐健慈朗の一人娘が買い物籠を下げて帰って来た。
English: While I entertained such thoughts, Kenjiro Shio’s only daughter returned home carrying a shopping basket.

Japanese: 入り口のところで目を丸くするその子が汐健慈朗の娘、汐松子。おれは親しみを込めて松坊と呼んでいる。
English: The girl staring wide-eyed from the entrance was Kenjiro Shio’s daughter, Matsuko Shio. I affectionately called her Matsu.

Japanese: 「よう、久しぶりじゃないかあ。なあ、今日はいい日だろ？　お前の王子様と一緒に来たんだぞ」
English: “Well, it has been a long time! Today is a fine day, is it not? I have brought your prince with me.”

Japanese: 「な、な、何をっ……そんなっ……」
English: “W-w-what are you—? That is...”

Japanese: 松坊は何度同じネタでからかっても同じように照れて赤面するあたりに、からかい甲斐がある。
English: No matter how often I teased Matsu in precisely the same way, she blushed with precisely the same embarrassment. It made teasing her very rewarding.

Japanese: 「なあリョウよ、松坊は一段と美人になったように思えるんだけど、これっておれの気のせいかな？」
English: “Say, Ryo. It seems to me that Matsu has grown even more beautiful. Do you suppose I am imagining it?”

Japanese: 「気のせいだろう」
English: “You probably are.”

Japanese: 一方、リョウは自分の興味のある話題にはやたらと興奮するくせに、それ以外にはまったく乗ってこないで眠そうにしているだけだから、からかう甲斐というものがない。
English: For his part, Ryo grew absurdly excited over subjects that interested him, but responded to everything else by looking sleepy and refusing to engage. There was no pleasure in teasing him.

Japanese: 「ど、どうして連絡くれなかったんですか？　こっちに帰って来てる時は連絡をくださいって言っていたじゃないですか」
English: “W-why didn’t you contact me? I asked you to let me know whenever you came back here.”

Japanese: 松坊は赤い顔のままむきになってリョウに抗議をする。
English: Still red in the face, Matsu earnestly protested to Ryo.

Japanese: 「さっさとアパートに戻るつもりだったんだ。だからここに来るのは予定外だったんだよ」
English: “I meant to return to my apartment immediately. Coming here was not part of the plan.”

Japanese: 「うちに寄るのが急だったとしても、Y地区に戻ってくるのも急だったんですか？　事前に連絡も出来ないくらい？　それはちょっと無理のある言い訳だと思うんですけど」
English: “Even if visiting us was sudden, was your return to Y District sudden as well? So sudden that you couldn’t contact me beforehand? I find that excuse rather difficult to accept.”

Japanese: 松坊は頬をふくらませてリョウを睨み付ける。
English: Matsu puffed out her cheeks and glared at Ryo.

Japanese: 確かにもっともだ。リョウはどうやって答えるつもりかと見守っていると、
English: Her objection was perfectly reasonable. I watched to see how Ryo would answer.

Japanese: 「他に考えることが一杯あって、連絡をするのがめんどくさかったんだよ」
English: “I had too many other things to think about. Contacting you seemed like a nuisance.”

Japanese: 言い訳するつもりもないらしい。それに、せめられているわりに、リョウは横柄な態度だ。松坊も松坊で、
English: Apparently, he did not intend to make excuses at all. Despite being the one under reproach, Ryo remained thoroughly arrogant. Matsu, for her part, said,

Japanese: 「めんどくさいなんて、困ります。これじゃあ、あり合わせのものでしかご飯が作れません……」
English: “You can’t just say it was too much trouble. Now I can only make dinner from whatever happens to be in the house...”

Japanese: と、かなり酷いことを言われているにもかかわらず、それによって怒りが持続するわけでもなく、ただ困っている。
English: Despite the rather dreadful thing he had said to her, she could not sustain any anger over it. She only seemed troubled.

Japanese: 「まあいいよ。普通のでいいんだ」
English: “That’s fine. An ordinary meal will do.”

Japanese: リョウはあくまで上からものを言う。
English: Ryo kept talking down to her.

Japanese: 本人達がそれで納得しているのならいいが、相変わらずよくわからん関係性の二人だ。
English: If the two of them found the arrangement satisfactory, then it was no concern of mine. Even so, theirs remained a relationship I could not quite understand.

Japanese: 昔から汐さんを父のように慕っているリョウは、勿論松坊とは兄妹のように親しい関係で……いや、むしろそれ以上に親密だ。少なくともおれは、リョウに松坊よりも親しくしている異性がいるなんて聞いたこともない。
English: Ryo had revered Mr. Shio like a father since childhood, and he was naturally as close to Matsu as a brother... No, closer than that. At least, I had never heard of Ryo being closer to any other woman.

Japanese: が、その接し方はいつもリョウの方が一方的に何かを言い、松坊はそれに従順に従っている。そういう力関係が出来てしまってるんだろうか？
English: Yet in their interactions, Ryo always set the terms, and Matsu obediently followed. Had some such balance of power become established between them?

Japanese: 松坊は優良企業シオクリーンの令嬢で、この辺りではなかなか尊重される立場なんだけれども、そういったプライドを見せることはない。いつも素直で、本気で怒ったところはおれも見たことがない。
English: As the young lady of the highly successful Shio Clean, Matsu occupied a rather respected position in the neighborhood. Yet she showed no pride in it. She was always sincere, and I had never once seen her truly angry.

Japanese: 「それじゃあ、出来る限りがんばって、なんとか作ります」
English: “Then I shall do everything I can and somehow manage to make something.”

Japanese: 松坊は自信なさげに言う。
English: Matsu did not sound confident.

Japanese: 「なあ、今日の飯はなんだ？」
English: “So, what are we having today?”

Japanese: そこへ汐さんが空気を読まないマイペースな言葉を投げかけると、松坊は、
English: Oblivious to the mood, Mr. Shio broke in with a question at his own unhurried pace. Matsu answered,

Japanese: 「ハンバーグと、きんぴらごぼうとひややっこです……」
English: “Hamburger steak, kinpira gobo, and chilled tofu...”

Japanese: 恥ずかしそうにうつむいた。
English: She lowered her head in embarrassment.

Japanese: 「こんなにお客さんがいると知っていたら、もっと贅沢なものを用意したのに……」
English: “If I had known we would have so many guests, I would have prepared something more extravagant...”

Japanese: おれはハンバーグと聞いてさっきの虎を切り刻んだシーンを思い出し、内心穏やかではなかったが、
English: The words hamburger steak brought back the sight of the tiger being cut to pieces, which left me inwardly unsettled. Nevertheless,

Japanese: 「いいじゃないか。そういう家庭料理が一番なんだよ！」
English: “That sounds excellent. Home cooking of that kind is best of all!”

Japanese: と胸を張っていった。
English: I declared it with my chest thrust out.

Japanese: そして松坊がキッチンへ去ってから、
English: After Matsu went into the kitchen,

Japanese: 「なあ、やっぱり松坊、本当に可愛くなってないか？　こんな感じの子だったっけ」
English: “Tell me, hasn’t Matsu really become much prettier? Was she always that sort of girl?”

Japanese: そうリョウに耳打ちしたが、彼は、
English: I whispered the question to Ryo. He merely replied,

Japanese: 「そうかなあ」
English: “Has she?”

Japanese: と気のない返事をするばかりだった。
English: His voice could not have been less interested.

Japanese: おれとリョウは、そこで遅めの昼食を頂いてから社長宅を出た。
English: Ryo and I ate a late lunch there, then left the president’s house.

Japanese: 昨日とはうってかわった薄曇りの空の下、おれ達は並んで滑走路通りの方へ歩き始めた。
English: Beneath a lightly overcast sky entirely unlike the day before, we began walking side by side toward Runway Street.

Japanese: 松坊が作ったハンバーグは絶品だった。つなぎを使わない挽肉だけで作った本格的な製法は、汐さんの趣味か、リョウの趣味か。ニンジンや玉ねぎが入っていたり、豆腐やおからがはいっているやつとは趣が違う、いかにも肉料理を食ったという食べ応えがあるハンバーグで、火加減も絶妙で噛むと肉汁があふれ出た。
English: Matsu’s hamburger steak had been exquisite. Was its authentic preparation—ground meat alone, with no binder—Mr. Shio’s preference, or Ryo’s? It bore no resemblance to versions padded with carrots and onions, or with tofu and soybean pulp. This was a hamburger steak that left one with the satisfaction of having eaten a true meat dish. It was cooked perfectly, and every bite released a flood of juices.

Japanese: 別の時に喰ったなら大変満足がいったのだろうけれど、あいにくその時おれは、どうにもあのスプラッターシーンが脳裏にちらついて、そのいかにも肉と言った食感は気色悪いものとしか感じられず、非常にもったいなかった。
English: At any other time, it would have left me entirely satisfied. Unfortunately, the splatter scene kept flickering through my mind, and I could experience that distinctly meaty texture only as something nauseating. What a terrible waste.

Japanese: 食べた後でもまだ吐き気のような胸のむかつきが収まらない。リョウにはそんな感性はないらしく、しれっとした顔をしている。おれが不必要に繊細なのかもしれないけれど、やっぱりこいつもちょっとおかしいと思う。
English: Even after the meal, the queasiness in my stomach would not subside. Ryo, apparently lacking any such sensibility, wore his usual unconcerned expression. Perhaps I was unnecessarily delicate, but I still thought there was something a little wrong with him.

Japanese: 「なんだ気分が悪いのか。無理して喰うからでしょ」
English: “What, are you ill? That’s what comes of forcing yourself to eat.”

Japanese: 隣を歩くリョウは冷たく言う。内心納得は出来ないが、反論したところで無駄だ。そんなのはおれもよく分かっている。
English: Ryo spoke coldly as he walked beside me. I could not agree with him, but arguing would be useless. Even I understood that much.

Japanese: 「女の子が出してくれた料理を残すなんて、おれには出来ない相談だな。……なあ、それよりもさ、リョウってさ、子供の時から汐さんとあんなふうに喋ったりしてたのか？」
English: “Leaving food a girl has made for me is simply beyond my power. ...More importantly, Ryo, did you speak with Mr. Shio that way even when you were a child?”

Japanese: 「うん」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: 「お前が大学に行ったのって、汐さんの影響があるんかねえ？」
English: “Was Mr. Shio’s influence part of the reason you went to university?”

Japanese: 「それもあるかな。何にしろ、子供の頃からそういう風に生きたかったんだよ。僕からすれば、みんなびっくりしたことの方が信じられない。何も隠してなんかいなかったろう？　常に、この広大無辺の世界の不思議や奥深さに対する賞賛を口にしていたじゃないか。世の中は凄いんだって。Ｙ地区は狭すぎるって」
English: “Perhaps. In any case, I wanted to live that way from the time I was a child. From my perspective, the unbelievable thing is that everyone was surprised. I never hid it, did I? I was forever proclaiming my admiration for the mystery and unfathomable depth of this vast world. I told you how extraordinary the world was. I told you Y District was too small.”

Japanese: 「不満そうにするなよ。あのな、そんなの、リョウがまたおかしなこと言ってるって、みんな聞き流してたから、誰も全然真に受けてなかったんよ」
English: “Don’t sound so aggrieved. Listen, everyone wrote it off as you saying something strange again. No one took you seriously in the least.”

Japanese: おれが事実を指摘してやると、リョウは不本意だという風に眉間にしわをよせ、
English: When I pointed out this simple fact, Ryo frowned as though deeply dissatisfied.

Japanese: 「僕はみんなも誘ったじゃないか。一緒に行きたければ、勉強も教えてやるし、学費の稼ぎ方も教えてやるって。なのに、そんな言われ方をするほうが不可解だ」
English: “I invited everyone to come with me. I said that if anyone wished to go, I would teach them how to study and how to earn their tuition. What I find incomprehensible is hearing it described that way.”

Japanese: 「だって、大学に行くなんて完全に想像を超えた進路だし、仕方ないでしょう？　……まあ、今になって思えば確かに有言実行ってだけなんだが、それはその通りなんだが、当時は、Y地区のガキどもは、みんな菅原リョウは街の住人の一人として生きてゆくと信じてたんよ。あの龍頭の息子だって誰も知らなかったしな。……しかし、お前には学生なんかやるより何か特別な才能があるような気がするんだけどなあ。それを腐らせてしまうのは勿体ない」
English: “Going to university was so completely beyond anything we imagined that our reaction was only natural. ...Looking back, yes, you did exactly what you said you would. That is true. But at the time, every child in Y District believed that Ryo Sugawara would live his life as one of the city’s people. None of us knew you were the Longtou’s son. ...Still, I feel that you possess some exceptional talent better suited to you than being a student. It would be a great shame to let that gift rot.”

Japanese: 「何言ってるんだよ」
English: “What are you talking about?”

Japanese: リョウはせせら笑う。
English: Ryo gave a scornful laugh.

Japanese: 「僕は好きにやってだだけさ。みんなと肌が合うなんて一度も思ったことはない。リーダーはいつもお前だったじゃないか。今だってそうだろう？　僕が進学を進めても誰も真に受けないのに、お前がグレートホール饅頭とかいうよくわからない仕事をはじめたら人が集まる。僕には理解出来ない世界だ。実際、僕にはそういう一番上に立つ役割は向いていないと思うよ。自分でもわかってる。好きなことを勝手に考えて、勝手に行動をするほうが向いてる。僕はとにかく何にもとらわれずに自由に生きたいんだ」
English: “I merely did as I pleased. I never once imagined that I belonged among the others. You were always the leader, not me. You still are, aren’t you? When I encouraged them to pursue further education, no one listened. When you started some incomprehensible enterprise called Great Hole Buns, people gathered around you. It is a world I cannot understand. In fact, I don’t believe I am suited to a position at the top of anything. I know that much about myself. I am better suited to thinking about whatever I please and acting on it as I please. Above all else, I want to live freely, bound by nothing.”

Japanese: 「そうは言うけどなあ。グレートホール饅頭はかなり重要な仕事なんだぞ？　よくわからないってのは失礼だな」
English: “You say that, but the Great Hole Bun project is important work. Calling the enterprise incomprehensible is terribly rude.”

Japanese: 「そうか。それはごめん」
English: “Is that so? I apologize.”

Japanese: 「おいおい、素直に謝られると困るなあ。……まあいいや、リョウ。とりあえず、今の生活は楽しいかい？」
English: “Come now, a sincere apology leaves me at a loss. ...Well, never mind. Ryo, are you enjoying your present life?”

Japanese: 「楽しいよ」
English: “I am.”

Japanese: リョウはこくりと頷いて、
English: Ryo gave a small nod.

Japanese: 「子供の時から、ずっと不思議だったんだ。生き物はすべて死んでしまうのに、なぜ生まれてくるのか。僕らはどういうかたちをしているのか。生命ってものはなんなのか。……僕がいまいるところでは、そのことだけを考えることが出来る。こんなに『無駄がない』という気持になったのは初めてだよ。ずっと、何をしても『こんなことをしてる場合じゃない』っていう焦りしかなかったのに、今はそれがなくなったんだ。生まれて初めて身体にぴったりあったサイズの服を着ているような感じだ」
English: “I wondered from the time I was a child: Why are living creatures born when they must all die? What shape do we have? What is this thing we call life? ...Where I am now, I can devote myself to those questions alone. For the first time, I feel that nothing in me is being ‘wasted.’ Before, no matter what I did, I felt only the anxiety that this was not what I ought to be doing. Now it is gone. It feels as though I have put on clothes that fit my body perfectly for the first time in my life.”

Japanese: 「そうかあ。でも、この街にもいろんな生命があるじゃないか。この街のみんなは実に様々な物を背負っている」
English: “I see. But this city contains all kinds of lives as well. Everyone here carries such very different burdens.”

Japanese: 「僕がしているのは波瀾万丈の人生とか、そういう話じゃないんだよ」
English: “I am not talking about eventful lives or people’s life stories.”

Japanese: 「まあ、何にしろ、そんなに楽しいんじゃ、うまく騙しておれの仕事を手伝ってもらうわけにもいかないなあ」
English: “Well, in any case, if you are enjoying it so much, I cannot very well deceive you into helping with my work.”

Japanese: おれが笑うと、リョウはちらとこちらを見て、そしてすぐに視線をそらす。
English: I laughed. Ryo glanced at me, then immediately looked away.

Japanese: 「どうしたん？」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「なんでもないよ」
English: “Nothing.”

Japanese: リョウはそう言うが、気まずそうに唇を一文字に引き締めている。
English: So Ryo said, but he looked awkward as he pressed his lips into a straight line.

Japanese: 「あ、わかったぞ。いま間接的に、おれたちとの青春を無駄だらけだって言ったことになってしまったから、気にしてるんだな」
English: “Ah, I understand. You have realized that you indirectly described the youth we shared as full of waste, and now it troubles you.”

Japanese: 「違うよ」
English: “That isn’t it.”

Japanese: 「いや、わかるよ。でも気にしなくていい。子供の時は誰だってサイズのあわない服を着せられるもんよ。おれたちだってみんなそうだったし、だから無駄に苦しんだんだ。その時代を共有出来るってことが、同世代のかけがえのない輝きなんよ。そう思わないか？」
English: “No, I understand. But there is no need to worry. When we are children, we are all made to wear clothes that do not fit. Every one of us was the same, and that is why we suffered needlessly. The fact that we shared those years is the irreplaceable brightness of growing up together. Don’t you think?”

Japanese: 「道夫は相変わらずじじ臭い。同い年とは思えないな」
English: “You still talk like an old man, Michio. It’s hard to believe we’re the same age.”

Japanese: そう言ってリョウは少し笑った。
English: Ryo smiled a little as he said it.

Japanese: 「そうだろう」
English: “Exactly.”

Japanese: おれは頷いてから、
English: I nodded, then said,

Japanese: 「まあ、本当にそれがやりたいならいいさ。ただ、この街に存在する何かから逃げてその道を選んだってのなら、絶対後悔するだろうけどね」
English: “Well, if that is truly what you want to do, then it is all right. But if you chose that path to escape from something that exists in this city, you will certainly regret it.”

Japanese: 「道夫は、人の良さそうな顔して、時々そういういやなことを言う」
English: “For someone with such a kindly face, you occasionally say remarkably unpleasant things.”

Japanese: リョウはしかめっつらを作って言う。
English: Ryo spoke with a scowl.

Japanese: 「どっちにしろ、街のためとか、何かのためとか、そういうの僕は好きじゃないんだ。とらわれている感じがする。人間味がないよ。僕はその時その時で、一番やりたいことだけをやるんだ。一度きりの人生なんだからね」
English: “In any case, I dislike doing things for the city, or for some cause, or anything of that kind. It feels like being bound. There is nothing human about it. At each moment, I will do only what I most desire to do. We have only one life.”

Japanese: 「そうかなあ、何かに殉じて一途に生きるのは、男らしいと思うけどなあ」
English: “Do you think so? I find there is something manly in devoting oneself wholly to a cause.”

Japanese: おれは肩をすくめ、
English: I shrugged.

Japanese: 「……まあいいや。それでさ、お前は今日これからどうするんだ？」
English: “...Well, never mind. What are you going to do for the rest of today?”

Japanese: そう話題を変えた。
English: Thus I changed the subject.

Japanese: 「とりあえずホテルに帰るよ。今日こそアパートに帰りたかったんだけど、それはちょっと取りやめかな」
English: “I’ll return to the hotel for now. I wanted to go back to my apartment today, but I suppose I’ll postpone that.”

Japanese: 「そうか。おれは滑走路通りに戻らないといけない。さっき携帯を見たらコンタからメールが何通も届いてたんよ。売り物のグレートホール饅頭をほったらかしにしてたのすっかり忘れてた」
English: “I see. I must go back to Runway Street. When I checked my phone earlier, I found several messages from Konta. I had entirely forgotten that I left all our Great Hole Buns unattended.”

Japanese: 「そうか。……饅頭は売れてるの？」
English: “I see. ...Are the buns selling?”

Japanese: 「正直、あんまり」
English: “To be honest, not very well.”

Japanese: 「あはは。だろうと思った」
English: “Ahaha. I thought as much.”

Japanese: 「なあ、おれ、饅頭売りに向いてないのかなあ？」
English: “Tell me, perhaps I am not suited to selling buns?”

Japanese: 他ではあまりいわない愚痴を、つい旧友に漏らしてしまうと、
English: Before I knew it, I had confided to an old friend a complaint I seldom voiced elsewhere.

Japanese: 「僕は向いてると思うけどね。そういう仕事を選ぶのは道夫らしいとも思う」
English: “I think you are suited to it. Choosing work of that kind also seems very much like you, Michio.”

Japanese: 「そうか。そう言われると安心するな。おれのまわりの連中は、みんな、もっと生まれもった能力を行かした仕事をしろって言うんよ」
English: “You do? Hearing that puts my mind at ease. Everyone around me says I should find work that makes greater use of the abilities I was born with.”

Japanese: おれがそう言うと、リョウはまた笑って、
English: At that, Ryo smiled again.

Japanese: 「そりゃまわりが言うことも一理あるさ。ある程度実用的な力を持ったタイプAはもうちょっと超能力を生かした仕事につくものだからね。それが一番稼げるんだし」
English: “They do have a point. Type As with reasonably practical powers generally find work that makes greater use of them. It earns the most money, after all.”

Japanese: 「でも、生まれ持った能力と、やりたいことが一致するわけじゃないからなあ」
English: “But the ability you’re born with doesn’t necessarily match what you want to do.”

Japanese: 「それは確かにそうだけれど」
English: “That is certainly true.”

Japanese: 「そういえば、リョウ、能力についてなんだけどさ」
English: “Speaking of abilities, Ryo...”

Japanese: 「なに？」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 「さっき、おれの能力のこと、なんか変な呼び方してたろ」
English: “Earlier, you used some strange name for my power.”

Japanese: 「サイコソード？」
English: “Psycho-Sword?”

Japanese: 「そうそう。その呼び方、もう二度としないでくれないかなあ」
English: “Yes, that. Would you kindly never call it that again?”

Japanese: 「なんで？」
English: “Why not?”

Japanese: 「だって恥ずかしいだろ」
English: “Because it is embarrassing.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ、『エクスカリバー』か？　それとも、『ファイナルエアカッター』と言えばいいのか？」
English: “Then should I call it ‘Excalibur’? Or perhaps ‘Final Air Cutter’?”

Japanese: 「そ、それもやめろ」
English: “S-stop those too.”

Japanese: 「なんだよ。お前がそう呼べって言ったんじゃないか」
English: “What are you talking about? You told me to call it that.”

Japanese: 「十四とか十五くらいの時だろ。もういい加減やめてくれよ……。あの時のおれは途方もなく恥ずかしい存在だったんだ。反省しているんだから、頼むから勘弁してくれないか」
English: “I was fourteen or fifteen. Surely it is time to stop. ...The person I was then is a source of boundless embarrassment to me. I have reflected upon my errors, so please, spare me.”

Japanese: 「仕方ないな。……じゃあ、今はその能力をなんて呼べばいいんだ？」
English: “I suppose I have no choice. ...What am I to call the power now, then?”

Japanese: 「特に名前はないよ」
English: “It has no particular name.”

Japanese: 「……なんだかつまらないな」
English: “...How dull.”

Japanese: リョウはどこまで本当なのか、残念そうに溜息をつく。
English: Ryo sighed in disappointment, though how much of it was sincere I could not tell.

Japanese: そしてまた沈黙が生まれた。
English: Silence fell between us once more.

Japanese: こうしてこいつと並んで歩くのは久しぶりだったし、今日はいろいろなことがあった。彼に聞かなくてはいけないことや、話さなくてはいけないことは沢山あるはずなんだ。
English: It had been a long time since I walked beside him this way, and a great many things had happened that day. Surely there were many questions I needed to ask him and many things I needed to say.

Japanese: だけど、おれは話すためにそれらにうまく順番をつけることが出来なかった。
English: Yet I could not sort any of them into an order that would let me begin.

Japanese: それに、余計なことは何も話さない方がいいような気もした。
English: I also felt that it might be better to say nothing unnecessary.

Japanese: 話さなくても、同じ少年時代を過ごしたおれたちは、きっと大事なことは共有出来ている。
English: Even without words, we who had passed the same boyhood together could surely share what mattered.

Japanese: 気づけば無言のまま滑走路通りにさしかかろうとしていた。数年前は何もいわなくともまた明日顔を合わせるのがわかっていたけれど今は違う。ここから先には、それぞれに違った『戻るべき場所』が待っている。
English: Before I knew it, we were approaching Runway Street without having spoken. A few years earlier, we had known without saying it that we would see one another again the next day. That was no longer true. Ahead of us waited two different ‘places we had to return to.’

Japanese: 少し寂しいが、それはおれたちが自分の道を見つけたということで、それは素晴らしいことなんだろう。
English: It was a little lonely. Yet it meant that each of us had found his own path, and that must surely have been something wonderful.

Japanese: 「じゃあな。何か困ったことがあれば連絡しろよ」
English: “Goodbye, then. If you find yourself in trouble, contact me.”

Japanese: 別れ際、滑走路通りの喧噪のなかでおれはそう言った。
English: I said it as we parted amid the noise of Runway Street.

Japanese: 「わかった。またな」
English: “All right. See you.”

Japanese: リョウはそう言ってはにかんだ。
English: Ryo spoke with a bashful smile.

Japanese: そして、おれはバーバラの店の方向へ。
English: And I went toward Barbara’s shop.

Japanese: リョウは、ホテルの方向へ。
English: Ryo went toward his hotel.

Japanese: 昼頃に指導教員の携帯電話に連絡をした。
English: Around noon, I telephoned my academic adviser on his mobile.

Japanese: 「ちょっとゴタゴタが長引いていまして、戻るのが遅れそうです」
English: “The complications here are taking longer than expected. I’m afraid my return will be delayed.”

Japanese: 『ゴタゴタってどういうことだい？　知り合いの結婚式に行ったんじゃなかったのか？』
English: “What sort of complications? I thought you went to an acquaintance’s wedding.”

Japanese: 「実家に戻ったところ、父が病気であまりよくない状態でして……」
English: “When I returned home, I found my father ill and in rather poor condition...”

Japanese: 『なるほど、それは大変だな。わかった、落ち着くまでそちらにいると良い。……しかし、残念だな。せっかく、新しい定石を覚えたから試そうと思っていたのに』
English: “I see. That is serious. Very well, stay there until matters have settled. ...It is a pity, though. I had just learned a new joseki and meant to try it against you.”

Japanese: 「僕は先生と囲碁を打つために研究室に通っているわけじゃないんですけどね」
English: “I don’t come to your lab just to play Go with you, Professor.”

Japanese: 昨夜ベッドのなかで暫く考えて、僕はこの街への滞在時間を伸ばすことに決めた。
English: After thinking for some time in bed the previous night, I had decided to extend my stay in the city.

Japanese: 率直に言って、その住まいで目にした父の病状が思った以上に悪かった。医師の診断がどの程度正確なものかは知るよしもないが、印象としては今にも死んでしまいそうだった。
English: To speak frankly, my father’s condition was worse than I had expected. I had no means of knowing how accurate the physician’s diagnosis might be, but my own impression was that he could die at any moment.

Japanese: いくら疎遠な父であったとは言え、僕がその長男であることはこのＹＳの幹部達なら誰でも知っている。独裁者の死は権力の移動を意味するし、その過程において、何かゴタゴタが起こらないともかぎらない。むしろ何も起こらないと考えるほうが不自然だろう。
English: Estranged though we were, every officer of YS knew that I was his eldest son. The death of a dictator means a transfer of power, and complications of some sort could easily arise in that process. It would be stranger, in fact, to assume that nothing would happen.

Japanese: その時重要な当事者の一人であるこの僕が遠く離れているというのは、やはり不安の方が先に立つ。妹のこともある。自分のこともある。
English: The thought that I, one of the people most directly involved, might be far away when that occurred naturally produced some anxiety. There was my sister to consider. There was also myself.

Japanese: 感情的な不快感はあるけれども、まあ経緯を見守る方が冷静な判断だろう。
English: The situation was emotionally distasteful, but it seemed more rational to stay and see how events unfolded.

Japanese: それに、ここにいたってまるきり無為というわけでもない。
English: Nor would staying here leave me entirely idle.

Japanese: あの不死身の虎のサンプルを手に入れた以上、ここにいても僕の個人的な活動を行うことが出来る。
English: Now that I had obtained a sample from the deathless tiger, I could pursue my private work even in this city.

Japanese: あの体組織がシャーレのなかでどれくらい生存出来るのかはわからないが、その調査や実験は有意義な暇つぶしとなるだろう。
English: I did not know how long the tissue would survive in a petri dish, but studying it and running experiments on it would give me a worthwhile way to pass the time.

Japanese: 単純に設備を考えたならば、大学に持ち帰って調べた方がよりよい実験が出来るのかもしれない。汐さんの地下室は個人のものとしては驚くほど充実しているが、やはり大学には叶わない。
English: In terms of equipment alone, I might have been able to perform better experiments by taking it back to the university. Mr. Shio’s basement was astonishingly well equipped for a private facility, but it could not rival the university.

Japanese: しかし、学校の施設を使うとなると、ある程度の説明がいる。サンプルをどうやって手に入れたなどという話になって、Ｙ地区について言及などされるのは、素性を隠して学生生活を送っている僕にとっては好ましくない事態だ。さらに、もしこのサンプルが重要なものだということになれば、研究は一学生である僕の手を離れて、他のもっと実績ある研究者にゆだねられてしまうかもしれない。そうなってしまってはまったく意味のないことだ。
English: Using the university’s facilities, however, would require a certain amount of explanation. Questions would arise about how I had acquired the sample, and any mention of Y District was undesirable while I was living as a student under a concealed identity. Furthermore, if the sample proved important, the research might be taken from my hands as a mere student and entrusted to some other researcher with a more distinguished record. That would render the entire business meaningless.

Japanese: この街でもある程度のことは出来るのだ。
English: There were still things I could do here in the city.

Japanese: 街の人間のどの程度が覚えているのかしらないが、汐さんは今でこそゴミ会社の社長だが、元々はグレートホール周辺の生態系を調査するために派遣されていた専門家であった。
English: I do not know how many residents still remember, but though Mr. Shio was now the president of a waste company, he had originally been dispatched as a specialist to study the ecosystem surrounding the Great Hole.

Japanese: Ｙ地区のゴミ処理状況の劣悪さに目を付けて事業で一発当てたが、今も本質的には研究者であることはかわらない。事業での膨大な利益を投資して自分のための研究室を用意し、研究に没頭している。そもそも、資金を調達しにくい研究を独力でおこなうためにゴミ会社を起こしたような人物である。
English: He had noticed the deplorable state of waste disposal in Y District and struck it rich in business, but in essence he remained a researcher. He invested his enormous profits in a laboratory of his own and immersed himself in research. Indeed, he was the sort of man who founded a waste company in order to finance research for which it would otherwise have been difficult to obtain funding.

Japanese: そして、何より彼はＹ地区の裏事情に精通している。
English: Above all, he possessed a thorough knowledge of Y District’s hidden affairs.

Japanese: もしあのサンプルが僕や汐さんの予想通り、このＹ地区の暗い部分と関係があるものだとしたら、大学のそうそうたる大先生達よりもよほど頼りになるのは間違いがない。
English: If that sample was connected, as Mr. Shio and I suspected, to the darker parts of Y District, then he would unquestionably prove far more dependable than the eminent professors at my university.

Japanese: もっとも、そういう効率的な部分を考慮しなかったとしても、単純に僕は汐さんと二人で何かを調べるという生活をもう一度やってみたかった。子供の頃はいつもそうしていて、色々なことを学んだ。学校へ行ってある程度知識が付いた今、また別の発見がありそうな気がする。この街には少年時代の僕の師となった大人は多いが、汐さんはそのなかでも最も影響のある人物なのだ。
English: Yet even apart from such considerations of efficiency, I simply wanted to spend my days investigating something with Mr. Shio again. We had always done so when I was a child, and I learned a great many things from him. Now that school had given me some measure of knowledge, I felt that I might make discoveries of another kind. Many adults in this city had served as mentors to me in boyhood, but Mr. Shio was the most influential of them all.

Japanese: 『君の家は、たしか自営業だとか言っていたな。どういう商売なんだ？』
English: “I believe you once said that your family ran a business. What sort of business is it?”

Japanese: 状況を簡単に説明すると、指導教官は厄介な好奇心を発揮して来た。
English: When I gave him a brief account of the situation, my adviser displayed his troublesome curiosity.

Japanese: 「ひとくちでは説明出来ませんが……色々なものを売ったり、仕事の仲介をしたり……」
English: “It is difficult to describe in a word... They sell various things, arrange work for people...”

Japanese: 『なんだ、結構大きな会社なのか？』
English: “What, is it a fairly large company?”

Japanese: 「地元ではそこそこ有名ですね」
English: “It is reasonably well known locally.”

Japanese: 『そりゃあ知らなかった。お坊ちゃんなんだなあ。道理で育ちが良さそうだと思ったよ。しかし、お父さんがそんな状態じゃ、息子である君に会社を継げという話もあるだろう』
English: “I had no idea. So you are a young master. I thought you seemed well bred. With your father in such a condition, though, there must also be talk of having you, his son, succeed him at the company.”

Japanese: 「まあ、なくはないです」
English: “There has been some.”

Japanese: 『お父さんも、継いでくれたらうれしかろう』
English: “Your father would be pleased if you agreed.”

Japanese: 「どうでしょうね。お前みたいな素人に任せられないって言われましたよ」
English: “I wonder. He told me that he could not leave it to an amateur like me.”

Japanese: 『そりゃあ、大学で生物なんかをやってる息子に、企業の経営者になれとは言えないだろう。お父さんなりのやさしさだよ』
English: “Naturally. He could hardly tell a son studying biology at university to become the head of a company. That is his way of showing kindness.”

Japanese: 「そうですかね」
English: “Is it?”

Japanese: 『そうに決まってる。それ以外にないだろ？　きみは非常に優秀だが、そういうところには案外鈍いんだなあ』
English: “Of course it is. What else could it be? You are remarkably gifted, but surprisingly obtuse in matters like this.”

Japanese: 指導教官に笑われてしまった。
English: My adviser laughed at me.

Japanese: 『実に立派なお父さんだ。でも、だからといって、情にほだされて会社を継ぐとか言い出して貰っても困るぞ』
English: “What an admirable father. Even so, I cannot have you yielding to sentiment and announcing that you intend to inherit the company.”

Japanese: 「そんなことは思いませんよ」
English: “I have no such intention.”

Japanese: 『とにかくきみには期待している。これからいろいろ大変だろうが、ちゃんと学校には戻ってきてくれよ。囲碁だって、このまま勝ち逃げされたらたまらん』
English: “In any case, I expect great things from you. I am sure the coming days will be difficult, but see that you return to school. I cannot tolerate your walking away with the lead in our Go matches.”

Japanese: 「その時は相手になりますよ。いくらやっても先生が勝ち越すことはないと思いますがね」
English: “When I get back, I’ll give you a game. However many we play, I doubt you’ll ever take the lead.”

Japanese: 電話を切った後、僕はやっと充実しはじめて来た学校での活動がここで中断されてしまうことを思い、溜息をついた。
English: After ending the call, I sighed at the thought that my work at school, just as it had begun to feel truly fulfilling, would now be interrupted.

Japanese: この街へ帰ってくると決めた時点では、このような成り行きは想像していなかった。
English: When I decided to return to this city, I had not imagined matters developing in this fashion.

Japanese: 父の症状が思いということは予測していたし、僕に後継者としての要請のようなものがあるのもわかってはいたが、僕はとにかく学校での研究が楽しくて楽しくて、用件だけ済ませたら、何が自分を引き留めてもとんぼ返りするだろうと思っていた。自分はそう選択すると考えていた。
English: I had anticipated that my father’s condition would be grave, and I understood that some demand would probably be made for me to succeed him. Yet I had been enjoying my research at school so immensely that I expected to settle my business and turn straight back, no matter what tried to detain me. I believed that was the choice I would make.

Japanese: しかしどういったことだろう？　僕は泥沼に足を踏み入れようとしている。
English: And yet, what was this? I was preparing to step into a quagmire.

Japanese: ことによっては、これによって僕の学生としての生活は終わりを告げてしまうかもしれない。
English: Depending on what followed, my life as a student might end here.

Japanese: 独力で学費を貯め、受験勉強をし、そうして手に入れた新生活。それは子供の頃から持っていた生命への興味を満たす大事な道のりの第一歩だ。
English: I had saved the tuition by my own efforts, studied for the entrance examinations, and won this new life. It was the first important step along the road toward satisfying the fascination with life that I had possessed since childhood.

Japanese: ずっと裏社会で暮らしていたから危惧はあったが、思ったよりも周囲の学生や教授達に受け入れられて、余計なことに気をさくことなく集中出来た。
English: My years in the underworld had caused me some concern, but the other students and professors accepted me more readily than I had expected, and I was able to concentrate without being distracted by anything else.

Japanese: 今まででも充分楽しかったが、この先もっと充実した世界が僕を待っているだろう。
English: It had already brought me ample pleasure, and a still richer world surely lay ahead.

Japanese: それをすべて棒に振ってしまうかもしれない。
English: I might be about to throw all of it away.

Japanese: ……まあ、いいか。
English: ...Well. Never mind.

Japanese: 楽しい日々を送るのも、そうでない日々を過ごすのも、さほど違いというものがあるわけでもなし。子供の頃からの夢が叶っても、叶わなくても、僕の心境が多少変わる程度であるし。
English: There was no very great difference between spending one’s days in happiness and spending them otherwise. Whether my childhood dream came true or did not, the only consequence would be some small change in my own state of mind.

Japanese: 結局人生というものは、ただ道を歩き続けるだけのものだと感じる。目的地も理由も知らぬまま歩き始め、泣いたり笑ったりしながら休まず見知らぬ道を歩き、終わりでも始まりでもないどこか乾いた場所で眠りにつくのだ。
English: In the end, life feels like nothing more than continuing to walk along a road. We begin without knowing the destination or the reason, and without rest we travel an unknown path, laughing and weeping, until we lie down to sleep in some dry place that is neither an end nor a beginning.

Japanese: 指導教官との電話の後、僕は汐さんに電話をかけた。
English: After the call with my adviser, I telephoned Mr. Shio.

Japanese: マウスが到着したら次の段階に進むことになっている。サンプルの新鮮さが重要なので、到着次第作業を行うことになっている。
English: We were to proceed to the next stage when the mice arrived. The freshness of the sample was important, so the work would begin as soon as they were delivered.

Japanese: そのあたりの状況を確認しようとしたのだが、電話は繋がらない。仕事に出ているのかもしれないし、電池が切れているのかもしれない。虎の出所について調べてくれるとも言ってくれた。それを行っているのかもしれない。
English: I meant to confirm the situation, but the call would not connect. He might have gone out on business, or his battery might have died. He had also agreed to investigate the tiger’s origin. Perhaps he was doing so now.

Japanese: メールで折り返しの連絡を催促する文章を送ると、当面僕のすることはなくなった。
English: I sent him a message requesting a return call, and for the moment had nothing more to do.

Japanese: そこで少し外に出て街でも見ようかと思ったところで、『あれ』の来る前兆があったのだ。
English: I was considering going outside to look around the city when I felt the warning that preceded the ‘thing.’

Japanese: 僕は外出を取りやめ、ソファーにもたれてじっとしていると、案の定『あれ』がやって来る。抗いようのない闇が僕の意識を覆い、強制切断させる。
English: I abandoned the outing and remained still against the sofa. As expected, the ‘thing’ arrived. An irresistible darkness engulfed my consciousness and severed it by force.

Japanese: ここ数ヶ月、僕は数日に一度くらいのペースで、どうしようもない睡魔に襲われて眠りに落ちてしまう。それは普通の眠りとは違って、揺すっても水をかけてもちっとも目を覚まさない、ほとんど昏睡と言って良いような深い深い眠りだった。
English: For the past several months, once every few days, I had been overcome by an irresistible sleepiness and fallen unconscious. This differed from ordinary sleep. Neither shaking nor dousing with water could wake me; it was so profoundly deep that one might almost call it a coma.

Japanese: 寝起きがやたらと悪いやつというのはよくいて、自分はかねがねそういう連中をなんて意志の弱いやつだと軽んじていたのだけれども、僕が悪かった。僕の方がひどいねぼすけになってしまった。
English: There are many people who are exceptionally difficult to wake, and I had always looked down upon them as weak-willed creatures. I was wrong. I had become a worse sleepyhead than any of them.

Japanese: 三十分から一時間で自然と目を覚ますから、時間にすれば長いとも言えないのだが、何しろその睡魔は突然やって来て、暴力的に僕の意識を落としてしまう。そして眠っている間は全くの無抵抗となってしまうわけで、なんというか、生き物としてはひどい欠陥だ。サバンナの野生動物ならばすぐに命を落としてしまうだろう。
English: I awakened naturally after thirty minutes or an hour, so the duration itself was not especially long. The sleepiness, however, arrived without warning and violently struck down my consciousness. While asleep, I was utterly defenseless. As defects in a living creature go, it was severe. A wild animal on the savanna would soon lose its life.

Japanese: サバンナの野生動物でなくて良かった。けれども、現代社会で暮らすホモサピエンスでも、これはこれで不便だ。
English: I was fortunate not to be a wild animal on the savanna. Even for a Homo sapiens living in modern society, however, the condition presented its inconveniences.

Japanese: 医者に言わせるとナルコレプシーでもないらしい。かといって原因もわからない。どんな検査をしても何の異常も見つからないのだ。医者の診断ははっきりしない。心因性かもしれないが、そうでもないような気もする。……何しろ、タイプAとかいう以上能力者がやたらと増えてしまったおかげで医学の定説は崩壊してしまったようなものだから、医者もわけがわからなくなっている。
English: According to the physician, it did not appear to be narcolepsy. The cause, however, was unknown. No examination revealed the least abnormality, and the diagnosis remained inconclusive. It might be psychogenic, though I felt that it might not. ...With the extraordinary proliferation of people with paranormal powers called Type As, the accepted principles of medicine had all but collapsed. The physicians themselves no longer understood what they were seeing.

Japanese: 世の中はあまりにも退屈で、眠くて眠くて仕方がないと、僕の意識の奥底ではそんな考えがあるのだろうか？
English: Was there some thought in the depths of my consciousness that the world was unbearably dull, and that I could do nothing but sleep?

Japanese: 意識の表面では思ったことさえないのだが。むしろ、飽きもせず変化をする、奥深く底知れない、とても素晴らしい世界だと、いつも感じている。
English: No such idea had ever crossed the surface of my mind. On the contrary, I had always found the world magnificent: changing without end, profound and unfathomable, and never once tedious.

Japanese: そして僕は眠りにつき、目が覚めるまで現実だと信じて疑わないような、やけにリアルな夢を見た。
English: Then I slept, and dreamed with such extraordinary realism that until I awoke, I never doubted the dream was reality.

Japanese: はっと目が覚めて時計をみると一時間と十分が過ぎていた。目が覚めると、いつも体がひどく重いが、眠気が残っていてまた眠りたくなるというようなことはない。その辺りも普通の睡眠とは違う。
English: I awoke with a start and looked at the clock. An hour and ten minutes had passed. My body was always terribly heavy upon waking, but no drowsiness remained to make me wish to sleep again. In that respect as well, it differed from ordinary sleep.

Japanese: ともあれ、僕はこれによってすっかり外出する意欲がなくなり、論文を読みあさっていると日が暮れた。
English: In any case, the episode entirely extinguished my desire to go out. I devoured academic papers until night fell.

Japanese: 僕は馬明が手配してくれたこのホテルは街の一等地にある小綺麗なホテルで、Ｙ地区特有のトラブルに巻き込まれたくないビジネスマンや観光客がよく利用するらしい。
English: The hotel Ma Ming had arranged for me was a tidy establishment in one of the finest parts of the city. It was apparently popular with business travelers and tourists who wished to avoid the troubles peculiar to Y District.

Japanese: 店員はみなノーマルで、日本語の他に、英語と北京語が通用すると公式にうたっている。料理は中華、フレンチ、和食から選べ、アレルギーや宗教上の禁忌にも対応してくれるそうだ。
English: Every member of the staff was a Normal, and the hotel officially advertised service in English and Mandarin as well as Japanese. Guests could choose Chinese, French, or Japanese cuisine, and the kitchen would reportedly accommodate allergies and religious prohibitions.

Japanese: 部屋は狭めだが、家具や内装は悪くはない。
English: The room was rather small, but the furniture and decor were not bad.

Japanese: 僕の部屋は最上階の一つ下で、窓からはＹ地区の夜景が見える。
English: My room was one floor below the top, and its window offered a nighttime view of Y District.

Japanese: ネット環境も完備されており、無線の高速回線がいつでも利用出来る。……もっとも、Ｙ地区はネット回線のインフラ設備だけは異様に整っていて、違法回線ながらどんな裏路地からでもそのような高速回線が利用出来るのだが。僕もこの子供の頃はよくお世話になったものだ。
English: The hotel also provided full internet access, with a high-speed wireless connection available at all times. ...Then again, Y District was unusually well equipped in that one area of infrastructure. Illegal though the lines were, the same high speeds were available from nearly every back alley. I had often availed myself of them as a child.

Japanese: 今日は発作のせいで結局このホテルから一歩も外に出なかったが、夕食はせめて外に出よう。そして、昨日泣かしてしまって、今も落ち込んでいるに違いない妹のためになにかプレゼントでも探してやろう。
English: The episode had kept me from taking a single step outside the hotel that day, but I would at least go out for dinner. I could also look for a present for my sister, whom I had reduced to tears the day before and who must still be disheartened.

Japanese: 外出の準備をしていたところで、またもや僕の行動を妨げるように、馬明からの電話があった。
English: I was preparing to leave when another telephone call from Ma Ming arrived to obstruct my plans.

Japanese: 『今日これから出られないか？　ちょっと会食に出て欲しいんだ』
English: “Can you come out now? I would like you to attend a dinner.”

Japanese: 今からグランドタワーでYS幹部による会議を兼ねた定例会食が行われるらしい。彼は僕にそれを見学しろと言っている。
English: A regular dinner meeting of the YS officers, which would also serve as a council, was apparently about to begin at the Grand Tower. He wanted me to observe it.

Japanese: その重い口調からすると、どうも気軽に参加してみたらというような安易なものではなく、何か切実な理由があるように察せられた。
English: From the gravity of his voice, I gathered that this was no casual invitation to come and see what it was like. He appeared to have some urgent reason.

Japanese: 「別にいいけれど、どうして？」
English: “I do not mind. But why?”

Japanese: ちょうど暇を持てあましているところだし、単純に興味もあった。
English: I had been struggling to fill my empty time, and the prospect itself interested me.

Japanese: 死期が近い龍頭に対して、有力者たちはどのように振る舞っているのか。その様子を観察するのは今後の僕や妹の運命を占う上での重要な参考情報となる。
English: How were the powerful men behaving toward a Longtou whose death was near? Observing them would furnish important information with which to judge the future awaiting my sister and me.

Japanese: 彼の雰囲気からすると、差し迫った何かがその会議にはあるようで、そのことも気になった。
English: His manner also suggested that something was imminent at this council, and I found myself curious about that as well.

Japanese: 『まあ、来ればわかる』
English: “Come, and you will understand.”

Japanese: 僕はそれを了承した。
English: I agreed.

Japanese: 会食の開始まであまり時間がないということで、馬明に車を差し向けてもらうのではなく、ホテルの前でタクシーを拾った。
English: There was little time before the dinner began, so rather than have Ma Ming send a car, I hailed a taxi in front of the hotel.

Japanese: 乗り込んで行き先をグランドタワーと言うと、それまで陽気に軽口などを叩いていたタクシー運転手がそれ以降ぎこちない表情と口調で対応するようになり、僕は複雑な気分になってしまう。
English: I climbed inside and gave the Grand Tower as my destination. The driver, who until then had made cheerful small talk, grew stiff in both expression and tone. The change left me with complicated feelings.

Japanese: 会食はグランドタワーの中層にある会食室で行われる。そこは文字通り来客などを食事でもてなすための部屋だが、父は重要な会談も食事や酒を楽しみながら行うことを好むため、実際には会議室や応接室と似たような使われ方をしているのだと馬明が説明する。
English: The dinner would be held in a dining chamber on one of the Grand Tower’s middle floors. The room existed, as its name suggested, to entertain guests over meals. My father, however, preferred to conduct important discussions while enjoying food and drink, so in practice it was used much like a conference room or reception chamber—or so Ma Ming explained.

Japanese: そうした使われ方にふさわしい高級感のある内装なのだが、ビル全体の内装が言えば近代風のデザインで統e一されているのに比べ、この部屋は赤や金をふんだんにもちいた中華風の意匠が施されていた。まあ一言で言えば、香港映画に出て来る富豪キャラの家に似ている。父の趣味が反映された結果かもしれない。
English: The furnishings possessed an elegance suited to that purpose. Yet whereas the building as a whole was unified by a modern design, this room was decorated in a Chinese style that made lavish use of red and gold. To put it simply, it resembled the home of a wealthy character in a Hong Kong film. Perhaps it reflected my father’s taste.

Japanese: まだ誰も来ていなかった。テーブルにはナプキンや食器が一人ごとに並べられている。
English: No one else had arrived. Napkins and tableware had been arranged around the table, one setting for each person.

Japanese: 僕はそうした会食の席に着かず、壁際に置いてあった、おそらく予備のものと思われる椅子に腰掛けた。
English: Rather than take one of those places, I sat in a chair against the wall that appeared to be a spare.

Japanese: 「どうしてそんな場所に座るんだよ」
English: “Why are you sitting there?”

Japanese: 馬明が怪訝そうに顔を顰めたが、
English: Ma Ming frowned in puzzlement.

Japanese: 「僕はここでいいんだよ」
English: “I’m fine here.”

Japanese: と一言返しただけで理由は口にしなかった。
English: I gave no reason beyond that brief reply.

Japanese: 龍頭の息子である僕が、これまでYSの仕事を何もしていないにもかかわらず、父の死期が近づいてから急にこんな会議に出席するとなれば憶測を生むだろう。
English: I was the Longtou’s son, yet I had never performed the least work for YS. If I suddenly attended such a council just as my father neared death, it would invite speculation.

Japanese: 僕は少しでも参加者達を刺激しないよう、会議の参加者と同格の立場でここにいるのではなく、あくまでも傍観するつもりでここに来ているのだという意志表示のつもりでこの椅子のポジションを選んだ。もっとも、今この場に僕が現れたというだけで刺激になっていまうのは避けられないわけで、ちょっと居場所を変えたくらいでどれだけその意図が伝わるのかはわからないが、まあ気持ち的なものだ。
English: I chose that chair to signal that I had come solely to observe, not to stand as an equal among the council’s participants. I wished to provoke them as little as possible. Of course, my mere appearance here now would inevitably be provocative. I had no idea how much of my intention could be conveyed by changing my seat, but the gesture gave me some peace of mind.

Japanese: 開始の時間が近づくと、参加者達が続々と集まってくる。
English: As the appointed hour approached, the participants arrived one after another.

Japanese: まずジョゼ・フェルナンデス。
English: First came José Fernandes.

Japanese: アウロラをはじめとする美人三姉妹の父だが、娘達の年齢のわりには随分と年を取っており、褐色の肌には樹皮のようなしわがきざまれ、髪の毛のほとんどは白くなっている。
English: He was the father of the three beautiful sisters, Aurora and the others, but was remarkably old in comparison with his daughters. Wrinkles like tree bark scored his brown skin, and his hair had gone almost entirely white.

Japanese: 彼はブラジル移民たちを一手に引き受けるリーダーだ。この街のブラジル移民はそれなりに規模の大きい集団だが、割合的に長期定住者はさほどではない。一時的に本国からのY地区にやって来て、ある程度稼いだら帰ってゆくような若者が多い。そういう人々に、この地での仕事を紹介するのが彼がこの街で昔から行っている役割である。
English: He was the sole leader of the Brazilian immigrant community. The Brazilians in this city formed a group of considerable size, but relatively few were long-term residents. Many were young people who came temporarily from their own country to Y District, earned a certain amount, and then returned home. Fernandes’s traditional role in the city was to help such people find work here.

Japanese: 滑走路通りやその北側の地域で飲食店、クリーニング店などを多数経営しており、わずかに売春の斡旋や武器の売買を行っているが、それ以外はいわゆる非合法的な活動はほとんど行っていない。彼のグループは元々同国人の互助会的なものであったが、今もその方針がそのまま継続している。YSのなかでおよそもっともギャングらしくない一派である。
English: He operated numerous restaurants, cleaners, and other businesses on Runway Street and to its north. He did a little business brokering prostitution and dealing weapons, but otherwise carried out almost none of what might be called illegal activity. His group had originated as a mutual-aid association for his countrymen, and it maintained that policy even now. It was probably the least ganglike faction in YS.

Japanese: ほぼ同国人だけでまとまっているために結束が強く、個人の気性も荒いものが多いが、他のグループとの対立は少ない。
English: Composed almost entirely of his fellow countrymen, it possessed strong internal solidarity, and many of its individual members had violent dispositions. It seldom came into conflict with other groups, however.

Japanese: 龍頭であるクリス・ツェーが頭角をあらわすよりも古くからY地区の顔役の一人であり、温厚で誠実な人柄から、同国人以外からも尊敬をあつめる存在だ。
English: He had been one of the prominent figures in Y District since before Chris Tse rose to power. His mild and sincere character won him respect even among people who were not his countrymen.

Japanese: 僕も昔から知っているが親しいというわけでもなく、さほど会話をしたことがない。
English: I had known him for many years, but we were not close and had spoken very little.

Japanese: 普段はいつもTシャツに動きやすそうなズボンをあわせたラフな格好だが、こうした場では清潔なスーツを身につけて来るようだ。年齢と経験に裏打ちされた重厚な雰囲気があり、こうして正装をしているといかにも黒社会の重鎮という風格がある。
English: He ordinarily dressed casually in a T-shirt and trousers that looked easy to move in, but for an occasion like this, he apparently wore a neat suit. He possessed the gravity born of age and experience, and in formal dress looked every inch an elder statesman of the underworld.

Japanese: 「珍しい人間がいるな」
English: “Here is an unusual face.”

Japanese: 部下も連れずに会場に単身であらわれた彼は、僕の方を見てそう言った。
English: He had come to the room alone, without a subordinate. Looking toward me, he said this.

Japanese: 「社会見学をしに来ました」
English: “I’m here on a field trip.”

Japanese: 僕が口にした言葉には特になんの反応も見せず、中央の席につくと、溜息をついた。
English: He showed no particular reaction to my answer. He took a seat near the center and sighed.

Japanese: 次にあらわれたのは、髪の毛を長く伸ばした色白の男である。目が血走って、唇が赤い。この人物はおそらく壬生屋タカシだろう。
English: The next arrival was a pale man who wore his hair long. His eyes were bloodshot and his lips red. This was probably Takashi Mibuya.

Japanese: 暗闇通りをはじめとする、裏路地……最近は『裏Y地区』などという言い方もされるらしい地域で、売春宿の総元締めをやっている、いわばY地区の売春王として知られる人物である。いや、正確には父が有名な売春王で、数年前にそれが死んで後を継いでから、その異名も継ぐようになった。
English: He was known as the prostitution king of Y District, the man who controlled the brothels of Darkness Street and the other back alleys—an area now apparently called ‘Back Y District.’ More precisely, his father had been the famous prostitution king. When his father died several years ago and Takashi succeeded him, the sobriquet passed down as well.

Japanese: 僕は直接的にはよく知らないが、その名前や噂はよく知っている。Y地区に住むもので壬生屋家のことを知らないものはいないだろう。その財力を隠そうともせずに一族そろって派手な暮らしぶりを送っている様はあまりも目立つし、貧しくて娘や妻を売らなくてはならないような家庭では否応なくつき合いを持つことになる。僕の少年時代でも、この壬生屋家を憎む子供が何人かいた。
English: I did not know him personally, but I knew his name and the rumors surrounding him. No resident of Y District could have been ignorant of the Mibuya family. The entire clan flaunted its wealth in so gaudy a manner that they were impossible to overlook, and any family poor enough to be forced into selling a wife or daughter inevitably had dealings with them. Even in my boyhood, I knew several children who hated the Mibuyas.

Japanese: 本来はYSとはかかわりなく活動を行っていたが、代替わりしてこのタカシが元締めになってからYSに加入した。
English: They had originally operated without any connection to YS. After the succession placed Takashi at their head, however, they joined the organization.

Japanese: 二人の女を連れている。女は二人とも厚化粧をして、じゃらじゃらと装飾品を身につけていた。はっきりいって下品である。
English: He had brought two women with him. Both wore heavy makeup and enough jewelry to clatter as they moved. To speak plainly, they were vulgar.

Japanese: どちらかが妻で、どちらかが愛人なのだろうか。二人とも愛人なのだろうか。彼女たちはこの場で同席は出来ないので、壬生屋が椅子にかけると愛想笑いをしながら部屋を出て行った。
English: Was one his wife and the other his mistress? Were both his mistresses? They could not accompany him at the table, and when Mibuya took his seat, they left the room wearing ingratiating smiles.

Japanese: それから後は次々と参加者が入って来る。
English: After that, the remaining participants entered in rapid succession.

Japanese: パラシュート通りに香港系の勢力を持つ、クリス・ツェーの父方の親戚に当たるマイケル・ツェー。
English: Michael Tse, a relative on Chris Tse’s paternal side, commanded a Hong Kong faction on Parachute Street.

Japanese: 口元だけが覗いて顔の上半分を隠す仮面をしているのは、血の気の多い荒くれ者を部下として多数抱える武闘派グループのボスにして、タイプAである異形の劉建志。
English: The man in a mask that concealed the upper half of his face, leaving only his mouth visible, was Ryu Kenshi: a misshapen Type A and the boss of a militant faction with many hot-blooded ruffians under his command.

Japanese: カジノを多数経営する、太っちょのイタリア人ダリオ・ボネットはいつも気の弱そうな態度をしているが、かつては暗殺や誘拐事件に多く関わった陰謀家である。
English: The fat Italian Dario Bonetto operated numerous casinos. He always appeared timid, but was a conspirator who had once been involved in many assassinations and kidnappings.

Japanese: 武器商人上がりの国籍不明の女、エリー・ホワイト。名前とは裏腹にいつも真っ黒な喪服を身につけている。
English: Ellie White was a former arms dealer of uncertain nationality. Despite her name, she always dressed in black mourning clothes.

Japanese: そして最後に部屋に入ってきたのが、廖志明（リャオ・チミン）であった。彼は息子の、トーマス・リャオを伴っている。
English: The last person to enter the room was Liao Chi-ming. He was accompanied by his son, Thomas Liao.

Japanese: 廖は僕の姿を見ても一瞥して通り過ぎただけだったが、息子のトーマスは、
English: Liao merely glanced at me and walked past, but his son Thomas said,

Japanese: 「あ、小謝？　どうしてここにいるの？」
English: “Ah, Siu Tse? Why are you here?”

Japanese: この場に緊張しているのか、びくついた様子で話しかけて来た。
English: He addressed me timidly, perhaps unnerved by the gathering.

Japanese: 彼は僕と同い年で、通称トミーと呼ばれている。廖志明は何度も結婚し、しかもそのすべてがブロンドの美女であるという実にわかりやすい性癖を持っているのだが、トミーはその最初の妻であるアメリカ人に生ませた長男だ。
English: He was my age and commonly called Tommy. Liao Chi-ming had married several times, and every one of his wives had been a beautiful blonde—a preference remarkable for its simplicity. Tommy was his eldest son, born to his first wife, an American.

Japanese: 「トミーこそ、いつこっちに帰って来たんだ？」
English: “When did you get back here, Tommy?”

Japanese: 幼い頃こそこちらにいたものの、数年前に母が故郷に戻る時に行動を共にし、アメリカで暮らしていたはずだ。
English: He had lived here in early childhood, but several years ago, he had accompanied his mother when she returned home and was supposed to have been living in America.

Japanese: 「もう、２年くらいこっちにいるよ……。急に呼び戻されたんだ。母さんといっしょに。父さんと再婚したんだよ。……あいかわらず、愛人はたくさんいるみたいだけど、今回は母さんも納得済みなんだ」
English: “I’ve been back here for about two years... He called us back without warning—Mother and me. They remarried. ...He still seems to have plenty of mistresses, but this time Mother agreed to it.”

Japanese: トミーは困ったような笑みを浮かべる。
English: Tommy gave an embarrassed smile.

Japanese: 少しふっくらした体型のトーマスは、母親譲りの色素の薄い髪と瞳を持ち、笑うと愛嬌のある顔立ちになる。
English: Thomas was somewhat plump, with the light-colored hair and eyes he had inherited from his mother. When he smiled, his face had an amiable charm.

Japanese: おっとりとした性格で、ギャングの息子というよりも、母親と共にアメリカの片田舎で生活をしていたほうが幸福な人生だと思うが、そうはいかなかったらしい。彼自身もこの環境に慣れないようで、幹部達の集まるこの場の雰囲気に完全に圧倒されているようだった。
English: With his gentle disposition, I thought he would have lived a happier life with his mother in some quiet corner of America than as the son of a gangster. Apparently, that was not to be. He himself did not seem accustomed to this environment and appeared thoroughly overwhelmed by the atmosphere of a room filled with officers.

Japanese: 「しっかりしなくちゃいけないとわかってるんだけど、どうも気圧されちゃって。……僕、ずっとここにいるのかな？」
English: “I know I need to pull myself together, but the people here rather intimidate me. ...Am I going to stay here forever?”

Japanese: 「おいトーマス」
English: “Thomas.”

Japanese: トミーは、この中で最も年齢が近く、知り合いである僕の側にもう少し居たいようだったが、父に呼ばれると渋々その隣の席についた。
English: Tommy appeared to wish he could remain a little longer beside me, the person closest to him in age and an old acquaintance. When his father called, however, he reluctantly took the adjoining seat.

Japanese: 廖は我が息子に、しかめっ面で何か言っている。おおよそ、僕とあまり関わるなとか、そういった話であろう。
English: Liao frowned as he said something to his son. Presumably, he was warning him not to associate too closely with me, or something of that sort.

Japanese: その、廖志明。
English: Liao Chi-ming himself was another matter.

Japanese: やせぎすの体を包むのはラメの入った銀色のスーツで、ディナーショーでの演歌歌手のような、どこか亜熱帯の密林にでも住んでいそうな蛇のような、なんとも言えないファッションセンスである。口ひげとあごひげの形も、あまり現代風とは言えない。肝臓を悪くしているかのように肌が黒く、黒目の小さい三白眼で、まあ魅力的と呼ぶにはほど遠い容貌であるが、YSのなかでは最も力のある権力者である。
English: His lean body was wrapped in a glittering silver suit. The ensemble suggested both an enka singer at a dinner show and a snake dwelling in some subtropical jungle; his taste in fashion defied simple description. The shapes of his mustache and goatee could hardly be called contemporary. His skin was as dark as though his liver were failing, and his sanpaku eyes had tiny black pupils. In short, his appearance was very far from attractive. Nevertheless, he was the most powerful man in YS.

Japanese: Y地区に住む様々な集団のなかで、おそらくもっとも経済力があるのは客家系の華僑たちだろう。彼らは人が集まり始めたY地区が現在のような一大歓楽街に成長するのに重要な役割を果たし、Y地区の地名などに中国由来のものが多いのは彼らの影響による。
English: Of the various communities living in Y District, the Hakka overseas Chinese probably possessed the greatest economic power. They had played a vital role in transforming the district, when people first began to gather here, into the great entertainment quarter it was now. Their influence accounted for the many Chinese-derived place names in Y District.

Japanese: YSが発足するまではこの地域の最大勢力であった。現在はクリス・ツェーの香港グループが中心的な存在になったとはいえ、その経済力は圧倒的だ。
English: Before the founding of YS, they had been the region’s largest power. Chris Tse’s Hong Kong group might now occupy the central position, but the Hakka economic strength remained overwhelming.

Japanese: この集団のリーダーが廖志明なのだ。
English: Liao Chi-ming led that community.

Japanese: 父から財産と地位を受け継いだ二代目であるが、ありがちなぼんくらという訳でもなく、特に商売に関しては抜け目ないと評判だ。
English: He was a second-generation heir who had inherited wealth and position from his father, but he was no stereotypical fool. He had a particular reputation for shrewdness in business.

Japanese: Y地区黎明期の頃から続く一大勢力を築いた一族の御曹司ということで、ギャングの家柄という言葉を使うことが許されるのならば、YSでは最も格のあるファミリーである。同じく旧世代かの有力組織であるフェルナンデスファミリーとはあまり仲が良くないが、お互いの影響力を考慮して表面上ではほとんど争いごとは起こさない。お互い不干渉を貫いている。
English: He was the scion of the house that had built one of the great powers of Y District, a force reaching back to the district’s earliest days. If one may speak of pedigree among gangsters, his family had the highest in YS. Relations with the Fernandes Family, another great organization of the old generation, were poor. In recognition of each other’s influence, however, they almost never entered into open conflict. Each maintained a policy of noninterference.

Japanese: 人格に関してはほとんどいい噂を聞かない。倨傲で、人を露骨に見下し、欲しいものを得るためには手段を選ばない。何より金と女に汚く、その種のトラブルには事欠かない。財力と暴力の使い方をよく知っており、自分より立場の弱い者から搾取するのが上手い。
English: One heard almost no favorable rumor about his character. He was arrogant, openly contemptuous of others, and indiscriminate in the means he used to obtain what he desired. Above all, he was corrupt where money and women were concerned, and trouble of that kind followed him without end. He understood how to wield wealth and violence and excelled at exploiting those weaker than himself.

Japanese: と書くと良いところが全くないようだが、部下や身内に対しては寛容で、むしろ非常に甘く、仲間からの信頼は厚い。
English: Written that way, he appears to possess no virtues at all. Yet toward his subordinates and relatives he was tolerant—indeed, excessively indulgent—and enjoyed their profound trust.

Japanese: 親から巨大な地位を受け継いだという背景や、品のない発言や人並み外れた好色のせいで、彼個人に対する世間での評価は低いようだが、僕はリーダーとしてはYSの幹部達のなかでも優秀な方だと、かねてから思っている。
English: His inherited stature, vulgar remarks, and extraordinary lechery seemed to have earned him a poor public reputation as an individual. I had long thought, however, that as a leader he ranked among the most capable officers of YS.

Japanese: ちっとも好きではないけれど。いやむしろきらいだけれど。
English: I did not like him in the least. In fact, I disliked him.

Japanese: とまれ、この廖こそが、カリスマ的リーダーであるクリス・ツェー亡き後のYSの運命を握っているはずだ。
English: In any event, this Liao was surely the man who held the fate of YS after the death of its charismatic leader, Chris Tse.

Japanese: 元々年下で、なおかつファミリーの格としても下である僕の父に対して、どこか軽んじているフシがある。昔からYSを離脱するのではないかという噂は何度も囁かれ、本人は明確にそれを否定したことがない。野心もあり、Y地区、及び近隣地域でも様々な事業を展開している。街を離れてあちこちを飛び回り、様々な人々との交流も持っているようだ。
English: He had always shown signs of looking down upon my father, who was younger than he and whose Family was of lower pedigree. Rumors that he would secede from YS had circulated many times over the years, and he had never clearly denied them. Nor did he lack ambition. He pursued businesses throughout Y District and the neighboring regions, traveled constantly beyond the city, and appeared to maintain relations with a wide variety of people.

Japanese: 僕は最近この街を離れてしまっていたので、現在の状況を詳しくは知らないが、この廖がクリス・ツェーの次の龍頭の座を狙っているのか、それともYSを抜けて独自のやり方で地域を支配しようと考えているのか、どちらの目的を持っているかというのが今後の状況において非常に重要になってくるのではないだろうか。
English: I had recently lived away from the city and did not know its present circumstances in detail. Even so, the future would depend greatly, I thought, on which course Liao intended to pursue: whether he sought Chris Tse’s seat as the next Longtou, or meant to leave YS and dominate the region by his own methods.

Japanese: 参加者が全員揃うと、ジェフリー・ウォンに伴われて車椅子の父が入って来る。
English: Once every participant had arrived, my father entered in a wheelchair attended by Jeffrey Wong.

Japanese: 「みな勢揃いで、ご苦労」
English: “Thank you all for assembling.”

Japanese: 龍頭であるクリス・ツェーは不敵な笑みを浮かべていった。
English: The Longtou, Chris Tse, spoke with a fearless smile.

Japanese: 僕も、いつまでも壁際の席に一人で座っているわけにもいかなかったので、テーブルの端の方の席に馬明と隣り合って座った。
English: I could not remain alone forever in my chair against the wall, so I took a place at one end of the table beside Ma Ming.

Japanese: それぞれの手元のグラスに、給仕の女達によってシャンパンが注がれる。そして皆に行き渡った。
English: The female attendants poured champagne into the glass before each person. When all had been served,

Japanese: 龍頭がグラスを掲げ、しゃがれてはいるが、瀕死の病人とも思えぬ朗々たる声で言う。
English: the Longtou raised his glass and spoke in a voice that, though hoarse, rang out with a fullness impossible to associate with a dying man.

Japanese: 「我々YSの、さらなる発展と、永久に続く固い結束に捧げる」
English: “To the further advancement of YS, and to the firm bonds that shall unite us forever.”

Japanese: そしてグラスに口をつけ、飲み干してテーブルに置く。
English: Then he put the glass to his lips, emptied it, and returned it to the table.

Japanese: すると、すべての参加者は同じようにグラスを掲げ、飲み干し、そしてテーブルに置く。
English: Every participant followed suit: raising a glass, draining it, and setting it down.

Japanese: どうしてなのか、何が起源なのか、よく分からないが、「乾杯」などのかけ声をかけず、こうした流れをすべて無言のうちに行うのがYS流の作法らしい。
English: I did not know why, or where the custom originated, but apparently the YS fashion was to complete this entire sequence in silence, without anyone calling out a toast such as ‘Cheers.’

Japanese: そして、会食が始まる。
English: The dinner began.

Japanese: 隣の席になった者や、連れ合いと雑談を始めるものも居れば、ただ黙々と食事を食べる者もいる。何か大事な話をするという雰囲気ではなく、ごく当たり前の会食にしか見えないが、これがどういう流れで幹部同士の話し合いになるのか。初参加の僕はちっとも勝手がわからない。
English: Some exchanged small talk with their neighbors or companions, while others ate steadily in silence. Nothing in the atmosphere suggested that an important discussion would occur. It looked like an entirely ordinary dinner, and as a first-time participant, I had no idea how it was meant to develop into a council among the officers.

Japanese: 「ねえ馬明。これは、ただ食べるだけなのかい？」
English: “Ma Ming, are we simply going to eat?”

Japanese: 僕は小声で隣の馬明に尋ねた。
English: I asked the question quietly of the man beside me.

Japanese: 「食事の間は雑談などをしてお互いの気持をほぐし、食後のお茶の時間に大事な会議を行うというのが、いつもの流れだな」
English: “The usual procedure is to relax everyone with small talk during the meal, then conduct the important council over tea afterward.”

Japanese: 言いながら彼はオードブルの牡蠣のコンフィをもう一皿注文した。
English: As he spoke, he ordered another plate of the oyster confit served as an hors d’oeuvre.

Japanese: コース料理でオードブルを追加注文するやつなんかいるのだろうかと思いながら、僕も自分の皿に手を付ける。今日はフレンチのようだ。
English: I wondered whether anyone else in the world ordered an additional appetizer in the middle of a set course, then began on my own plate. Today’s cuisine appeared to be French.

Japanese: 料理が一皿一皿運ばれて来る。食事で気持をほぐしながら、と言ったけれども、そんな雰囲気でもない。あちこちでひそひそと囁くような話し合いがなされてはいるが、食器のカチャカチャとなる音の方が大きいくらいだ。
English: The dishes arrived one after another. Ma Ming had spoken of relaxing over the meal, but the atmosphere scarcely deserved the word. Quiet, whispered discussions were taking place here and there, yet even the clatter of cutlery was louder.

Japanese: 龍頭は食事に手を付けず、左右に座ったエリー・ホワイトやマイケル・ツェーと談笑をしている。もう経口での食事に耐えられる体ではないのかもしれない。
English: The Longtou did not touch his food. He sat conversing pleasantly with Ellie White and Michael Tse on either side. Perhaps his body could no longer tolerate taking food by mouth.

Japanese: 売春王の壬生屋は、ふとっちょイタリア人のダリオと、真顔で囁き合っている。同じ暗闇通りを根城とするこの二人は、以前は何かとやりあっていたはずだが、僕の知らないうちに和解したのだろうか。
English: Mibuya, the prostitution king, was whispering with a grave expression to the fat Italian Dario. The two men, both based on Darkness Street, had once clashed at every opportunity. Had they reconciled without my knowledge?

Japanese: フェルナンデスや、劉建志は誰とも喋らずに黙々と食べている。
English: Fernandes and Ryu Kenshi spoke to no one and ate steadily in silence.

Japanese: 廖は料理にほとんど手を付けずに、ニヤニヤとトミーに囁き、トミーは眉間にしわを浮かべながらそれを聞き、ただ頷くばかりだ。
English: Liao scarcely touched his food. He whispered to Tommy with a grin while Tommy listened with a furrowed brow and did nothing but nod.

Japanese: 一通りのコースが終わり、それぞれに紅茶やら珈琲やら、リクエストした飲み物が運ばれてくる。
English: When the entire course had ended, tea, coffee, and the other requested drinks were brought to each guest.

Japanese: 「さて」
English: “Now, then.”

Japanese: 龍頭がそう言って居住まいを正すと、その場の空気が張り詰めたものに変わった。
English: The Longtou straightened himself as he spoke, and the atmosphere in the room turned taut.

Japanese: 「今日は大事な話がいくつかある」
English: “We have several important matters to discuss today.”

Japanese: 「その前に、いいかな？」
English: “Before that, may I?”

Japanese: 廖がうすら笑いを浮かべながら言う。
English: Liao spoke with a thin smile.

Japanese: 「なんだ」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「龍頭、それからみなさんに、一つ提案がある」
English: “Longtou—and all of you—I have a proposal.”

Japanese: 廖は立ち上がって一同を見回すと、
English: Liao rose and surveyed the room.

Japanese: 「私が今日提案したいのは、薬の売買の件だ」
English: “My proposal today concerns the drug trade.”

Japanese: 「またその話か」
English: “That again?”

Japanese: 龍頭は露骨に顔を顰める。
English: The Longtou frowned openly.

Japanese: 「うんざりさせて申し訳ないが、またさせて貰う。今状況は非常に深刻なのだ。どうなっているのか、それを知って貰いたい」
English: “I apologize for wearying you, but I shall raise it again. The present situation is extremely serious. I want all of you to understand what is happening.”

Japanese: 廖は咳払いをして、
English: Liao cleared his throat.

Japanese: 「知っての通り、我々YSは薬物の取引を行っておらず、Y地区での薬物利権は　”老人達”　が独り占めしている。これはあまりにも馬鹿げているし、非常に問題のある状態だとは思わないか？　何故彼らに利益を独占させている？　利益だけでなく、街の秩序の上でもよろしくない。老人達では外部からの圧力を防ぐことが出来ないんだよ。先週、老人達から要請されて、無許可の売人を二人始末したろう？　なぜ我々が彼らの走狗のようになって、汚れ仕事を引き受けなければならない？」
English: “As you know, YS does not deal in drugs, and the ‘Elders’ possess a monopoly on the drug interests of Y District. Do you not find this state of affairs both absurd and deeply problematic?
