English: In the end, Tachikawa said nothing about it.

Japanese: 「ここが、今夜の診察所です」
English: “This is tonight’s examination room.”

Japanese: ステッキを上げて、背後の児童施設を美紗に示した。
English: He lifted his cane and indicated the children’s home behind him.

Japanese: 「ここは捨て子が多い街です。ノーマルもタイプAも居ますが、一番多いのはタイプBですね。この街で生まれた子供だけでなく、よその地域からも捨てに来ているらしいです。何しろ、Y地区はミュータントが多いことで知られていますからね。この街に捨てれば、仲間が多くて幸せに暮らせると考えるのかもしれません」
English: “Many children are abandoned in this city. Some are Normal, some Type A, but Type Bs are the largest group. Apparently, people bring children here from other regions as well as abandoning those born in the city. Y District is known for its large mutant population. Perhaps the parents imagine that if they leave a child here, the child will have many companions and live happily.”

Japanese: 鞄の中から診察道具を取り出し、施設職員の用意してくれた机の上に並べながら太刀川は説明する。
English: Tachikawa explained while removing his instruments from the bag and arranging them on a desk the facility’s staff had prepared.

Japanese: 「あ、手伝います！」
English: “Oh, let me help!”

Japanese: ぼんやり立ったまま話に耳を傾けていた美紗は、我に返ってそう申し出たが、太刀川は首を横に振る。
English: Misa had been standing idly and listening. Coming to herself, she made the offer, but Tachikawa shook his head.

Japanese: 「今日は見学してくれればよいのです。こうした場所の患者達を見るのも仕事の役に立つかもしれません」
English: “Today, you need only observe. Seeing patients who live in places like this may be useful in your work.”

Japanese: 一通り道具を並べ終えると、最後にカルテのファイルを取り出し、美紗に手渡した。
English: Once he had arranged all the instruments, he removed a file of medical charts and handed it to Misa.

Japanese: 「子供が入って来たら名前を言うのでその子のカルテを渡してください。あなたの今日の仕事はそれだけです」
English: “When a child enters, I will give you the name. Hand me that child’s chart. That is the whole of your work tonight.”

Japanese: そう告げると太刀川は若い女性職員を呼び、子供を一人ずつ部屋に入れるよう伝えた。
English: After giving the instruction, Tachikawa called a young female staff member and told her to bring the children into the room one at a time.

Japanese: 「今日は十人くらいみましょう。状態のよくない子から入れてください」
English: “We will see approximately ten today. Begin with the children in the poorest condition.”

Japanese: 「今ちょっと、寝る前のお祈りの時間でして……」
English: “They’re just saying their prayers before bed...”

Japanese: 「ああ、結構。それが終わってからにしてください」
English: “That is fine. Bring them when the prayers are over.”

Japanese: 職員は礼をして、部屋を出て行く。そしてすぐに戻ってくると、
English: The staff member bowed and left the room. She soon returned.

Japanese: 「インスタントで恥ずかしいのですが」
English: “I’m afraid it’s only instant.”

Japanese: そう言って、二人分のコーヒーを置いていった。
English: With those words, she left two cups of coffee.

Japanese: この感じからすると、太刀川がここで診察を行うのは一度や二度ではないようだ。
English: Her manner suggested that Tachikawa had conducted examinations here many times before.

Japanese: 太刀川は早速コーヒーに手を付ける。美紗も同じように手を伸ばし、そして落ち着かぬままキョロキョロと視線を動かす。
English: Tachikawa immediately began drinking his coffee. Misa reached for hers as well, her restless gaze roaming around the room.

Japanese: そこは普段は応接室として使われているらしい。ソファーやローテーブルは診察がしやすいように部屋の隅に追いやられ、かわりに子供を座らせるためのパイプ椅子を部屋の中央に置いている。
English: Apparently, the room ordinarily served to receive visitors. The sofas and low table had been pushed into a corner to make space for the examinations. A folding chair for the children stood in the center instead.

Japanese: 壁際の棚の上には、子供が作ったらしい、折り紙や紙粘土細工が飾られており、職員と子供達がにこやかな顔で写る集合写真などもあった。
English: Shelves against the wall displayed what appeared to be the children’s origami and modeling-clay creations. There were also group photographs of staff and children smiling together.

Japanese: 太刀川はここで無料で子供達を診ているそうだ。美紗は彼がこんなところで慈善活動を行っているということに、イメージと違うような、むしろ逆にしっくり来るような、どっちつかずの印象を持った。
English: Apparently, Tachikawa examined the children here without charge. Learning that he performed charity work in a place like this left Misa unsure what to make of it. It seemed unlike the man she knew and, at the same time, entirely appropriate.

Japanese: 「まあタイプBの子供をここに捨てるという気持はなかなか理にかなっています」
English: “In fact, there is a certain logic to abandoning a Type B child here.”

Japanese: 太刀川はうつむき加減でコーヒーを啜りながら先ほどの話の続きをする。
English: Tachikawa continued his earlier explanation, head lowered slightly as he sipped his coffee.

Japanese: 「ここではタイプBだからというだけで差別されることはありませんし、彼らのための仕事もたくさんあります。朝の稲荷神社の方に行ったことがありますか？　あの辺りではよく斡旋業者が大声を張り上げていて、日雇いの肉体労働者をトラックに乗せています。タイプBの方が多いようですね。発症している方も見えます。ノルマ方式の作業だと、タイプBの方は相当稼ぐそうですよ。女性だったらもっと沢山稼ぐことが出来ます。Y地区はそういう施設は多いですからね。症状が重くなってしまうとなかなか仕事もないようですが。それでもY地区は、タイプBに限らず、マイノリティ全般には優しい町だと言えるでしょう」
English: “No one here discriminates against them simply for being Type B, and a great deal of work is available to them. Have you visited the area around Inari Shrine in the morning? Placement brokers frequently shout for workers there and load day laborers into trucks. Many appear to be Type B, including some whose symptoms have manifested. I am told that Type Bs can earn considerable sums on quota-based jobs. A woman can earn even more. Y District contains many establishments of that kind. Once their symptoms grow severe, there seems to be very little work for them. Nevertheless, Y District may fairly be called a city kind to minorities in general, not only to Type Bs.”

Japanese: 美紗にはあまり幸福な将来にも、優しい社会にも聞こえなかったが、太刀川は皮肉や冗談のつもりで言っているわけでもないようだ。自分とは価値観の規準が大分異なっていて、そして、太刀川のそれの方がシビアで現実的であるような気がして、訳もなく恥ずかしくなった。
English: To Misa, this sounded neither like a happy future nor a kind society. Yet Tachikawa did not appear to be speaking ironically or making a joke. His standards seemed very different from her own—and his the harsher and more realistic of the two. For no reason she could explain, Misa felt ashamed.

Japanese: 「どうして、Y地区にはタイプBが多いのですか？」
English: “Why are there so many Type Bs in Y District?”

Japanese: 「元々、この街自体が、基地の撤去後の野原に世間のあぶれものが集まって出来たという経緯もあるのでしょうが、それだけでもないでしょう。タイプBはグレートホールの側を好むという統計があります。さらに、グレートホールの近くではタイプBの出生率があがり、その程度を示すアウラー指数も他の地域より高くなる傾向があり、発症率も高いです。タイプAも同様です」
English: “The history of the city may be one reason. It began when society’s outcasts gathered on an empty plain after the military base was removed. But that cannot be the entire explanation. Statistics show that Type Bs prefer proximity to the Great Hole. The Type B birth rate also rises near it, as does the Aura Index used to indicate the degree of that tendency. The rate at which symptoms manifest is also higher. The same is true of Type As.”

Japanese: 「それは知っています。ミュータントとグレートホールに、何か関係性があるんでしょうか？」
English: “I know that much. Is there some connection between mutants and the Great Hole?”

Japanese: 「直接的な関係性は見つかっていません。そもそも、グレートホールはただの深い穴です。探索機が何度も下ろされて、それ以外の何物でもないことははっきりしています。ミュータントと何か関係があるとすれば、グレートホールにつきものの周辺の汚染物質でしょうね」
English: “No direct connection has been found. To begin with, the Great Hole is simply a deep pit. Probes have been lowered repeatedly, and it is clear that the pit is nothing more. If there is any connection to mutants, it would most likely involve the contaminants associated with the area around the Great Hole.”

Japanese: 「患者さんの妄想に、よくグレートホールが出て来るようなのですが……」
English: “The Great Hole seems to appear very often in our patients’ delusions...”

Japanese: 「世間ではまだまだミステリアスなものとして認識されているようですし、雄大で恐ろしいイメージもありますから、患者からすれば格好の妄想の材料なのでしょう」
English: “The public still regards it as something mysterious, and it carries images of immensity and terror. For a patient, it presumably makes excellent material for a delusion.”

Japanese: 美紗は何かもっと別の、科学とはまた違う繋がりが、患者とグレートホールの間にあるような気がしたが、それを口にすると馬鹿にされそうで言えなかった。幽霊とか、占いとか、そういったものも好きだが、普段は恥ずかしくてそのことについて語れないのと一緒だ。
English: Misa felt that there was some other connection between the patients and the Great Hole, one that had nothing to do with science. But she could not say so, afraid that Tachikawa would think her foolish. She felt the same way about her interest in ghosts and fortune-telling: ordinarily, embarrassment kept her from speaking of either.

Japanese: こういった自分の考え方は、医療従事者として似つかわしくないような気もする。
English: At times, she wondered whether such thinking was unbecoming in a medical professional.

Japanese: 「うちの病院が出来たのも、グレートホールの影響を考えてのことなのでしょうか」
English: “Was our hospital built there because of the Great Hole’s influence as well?”

Japanese: 「それは単に、他に建てる場所がなかったからですよ。純粋に治療を考えたら、グレートホールから遠い方がいいに決まってます」
English: “No. It was built there simply because there was nowhere else to put it. If treatment alone were the concern, farther from the Great Hole would obviously be better.”

Japanese: 太刀川のカップが空になる頃、最初の患者が入って来た。
English: As Tachikawa emptied his cup, the first patient entered.

Japanese: 六、七才くらいの活発そうな少女で、顔やキャミソールからはみ出した首筋や肩が真っ黒に日焼けしている。顔には大きなやけどのあとがあり、笑うと、白い八重歯がさわやかに映えた。そしてその目は金色である。
English: She was a lively-looking girl of six or seven. Her face and the neck and shoulders exposed by her camisole had been tanned almost black. A large burn scar marked her face, and when she smiled, one white, protruding canine stood out brilliantly. Her eyes were gold.

Japanese: 「三井遙香ちゃん」
English: “Haruka Mitsui.”

Japanese: 「はい！」
English: “Yes!”

Japanese: 太刀川の問いに、少女は即座に大きな声で返事をする。美紗はアルファベット順に並べられたカルテから「Ｈａｒｕｋａ　Mｉｔｓｕｉ」と書かれたファイルを探し出して、太刀川の脇の机に置く。
English: At Tachikawa’s call, the girl answered immediately and at great volume. Misa searched through the charts arranged alphabetically, found the file labeled ‘Haruka Mitsui,’ and placed it on the desk beside Tachikawa.

Japanese: そのままカルテに書かれた文章を読むと、少女は発症はしていないが、金眼があらわれやすく、それによる身体能力の向上度も高い。本人はそれを自覚しておらず、たびたび問題行動を起こすらしい。
English: According to the chart, the girl had not developed symptoms, but her eyes frequently turned gold and the resulting increase in her physical ability was unusually great. Apparently, she was unaware of the change and often caused trouble as a result.

Japanese: こんな少女も、将来は不幸になってしまうのだろうかと美紗が暗い気持ちになっていると、
English: Misa’s thoughts darkened. Would even a girl like this be doomed to unhappiness one day?

Japanese: 「じゃあ、その椅子に座って……」
English: “Now, sit in that chair...”

Japanese: 少女は職員が座るよう指示したのもきかず、笑顔のままタタタと彼に駆け寄ると太刀川の身体にしがみついた。
English: The girl ignored the staff member’s instruction to sit. Smiling, she pattered over to Tachikawa and wrapped herself around him.

Japanese: 「せんせいっ、大好きぃっ！」
English: “Doctor, I love youuu!”

Japanese: 少女は親愛の情を示したつもりなのだろうが、彼女の身体は想像以上の筋力があるようで、腰の辺りからめきめきと音がする。
English: The girl presumably meant only to display her affection. But her small body appeared to possess far more strength than it suggested, and something around Tachikawa’s waist began to creak.

Japanese: やはり金眼が発動したタイプＢというのは、子供であっても凄い力があるものだ。美紗が病院で見ているような薬によって
English: Even a child possessed tremendous strength once a Type B’s golden eyes appeared. Unlike the Type Bs Misa saw at the hospital, dulled by medication—

Japanese: 太刀川は口元を引きつらせてうめき声をあげる。
English: Tachikawa’s mouth drew tight as a groan escaped him.

Japanese: 「こ、こら」
English: “N-now, stop that.”

Japanese: 美紗も駈け寄ったが、それより職員の方が早かった。少女の頭を軽くはたいて、太刀川から引きはがす。
English: Misa rushed over, but the staff member was faster. She lightly smacked the girl on the head and pulled her away from Tachikawa.

Japanese: 「へへへ」
English: “Hehehe.”

Japanese: 少女は悪びれもせずに屈託のない笑顔を浮かべている。
English: The girl smiled without a trace of guilt or concern.

Japanese: 一方太刀川はその独特の髪型を乱し、ぜえぜえと荒く呼吸をしながら、
English: Tachikawa, meanwhile, stood with his distinctive hair in disarray, breathing heavily.

Japanese: 「あいかわらず、ちょっと元気すぎるようですね」
English: “As usual, you appear to be slightly too energetic.”

Japanese: そんなことを言ったので、美紗はついうっかり噴き出してしまった。
English: At that, Misa could not help bursting into laughter.

Japanese: 朝に、先日結婚したばかりの馬明の娘である馬美美（マー・メイメイ）から電話があった。中国人同士は結婚してもお互い名字がかわらないが、日本人と結婚したそうだから名がかわっているのかもしれない。興味はないから聞く気もないけれど。
English: That morning, Ma Meimei—Ma Ming’s recently married daughter—called me. Chinese people did not change their surnames when they married one another, but she had married a Japanese man and might now have a different name. I had no interest, so I did not intend to ask.

Japanese: 用件は、今日の昼から個人的な昼食会を行うので来ないかという誘いだった。
English: She was holding a private luncheon that afternoon and called to invite me.

Japanese: これが馬明の言っていたパーティだろう。そして参加者も馬明が言っていたとおりだった。
English: This was presumably the party Ma Ming had mentioned. The guests, too, were exactly those he had named.

Japanese: 廖志明の息子のトミーに、ジョゼ・フェルナンデスのところの三姉妹もやって来る。二路元帥である馬明の娘が主催するこの集まりに、さらに僕が行くことになればYSの有力幹部のジュニア世代そろい踏みとなる。
English: Tommy, the son of Liao Chi-ming, would attend, as would all three daughters of José Fernandes. With the daughter of Second Route Marshal Ma Ming as our hostess and myself added to the party, the junior generation of YS’s leading officers would be assembled in full.

Japanese: 話によると、こうした会合は美美の主催によりたびたび行われているらしい。外の街に出ていた僕は知らなかったが、今回近くにいるので、参加したらどうかとのこと。
English: According to Meimei, she often hosted gatherings of this kind. I had known nothing of them while living outside the city, but now that I was nearby, she thought I might join them.

Japanese: 汐さんがいない以上、汐家に留まっていても研究室にも入れないし、することがない。僕はその場で参加を了承し、時間になるとそのまま汐家から向かった。
English: Mr. Shio was away. Remaining in his home would leave me with nothing to do, since I could not enter the laboratory without him. I accepted immediately and, when the time came, went directly there from the Shio residence.

Japanese: 会場は美美の新居ではなく、馬明の屋敷であった。
English: The gathering was held not in Meimei’s new home, but at Ma Ming’s estate.

Japanese: ここも、子供の頃からよく訪れている家である。案内されなくともその構造はよく知っている。リビングルームに足を踏み入れると、すでにテーブルには料理が並べられていた。
English: This too was a house I had visited frequently since childhood. I knew its layout well enough not to need a guide. When I entered the living room, dishes already covered the table.

Japanese: 屋敷付きの調理人が作ったのであろう、広東風の料理である。
English: The Cantonese food had presumably been prepared by the estate’s cook.

Japanese: 「ようこそ。今日はよく来てくれたね」
English: “Welcome. I’m glad you came today.”

Japanese: 美美は笑顔で僕を出迎える。
English: Meimei greeted me with a smile.

Japanese: 「どうも。式では申し訳なかった」
English: “Thank you. I’m sorry about the wedding.”

Japanese: 「いいんだよ。別に。お父さんも久しぶりに小謝とじゃれあえて楽しそうだったよ」
English: “It’s fine. Really. Father looked as though he enjoyed horsing around with Siu Tse again after so long.”

Japanese: 「ご主人は？」
English: “Where is your husband?”

Japanese: 「お父さんと二人で出かけてる。自分の店を案内するんだって。すごい緊張した顔で出て行ったわ」
English: “He went out with Father. He said he would show Father around his shop. He looked terribly nervous when they left.”

Japanese: 「そりゃギャングに縄張り案内されても生きた心地はしないだろう。ご主人は一般の人なんでしょう？」
English: “No one would feel at ease with a gangster showing him around the territory. Your husband is an ordinary civilian, isn’t he?”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、美美は笑う。
English: At my remark, Meimei laughed.

Japanese: 「最近会う機会がないんだけど、シウちゃんは元気？」
English: “I haven’t had a chance to see her lately. Is little Siu doing well?”

Japanese: 「僕もちょっと会っただけだけど、相変わらずだったな」
English: “I only saw her briefly myself, but she was the same as ever.”

Japanese: 僕は給仕の女が渡してくれた、食前酒の入ったグラスを受け取りながらそう答えた。
English: I answered while accepting a glass of aperitif from a female server.

Japanese: 「松子ちゃんは？」
English: “And Matsuko?”

Japanese: 「今日は仕事だって」
English: “She said she had work today.”

Japanese: 「働いてらっしゃるの？」
English: “She has a job?”

Japanese: 「どこかの施設で孤児の面倒を見てるらしい」
English: “Apparently, she looks after orphans at some sort of facility.”

Japanese: 「まあ、あんなに資産のある家のお嬢様が、えらいわねえ。ここにいる若者たちは、誰も額に汗して働いてなんかいないっていうのに。みんな見習ったほうが良いわ」
English: “My. A young lady from such a wealthy family, doing honest work. None of the young people in this room have ever broken a sweat for a living. They should all follow her example.”

Japanese: 美美は口元を抑えて笑う。
English: Meimei covered her mouth as she laughed.

Japanese: 彼女が幸せそうで良かった。親同士が義兄弟だという縁があり、一つ上の彼女は、ほとんど生まれた頃からの知り合いだ。
English: I was glad to see her happy. Our fathers had sworn brotherhood, and Meimei, one year older than I, had known me almost from the day I was born.

Japanese: 馬明などはどうしても二人をくっつけたいようだったが、結局お互いを異性として見る機会のないまま今日を迎えている。
English: Ma Ming had plainly wanted to bring us together, but we had reached this day without either of us ever seeing the other as a man or a woman.

Japanese: 馬明は美美の兄である長男の世傑と、僕の妹である筱喬の関係にも色気があったようだが、父が筱喬を異様に溺愛していたのと、世傑が期待通りの育ち方をしなかったためにいつしか口にすることもなくなった。
English: He had apparently entertained similar hopes for Meimei’s older brother Sai-kit, the eldest son of the family, and my younger sister, Siu-kiu. In time he ceased to mention the possibility, both because my father doted upon Siu-kiu to a remarkable degree and because Sai-kit had not developed as Ma Ming had hoped.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、お兄さんは？」
English: “Speaking of which, where is your brother?”

Japanese: 「あの人は、ちょっと……」
English: “He’s... well...”

Japanese: 「やあ美美、こんにちは。そして小謝、昨日はどうも」
English: “Hello, Meimei. And Siu Tse, thank you for yesterday.”

Japanese: 美美が顔を曇らせたところで、トーマス・リャオ……トミーが現れた。
English: Just as Meimei’s expression clouded, Thomas Liao—Tommy—appeared.

Japanese: 昨日の緊張の場面とはうってかわって、にこやかでリラックスをした表情をしている。
English: In complete contrast to the tense scene the day before, his face was relaxed and cheerful.

Japanese: 「なんだか、大変なことになったねえ。あ、こちらは僕の大切な女性であるアイスだ」
English: “Things have certainly become complicated, haven’t they? Oh, and this is Ice, the woman dearest to me.”

Japanese: 「ボディガードのアイスです」
English: “I am Ice, his bodyguard.”

Japanese: 紹介された背の高い女性は、丁寧に日本風のお辞儀をする。
English: The tall woman he introduced bowed politely in the Japanese fashion.

Japanese: 偽名かニックネームのように思えるその名前からは正体不明だが、日本人だろうか？　それとも中国人か。肌と髪の色からするとその辺りだろうが、言葉からも立ち居振る舞いからも正確な国籍がよくわからない。
English: Her name sounded like a nickname or an alias and revealed nothing about her identity. Was she Japanese? Chinese? Her skin and hair suggested some origin in that part of the world, but neither her language nor her manner allowed me to determine her nationality precisely.

Japanese: 美人といえる顔立ちだが、その片側半分がやけどで爛れ、気の毒なほど容姿の印象を破壊している。前髪を片方垂らしていたが隠し切れていない。
English: Her features might have been called beautiful, but burns had disfigured one entire side of her face, sadly destroying that impression. She had let the hair on one side fall across it, but could not conceal the damage.

Japanese: ボディーガードと言うからには、ただの女ではなくタイプAか何かだとは思うが、このやけどは特質変異とも違うだろう。
English: If she worked as a bodyguard, she presumably was no ordinary woman, but perhaps a Type A. The burns, however, did not seem to be a mutation.

Japanese: 肌の露出を嫌っているのか、首を隠す高い襟の服と、長袖長ズボンという出で立ちで、すっぽりと全身を隠している。衣服の下にタイプAである証があるのかもしれないが、その姿のままでは特質変異らしき特徴を見つけることは出来ない。
English: Perhaps she disliked exposing her skin. A high collar covered her neck, and long sleeves and trousers concealed her entire body. Some sign that she was Type A might lie beneath those clothes, but as she stood, I could find no feature that resembled a mutation.

Japanese: 「これからこの街はどうなるんだい？　僕にはよくわからないけれど、なんだかきな臭い感じはするんだよ」
English: “What do you think will happen to this city now? I don’t really understand any of it, but I do have the feeling that something ugly is brewing.”

Japanese: この街がどうなるか。それはきみの父親である廖志明次第だと言いたかったが言わなかった。
English: I wanted to tell him that what happened to the city depended upon his own father, Liao Chi-ming, but I refrained.

Japanese: トミーは抜け目ない父親とはまるで正反対の人柄で、よく言えば鷹揚で温厚。別の言い方をすればお人好しで少々抜けている。
English: Tommy’s character was the perfect opposite of his shrewd father’s. Put kindly, he was easygoing and gentle. Put otherwise, he was too trusting and somewhat slow on the uptake.

Japanese: 昨日の会食を体験しても、何の切迫感もなく木訥とした口調で語るのは僕からすれば不思議に思えるが、それが彼の個性であり良さなのだ。
English: After what he had experienced at yesterday’s dinner, his complete lack of urgency and his plain, artless tone seemed strange to me. Yet this was his nature, and one of his virtues.

Japanese: 「ありがとうございます。もう一つ貰えますか？」
English: “Thank you. Could I have another?”

Japanese: グラスを渡してくれた給仕の女にトミーがにっこりと微笑みかけると、給仕はその丁寧な物腰に戸惑いながらもう一つ手渡す。トミーはそれを手ずからアイスに渡した。アイスは遠慮して断ろうとしたが、彼は無理矢理握らせるようにして、それを許さなかった。
English: Tommy smiled brightly at the server who had handed him a glass. Disconcerted by his courtesy, she gave him another. Tommy personally offered it to Ice. She tried to decline out of deference, but he all but pressed it into her hand and would permit no refusal.

Japanese: 「みんな、今日は小謝が来てくれたよ」
English: “Everyone, Siu Tse is here today.”

Japanese: 美美は振り返り、ちょうど部屋に入ってきた三姉妹に声をかける。
English: Meimei turned and called to the three sisters as they entered the room.

Japanese: 「みなさんこんにちは」
English: “Hello, everyone.”

Japanese: 近づいて来て、代表で挨拶をしたのは長女のアウロラだ。
English: Aurora, the eldest, approached and offered the greeting on behalf of the others.

Japanese: 「どうも」
English: “Hello.”

Japanese: 僕は軽く頭を下げた。
English: I inclined my head slightly.

Japanese: 世間で美女と名高い三人が勢揃いして並ぶとなかなか威圧感がある。
English: The three sisters were all celebrated beauties. When they stood assembled in a row, the effect was rather intimidating.

Japanese: 「小謝、来てくれたのね。でも今日は料理をひっくり返さないでよ」
English: “Siu Tse, you came. Try not to overturn the food today.”

Japanese: 顔を合わせてそうそうアウロラがそんな風にからかうので、僕は思わずむっとしてしまうと、
English: Aurora began teasing me the moment we met, and I could not help bristling.

Japanese: 「あら怒らないで。私小謝のこと大好きよ」
English: “Oh, don’t be angry. I love you, Siu Tse.”

Japanese: 僕の手を握ろうとしたので、
English: She tried to take my hand.

Japanese: 「僕はきみが苦手だな」
English: “I never did know what to do with you.”

Japanese: その手を振り払うと、アウロラは可笑しそうに笑う。
English: I brushed her hand away, and Aurora laughed in delight.

Japanese: 派手で社交家の長女アウロラ。皮肉屋で気むずかしい次女のアナ・クララ。控えめで大人しい三女のリタ。三人姉妹を簡単に説明すればそのようになる。
English: The flamboyant, sociable eldest sister, Aurora; the sardonic, difficult second sister, Ana Clara; and the reserved, quiet youngest, Rita. Such was the simplest description of the three.

Japanese: 「美美、結婚おめでとう。式は出席出来なくてごめんなさい。どうしても行けない用事があったの」
English: “Congratulations on your marriage, Meimei. I’m sorry I couldn’t attend the wedding. There was something I absolutely could not miss.”

Japanese: アナ・クララは僕とアウロラのやりとりを尻目に、主催者にそう挨拶をした。
English: Ignoring the exchange between Aurora and me, Ana Clara offered her greeting to our hostess.

Japanese: 「ありがとう。式のことは気にしなくていいのよ。こうして会いに来てくれたんだから」
English: “Thank you. Don’t worry about the wedding. You came to see me now, and that’s enough.”

Japanese: 美美はにこやかにそう返す。
English: Meimei answered with a warm smile.

Japanese: 「そう言ってくれれば助かるわ。でも、私たちのうちであなたが最初に結婚するなんてびっくり。男の子っぽくて、さばさばしてて、一番そんな風じゃなかったのに。しかも結婚前に子供まで出来ちゃうなんて」
English: “That’s kind of you. Still, I can’t believe you were the first among us to marry. You were such a tomboy, so straightforward—the last person I expected. And then you even became pregnant before the wedding.”

Japanese: 「そう？」
English: “Really?”

Japanese: 美美ははにかんで肩をすくめる。
English: Meimei gave a bashful shrug.

Japanese: 「本当にびっくりよ。……あら小謝、久しぶりね。元気だった？」
English: “It truly surprised me. ...Oh, Siu Tse, it’s been a long time. Have you been well?”

Japanese: アナ・クララは次は僕にそう話しかける。
English: Ana Clara addressed me next.

Japanese: 「まあね」
English: “Well enough.”

Japanese: 「学生生活は楽しいでしょ？　私も、もっと長くいたかったわ。ジョゼ・フェルナンデスの娘じゃない、私自身として生きられたのってあのときだけ。ああいうのが青春だったのかしら」
English: “Student life must be enjoyable. I wish I could have stayed longer. That was the only time I ever lived as myself, rather than as José Fernandes’s daughter. Was that what people mean by youth?”

Japanese: 去年大学を卒業したアナ・クララはそう言って溜息をつく。
English: Ana Clara, who had graduated from university the year before, sighed.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、アウロラとアナ・クララも大学に行ってる間、小謝みたいにマンション暮らしをしてたんだよね」
English: “Come to think of it, you and Aurora lived in an apartment like Siu Tse while you were at university, didn’t you?”

Japanese: トミーが言うと、アナ・クララは頷き、
English: At Tommy’s question, Ana Clara nodded.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。お姉ちゃんと二人で暮らして、お姉ちゃんが卒業してからは一人で住んでた。こっちにいるときはいつも誰かしら人がいたからね。全然ちがったよ」
English: “That’s right. I lived with my sister, then alone after she graduated. Back here, there was always someone around. It was completely different.”

Japanese: 「へえ、楽しそうだなあ。僕も一度一人で暮らしてみたいよ」
English: “That sounds wonderful. I would like to live alone at least once.”

Japanese: トミーは心底羨ましそうに溜息をつく。母親にアメリカにつれて行かれたり、父親に呼び戻されてY地区に来たり、振り回された生活をしている彼には外からは見えないストレスもあるのだろう。
English: Tommy sighed with heartfelt envy. His mother had taken him to America; his father had summoned him back to Y District. A life spent being pulled about by others had presumably placed him under pressures invisible from the outside.

Japanese: 「楽しかったよ。お父さんの教育方針らしいんだけど、普通の女子大生みたいな生活をしろってさ。ぼろくて古いマンションで、仕送りも最低限しかなかったんだ。自炊しないと電気代が払えなくなっちゃうくらい！　だからアルバイトだってしたんだよ」
English: “It was wonderful. Apparently it was Father’s educational philosophy: he wanted us to live like ordinary university girls. We stayed in an old, run-down apartment and received only the minimum allowance. If we didn’t cook for ourselves, we couldn’t even pay the electric bill. We had part-time jobs too.”

Japanese: 「そうなのよ。この子は家庭教師をしてたわ。私なんか、レストランで料理運んだりしてたのよ？　こうやって、お皿三枚片手で運べるんだから」
English: “Exactly. This one tutored students. I carried plates in a restaurant, if you can imagine it. I can hold three plates in one hand, like this.”

Japanese: アウロラが皿を運ぶ仕草をやってみせると、トミーは感心してうなずく。
English: Aurora demonstrated how she had carried them, and Tommy nodded with admiration.

Japanese: 「すごいねえ。二人が働いてるところなんて想像出来ないや」
English: “Amazing. I can’t imagine either of you working.”

Japanese: 「私たち意外と働きものなのよ？　家のことだって、分担してやってるんだもの。テーブルを吹いたり、床を磨いたりね。お父さんだって当番の日はやるわ。自分でバケツに水を汲んで、雑巾でごしごしこするのよ。家に住まわしてる若い人と一緒に汗だくになってね。そういうことをしないと人間は駄目になるって、昔からそうだったんだから」
English: “We’re surprisingly industrious. We divide the housework between us too—wiping tables, polishing floors. Father takes his turn when his day comes. He fills a bucket with water himself and scrubs with a rag until he’s dripping with sweat beside the young people who live in our house. He’s always said that people rot if they never do that kind of work.”

Japanese: 「そうなんだ！　うちでは全部お手伝いさんがやってくれてるよ。なんだか尊敬しちゃうなあ」
English: “Really? At our house, the servants do everything. I can’t help admiring you.”

Japanese: トミーは目を丸くして驚く。
English: Tommy’s eyes widened in surprise.

Japanese: 「小謝だって、子供の時はレストランに預けられてたから、掃除でも料理でもなんでも出来るんでしょ？　何にも出来ないのが僕だけだと思うと、なんだか情けないよ。……ねえ、アイスは出来る？」
English: “Siu Tse was raised in a restaurant as a child, so he can clean and cook and do everything else too, can’t he? It makes me feel pathetic to think that I’m the only one who can’t do anything. ...What about you, Ice?”

Japanese: 急に話題をふられたアイスは、周囲に視線をやってこの場で自分が発言すべきかどうか若干迷いを見せてから、
English: The abrupt question caught Ice unprepared. She looked at the people around her and hesitated over whether it was her place to speak.

Japanese: 「ええ、まあ、一通りは……」
English: “Yes, well... I can manage the usual things.”

Japanese: 控えめな声でそう言った。
English: She spoke in a subdued voice.

Japanese: 「そうかあ！　じゃあ今度屋敷でも何か作ってくれるかい？」
English: “I see! Then would you cook something at the estate next time?”

Japanese: 「……私の料理は貧しい家庭料理なので、トミー様のお口に合うかどうか……」
English: “...All I know is humble home cooking, so I don’t know whether it would suit your taste, Master Tommy.”

Japanese: 「いいんだよ。僕は、きみがどんな料理を食べて育ったか知りたいんだ」
English: “That doesn’t matter. I want to know what food you ate when you were growing up.”

Japanese: トミーはアイスの手を両手で握って真顔で頼む。
English: Tommy took both of Ice’s hands in his own and made the request with perfect seriousness.

Japanese: 「は、はい。どうしてもとおっしゃるなら……」
English: “Y-yes. If you truly insist...”

Japanese: 「お願い。僕はきみことならすべてを知りたいといつも考えているって忘れないで」
English: “Please. Never forget that I always want to know everything about you.”

Japanese: 「トーマス様……」
English: “Master Thomas...”

Japanese: そして二人は見つめ合う。
English: The two gazed into each other’s eyes.

Japanese: 僕は二人の人目をはばからないやりとりに若干戸惑いを感じたが、アウロラなどが気にせずに美美と雑談などをはじめたところを見ると、今回が特別だということでもなく、いつものことなのだろう。
English: Their exchange, conducted without the slightest regard for the people watching, left me somewhat disconcerted. Aurora and the others ignored it and began chatting with Meimei, however. Evidently, this was nothing exceptional, but a regular occurrence.

Japanese: 親たちの間では色々とあるが、子の世代は年も近く、幼い頃からの知り合いで、性格的にも穏やかなものが多いから割合仲が良い。僕が参加するのは初めてだが、彼らの話からすると、こうした会合はしょっちゅう行われているようだ。
English: There were all manner of complications among their parents. The children, by contrast, were close in age, had known one another since childhood, and were mostly mild by nature. As a result, they got along reasonably well. This was my first time attending, but their conversation suggested that such gatherings took place frequently.

Japanese: 「そうです。月に一度くらいはやっています」
English: “That’s right. We hold one about once a month.”

Japanese: 雑談に交じれないでぽつんと突っ立っていたリタに聞いてみると、彼女はそう答えた。
English: Rita had been standing alone, unable to enter the conversation. When I asked her, she gave that answer.

Japanese: 「いつもこのメンツで？」
English: “Always with this group?”

Japanese: 「いえ、今日は少ないです。普段は、美美さんの友達の方とか、お姉ちゃんの友達とか、もっと色んな人がいて……ウォンさんのところのご姉妹とか、ボネットさんのところのサウル君とかも前はよく来ていました。サウル君はとにかく女性にちょっかいをかけるので、出入禁止になってしまいましたが……」
English: “No, there are fewer people today. Usually some of Meimei’s friends come, and my sisters’ friends, and many others... The Wong sisters and Saul from the Bonetto family used to attend often as well. Saul simply would not stop bothering the women, though, so they banned him from coming...”

Japanese: カジノ王ダリオ・ボネットの息子のサウルも参加していたというのは意外だった。
English: I was surprised that Saul, the son of casino king Dario Bonetto, had attended these gatherings.

Japanese: ボネットファミリーと馬明は特別仲が悪いというわけでもないが、同じYSでもほとんど接点のない関係である。
English: The Bonetto Family and Ma Ming were not particularly hostile to each other, but despite belonging to the same YS, they otherwise had very little to do with one another.

Japanese: 「今日は微妙な時期だし、僕も来るからメンバーを絞ったのかな？」
English: “The timing is delicate, and I’m attending today. Did Meimei perhaps limit the guests for those reasons?”

Japanese: 「すみません。それは私にもわかりません」
English: “I’m sorry. I don’t know either.”

Japanese: リタは首を左右に振る。
English: Rita shook her head.

Japanese: 「でも、いいことだと思います。私たちの世代がこうやって交流を深めていければ、この先のことに何か良い影響があるかもしれないですし……」
English: “But I think these meetings are a good thing. If our generation keeps building stronger ties this way, perhaps it will help us somehow in the future...”

Japanese: 彼女の口からそういう言葉が飛び出るとは思っていなかったので、思わずその顔をまじまじと見つめてしまった。
English: I had not expected words like those from her and found myself staring intently into her face.

Japanese: 「あら、二人きりで何をじっくり話し合ってるの？」
English: “My, what are the two of you discussing so earnestly all alone?”

Japanese: 振り返ると、目の前にはいつのまにかアナ・クララが立っていて、うっすらと笑っている。
English: I turned. Ana Clara had somehow appeared directly before us and was smiling faintly.

Japanese: その頬は、既にアルコールで赤くなりはじめていた。
English: Alcohol had already begun to redden her cheeks.

Japanese: 「こっちに来て、みんなで話しましょうよ。小謝と会うのなんて久しぶりなんだから、たくさん話してもらうわ」
English: “Come over here and talk with everyone. We haven’t seen Siu Tse in ages, so he’s going to tell us all kinds of things.”

Japanese: そう言って、僕の袖を掴むとぐいと引っ張る。
English: She seized my sleeve and pulled hard.

Japanese: この次女も、長女に劣らず酒癖が悪いのだ。
English: When drinking, the second sister behaved no better than the first.

Japanese: 僕は酔って今日一日を台無しにするつもりもなかったので、最初の食前酒を飲んだ他にはいくら勧められてもアルコールに手を付けずに過ごした。
English: I had no intention of growing drunk and ruining the entire day. After my first aperitif, I refused every offer and passed the afternoon without touching any more alcohol.

Japanese: アウロラと美美がよく喋り、時々アナ・クララが二人の話を混ぜっ返す。トミーは自分からはほとんど喋らずに、彼女たちの会話に会わせて笑い、時々連れてきたアイスに耳打ちして何かを説明した。リタも黙って、姉たちの会話を眺めている。
English: Aurora and Meimei did most of the talking, with Ana Clara occasionally cutting in to stir things up. Tommy seldom spoke on his own; he laughed along with the women and sometimes whispered an explanation to Ice. Rita too remained silent, watching her sisters converse.

Japanese: 話はアウロラの趣味のピアノ演奏の話や、美美の新婚生活などについてのやくたいもない世間話ばかりだった。今YSに降りかかっている問題について彼女たちが触れないのは、あえてそうしているのか、そもそも興味がないのか、こうして見ていてもよくわからない。リタの先ほどの発言からするとまるっきり無知でいるというわけでもないはずだが。
English: They discussed nothing but idle subjects: Aurora’s piano playing, Meimei’s newlywed life, and the like. Whether they deliberately avoided the problems descending upon YS or simply had no interest in them, I could not determine by watching. Rita’s earlier remark suggested that they were not wholly ignorant.

Japanese: すべて承知の上でこうして、昔とちっともかわらない馬鹿話をしているのだとすれば、それはそれで悪くはない。
English: If they understood everything and still gathered to trade the same foolish talk as ever, perhaps there was something to be said for it.

Japanese: 黙っていると彼女たちのペースに巻き込まれて、世間話につき合わされてしまう。しかも僕は年下の部類に入るから、変なからかわれかたをしてばかりなのだ。
English: Silence left me at the mercy of their pace, forced to participate in their gossip. Worse, I was one of the younger people there, so they kept finding strange ways to tease me.

Japanese: 僕はいやになって無理矢理トミーを相手にチェスを指し始めたが、女どもはお構いなく話しかけてくる。
English: At last I tired of it and forced Tommy into a game of chess, but the women continued addressing me as though nothing had changed.

Japanese: 「ねえ小謝。あのゴミ屋のお嬢様と別れて、私と結婚する気ない？　私に求婚してくるのはオジサンばっかりでうんざり」
English: “Say, Siu Tse. Why don’t you leave that waste dealer’s daughter and marry me? I’m sick of being proposed to by nothing but old men.”

Japanese: とアウロラがその大きな胸を揺らしながら言うと、
English: Aurora said it, her ample breasts swaying as she spoke.

Japanese: 「それがいいわ！　そうしたら、フェルナンデスファミリーと一緒になって、YSの未来も安泰よ。ツェーおじさんもきっと喜ぶわ」
English: “What a wonderful idea! Then you could unite with the Fernandes Family and secure the future of YS. Uncle Tse would surely be delighted.”

Japanese: などと、妊娠中のために酒など口にしていないはずの美美が同調する。
English: So agreed Meimei, who was pregnant and therefore could not possibly blame the alcohol.

Japanese: 僕は無視をして、盤上のナイトを動かす。トミーは頭を抱えている。囲碁のルールはわからないというのでトミーに合わせてチェスを選んだ。
English: I ignored them and moved a knight across the board. Tommy clutched his head. He did not know the rules of Go, so I had chosen chess for his sake.

Japanese: 彼はそれなりに自信があったらしいが、もうはじめの頃の余裕はなくなっている。
English: He had apparently possessed some confidence at first, but all his early composure was now gone.

Japanese: 「姉さんやめときなよ。冗談でもそんなこと言うと、リタが怒るわよ」
English: “Give it up, Aurora. Even as a joke, that kind of talk will make Rita angry.”

Japanese: アナ・クララがニタニタと笑いながら言って、
English: Ana Clara said it with a broad, mischievous grin.

Japanese: 「ちっ、違います！」
English: “Th-that’s not true!”

Japanese: リタが真っ赤になって否定する。
English: Rita turned scarlet as she denied it.

Japanese: 一体、何の話をしているのやら……。
English: What in the world were they talking about?

Japanese: 彼女たちは何やらわいわいと騒ぎながら料理のテーブルの方へ揃って歩いて行く。
English: The women walked off together toward the table of food, still raising a commotion over something.

Japanese: 「なんだかめちゃくちゃ疲れる。トミーは毎回こんなのに参加しているの？」
English: “This is exhausting. Do you come to these every time, Tommy?”

Japanese: 僕が溜息をつくと、彼はルークに手を伸ばしながら、
English: I sighed. He reached toward a rook as he answered,

Japanese: 「そうだよ。みんな賑やかで明るくてとても楽しい」
English: “That’s right. Everyone is so cheerful and lively. It’s tremendous fun.”

Japanese: 言ってから、またルークから手を放した。迷っているようだ。
English: Then he took his hand away from the rook. He seemed uncertain.

Japanese: 「賑やかすぎるんじゃないか？」
English: “Aren’t they a little too lively?”

Japanese: 「僕はちょうどいいと思うよ。なんていったって、屋敷にいると息が詰まって仕方がないんだ。父さんはやたらと僕に仕事のための勉強をさせようとするし、部下の人たちはみんなぴりぴりしてるし」
English: “I think it’s just right. The estate is so stifling that I can hardly bear it. Father is always making me study for the business, and all his men are perpetually on edge.”

Japanese: トミーは肩をすくめる。そして溜息をつくと、チェス盤を覗く込むようにしてた上体を起こし、ドリンクに手を付ける。
English: Tommy shrugged. With a sigh, he straightened up from where he had been leaning over the chessboard and reached for his drink.

Japanese: 「どうも、敗戦濃厚だな。ちょっと休憩だ」
English: “This is beginning to look very much like defeat. I need a short break.”

Japanese: 「降参するかい？」
English: “Do you resign?”

Japanese: 「いや」
English: “No.”

Japanese: トミーは首を横に振ると、
English: Tommy shook his head.

Japanese: 「父さんは僕を立派な跡継ぎにしたいみたいなんだけど、正直僕には荷が重いよね。多分小謝と比べてるんだと思う。でも僕に小謝みたいに出来るようになれって言ったって土台無理な話なんだよ。僕には特別な才能はなんにもないんだ」
English: “Father seems determined to make me a worthy heir, but honestly, the burden is too much for me. I think he is probably comparing me to you. But telling me to become like Siu Tse is asking for the impossible. I have no special talent at all.”

Japanese: トミーは言葉の割には卑屈な様子もなく、いたって自然な調子でそう言う。
English: Despite his words, Tommy sounded neither abject nor self-pitying. He said it all quite matter-of-factly.

Japanese: 確かに彼はあまりにも人柄がおっとりとしていて、父の廖志明のように部下や仲間を統率して物事を成すというタイプではないだろう。それを自分のようなギャングにしようとしつけている廖という人物が、僕にとっては何やらおかしく感じられる。
English: He was certainly too easygoing to be a man who commanded subordinates and allies to accomplish his designs, as his father Liao Chi-ming did. It struck me as oddly absurd that Liao would try to mold a son like this into a gangster after his own image.

Japanese: 「きみのお父さんは相当怜悧な人だと思うけれど、息子に対しては目が曇るというか、期待しすぎているというか、溺愛しているんだねえ」
English: “I consider your father an exceptionally shrewd man. But when it comes to his son, his judgment clouds—or perhaps he expects too much. He must dote upon you terribly.”

Japanese: 僕が素直に感心すると、
English: I offered the observation in genuine admiration.

Japanese: 「あはは、確かに期待はされているね！　応えることは全然出来ていないけれど」
English: “Ahaha, he certainly expects a great deal! I haven’t managed to meet those expectations at all.”

Japanese: 「……あの女性は、どういう人なんだ？　きみのボディガードって言ってたけれど」
English: “...What kind of woman is she? You called her your bodyguard.”

Japanese: 僕は、二人で離しているのがよほど気になるのか、遠くからチラチラとこちらに視線を向けているアイスについて尋ねた。
English: I asked about Ice, who kept glancing toward us from across the room, apparently concerned by our private conversation.

Japanese: 「彼女はああ言っていたし、そういうことになっているけれど、それはただの建前だよ。僕のことを守れなんて一言も言ったことがないし、そんな危ないことはしてほしｋない。僕にとってはもっと大事な存在だよ。とても素晴らしい女性なんだ」
English: “That is what she called herself, and officially that is what she is. But it’s only a pretense. I have never once asked her to protect me, and I don’t want her doing anything so dangerous. To me, she is far more important. She is a truly wonderful woman.”

Japanese: トミーは目をきらきらさせてそう言った。
English: Tommy’s eyes shone as he spoke.

Japanese: 素直な人間で、その話題になった途端に表情がぱっと輝くのを見れば彼がアイスに対してどう思っているのか口にせずともわかる。
English: He was an open, guileless man. The way his expression lit the moment the subject arose made his feelings for Ice obvious without any declaration.

Japanese: 「お父さんは何て言ってる？」
English: “What does your father say?”

Japanese: 「あまり親しくするなって言ってるけど……」
English: “He tells me not to become too close to her...”

Japanese: そうだろう。
English: Of course he did.

Japanese: あの焼けどの痕と、特有の雰囲気から察するに、彼女はあまり素性の良い人間ではなさそうだ。
English: Judging solely from the burn scars and her peculiar air, she did not seem to come from a particularly respectable background.

Japanese: タイプAだかタイプBだか、それ以外の何かだか知らないが、人より優れた特殊な能力か技術があって、それを理由にボディガードという名目を立てて側に置いているのだろう。廖がエリオットというボディガードをいつも連れているように。
English: Whether she was Type A, Type B, or something else entirely, she presumably possessed some extraordinary ability or skill. The title of bodyguard provided a pretext for keeping her near him, just as Liao always brought along a bodyguard named Elliott.

Japanese: 「でも、何と言われても、これだけは従えないな。例え父さんだろうとね」
English: “But whatever anyone says, this is the one command I cannot obey. Even if it comes from Father.”

Japanese: トミーは笑いながらそう言った。
English: Tommy said it with a smile.

Japanese: 「立派なもんだね」
English: “How admirable.”

Japanese: 皮肉ではなかったが、皮肉と受け取られても仕方ないような言い方だった。
English: I was not being sarcastic, though no one could have been blamed for hearing sarcasm in my tone.

Japanese: が、トミーは別に悪く取ったりはしないだろう。
English: Tommy, however, would not take it badly.

Japanese: 「そういえば」
English: “That reminds me.”

Japanese: 彼はふと話題を変える。
English: He changed the subject without warning.

Japanese: 「小謝は、こないだ言われたように、お父さんの跡をつぐの？」
English: “Will you succeed your father, as he asked you to the other day?”

Japanese: 今の僕の立場では、廖志明の息子であるトミーに対してはどちらとも答えようのない質問だったが、本人は繊細な部分に触れる質問をした自覚がないらしい。
English: Given my present position, this was not a question I could answer either way before the son of Liao Chi-ming. Tommy himself appeared unaware that he had touched upon anything sensitive.

Japanese: 「是非そうすべきだよ。あの時の龍頭の顔は、とても真剣だった。心底小謝に自分の事業を引き継いで欲しいんだよ。もし小謝がうんと言えば、とても喜ぶと思うし、病気と戦うはげみにもなる」
English: “You certainly should. The Longtou was completely serious that day. He truly wants you to inherit his work. If you agreed, I think it would make him extremely happy—and give him strength in his fight against the illness.”

Japanese: 僕の気持は決まっていたが、こたえず、グラスの炭酸水を飲んだ。
English: My mind was settled, but I did not answer. I drank from my glass of sparkling water.

Japanese: 「僕は賛成だよ。きっと、アウロラたちも賛成してくれるし、協力もしてくれると思う。僕らは子供の時から、いつか小謝が龍頭になるって信じてたからね」
English: “I support you. I’m sure Aurora and the others will support you and lend their help as well. Ever since we were children, we’ve all believed that one day Siu Tse would become Longtou.”

Japanese: 「ありがとう」
English: “Thank you.”

Japanese: と僕が言ったのは、ごく単純に彼の優しい言葉に対する感謝の意味だった。
English: I meant nothing more than simple gratitude for his kind words.

Japanese: 「別に謝ることないよ。……よし、やっと手が決まったぞ。これはどうだ？」
English: “There’s nothing to thank me for. ...Good, I’ve finally chosen my move. What do you say to this?”

Japanese: トミーは自信満々にクイーンを動かして僕のナイトを取ったが、それが悪手で、それから三手後には彼のキングは詰まされることとなった。
English: With perfect confidence, Tommy moved his queen and took my knight. It was a bad move. Three moves later, his king was checkmated.

Japanese: 思ったよりも楽しい会合だったかもしれない。
English: Perhaps I had enjoyed the gathering more than I expected.

Japanese: 僕の少年時代は彼らよりもむしろ街の連中とのつき合いの方が深い。彼らと会うのは、何かYSの会合のようなお仕着せの場面でが多かったが、それでも僕らが物心つく前からの幼なじみであり、YS幹部のジュニア世代だという共通した立場は、他の人間とは共有出来ないものだ。
English: In boyhood, I had been closer to the people of the streets than to anyone here. Most of my meetings with these children had occurred in prescribed settings resembling YS functions. Even so, we had known one another since before we were old enough to understand anything, and we occupied the same position as the junior generation of YS officers—a bond no outsider could truly understand.

Japanese: そして、子供の頃からの知人と、大人になってからまた話すと、人間というものはさほどかわらないということも実感させられる。アウロラは幼い頃からおしゃまだし、アナ・クララは理屈っぽく、リタは二人の姉の影にいつも隠れている。トミーは少し抜けていて、美美はいつでも僕の姉気取りだ。きっと彼らも、僕のことを子供の頃の姿と重ねて見ているのだろう。
English: Speaking again as adults to people one had known in childhood also drove home how little human beings changed. Aurora had been precocious even as a little girl; Ana Clara argumentative; Rita forever hidden in the shadows of her two sisters. Tommy had always been slightly slow, and Meimei always pretended to be my older sister. They, too, presumably saw me now through the child I had once been.

Japanese: だからお互いに子供に戻ったように話すことが出来る。それぞれ大人としての悩みを隠しているにしろ。
English: That allowed us to speak as though we had all become children again, even if each of us concealed the troubles of adulthood.

Japanese: 宴はこれからというところだったが、僕は不意に目眩を感じ、意識がじわじわと闇に浸食されてゆくのを感じた。例の発作が始まろうとしているのだ。
English: The party was only beginning in earnest when a sudden wave of dizziness passed through me and I felt darkness gradually invade my consciousness. One of the familiar episodes was about to begin.

Japanese: 「悪いけど、すごく眠くなった。少し昼寝をさせてもらうよ」
English: “I’m sorry, but I’ve become terribly sleepy. I’m going to take a short nap.”

Japanese: 「えー、なんで急に眠るのよ？　まだちょっとお話しましょ」
English: “What? Why would you suddenly go to sleep? Stay and talk a little longer.”

Japanese: アウロラが僕の腕を掴もうとすると、
English: Aurora tried to seize my arm.

Japanese: 「まあまあ、眠らせてあげなよ。昼寝だけがこの人の唯一の趣味みたいなものなんだから」
English: “Now, now, let him sleep. Napping is practically this man’s only hobby.”

Japanese: 僕の体質を知っている美美がそう割り込んで、なおも食い下がろうとするアウロラを引きはがすと、目配せをくれる。
English: Meimei, who knew my constitution, intervened and pulled Aurora away when she persisted. Then she gave me a knowing look.

Japanese: 僕は有り難く目配せを返し、別室のソファーに倒れ込んだ。
English: I returned the look gratefully and collapsed onto a sofa in another room.

Japanese: 目を覚ますと十五時。丁度宴が終わろうとする時刻だった。
English: When I woke, it was three in the afternoon, precisely when the party was drawing to a close.

Japanese: 「小謝！」
English: “Siu Tse!”

Japanese: 別れ際、迎えの車に乗り込もうというところで、アウロラはドアに手をかけたまま僕を振り返る。
English: As we parted, Aurora was about to climb into the car that had come for her. With one hand on the door, she looked back at me.

Japanese: 「あなたがこの街の次のボスよ！」
English: “You are the next boss of this city!”

Japanese: 突然何を言うのかとその顔をじっと見つめると、アウロラは意味ありげに笑い、そして車に乗り込んだ。
English: I stared into her face, wondering what could have prompted the sudden declaration. Aurora gave me a meaningful smile and climbed into the car.

Japanese: 汐さんと連絡がついたので僕はその足で再び汐家に舞い戻った。
English: I got in touch with Mr. Shio and went straight back to his house.

Japanese: 松子が仕事で出払った静かな家で、汐さんは一人でグラスに注がれた琥珀の液体を舐めていた。かたわらには、彼のお気に入りのテネシーウィスキーのボトルがある。
English: The house was quiet with Matsuko away at work. Mr. Shio sat alone, sipping an amber liquid from a glass. Beside him stood a bottle of his favorite Tennessee whiskey.

Japanese: 「よくつまみも水もなくそんな強い酒を飲めるもんだね」
English: “I don’t know how you drink liquor that strong without food or water.”

Japanese: 僕が呆れて言ったが、彼はそれには答えず、
English: I spoke in amazement, but he ignored the remark.

Japanese: 「亮、服を着替えて手を洗え。さっそく地下室へ行くぞ」
English: “Ryo, change your clothes and wash your hands. We’re going straight to the basement.”

Japanese: 一方的に言って立ち上がった。
English: He stood without waiting for an answer.

Japanese: 僕は言われたとおり風呂場で清潔な服に着替え、アルコールで手指消毒を行ってから地下の実験室へ降りる。そこでは白衣を着た汐さんが机の上に例の虎の肉片の入ったシャーレを置き、傍らのモニターに映ったグラフを眺めていた。
English: As instructed, I changed into clean clothes in the bathroom and disinfected my hands with alcohol before descending to the underground laboratory. Mr. Shio was there in a white coat. A petri dish containing the tiger tissue sat on the table, and he was studying a graph displayed on the monitor beside it.

Japanese: 「見ろ」
English: “Look.”

Japanese: 言われて僕はシャーレのなかをのぞき込む。
English: I bent over the petri dish as instructed.

Japanese: 「なんだか弱ってるような気がするんだけど」
English: “It seems weaker somehow.”

Japanese: 「その通りだ。反応がきわめて微弱になっている。ほら、こっちの画面を見ろ。このグラフが活動力の推移を意味してるが、このままだと、今日か、明日には活動を停止するだろうな」
English: “It is. The response has grown extremely faint. Look at this screen. The graph shows the change in its activity level. At the present rate, it will cease activity today or tomorrow.”

Japanese: 「コアの培養は失敗か。思ったより生命力がなかったみたいだね。僕らのやりかたがまずかったのか、僕らが知っているものとは根本的に違うのか……傾向値はいくつだったの？」
English: “So culturing the core has failed. It possessed less vitality than we thought. Perhaps our method was wrong, or perhaps it is fundamentally different from the things we know... What was its tendency value?”

Japanese: 「２７００程度だな」
English: “Approximately twenty-seven hundred.”

Japanese: 僕は口笛を吹き、
English: I whistled.

Japanese: 「ちょうどいい数値だ」
English: “A perfect value.”

Japanese: 血液を分析することで計測されるタイプBの傾向値は、７００を越えれば金眼や発作といった症状が見られ、身体能力の向上もはっきりと認識されるため、このあたりがタイプBとノーマルの境目とされている。１０００を越えれば女性でもノーマルの男性以上の身体能力を持つのが普通で、１４００にもなれば、個人差はあるがスポーツ選手として一流の成績を残せると言われていた。
English: The Type B tendency value was measured through blood analysis. Above seven hundred, symptoms such as golden eyes and episodes appeared, with a clearly perceptible increase in physical ability. That level was therefore conventionally treated as the boundary between Type B and Normal. Above one thousand, even a woman would ordinarily possess greater physical abilities than a Normal man. At fourteen hundred, depending upon individual variation, a person was said to be capable of first-rate athletic performance.

Japanese: ２７００というのは、一般的にはまず見られない数値だ。１６００程度の傾向値をもつ飼料を与えた場合の研究データなどは存在するが、ここまで高いもので行った例は見たことがない。
English: A value of twenty-seven hundred was almost never observed under ordinary circumstances. Research data existed for subjects given feed with a value of approximately sixteen hundred, but I had never seen an experiment performed with anything this high.

Japanese: しかし、僕たちにとって、この実験は　”二回目”　になる。
English: For us, however, this would be the second experiment.

Japanese: 「何にしろ、組織が少しでも新鮮なうちに行いたい。さっさと始めよう」
English: “In any event, we should perform it while the tissue remains as fresh as possible. Let’s begin.”

Japanese: 「僕が来るのを待たずにやってくれてても良かったのに」
English: “You could have started without waiting for me.”

Japanese: 「お前がやらないと意味がないだろう？」
English: “There would be no point unless you did it.”

Japanese: 汐さんはぶっきらぼうに言って、立ち上がる。
English: Mr. Shio rose after the blunt reply.

Japanese: 別室には金属の大きな棚があり、そこには透明なプラスチックのケージが並べられている。そのケージの中には今日届いたばかりの真っ白なネズミ達がおり、棚全体がカサカサと音を立てていた。
English: A separate room held a large metal rack lined with transparent plastic cages. The pure-white mice delivered that day occupied the cages, and the entire rack rustled with their movement.

Japanese: 「マウスは何匹用意出来たの？」
English: “How many mice did you obtain?”

Japanese: 「傾向値３００のノーマルが十匹、傾向値９００のタイプBが十匹で、計二十匹だ」
English: “Ten Normals with a tendency value of three hundred and ten Type Bs with a value of nine hundred. Twenty in all.”

Japanese: 「もう少し用意した方が良かったのでは？」
English: “Shouldn’t we have acquired more?”

Japanese: 「こんなもんだろう。これでも多いくらいだよ」
English: “This should be enough. If anything, it’s too many.”

Japanese: 「まあそうだね」
English: “I suppose so.”

Japanese: 「組織の方をもっと大きく切断してくれればよかったんだが」
English: “I wish you could have cut away a larger portion of tissue.”

Japanese: 「そうしたかったんだけれど、なかなか思うようにいかなかった。急いでいたしね」
English: “I wanted to, but I couldn’t manage it. I was in a hurry.”

Japanese: 「まあ、これでやってみるしかない。結果が出るかどうかはわからないが」
English: “We have no choice but to try with this. Whether it will produce a result is another question.”

Japanese: これからこのマウスに、あの時虎の死骸から持って来た組織を餌として与える。ゲル状になった　”生きている”　組織と、大きく切り取ってきたもう動かない塊の肉の両方だ。そうして、逐一傾向値を調べ、再生能力の有無を確かめるというのが今回の実験の概要である。
English: We would feed the mice the tissue we had taken from the tiger’s carcass: both the gelatinous, ‘living’ tissue and the larger, inert mass of flesh we had cut away. We would measure the mice’s tendency values at each stage and test for regenerative ability. That was the experiment in outline.

Japanese: タイプBの傾向値というものは、食物によって増加する。傾向値の高いものを摂取し続けると、食べた方の傾向値も上がり、一定限度をこえるとタイプBとしての特徴を有しはじめるのだ。
English: Type B tendency value increased through food. When an animal or person continued consuming material with a high value, the eater’s value rose as well. Beyond a certain limit, Type B traits began to appear.

Japanese: そもそも、人間にこれほどまでにタイプBが誕生するようになったもの、食物が原因だった。今でも正確に特定することは出来ていないが、おそらくアジアの某国で生産されが穀物が原因だと推測されている。
English: According to the prevailing account, food had also caused Type Bs to emerge in such great numbers among humans in the first place. No exact source had been identified even now, but researchers suspected grain produced in an unnamed Asian country.

Japanese: とにかく、何らかの農産物が、なんらかの理由で異常に高い傾向値を持ってしまったのだ。そして、これを輸入した国々で大量のタイプBが発生したというのが現在支持されているタイプB発生のメカニズムである。
English: Some agricultural product had, for reasons unknown, acquired an abnormally high tendency value. It was then imported by countries in which large populations of Type Bs emerged. This was the currently accepted mechanism for the Type B phenomenon.

Japanese: 傾向値の測定方法が発見されたのはタイプB問題が発生してから大分あとのことで、気がついた時には、世界中の人間や動物に膨大なタイプB傾向が蓄積され、取り除くのは不可能な状態になっていた。
English: The means of measuring tendency value was discovered long after the Type B problem began. By the time anyone recognized what had happened, Type B tendency had accumulated to enormous levels in humans and animals throughout the world and could no longer be removed.

Japanese: 現在では、まともな食卓からはタイプB傾向値の高いものが排除されているが、しかし一旦蓄積されたタイプB傾向値というものは、子の代、孫の代にまで受け継がれる。だから食事として新しく摂取しなくとも、親がタイプBならば子がタイプBになる確率は高く、また子がタイプBでなくとも、孫や、その子がタイプBにならないという保証はない。
English: Today, foods with high Type B tendency values had been excluded from any so-called proper diet. Yet a value already accumulated could pass to a person’s children and grandchildren. Thus, even without fresh intake through food, a Type B parent was highly likely to produce a Type B child. And even if the child was not Type B, no one could guarantee that a grandchild or later descendant would not be.

Japanese: このように、一度タイプBによって汚染された血はなかなか元には戻らず、これがタイプB発症者やその家族が差別を受けたり、結婚が出来なくなる理由の一つになっている。
English: Thus, blood once ‘contaminated by Type B,’ as the phrase had it, did not readily return to its former state. This became one reason symptomatic Type Bs and their families suffered discrimination or found themselves unable to marry.

Japanese: ちなみに、我が家の母親はタイプBであったから、同じタイプBである妹の筱喬だけでなく、僕の傾向値もそれなりに高い。妹の筱喬は８００程度で、僕も５００は越えている。ノーマルでいられるギリギリの数値だ。僕くらいの傾向値でも発症する人はいるというから、ほとんどタイプBの世界に足を踏み入れていると言えるのかもしれない。傾向値の高いものを食べ続ければ僕もいつかタイプBになるだろう。
English: My own mother had been Type B. Consequently, not only my Type B sister Siu-kiu, but I myself possessed a fairly high tendency value. Siu-kiu’s was approximately eight hundred; mine exceeded five hundred, barely low enough for me to remain Normal. Some people were said to develop symptoms even at a value like mine, so perhaps I had already set foot in the Type B world. If I continued eating food with a high tendency value, I too would eventually become Type B.

Japanese: とにかく、タイプBというのは食べることでうつるのだ。
English: In short, Type B could be transmitted through eating.

Japanese: だから、今回このマウスに傾向値２７００もある餌を与え続ければ、当然その傾向値は高くなるだろう。そこは今回の実験にとって重要な部分ではない。問題は、傷がその場で治癒し、肉片になっても生き続ける、その異常な再生力が引き継がれるかという一点である。
English: Naturally, if these mice continued eating feed with a tendency value of twenty-seven hundred, their own values would rise. That was not the important part of this experiment. The sole question was whether they would inherit the extraordinary regenerative ability that healed wounds instantly and allowed separated pieces of flesh to remain alive.

Japanese: 一般的に、タイプBは普通の人間よりも怪我や病気の治りがいい。だから道夫なども誤解していたのだろうけれど、しかし、世間によくあるタイプBは、いくら傾向値が高くなとも肉片のまま動いて生き続けるなどということはありえない。
English: Type Bs were generally quicker than ordinary people to recover from injuries and illnesses. That was presumably why Michio and the others had misunderstood. But however high an ordinary Type B’s tendency value grew, its severed flesh could never continue moving and living on its own.

Japanese: この虎は、タイプBには違いないが、特殊なタイプBなのだ。その非常識さは、ある意味タイプAの超能力に通じるものがある。
English: This tiger was unquestionably Type B, but it was a special Type B. The sheer absurdity of its condition resembled, in one sense, the superhuman powers of Type A.

Japanese: タイプBはタイプAに比べればまだまともな研究がなされているが、この『特殊なタイプB』というものの存在は、世間ではそれほど認知されていない。ミュータントの研究は何かと秘匿されるものだから、どこかでは事実が認識され、こっそり研究されているのかもしれないが、そうだとしても僕らには知りようがない。少なくとも公開された研究論文にはそれについて書かれたものはないようだ。
English: Type B had at least been subjected to more serious research than Type A, yet the existence of these ‘special Type Bs’ was not widely recognized. Mutant research was forever being concealed. Perhaps someone, somewhere, knew the truth and studied it in secret, but we had no means of knowing. At the very least, no published research paper appeared to address it.

Japanese: だが、僕と汐さんはこの普通のタイプBと同じものとは言いがたい、『特殊なタイプB』が存在することを大分前から知っていた。そして検証実験も行っていたのだが、ある時を境に途絶えていた。今回の実験は、それらの結果を踏まえた上で、新しい結論を導くものでなくてはいけない。
English: Mr. Shio and I, however, had known for many years that there were ‘special Type Bs’ who could scarcely be described as the same thing as ordinary Type Bs. We had also conducted experiments to verify what we knew, until a certain event brought the work to a halt. This experiment would have to build upon those results and lead us to a new conclusion.

Japanese: 今までの実験では特殊性の再現を上手くコントロールすることが出来なかった。発生させられなかったわけではないが、条件がさっぱりわからなかったのである。
English: In the earlier experiments, we had failed to control the reproduction of the special trait. We had not been wholly unable to produce it, but had never understood the conditions.

Japanese: しかし今回の実験を始めるにあたって、一つ条件を仮定した。それが当たっていれば、この少ないマウスでも、一匹くらいは特殊化するかもしれない。
English: This time, before we began, we hypothesized one necessary condition. If the hypothesis was correct, even among this small number of mice, perhaps one would become special.

Japanese: まず、ノーマルラット三匹と、タイプBラット三匹を選び出し、それにシャーレのなかでうごめく、僕たちが　”コア組織”　と呼ぶ方の体細胞を摂取させた。ラットを一匹ずつ掴み、コア組織を口元にねじ込むようにして直接囓らせるのだ。
English: First, we selected three Normal mice and three Type B mice, then fed them the somatic cells writhing in a Petri dish—the material we called ‘core tissue.’ We grasped each mouse in turn, forced the core tissue up to its mouth, and made it gnaw the living tissue directly.

Japanese: この直接囓らせる、というのがこれまでと違う点だった。今までは、抜き取った特殊タイプBの血液を保管して、それを飼料に混ぜ込んで与えていた。しかし、生体を直接食べさせたらどうだろう？　これまでの失敗は、保存段階において、組織のなかの大事な要素が失われていたのかもしれない。もっとも新鮮なかたちで摂取させたら、また違った結果が出るのかもしれない。
English: Making them gnaw it directly was the departure from our previous method. Until now, we had stored blood drawn from a special Type B and mixed it into their feed. But what if we made them eat living tissue itself? Perhaps some vital element in the tissue had been lost during storage, causing our past failures. If they consumed it in the freshest possible form, perhaps the result would be different.

Japanese: 六匹に無理矢理食べさせると、コア細胞は綺麗になくなった。
English: Once we had forced all six to eat, the core tissue was completely gone.

Japanese: この六匹が、今回の実験の本命となる。
English: These six would be the principal subjects of this experiment.

Japanese: 次は、残ったマウスたちにあたえる飼料の作成作業を行わなくてはならない。
English: Next, we had to prepare the feed for the remaining mice.

Japanese: 冷凍していた虎の肉塊を洗浄し、汚れや痛みの酷い場所を切除して捨てると使用出来る部分は少なくなってしまう。
English: We washed the frozen mass of tiger meat, then cut away and discarded the worst of the dirt and decay. That left us with very little we could actually use.

Japanese: それを餌として切り分ける作業をしながら実験の展望について考えていると、非常に楽しかった。今僕は、ここ数日ずっと脳の中を支配していたYSだの龍頭だのという言葉が消え、純粋に科学について考えている。これは子供の頃から変わらない楽しみで、少年時代の僕をいつも救ってくれていたのを思い出す。やっぱり、これが僕の本当の人生なのかもしれない。
English: As I cut it into portions of feed and considered the experiment’s prospects, I found myself tremendously happy. The words YS and Longtou, which had ruled my mind for days, had vanished. Now I was thinking about science alone. It was the same pleasure I had known since childhood, the pleasure that had always saved me as a boy. Perhaps this really was my true life after all.

Japanese: そんなことを思い始めたころ、汐さんが口を開いた。
English: Just as that thought began to take hold, Mr. Shio spoke.

Japanese: 「昨日今日と、仕事の合間にな、この滑走路通りを襲った虎が、どこからやって来たのか調べていたんだ」
English: “Yesterday and today, in the time I could spare from work, I’ve been investigating where the tiger that attacked Runway Street came from.”

Japanese: 僕は彼の顔を見た。彼の視線はディスポの手袋をはめた自分の指先の作業に向けられたままだったので、僕も手元に視線を戻しながら聞く。
English: I looked at him. His gaze stayed fixed on what he was doing with his gloved hands, so I looked back down at my own work and listened.

Japanese: 「あのあと、西通りの方の一軒家で、壊れた鉄檻と、食い殺された老人が転がっているのが見つかったんだそうだ。虎は、おそらくそこで飼われていたんだろう」
English: “Afterward, they apparently found a broken iron cage and an old man who’d been killed and eaten at a house over on West Street. The tiger was probably being kept there.”

Japanese: 「どういう人だったの？」
English: “What kind of man was he?”

Japanese: 「フルカワって名前に記憶はないか？」
English: “Does the name Furukawa mean anything to you?”

Japanese: 「……いや、ちょっと思い出せないな……」
English: “...No, I can’t quite place it...”

Japanese: 「そうか。お前の父親ならよく知っているだろう。元々、YS、というか義勝でそれなりの地位にいたらしい。大分前に引退して、近くの主婦に乾物を売るような店をやって、のどかに暮らしていたようだ」
English: “I see. Your father would know him well. Apparently, he once held a fairly prominent position in YS—or rather, in Yisheng. He retired a long time ago and seems to have lived a quiet life, running a shop that sold dried goods to local housewives.”

Japanese: 「義勝時代の有力者だってことは、もしかして？」
English: “If he was an influential figure back in Yisheng’s day, then could it be...?”

Japanese: 「そうだよ。あの虎は『ローズ・クラブ』の虎だ。お前の想像は当たっていたんだ」
English: “Yes. That tiger came from the Rose Club. Your guess was right.”

Japanese: 汐さんが言うと、思わず僕の口から溜息がもれる。
English: At Mr. Shio’s words, a sigh escaped me.

Japanese: 『ローズ・クラブ』というのはかつてこの街にあった秘密クラブの名前だ。
English: The Rose Club was the name of a secret club that had once operated in this city.

Japanese: そこでは、普通の賭博、売春といったものだけではなく、もっとおぞましい様々なショーやサービスが提供されていた。それらは、特に選ばれた会員のみに利用を許されていたもので、その実態が明らかになったのはクラブがなくなって何年も経ってからのことだった。
English: It provided not only ordinary gambling and prostitution, but an array of far more appalling shows and services. Access to those was restricted to specially selected members, and the reality of what took place there did not come to light until many years after the club had disappeared.

Japanese: そうして、後年明らかになったものの一つに『死なない女』という残酷ショーがあった。
English: Among the things later brought to light was a brutal show called The Woman Who Wouldn’t Die.

Japanese: 内容はごくシンプルで、手足を鎖で縛り付けた女を生きたまま虎に食わせるというものなのだが、これがただの残酷ショーとちょっと違うのは、いくら食わせても女は死なないという点であった。
English: Its premise was perfectly simple: a woman was chained by her arms and legs and fed alive to a tiger. What made it a little different from an ordinary spectacle of cruelty was that no matter how much of her the tiger ate, the woman did not die.

Japanese: 体の半分も食われてしまったような状況でも、まるで活き作りの魚のように女は死なずに動き、そして一週間もすれば五体揃った健康な姿で客の前に姿を現す。
English: Even after half her body had been devoured, she would continue to move without dying, like fish served as live sashimi. A week later, she would appear before the guests again, healthy and whole in every limb.

Japanese: 当時はおなじ姿の女を何人も用意したというような噂も流れていたようだが、真実は、この女もまた『特殊なタイプB』だったのだろう。だとすれば松子となんらかの関係があったと予想されるが、今のところはっきりとした繋がりはない。
English: Rumors at the time apparently claimed that the club had prepared several identical-looking women. More likely, however, this woman had also been a special Type B. If so, one would expect some connection to Matsuko, though none had yet been established.

Japanese: 隆盛を誇った『ローズ・クラブ』は、その後義勝の龍頭であったクリス・ツェー、つまり若き日の僕の父によって壊滅させられることになる。
English: The once-prosperous Rose Club would later be destroyed by Chris Tse, Yisheng’s Longtou—in other words, my father as a young man.

Japanese: このとき、ショーで女の肉を食べていた虎が、義勝の幹部であったその老人に引き取られたのだとしたら？
English: What if the tiger that had eaten the woman’s flesh in that show was taken in afterward by the old man, who had been one of Yisheng’s senior members?

Japanese: そして、今目の前で僕らに切り刻まれている肉片になったのだとしたら？
English: And what if it had ended up as the pieces of meat Mr. Shio and I were now carving apart?

Japanese: 『特殊なタイプB』である女の肉を直接食べ続けた虎が、同じように『特殊なタイプB』であったわけだ。
English: That would mean a tiger which had continued to eat the flesh of a special Type B had itself become a special Type B.

Japanese: その情報は、僕と汐さんの仮定を補強するものだった。
English: The information strengthened the hypothesis Mr. Shio and I had formed.

Japanese: 「前よりもっと、うまくいきそうな気がしてきたよ」
English: “I’m starting to feel even more confident that this might work.”

Japanese: にわかに緊張を覚えながら、僕はすっかり乾いた口でそう言った。
English: My mouth had gone completely dry with sudden nervous excitement as I spoke.

Japanese: 「もしすべてがお前の想像通りだったらどうする？」
English: “What will you do if everything is exactly as you imagine?”

Japanese: 「どうするって、何が？」
English: “What do you mean, what will I do?”

Japanese: 「実験の結果がうまくいけば、我々は特殊化をある程度コントロール出来ることになる。そうしたら、人間にも使えるんじゃないか？　たとえば、体がグズグズと崩れ落ちるような末期患者でも、うまく特殊化させたならば、その再生力で生き延びられるかどうか……」
English: “If the experiment succeeds, we’ll have gained some measure of control over specialization. Couldn’t it then be used in humans? Take a terminal patient whose body is practically falling apart—if we could successfully make that person special, might that regenerative power keep them alive...?”

Japanese: 「ああ」
English: “Oh.”

Japanese: 真顔だったので気がつかなかったが、汐さんは父親のことで僕をからかっているのだと、そこまで聞いてやっと理解した。
English: His face had been so serious that I failed to notice at first, but only then did I realize Mr. Shio was teasing me about my father.

Japanese: 「そんなの、いくらなんでも時期尚早じゃないかな。今回うまくいっても、このサンプル数じゃ参考結果にしかならない。人にやるにはリスクも大きすぎるし、考えてみたこともなかった」
English: “Surely that’s far too premature. Even if this experiment works, a sample size this small will only give us a preliminary result. The risks of trying it on a human would be much too great. It never even occurred to me.”

Japanese: 僕は一旦はそう否定してみたものの、
English: That was my initial rejection of the idea, but then—

Japanese: 「……いや、そういうのもアリなのかな？」
English: “...No, wait. Maybe that is worth considering?”

Japanese: 「あっはははは」
English: “Ah-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

Japanese: 首をひねって考え直すと、珍しく汐さんが声を立てて笑った。
English: I cocked my head and reconsidered. Mr. Shio did something rare: he laughed aloud.

Japanese: すべての作業を終えた。こうして準備を終えたら、あとの細かい作業と定期的なデータ採取は、いつもこうした場合に汐さんが雇っているアルバイトがこなしてくれるだろう。
English: We finished our work. With the preparations complete, the remaining minor tasks and regular data collection could be left to the part-timer Mr. Shio always hired for experiments like this.

Japanese: そして実験室のフラスコでコーヒーを一杯入れて一息つくと、ちょうど松子が帰って来る時刻になっていた。僕らは地下室を出て、何食わぬ顔でリビングルームのテレビなどを見はじめる。
English: After brewing a cup of coffee in a laboratory flask and taking a short rest, we found it was almost time for Matsuko to return. We left the basement and began watching television in the living room with perfect innocence.

Japanese: ちょうどプロ野球の試合もはじまる頃合いで、汐さんは贔屓チームの選手たちのプレーにぶつくさ文句を言いながら、飲みかけだったウィスキーをまた飲み始める。
English: A professional baseball game was about to begin. Mr. Shio resumed drinking his unfinished whiskey while grumbling at the way his favorite team’s players performed.

Japanese: 野球にちっとも興味がない僕は、頬杖をついてなんとなく画面を眺めている。
English: I had no interest in baseball whatsoever, so I rested my cheek on one hand and vaguely watched the screen.

Japanese: 「ただいま」
English: “I’m home.”

Japanese: やがて松子が自前の買い物袋に近所で購入した食材を詰めて帰って来た。
English: Before long, Matsuko returned, carrying groceries from nearby shops in her own shopping bags.

Japanese: 「あ、もう二人揃っていたんですね！　これから急いで食事を作るので、待っていてください！」
English: “Oh, you’re both here already! I’ll hurry and make dinner, so please wait just a little!”

Japanese: 黙って野球観戦している二人の姿を認めると、パタパタとスリッパを鳴らしてキッチンへ去ってゆく。
English: At the sight of the two of us silently watching baseball, she pattered away to the kitchen, slippers clapping against the floor.

Japanese: 「そんなに急がなくてもいいよ」
English: “You don’t have to rush so much.”

Japanese: 僕は彼女の消えた方向に向かってそう声をかけた。
English: I called out in the direction she had disappeared.

Japanese: 「でも、腹ぺこですよね？」
English: “But you must be starving, aren’t you?”

Japanese: 「子供じゃないんだから、それくらい待てるよ」
English: “I’m not a child. I can wait that long.”

Japanese: 「ありがとうございます。でも、待たせるのはいやなんです」
English: “Thank you. But I don’t like to keep you waiting.”

Japanese: キッチンから食材の梱包などを剥がす物音がして、僕は渋々口を閉ざした。
English: I heard the sound of packages being opened in the kitchen and reluctantly held my tongue.

Japanese: 「亮、親父さんの状態はまずいのか？」
English: “Ryo, is your father in bad shape?”

Japanese: やりとりを黙って見ていた汐さんはそう尋ねる。
English: Mr. Shio, who had silently watched our exchange, asked.

Japanese: 「まあ良くはないです。……料理が出来るまで、一局どうです？」
English: “Well, he isn’t doing well. ...How about a game while dinner’s cooking?”

Japanese: 「やらん。お前と碁を打っても負けるだけだからな」
English: “No. If I play Go with you, I’ll only lose.”

Japanese: 汐さんは断固として首を横に振り、
English: Mr. Shio shook his head emphatically.

Japanese: 「おい、お前は、何があっても父親と同じ世界に足を踏み入れてはいかんぞ」
English: “Listen. Whatever happens, you must not set foot in the same world as your father.”

Japanese: 僕がそらそうとした話題を引き戻す。
English: He dragged the subject back from my attempt to divert it.

Japanese: こんな具合に汐さんが唐突に自分の考えを突きつけるのは今に始まったことではない。
English: This was hardly the first time Mr. Shio had confronted me with his views without warning.

Japanese: 「あんなのは、ろくな商売じゃない。人を脅したり騙したり、欲望につけこんで金を儲けるんだ」
English: “That is no decent line of work. You make money by threatening people, deceiving them, and taking advantage of their desires.”

Japanese: 「ろくな商売じゃないのは認めるけど、人を騙したり脅したり欲望につけこんだりって、どの商売でもおんなじじゃないかなあ……」
English: “I’ll grant you it isn’t a decent line of work. But threatening people, deceiving them, taking advantage of their desires... Isn’t every business the same in that respect?”

Japanese: 「まったく、屁理屈の好きな小僧だ。とにかく、犯罪はいかん。わかってるだろう？」
English: “Honestly, you argumentative little brat. The point is, crime is wrong. You do understand that, don’t you?”

Japanese: 「そりゃ、分かってるけれども」
English: “Of course I understand, but...”

Japanese: 何故か汐さんが、僕が父親の事業を引き継ぐことを前提に話をしている。僕は、そんなにも後を継ぎそうな雰囲気をだしていたのだろうか？
English: For some reason, Mr. Shio was speaking as though it were a foregone conclusion that I would inherit my father’s business. Had I really been giving off such a strong impression that I would succeed him?

Japanese: どうして急にこんな話題を選んだのか不思議だった。が、汐さんの唇から飛び出した次の言葉には、さらにもっと驚かされた。
English: I wondered why he had suddenly chosen this subject. But the next words out of his mouth startled me still more.

Japanese: 「なあ、お前、この際だから松と結婚しないか？」
English: “Listen, why don’t you take this opportunity to marry Matsu?”

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 思わず大きな声を出してしまうと、
English: My voice rose before I could stop it.

Japanese: 「どうしましたか？」
English: “Is something wrong?”

Japanese: 松子が向こうから質問してくる。
English: Matsuko called to us from the kitchen.

Japanese: 「いや、なんでもない！」
English: “No, it’s nothing!”

Japanese: 僕は慌てて松子にそう返してから、
English: I hurriedly called back to her.

Japanese: 「急に何を。この際って、どの際だかさっぱりわからない……」
English: “What brought this on? What ‘opportunity’ are you even talking about...?”

Japanese: 声をひそめて汐さんの裾を引いた。
English: Then I lowered my voice and tugged at Mr. Shio’s sleeve.

Japanese: 「身を固めないでふらふらしているから、ギャングのボスになろうなんて誘惑に取り憑かれるんだ。松を嫁に貰って家庭を持て。おれのあとを継げ。それが一番いい」
English: “You’re at loose ends because you refuse to settle down, and that’s why you’ve let yourself be seduced by the idea of becoming a gang boss. Take Matsu as your wife and start a family. Succeed me. That’s the best thing for you.”

Japanese: その声は普段喋っている通りのトーンで、松子に聞こえてしまわないか僕はどぎまぎしたが、彼は無頓着だった。
English: He said all this at his normal speaking volume. I fidgeted nervously at the thought that Matsuko might hear, but he paid it no mind.

Japanese: 「所帯を持ったら、二人で街を出ていって研究者なり会社員なりになってもいい。望むときだけおれの会社を継げばいい。学費を稼ぐっていうんで仕事を手伝って貰ったが、社員達にえらく評判がいいんだよ。謝亮って名前を捨てて、菅原亮としてうちに正式に入ってくれよ。そうして貰えればおれも安心だ。なあ、お前は親父さんと違うんだ。おれもそんなに真っ当な仕事をしてきたわけじゃないが、マフィアとかヤクザってのはきらいなんだよ」
English: “Once you’ve started a family, the two of you can leave the city and become researchers, office workers, whatever you please. You need only take over my company if the day comes when you want it. I had you help with the business because you said you needed money for tuition, and you’re remarkably popular with the employees. Give up the name Tse Leung and formally join us as Ryo Sugawara. If you did that, I could rest easy. Listen, you’re not your father. It isn’t as though all my own work has been respectable, but I despise the Mafia and the yakuza.”

Japanese: 「嫌いなのは知ってるよ」
English: “I know you do.”

Japanese: 僕は肩をすくめ、
English: I shrugged.

Japanese: 「この街でクリス・ツェーと汐健慈朗と言えば、押しも押されもしない暴力と金のビッグネームだ。その両方から後継者になれと言われるなんて光栄だ。まったく素晴らしい……と言いたいところだけど、どういう風の吹き回しなんだい？　本当に、突然どうしてしまったのさ。なんだか変じゃないか。結婚だのなんだの、今まで一言も言ったことないのに」
English: “In this city, Chris Tse and Kenjiro Shio are the two undisputed giants of violence and money. To have both ask me to become their successor is an honor. I’d love to say it’s all marvelous... but what brought this on? Honestly, why so sudden? You’re acting strange. You’ve never said a single word about marriage or anything like it before.”

Japanese: 「変でもなんでもない。お前が、おやじさんのあとを継ごうとしているからだ」
English: “There is nothing strange about it. I’m saying this because you intend to succeed your father.”

Japanese: 「まだ継ぐって、はっきり決まったわけじゃないけれど……」
English: “It hasn’t been definitively decided that I’ll succeed him...”

Japanese: 僕は肩をすくめて言った。
English: I said it with a shrug.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、継がないのか？」
English: “Then you won’t?”

Japanese: 汐さんにこれだけ言われれば、僕も本心を口にしないわけにはいかない。
English: After Mr. Shio had pressed me this far, I could hardly refuse to tell him what I truly intended.

Japanese: 「人に言うのは初めてだけど、YSには入るつもりだよ」
English: “I’ve never told anyone this before, but I do intend to join YS.”

Japanese: 「ほら、そうだろう。まったく、気の迷いとしか言いようがない。昔はギャングは嫌いだったのになあ。それに、科学者になって世界の真実を解き明かすってのが子供の頃からの夢だったじゃないか。忘れてしまったのか？」
English: “There, you see? I can only call this a moment of madness. You used to hate gangsters. And ever since you were a child, your dream was to become a scientist and uncover the truth of the world. Have you forgotten that?”

Japanese: 「忘れてないよ。……僕もよく考えたんだ。YSに入れば少なからず今あるものを捨てなければならなくなるのはわかってる。でもこれも運命なのかもしれないってね。僕のなかにこの血が流れている以上逃げ切るなんて出来ないのだろうし、逃げるのはあまり好きじゃない」
English: “I haven’t forgotten. ...I’ve given this a great deal of thought myself. I know that joining YS will mean giving up at least some of what I have now. But I wonder if this might be fate. As long as this blood runs through me, I doubt I could ever escape it completely—and I’ve never cared much for running away.”

Japanese: 「やりたいことをやるのは逃げじゃないさ。私も科学者をやめるとき、そんな風に自分に対して言い訳をしたものだ。でも今は後悔しているよ。こんな、企業の社長なんて、人生を無駄にしてしまった」
English: “Doing what you want with your life is not running away. When I left science, I made the same sort of excuse to myself. Now I regret it. Becoming the president of some company... I’ve wasted my life.”

Japanese: 「僕は汐さんの人生好きだよ」
English: “I like the life you’ve lived, Mr. Shio.”

Japanese: 「……私は失敗者だ」
English: “...I’m a failure.”

Japanese: 「僕はそうは思わない。それにね、結局のところ、僕が本当に何が好きなのかなんてわかりゃしないんだよ。僕は子供のころから色んなことを知りたかったのは確かだけど、それは科学者じゃなくてもいいってことに気がつき始めている。日々移り変わる景色をぼんやり眺めていたり、路地裏を散歩するだけでも学ぶことは多い。確かに、ここの地下室だったり、学校の研究室にいたりするのはすごく刺激的で楽しいけどね」
English: “I don’t think so. Besides, when all is said and done, I haven’t the slightest idea what I truly like. It’s true that I’ve wanted to learn all sorts of things since childhood, but I’m beginning to realize I don’t need to be a scientist to do that. There is plenty to learn just by idly watching the scenery change from day to day, or taking a walk through the back alleys. I admit that being here in this basement, or in the university laboratory, is tremendously exciting and enjoyable.”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、汐さんは暫く考えた後、
English: When I finished, Mr. Shio thought for a while before answering.

Japanese: 「……なあ亮よ。本気で裏社会の人間になってしまうのか？　そうして、私や松と別の世界に行ってしまうのか？　それはあまりに寂しすぎやしないか」
English: “...Tell me, Ryo. Do you truly mean to become a man of the underworld? To go away into a world apart from Matsu and me? Wouldn’t that be terribly lonely?”

Japanese: 「そうかもしれない。でも、それは季節が変わるようなものだよ。……それにそのうちギャングになるとしても、今はまだそうじゃない。本当にそうなってしまうまでは、今のままでいたいんだけど……だめかな？」
English: “Perhaps. But it would be no different from the changing of the seasons. ...Besides, even if I eventually become a gangster, I’m not one yet. Until the day it truly happens, I want to carry on just as I am now... Is that wrong?”

Japanese: 「それは構わないが……」
English: “No, I have no objection to that, but...”

Japanese: 汐さんは残念そうだった。
English: Mr. Shio looked disappointed.

Japanese: 松子と結婚し、研究をして暮らす。それが出来ればどれだけ平和で充実した毎日が送れるだろう。
English: To marry Matsuko and spend my life in research—how peaceful and fulfilling every day could be, if such a thing were possible.

Japanese: でもそれは出来ない。
English: But it was not possible.

Japanese: たとえば彼女自身が自分で言ったのならまだしも、こんな風に汐さんに言われてうんと言えるはずもない。
English: If she herself had said it, that might have been another matter. There was no way I could consent to a proposal made on her behalf by Mr. Shio.

Japanese: そして、僕はこの間「街を出て一緒に暮らそう」という提案を断られたばかりだ。
English: And only recently, she had rejected my suggestion that we leave the city and live together.

Japanese: そんなことを考えていると、キッチンの方からガシャガシャンと、金属で出来た何かを盛大にひっくり返す音が聞こえた。
English: As I thought about that, a tremendous metallic clatter sounded from the kitchen, as though something had been knocked completely over.

Japanese: すぐに立ち上がって駆けつけると、松子が床に座り込んで、手を押さえている。その付近には、刻まれた野菜が散乱し、銀色のボールがひっくり返っている。
English: I leapt up and ran in. Matsuko sat on the floor, clutching one hand. Chopped vegetables lay scattered around her, and a metal mixing bowl had overturned nearby.

Japanese: 「怪我をしたのか？」
English: “Are you hurt?”

Japanese: 尋ねると、彼女は恥ずかしそうにうつむき、
English: At my question, she lowered her head in embarrassment.

Japanese: 「すみません。馬鹿なんです。買い物袋の端が引っかかっていたのに気づかずに引っ張ったら、お皿とかが全部ひっくりかえってしまって……。お皿はなんとか落ちる前に助けられたんですが……」
English: “I’m sorry. That was so stupid of me. The edge of a shopping bag had caught on something, and I pulled without noticing, so all the dishes and everything went flying... I managed to save the plates before they hit the floor, but...”

Japanese: そして僕に、左手の指の股の間に挟んだ三枚の皿を見せる。落ちようとしている皿を片手で三枚掴むというのは、他の人間にはなかなか出来ない芸当だろう。
English: She showed me three plates wedged between the fingers of her left hand. Snatching three falling plates with one hand was a feat few other people could have managed.

Japanese: その一方で体の影に隠そうとしていた右手を取ると、固く握りしめた指の間から止めどもなく血液が流れ出ていた。
English: I took the right hand she had been trying to hide behind her body. Blood streamed between her tightly clenched fingers without stopping.

Japanese: 「手を開いて見せて」
English: “Open your hand and let me see.”

Japanese: 言うと松子は渋々右手のひらを開く。それぞれの指の内側に、ぱっくりと切れ目が刻まれ、そこから血液があふれている。
English: At my instruction, Matsuko reluctantly opened her right palm. Deep cuts gaped along the inside of every finger, blood welling from each one.

Japanese: 「お皿の方に集中していたら、うっかり包丁を握ってキャッチしてしまって……。ごめんなさい。こんなに割ったり、汚したりして……」
English: “I was concentrating on the plates, and I accidentally grabbed the knife by the blade... I’m sorry. I’ve broken things and made such a mess of everything...”

Japanese: 「包丁とか皿とか落としたって大したことじゃないんだから」
English: “Dropping a knife or a few dishes is no great disaster.”

Japanese: 僕はひとまず溜息をつく。
English: For the moment, I let out a sigh.

Japanese: 「ほんとうに、恥ずかしいです」
English: “It really is so embarrassing.”

Japanese: 彼女は肩をすくめてばつが悪そうにする。
English: She hunched her shoulders, looking deeply uncomfortable.

Japanese: 松子の場合、このくらいの傷ならば何も心配する必要はない。
English: With Matsuko, an injury of this degree was no cause for concern.

Japanese: その証拠として、こうして眺めている間にも、傷はみるみるうちにふさがってゆく。
English: Indeed, even as we watched, the wounds rapidly closed before our eyes.

Japanese: そして二十秒ほどしてから血を拭き取ると、もうどこを見ても肌の上に傷を見つけ出すことが出来なかった。
English: After about twenty seconds, I wiped away the blood. There was no longer a wound to be found anywhere on her skin.

Japanese: それから二日、昼は汐家にマウスの状態を観察しに行き、夜はホテルに帰って寝た。
English: For the next two days, I visited the Shio residence by day to observe the mice and returned to the hotel to sleep at night.

Japanese: いつ父の容体の変化などがあるかもわからず、いざというときにわかりやすい場所にいた方が良いだろうというつもりだったが、特に何事もなかった。
English: My father’s condition might change at any time, and I thought it best to remain somewhere easy to find in case of an emergency. Nothing in particular happened, however.

Japanese: 一方、実験の方は早くも変化があらわれていた。
English: The experiment, on the other hand, was already producing changes.

Japanese: 死んだ肉を与えた１４匹のマウスたちは、１００から２００傾向値が上昇した。これは、特殊なタイプBを用いなくとも、ごく普通のタイプB傾向値の高い食物を与えた時でも起こる普通の現象である。
English: The fourteen mice fed the dead flesh experienced increases of one to two hundred in their tendency values. This was an ordinary phenomenon, one that also occurred when mice were given ordinary feed with a high Type B tendency value, without any special Type B being involved.

Japanese: そして、そのマウスたちには傾向値が上がった他にはなんの変化もみられなかった。
English: Those mice exhibited no change other than the rise in tendency value.

Japanese: 問題は、コア組織を与えた六匹のマウスだ。
English: The question was what had happened to the six fed the core tissue.

Japanese: 「おい、やっぱり効果覿面だ」
English: “Just as we thought—the effect is unmistakable.”

Japanese: その日汐邸を訪れた僕に、汐さんは若干興奮した面持ちでそう告げた。
English: Mr. Shio greeted me with those words when I visited his home that day, a trace of excitement on his face.

Japanese: 「何か特別なことが起こったの？」
English: “Has something unusual happened?”

Japanese: 「起こったとも。まあ、来てくれ」
English: “It certainly has. Come along.”

Japanese: 僕は早速地下の研究室に降りた。
English: I immediately followed him down to the basement laboratory.

Japanese: コア細胞を与えたマウスは一匹ずつ別々のケージに入れられている。その計六つのケージは、研究室中央のテーブルの上に並べられていた。
English: Each mouse fed the core tissue had been placed in a separate cage. The six cages stood in a row on the table at the center of the laboratory.

Japanese: そのゲージのうち、僕が到着した時点でなかにマウスが入っていたのはわずかに二つであった。残りのゲージはすでに空で、中で過ごしていたマウスたちはゲージの脇に置かれた金属トレイの上で死体となって並べられ、足にはタグが付けられている。
English: By the time I arrived, only two of those cages still contained mice. The others were already empty. Their former occupants lay dead on a metal tray beside the cages, tags fastened to their legs.

Japanese: 生き残った二匹のマウスも、あきらかに以前とは様子が違っていた。
English: The two survivors were also plainly different from before.

Japanese: 一匹は、僕たちの姿を見ると狂ったようにゲージのなかを走り回り、明らかな興奮を見せている。もう一匹は、ゲージの隅の方に蹲り、体を膨らませたりしぼませたりして深い呼吸を行っている。
English: One caught sight of us and raced madly around its cage, visibly agitated. The other crouched in a corner, its body expanding and contracting with deep breaths.

Japanese: そして両方とも、その瞳を金色に輝かせていた。
English: Both had eyes that shone gold.

Japanese: 「なるほど……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 僕はある程度自体を察し、頷く。
English: I understood enough to nod.

Japanese: 「録画によると、摂取して三十三時間程度で相次いで反応が出ている。死んだマウスは、平均して１０００程度傾向値が上がっている。ノーマルマウスはすべて金眼現象が現れてタイプBになり、タイプBマウスは二匹が異常動作により発症が確認され、その一時間後に死んだ」
English: “According to the recordings, the reactions began one after another approximately thirty-three hours after ingestion. The dead mice showed an average increase of about one thousand in tendency value. All the Normal mice exhibited golden eyes and became Type B. Two of the Type B mice displayed abnormal behavior confirming the onset of symptoms, then died an hour later.”

Japanese: 汐さんは端末を操作し、時系列に並べられた観察記録を読み上げる。
English: Mr. Shio operated the terminal and read aloud from the observational record arranged in chronological order.
