English: “I will tell you all about that brat later. First, answer my question. What do you plan to do now?”

Japanese: 「警察には突き出さない」
English: “We won’t hand you over to the police.”

Japanese: 「あなたは好きに生きればいいわ」
English: “Live however you like.”

Japanese: 私たちはそう言った。彼は片方の眉をつり上げ、少し驚いたような顔をする。
English: When we said this, he raised one eyebrow, looking slightly surprised.

Japanese: 「あなたが誰を殺そうが私たちには関係がないもの。殺すしかないならそうすればいい」
English: “We do not care whom you kill. If you have no choice but to kill, then go ahead.”

Japanese: 「世の中で一番の罪は、人を殺すことじゃなくて、自分を殺すことでしょう？」
English: “The greatest sin in the world isn’t killing another person, but killing yourself. Isn’t that so?”

Japanese: 「あなたは人殺しとして生まれたんだから、自信をもって人殺しとしてのくだらない人生を送ればいいのよ。人殺しのくせに、善人のフリして自分の悪口を言うだなんて卑怯だわ。本当は自分のこと大好きなくせに」
English: “You were born a murderer, so hold your head high and live your worthless life as one. It is cowardly to be a murderer, pretend to be good, and badmouth yourself. You adore yourself, really.”

Japanese: 「好き勝手に生きて、そして最後は人殺しとして残酷でむごいやりかたで殺されればいいじゃない」
English: “Live exactly as you please. Then, in the end, be killed as a murderer in some cruel and brutal fashion.”

Japanese: 「私たち、どんなものにも善悪なんか決めるつもりはない」
English: “We have no intention of judging anything as good or evil.”

Japanese: 「ただ色んなことを、もっとよく知りたいの」
English: “We just want to understand all kinds of things better.”

Japanese: 「それに、あなた、ちょっと私たちの友達に似てるわ」
English: “Besides, you resemble one of our friends a little.”

Japanese: 「はっはっはっ」
English: “Hahahaha.”

Japanese: 彼は声を立てて笑った。
English: He laughed aloud.

Japanese: 「よく喋るガキだな。その好奇心は必ずおまえたちを殺すだろう」
English: “You brats sure talk a lot. That curiosity will get you killed one day.”

Japanese: 「そんなことはどうでもいい」
English: “That doesn’t matter.”

Japanese: 「とにかく答えたよ。だからこっちの疑問にもこたえて」
English: “Anyway, we answered you. Now answer us.”

Japanese: 「ふむ……ちょっと待て」
English: “Hmm... Wait a moment.”

Japanese: 彼はそう言い、顎を傾けて視線を中空にやった。
English: He tilted his chin and turned his gaze toward empty air.

Japanese: 「どうする？　……ああ、そうか。わかった」
English: “What should we do? ...Ah. I see. Understood.”

Japanese: 彼は独り言のように、空に向かって喋る。
English: He addressed the air as though talking to himself.

Japanese: そこで使われた言葉は、サーシェンカが使ったものと同じ言葉だった。
English: He used the same language Sashenka had spoken.

Japanese: 「本来ならおまえたちは始末すべき対象となんだが、あのガキのお気に入りだし、危害もなさそうなので、特別に生かしておくそうだ」
English: “Ordinarily, you would be targets for disposal. But apparently you are that brat’s favorites and pose no danger, so an exception will be made and you will be left alive.”

Japanese: その口ぶりは自信と落ち着きに満ちたものだ。
English: He spoke with complete confidence and composure.

Japanese: 私たちのタイプAとしての『ちから』は知らないとしても、タイプBとしての身体能力を見た上でこう言っているのだから、彼も何か特別な力を隠しているのだろうと私たちは考えたが、いまここでそれを詮索しようとは思わなかった。
English: We assumed he knew nothing of our Type A ‘power.’ Yet he had said this after seeing our physical abilities as Type Bs, so we suspected that he too was concealing some special power. We had no desire to investigate it here and now.

Japanese: 「それは光栄だね」
English: “That is an honor.”

Japanese: 「で、私たちへの質問の答えは？」
English: “And the answers to our questions?”

Japanese: 「まあ焦るな。今あのガキを連れてきてやる。それを見れば、おれたちの関係はよくわかるだろう」
English: “Do not be so impatient. I will bring the brat here now. Once you see that, our relationship should be clear.”

Japanese: 「待ってよ。あなたは何者なの？」
English: “Wait. Who are you?”

Japanese: 「人にはコシチェイと呼ばれている。……今はそれだけで充分だろう」
English: “People call me Koschei. ...That is enough for now.”

Japanese: 彼はそう言うと、ガクンとうなだれた。
English: After he spoke, his head dropped abruptly.

Japanese: 突然気を失ったように見えた。
English: It appeared that he had suddenly lost consciousness.

Japanese: そしてそのまま動かない。
English: He remained motionless.

Japanese: 驚いた私たちが声をかけようとしたとき、その姿に変化が起きた。
English: As we prepared to call out in surprise, his appearance began to change.

Japanese: 彼の髪型が金髪の癖っけに変わり、若干からだが縮んで、全体的に細くもなった。
English: His hair became blond and wavy. His body shrank slightly and grew slender overall.

Japanese: そして、彼はゆっくりと顔を上げる。
English: Then he slowly raised his face.

Japanese: 「「サーシェンカ！」」
English: “Sashenka!”

Japanese: 私たちは同時に叫んだ。
English: We shouted together.

Japanese: 「……あれ、ここは……」
English: “...Huh? Where am I...?”

Japanese: 眠そうにまぶたを擦る彼は、どこからどう見ても、さっき上の階のベッドの上に置いてきたはずのサーシェンカそのものだった。
English: He rubbed his eyelids sleepily. However we looked at him, he was unmistakably the Sashenka we believed we had left on the upstairs bed moments before.

Japanese: 「老人達ははまだ連絡をよこさない。彼らは新体制に従うつもりがないのでしょうか」
English: “The Elders still haven’t contacted us. Do they intend to refuse the new regime?”

Japanese: ジェフリー・ウォンは苛立ちを隠せずそう言った。
English: Jeffrey Wong spoke without concealing his irritation.

Japanese: クリス・ツェーが息を引き取った居室は、そのまま二代目の執務室となっている。
English: The room in which Chris Tse had breathed his last had been left intact and made into the second Longtou’s office.

Japanese: 遺言によってクリスの叔父であるマイケル・ツェーが龍頭となった。そして、いよいよ本格的に執務を行うこととなった彼は、この部屋で部下の報告を受けたり、来客の対応を行っている。
English: Chris’s will had made his uncle, Michael Tse, the Longtou. Now that he had begun attending to his duties in earnest, it was here that he received reports from subordinates and met with visitors.

Japanese: といっても、実際にそれらの仕事を行っているのは父の義兄弟であり腹心であったジェフリー・ウォンだ。僕も立場的には彼と同じ補佐官ということになっていたが、実際は見習いのようなものだ。ジェフリーの側にいてその仕事ぶりを見学することが仕事だった。
English: In reality, however, Jeffrey Wong performed that work. He had been Father’s sworn brother and closest aide. My formal position made me an adviser just as he was, but in practice, I was more of an apprentice. My work consisted of remaining at Jeffrey’s side and watching him work.

Japanese: ようするに何もしなくていいということで、なかなか良い身分である。個人的には時間の無駄のようにも思えるが、この配置が父の遺言だそうだから、当面は大人しくつき合うほかないのだろう。
English: In other words, I was required to do nothing—an enviable position. Personally, it struck me as a waste of time, but I was told that Father had arranged it in his will. For the present, I would presumably have to go along with it quietly.

Japanese: その僕の教師であるべきジェフリーが、どうもイライラと感情的になっている。
English: Yet Jeffrey, who was supposed to serve as my teacher, seemed irritable and emotional.

Japanese: 「昨日の今日だし、そう焦る必要はないのでは？」
English: “It only happened yesterday. Is there any need for such haste?”

Japanese: 黙っているつもりだったが、ジェフリーの苛立ちが尋常じゃなかったので、言わないわけにはいかなかった。
English: I had intended to remain silent, but Jeffrey was so agitated that I could hardly keep from speaking.

Japanese: そんな僕を、彼は苦々しく見て、
English: He gave me a bitter look.

Japanese: 「老人達には他の重要人物と同様、真っ先に連絡をしています。それが、葬儀にも来ず、就任式にもあらわれず、そして未だに連絡がない。これは、我々を軽く見ているということなのですよ」
English: “We contacted the Elders before anyone else, together with the other important figures. Yet they did not attend the funeral, did not appear at the installation, and have yet to reply. They are treating us with contempt.”

Japanese: 「軽く見ている、というより、まだ様子見をしているんだろう」
English: “Rather than contempt, I imagine they are waiting to see what happens.”

Japanese: YSの新体制がどのように動くのか、老人達はそれを決めるために、我々の様子を観察しているのだと思う。
English: I believed the Elders were observing us so they could decide how to respond to the new YS regime.

Japanese: 「状況によってつき合い方を変えようと考えていること自体、我々を軽く見ているということです」
English: “The very fact that they intend to alter their relationship with us according to circumstances means that they hold us in contempt.”

Japanese: 「だって、それは当然だよ。だから我々は……」
English: “But that is only natural. Which is why we must—”

Japanese: 「小謝、あなたはまだ余計な口出しをしなくて結構。しばらくは黙ってやり方を見ていてください。とにかく、状況は思ったよりもよくありません。我々が影響力を失えば、街の外の連中もこの街へ手を出すでしょう。先代が友好関係を築いた者達も、こうなればいつ手のひらを返すかわかりません。我々は、先代がなくとも以前と同じ力を持っていることを証明しなくてはいけないのです」
English: “Siu Tse, there is no need for you to offer unnecessary opinions yet. For a time, remain silent and observe how matters are handled. In any event, the situation is worse than we anticipated. If we lose our influence, outsiders will begin making moves on the city. Even the people with whom the former Longtou established friendly relations may turn upon us at any moment. We must demonstrate that we possess the same power as before, even without him.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは眉間にしわをよせ考え始める。
English: Jeffrey began to think, creases drawn between his brows.

Japanese: 余計な口出しをするなとはよく言ったものだ。腹が立たないでもなかったが、それよりも驚きが先に立った。
English: He had some nerve telling me not to interfere. I was angry too, of course, but surprise came first.

Japanese: 父の側近として振る舞っていたときは、もっと冷静な印象だった。今が我々にとって簡単な状態ではないのはわかるが、そんなことは事前に予想出来たわけだし、今更ぴりぴりするのは遅すぎる。
English: When he had acted as Father’s aide, I had thought him far calmer. I understood that our present position was difficult, but the difficulty had been predictable. It was rather late to become so overwrought now.

Japanese: クリス・ツェーという絶対的な信頼を抱いていた義兄弟を失ったことが、彼に不要のプレッシャーを与えているのかもしれない。
English: Perhaps the loss of Chris Tse, the sworn brother he had trusted absolutely, had placed him under needless pressure.

Japanese: とにかく、ジェフリーは今日は朝からずっとイライラとしっぱなしだ。
English: Whatever the reason, Jeffrey had remained irritable since morning.

Japanese: ジェフリーの不快の原因は、今話題にした老人達だけではない。
English: The Elders were not his only source of displeasure.

Japanese: 就任の儀式時の、壬生屋タカシがマイケル・ツェーにとった不遜な態度や、儀式が終わるや否や、その後の宴会に参加せずにさっさと帰ってしまった廖志明の振る舞いやら、数え上げればきりがないようだ。
English: There was Takashi Mibuya’s insolent behavior toward Michael Tse at the installation, and Liao Chi-ming’s departure immediately after the ceremony without attending the banquet. The list, apparently, had no end.

Japanese: 明白な権威の衰えに焦る気持ちはわからなくもないが、それも予想していたことのはずだ。
English: I could understand his fixation upon the obvious decline in our authority, but surely we had expected that as well.

Japanese: 名目上の最高責任者である第二代龍頭マイケル・ツェーは事情が分かっているのかどうなのか、のほほんとした顔で苛立つジェフリーを眺めている。
English: Michael Tse, the nominal supreme authority and second Longtou, watched the irritated Jeffrey with a placid expression that gave no sign whether he understood the situation.

Japanese: 「龍頭は、何か意見はないのですか？」
English: “Does the Longtou have no opinion?”

Japanese: 僕が尋ねてみても、
English: Even when I asked him directly, all he offered was this smiling reply.

Japanese: 「いやあ、執務に関してはすべてウォン君に任せているから。彼がうまいことやってね、小謝にいいかたちで繋いでくれれば良い。私はただのつなぎだからね」
English: “Well, I’ve entrusted all administrative work to Wong. He need only handle it properly, then hand everything over to Siu Tse in good order. I am merely a bridge between the two of you.”

Japanese: ニコニコとそんなことを答えるだけで、まるきり頼りにならない。
English: He was completely useless.

Japanese: ともかく、何も苛立つことも驚くこともなく、すべてが予想通りに運んでいるのに今更何を苛立っているのか。
English: In any case, everything was proceeding exactly as expected, with nothing that ought to have surprised or irritated us. Why become irritated now?

Japanese: さて、今の僕はこうしてぼんやりと無為にジェフリーの側に突っ立っているわけだが、今の僕の仕事がこれだけで、他にまるきり何もしていないというわけではない。
English: At present, then, I spent my time standing idly at Jeffrey’s side. That did not mean this nominal position as adviser was my only work, or that I did nothing else at all.

Japanese: YSの龍頭の地位こそマイケル・ツェーが引き継いだが、ツェー・ファミリーつまり旧『義勝』の盟主は僕ということになっている。挨拶回りというわけではないが、彼らにあらためて自分の新しい立場を説明し、また彼らの考えや人柄を知っておくために空いている時間は彼らの元を訪ねた。
English: Michael Tse had inherited the position of Longtou of YS, but I had become head of the Tse Family—in other words, the old Yisheng. It was not precisely a formal round of greetings, but whenever time permitted, I visited its members to explain my new position and learn their thoughts and characters.

Japanese: それまで見向きもしなかったのに急に後継者としてＹＳに入った僕を、まず自分の足場となるべき旧義勝の面々がどう受け止めているのか、まず何よりも、それを把握したかったのだ。
English: Until now, I had paid them no attention, then abruptly entered YS as the successor. Before all else, I wanted to understand how the old Yisheng—the base I would have to rely on—regarded me.

Japanese: これは、なかなか発見があり、刺激的な仕事だった。
English: I learned a remarkable amount from the work and found it stimulating.

Japanese: 彼らの多くは血の繋がりがあったり、父と出身地を同じくするものばかりで、幼い頃から顔見知りといっていいような人間ばかりだったが、新しい立場で出会うと、意外なほどにYSの他ファミリーに対して敵愾心が強かった。
English: Most were blood relatives or came from the same region as Father, and nearly all had known me since childhood. Yet approaching them in my new position revealed a hostility toward the other families of YS far stronger than I had imagined.

Japanese: 父がYSという連合組織を作る前の敵対時の怒りや憎しみは、長い時間をおいてもそのまま保存されており、その死によってまた言葉や態度としてあらわれるようになったのだろうか。
English: Had the anger and hatred from the days of conflict before Father created the YS alliance remained preserved through all those years, only to emerge again in words and behavior upon his death?

Japanese: そうして、彼らが皆ジェフリーの強硬な態度を絶賛しているのを知ってしまうと、僕から見ればときに不自然にも思えるジェフリーの態度は、こうしたファミリーの空気に後押しされてのものだったのだと納得がいった。
English: Once I learned that every one of them acclaimed Jeffrey’s hard line, I understood that his behavior—which sometimes appeared unnatural to me—grew out of this atmosphere within the family.

Japanese: 僕は父の死後、他のファミリーの動向ばかり気にしていたが、自分の地盤である旧義勝そのものも排他的な集団へかわろうとしているのだ。いや、もともとそういう集団であったのは間違いないが。
English: After Father’s death, I had concerned myself almost entirely with the movements of the other families. But my own base, the old Yisheng itself, was transforming into an exclusionary group. Or rather, there could be no doubt that it had always been one.

Japanese: とまれ、YSの各所で激しい感情が醸成されている。
English: In short, fierce emotions were brewing throughout YS.

Japanese: それまでは大きな衝突はなんとか避けられるのではないかという思いが頭のどこかにあったが、こうした経験を経て、僕の頭からもその考えはもう消え去っていた。
English: Somewhere in my mind, I had continued to think that a major conflict might somehow be avoided. After these experiences, that belief vanished even from me.

Japanese: そうして僕は日々街をうろついていたが、新入りの僕がしなくてはならない仕事はそれだけではない。ファミリーが持つ資産の内容、ファミリーで行っているあらゆる経済活動の収支報告書……直接経営する飲食店やカジノの帳簿や、用心棒代やら各種設備のリース料やらというかたちで徴収されるみかじめ料に関する帳簿、正式な書類がなければメモでもかまわないが、とにかく手に入る限りの書類を集め、それに目を通していた。
English: I spent my days walking throughout the city, but those visits were not my only obligation as a newcomer. I gathered every document I could obtain and read through them: inventories of the family’s assets; statements for every part of its economic activity; ledgers from the restaurants and casinos it operated directly; ledgers for protection money collected in the form of security fees, equipment leases, and so forth. If no formal record existed, even a memorandum would do.

Japanese: とにかく僕には情報が足りない。その他、自分のファミリーだけでなく、YS全体や、他のファミリーの状況まで把握しようとすれば、書類の山が出来る。
English: Above all, I lacked information. If I meant to grasp the state not only of my own family, but of YS as a whole and each of its other families, the papers formed a mountain.

Japanese: 空いた時間を使って少しずつ情報を崩しているのだが、それでも時間が足りない。正直言って、名目だけの補佐官としてぼんやりジェフリーの側に突っ立っている時間が一番不必要に思えるのだが、そういうわけにもいかない。
English: I worked through the information little by little whenever I had an empty moment, but there was never enough time. Frankly, the hours I spent standing vacantly beside Jeffrey as an adviser in name alone seemed the most unnecessary of all. Yet there was nothing I could do about them.

Japanese: ろくに睡眠時間もとれないような忙しい時間を過ごしはじめたところで、一つ事件が持ち上がった。
English: Just as my days became so busy that I could scarcely find time to sleep, an incident arose.

Japanese: 新龍頭が就任してから三日が過ぎた日の夕暮れのことである。
English: It was evening, three days after the new Longtou’s installation.

Japanese: クリス・ツェーの資産整理について話し合っていたところ、何やら重要な電話が入ったと、先代の死後も引き続き龍頭の従者のような仕事をしているレイレイが取り次いだ。
English: We were discussing the disposition of Chris Tse’s estate when Leilei, who had continued serving the Longtou as an attendant after the former Longtou’s death, announced that an apparently important call had come in.

Japanese: 相手は、暗闇通りでいくつかの飲食店を営む有力オーナーである。
English: The caller was an influential proprietor who operated several restaurants on Darkness Street.

Japanese: 「それは、本当のことですか？」
English: “Is that true?”

Japanese: 電話を受けたジェフリーが青筋の入った額にしわを寄せる。
English: Jeffrey took the call with a furrowed brow and a vein standing out on his forehead.

Japanese: 通話を切ったあと、彼は苦い顔で事態を説明した。
English: After ending it, he explained the circumstances with a bitter expression.

Japanese: 「どうも、劉建志が酔っ払って、店で大暴れをしたようです」
English: “It appears Ryu Kenshi became drunk and went on a rampage in an establishment.”

Japanese: 暗闇通りのバーで一人で酒を飲んでいた劉建志が他の客の連れていた女に声をかけ、怒った客と大げんかをしたらしい。
English: Ryu had been drinking alone in a bar on Darkness Street when he tried to pick up a woman accompanying another patron, apparently provoking an enormous fight with the angry man.

Japanese: トレードマークの仮面をしていなかったらしく、その時点では客も店員も彼の正体に気がつかなかった。
English: He had not been wearing his trademark mask, so neither the patrons nor the employees recognized him at first.

Japanese: そうして、泥酔したとはいえ腕っ節の強い劉建志はさんざんに相手をやっつけ、喧嘩相手は女を置いて命からがら逃げ出したのだが、店の設備を破損し、相手の血で汚し、大変な有様だったという。
English: Drunk though he was, Ryu Kenshi possessed tremendous strength. He beat the other man severely, and his opponent fled for his life, abandoning the woman. The struggle damaged the establishment and splattered it with the man’s blood, leaving a dreadful scene behind.

Japanese: それについて店主が苦情を言うと、彼はこの店主も殴り倒し、そして堂々と自分の名を告げ、奪い取った女をさらうようにしてその場を去った。
English: When the proprietor complained, Ryu beat him down as well, proclaimed his own name, and left with the woman he had taken, practically abducting her.

Japanese: 「ひどいなあ。被害者には気の毒だが、劉建志らしい話だ」
English: “How awful. I feel sorry for his victims, but it sounds exactly like Ryu Kenshi.”

Japanese: 僕は思わず笑ってしまったが、ジェフリーはその失笑に溜息をつき、首を横に振る。
English: I laughed despite myself. Jeffrey sighed at my laughter and shook his head.

Japanese: 「とんでもない。無用の私闘はYSの掟に反しています。これは懲罰ものですよ」
English: “This is no laughing matter. Pointless private violence violates the rules of YS. He must be punished.”

Japanese: 「この街で長く暮らしているけど、私闘を禁じてるなんてはじめて知った。構成員がしょっちゅう市民と喧嘩してるじゃないか」
English: “I’ve lived in this city a long time, but this is the first I’ve heard that private fights are forbidden. Members are constantly fighting with ordinary citizens.”

Japanese: 「YSが侮辱されたり、正当な理由があれば不問です。しかし、酒で酔って女を奪おうと喧嘩をふっかけるなど、ありえないことです。そもそも部下も連れずに一人でふらりと飲みに行くのがあまりに不用意です。劉建志はただのチンピラではなく、YSの重要な立場にある人間です。こんなくだらないことで騒ぎを起こすようでは、とてもその地位に相応しいとは言えません」
English: “If YS has been insulted, or if there is a legitimate reason, we do not intervene. But drunkenly starting a fight to take a woman is unthinkable. It was grossly careless for him to wander off drinking alone without even taking subordinates. Ryu Kenshi is no common thug; he occupies an important position in YS. If he causes disturbances over something so trivial, he cannot possibly be considered worthy of that position.”

Japanese: 「それはもっともだ。けれど、街の人間は劉建志が昔どういう人間だかみんな知っている。今更評判どうこうって話でもない。そもそも、彼は先代の死を悲しむあまり飲み過ぎたんだろう」
English: “That is fair. But everyone in the city knows what kind of man Ryu Kenshi used to be. It is hardly a question of his reputation at this late date. Besides, he probably drank too much because the former Longtou’s death grieved him.”

Japanese: 「それは理由にはなりません。幹部としての振るまいが出来ないのならば、ふさわしい地位に戻って貰うだけです。そもそも彼は、最初から器ではなかったのです」
English: “That is no excuse. If he cannot conduct himself as an officer, he need only be returned to a rank appropriate for him. He never possessed the stature for his position in the first place.”

Japanese: ジェフリーが異様な緊張感でこわばった顔でそう言った。幹部に対する降格人事というのは、やはり彼をしても気が張り詰める仕事なのだろう。
English: Jeffrey’s face was rigid with an unusual tension as he spoke. Even he must have found it nerve-racking to demote an officer.

Japanese: 彼はすぐに龍頭であるマイケル・ツェーの名で劉建志を呼び出した。
English: He immediately summoned Ryu Kenshi in the name of Michael Tse, the Longtou.

Japanese: すると、劉建志は一時間ほどで執務室に姿を現す。
English: Ryu appeared in the office about an hour later.

Japanese: この日はトレードマークの仮面を身につけており、その表情こそ窺えなかったが、背を丸めてポケットに手を突っ込むという姿でマイケル・ツェーの前に立ち、自分の不機嫌さを隠そうともしなかった。
English: That day he wore his trademark mask, concealing his expression. Even so, he made no attempt to hide his displeasure as he stood before Michael Tse, back bent and hands thrust into his pockets.

Japanese: 「なんで呼び出したか、聞いていますね？」
English: “You have been told why you were summoned, I assume.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは感情の消え失せた冷たい表情でそう尋ねた。
English: Jeffrey asked with a cold, impassive expression.

Japanese: 「さっぱりわかりませんね」
English: “I haven’t the faintest idea.”

Japanese: 劉はふてくされているようだった。
English: Ryu appeared sullen.

Japanese: 「先日、飲食店で狼藉を働いた件に関してです」
English: “It concerns your misconduct at an establishment the other day.”

Japanese: 「記憶にありませんな。どこからそんな話を聞いたんです？」
English: “I don’t recall any misconduct. Where did you hear such a story?”

Japanese: 「どこかは言えませんが、苦情が上がっているのは確かです。それに、現場には多くの目撃者がいます。我々としては無視出来ない案件です」
English: “I cannot reveal the source, but I can say with certainty that a complaint was made. There were also many witnesses. We cannot ignore this affair.”

Japanese: 「ああ、なるほど。オーナーのヤンか。やっぱりそうですか。ねえ、あいつの店の集金は、うちがやってるんですよ？　文句があるならおれに直接来いと言ったのに。あの野郎、普段おれにおべっかばっかりつかってるくせに、くだらない告げ口なんかしやがって」
English: “Ah, I see. Yang, the proprietor. I thought so. Listen, my family collects from his establishment. I told him that if he had a complaint, he could bring it directly to me. That bastard does nothing but flatter me to my face, then goes running to you with some petty tale.”

Japanese: 案の定、劉は話を漏らした人間への怒りを露わにする。
English: As expected, Ryu openly directed his anger toward the man who had reported him.

Japanese: 「自分の縄張りの店でそんな破廉恥なことをするのがなおさらひどいと言っているのです。……しかし、理由があるのならばあなたの言い分も聞きます。何かありますか？」
English: “I am telling you that such shameless conduct is worse when it occurs in an establishment within your own territory. ...Still, if you have a reason, we will hear your account. Do you have one?”

Japanese: ジェフリーの冷徹な声に劉は舌打ちをして、
English: Ryu clicked his tongue at Jeffrey’s cold voice.

Japanese: 「なんであんたばっかり喋ってる。龍頭の意見はないんですか？」
English: “Why are you doing all the talking? Does the Longtou have no opinion?”

Japanese: 「私の言葉は龍頭のご意見です」
English: “My words express the Longtou’s opinion.”

Japanese: 「龍頭に聞いているんですがねえ」
English: “I asked the Longtou himself.”

Japanese: 「私は、ウォン君と同意見だ。軽率だと思う」
English: “I agree with Wong. Your behavior was reckless.”

Japanese: マイケル・ツェーは一言言って、あとは困った顔で黙ってしまう。
English: Michael Tse said that much, then fell silent with a troubled expression.

Japanese: 「あははは！　これじゃ腹話術の人形だよ。クリス様ならこんな情けない茶番はしなかった」
English: “Ahahaha! He’s a ventriloquist’s dummy. Lord Chris would never have put on a pathetic farce like this.”

Japanese: 「劉建志。龍頭への侮辱は降格だけでは済まないのを知っていますか？」
English: “Ryu Kenshi. Do you understand that insulting the Longtou will cost you more than a demotion?”

Japanese: 「これは失礼！　侮辱ではないんですよ。ただ、先代が懐かしくなっただけでしてね」
English: “My apologies! I meant no insult. I merely found myself missing the former Longtou.”

Japanese: 「どんな理由があれ、龍頭の前では言葉を慎みなさい」
English: “Whatever the reason, guard your tongue before the Longtou.”

Japanese: 「気に障ったとおっしゃるのなら、謝罪します。しかし、本人が一言も口を利かずに側近が全部喋るだなんて、新しい龍頭は王様か何かなんですかねえ？　随分偉いものですな」
English: “If you tell me I have offended him, then I apologize. But when the man himself never opens his mouth and his aide says everything for him, is our new Longtou some sort of king? How very exalted.”

Japanese: 「劉建志どの」
English: “Mr. Ryu Kenshi.”

Japanese: 「いや、重ね重ね失礼」
English: “No, no. My apologies again.”

Japanese: 劉は億劫そうに礼をし、
English: Ryu bowed as though even the effort bored him.

Japanese: 「話がそれだけなら、帰らせてもらってもいいですかね？　喪に服している間にサボってしまった仕事が溜まっているんですよ」
English: “If that is all, may I leave? I neglected my work while I was in mourning, and it has begun to pile up.”

Japanese: 「結構。処分はあとで連絡します」
English: “Very well. You will be informed of your punishment later.”

Japanese: 劉は最後に、マスクから見える口元にひきつったような笑顔を浮かべると、そのままくるりと背を向けて、カツカツ足音を立てて執務室を出て行った。
English: The part of Ryu’s mouth visible beneath the mask twisted into a smile. Then he turned on his heel and left the office with hard, ringing footsteps.

Japanese: 「ヤンとかいう人物にやたら怒っていたけど、実際その人から苦情があったのかい？」
English: “He seemed awfully angry at that man Yang. Did the complaint actually come from him?”

Japanese: ドアが閉まった後、僕はそう訊ねた。
English: I asked once the door had closed.

Japanese: 「そうです。まあ、隠そうとしても無駄でしたね。しかし、あのようなチンピラの論理で逆恨みとは、まったく人間が小さい」
English: “Yes. It appears there was little use in concealing it. Still, to bear a grudge over that, with all the logic of a common thug... What a petty man.”

Japanese: 「先代はどうしてあんな男を幹部にしたのだろう？　いくらタイプAの力で無類の戦闘力があるといったって、今のYSみたいな経済重視の組織では扱いにくい人間だろうに」
English: “Why did the former Longtou make such a man an officer? No matter how unrivaled his Type A power makes him in combat, a man like that is difficult to employ in an organization so focused upon commerce as YS is now.”

Japanese: 「先代にとっては、従順で有能な猟犬だったのですよ。それに、我々は、おそらく小謝が思っている以上に、彼のような戦闘力を必要とする組織です」
English: “To the former Longtou, he was an obedient and capable hound. Besides, ours is an organization that requires fighters like him more than you probably imagine, Siu Tse.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは最後の言葉を口にするとき、暗い目つきになった。
English: Jeffrey’s eyes darkened as he spoke those final words.

Japanese: 「……まあ、彼は我々のために汚い仕事を請け負ってくれた功労者ではあります」
English: “...And he has served us well by taking on our dirty work.”

Japanese: 「それなら、あんな一方的に叱責するより、懐柔して引き続き仕事をさせた方が良いのでは？」
English: “In that case, rather than scolding him so one-sidedly, wouldn’t it be better to win him over and keep him working for us?”

Japanese: 「難しいですね。彼は我々を軽蔑していますし……それに、どうも廖と接触を持っているようです」
English: “That would be difficult. He despises us... and it appears he has been in contact with Liao.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは肩をすくめて溜息をつく。
English: Jeffrey shrugged and sighed.

Japanese: 「本来野心の強い男で、我々よりも廖志明の方を利用価値が高い相手と見ています。もし彼が、あの短慮で、牙を我々に剥いたらと考えると、力を持たせたままでいるのは危険です」
English: “He has always been ambitious, and he considers Liao Chi-ming more useful than we are. Given his rashness, it would be dangerous to leave him in power if he might bare his fangs at us.”

Japanese: 「なあウォン君。あの劉という男が、どうしても我々に従わなかったらどうするつもりなのか？　大人しく降格を受け入れるようには見えなかったが……」
English: “Tell me, Wong. What do you intend to do if this Ryu refuses to obey us under any circumstances? He did not look likely to accept a demotion quietly...”

Japanese: 僕たちのやりとりを横で聞いていたマイケル・ツェーは、不安そうにそう言った。
English: Michael Tse, who had been listening beside us, asked anxiously.

Japanese: 「このまま私たちを無視し続けるのならば、降格ではすまないでしょう。彼は他の幹部とは違って、先代がファミリーを持たせてやったわけですから、我々が主筋に当たるのですから。逆らうことは絶対に許されません。今後彼のような不届き者が出ないためにも」
English: “If he continues to ignore us, demotion will no longer be sufficient. Unlike the other officers, he received his family from the former Longtou, making ours the house to which he owes allegiance. Defiance can never be permitted, particularly if we wish to prevent more malcontents like him from appearing.”

Japanese: 「つまり？」
English: “Meaning?”

Japanese: 「掟では、重大な命令違反は死をもって償うことになっています」
English: “Under the rules, grave disobedience must be paid for with death.”

Japanese: 「死とは……」
English: “Death...”

Japanese: 龍頭は、そのきつい物言いにぎょっとしたようだった。
English: The Longtou appeared startled by the severity of the statement.

Japanese: 「そうしたやりかたをとらなければ、我々がYSを支配してゆくことなど到底不可能なのですよ」
English: “Without methods of that kind, it would be utterly impossible for us to rule YS.”

Japanese: ジェフリーが座った椅子に背を預けると、背もたれからキイと音が鳴る。
English: When Jeffrey leaned back in his chair, the backrest creaked.

Japanese: 彼は隈のうかんだ目元を指先で揉んでから、
English: He rubbed at the dark circles under his eyes with his fingertips before continuing.

Japanese: 「カリスマである先代を失った今、我々が過去の地位を維持するのは非常に困難です。他のファミリーは、現状をよしとしないものばかりですからね。実力をしらしめてゆくしかありません」
English: “Now that we have lost the former Longtou and his charisma, preserving our former position will be exceedingly difficult. Almost every other family finds the current order unacceptable. We have no choice but to demonstrate our strength.”

Japanese: 悲痛な顔で溜息をつく。
English: He sighed, his face anguished.

Japanese: 「気乗りしなさそうだね」
English: “You don’t sound eager.”

Japanese: 「私は荒っぽいのはさほど得意ではないのです。しかし、先代からこの地位を与えられた以上は、なんとしてもYSを衰退させるわけには行きません」
English: “Violent measures do not come naturally to me. But having accepted this position from the former Longtou, I cannot allow YS to decline, no matter what it takes.”

Japanese: 「馬明はなんて言ってる？」
English: “What does Ma Ming say?”

Japanese: 「久しぶりの喧嘩で血が騒ぐと笑ってますよ。どういう神経をしているのだか」
English: “He laughs that his blood is stirring at the prospect of his first fight in so long. I cannot imagine how that man is wired.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは呆れたように言い、
English: Jeffrey spoke in exasperation, then continued.

Japanese: 「ともあれ、我々がYSの執行部に居る間は、いかなる造反も、ルール違反も許しません。それは我々が執行部としてあり続ける以上、絶対に譲ってはならないラインなのです。……とりあえず、劉建志がどう振る舞うか。その結果次第で、私たちはとても重要な仕事が必要になるでしょう」
English: “In any case, so long as we form the executive of YS, we will permit no rebellion and no violation of its rules. As long as we remain in charge, that is a line upon which we can never yield. ...For now, we shall see how Ryu Kenshi behaves. Depending upon the result, we may have some very important work to do.”

Japanese: ジェフリーの言う『結果』は思ったより早くあらわれた。
English: The ‘result’ of which Jeffrey spoke arrived sooner than expected.

Japanese: それから二日後、暗闇通りの飲食店オーナーであるヤンが、自宅にて妻と二人の娘と共に死体となって発見されたのである。
English: Two days later, Yang, the restaurant proprietor from Darkness Street, was found dead at home with his wife and two daughters.

Japanese: 発見者は彼の家に食料品を届けているパラシュート通りの食料品店の店員で、ツェーファミリーと繋がりの深い店だったため、警察ではなく我々に連絡が来た。
English: They were discovered by an employee of a Parachute Street grocery that delivered food to his home. The shop had close connections with the Tse Family, so the report came to us rather than the police.

Japanese: 「暗闇通りじゃ、劉の仕業とは限らんだろう。なにか証拠はあったのか？」
English: “On Darkness Street, Ryu is hardly the only possible culprit. Was there any evidence?”

Japanese: かけつけて来た馬明が尋ねると、ジェフリーは引き出しから重いものを取り出し、どさりと机の上に置いた。
English: When Ma Ming asked, Jeffrey removed something heavy from a drawer and set it on the desk with a thud.

Japanese: それは、透明なビニール袋で、中には血で汚れた自動拳銃が入っている。
English: It was a transparent plastic bag containing an automatic pistol stained with blood.

Japanese: 「弾倉のなかで暴発しています。これは劉の能力で間違い有りません」
English: “The rounds went off inside the magazine. There can be no doubt that this was Ryu’s ability.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは物憂げな顔で馬明にそう説明すると、
English: Jeffrey explained it to Ma Ming with a melancholy expression.

Japanese: 「何かしでかすかもしれないとは思いましたが、まさか一家皆殺しにするとは。彼は気が狂っているのでしょうか？　それとも、タイプBの血でも目覚めたのですか？」
English: “I thought he might cause some trouble, but I never imagined he would slaughter an entire family. Has he lost his mind? Or has some Type B blood awakened in him?”

Japanese: 「兄貴が死んで、何もかもむしゃくしゃして仕方がないのさ。その気持はわからんでもないがね。……さてどうする？　彼は言い訳のきかないことをしでかしてくれたわけだが」
English: “Big Brother’s death left him so furious at everything that he can’t contain himself. I cannot say I wholly fail to understand the feeling. ...Now, what do we do? He has done something for which no excuse will serve.”

Japanese: 「どうもこうも、ここまでしては他に方法はありません。ヤンは我々の庇護下にある店舗のオーナーで、なおかつ執行部に対して忠実に情報を提供してくれました。それを逆恨みして一家皆殺しにしたのですよ？　このような殺人は最大級の犯罪です。結論は一つしかありません。……龍頭、異論はありませんね？」
English: “What else can we do? After this, there is no other course. Yang owned an establishment under our protection, and he loyally supplied the executive with information. Ryu resented him for it and slaughtered his entire family. A murder of this nature is a crime of the highest order. Only one conclusion is possible. ...Longtou, you have no objection?”

Japanese: 「ああ、私からは何もない」
English: “No. I have none.”

Japanese: さすがのマイケル・ツェーも、このときばかりは顔を緊張でこわばらせている。
English: Even Michael Tse’s face had grown rigid with tension now.

Japanese: 「小謝の意見も聞いておきましょうか」
English: “We should hear Siu Tse’s opinion as well.”

Japanese: 僕も言うことはなにもない。黙って肩をすくめた。
English: I had nothing to say either. I merely shrugged in silence.

Japanese: 「誰も反対しないのならば、決定ですね」
English: “If no one objects, the decision is made.”

Japanese: ジェフリーが頷くと、劉建志の処刑はすんなりと決まった。
English: Jeffrey nodded, and Ryu Kenshi’s execution was settled without difficulty.

Japanese: そして次は、どうやってその処刑が行われるかだ。
English: The next question was how that execution would be carried out.

Japanese: 「実際には、暗殺という形で直接彼の住まいに乗り込んで殺害することになります。呼びつけて従うような相手ではありませんからね」
English: “In practice, we will have to go directly to his residence and assassinate him there. He is not a man who will obey a summons.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはそう断言をする。
English: Jeffrey declared it flatly.

Japanese: 寝込みを襲って一方的に殺害するだけだから難しい仕事ではなさそうだが、何しろ相手はタイプＡとして優れた戦闘力を持つ男だ。何か失敗すれば、返り討ちにされる可能性もある。
English: At first glance, murdering him in his sleep seemed simple. But he was a Type A with exceptional combat ability. If anything went wrong, he might turn the tables and kill us instead.

Japanese: 「さて、誰にこの作戦を実行させるか、ですが……。誰か心当たりはありますか？」
English: “The question, then, is who should carry out the operation. ...Does anyone come to mind?”

Japanese: 「……なかなか難しいな」
English: “...That is a difficult question.”

Japanese: 馬明は首をひねる。
English: Ma Ming tilted his head.

Japanese: 「本当なら寝込みを襲うだけの簡単な仕事だが、相手はサイキックだ。誰だってサイキックを相手にするのは不安だ。しかも、相手はあの劉建志だ。最近の若い連中は骨がないやつばかりだから、恐れてしまうかもしれないな。ほら、いつだったか、強盗を返り討ちにした件もある」
English: “Ordinarily, attacking a sleeping man would be easy work. But he is a psychic, and anyone would feel uneasy facing a psychic. Worse, the man is Ryu Kenshi. Young men these days have no backbone. They may lose their nerve. Remember the time he turned the tables on those robbers?”

Japanese: 「その話、事実なのかい？」
English: “Was that story true?”

Japanese: 僕も聞いたことがあるが、どうも眉唾っぽく思っていた劉建志の武勇伝だ。
English: I had heard that story about Ryu Kenshi’s exploits myself, though it had always struck me as dubious.

Japanese: 暗闇通りで女を買い、ホテルにしけこんでまさに行為を居たそうとしたところに、銃で武装した強盗が現れた。劉建志は持ち前の超能力で相手の銃を向こうかし、三人の強盗達を逆に射殺した上で、行為を再開し、その死体の転がる部屋で最後までやり遂げたと言う。
English: He had hired a woman on Darkness Street and taken her to a hotel. Just as they were about to have sex, three armed robbers appeared. Ryu Kenshi used his psychic power to disable their guns, killed all three instead, then resumed the act and carried it through to the end in the room where their bodies lay.

Japanese: 「事実だとも。その事件のあと、女がおかしくなっちまってな。その辺りでナンバーワンの稼ぎ頭だったから、何かと話題になって大変だったんだ」
English: “It is true. The woman lost her mind after the incident. She had been the highest earner in that part of the street, so the story caused quite a commotion.”

Japanese: 「そうか。彼の能力からすれば不可能ではないだろうけど……僕が街を出てからのことだから、全然しらなかったな」
English: “I see. His ability would make it possible... It happened after I left the city, so I knew nothing about it.”

Japanese: 「とにかくあいつは滅法強い。それを倒す勇気と能力があって、しかも、口の硬い男が必要だ」
English: “In any case, he is phenomenally strong. We need a man with both the courage and ability to defeat him—and who can keep his mouth shut.”

Japanese: 「警戒させないうちに襲撃出来るチャンスは一度きりですからね。確実に仕事を遂行出来る、信頼出来る人物でなければいけません」
English: “We have only one opportunity to attack before he grows wary. It must be someone we can trust to complete the work without fail.”

Japanese: 「適任者がいないのかい？」
English: “You don’t have anyone suitable?”

Japanese: 「ただ威勢のいいだけのやつならたくさん居るし、劉建志に恨みがあるやつもいる。しかし、確実に仕留められる能力となると、なかなか思い浮かばない。今までは、劉建志がそうした仕事を一手に引き受けていたものだが、あいつに自分を殺させるわけにはいかないからな」
English: “We have plenty of men with more nerve than sense, and some who bear grudges against Ryu Kenshi. But when I consider who actually has the ability to kill him without fail, no one comes readily to mind. Until now, Ryu Kenshi was the man who handled every such task. We can hardly have him kill himself.”

Japanese: 馬明は渋い顔をする。
English: Ma Ming grimaced.

Japanese: 「誰もいないなら、僕がやろうか？」
English: “If there is no one else, shall I do it?”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、
English: When I said that,

Japanese: 「突然何を言い出すんですか。そんなこと出来るわけないでしょう？」
English: “What are you talking about all of a sudden? Of course you cannot do such a thing.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは苦い顔をするが、
English: Jeffrey made a bitter face, but Ma Ming spoke before he could continue.

Japanese: 「いや、それは良い考えかもしれない」
English: “No. That may be a good idea.”

Japanese: 「小謝にそんな仕事はさせられない。危険すぎる」
English: “We cannot give Siu Tse such work. It is far too dangerous.”

Japanese: 「彼は勝算もなくこんなことを言い出す人間ではないよ。……何か秘策があるんだろ？」
English: “He is not the sort of man to propose this unless he thinks he can pull it off. ...You have some secret plan, don’t you?”

Japanese: 馬明の問いに、僕は肩をすくめ、
English: At Ma Ming’s question, I shrugged.

Japanese: 「べつに秘策ってほどじゃないさ。ただ僕はある程度は彼の能力について知っている」
English: “I wouldn’t call it a secret plan. I just know something about the nature of his power.”

Japanese: 「そりゃ、能力は誰でも知っていますよ。銃などの武器を遠隔操作する力でしょう？　刃物などで襲うつもりですか？　相手は自分の銃を自由に使えるというのに」
English: “Everyone knows his power. He can control guns and other weapons from a distance, correct? Do you intend to attack him with blades while he remains free to use his own gun?”

Japanese: ジェフリーは溜息をついて首を横に振る。
English: Jeffrey sighed and shook his head.

Japanese: 「みんなそう思ってるだろうけど、僕はちょっと違う能力だと思っている。……まあ、任せてくれたらわかるよ。僕の考えでは、ノーマルと同じように始末出来る筈だ」
English: “That is what everyone believes, but I think his power is somewhat different. ...Well, if you entrust the matter to me, you will understand. By my reasoning, he can be disposed of in exactly the same fashion as a Normal.”

Japanese: 「まず作戦を聞きましょう。話はそれからです」
English: “First, let us hear your plan. We can discuss the rest afterward.”

Japanese: 「いやだね」
English: “No.”

Japanese: 「なぜですか？」
English: “Why not?”

Japanese: 「そうして、僕の考えたことを別の人間にやらせるつもりでしょう？　冗談じゃない。今回は自分で実行する」
English: “Because then you intend to have someone else carry out what I devised, don’t you? Absolutely not. This time, I will carry it out myself.”

Japanese: 「そうは言っても、言わなければ小謝の考えが適切かどうかわからないでしょう？」
English: “Even so, unless you explain it, we cannot determine whether your idea is sound.”

Japanese: 「僕の考えを採点するつもりなら、余計なお世話というものだよ。大体そんなこと出来るのかい？」
English: “If you intend to grade my ideas, that is the last thing I need. Are you even capable of doing that?”

Japanese: 僕が率直に言うと、彼はさすがにむっとしたようだった。
English: My bluntness finally seemed to offend him.

Japanese: 「はっはっは、そう言ってやるな小謝。こう見えてもジェフリーも若い頃はそれなりに喧嘩をしていたんだぞ？　確かに余り得意ではなかったが、経験はあるんだ」
English: “Hahaha, don’t speak to Jeffrey that way, Siu Tse. Believe it or not, even he got into his share of fights when he was young. Admittedly, he was never especially gifted, but he does have experience.”

Japanese: 馬明は場の空気を和らげるようにそう言うと、
English: Ma Ming said it as though to ease the atmosphere, then turned to Jeffrey.

Japanese: 「なあジェフリー。信じてやろうじゃないか。そろそろ彼にもファミリーの一員としての初仕事をさせるべきだ。このまま、何もしない補佐をさせていても、本人のためにもファミリーのためにもならんよ。それはわかっているだろう？」
English: “Listen, Jeffrey. Let us trust him. It is time we gave him his first job as a member of the family. Keeping him forever as an adviser who does nothing will help neither the man himself nor the family. You understand that, don’t you?”

Japanese: 「そうだが、しかし、これはあまりにも危険だ……」
English: “I do, but this is far too dangerous...”

Japanese: 「小謝、本当に自信があるんだな？」
English: “Siu Tse, you’re sure you can do it?”

Japanese: 「まあ、それなりに」
English: “Reasonably.”

Japanese: 僕は肩をすくめて、
English: I shrugged.

Japanese: 「人と道具さえ集められれば」
English: “Provided we can gather the people and equipment.”

Japanese: 「集められる目星はついてるんだな？」
English: “You already have some idea where to find them?”

Japanese: 「もちろん」
English: “Of course.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ、いいじゃないか」
English: “Then there is no problem.”

Japanese: 「いや、無茶苦茶です。小謝を参加させるわけには行きません」
English: “No, this is absurd. Siu Tse cannot participate.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはなおも食い下がる。
English: Jeffrey continued to resist.

Japanese: 「人材は確保するし、バックアップはおれが全面的に行う。処刑は汚れ仕事だが、劉は名高い嫌われ者だし、彼を小謝が始末したとなればみな彼を認めるだろう。まさに小謝の初仕事にふさわしい。……おい、まず人材は、誰がほしいんだ？」
English: “I will secure the necessary personnel and provide complete support. Execution is filthy work, but Ryu is famously detested. If Siu Tse disposes of him, everyone will acknowledge him. It is precisely the right first task for him. ...Now, whom do you want?”

Japanese: 「まず天明と天祥が必要だね。あとは、二、三人荒っぽいことに実績がある人間を貸して欲しい。あと世傑がいれば間違いない」
English: “First, I need Tin-ming and Tin-cheung. Then lend me two or three people with proven experience in violent work. And if Sai-kit is present, there can be no mistake.”

Japanese: 「おい小謝、世傑ってお前……」
English: “Listen, Siu Tse. Sai-kit is...”

Japanese: 驚きの声をあげたのは馬明だ。
English: It was Ma Ming who cried out in surprise.

Japanese: 「約束だろう？　きみが何を言っても借りるからね。世傑が帰って来て父さんの葬儀に参加したことは知ってるんだ。今近くにいるんでしょ？　それなら、すぐに参加出来るはずだ。万全を期すには彼のような経験のある優秀な紅棍が必要なんだ」
English: “You made a promise. Whatever you say, I mean to borrow him. I know Sai-kit returned and attended Father’s funeral. He is nearby now, isn’t he? Then he should be available at once. To be sure of success, we need an experienced and highly capable Red Pole like him.”

Japanese: 馬明は渋い声でうなり声を上げる。
English: Ma Ming gave a sour groan.

Japanese: 「わかった。認めよう！　よしジェフリー。これなら心配はないだろう。お前の二人の娘はこのような仕事には非常に役に立つ。そして経験豊富な部下をつければ、小謝なら立派にやりとげるよ」
English: “Very well. I accept! There, Jeffrey. Surely that puts your mind at ease. Your two daughters will be exceptionally useful in work of this kind. Give Siu Tse some experienced subordinates as well, and he will see it through splendidly.”

Japanese: 「普通の相手なら万全ですが、それなら最初から悩みません。相手は劉建志です。何がおこるかわかりません。もし万が一小謝の身に何かがあったら我々旧義勝の死活問題です。世傑を参加させるなら、彼をリーダーにして実行させれば済むことじゃないですか」
English: “Against an ordinary target, those preparations would be perfect, but then we would never have struggled over the question to begin with. The target is Ryu Kenshi. We cannot know what may happen. If anything should happen to Siu Tse, it would threaten the survival of the old Yisheng itself. If Sai-kit is participating, why not place him in command and leave the operation to him?”

Japanese: ジェフリーは渋るが、しかし馬明は譲らない。
English: Jeffrey remained reluctant, but Ma Ming would not yield.

Japanese: 「あいつをリーダーだなんてとんでもない！　それに、心配はもっともだが、小謝は大丈夫。兄貴だって危険をいとわず仕事をしてのぼりつめたんだ。小謝も同じ道を歩むべきだ。なにより、こいつなら誰よりうまくやるだろう。……それに、劉を取り立てたのはもともと兄貴なんだ。兄貴の息子である小謝の手で引導を渡すのが一番筋が通っているし、奴に対する慈悲でもある」
English: “Sai-kit in command? Out of the question! Your concern is reasonable, but Siu Tse will be fine. Big Brother rose to his position by performing dangerous work without regard for the risk. Siu Tse should follow the same path. More than that, I expect he will handle it better than anyone. ...Besides, it was Big Brother who raised Ryu to his position. It is only proper that Big Brother’s son, Siu Tse, deliver the deathblow—and it will be a mercy to the man as well.”

Japanese: 「……私はどうしても、危険に思えますが……」
English: “...I cannot help considering it dangerous...”

Japanese: 「ジェフリー」
English: “Jeffrey.”

Japanese: まだ迷いを見せる彼に、僕は言った。
English: I addressed him as he continued to hesitate.

Japanese: 「初代の遺言通り、僕を将来の龍頭として考えるつもりならば、そろそろ僕を信用した方がいい。これは忠告だ」
English: “If you intend to honor the first Longtou’s will and regard me as the future Longtou, then it is time you began to trust me. Consider that advice.”

Japanese: 「そうだろう！　まったくそのとおりだ！」
English: “Precisely! Exactly right!”

Japanese: 大声で賛成したのは馬明だった。
English: Ma Ming shouted his agreement.

Japanese: 「……そこまで言うならば仕方ありません」
English: “...If you insist upon putting it that way, I have no choice.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは腕組みをして考えた後、
English: Jeffrey folded his arms and considered for a time.

Japanese: 「わかりました。しかし、絶対に無茶はしないでください」
English: “Very well. But you must not do anything reckless.”

Japanese: ――劉建志。三十二才。生まれたのはY地区の外れにある溝平B団地……通称ヘドロ団地。Y地区のなかでもつまはじきにされるようなろくでなしたちが住み着く、半分廃墟となった建物が彼の故郷だ。
English: Ryu Kenshi. Thirty-two years old. Born in the Mizohira B Housing Complex at the edge of Y District—better known as the Sludge Housing Complex. That half-ruined building, inhabited by wretches rejected even within Y District, was his birthplace.

Japanese: 両親は揃って救いがたいジャンキーで、幼い頃から虐待されて育ったが、劉が十三才になると銃を持って二人を射殺した。これが彼にとって初めての殺人だ。
English: Both his parents were irredeemable addicts, and they abused him from early childhood. At thirteen, Ryu took a gun and shot them both to death. It was his first murder.

Japanese: そのまま団地を出て暗闇通りに住み着き、能力を使って売春宿の用心棒として過ごす。一匹狼で、不良少年のグループとはあまり交流しなかった。
English: He left the complex immediately afterward and settled on Darkness Street, where he used his ability to work as a brothel guard. A lone wolf, he had little interaction with the gangs of delinquent boys.

Japanese: 身長１８３センチ。体重は８５キロ。右利き。好きな音楽のジャンルはレゲエ。好きな映画は富川修二郎監督の港町シリーズ。煙草とマリファナを好み、酒は強くはなく、酒乱のケがあり、普段は自重している。靴下はチェック柄のものしか穿かない。エトセトラ、エトセトラ。
English: Height: 183 centimeters. Weight: 85 kilograms. Right-handed. Favorite genre of music: reggae. Favorite films: director Shujiro Tomikawa’s Harbor Town series. He liked cigarettes and marijuana. He could not hold his liquor and tended toward drunken violence, so he ordinarily restrained himself. He wore nothing but checkered socks. Et cetera, et cetera.

Japanese: 彼の家は暗闇通りから路地を一つ入った場所のビルの中にある。
English: His home was in a building one alley off Darkness Street.

Japanese: 古い雑居ビルを買い取ったもので、中には彼の住まいの他に、幾人かの部下の住居も入っており、他の階にはダーツバーやカジノも営業している。
English: He had purchased an old mixed-use building. In addition to his own residence, it contained quarters for several subordinates, while a dart bar and casino operated on other floors.

Japanese: 午前五時、日が明ける直前の時刻にその建物を襲撃することにした。
English: We decided to assault it at five in the morning, immediately before dawn.

Japanese: 今回の作戦のために、旧義勝のなかで暗殺において実績のある二人の紅棍……一人は普段精肉屋をやっている射撃の名手姜浩強、もう一人は学生時代クレー射撃の選手だった林徳軒という、射撃の腕前に定評のある人間を借り受けた。最近YSでは抗争は減ったけれども、二人ともこうした仕事の経験があるという話だった。
English: For this operation, I borrowed two Red Poles from the old Yisheng who had proven themselves in assassination. One was Jiang Haoqiang, an expert marksman who ordinarily worked as a butcher. The other was Lin Dexuan, who had competed in clay shooting as a student and was likewise renowned for his skill with a gun. Violent conflicts had become less common within YS in recent years, but both men were said to have experience in work of this nature.

Japanese: これと、僕の選んだ四人を足した計六人がビルの近くの真っ暗な路地で蹲っている。周囲にはゴミ箱から漂う生臭いにおいが漂っている。周囲の不自然な改築を繰り返した建物は闇の中でもいびつなシルエットを持ち、ひっそりと息づいている。
English: Together with the four I had selected, that made six of us crouching in a pitch-black alley near the building. The raw stench of refuse drifted from the garbage containers around us. Even in darkness, the surrounding buildings—each subjected to one unnatural alteration after another—cut distorted silhouettes and seemed to breathe in silence.

Japanese: ああ、これがY地区の路地の夜だ。僕は再びY地区のまっただ中に戻って来たのだ。
English: Ah, this was the Y District alleyways at night. I had returned once more to the very heart of the district.

Japanese: 「誰がいる？」
English: “Who is inside?”

Japanese: 僕が囁くように尋ねると、それまでじっと集中して能力を使っていた天明は顔を伏せたまま、
English: I asked in a whisper. Tin-ming, who until then had been standing perfectly still and concentrating as she used her ability, answered without raising her face.

Japanese: 「……劉幹部の部屋に六人。……部下達の居室には、誰もいません。……二階のカジノに一人。……三階のダーツバーは誰もいないようです」
English: “...Six people in Officer Ryu’s rooms. ...No one in the subordinates’ quarters. ...One person in the casino on the second floor. ...The dart bar on the third floor appears empty.”

Japanese: ジェフリー・ウォンの二人の娘、黄天明と黄天祥は共にタイプAで、その特質変異と引き替えにレーダーのようにある程度以上の生命体を感知する能力を授かっている。
English: Jeffrey Wong’s two daughters, Wong Tin-ming and Wong Tin-cheung, were both Type As. In exchange for their trait mutations, each had been granted an ability that sensed living things above a certain size, much like radar.

Japanese: 普段は龍頭のそばに控えて招かざる人物の接近を許さぬよう見張っているのだが、今日は目的の人物の状態を把握するために連れて来たのだ。
English: Ordinarily, they remained beside the Longtou and watched for the approach of unwelcome persons. Today, I had brought them to monitor the condition of our target.

Japanese: 「劉の部屋の六人は何をしているかわかるかい？」
English: “Can you tell what the six people in Ryu’s rooms are doing?”

Japanese: 「うーん……定かではないですが、六人とも移動してはいないで、部屋でじっとしています」
English: “Hmm... I cannot be certain, but none of the six is moving. They are all staying still in the room.”

Japanese: 彼女たちの感知能力は個人の姿形を見分けるようなものではなく、ぼうっと蝋燭の炎のように生命の存在を感じ取っているのだと聞いたことがある。
English: I had heard that their ability could not distinguish a person’s figure or shape. They sensed the presence of life only as a dim impression, like the flame of a candle.

Japanese: だから、移動しているか、止まっているかがわかるくらいで、それ以上の詳しい動作はわからないのだろう。
English: They could therefore tell whether a presence moved or remained still, but presumably could not make out any more detailed movements.

Japanese: 他の部屋に誰もいないとなると、部下たちを自分の部屋に呼んで酒でも飲み、そのまま雑魚寝でもしているのかもしれない。まだ起きて話し込んでいるということも考えられるが。
English: If none of the other rooms were occupied, Ryu might have called his subordinates into his own rooms for drinks, and they might all have crashed there together. Or they might still be awake, talking.

Japanese: いずれにしろ、一カ所に集まっているというのは僕らにとってこの上なく好都合だった。
English: Whatever the case, having all of them gathered in one place could not have suited us better.

Japanese: １０分ほどそこで待機して彼らの動向を窺ったが、やはりほとんど動きがない。彼らが動き出す前に、そのまま突入することにした。
English: We waited there for about ten minutes, watching for movement, but they remained almost entirely still. We decided to enter before they began moving.

Japanese: 「小謝。やっぱり危険ですよ。……突入なんかしないで、毒ガスでいぶり出すとか、爆弾を投げ込むとか、そういう方法はないんでしょうか？」
English: “Siu Tse, this truly is dangerous. ...Instead of going inside, couldn’t we smoke them out with poison gas, or throw in a bomb, or use some method like that?”

Japanese: 黄天明が心配そうに言う。
English: Tin-ming said anxiously.

Japanese: 「きみは面白いことを言う。街中で致死量の毒ガスをばらまくとか、派手に爆発させるとか、近隣住民ごと吹っ飛ばそうっていうのかい？　なかなかダイナミックで素敵なアイデアだと思うけれど、残念ながら僕らはテロリストではないんだ」
English: “You have fascinating ideas. Do you suggest releasing a lethal concentration of gas in the middle of the city? Setting off a spectacular explosion and blowing up all the neighboring residents along with them? It is a wonderfully dynamic proposal, but unfortunately, we are not terrorists.”

Japanese: 「す、すみません。でも、小謝が心配で……」
English: “I-I’m sorry. But I’m worried about you, Siu Tse...”

Japanese: 天明は謝りながらもなお不安げな視線を送ってくる。
English: Tin-ming apologized, but kept looking at me anxiously.

Japanese: 「あの……よく警察とかが、犯罪を起こしたタイプAを逮捕するために、能力をおさえる薬を使いますよね？　ああいうのは、手には入らないんですか？」
English: “Um... The police use drugs that suppress Type A abilities when they arrest Type As who have committed crimes, don’t they? Is there no way to obtain something like that?”

Japanese: 妹の天祥が控えめに提案する。
English: Her younger sister, Tin-cheung, offered the suggestion more timidly.

Japanese: 「いい提案だ。確かにあれがあればベストだ。でも、無理だってさ。エリーが言うには、銃器や麻薬を手に入れるよりもよほど入手しにくいシロモノらしい。ミュータント研究はどこも秘密主義だから仕方ないね」
English: “A good proposal. That certainly would be ideal. But apparently, it is impossible. Ellie tells me that stuff is far harder to obtain than guns or narcotics. Mutant research is secretive everywhere, so there is little to be done.”

Japanese: 僕は肩をすくめて、
English: I shrugged.

Japanese: 「まあ、そんなものなくても楽勝でしょう。……と言っても、僕は信用出来ないかな？　とりあえず、特別な助っ人も連れてきてるんだから安心してくれよ」
English: “Well, this should be easy even without anything like that. ...Or can you not trust me? In any event, I’ve brought in some special help, so don’t worry.”

Japanese: 「それ、アタシのこと？」
English: “You mean me?”

Japanese: 世傑が何故かいやそうな顔をして言う。
English: For some reason, Sai-kit looked displeased.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。期待しているんだ」
English: “Yes. I have great expectations of you.”

Japanese: 「いやんなっちゃうわ。アタシ、期待されるのと信頼されるのは苦手なの」
English: “Oh, how tiresome. I’m no good at having people trust me or expect things of me.”

Japanese: 彼は顔を顰め、肩をすくめた。
English: He frowned and shrugged.

Japanese: 「まあ、私もアンタには期待してるわよ。噂はかねがね聞いてるし……この間の滑走路通りで、あの見土が人食い虎をやっつけたときもアンタが一緒にいたって聞いてるわ」
English: “Well, I have expectations of you too. I’ve heard one story after another... including that you were with that Mido on Runway Street the other day, when he defeated the man-eating tiger.”

Japanese: 「詳しいな」
English: “You are well informed.”

Japanese: 僕は顔を顰める。
English: I frowned.

Japanese: 「そりゃそうよ。でも、おもしろいものよね。劉は　”龍頭の猟犬”　って呼ばれてたわけでしょ？　虎に続いて犬とは、よくよく猛獣退治に縁のあることね」
English: “Naturally. Still, it is amusing. Ryu was called ‘the Longtou’s hound,’ wasn’t he? First a tiger, and now a dog. You certainly have a way of ending up on hunts for dangerous beasts.”

Japanese: 世傑はおほほと笑い、僕のしかめっ面はさらに厳しいものとなる。
English: Sai-kit gave an affected little ‘ohoho,’ and my scowl deepened further.

Japanese: 「僕は人間を相手にする方が好きなんだけれどもね。……さて、それじゃあそろそろはじめるか。ビジネスの時間だ」
English: “I prefer dealing with human beings. ...Now, shall we begin? It is time for business.”

Japanese: 黄姉妹はその場に残し、残りの四人が突入部隊と決めてあった。襲撃を前に、僕らは黄色と白のツートンカラーのカプセルを一錠ずつ飲み込む。これは『ピーク』という興奮剤で、集中力と筋力の増強が見込める。軍隊のために開発された薬で、今は街の不良の喧嘩から、ギャングの抗争までよく使われるありふれた薬だ。効果が切れたあとの虚脱感がつらいものの、今回のような短い作戦ならば充分に役に立つだろう。
English: The Wong sisters would remain behind, while the other four of us formed the entry team. Before the assault, we each swallowed one yellow-and-white capsule. It was a stimulant called Peak, which was supposed to improve concentration and increase muscular strength. Developed for military use, it was now commonplace in everything from street fights among the city’s delinquents to gang warfare. The exhaustion after its effects wore off was severe, but for a short operation like this one, it would serve well enough.

Japanese: そうして僕たちは、裏口の側に移動する。
English: We moved over beside the rear entrance.

Japanese: 建物に特別なセキュリティシステムはなく、鍵はあらかじめ合い鍵を作ってあるのでそれを使って、この裏口から普通に侵入するだけだ。
English: The building possessed no special security system. We had prepared a duplicate key in advance, so we could simply use it to enter through the rear door.

Japanese: 僕はこの場面で、ふと、この作戦中に例の発作が訪れて、眠りこけてしまわないかと心配になった。
English: At that moment, I found myself worrying that one of my familiar episodes might strike during the operation and leave me fast asleep.

Japanese: いつもは大体前兆が現れてから意識を失うまで五分くらいかかり、予兆もなく突然倒れてしまうのは滅多にないが、ありえないことではない。交戦中に倒れてグースカ眠りはじめては何もかも台無しである。
English: Ordinarily, approximately five minutes passed between the first warning sign and my loss of consciousness. I rarely collapsed without warning, but it was not impossible. If I fell in the middle of combat and began snoring peacefully, it would ruin everything.

Japanese: 可能性としては極めて薄いのだとしても、最悪のトラブルというものは、最悪のタイミングで起こるものだ。
English: However unlikely the possibility, the worst problem invariably occurs at the worst possible moment.

Japanese: まあ、その時は、その時だ。
English: Well, if it happened, it happened.

Japanese: その場で持ち物の最終確認をして、お互いが無言で頷きあう。そして僕は、世傑に突入の合図を目配せした。
English: We checked our gear one last time and nodded to one another in silence. I then gave Sai-kit the signal to enter with a glance.

Japanese: 彼が蝶番が錆び付いたドアをキイと音を鳴らしながら開くと、誘導灯が薄暗い緑色の光で部屋を照らす裏玄関となる。
English: The rusted hinges squealed as he opened the door, revealing a rear entry hall lit by the dim green glow of an emergency sign.

Japanese: ビルで営業する店舗の搬入口として使っているだろう、このホールの片隅には、段ボールや飲料水のタンクが積まれている。そしてすぐ目の前には細く狭い階段があった。
English: The hall was presumably used as a delivery entrance by the businesses in the building. Cardboard boxes and tanks of drinking water stood piled in one corner, and a narrow, cramped staircase rose immediately before us.

Japanese: 目的の劉の部屋は一番上の四階にあり、エレベーターは設置されていないから、そこに辿り着くにはこの階段を昇るほかない。
English: Ryu’s rooms occupied the fourth and highest floor. The building had no elevator, leaving this staircase as the only way to reach them.

Japanese: 二人が肩を並べると窮屈になるこの階段を、僕らは一人ずつ昇った。
English: The stairs were too narrow for two people to walk comfortably abreast, so we climbed in single file.

Japanese: 僕らはそれぞれの肩にライフルを担いでいる。これは劉建志を倒すために用意した特別な武器だ。普通の火器では彼を倒すことが困難であるため、エリー・ホワイトの協力によって急遽調達された。
English: Each of us had a rifle slung over one shoulder. These were special weapons prepared to defeat Ryu Kenshi. Ordinary firearms would have great difficulty killing him, so they had been procured at short notice with Ellie White’s assistance.

Japanese: 劉建志は、そのタイプAとしての能力によって、遠くに設置した爆弾や銃を任意のタイミングで作動させて目標を攻撃したり、敵対者の持つそれらを暴発させて無力化させることが出来る。
English: With his Type A ability, Ryu Kenshi could trigger guns and bombs planted at a distance whenever he chose, using them to attack a target. He could also force weapons held by his enemies to discharge and render them useless.

Japanese: 一般的には銃器や爆発物を遠隔操作する能力だと思われているようだが、僕が分析した限りではちょっと違う。彼の能力は、火薬に着火するというものだ。
English: His ability was generally believed to control firearms and explosives from a distance, but my analysis produced a somewhat different conclusion. His power ignited gunpowder.

Japanese: タイプAが自分の能力を告白することは命取りだから、彼自身がそう明言したことはないし、僕以外でそれに気がついている者がいるのかどうかもわからないが、彼が能力を使った場面を考えるとほぼ間違いがない。
English: For a Type A, confessing the nature of one’s ability can be fatal. Ryu had never stated it himself, and I did not know whether anyone else had noticed, but his recorded uses of the ability left almost no room for doubt.

Japanese: 今回の仕事が決まってから彼が能力を使った記録にあたったのだが、着火すると言っても何にでも火を付ける能力ではないようで、木材やガソリンに火を付けたという例は見られなかった。対象は火薬限定なのだろう。
English: After the operation was approved, I examined those records. Although his ability caused ignition, it did not appear capable of setting fire to just anything. There was no example of him igniting wood or gasoline. Gunpowder was presumably its sole target.

Japanese: 相手が振り回す拳銃の弾倉内に収められた銃弾の火薬を発火させ、思いのままに暴発させているところなどを見ると、能力のすばやさと精密性はすさまじいものがあるらしい。もしかしたら、彼の能力にはただ着火させるだけでなく、特定の範囲内の火薬を感知するような力も含まれているのかもしれない。その感知した火薬のなかから、選んだものを自由に発火出来るのかもしれない。
English: He had ignited the propellant in cartridges held inside an opponent’s pistol magazine and made them discharge at will, suggesting terrifying speed and precision. Perhaps his ability did more than ignite gunpowder: it might also detect gunpowder within a particular range. He might then choose freely among the charges he sensed and ignite whichever one he wished.

Japanese: いずれにしろ、非常にすぐれた能力で、お互い銃を手にして戦うような場面ではほとんど無敵と言って良いだろう。そうでなくとも、近代兵器というのはそのほとんどに火薬を使用している。これらを特別な仕掛けもなしに肉体一つで操れるということは、あらゆる場面で役に立つに違いない。
English: In any event, it was an exceptional power. In any exchange where both sides carried guns, he could be called nearly invincible. Even beyond firearms, almost every modern weapon used gunpowder. The power to control such weapons with nothing but his own body, and without any special mechanism, must have been useful in every imaginable situation.

Japanese: が、能力の内容さえわかっていれば、対処自体は可能だ。
English: But once the nature of the ability was understood, countermeasures were possible.

Japanese: 世間の多くの人は、すぐれたサイキックを相手にするとなると、常人とは違うというだけで必要以上の恐れを抱いてしまうものだけど、誰が相手でも、どんな場合でも、同じことをするだけだ。そこにあるものだけを見ればいい。
English: When facing a formidable psychic, most people grow excessively afraid simply because the opponent differs from an ordinary human being. Yet whoever the opponent may be, and whatever the circumstances, one need only do the same thing: look solely at what is actually there.

Japanese: 今回用意したこの銃ならば、彼の能力でも無効化することは出来ない。それでも、その場にある他の銃は彼の思いのままであるため、油断は出来ないが。
English: He could not neutralize the guns we had prepared. Even so, every other gun present would remain subject to his will, so we could not let our guard down.

Japanese: 軍隊や警察の最新装備として実用されつつあるタイプA能力を無効化するガスを用意出来ればもっと良かったが、これはエリー・ホワイトの調達ルートを持ってしても手に入れることは不可能だった。
English: It would have been better to obtain the Type A ability-neutralizing gas now being fielded by militaries and police forces as cutting-edge equipment, but even Ellie White’s procurement channels could not secure it.

Japanese: 「ねえ猟犬で思い出したんだけど、小謝、むかーしパラシュート通りに住んでいた、オズワルドという男を知ってる？」
English: “Speaking of hounds, Siu Tse, do you remember a man named Oswald who lived on Parachute Street a long time ago?”

Japanese: 先頭を行く馬世傑が、足取り重く億劫そうに階段を昇りながら、そのすぐ後ろを行く僕に話しかけた。
English: Ma Sai-kit led the way, trudging up the stairs as though every step were a chore and speaking to me as I followed immediately behind.

Japanese: 「聞いたような名前だけれど誰だっけ」
English: “The name sounds familiar. Who was he?”

Japanese: 「禿げた白人の男よ。犬を沢山飼ってた」
English: “A bald white man. He kept a great many dogs.”

Japanese: 父とちっとも似ないスリムな体を黒いスーツに包んだその長髪の優男は、父の『強く男らしくあるべし』という教育方針で、物心つく前から様々な流派の武術教師を雇われ、そしていずれも高いレベルで習得していたが、肝心の男らしさは全く身につかず、子供の頃から女言葉を使う。
English: The slender body that bore no resemblance to his father’s was clothed in a black suit, and long hair framed Sai-kit’s delicate face. Ma Ming’s educational principle had been that his son must grow strong and manly, so he had employed instructors from various martial traditions before Sai-kit could even remember. Sai-kit mastered every one to a high degree. Yet he acquired none of the intended masculinity and had used feminine speech since childhood.

Japanese: 人に同性愛者と疑われても否定をしないが、実際には過度の女好きで、しかも女に容赦がない。彼によって破滅した女は多い。そもそも、YSの若き紅棍として頭角を現していた彼を、父の馬明が自らクリス・ツェーに願い出て組織から追放した理由も女がらみのトラブルだった。
English: When people suspected him of being homosexual, he made no attempt to deny it. In reality, he was an inveterate womanizer—and merciless toward women. He had ruined many of them. Indeed, trouble involving a woman was the reason Ma Ming himself had petitioned Chris Tse to expel his own son from the organization, despite Sai-kit’s rising prominence as a young Red Pole of YS.

Japanese: ちなみに、今日は彼に限らず全員が黒いスーツを着ていたが、それは彼の断固たる主張によるもので、汚れ仕事を行うときは喪服を着るのが彼にとって死にゆくものへの敬意だとか、ポリシーだとか、よくわからない美学をごちゃごちゃと語っていた。
English: Incidentally, everyone wore a black suit that day, not only Sai-kit. He had insisted upon it, rambling about some muddled personal aesthetic—wearing mourning clothes for filthy work was his way of respecting those about to die, or a matter of principle, or something of the sort.

Japanese: 「ああ、それなら覚えてる。有名人じゃないか。でかい犬を何匹も一片に散歩させて、すれ違う人がこわがるのを見てニヤニヤしていたやつだろう？」
English: “Ah, now I remember. He was famous. He used to walk several enormous dogs at once and grin at everyone who drew back in fear, didn’t he?”

Japanese: 「そうよ。慈善活動という名目で、行き場のない犬を引き取って、犬屋敷みたいにして住んでた男」
English: “That’s him. He took in unwanted dogs under the name of charity and lived in a house that was almost a kennel.”

Japanese: 彼がそう言ったところで、さしかかろうとしていた二階のドアがギイと開いて、従業員が姿を現した。
English: Just as he finished, the second-floor door we were approaching opened with a creak and an employee appeared.

Japanese: ギョッとする男に、世傑はドアが開きかけた時点で無造作な動作ながら素早く照準を合わせライフルの引き金を引く。暗闇のなかでカチャッという銃自体の作動音とプシュッと空気の抜ける音が同時に鳴り、相手が悲鳴を上げる間もなく倒れた。出血は確認出来なかったが急所に命中したのだろう。
English: The man recoiled. Before the door had opened fully, Sai-kit aimed with a motion that appeared casual but was extraordinarily fast and pulled the trigger. The click of the rifle’s mechanism sounded together with a rush of escaping air in the darkness. The other man fell before he could scream. I could see no blood, but the shot had presumably struck a vital point.

Japanese: このライフルは拳銃よりもさらに威力が劣る武器だが、当たり所が良かったとは言え一撃で倒したところを見ると、近距離で用いる分には問題がないようだ。ただ反響する階段で使うと思ったより射撃音が大きい。
English: The rifle possessed still less power than a pistol. Granted, the shot had struck a favorable spot, but bringing the man down in one hit suggested that it would serve perfectly well at close range. Its report was louder than I had expected when used in the echoing stairwell.

Japanese: 「アタシ、あのイギリス人と結構親しかったのよね」
English: “I was rather close to that Englishman.”

Japanese: 僕が自分のライフルを差し出すと、世傑は今一発撃ったライフルをそれと交換し、何事もなかったかのように会話を続けながら階段を昇る。
English: I offered Sai-kit my own rifle. He exchanged it for the one he had just fired and continued climbing the stairs and talking as though nothing had happened.

Japanese: 「それは初耳だね」
English: “That is the first I’ve heard of it.”

Japanese: 僕たちは床に倒れた男の死体を踏まぬように足を置くが、何しろ暗く、靴底で流れ出た血液を踏んでしまった。
English: We placed our feet carefully to avoid stepping on the body. But the stairwell was dark, and our shoes still came down in the blood spreading from it.

Japanese: 「あの男、最後は奥さんに殺されてしまったでしょう？　その理由が、まったく傑作なのよ」
English: “His wife killed him in the end, remember? The reason was a masterpiece.”

Japanese: 「飼い犬と性交してるのをばれて逆上したんだった」
English: “She discovered him having sex with one of his dogs and flew into a rage.”

Japanese: 「アハハ、それ、それ。アタシ、実はその趣味について彼が生きてる時から聞いて知っていたのよねえ」
English: “Ahaha, yes, that. The truth is, I had already heard about that habit while he was still alive.”

Japanese: 「へえ、妙な繋がりがあるんだね」
English: “I see. You had a peculiar connection.”

Japanese: 僕は階段の先を見上げた。
English: I looked toward the top of the staircase.

Japanese: 目指す階まであとわずか。そこで、僕の目的の人物が待っている。
English: The floor we sought was only a little farther. My target waited there.

Japanese: 「特殊な性癖の人って、昔からとても興味があるのよ。人間の業の深さを感じるでしょう？　それである時ね、彼の性癖が気になって、尋ねたことがあるの。ここに、メスの柴犬、シェパード、ゴールデンレトリバー、チワワなんかがいたとして、どれが一番そそるんですかって。そしたら彼、首を振ってこういうの。『その中には私の好みの犬はいない』って。アタシは『じゃあ、他のどんな犬種でもいいので、好きな犬をあげてください』って言ったのね。すると彼はもう一度首を振って、『犬種の問題じゃないんだ』と言うのよ。そのあと好みの犬を教えてくれたんだけど、結局彼が好きな犬というのはどんな犬だったと思う？」
English: “I’ve always been fascinated by people with unusual sexual tastes. They make you feel the depths of human depravity, don’t they? So once, his tastes interested me enough that I asked him a question. Suppose there were a female Shiba Inu, German shepherd, golden retriever, and Chihuahua here—which would arouse him most? He shook his head and said, ‘There isn’t a dog I like among them.’ So I asked, ‘Then name any other breed you like.’ He shook his head again and answered, ‘It isn’t a question of breed.’ Then he told me what sort of dog he preferred. What do you think it was?”

Japanese: 「犬種の問題じゃないのなら、境遇かな？　ボランティアで不幸な犬を拾っていたから、虐待されていた犬ほど好みだとか……」
English: “If it wasn’t a question of breed, perhaps it was a question of circumstances. He rescued suffering dogs as charity—did he prefer the ones that had been abused most severely?”

Japanese: そして僕たちは、ようやく目指す階のドアの前に辿り着いた。
English: At last, we reached the door to our destination floor.

Japanese: 「ちがうわ」
English: “Wrong.”

Japanese: 世傑は声を落とし、ドアノブをひねる。
English: Sai-kit lowered his voice and turned the doorknob.

Japanese: その向こうには廊下があるが真っ暗だった。世傑がペンライトで照らすと、奥の右手にドアが見える。あのドアの向こうに、ターゲットがいる。
English: The corridor beyond was completely dark. When Sai-kit illuminated it with a penlight, we saw a door toward the back on the right. Our target waited beyond it.

Japanese: 僕たちはドアをくぐり抜け、廊下に足を踏み入れた。少し広くなったので、二人ずつ肩を並べて歩く。
English: We passed through the first door and entered the corridor. It was somewhat wider, allowing us to proceed two abreast.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、どんな犬が好みだったのさ」
English: “Then what kind of dog did he prefer?”

Japanese: 僕はひそめた声でそう尋ねる。
English: I asked in a lowered voice.

Japanese: 「それが、おっかしいのよ。彼はこう言ったの」
English: “That is the hilarious part. This is what he told me.”

Japanese: 劉の居室へ繋がるドアの前に立つと、その向こうから人の気配がする。彼らは眠ってはいないようだ。
English: When we stopped before the door to Ryu’s residence, we sensed people beyond it. They did not appear to be asleep.

Japanese: 世傑はニヤニヤと笑いながらそのノブを握り、
English: Sai-kit grinned as he grasped the knob.

Japanese: 「『私が好きなのはメス犬じゃない。オスだけだ』ってね。ねえ、あの男は犬をファックしていたんじゃなくて、犬にファックされていたのよ」
English: “‘I don’t like female dogs. Only males.’ You see, he wasn’t fucking the dogs. The dogs were fucking him.”

Japanese: そして彼は僕らに目配せをして合図を送ってから、鍵を開け、そしてドアを開け放った。
English: He exchanged a look with us to signal the moment, unlocked the door, and flung it open.

Japanese: 世傑を先頭に、ライフルを構えた僕たちは一斉に部屋になだれ込む。
English: With Sai-kit at the front, all of us rushed into the room with our rifles raised.

Japanese: 部屋の中は薄暗かった。マリファナの匂いがたちこめ、どこかのスピーカーがレゲエを鳴らしていた。
English: The room was dim. The odor of marijuana filled the air, and reggae played from a speaker somewhere.

Japanese: 彼らは揺らめくランプの炎を取り囲み、あるものはぐったりと背もたれによりかかり、また別のものは煙の立ち上るものを咥えている。劉建志は街のチンピラあがりだが、彼も、その仲間達も、昔を彷彿とさせるようなラフいでたちで、安っぽいアクセサリーをじゃらじゃらと身につけ、肌の刺青を露出させている。
English: They surrounded the flickering flame of a lamp. Some slumped against the backs of their seats, while others held smoking objects between their lips. Ryu Kenshi had risen from the street thugs of the city, and both he and his companions wore rough clothes evocative of those days, with cheap ornaments jangling over exposed tattoos.

Japanese: このなかで、まず狙うのは劉建志。
English: Ryu Kenshi was our first target among them.

Japanese: 彼はトレードマークのマスクをしていなかったが、そのせいでかえってすぐに本人だと断定出来た。
English: He was not wearing his trademark mask. That made it easier, rather than harder, to identify him with certainty.

Japanese: 危険なときに立ち入るとき、部下にマスクをかぶらせて偽装するのはよく彼が使う手だ。そうでなくとも、座興で別の人間にかぶらせるなどしていたら、僕たちは判断を間違える可能性がある。
English: When he expected danger, he often disguised a subordinate with the mask. Even if someone else had put it on as a joke, with no such plan in mind, we might have selected the wrong target.

Japanese: しかし、特質変異によって生じた額の口は、他の誰とも見間違えることのないものだった。
English: But the mouth upon his forehead, born from his trait mutation, could not be mistaken for that of any other person.

Japanese: 僕たちは手にしたライフルを劉に向ける。彼はちょうどドアが視界に入る場所に座っていて、僕らの姿をその両目でしっかりと確認をしたが、何も出来なかった。能力を使うことさえ出来たか、どうか。テーブルに置いた銃に手を伸ばそうとしたその体を、いくつかの銃弾が貫いた。
English: We aimed our rifles at Ryu. He sat where the door lay directly within his field of view and saw us clearly with both eyes, but he could do nothing. Whether he could even have invoked his ability was uncertain. As he reached toward the gun upon the table, several projectiles tore through his body.

Japanese: 僕らの手にした武器は、狩猟に使うプリチャージ式の空気銃だ。事前にポンプで空気を圧縮しておき、引き金を引くとその圧力で弾が飛ぶ。海外製の鹿や熊さえも仕留めることが出来る大口径のものを、さらに改造で威力を上げている。
English: Our weapons were precharged pneumatic air rifles used for hunting. Air was compressed in advance with a pump, and when the trigger was pulled, that pressure launched the projectile. These large-bore foreign models could kill even deer and bears, and modification had increased their power still further.

Japanese: 当然どこにも火薬は使われておらず、劉が能力を使っていつものように暴発させようとしたところで、出来るものではない。畢竟、彼のようなタイプAでもこうして銃弾の的になるしかない。
English: Naturally, they used no gunpowder anywhere in their mechanism. Even if Ryu invoked his ability and attempted to make them discharge as he ordinarily did, there was nothing for it to ignite. In the final analysis, even a Type A like him could do nothing but become a target for our projectiles.

Japanese: そのすぐれた能力で幾多もの修羅場をくぐってきたタイプAと言えども、肝心の能力が使えない上に、手の内を知り尽くした組織の同志が油断したときを狙えばあっけないものだ。
English: He was a Type A who had survived countless scenes of carnage with his exceptional ability. Yet deprived of that ability and attacked in an unguarded moment by comrades who knew every card in his hand, he proved terribly fragile.

Japanese: 劉の体が後ろ向きに倒れるが、それが完全に倒れるのを待たず、僕たちは彼のためだけに用意したエアライフルを捨て、第二の武器を取り出した。それは小型のサブマシンガンだった。
English: Ryu’s body fell backward. Without waiting for it to reach the floor, we discarded the air rifles prepared solely for him and drew our secondary weapons: compact submachine guns.

Japanese: 空気銃のマガジンには五発装填できた。構造上、一発撃つごとに威力が落ちる。マガジンひとつ分程度の銃弾なら殺傷力を維持したまま打ち終えることが可能なのは前もってテスト済だけれども、こうした室内の乱戦で使うには心許ない。連射能力が低く、一発撃つごとにレバーを引いて新しい弾を装填させるという余計な動作もある。
English: An air-rifle magazine held five rounds. By the nature of the mechanism, power declined with every shot. Our advance tests showed that we could fire one complete magazine while maintaining lethal force, but the weapons were unreliable for a confused battle inside a room. Their rate of fire was low, and each shot required the additional motion of operating a lever to chamber the next round.

Japanese: 新しく取り出したサブマシンガンはそれこそ雨のように銃弾をばらまくことが出来、屋内での制圧力は圧倒的だった。しかも相手はマリファナによって動きも判断力も鈍い。彼らを仕留めるのは、銃でテロリストを殺すコンピューターゲーム『Red Fire』の一面をイージーモードでクリアするよりはるかに簡単な仕事だった。
English: The submachine guns we now held could scatter bullets like rain and offered overwhelming firepower for controlling an indoor space. Our opponents’ movements and judgment had also been dulled by marijuana. Killing them was far easier than clearing the first level of Red Fire—a computer game about shooting terrorists—on easy mode.

Japanese: 瞬く間に劉の脇にいたもう一人、スキンヘッドの南米人は蜂の巣となってがっくりと崩れ落ち、隆が拾おうとしたテーブルの銃に手を伸ばした角刈りのアジア人が次の犠牲者となった。
English: In an instant, the bald South American beside Ryu was riddled with bullets and collapsed. A crew-cut Asian man reaching for the gun upon the table—the same one Ryu had tried to take—became our next victim.

Japanese: 他のメンバーは、銃弾の雨のなか咄嗟にソファーの裏に隠れるなどして、ひとまず視界から姿を消した。
English: The other occupants vanished from view for the moment, reacting to the rain of bullets by diving behind a sofa or seeking similar cover.

Japanese: 僕は視界が光で満ちあふれ、なんとも魂が輝くような陶酔感を感じた。それは興奮剤のせいだけでなく、脳内にドーパミンが分泌されているからだ。
English: Light flooded my vision, and I felt an intoxication as though my soul itself shone. It came not only from the stimulant, but from dopamine released inside my brain.

Japanese: 例えばギャンブルで大金をかけたとき、登山などをして死の瀬戸際に立たされたとき、そういった極限状態になるとなんとも言えない幸福感を覚える。その結果、スリルというものが自分の生きている実感だと勘違いをするバカが良くいるが、たんに脳内麻薬でラリっているだけのことだ。危険のなかでないと生きる実感がないとか格好つけているやつは、単にこの薬物の中毒で日常が物足りなくなっているだけだ。
English: The same indescribable happiness appears when a person stakes an enormous sum upon a wager, or stands at the brink of death while climbing a mountain. Many fools consequently mistake the thrill itself for a sense of being alive. In reality, they are merely intoxicated by chemicals produced within their own brains. Anyone who preens that he can feel alive only when in danger has simply become addicted to that drug and can no longer find ordinary life sufficient.

Japanese: 僕ら人間は、そもそもハッピーな気持ちで快感に満たされながら危険を冒し、殺し合うことが出来るように作られている。それは肉体の問題であり、そこには思想的真実はない。
English: We human beings were made capable of taking risks and killing one another while flooded with happiness and pleasure. It was a matter of the body; there was no ideological truth behind it.

Japanese: 嗚呼、この、暴力を行使している瞬間の陶酔感はなんとも不快だ。僕はどうしても好きになれない。早く終わらせたくて仕方がない。
English: Ah, how repulsive this rush I felt while committing violence was. I could never like it. I wanted nothing more than to finish quickly.

Japanese: 黄姉妹の言葉によれば敵は六人。既に三人倒したから残るは三人。
English: According to the Wong sisters, there had been six enemies. We had already brought down three, leaving three more.

Japanese: 世傑の目配せに従い、僕たちは彼らが盾にとったソファーに銃弾を送り込んだ。
English: Following Sai-kit’s signal, we poured bullets into the sofa they had taken as a shield.

Japanese: ソファーはなかなかに頑丈で、僕らの武器では貫通したかあやしい。僕が手を上げ、一端銃撃をやめさせて気配を窺うと、不意にソファーの向こうに一人が立ち上がり、部屋の向こう側へ向けて逃げ出そうとする。
English: The sofa was surprisingly sturdy, and I could not tell whether our rounds had penetrated. I raised a hand to stop the fire for a moment and listened for movement. Without warning, one person rose beyond the sofa and attempted to flee toward the far side of the room.

Japanese: しかし、世傑はそれを許さない。
English: Sai-kit stopped him.

Japanese: 素早く構えるとその背中に銃弾を命中させた。男は顔から床に倒れ、胸に空いた穴からとめどもなく流れる血液がすぐに黒い水たまりを作った。
English: He raised his weapon with tremendous speed and put a bullet into the man’s back. The man struck the floor face-first. Blood pouring without end from the hole in his chest swiftly formed a black pool.

Japanese: そして再び部屋に静寂が戻る。すると、ソファーの向こうに荒い呼吸音があるのが聞こえた。
English: Silence returned to the room. Then we heard harsh breathing beyond the sofa.

Japanese: 「まだ生きている」
English: “Someone is still alive.”

Japanese: このまま銃撃を再開するか、回り込んで確実にクリアリングするか、判断を求めて世傑に視線を怒ったところで、
English: I looked to Sai-kit for a decision: resume firing, or circle the sofa and clear it with certainty. Before he could answer, a voice came from the other side.

Japanese: 「お、おい！　ちょっと待ってくれ」
English: “H-hey! Wait a moment!”

Japanese: ソファーの向こうから、恐怖に震える声がした。
English: The voice trembled with terror.

Japanese: 「誰か知らないが、助けてくれ！　おれは劉の部下じゃない。たまたま遊びに来ていただけなんだ！　もう大けがもしている。とても抵抗なんか出来やしない……」
English: “I don’t know who you are, but spare me! I’m not Ryu’s subordinate. I only happened to come here for a visit! I’m already badly injured. I couldn’t resist you if I tried...”

Japanese: 僕はもう一度世傑の顔を見た。彼は顔を横に振る。
English: I looked at Sai-kit again. He shook his head.

Japanese: 「わかったわ。助けてあげる。だから、両手を頭の後ろに重ねて立ち上がってちょうだい」
English: “Very well. I’ll spare you. Place both hands behind your head and stand up.”

Japanese: 世傑は朗々と通る声でそう呼びかけた。
English: Sai-kit called out in a clear, resonant voice.

Japanese: 「む、無理だ！　足にたまが当たって、とても立ち上がれない……」
English: “I-I can’t! I was shot in the leg. There’s no way I can stand...”

Japanese: 「出来ないならいいわ。さようなら」
English: “If you can’t, that’s fine. Goodbye.”

Japanese: 「ま、待ってくれ！　やってみる！　やってみるから待ってくれ……くっ……畜生、なんでこんな……」
English: “W-wait! I’ll try! I’ll try, so wait... Ngh... Damn it. Why did this...”

Japanese: ソファの向こうの荒い息に、うめき声が混じり、そして漸くその人物はよろよろと立ち上がった。
English: Groans mingled with the ragged breathing beyond the sofa. At last, the person rose unsteadily into view.

Japanese: そこにいるのは筋肉の隆々とした、逞しい男で、よほど痛むのか、顔や肌にびっしりと汗を浮かべ、全身をプルプルと震わせている。
English: He was a powerfully built, muscular man. The pain must have been severe: sweat covered his face and body, and he trembled all over.

Japanese: その苦痛に歪む顔には、金色に光る目があった。タイプBなのであろう。
English: Golden eyes shone in his pain-contorted face. He appeared to be Type B.

Japanese: 「やったぞ。……だから、命だけは……」
English: “I did it... So please, at least spare my life...”

Japanese: 「やれば出来るじゃない」
English: “There, you could do it after all.”

Japanese: 世傑は無表情に銃を上げると、正確な射撃で彼の頭を打ち抜いた。
English: Sai-kit raised his gun without expression and shot the man cleanly through the head.

Japanese: するともうソファーの向こうに気配はなくなった。
English: No presence remained beyond the sofa.

Japanese: しかし、計算ではあと一人残っている筈である。
English: By our count, however, there should have been one more person.

Japanese: 世傑はさほど緊張の見えない顔で僕に目配せをすると、軽い足取りでソファーの向こうを覗いた。そしてまた僕たちを見て、
English: His face betraying little tension, Sai-kit glanced at me, then stepped lightly around the sofa and looked behind it. He turned to us once more.

Japanese: 「どうやら終わってたようね」
English: “Looks like that one was already done for.”

Japanese: と言った。
English: he said.

Japanese: 僕は溜息をつき、彼に近づく。そして自分の目でソファーの裏を確認すると、そこに転がっていたのは若い女の死体だった。
English: I sighed and approached him. When I looked behind the sofa with my own eyes, I found the body of a young woman lying there.

Japanese: 僕はその死体を爪先で押してごろりと転がすと、血まみれの顔がこちらを向いた。
English: I pushed the body with the toe of my shoe and rolled it over, turning its blood-covered face toward us.

Japanese: 「この子を知ってる？」
English: “Do you know her?”

Japanese: 世傑は僕を振り返る。
English: Sai-kit looked back at me.

Japanese: 「調査してあるよ。劉の娘だ。確か劉が十七才に生ませた娘だったはずだから、十五才かな」
English: “I’ve looked into her. She’s Ryu’s daughter. If I remember correctly, he fathered her when he was seventeen, so she must be about fifteen.”

Japanese: 「そう。そりゃ、随分と気の毒な場所に居合わせてしまったものね」
English: “I see. What a terribly unfortunate place for her to find herself.”

Japanese: 世傑はそう言うと、肩をすくめる。
English: Sai-kit shrugged.

Japanese: ともあれ、すべての仕事はこれで終わった。僕は緊張から解き放たれ、溜息をついた。
English: In any event, the work was finished. As the tension released me, I sighed.

Japanese: 姜浩強は煙草に火を付ける。林徳軒は携帯電話を取りだして誰かにメールを打ち始めた。
English: Jiang Haoqiang lit a cigarette. Lin Dexuan produced his mobile phone and began writing an email to someone.

Japanese: 部屋のマリファナの匂いは銃の硝煙の匂いで大分打ち消されてはいたが、ゆったりとしたレゲエのBGMは相変わらずだった。その一方で、目に映る光景はさっきとは全く違う、死体の転がる凄惨な殺人現場となっている。
English: The smell of marijuana in the room had been largely overwhelmed by the gunsmoke, but the laid-back reggae continued to play in the background. Everything visible, however, had changed completely. The room was now a gruesome murder scene strewn with bodies.

Japanese: 先ほどまでここでくつろいでマリファナ遊びに興じていた六人もの人間は、一瞬にして血を流す死体に変わっていた。彼らはもう人間としては存在せず、これらの肉塊は微生物たちの養分となって腐り行く。
English: The six people who had relaxed here with marijuana only moments before had become bleeding corpses in an instant. They no longer existed as human beings. These masses of flesh would decay into nourishment for microorganisms.

Japanese: こんな場面を、犯行者がアップロードしたネットの映像や、新聞の記事で見たことはあるが、製作者の一人として現場に立つことになるとは思わなかった。今僕はどういう心境なのだろうか？
English: I had seen scenes like this in newspaper articles and in videos uploaded to the internet by the perpetrators. I had never imagined standing inside one as one of the people who had created it. What did I feel now?

Japanese: 僕はあどけない少女だった死体をじっと眺めた。
English: I stared at the body that had belonged to an innocent-looking girl.

Japanese: 見事に頭を打ち抜かれ、顔はまったくわからなくなっているが、若干派手目の服装はこのあたりではごく辺り前の物で、おそらく普段は普通の若者として遊び歩いていたのだろう。ここに遊びに来ていなければ、明日からも同じように遊べたに違いない。
English: A bullet had destroyed her head so completely that her face was no longer recognizable. But her somewhat showy clothes were perfectly ordinary in this part of the city. She had probably spent her days going out and amusing herself like any other young person. Had she not come here, she would surely have gone on doing the same tomorrow.

Japanese: それから、その父だった死体を眺めた。
English: Then I looked toward the body that had been her father.

Japanese: 百戦錬磨の彼にしてはあまりに油断しすぎているようにも思えたが、まあ無理もないのか。
English: For a man who had survived a hundred battles, he appeared to have been far too careless. Yet perhaps that was only natural.

Japanese: いまはどこかと抗争しているわけでもないし、彼が頻繁にトラブルを起こす市民達は、普通YSの名を恐れて復讐などしない。まさか、執行部が、先代の抜擢した幹部である自分に死を下すなんて想像もしなかったろう。もっと警戒をしていれば、僕らは襲撃自体を諦め、彼もまた明日を生きられたろう。
English: There was no conflict underway with another faction, and the citizens with whom he so frequently caused trouble ordinarily feared the name of YS too much to seek revenge. He could never have imagined that the executive would condemn him to death when the former Longtou himself had elevated him to officer. Had he been more cautious, we would have abandoned the attack itself, and he too might have lived to see tomorrow.

Japanese: 僕も彼を殺すことになるとは、ちょっと前まで想像もしていなかった。
English: Until a short time ago, I had never imagined that I would kill him either.

Japanese: この劉建志という人物のことはさほど嫌いではなかった。凶暴で頭は悪いけれど、その直情的でシンプルな人間性は、むしろ好きな方だ。子供の時からその豪快な行動の噂は聞いていた。
English: I had never especially disliked Ryu Kenshi. He was violent and stupid, but I rather enjoyed his direct and simple character. I had heard stories of his larger-than-life exploits since childhood.

Japanese: 「あまり気にしないことです」
English: “Best not to dwell on it.”

Japanese: 姜浩強が僕にそう話しかけた。
English: Jiang Haoqiang addressed me.

Japanese: 「この世界は、こういうものです。死んだ連中も誰かを殺してここまでやって来た。劉は特に罪深い二年でした。仲間も家族も、こうなるのは当然です」
