English: “This is the nature of our world. The dead reached this point by killing other people themselves. Ryu was an especially sinful man. It is only natural that his companions and family should meet the same end.”

Japanese: 僕はただ首を横に振り、
English: I merely shook my head.

Japanese: 「何も気にしていないよ。気にするかと思っていたけど、そうでもない。そのかわり、ちょっと、思い出した」
English: “I’m not concerned at all. I expected I might be, but apparently not. Instead, I remembered something.”

Japanese: 「何をですか？」
English: “Remembered what?”

Japanese: 「……子供の時のことだよ。昔、ヤツ川の畔にヌートリアが増えたことがあったでしょう？　あれを捕まえたことがあるんだ」
English: “...Something from my childhood. Do you remember when the nutria population exploded along the banks of the Yatsu River? I once caught one.”

Japanese: 「ヌートリア？」
English: “A nutria?”

Japanese: 「大きなネズミというか、カピバラというか、そんな動物だよ。……味がとにかく旨いってことで、みんなは肉に興味があった。僕は哺乳類の内臓が教科書で見た通りになっているのか確かめてみたかった。それで、みんなで自転車で繰り出したんだ」
English: “An animal like an enormous rat, or perhaps a capybara. ...Everyone was interested in the meat, which was said to be exceptionally good. I wanted to discover whether a mammal’s internal organs truly looked as they did in my textbooks. So all of us rode out there on our bicycles.”

Japanese: 「はあ」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 彼は僕の意図が読めず、生返事をする。
English: Unsure where I was going with this, he offered a noncommittal response.

Japanese: 「僕らはべつに動物をいじめたかったんじゃなくて、魚を食べるために釣りに行ったり、食用蛙が案外うまいと聞いてみんなで石を投げ込んだのと同じような雰囲気だったと思う。普段は猫や犬に石をぶつけたりといった、弱い物いじめにはみな抵抗があるような感じだったんでだけれど、食べるとなると、不思議なもので、そういう感覚はなくなるんだ。わかる？」
English: “We didn’t particularly want to torment an animal. I think it felt the same as when we went fishing because we meant to eat the fish, or when we heard edible frogs were surprisingly good and all went out to stone them. Ordinarily, everyone seemed reluctant to bully something weaker by throwing stones at cats or dogs. Yet once we meant to eat the animal, that resistance mysteriously vanished. Do you understand?”

Japanese: 僕は彼の返事を待たずに続ける。
English: I continued without waiting for his answer.

Japanese: 「それで、結局一匹捕まえることができた。みんなえらい興奮してたよ。押さえつけて、棒で殴り殺してから、僕がナイフを手にとって、解体をしたんだ。……今思い返してみれば、あれが僕にとって生まれて初めての動物の解剖実験だったんだなあ。……まあそれはともかく、腹を割いたところで、はじめてそいつがメスだったってのがわかったんだ。何でかっていうと、子宮から胎児がゴロゴロと出て来たんだよ」
English: “In the end, we caught one. Everyone was tremendously excited. We pinned it down, beat it to death with a stick, and then I took a knife and cut it apart. ...Looking back, that was the first animal dissection of my life. ...But never mind that. When I opened its belly, we learned for the first time that it was female. Do you know how? Fetuses came tumbling out of the uterus.”

Japanese: 僕は姜を振り返る。
English: I turned toward Jiang.

Japanese: 「みんな気持ち悪がったけど、焼いてみて味が旨いとわかると全部食った。なんとなく、その時の気持を思い出して、ぼうっとしてたんだ。いま」
English: “Everyone found it disgusting, but once we cooked the meat and discovered it tasted good, we ate all of it. I suppose I remembered how I felt then. That was why I was staring into space just now.”

Japanese: 彼は眉間にしわをよせて、困惑の表情を作る。
English: He frowned in confusion.

Japanese: 「……まあ、それだけです。ああ、べつに、遺体を解剖して人間の内臓を見てみたいと思ったっていう話じゃないよ？」
English: “...Well, that is all. Ah, I don’t mean that I wanted to dissect these bodies and see the organs inside them.”

Japanese: 「はあ、それはわかっていますが」
English: “Yes. I understood that much, but...”

Japanese: 姜は生返事を返す。
English: Jiang offered another noncommittal reply.

Japanese: まあ、とにかく僕を心配する必要なんかないんだ。本当は僕は前に一度だけ人を殺したことがあるし、その時銃も使った。
English: In any case, no one needed to worry about me. The truth was that I had killed a person once before, and I had used a gun then as well.

Japanese: そして僕は傍らに倒れていた椅子を起こして腰掛けようとしたが、足の一本が銃弾で打ち砕かれていてうまく立たせることが出来なかった。
English: I righted a chair lying beside me and attempted to sit, but a bullet had shattered one of its legs, and I could not make it stand properly.

Japanese: 僕は溜息をつく。
English: I sighed.

Japanese: とにかく、作戦としては完全なかたちで遂行することが出来たわけだ。予定したことがその通り完了しただけで、それほど嬉しくもないが、一つの成果を出したことにはかわらない。
English: In operational terms, everything had been completed perfectly. The plan had simply unfolded as intended, so it did not make me especially happy. Nevertheless, we had achieved one result.

Japanese: これはすべてのはじまりだ。これで僕は、正式にファミリーの一員となったのだ。
English: This was the beginning of everything. I had now become a formal member of the family.

Japanese: 緊張感が抜けるにつれて、じわじわと体中に疲労が満ちてゆく。脳を麻痺させていたドーパミンの影響が消え、世界に満ちあふれていた光が消えてゆく。
English: As the tension drained away, fatigue gradually filled my entire body. The dopamine that had numbed my brain lost its hold, and the light that had flooded the world went with it.

Japanese: そんななか、気がつけば世傑がデジカメを手に持って、凄惨な部屋の全景を、そして死体の一つ一つを撮影している。
English: Amid all this, I noticed Sai-kit holding a digital camera. He was photographing the gruesome room as a whole, then each individual body.

Japanese: 「もういいんじゃない？　作戦完了の報告写真は、もう充分撮れたはずだ」
English: “Isn’t that enough? You must have all the photographs you need to prove the job is done.”

Japanese: 僕が尋ねると、彼は笑顔を作り、
English: At my question, he smiled.

Japanese: 「これは趣味」
English: “These are for my hobby.”

Japanese: 「趣味？」
English: “Your hobby?”

Japanese: 「アタシは時間があるときはいつも殺した相手の写真を撮っているのよ。大事なメモリーだからね」
English: “Whenever time permits, I photograph everyone I kill. They are precious memories.”

Japanese: 「いい趣味だ」
English: “An excellent hobby.”

Japanese: 「そうでしょ」
English: “Isn’t it?”

Japanese: 彼はクスクスと笑い、撮影を再開した。
English: He giggled and resumed taking photographs.

Japanese: ぼんやりそれを眺めていると、段々まぶたが重くなってきた。
English: As I watched him in a daze, my eyelids gradually grew heavy.

Japanese: なんてことだろう？　こんな時に、例の睡魔がやって来てしまったらしい。
English: What was this? It appeared that the familiar sleepiness had arrived at this of all moments.

Japanese: 「なんだか眠くなった。一時間くらいここで眠っても安全だと思う？」
English: “I’m getting sleepy. Do you think it would be safe to sleep here for an hour?”

Japanese: 世傑に尋ねると、
English: I asked Sai-kit.

Japanese: 「まあ大丈夫かな。しかし、こんな地獄絵図みたいな部屋のなかで眠たくなるなんて、それも初仕事だっていうのに、なんてあきれた人なのかしら！」
English: “I suppose it would be safe. But falling asleep in a room like a vision of hell—and on your very first assignment! You truly are unbelievable.”

Japanese: 僕だってそう思う。いくら終わったとはいえ、今さっきまで殺しあいの興奮のまっただなかにいたのだ。興奮剤の『ピーク』だってまだ効き目が切れていないはずだ。どんな精神構造をしているのかと、自分の神経に問うてみたい。
English: I thought so too. The battle had ended, but only moments before, I had stood in the very heart of lethal excitement. The stimulant Peak should still have been active as well. I wanted to ask my own nervous system what sort of mental structure it was built around.

Japanese: 「眠たくなったんだからしょうがないよ」
English: “I’m sleepy. I can’t help it.”

Japanese: そう言う他ない。実際それは嘘偽りのない率直な感想だ。
English: There was nothing else I could say. It was, quite literally, how I felt.

Japanese: 僕は世傑が驚くのを尻目に、銃弾を受けて穴だらけになったソファーを手で払い、血液で濡れていないのを確認してからごろりと横になる。すると、睡魔はすぐに僕の意識を消し飛ばした。
English: Ignoring Sai-kit’s amazement, I brushed the debris from the sofa riddled with bullet holes, confirmed that it was not wet with blood, and stretched out upon it. The sleepiness immediately extinguished my consciousness.

Japanese: 眠りから覚めた僕の目に、まず入ってきたのはいつの間にか部屋にやって来ていた黄姉妹の姿だった。
English: When I woke, the first thing I saw was the Wong sisters, who had entered the room at some point.

Japanese: 彼女らは青ざめた顔でこちらを見つめており、そして僕が何も口にするまでもなく、
English: They stared at me with pale faces. Before I could say anything, they spoke in turn.

Japanese: 「初仕事、お見事でした」
English: “A splendid first assignment, Master Siu Tse.”

Japanese: 「劉建志ほどのものを相手に、よくぞご無事で」
English: “To have faced a man of Ryu Kenshi’s stature and returned unharmed...”

Japanese: と順番に口を開く。
English: they said in turn.

Japanese: 「ありがとう。でも、夜中に完全武装して襲ったんだからまあ当然だよ。相手が本気で警戒してたらわからなかったけどね」
English: “Thank you. But we attacked fully armed in the middle of the night. This much was only natural. I cannot say what would have happened if he had been genuinely alert.”

Japanese: 「ご謙遜を」
English: “You are too modest.”

Japanese: その時僕は、黄姉妹の表情が異常にこわばっているのに気がついた。
English: Then I noticed how unusually tense the Wong sisters looked.

Japanese: 「こういうのは慣れていないのかい？」
English: “You are not accustomed to this sort of thing?”

Japanese: 僕が尋ねると、彼女らは申し訳なさそうに頷き、姉妹で交互に話す。
English: At my question, they nodded apologetically and took turns answering.

Japanese: 「お恥ずかしい話ですが」
English: “It is shameful to admit...”

Japanese: 「僕たちは、いつもクリス様の側で不審者の接近を見張るのが仕事で、このように襲撃に参加するのは初めてなのです」
English: “Our work has always been to remain beside Lord Chris and watch for the approach of suspicious persons. This is the first time we have participated in an assault of this nature.”

Japanese: 「実際、僕らがお仕えするようになってから、そんな不届きものはあらわれていませんし」
English: “In fact, no such intruder has appeared since we entered his service.”

Japanese: 「それは悪いことをした」
English: “Then I owe you an apology.”

Japanese: 彼女らは、その能力で敵の生命が消えてゆくさまを見ていたのだろう。そしてこの現場の惨状も耐えがたいのかもしれない。
English: Through their ability, they had presumably sensed the lives of our enemies disappearing. Perhaps they also found the horror of this scene difficult to endure.

Japanese: 本人たちが気にするようなことではない。子供の頃から業界で働いているとはいえ姉妹は僕と年のかわらない女性なのだし、こうした場面を見たことがないのなら、これくらいの動揺は無理もないことだ。
English: It was nothing for which they ought to blame themselves. Though they had worked in this world since childhood, the sisters were women my own age. If they had never seen such a scene before, a measure of distress was only natural.

Japanese: 「いえ、いいんです。これからはクリス様のかわりに小謝様の側でお仕えするよう、父に言われておりますので」
English: “No, it is quite all right. Father has told us that from now on, we are to serve beside you in place of Lord Chris, Master Siu Tse.”

Japanese: その言葉に、僕は思わず顔を顰めた。
English: At those words, I frowned despite myself.

Japanese: 「そこまでするほどじゃない。僕は龍頭でもなんでもないんだから」
English: “There is no need to go so far. I am not the Longtou or anything of the kind.”

Japanese: 言うと、姉妹は戸惑いを見せる。
English: The sisters appeared troubled by my answer.

Japanese: その顔を見て、自分がこの先リーダーとしてやってゆくためには、こうした他人の献身を笑顔で受け入れて彼らのモチベーションを高めていかなければならないのだと気がついた。
English: Seeing their faces, I realized that if I meant to lead others from now on, I would have to accept such devotion with a smile and use it to keep them motivated.

Japanese: しかし、そんな振る舞いは、今の僕には難しそうだった。
English: For the moment, such behavior seemed beyond me.

Japanese: 「それにしても、本当にアンタ、銃で人を撃つの初めてなの？」
English: “Still, was this truly your first time shooting a human being?”

Japanese: 帰ろうとして立ち上がると、世傑がそう訊ねた。
English: As I rose to leave, Sai-kit asked the question.

Japanese: 「人を撃つどころか生き物を撃ったことがない。今回この仕事をするにあたって、昨日グランドタワーの駐車場で練習したくらいだよ」
English: “I had never shot any living thing, much less a person. To prepare for this work, I practiced in the Grand Tower parking lot yesterday. That is the extent of my experience.”

Japanese: 「信じられないわ」
English: “I cannot believe it.”

Japanese: 「これだけ近距離で、あれだけ的が大きければ当てるだけなら誰でも出来るさ」
English: “At this distance, with targets that large, anyone could hit them.”

Japanese: 「違うのよ。人間ってさ、人を殺すのってすごい抵抗があるものなのね。だから、最初に生きている人間を撃つときってどんなに射撃が上手くても、無意識に弾をそらしていないところを撃っちゃうものなの。でも、アンタの弾は全部人間に向かって飛んでたわ。迷いなく」
English: “That isn’t what I mean. Human beings feel tremendous resistance to killing another person. The first time someone fires upon a living human being, however skilled a marksman he may be, his aim drifts unconsciously and he shoots where no one is standing. But every one of your bullets traveled toward a human being. Without hesitation.”

Japanese: 世傑は右手の人差し指と親指を立てて鉄砲を撃つ真似をして、
English: Sai-kit raised the thumb and forefinger of his right hand and mimed firing a pistol.

Japanese: 「本当に今日がはじめてなら、アンタ、才能があるわよ」
English: “If today truly was your first time, then you have a gift.”

Japanese: 感心したように一人頷くが、人殺しの才能があると言われても、僕は肩をすくめるしかなかった。
English: He nodded to himself in admiration. Told that I possessed a talent for killing people, I could only shrug.

Japanese: そして僕は、一反は起き上がったソファーに再びもたれて溜息をつく。
English: I sank back against the sofa from which I had just risen and sighed once more.

Japanese: なんだかひどく疲れた。
English: I felt terribly tired.

Japanese: むしょうに松子に会いたい。YSの仕事をするようになってから、彼女と一度も会っていないし、彼女からの連絡も返さないでいる。どうしても、そんな気になれなかったからだ。
English: I wanted desperately to see Matsuko. I had not seen her once since beginning my work for YS, and I had left every message from her unanswered. I had been unable to bring myself to respond.

Japanese: だけれど、今はとにかく会いたい。そして、子供の時からずっと続く、彼女と二人きりでいるときにしか生まれないあの特別な空気に身を浸したかった。
English: Now, however, I wanted above all else to see her. I wanted to immerse myself in that special atmosphere that had existed since childhood and arose only when the two of us were alone.

Japanese: しかしそれは、今の僕にはかなわぬことだ。
English: Yet that was impossible for me now.

Japanese: 夜が明けてからグランドタワーに帰還すると、劉の処刑を伝える書面がジェフリーによって起草され、それに劉建志の遺体写真が添付されたメールが、龍頭マイケル・ツェーの名で組織に所属するすべての人物に送信された。
English: When we returned to the Grand Tower after dawn, Jeffrey drafted a document announcing Ryu’s execution. An email containing it, together with a photograph of Ryu Kenshi’s body, was sent in the name of Longtou Michael Tse to every person in the organization.

Japanese: 「もうごちゃごちゃくだらないことを考えたって仕方ねえ。廖の野郎を殺すのが一番だ」
English: “There’s no point thinking ourselves in circles over this rubbish. The best thing we can do is kill that bastard Liao.”

Japanese: 馬明はもうとっくに考えるのを放棄して、同じ自説を繰り返し訴えている。
English: Ma Ming had long since given up thinking and was simply repeating the same proposal over and over.

Japanese: 「YSの中で争ってる場合じゃねえんだよ。内紛をしていれば、老人達も大人しくしてはいないだろうし、木下組の連中もちょっかいを出してくるのは確実だ」
English: “This is no time for YS to be fighting among itself. If we fall into an internal struggle, the Elders won’t stay quiet, and the Kinoshita-gumi are certain to make a move on us.”

Japanese: 木下組というのは日本最大の広域暴力団U会系の暴力団で、この辺りの都市では大きな勢力を持っている。一時はY地区にも進出をはかり、先代のクリス・ツェー率いるYSと抗争になったこともある。現在はY地区へは手出ししないという約束を取り付けているが、多くの人と金が集まるこの街に対する野心を失ったわけではないだろう。
English: The Kinoshita-gumi was an affiliate of the U-kai, Japan’s largest national criminal syndicate, and held considerable power in the cities around us. It had once attempted to expand into Y District, bringing it into conflict with YS under the former Longtou, Chris Tse. We had since secured its promise to leave Y District alone, but there was little chance that it had lost its appetite for a city where so many people and so much money converged.

Japanese: 「迷ってる場合じゃない。やるしかねえんだよ」
English: “We can’t afford to hesitate. We have to act.”

Japanese: 荒ぶる馬明とは対象的に、ジェフリー・ウォンはしかめっ面でその考えを黙殺するのみだ。
English: In contrast to the raging Ma Ming, Jeffrey Wong merely frowned and refused to dignify the idea with a response.

Japanese: 可哀想にジェフリーはすっかり憔悴しきっている。目の下のくまは濃く、頬の肉も幾分そげ落ちたようだ。
English: Poor Jeffrey was thoroughly worn down. The shadows beneath his eyes were deep, and even his cheeks appeared to have lost some flesh.

Japanese: 自分の醜態が町中にばらまかれているのが相当きついらしい。まあ当然だろう。そんな目に遭ったら、誰だってきつい。僕だってきつい。
English: Having evidence of his disgrace scattered throughout the city had apparently taken a considerable toll. Naturally it had. Anyone would find such treatment difficult. I certainly would.

Japanese: くだらない手ではあるけれど、相手を消耗させるという点においては案外有効なものだと感心してしまう。消耗すれば当然普段よりミスが増えるだろうし、まるっきり無駄というわけでもないのだ。
English: The tactic was contemptible, but I found myself impressed by how unexpectedly effective it was at exhausting its target. Exhaustion would naturally produce more mistakes than usual, so the effort was not entirely pointless.

Japanese: こういうやり方もアリなのか。ジェフリーの顔を見ながらそんなことを考えた。
English: Perhaps this sort of method had its uses too. I considered the possibility as I looked at Jeffrey’s face.

Japanese: そしてその顔を見ると、僕でさえあのビラに印刷されていたジェフリーのヨガる顔を無意識のうちに思い出してしまうのだから残酷だ。
English: And it was cruel that even I, upon seeing that face, involuntarily recalled the image on those flyers of Jeffrey in the throes of orgasm.

Japanese: だがジェフリーはそのことに対して一言も恨み節を言わない。自分の落ち度だと感じているのか、話題に触れたくないのか、おそらく両方だろう。
English: Yet Jeffrey had not uttered one resentful word about it. Perhaps he regarded it as his own failing; perhaps he simply did not want the subject raised. Most likely both.

Japanese: ビラのことは無視し、これまで通り職務を遂行していきたいという考えのようだが、馬明の方がそれでは納得がいかないようだった。
English: He appeared determined to ignore the flyers and discharge his duties as before, but Ma Ming plainly found that response unacceptable.

Japanese: 「町中のやつが、廖の仕業だと思っている。それで何もしなければ、お前はただ笑われるだけじゃなく、腰抜けだと軽蔑されるようになるぞ」
English: “Everyone in the city thinks Liao did it. If you do nothing, they won’t merely laugh at you. They’ll despise you as a coward.”

Japanese: 「しかし、証拠がないんだ。あの件に廖が関わっていたという証拠が。どれだけうまくやったのか知らないが、実行犯も主犯も、まったく見つからないんだよ」
English: “But we have no proof. No proof that Liao had anything to do with it. I don’t know how skillfully it was done, but we have found neither the people who carried it out nor whoever was behind it.”

Japanese: しつこい馬明に根負けして、ついにジェフリーもその話題につきあった。
English: Worn down by Ma Ming’s persistence, Jeffrey finally consented to discuss the subject.

Japanese: 「警察や法律家じゃあるまいし、我々の行動に証拠なんか必要ない！　そうであるとみなが確信出来ればそれで決まりだ！　大体、他に犯人がいるわけないだろうが。これはお前個人じゃなく、我々ファミリーに対する挑戦なんだよ。あの野郎の命をとるんだ。それ以外に我々が名誉を回復する方法はない。会議か何かでグランドタワーにやって来たところでそのアタマを銃で撃ち抜いてやるだけだ。簡単な話だよ」
English: “We’re not the police or lawyers. We don’t need proof before we act! If everyone is convinced he did it, then that settles the matter! Who else could possibly be responsible? This wasn’t a challenge to you alone. It was a challenge to our family. We take that bastard’s life. There is no other way to restore our honor. The next time he comes to Grand Tower for a meeting or anything else, we put a bullet through his head. Simple.”

Japanese: 馬明はジェフリーの言い分がまったく気にいらない様子だ。
English: Ma Ming appeared utterly disgusted with Jeffrey’s argument.

Japanese: 「お前はお行儀が良すぎる。それじゃこの先やっていけないぞ」
English: “You’re too well behaved. You won’t survive like that.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは静かに首を振って答える。
English: Jeffrey quietly shook his head before answering.

Japanese: 「我々には大義名分が必要だ。劉建志を処刑した時のように、廖志明を殺すならばそれに見合った罪が必要だ。私個人を中傷したというだけでは、仮に証拠があったとしても、YSとして殺す理由にはならない」
English: “We require a legitimate cause. Just as when we executed Ryu Kenshi, Liao Chi-ming would need to have committed a crime commensurate with his death. Even if we possessed proof that he had slandered me personally, that alone would not give YS cause to kill him.”

Japanese: 「じゃあどうするつもりだ！　お前が愛人と愉しんでいようがいまいが勝手だが、それを公然と笑いものにされたというのがいかん。侮辱されても黙っているというのは、軽く見られるだけだ。お前はやはり自分を政治家か何かと勘違いしている。スキャンダルで世間の非難を浴びたから、補佐役を降りるとでも言い出しかねない」
English: “Then what do you propose to do? Whether or not you amuse yourself with a mistress is your affair. What matters is that they made a public spectacle of you for it. If you suffer an insult in silence, people will only take you lightly. You still imagine yourself some sort of politician. Next you’ll say the public outrage over your scandal obliges you to resign as chief adviser.”

Japanese: 「場合によってはそれも必要だと思っている」
English: “Depending upon the circumstances, I believe that may indeed be necessary.”

Japanese: 「これは呆れる！　どうしちまったんだよ、おい！　一体全体どんな優良企業の役員のつもりでいるんだい？　我々はマフィアなんだ。愛されたり、支持されるよりも、恐れられることが重要だ！　恐怖なくして我々の仕事など存在しない。思い出せ！　腰抜け！」
English: “Unbelievable! What happened to you? What kind of respectable corporate executive do you imagine you are? We are the mafia. Being feared matters more than being loved or supported! Without fear, our business cannot exist. Remember that, you coward!”

Japanese: 馬明は激昂して机を叩くが、ジェフリーはその挑発には乗らない。
English: Ma Ming slammed the desk in a fury, but Jeffrey refused to rise to the provocation.

Japanese: むしろその声はますます低く冷徹になる。
English: If anything, his voice grew lower and colder.

Japanese: 「みなで裏通りをかけずり回っていた頃とは違う。我々はクーラーもないあばら屋で半裸で会議をしていた『義勝』ではなく、街で一番大きいビルを根城にする『YS』なんだよ。マフィアにも品格というものがある」
English: “Things are different from when we all ran through the back streets together. We are no longer ‘Yisheng,’ holding meetings half naked in a shack without air-conditioning. We are ‘YS,’ headquartered in the largest building in the city. Even the mafia must possess dignity.”

Japanese: 「まったく、なんてつまらない男に成り下がってしまったんだ！　お前は！」
English: “What a tedious man you’ve become! Honestly!”

Japanese: 馬明はもう一度机を叩く。
English: Ma Ming struck the desk once more.

Japanese: 「つまらないもなにも、YSとこの街がギブアンドテイクの関係にあるのは確かだ。我々は警察や法律が意味をなさないこの街に暴力によってある程度の秩序をもたらし、その見返りとして住人は我々に協力してくれている。この関係を崩しては我々は存在価値を失う」
English: “Tedious or not, it remains true that YS and this city exist in a relationship of give-and-take. Through violence, we provide a measure of order in a city where the police and the law mean nothing. In return, its residents cooperate with us. If we destroy that relationship, we lose our reason to exist.”

Japanese: 「だからおれは、公然と侮辱されて何もしかえしをしないような指導者が率いるマフィアじゃ、街の連中からもなめられ、やつらを従わせる恐怖感も、やつらからの信頼も失うと言っている！」
English: “And I am telling you that if this mafia is led by a man who does nothing when he is publicly humiliated, the people of the city will despise us. We will lose both the fear that keeps them obedient and the trust they place in us!”

Japanese: 「私はそうは思わない。重要なのはフェアであることだ」
English: “I disagree. What matters is that we are fair.”

Japanese: こうした二人のやりとりを、僕はなんだかおかしく見守っていた。中傷された本人が慎重論を口にして、蚊帳の外にいる人間が本人以上に激怒して報復を訴えている。
English: I watched their exchange with a certain amusement. The man who had been slandered was urging restraint, while a man entirely outside the affair was angrier than the victim himself and clamoring for revenge.

Japanese: 父が生きているころは、この間でうまくバランスをとっていたのかもしれないが、第二代龍頭はおろおろしながら不安げに二人を見守るだけだ。
English: Perhaps Father had once maintained a skillful balance between them, but the second Longtou could do no more than watch the two men in nervous bewilderment.

Japanese: もっとも僕も今この場で黙って傍観しているわけだから、あまり二代目のことを悪くも言えないのだが。
English: Then again, I too was standing by in silence, so I could hardly criticize the second Longtou too severely.

Japanese: しかし、今黙っているといっても、このジェフリーの問題についてすべてを放棄したわけではない。
English: My silence did not mean I had given up on Jeffrey’s situation entirely, however.

Japanese: 「ジェフリー、心配しなくてもいいよ。廖志明に、こんな素晴らしく卑劣な行為を選んだことを後悔させる方法はいくらでもあるんだ」
English: “Jeffrey, there’s no need to worry. There are any number of ways to make Liao Chi-ming regret choosing such a magnificently underhanded tactic.”

Japanese: 僕は横合いからそう口をはさんだ。
English: I interjected from the side.

Japanese: 「小謝、まさか何かするつもりではありませんね？」
English: “Siu Tse, you aren’t planning anything, are you?”

Japanese: 僕が頷くと、ジェフリーは苦い顔をして、
English: When I nodded, Jeffrey grimaced.

Japanese: 「何かするならば、事前に告知してください。廖志明への対応は非常に重要です。勝手にいろいろとされては困ります」
English: “If you intend to act, notify me in advance. Our response to Liao Chi-ming is an extremely serious matter. I cannot have you undertaking things at your own discretion.”

Japanese: 「まるで僕の指導教官になったみたいだ」
English: “You sound exactly like my faculty adviser.”

Japanese: 僕は肩をすくめる他ない。
English: I could only shrug.

Japanese: そうして彼らの議論が紛糾し、聞いている僕の方が疲れ始める頃、一通のメールが届いた。
English: Their argument became so tangled that even I was growing tired of hearing it when an email arrived.

Japanese: それはYSの幹部同士のやりとりに使われる、ごく限られた人間しか知らないアドレス宛のメールで、発信者は廖志明であった。
English: It had been sent to an address used for correspondence among YS officers and known only to that very small circle. Its sender was Liao Chi-ming.

Japanese: 僕と馬明とジェフリーの三人は、レイレイがプリントアウトして持って来たその手紙をのぞき込み、そして最後まで読み終わると、お互いに困惑の顔を向け合った。
English: Leilei printed the message and brought it to us. Ma Ming, Jeffrey, and I crowded around the letter, read it to the end, then looked at one another in confusion.

Japanese: 内容は、廖の屋敷に侵入者があったという報告であった。
English: It reported that an intruder had entered Liao’s residence.

Japanese: 誰もいないはずの部屋で物音がして、駆けつけると黒衣の女が立っていたらしい。足元には搬入したばかりの胸像が切断されていたが、女はそれを可能にするような道具は何も持っていなかった。
English: A noise had been heard in a room that ought to have been empty. When people rushed to investigate, they allegedly found a woman dressed in black. A bust that had only just been brought into the room lay severed at her feet, although she carried no implement capable of cutting it.

Japanese: 女は「街の怒りを代表するものだ」と名乗り、YSの幹部である廖志明の命を狙いに来たのだと言った。ボディガードのエリオットが発砲すると幽霊が消えるかのように姿を消して退散し、廖は難を逃れたと言う。
English: The woman had called herself ‘a representative of the city’s anger’ and said she had come for the life of Liao Chi-ming, an officer of YS. When his bodyguard Elliott opened fire, she vanished like a ghost and withdrew, leaving Liao unharmed—or so the report said.

Japanese: メールには切断された銅像の画像が添付されていた。
English: An image of the severed bronze bust was attached to the email.

Japanese: これだけだったら、驚きのニュースではあるにしろ、僕たちがそこまで困惑することはなかったろう。
English: Had that been all, the news would certainly have surprised us, but not left us quite so perplexed.

Japanese: 報告のあとに書かれた廖の言葉がふるっている。
English: The words Liao appended to his report were remarkable.

Japanese: 『当人はYSに恨みある者だと名乗っていたが、このような不審者の言葉を素直に信じるのは難しい。そもそも、もし言った通りの理由ならば、真っ先に龍頭どのを襲うのが自然である。なのに最初に標的にしたのは私だった。……あるいはこの女は私個人に恨みがある者によって雇われたというのが真実かもしれない。となれば、最近私に対して憎しみをもった者が真犯人と考えるのが自然だろう。残念ながら心当たる者がいないのだが、逆恨みかもしれぬ。そうであれば危険が及ぶのは私だけだろうが、しかし、本人が言ったとおり、YS全体を憎んでいる人物による犯行という可能性もなくはない。諸兄は念のため、身辺の警備体制などを見直されるべきである』
English: ‘The individual claimed to bear a grudge against YS, but it is difficult to take the word of such a suspicious person at face value. If her stated reason were genuine, it would be natural for her to attack the Longtou first. Yet I was her first target. ...Perhaps the truth is that this woman was hired by someone who holds a personal grudge against me. In that case, it would be natural to suppose that the true culprit is someone who has recently come to hate me. Regrettably, no such person occurs to me, though the motive may be misplaced resentment. If so, I alone should be in danger. However, one cannot entirely exclude the possibility that, as she claimed, this was the work of someone who hates YS as a whole. As a precaution, I recommend that each of you review the security arrangements surrounding your person.’

Japanese: 「なんだか、おれ達が刺客を雇ったと言いたいみたいだな」
English: “It sounds as if he’s trying to say we hired the assassin.”

Japanese: 馬明が苦い顔で言ったとおり、とりようによってはそのような当てこすりをしているようにも読める。
English: As Ma Ming observed with a grimace, it was possible to read the message as precisely that sort of insinuation.

Japanese: 「失礼な野郎だ！　本当に送り込んでやろうか！」
English: “The insolent bastard! Perhaps we ought to send one for real!”

Japanese: 「いや待て馬明。それじゃ廖の思うつぼだ。彼の警備は常に厳重だが、メールによると今回の件で警備を強化するとも書いてある。成功の見込みはさらに薄くなった」
English: “No, wait, Ma Ming. That would play directly into Liao’s hands. His security is always formidable, and the email says he will strengthen it further in response to this incident. Our chances of success have only diminished.”

Japanese: 「そんなもの、武器と人を揃えてしっかり計画を練ればどうにでもなる。なあ小謝？」
English: “With enough weapons and men and a proper plan, we could manage it. Isn’t that right, Siu Tse?”

Japanese: 「いや、今回はそんな簡単なものじゃないと思うよ。廖は用心深い。僕がやったような襲われる心配をしてないやつの寝起きを襲うのとは違うんだ」
English: “No. I don’t think this one would be so simple. Liao is cautious. It would be nothing like what I did—attacking a man in his sleep who had no fear that anyone would come for him.”

Japanese: 僕の返事に顔を歪める馬明に、ジェフリーはさらに言う。
English: Ma Ming twisted his face at my reply, and Jeffrey continued.

Japanese: 「いずれ決定的な対立は避けられないとしても、現段階で挑発に乗って戦争を仕掛けるのは下策だ。我々の方から無用の血を強いるような真似をすれば、幹部の多くは廖に味方するだろう。そうなればフェルナンデスも中立とは限らない。我々が窮地に立つことになる」
English: “Even if a decisive confrontation is ultimately unavoidable, launching a war now because we took his bait would be folly. If we are the ones to force needless bloodshed upon YS, many of the officers will side with Liao. Even Fernandes may not remain neutral. We would place ourselves in an untenable position.”

Japanese: 「ふざけてやがる」
English: “This is bullshit.”

Japanese: ジェフリーの言葉に一応は納得したようだが、それでも馬明の怒りは到底収まらないようだった。
English: Ma Ming appeared to accept Jeffrey’s argument in principle, but he was far from appeased.

Japanese: 「それにしても、うさんくさいメールですな」
English: “Nevertheless, this is a deeply suspicious email.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは文面を改めて眺めながらそう言った。
English: Jeffrey spoke as he examined the text once more.

Japanese: 「一体どれくらい真実が書かれているのか。そもそも、本当に襲撃者はあったのか？　自分達の武装強化を正当化し、我々へのいわれのない不信感を煽るのが目的ではないのか？」
English: “How much of it is true? Was there genuinely an attacker at all? Is his real purpose not to justify strengthening his own forces while fomenting groundless suspicion of us?”

Japanese: 「……とりあえず、この件は調査が必要なようですな」
English: “...For the present, it appears this matter requires investigation.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは厳かにそう言った。
English: Jeffrey pronounced the conclusion gravely.

Japanese: 「ひとまず、廖志明に詳しい話をききましょう。……レイレイ、廖志明につないでくれませんか？」
English: “First, we will obtain a fuller account from Liao Chi-ming. ...Leilei, would you connect me with him?”

Japanese: 「僕がかわりに話そうか？」
English: “Would you like me to speak to him instead?”

Japanese: 例のスキャンダル写真のことがあるから、冷静に会話が出来るか心配だった。
English: In light of the scandalous photograph, I was concerned that Jeffrey might not be able to converse calmly.

Japanese: 「その方がいいかもしれないな」
English: “That might be better.”

Japanese: 僕の意図を察して馬明も同調してくれるが、
English: Ma Ming understood my intent and agreed, but—

Japanese: 「私の方が良いでしょう。これは筆頭補佐官である私の役目です」
English: “I am the better choice. This is the duty of the chief adviser.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはにべもない。
English: Jeffrey rejected the suggestion flatly.

Japanese: 廖志明との通話は十分に満たない短い時間で終わった。その間、ジェフリーの口調は普段よりも若干固くは感じられたが、取り乱すこともなく、相手の声は聞こえなかったにしろ、受け答えも妥当のように思えた。
English: The call with Liao Chi-ming ended in less than ten minutes. Jeffrey’s tone sounded slightly more rigid than usual throughout, but he never lost his composure. Although we could not hear the other man’s voice, Jeffrey’s answers appeared reasonable.

Japanese: 「襲撃者が現れたのは事実だが、その能力については目の当たりにしてもおらず、全く推測も出来ない、ということだ」
English: “He says that an attacker did appear, but he did not witness her ability and cannot even speculate as to its nature.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはそう言って、机の上に投げ出すように両手を置いて、その指を組んだ。
English: Jeffrey rested both hands on the desk and interlaced his fingers as he spoke.

Japanese: 「フードで顔が隠されていたが、声からするとまったく知らない人物だった。使った言葉は発音のおかしい英語。屋敷のまわりを監視しているカメラにも何も写っていなかったらしい。おそろしい相手だから、くれぐれも気をつけるように、とのことだ」
English: “Her hood concealed her face, but judging by her voice, she was a complete stranger to him. She spoke English with a strange accent. Apparently none of the cameras monitoring the area around the residence recorded anything. He warns us that the adversary is terrifying and that we must exercise the greatest possible caution.”

Japanese: 「身に染みる忠告痛み入るね」
English: “We are profoundly grateful for advice born of such intimate experience.”

Japanese: 僕は苦笑してしまう。
English: I could not help smiling bitterly.

Japanese: 襲撃者の能力の手がかりや容姿など、一番大事な情報だけが完全に抜け落ちている。これで気をつけろ、はない。
English: The most important information—clues to the attacker’s ability or appearance—was entirely absent. Under those conditions, telling us to exercise caution was absurd.

Japanese: もし廖の言っていることがすべて事実だとしたら、あの厳重な警備を突破して屋敷に潜り込み、しかも銅像をこわすなんていういたずらをやってのけた高度な能力者を、能力の手がかりもなしにどう対策しろというのだろう？
English: If everything Liao said was true, then someone with an extraordinarily powerful ability had penetrated that formidable security and even indulged in the prank of destroying a bronze bust. How were we supposed to prepare for such a person without the slightest clue to her ability?

Japanese: 「どこまで本当で、どこが嘘やら」
English: “Who knows where the truth ends and the lies begin?”

Japanese: 馬明は溜息をつく。
English: Ma Ming sighed.

Japanese: 「僕は、我々を狙うタイプA自体は存在するんだと思うよ」
English: “I do think a Type A who means to attack us actually exists.”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、ジェフリーはこちらに視線をやり、
English: At my words, Jeffrey looked at me.

Japanese: 「根拠はありますか？」
English: “Do you have grounds for that conclusion?”

Japanese: その言い方はなんとなくトゲがある。僕がたびたび彼の意向を無視したような言動をとるのを、少なからず不快に思っているのかもしれない。
English: There was something faintly barbed in the question. Perhaps my repeated tendency to speak and act in defiance of his intentions displeased him more than a little.

Japanese: 「根拠って言うほど確かなものじゃないけど、完全なでっち上げだとしたら、書かれた情報がいびつで不自然すぎるからね。おそらく廖は、僕らを狙う何者かの存在を察知していて、それが実際に行動を起こした時、自分に疑いがかかることを避けるためにこんな手紙を事前に送りつけたんだ。もちろん、僕らが襲撃者に殺されること自体は大歓迎だから襲撃者の能力といったような大事な情報は教えない。……そう考えると不自然さは消える」
English: “Nothing firm enough to call grounds. But if the entire story were fabricated, the information he gave us would be too lopsided and unnatural. I suspect Liao learned that someone meant to attack us and sent this letter in advance so that suspicion would not fall upon him once the person acted. Of course, he would be delighted if the attacker killed us, so he withheld the important information, such as the nature of her ability. ...Viewed that way, the peculiarities disappear.”

Japanese: 「そうだ！　きっとそうに違いない。今すぐ廖を呼んで絞り上げよう」
English: “Exactly! That must be it. Summon Liao at once and squeeze the truth out of him.”

Japanese: 馬明は手を打って喜ぶが、
English: Ma Ming clapped his hands in delight, but—

Japanese: 「そんなこと出来るわけないでしょう。こんなのは所詮僕の想像だし、それこそ執行部の暴走だって、廖に口実を与えることになる」
English: “We plainly cannot do that. This is only my speculation. It would hand Liao the perfect grounds for accusing the executive of running wild.”

Japanese: 僕は苦い顔をする。
English: I grimaced.

Japanese: 先日、劉を殺したことで、幹部達は少なからず動揺している。その死を悲しむような者は少なかったが、新しい執行部が内規にふれたとはいえ、香港派として知られている幹部を殺害して峻烈な姿勢を示したのだ。
English: Our killing of Ryu Kenshi the other day had badly unsettled the officers. Few had mourned him, but the new executive had nevertheless killed an officer known to belong to the Hong Kong faction for violating the internal code, demonstrating an implacable severity.

Japanese: 新執行部をなめていた彼らに一定の緊張感を与えることには成功したようだが、それが我々にとって好ましい反応を引き起こすかどうかは、まだはっきりとはしない。
English: We appeared to have succeeded in instilling a measure of tension among people who had held the new executive in contempt. It was not yet clear, however, whether that tension would provoke a reaction favorable to us.

Japanese: 現在のところ、YSの覇権を争う舞台に上がっているのは我々と廖志明で、あとの連中は照明のあたらない観客席で自らの態度を保留している。まあ、廖志明もはっきりとそう言ったわけではないが、最近の発言や態度を知っているものならば、その野心を疑うものはいないだろう。
English: At present, we and Liao Chi-ming occupied the stage upon which the contest for supremacy over YS was being fought. The others withheld judgment from seats beyond the reach of the lights. Liao had never explicitly declared himself a contender, naturally, but no one acquainted with his recent words and conduct could doubt his ambition.

Japanese: その廖は他の幹部を仲間につけて、正式な手順で我々を執行部の座から追放しようとしている。ここで隙を見せるようなことは出来ない、というのが僕の基本的な考え方だ。
English: Liao meant to bring the other officers over to his side and use formal procedure to expel us from the executive. My fundamental position was that we could afford to expose no weakness now.

Japanese: 「まあ、襲撃者が存在するという前提で調べ、警備も固めましょう。この件について今できることはそれしかない。我々は、他にも沢山の仕事を抱えているのですから」
English: “Very well. We will investigate on the assumption that the attacker exists and strengthen our security as well. There is nothing else we can do about the matter at present. We have a great many other duties to attend to.”

Japanese: 最後にジェフリーはそう言って、溜息をついた。
English: With those final words, Jeffrey sighed.

Japanese: 結局その日はそれ以上顔をつきあわせても何も進展がないということで、解散し、それぞれの仕事に戻ることとなった。
English: Ultimately, we concluded that remaining there together any longer that day would produce no progress. We dispersed and returned to our respective work.

Japanese: グランドタワーを出る前に、久しぶりに筱喬に会っていこうかと、ふと思った。思えば父が死んでからこっち、たまに顔を合わせる程度で会話らしい会話をしていない。
English: Before leaving Grand Tower, I suddenly thought that I might visit Siu-kiu for the first time in a while. Since Father’s death, I had done little more than exchange an occasional glance with her, never anything that deserved to be called a conversation.

Japanese: 忙しかったのもあるが、僕がなんとなく避けていたというのも間違いではない。
English: I had been busy, but it was also true that I had somehow been avoiding her.

Japanese: 幼い頃、あれだけ一人で生きることを強調していた僕が、結局父のあとを継ぐ形になってしまったことが、なんとなく気まずかった。そして劉建志を殺してからは、そのことが話題になるのが面倒で、なおさら足が遠のいた。
English: As a child, I had placed such emphasis upon living independently, only to end up succeeding Father after all. The result made me feel vaguely uncomfortable. After killing Ryu Kenshi, I had found the prospect of that subject arising too troublesome and stayed away even more.

Japanese: しかし、いつまでも避けているわけにもいかないだろう。僕らは二人きりの兄妹なのだ。
English: But I could hardly avoid her forever. We were each other’s only sibling.

Japanese: 意を決して、そのドアの前に向かうとノックした。
English: I made up my mind, went to her door, and knocked.
“Who is it?”

Japanese: 「僕だよ」
English: “It’s me.”

Japanese: 「……お兄ちゃん？」
English: “...Big Brother?”

Japanese: 内側から静かにドアが開き、そして僕たちは顔を合わせた。
English: The door quietly opened from within, and we stood face-to-face.

Japanese: 筱喬は僕の顔を見ると、ぎょっと驚きの表情を見せる。
English: The instant Siu-kiu saw me, she looked startled.

Japanese: 「どうかした？」
English: “Is something wrong?”

Japanese: 「ううん、なんでもない」
English: “No. It’s nothing.”

Japanese: 筱喬はあきらかに動揺しながら否定する。そして僕を部屋に招き入れると、窓の側のレースのカーテン越しに日の差し込む椅子に腰掛けた。身体が重そうな気怠い雰囲気で、少し痩せたようだった。
English: Visibly shaken, Siu-kiu denied it. She invited me into the room, then sat in a chair beside the window, where sunlight filtered through the lace curtains. She moved as though her body felt heavy and wore a languid air; she also looked somewhat thinner.

Japanese: 彼女は父が死んだ後も引き続きこのグランドタワーで生活をしている。
English: She had continued to live in Grand Tower after Father’s death.

Japanese: 父のかわりに彼女の面倒を見ているのは第二代龍頭であるマイケル・ツェーだった。そして普段はマイケルの妻子や、他のグランドタワー住みの幹部の女家族と交流しながら過ごしているらしい。
English: The second Longtou, Michael Tse, had taken Father’s place in looking after her. She apparently spent her days in the company of Michael’s wife and children and the female relatives of other officers who lived in Grand Tower.

Japanese: 初代龍頭の娘である筱喬が組織のVIPなのは確かだし、しかも世間知らずの上にタイプBであるから、保護という意味でも叔父であり龍頭でもあるマイケル・ツェーがこのビルで面倒を見るのはまあ妥当だろう。
English: As the first Longtou’s daughter, Siu-kiu was undoubtedly a person of importance to the organization. She was also ignorant of the outside world and a Type B. It was therefore reasonable, in terms of her protection, that Michael Tse—both her uncle and the Longtou—should care for her in this building.

Japanese: ビルの外に置いたら、どういった人間と接触したり、利用されるかわからない。
English: If we placed her outside it, we could not know what kind of people might approach or exploit her.

Japanese: 「この間はひどいこと言ってごめんなさい」
English: “I’m sorry I said such awful things the other day.”

Japanese: 「気にしていない。最近の生活はどうだ？」
English: “It didn’t bother me. How have things been lately?”

Japanese: 僕は手近な椅子に腰掛けてからそう訊ねた。
English: I sat down in a nearby chair and asked.

Japanese: 「龍頭になったマイケルおじさんも、その奥さんも、すごく優しくしてくれて快適だよ」
English: “Uncle Michael, now that he’s the Longtou, and his wife have both been terribly kind. I’m comfortable here.”

Japanese: 「それはよかった」
English: “I’m glad.”

Japanese: 「でも、なんだか浮き足立ってて、落ち着かない感じ。……お兄ちゃんはまだホテルにいるの？」
English: “But everyone seems restless. It never feels calm. ...Are you still at the hotel, Big Brother?”

Japanese: 「もうホテル暮らしはやめた。何日かこのビルにも住んでたんだれどね、ここじゃ、気軽に人と会えなくて、どうも仕事にならないからやめた」
English: “I stopped living at the hotel. I did stay in this building for a few days, but it’s impossible to meet people casually here, so I couldn’t get any work done. I left.”

Japanese: 「ここにいた時があったなんて、ちっとも知らなかった！　どうして教えてくれなかったの？　お兄ちゃんと近くで暮らせるなんて、本当に久しぶりなのに」
English: “I had no idea you were here! Why didn’t you tell me? It’s been so long since you and I could live near each other.”

Japanese: 「一番忙しい時期だったからね」
English: “That was when I was busiest.”

Japanese: 「……それなら仕方ないね。じゃあ今は、どこにいるの？」
English: “...Then I suppose it couldn’t be helped. Where are you staying now?”

Japanese: 「滑走路通りの近くに住んでるメンバーの家に間借りしてる。……そのうち、昔みんなが住んでいたあの家を掃除して使ってもいいかもしれないな。覚えてるだろう？」
English: “I’m staying with a member who lives near Runway Street. ...In time, perhaps we could clean out that old house where we all lived and use it again. You remember it, don’t you?”

Japanese: 「うん、いいな……」
English: “Yes. That would be nice...”

Japanese: 筱喬は物憂げに目を細める。
English: Siu-kiu’s eyes narrowed wistfully.

Japanese: 「そうなったら、お前も暮らすか？」
English: “Would you like to live there too, if we did?”

Japanese: 「そんなこと、出来るの？」
English: “Could I really?”

Japanese: 「出来るよ。このビルが安全だとは言うけれど、今の状況ではそれほどのものだとは思わない」
English: “You could. They call this building secure, but right now I’m not sure I would.”

Japanese: このビルは確かに優れた防御設備ではあるとは思う。通常の設備を用いた機械的な警戒システムの他に、黄姉妹のレーダーのような生命感知能力がある。それによって、たとえば留守の間に何物かが侵入してどこに隠れていようともすぐに見つけだしてしまうし、かつては、それに加えて龍頭の透視能力があったのだから、文字通り城塞のように機能していたのだろう。
English: I did think the building was well defended. Beyond its ordinary mechanical security systems, the Wong sisters had a radar-like ability to detect life. If someone entered while the building was empty and hid anywhere within it, for example, they would be discovered at once. And formerly there had also been the Longtou’s clairvoyance. The building must literally have functioned as a fortress.

Japanese: しかしそれはあくまでも、明白な敵意をもった侵入者に対する防衛能力であって、身内の裏切りや客の予期せぬ変心を発見したり排除するものではない。透視能力のある先代龍頭なら、どんなに偽装しても隠し持った武器を見つけ出すことが出来たが、彼はもういない。
English: Yet those systems defended only against intruders with evident hostile intent. They could neither detect nor prevent treachery from within or an unexpected change of heart in a guest. The former Longtou’s clairvoyance could uncover a concealed weapon no matter how skillfully it was hidden, but he was gone.

Japanese: このビルにはＹＳの様々な関係者が訪れる。現在我々が警戒しなくてはいけないのは、いずれもＹＳ内部の人間なのだから、こうした警備体制はほどんと用を為さない。
English: All manner of people connected to YS visited the building. And everyone we presently needed to guard against belonged to YS, making these defenses almost entirely useless.

Japanese: 先代の死によって最も信頼出来る筈の我々旧義勝のメンバーにも動揺がある。ジェフリーをはじめとする新体制に馴染めない誰かが他のファミリーに工作をされ、手土産に筱喬の身柄を、なんていうのは極端な想像ではあるが、非現実的なほどではない。
English: The former Longtou’s death had unsettled even the members of the old Yisheng, who ought to have been the most trustworthy of all. The idea that someone unable to accept the new regime under Jeffrey might be suborned by another family and bring them Siu-kiu as a gift was an extreme conjecture, but not an altogether unrealistic one.

Japanese: 街に住むのが安全だとは言わないが、少なくともＹＳ関係者がやって来ることはない。
English: I would not call life in the city safe, but at least no one connected to YS would visit her there.

Japanese: それと、廖志明の屋敷を襲ったタイプＡのように、厳重な警備を突破して易々と侵入できるほどの能力の持ち主ならば、このビルの警備体制をあてにしてここに居たって全く意味がないかもしれない。
English: Then there was the possibility of a person like the Type A who had attacked Liao Chi-ming’s residence—someone capable enough to penetrate formidable security with ease. If such a person existed, placing any confidence in this building’s defenses might be entirely meaningless.

Japanese: もっとも、そんな存在するかどうかもわからない、能力の実態も掴めていないタイプAを想定しても仕方がないが……。
English: Of course, it was pointless to plan around a Type A whom we did not know to exist and whose ability we had not even begun to understand...

Japanese: それに安全面だけでなく、とにかく僕は、筱喬をＹＳから遠ざけたかった。
English: Security aside, however, my overriding desire was to separate Siu-kiu from YS.

Japanese: 「もうちょっと落ち着いたら、このビルから出た方がいい」
English: “Once things settle down a little, you should leave this building.”
“I see...”

Japanese: 筱喬は肘掛けに肘を立て、頬杖をついている。
English: Siu-kiu rested an elbow on the arm of her chair and propped her cheek on one hand.

Japanese: もっと喜ぶかと思ったがさほどでもない。
English: I had expected more enthusiasm from her, but saw very little.

Japanese: 彼女は溜息をつき、
English: She sighed.

Japanese: 「小さい頃は幸せだったな。あの家で、お兄ちゃんとお母さんが毎日近くにいて、お父さんも月に一度くらいはプレゼントを持って来てくれた」
English: “We were happy when we were little. You and Mother were always nearby in that house, and Father came with presents about once a month.”

Japanese: 僕が定食屋にあずけられるまでの時間、僕はそこで母と妹と暮らした。
English: I had lived there with my mother and sister until I was placed with the people who ran the set-meal restaurant.

Japanese: そして母が発症すると、僕は定食屋からまたその家に戻り、筱喬と一緒に母親の面倒を見た。
English: When Mother’s symptoms manifested, I returned from the restaurant to that house, where Siu-kiu and I cared for her together.

Japanese: 母が死ぬと、筱喬はグランドタワーに引き取られ、僕は短い期間街で一人暮らしをした後に進学してY地区を出た。
English: After Mother’s death, Siu-kiu was taken into Grand Tower. I lived alone in the city for a brief period, then left Y District to continue my education.

Japanese: 「あの頃に戻りたい」
English: “I want to go back to those days.”

Japanese: 「それは無理だな」
English: “That isn’t possible.”

Japanese: 「わかってる。……もうシウも子供じゃないんだよね」
English: “I know. ...Siu isn’t a child anymore.”

Japanese: 「……何かしたいことがあるか？　今だったらお前は自分の人生を選び直せる。あの家じゃなくても、この街を出て暮らすことも出来る」
English: “...Is there something you want to do? You have the chance to choose your life again now. You needn’t return to that house. You could leave this city and live somewhere else.”

Japanese: 「無理だよ。この街の外でタイプBが普通に暮らせるところなんかないわ」
English: “I can’t. There’s nowhere outside this city where a Type B can live an ordinary life.”

Japanese: 「そうでもない。お前くらいの年で、一人暮らしをして居るタイプBの女の子は学校にもたくさんいた。お前も知らない街で、そうやってYSと無関係な人間として生きて行くんだ」
English: “That isn’t true. There were plenty of Type B girls your age living by themselves at my university. You can live the same way in a city where no one knows you, as someone with no connection to YS.”

Japanese: 「ちょっと前まではお兄ちゃんも、そうやってYSと無関係な生活をしていたんだね」
English: “Until a little while ago, you were the one living without any connection to YS, weren’t you?”

Japanese: 「そうだ」
English: “That’s right.”

Japanese: 「それで、そのときはシウがこのビルでYSの人たちと一緒に暮らしてた。そして今はこれが反対になって、お兄ちゃんがYSに入り、私が無関係な人として暮らせって言うんだ」
English: “And while you did, Siu lived in this building with the people from YS. Now we’ve traded places: you’ve joined YS, and you’re telling me to live as though I have no connection to it.”

Japanese: 「何を言いたい？」
English: “What are you trying to say?”

Japanese: 筱喬はじっと僕の目を見る。
English: Siu-kiu stared into my eyes.

Japanese: 「……お兄ちゃんが学生をやめてYSに入ったのは、シウのみがわりになって、シウをYSから解放するため？」
English: “...Did you leave school and join YS so you could take Siu’s place and set her free?”

Japanese: 僕は答えにつまってしまった。
English: I could find no answer.

Japanese: 筱喬が状況をそんなかたちで把握しているとは思わなかった。自分を取り巻く状況について、僕が想像していたよりも冷静に認識している。
English: I had not imagined that Siu-kiu understood the situation in those terms. She saw her own circumstances far more clearly than I had supposed.

Japanese: 「そうじゃない」
English: “That isn’t why.”

Japanese: 結局そう答えたが、返答までの一瞬の間が、彼女に言葉の内容とは別の意味を悟らせてしまったろう。
English: That was the answer I eventually gave her. Yet the instant of silence before it must have told her something different from the words themselves.

Japanese: 「やっと自由になれたのに、足手まといになっちゃってごめんなさい」
English: “You had finally won your freedom. I’m sorry I became a burden.”

Japanese: 「本当に違うんだ。シウは勘違いをしている。僕は誰かの身代わりになるなんてことだけのために行動したりはしない。自分にとって意味があるから戻って来たんだ」
English: “It truly isn’t that. You misunderstand me, Siu. I would never act for no reason but to take another person’s place. I returned because there is something here that matters to me.”

Japanese: 「……そうなの？」
English: “...Is that true?”

Japanese: 筱喬は信じてはいないようだった。
English: Siu-kiu did not appear to believe me.

Japanese: 「僕はなんだっていいのさ。実験を繰り返して新しい発見をするのも楽しいが、この奇妙な街で奇妙な連中を観察するのも悪くないだろうよ。いつか死ぬときに、まあまあ悪くない人生だったと思えるならば、何をしたって一緒さ」
English: “I don’t particularly care what I do. Repeating experiments and making new discoveries is enjoyable, but observing the strange inhabitants of this strange city isn’t bad either. So long as, when I eventually die, I can think my life was tolerable enough, one choice is much like another.”

Japanese: 僕は笑ってみせ、
English: I gave her a smile.

Japanese: 「つき合ってみて思ったけれどね、僕はこの世界の、欲望に素直で、行動もシンプルな連中がそこまで嫌いじゃないかもしれない。何か野生動物の群れのなかで暮らしているような気がするよ。彼らを観察するのは悪くない。ある意味、自然科学的なフィールドワークみたいなもんさ」
English: “Now that I’ve spent some time with them, I think I may not dislike the people of this world quite as much as I expected. They are honest about their appetites, and their actions are simple. I feel as though I’m living among a pack of wild animals. Observing them is not unpleasant. In a sense, it resembles fieldwork in the natural sciences.”

Japanese: 「でも、それは……」
English: “But that...”

Japanese: 筱喬は言いかけてから、目をそらして、口をつぐんだ。
English: Siu-kiu began to speak, then looked away and closed her mouth.

Japanese: 「言ってご覧」
English: “Go on. Tell me.”

Japanese: 促すと、彼女は再び僕に視線を向ける。
English: At my prompting, she met my eyes again.

Japanese: 「そんな風に考えたら、だめだよ。お兄ちゃんも、きっとこの世界に取り込まれてしまう。ＹＳから離れなきゃいけないのはシウじゃなくてお兄ちゃんだよ。お兄ちゃんが街を出た判断は間違ってなかったんだ」
English: “You can’t think that way. This world will swallow you too. I’m not the one who needs to leave YS. You are. You were right when you chose to leave the city.”

Japanese: 彼女の目は真剣だった。言葉には熱っぽい訴えがあり、確信めいたものが感じられた。
English: Her eyes were grave. There was heat in her appeal, and something very like conviction.

Japanese: 言葉の内容よりも、その態度が僕に驚きのようなものを与える。
English: Her manner, more than the content of her words, almost surprised me.

Japanese: 「そんなことはないさ。それより……」
English: “That isn’t true. More importantly—”

Japanese: 「このままだったら、きっとお兄ちゃんは近いうちに死ぬよ」
English: “If this continues, you’re going to die soon.”

Japanese: 話題を変えようとした僕を、彼女は許さない。
English: She refused to let me change the subject.

Japanese: 「私、もしかしたら人の死ぬのがわかるのかもしれない。お母さんの時も、お父さんの時も、もうすぐ死ぬって本当にわかる前から、会うとなんだか変にモヤモヤとした感じがしてたの。その他にも何人か、そういう人がいた。……その時はなんだかわからなかったけど、今になって思うと、みんなそれから二、三年のうちに死んじゃってる」
English: “I think I may be able to tell when people are going to die. With Mother and Father, long before there was any real way to know they would die soon, I felt this strange haze whenever I saw them. There were a few other people too. ...I didn’t understand it then, but when I look back now, every one of them died within two or three years.”

Japanese: 自分の意識が世界と繋がっているような気がして、目の前の出来事が、すべて自分が予知していたもののように感じてしまう。……タイプBの症状の一つにはそういった錯覚があるのを僕は知っている。
English: I knew of a Type B symptom in which a person felt as though their consciousness were connected to the world and everything before them seemed to be something they had predicted.

Japanese: 心配になって僕は筱喬の顔をじっと見た。目は金色にはなっていないし、興奮や過度の緊張も見られない。過去に見たタイプB発症者の感じとは違っているが、タイプBの発症パターンというのは、専門家でも把握しきれないほど様々な形で現れるそうだから油断は出来ない。
English: Concerned, I studied Siu-kiu’s face. Her eyes had not turned gold, nor did I see agitation or excessive tension. She did not resemble the symptomatic Type Bs I had observed in the past. But the patterns of Type B symptom onset reportedly varied so widely that even specialists could not understand them completely, and I could not afford to dismiss the possibility.

Japanese: 「いまのYSの偉い人たちは、みんな会うとそういうもやもやがある。きっと、もうすぐ死んじゃうんだと思う。お兄ちゃんも、前はそんな感じしなかったのに、YSに入った今、それをすごく感じるんだ。だから、さっき顔を見たとき驚いたの。ねえ、今すぐ抜けられない？　私、お兄ちゃんが死んだらどうしていいかわからない」
English: “Whenever I see any of the important people in YS now, I feel that same haze. I think they’re all going to die soon. I never used to feel it from you, but now that you’ve entered YS, it’s terribly strong. That’s why I was so startled when I saw your face. Big Brother, can’t you leave right now? I don’t know what I’ll do if you die.”

Japanese: 「YSの偉い人たちって、誰のことだ？　ジェフリー？　馬明？」
English: “Which important people in YS do you mean? Jeffrey? Ma Ming?”

Japanese: 「二人とも。龍頭になったマイケルおじさんからはそれを感じないわ。きっと、上手く生き延びるんだと思う」
English: “Both of them. I don’t feel it from Uncle Michael now that he’s the Longtou. I think he’ll find some way to survive.”

Japanese: 「なんだか変にリアリティのある話だね」
English: “That sounds oddly plausible.”

Japanese: 僕が肩をすくめると、
English: I shrugged.

Japanese: 「信じられないのはわかるよ。私もそんなのありえないとずっと思ってたし、そんないやなものが予知できちゃうなんて嫌で嫌でしかたなかったんだけど、どうしてもそうとしか思えないから。……お父さんだって、ああいう特別な力があったんだし……」
English: “I understand why you can’t believe me. For a long time, I thought it couldn’t possibly be true. I hated the thought that I could predict something so awful—I hated it more than anything. But I can’t find any other explanation. ...And Father did have a special power of that kind...”

Japanese: 「タイプAの資質はタイプBと違って遺伝しないよ」
English: “Unlike Type B, the disposition toward Type A abilities is not hereditary.”

Japanese: 僕は手を伸ばし筱喬の頭を撫でると、
English: I reached out and stroked Siu-kiu’s head.

Japanese: 「大丈夫。僕はそう簡単には死にやしない。この世の中で、やりたいことがまだたくさんあるんだ。だから心配しなくていいよ」
English: “It will be all right. I won’t die so easily. There is still a great deal I want to do in this world. You needn’t worry.”

Japanese: そう答えたとき、僕の胸ポケットのなかで携帯電話が振動した。
English: As I gave her that answer, the mobile phone in my breast pocket vibrated.

Japanese: 地下の駐車場に待たせている運転手からの電話で、会食の時間が迫っているとのことだった。
English: It was a call from the driver waiting in the underground garage. The time for my dinner engagement was approaching.

Japanese: 今日の相手は、クリス・ツェーの大叔父にあたる人物で、滑走路通りの裏手にいくつかのアダルトショップを経営している。ファミリーに古くからいる重要人物の一人だ。もう老境に達して一線を退いているが、発言にはそれなりの影響力があり、今日は彼の要望で自宅に招かれている。
English: The man I was to meet that day was Chris Tse’s great-uncle, who operated several adult shops behind Runway Street. He was an important, long-standing member of the family. Though advanced age had taken him out of active work, his words still carried considerable influence, and he had invited me to his home at his own request.

Japanese: おそらく、彼好みに油たっぷりで仕上げられた豪勢な広東料理を肴に、何か有り難い説教でもしてくれるつもりなのだろう。若い時の殺人やら、レイプやらの話が大好きな老人だ。
English: Presumably he intended to serve some sumptuous Cantonese food prepared with as much oil as his tastes demanded and deliver an edifying lecture or two over dinner. The old man dearly loved telling stories about the murders and rapes of his youth.

Japanese: 僕はちっとも面白くもないが、馬明がファミリー内での繋がりは大事にしろというので従っている。どんな役職についても、基本的には年長者を立てるのが我々の伝統なのだそうだ。
English: I found none of it remotely interesting, but Ma Ming insisted that I must value my connections within the family, and so I complied. No matter one’s position, deference to one’s elders was apparently our tradition.

Japanese: 父も、こうした身内の長老の呼び出しには素直に従っていたそうで、彼のような人物が大人しく話を聞いている姿を想像するとおかしいが、僕も他人事ではない。先のことはわからないが、今はある程度ルールに従うのが賢明だろう。
English: Father himself was said to have answered obediently when elderly relatives of this kind summoned him. The thought of a man like him sitting quietly through their lectures was amusing, but I was in no position to laugh. I could not know what lay ahead; for the present, it would be prudent to observe the rules to some degree.

Japanese: 「悪いが、行かなくちゃいけない。今度時間をとって話をしよう」
English: “I’m sorry, but I have to go. We’ll make time to talk again.”

Japanese: 「……待ってる。私ももっと話したい」
English: “...I’ll be waiting. I want to talk more too.”

Japanese: 筱喬がそう言うのを聞いてから、僕はその部屋を後にした。
English: After hearing Siu-kiu say it, I left her room.

Japanese: その日はY地区ではよくあるくずついた一日で、どんよりと曇った灰色の空から静かな雨がしとしとと降ったりやんだりを繰り返していた。
English: It was the sort of unsettled day common in Y District. A quiet rain fell in fine drops from the dull gray sky, stopped, then began again.

Japanese: 僕はファミリーの連中に提出させた帳簿を夜っぴてデータ化し、グラフにまとめたりしていたので朝から睡眠不足で頭が重かった。何でも数字を求め、グラフにしてしまうのが大学に通うようになってから身についた癖だ。
English: I had spent the entire night digitizing the ledgers the family members had submitted and assembling graphs from the data, leaving me foggy-headed with fatigue all morning. My university years had given me the habit of reducing everything to numbers and turning those numbers into graphs.

Japanese: YS龍頭であった父の部下は、第二代龍頭のマイケル・ツェーがすべて譲り受けることになったから、現在のところ、僕の唯一の個人的な部下は世傑だけだった。彼と共に車に乗って昼過ぎにグランドタワーに到着すると、いつも車のドアを開けてくれるスーツ姿の部下に挨拶をし、エレベーターに乗った。
English: Every subordinate who had served Father as Longtou now passed to the second Longtou, Michael Tse. At present, therefore, Sai-kit was my sole personal subordinate. He and I arrived at Grand Tower by car in the early afternoon. After greeting the suited man who always opened the car door for us, we entered the elevator.

Japanese: 世傑は最近気にいっているワインの銘柄の話を、僕が聞いていないのに一方的にして、それから彼の父の馬明が最近いきいきと仕事に取り組んでいることを話した。先代が死んで責任が増えたことと、きなくさい状況が生む緊張感が、彼にやりがいを与えているのだろうと世傑は分析した。
English: Without caring whether I was listening, Sai-kit delivered a monologue about a brand of wine he had recently taken to. He then told me that his father, Ma Ming, had lately thrown himself into his work with unusual vitality. Sai-kit’s analysis was that the greater responsibility following the former Longtou’s death, together with the tension produced by these ominous circumstances, had given him a renewed sense of purpose.

Japanese: 最上階でレイレイと会うと、今日は筱喬が街に買い物に出ていることを伝えてくれた。僕が先日積極的に筱喬を街に出すよう龍頭に要望したのを、早速実行に移してくれたらしい。今日は服や部屋に置く小物を見に、Y地区の外に行っているのだそうだ。
English: When we met Leilei on the top floor, she told me that Siu-kiu had gone shopping that day. The Longtou appeared to have acted promptly upon my recent request that Siu-kiu be encouraged to leave the tower. She had gone outside Y District to look at clothes and little things for her room.

Japanese: Y地区のなかの方が何かとトラブルの種が多いと誰かが判断したのだろうが、賢明だろう。
English: Someone must have judged that Y District itself offered too many opportunities for trouble. That was probably wise.

Japanese: 執務室ではジェフリーが自分でポットを持ってコーヒーを淹れていた。コーヒーは彼の数少ない趣味で、生のままの豆を売っている店に自ら足を運び、焙煎の仕方まで指定して買ってくる。それを飲むたびに使用する分だけハンドミルで挽いて、こだわりの温度にあたためたお湯を使って抽出する。どんなに忙しくても、昼食後の一杯だけはそうやって自分で淹れる。
English: In the office, Jeffrey was brewing coffee for himself. Coffee was one of his few pleasures. He personally visited a shop that sold green beans and specified how they were to be roasted. Each time he drank it, he ground only the amount he required in a hand mill and brewed it with water heated to his chosen temperature. However busy he became, he always prepared his after-lunch cup himself.

Japanese: 他人には全くわからないが、同じように淹れても日によって味が違うと本人は力説し、うまく淹れられた日は上機嫌で、思ったのと違っていれば不機嫌になる。
English: No one else could detect the slightest difference, but he insisted that the taste varied from day to day even when he followed the same procedure. When the coffee came out well, it put him in an excellent mood; when it differed from what he had intended, he became irritable.

Japanese: その日はよほど上手に淹れられたらしく、青白い肌と、目の下のくまが一層こくなった顔に笑顔を浮かべて、僕と世傑を出迎えた。
English: That day’s cup must have been an extraordinary success. Jeffrey welcomed Sai-kit and me with a smile on his pallid face, though the shadows beneath his eyes had grown darker still.

Japanese: 「一杯どうですか？」
English: “Would you care for a cup?”

Japanese: 彼は僕らのためにも珈琲を注いでくれる。
English: He poured coffee for us as well.

Japanese: 僕は何も淹れずの飲み、酒飲みのくせに甘党の世傑は砂糖とミルクを大量に入れる。ジェフリーはその様子をちらと見たが、何も言わず、笑顔も崩さなかった。
English: I drank mine black. Sai-kit, a drinker with a sweet tooth, added a vast quantity of sugar and milk. Jeffrey cast one glance at the spectacle but said nothing, and his smile never faltered.

Japanese: 来客の予定もなく、珍しく平穏な一日になる筈だった。
English: We expected no visitors. For once, it should have been a peaceful day.

Japanese: 馬明は自分の子分達と滑走路通りに新しく出来たエクアドル料理店を食べに行っているらしい。やがて第二代龍頭のマイケル・ツェーがやって来ると、僕たちは四人で珈琲を飲むこととなった。
English: Ma Ming had apparently gone with his men to eat at a newly opened Ecuadorian restaurant on Runway Street. When Michael Tse, the second Longtou, eventually joined us, the four of us drank coffee together.

Japanese: まずジェフリーから報告があった。廖志明に関する調査は現在なんの進展もないらしい。例のタイプAについても、何もわからない
English: Jeffrey began with his report. The investigation of Liao Chi-ming had apparently made no progress. We had learned nothing about the Type A in question either.

Japanese: 僕は帳簿を見て気がついた問題点を指摘した。
English: I raised the problems I had discovered in the ledgers.

Japanese: 香港の黒社会時代の古い伝統と儀式で飾られた不合理そのもののシステムが、我々の経済力を削いでいる。廖志明の客家系グループのような現代の会社組織めいたすっきりとしたものにしなければ彼らに対抗してゆくのは難しい。この先ファミリーのあり方を変えて行くべきだろう。
English: An irrational system decorated with ancient traditions and rituals from the Hong Kong underworld was sapping our economic strength. If we meant to compete with the clean, modern corporate structure of a Hakka-affiliated group such as Liao Chi-ming’s, the family would have to change the way it operated.

Japanese: ジェフリーは一定の理解を示したが、香港時代からの古老たちが納得しないだろうと予測を述べた。
English: Jeffrey demonstrated a measure of understanding, but predicted that the old guard from the Hong Kong days would never consent.

Japanese: 「何をするにも、彼らが天寿を全うしてからですね」
English: “Whatever we mean to do must wait until they have lived out their natural lives.”

Japanese: とジェフリーは言ったが、僕はそれほど気長ではなく、天寿というアテのないものをのんびりと待つことは出来そうにない。
English: So Jeffrey said. I was less patient. I did not think I could wait serenely for so uncertain a deadline as a natural death.

Japanese: 黙って考えていたら、
English: As I considered the matter in silence,

Japanese: 「最近小謝は金のことばかり考えているなあ」
English: “Siu Tse thinks about nothing but money these days.”

Japanese: と二代目がからかった。
English: The remark came from the second Longtou.

Japanese: 「そりゃ、金と暴力は僕らにとって一番大事なものですからね。……それより龍頭、そろそろ筱喬にもグランドタワーの外での暮らしを体験させたいのですが、どうですか？」
English: “Naturally. Money and violence are the two things that matter most to us. ...More importantly, Longtou, I would like Siu-kiu to begin experiencing life outside Grand Tower. What do you think?”

Japanese: 「それはいつでも問題ないでしょう」
English: “There would be no objection whenever you chose to do it.”

Japanese: 二代目の代わりにこたえたのはジェフリーだった。
English: Jeffrey answered in place of the second Longtou.

Japanese: 「ただ、それなりの安全が確保出来る形でないと困りますがね」
English: “Provided, of course, that arrangements are made to ensure an appropriate degree of safety.”

Japanese: それから話は雑談へと移り、世傑がY地区出身の歌手ミムラが昔滑走路通りのバーでアルバイトをして居たころの話をし、龍頭が少年時代のクリス・ツェーの話や、やんちゃ坊主だった馬明の話などをした。無駄話をしながら、僕と龍頭で囲碁を打った。龍頭はそれなりに自信があったらしく、僕にあっというまに負かされてしまうと、暫く言葉を失って呆然としていた。二度挑んで来たが、どちらも同じ結果で、最後には「もう小謝とは囲碁を打ちたくないなあ」と言い、「僕の一番の特技なんです」と僕がフォローをしても力なく笑うだけだった。
English: The conversation then turned to idle subjects. Sai-kit spoke of the days when Mimura, a singer from Y District, had worked at a bar on Runway Street. The Longtou told stories about Chris Tse as a boy and Ma Ming as a little terror. As we chatted, the Longtou and I played Go. He appeared reasonably confident at first, but sat speechless in a daze when I defeated him almost at once. He challenged me twice more with the same result. At last he said, ‘I don’t believe I care to play Go with Siu Tse again.’ Even when I reassured him that it was my greatest talent, he could manage only a feeble smile.

Japanese: 街に戻って自分の業務を再開しようとした時に、部屋の和やかな雰囲気を打ち破る荒々しい跫音を立ててジェフリーの部下が部屋に駆け込んできた。
English: I was preparing to return to the city and resume my own work when one of Jeffrey’s men shattered the room’s amiable atmosphere, charging through the door with thunderous footsteps.

Japanese: 「一体、どうしたんだ？」
English: “What in the world has happened?”

Japanese: ジェフリーは怪訝な顔をする。
English: Jeffrey looked at him in bewilderment.

Japanese: 「非常事態です！　何者かが、ビルに侵入しました！」
English: “It’s an emergency! Someone has entered the building!”

Japanese: 男の狼狽ぶりはただごとではない。思わず、ジェフリーと僕は顔を見合わせる。
English: The man’s panic was extraordinary. Jeffrey and I instinctively exchanged looks.

Japanese: 「どういうこと？　警備の方からは何も連絡がないけど？」
English: “What do you mean? We haven’t heard anything from security.”

Japanese: 世傑は首をひねる。
English: Sai-kit tilted his head.

Japanese: 今ははいってきた男はモニタールームで監視カメラの映像をチェックしていたはずである。監視カメラは主にビルの内部や、人の目の届かない死角をフォローするもので、不審者が侵入したのなら、まずそちらの方から異状を知らされているはずだ。この部屋には、彼らの手元の端末からワンボタンで繋がる電話機が設置されている。
English: The man who had just entered should have been checking the surveillance-camera feeds in the monitor room. Those cameras primarily covered the building’s interior and blind spots beyond ordinary view. If a suspicious person had entered, we should have heard from the monitor room first. The operators’ terminals could connect to a telephone in this office at the press of a single button.

Japanese: 「それが、本当に侵入してきたんです。……私どもにも、何がなんだか……」
English: “But someone truly has entered. ...We don’t understand it either...”

Japanese: 男の顔はすっかり蒼白になっている。
English: The man’s face had gone entirely white.

Japanese: 「とにかく、早く、こちらへいらしてください！　実際に見て頂かないと、どう説明したらいいのか……」
English: “Please, come at once! Unless you see it for yourselves, I don’t know how to explain...”

Japanese: 「ただごとではないようだな。わかった、行こう」
English: “This is evidently no ordinary matter. Very well. Let us go.”

Japanese: ジェフリーがそう言って頷いたときには、僕はもうモニタールームに向かって駆け出していた。
English: By the time Jeffrey nodded, I had already begun running toward the monitor room.

Japanese: 嫌な予感がしてたまらない。
English: I could not shake an ominous feeling.

Japanese: モニタールームは執務室を出てすぐのドアの向こうにある、目と鼻の先の部屋である。
English: The monitor room was only a few steps away, behind the first door outside the office.

Japanese: そこには常時二人か三人の部下が配置され、ビルの各所から送られてくる監視カメラの映像をチェックしている。普段はサイキックの黄姉妹もこの部屋に居て、彼らと連携をとりつつ龍頭の身辺の安全を確保しているが、黄姉妹の不在時は表の警備員と警報システム、そしてこのカメラの監視員でビルを守っている。
English: Two or three men were stationed there at all times, checking the feeds sent by surveillance cameras throughout the building. The psychic Wong sisters were ordinarily present as well, coordinating with them to ensure the Longtou’s personal safety. In their absence, the building was protected by the guards at the entrances, the alarm system, and the surveillance staff in this room.

Japanese: まっさきに部屋のドアを開けて足を踏み入れると、黄姉妹と、そしてもう一人の監視員が、いま僕らに異変を告げた男と同じような動揺を浮かべて壁一面に並ぶモニターの前に立っている。
English: I was first through the door. The Wong sisters and another surveillance operator stood before the bank of screens covering one wall, displaying the same agitation as the man who had reported the emergency.

Japanese: 「小謝！」
English: “Siu Tse!”

Japanese: モニターを見つめていた監視役の男が僕の名を呼ぶ。
English: The surveillance operator staring at the screens called my name.

Japanese: 黄姉妹もその声で僕を振り返り、
English: At his voice, the Wong sisters turned toward me as well.

Japanese: 「大変なことが……とても、信じられません」
English: “Something terrible has... I can hardly believe it.”

Japanese: 天明が震える声で言った。
English: Tin-ming’s voice trembled.

Japanese: 「何が起きたの？」
English: “What happened?”

Japanese: 「一階ロビーです。現在の状況を、中央のモニターにうつします」
English: “The first-floor lobby. We will put the current view on the central monitor.”

Japanese: 監視役の男が手元のパネルを操作する。
English: The surveillance operator worked the panel before him.

Japanese: すると、中央の一番大きなメインモニターに、目を疑うような光景が映し出された。
English: The largest screen in the center displayed a sight that made me doubt my eyes.

Japanese: 「あっ殺されてる」
English: “Oh. Someone’s been killed.”

Japanese: 僕が思ったまま口にすると、
English: I said exactly what occurred to me.

Japanese: 「そりゃ、だから呼ばれたんでしょうよ」
English: “Why do you think they called us?”

Japanese: 世傑がとなりで苦い顔をする。
English: Sai-kit grimaced beside me.

Japanese: 「ひっ」
English: “Eek.”

Japanese: 女の声に振り返ると、龍頭やジェフリー達が部下を引き連れて到着し、僕の後ろでモニターの光景に呆然としている。
English: I turned toward the woman’s voice. The Longtou and Jeffrey had arrived with their subordinates and now stood behind me, staring dumbstruck at the screen.

Japanese: 悲鳴を上げたのはレイレイで、このひょんなことからYSで働くこととなった哀れな少女はすっかり全身を硬直させてしまっていた。
English: The scream had come from Leilei. The unfortunate girl who had found herself working for YS through such a strange turn of events had gone rigid from head to foot.

Japanese: 男が言った通り、そこはグランドタワーの一階ロビーの光景だった。部屋の天井隅に、入り口付近の床を見下ろすように取り付けられたカメラには、窓から差し込む自然光が床材として使われた大理石で反射する様子や、中央に敷かれた鮮やかな模様の手織り絨毯が大写しになっている。
English: As the man had said, the image showed the first-floor lobby of Grand Tower. The camera had been installed in a corner of the ceiling, looking down upon the floor near the entrance. Natural light from the windows gleamed on the marble, and a vividly patterned, handwoven carpet filled the center of the frame.

Japanese: それだけなら、僕が毎日のように通り過ぎる部屋の景色だが、ドアの付近に、印象を全く変えてしまうものが映っているのである。
English: Without what lay beside the door, it would have been the same room through which I passed nearly every day. That alone transformed the entire impression.

Japanese: 一言で言って血の海。
English: In one phrase, it was a sea of blood.

Japanese: 鮮血が絨毯と床に飛び散り、そのなかに塊がいくつか転がっている。それは人の腕だったり、胴体だったり、足……つまりそこには、バラバラに切断された人間の死体が映っているのだ。
English: Fresh blood covered the carpet and floor, with several lumps scattered among it—human arms, a torso, legs. In other words, the screen displayed a dismembered corpse.

Japanese: 切り離された腕や足には、死者が身につけていた黒いスーツの袖やズボンが着ていたときの形のまま、例えば手首のあたりからのぞく白いシャツまでも乱れがなく、とても鋭利な包丁で海苔巻きを切断したような印象だった。
English: The black sleeves and trouser legs remained undisturbed upon the severed arms and legs, even the white shirt showing neatly at the wrist. The body gave the impression of a sushi roll sliced with an exceedingly sharp knife.

Japanese: 「門の方も、地下の駐車場も、人の出入りする場所のカメラには何も映っていないし、守っている連中も誰もやられていないんです。なのに、ロビーだけ、こんな……」
English: “None of the cameras covering the gate, the underground parking garage, or any other entrance shows a thing. And none of the men guarding them have been attacked. But the lobby alone is... like this...”

Japanese: 最初に駆け足で僕らに報告してくれた男もこの部屋に戻っていて、そう説明してくれる。
English: The first man, who had run to report the incident, had returned to the room and now supplied the explanation.

Japanese: 「へえ、それはすごいね」
English: “Huh. That’s impressive.”

Japanese: 「見てよ小謝。あれ、拳銃じゃない？　持ってた拳銃まで綺麗に切断されてるわ」
English: “Look, Siu Tse. Isn’t that a pistol? Even the gun he was holding has been cut clean through.”

Japanese: 世傑が指さす黒い物体は、画面では小さく、確認がしにくかったが、確かに見ようによっては引き金の付け根あたりで真っ二つに切断されたオートマチックの拳銃のように見える。
English: The black object Sai-kit indicated was small and difficult to make out on the screen. From one angle, however, it did indeed resemble an automatic pistol severed in two near the base of its trigger.

Japanese: 「こんなの見たことない。血の気が引いちゃうわ」
English: “I’ve never seen anything like it. It makes my blood run cold.”

Japanese: 世傑は溜息をついて首を左右に振る。
English: Sai-kit sighed and shook his head.

Japanese: 画面上で遺体になっているのは、おそらく田尻健太郎。YSには、どのファミリーにも属さないで龍頭と直接契約してYS自体に所属する形の組織員も多いが、彼もその一人で、先代の龍頭の前で入会の儀式を執り行って構成員となった人物だ。
English: The body on the screen was probably Kentaro Tajiri. Many members of YS belonged to no family at all, but contracted directly with the Longtou and thereby joined YS itself. Tajiri was one of them, initiated into the organization in a ceremony before the former Longtou.

Japanese: この間結婚式のすぐ後に、まだ生きていた父を訪ねた時に僕を扇動してくれた黒服である。いつも一階ロビーに居て出入りする人間にうやうやしく礼をする人物で、あまりにその仕草が丁寧なので、一度訊ねてみたことがある。
English: He was the man in black who had egged me on when I visited Father while he was still alive, immediately after the wedding. He was always in the first-floor lobby, bowing reverently to everyone who entered or left. His movements were so unfailingly courteous that I once asked him about them.

Japanese: すると、以前は他の街で小さなやくざ組織に所属していたと教えてくれた。古い組織で、上下関係が厳しく、礼儀を一通り身につけさせられたのだと言う。その組織が経済的な事情で潰れ、流れるようにしてこのY地区にやって来て、そしてこの街の女と結婚し、YSに入ったのだそうだ。家には小さな女の子とその弟がいると言う。
English: He told me that he had once belonged to a small yakuza organization in another city. It had been an old group with a strict hierarchy, where he had been taught the standard forms of etiquette. Financial difficulties destroyed the organization; he drifted into Y District, married a woman from the city, and joined YS. There was a young girl and her little brother waiting at home.

Japanese: このビルにやって来る時にはいつも目にする人物で、今日もここに上がってくるときに世傑と共に挨拶をしたばかりだ。
English: I saw him whenever I came to this building. Sai-kit and I had exchanged greetings with him only that day on our way upstairs.

Japanese: 「彼が殺される瞬間の録画を再生出来る？」
English: “Can you play the recording of the moment he was killed?”

Japanese: 僕が訊ねると、
English: I asked the question.

Japanese: 「は、はい。今すぐ流します。……今から、ちょうど五分前の映像です」
English: “Y-yes. I’ll play it at once. ...This is the feed from exactly five minutes ago.”

Japanese: 顔色は悪く、声も明らかに動揺していたが、前もって準備していてくれたらしく、監視役の男はすぐにその場面を再生したので、僕はその仕事ぶりに感心した。
English: His face had gone pale and his voice was plainly shaken. He nevertheless seemed to have prepared in advance, for the surveillance operator replayed the scene at once, and I found myself impressed by his work.

Japanese: 「私も見たのですが、見直しても何が何やらわけがわからなくて……」
English: “I watched it myself, but no matter how often I look, I cannot understand what happened...”

Japanese: 男がそう言った通り、すべてはあまりに一瞬のうちに起きてしまう。
English: As he said, it all happened far too quickly.

Japanese: まず、いつもと同じように田尻がドアの側にぼんやりと立っている場面から始まる。そして次の瞬間には、彼のいた場所には別の人物が立っており、同時に手足は床の上に転がり、さらに画面外から血をふきながら彼の頭がついた胴体がふってくる。
English: The recording began with Tajiri standing vacantly beside the door as usual. In the next instant, another person stood in his place. His arms and legs lay scattered across the floor, while his torso and attached head fell into the frame from above, spraying blood.

Japanese: そこで、
English: At that point,

Japanese: 「あっ」
English: “Ah.”

Japanese: と後ろで声をあげたのは、これまで黙っていた第二代龍頭マイケル・ツェー。
English: It was the second Longtou, Michael Tse, who had remained silent until then.

Japanese: 「これ、黒い服の女」
English: “That is the woman in black.”

Japanese: 彼が画面を指さすとおり、血の海の上に立っているのは、だぶだぶの黒い服を着た細身の女であった。彼女はフードをかぶり、白い素足で田尻の死体を踏みしめ、そしてぼんやり辺りを見回してから、ぴょんとジャンプをし、そしてそのまま着地を待たずに空中で消えてしまう。
English: As he pointed out, a slender woman in loose black clothing stood amid the sea of blood. A hood covered her head, and her bare white feet pressed against Tajiri’s body. She looked around blankly, gave a small leap, then vanished in midair without waiting to land.

Japanese: 小柄な背格好で、女というよりもむしろ少女と表現したほうが相応しく思える。
English: She was so small that ‘girl’ seemed more appropriate than ‘woman.’

Japanese: 「待ってよこれ。肝心の場面がカットされてるじゃないの？　女が殺すシーンと、女が去ってゆくシーン両方が映ってないわ」
English: “Wait. The crucial parts have been cut out, haven’t they? The scene where she kills him and the scene where she leaves are both missing.”

Japanese: 世傑が苦い顔をして言うと、男は首をふり、
English: Sai-kit spoke with a bitter expression, but the man shook his head.

Japanese: 「そう見えますが、これが何も編集していないリアルタイムの映像なんです」
English: “It does look that way, but this is the unedited, real-time feed.”

Japanese: そう言いながら男は何度か繰り返して見せてくれたが、やはり、すべてが間のコマを何枚も抜き去ったような唐突さだ。
English: He replayed it several times as he spoke. Each time, the events remained as abrupt as though several intervening frames had been torn away.

Japanese: 「な、なあこれ、廖志明が言ってたタイプAの女ってやつじゃないか？　あの、銅像をスッパリと切断した……」
English: “I-isn’t that the Type A woman Liao Chi-ming told us about? The one who cut the bronze statue clean in two...?”

Japanese: マイケル・ツェーがジェフリーに囁くように尋ねる。
English: Michael Tse whispered the question to Jeffrey.

Japanese: 「確かに、特徴は全く同じです」
English: “The features match.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは低い声でそうこたえる。
English: Jeffrey answered in a low voice.

Japanese: 「こ、これがそのタイプAだとしたら、私たちを殺しに来たってことか？　こんなわけのわからないものに、どう対応すればいいんだ？」
English: “I-if this is that Type A, has she come to kill us? How can we possibly respond to something so incomprehensible?”

Japanese: その問いには、ジェフリーは返答をせず黙ったままだった。
English: Jeffrey remained silent and offered no answer.

Japanese: 「この映像、スローに出来る？　問題の場面はコマ送りで」
English: “Can you slow the recording down? Take us through the relevant moment frame by frame.”

Japanese: 彼らのやりとりをモニターに目を向けたまま背中で聞いていた僕は、男にそう注文した。
English: I had listened to their exchange with my back turned and my eyes fixed upon the monitor. Now I gave the man his instructions.

Japanese: すると、彼はすぐにその通り再生をしてくれる。
English: He immediately replayed it as I had requested.

Japanese: 「コマ送りでも、全く同じね……。これ、テレポーテーションってやつなの？」
English: “Even frame by frame, it looks exactly the same... Is this what they call teleportation?”

Japanese: 世傑は唇を噛む。
English: Sai-kit bit his lip.

Japanese: 「こう、立ってる彼がいて、そのすぐ次のコマでもう同じ場所にこの女が現れている。すり替えたみたいに。でもすり替えたのは胴体だけで、ほら、このコマだとまだ腕は空中に浮いているし、足の太ももから下はもとどおり。……あれー胴体はどこへいったのかなって思いながら見ていると、次のコマからは腕は血を出しながら足元に落下しはじめ、足は自立を保てずに倒れる。そして、もう少しコマが進むと、画面の上の方から、なくなっていた胴体がおかえりなさいして……」
English: “Here he is, standing there, and in the very next frame this woman has appeared in exactly the same spot. As though they changed places. But only his torso changed places. See? In this frame his arms are still suspended in the air, and both legs remain where they were from the thighs down. ...You find yourself wondering where the torso went. In the next frame, the arms begin falling to the floor and shedding blood, while the legs can no longer stand by themselves and collapse. Then, several frames later, the missing torso comes home to us from the top of the screen...”

Japanese: 世傑は溜息をつき。
English: Sai-kit sighed.

Japanese: 「廖からきたメールの女だとしたら、ふらりと立ち寄った訳でもなくて、龍頭の命を狙いに来たわけでしょう？　こんなの、とても相手に出来ないわ。……ねえ、天明、あんたの能力でこの女の今の居場所はわかる？」
English: “If she is the woman from Liao’s email, she didn’t simply drop in on a whim. She came for the Longtou’s life, didn’t she? We can’t possibly fight something like that. ...Tin-ming, can your ability locate her now?”

Japanese: 天明は顔を横に振り、
English: Tin-ming shook her head.

Japanese: 「すみません。私たちの力は、あくまでも人間の生命をぼんやりとした明かりとしてその場所を感知するだけなんです。個々を見分ける力はありません。いるはずのない場所の生命や、おかしな動きをしてしないと、不審者を見分けることが出来ません。今回の襲撃は、近づいてくるのに全然気がつきませんでした。カメラに映ってからは、おそらくまだビルに居るはずのこの女をなんとか特定しようとしているんですが、ビルの下層は遠くて、人が多いから、どうも判別しにくくて……」
English: “I’m sorry. Our power does nothing more than detect the location of human lives as vague lights. We cannot distinguish one person from another. We can only recognize an intruder when a life appears somewhere no one should be, or moves in an abnormal way. This time, we had no idea the attacker was approaching. Since she appeared on camera, we have been trying to identify the woman, who is probably still inside the building. But the lower floors are distant and crowded, and it is extremely difficult to distinguish her...”

Japanese: 「そうなの……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 考え込んでしまう世傑にかわってジェフリーが訊ねる。
English: When Sai-kit fell into thought, Jeffrey asked instead.

Japanese: 「天明、中層には誰もいないか？」
English: “Tin-ming, is there anyone on the middle floors?”

Japanese: グランドタワーは最上階付近はYSの幹部やその家族たちが住み、一階や地下の下層には各種施設や業者が店舗や住居を構えているが、その間となる中層はほとんど人が立ち入らない空き部屋ばかりになっている。
English: The upper floors of Grand Tower housed the officers of YS and their families, while the ground floor and basement contained various facilities, shops, and residences. The middle floors between them, however, consisted almost entirely of vacant rooms into which hardly anyone ventured.

Japanese: これは利用するうちに自然とそうなったのか、先代に意図があって計画的に部屋を割り振ったのかはわからないが、もし何か不心得者が忍び込んだとしても、ここを通過する段階で黄姉妹が能力で発見出来るようになっている。
English: I did not know whether the pattern had arisen naturally as the tower came into use or whether the former Longtou had deliberately assigned the rooms that way. In either case, it allowed the Wong sisters to spot anyone who slipped in as they passed through those floors.

Japanese: 「今のところ、誰もいません」
English: “At present, no one.”

Japanese: 「そうか。じゃあとりあえず下層に意識を集中してて欲しい。……さて、じゃあこれからどうすべきか」
English: “I see. Then for the moment, focus on the lower floors. ...Now, what are we to do?”

Japanese: ジェフリーは腕組みをする。
English: Jeffrey folded his arms.

Japanese: 「まずさ、下層の人たちにアナウンスして、避難させたらどうかな？」
English: “Why don’t we begin by making an announcement to the people downstairs and evacuating them?”

Japanese: 僕が提案すると、
English: I suggested it.

Japanese: 「下層には業者も多く、我々の指示が直接届くものばかりではありません。館内放送で伝えれば、相当の混乱が予想されますが……」
English: “There are many independent businesses on the lower floors, and not all of them answer directly to us. A public announcement over the building’s system would cause considerable confusion...”

Japanese: 「でも、このままじゃ天明たちがいても相手を見つけることが困難だよ。もっと人を減らさないと」
English: “But as things stand, Tin-ming and Tin-cheung will have difficulty finding the attacker. We need to reduce the number of people down there.”

Japanese: 「……そうですね」
English: “...Yes, that is true.”

Japanese: ジェフリーがちらと龍頭の顔を見ると、
English: Jeffrey glanced toward the Longtou.

Japanese: 「わ、私はかまわんが……」
English: “I-I have no objection...”

Japanese: 「それならば、小謝の言う通り、避難させましょう。それから上層にいる、我々の家族や、業務にあたっている部下達にもすぐ指示を出したほうがいいでしょうね。家族はすぐに避難できるよう三十階のロビーに集合させる。部下達には、武器を持ってこのモニタールーム前に集合させます」
English: “Then we will do as Siu Tse proposes and evacuate the lower floors. We should also send immediate instructions to our families above and the men at work there. Have the families assemble in the thirtieth-floor lobby, prepared to evacuate at once. Order our men to collect their weapons and gather outside this monitor room.”

Japanese: 彼は緊張のおももちでそう言うと、
English: His face tense, Jeffrey continued.

Japanese: 「さて、そして問題の侵入者にはどう対処すべきか……」
English: “Now, the question is how to deal with the intruder herself...”

Japanese: 「小謝、何か作戦はないの？　アタシはこんなタイプA見たことないわよ」
English: “Siu Tse, don’t you have a plan? I’ve never seen a Type A like this.”

Japanese: 世傑が促すけれども、僕だってこんな相手は初めてだ。
English: Sai-kit urged me on, but I had never faced anyone like her either.

Japanese: 「まあ、一筋縄ではいかない感じだねえ」
English: “She does not look like someone we can handle by any simple method.”

Japanese: 僕が腕組みして考えはじめると、
English: I folded my arms and began to think.

Japanese: 「小謝、いま我々はどうしたらいいんだろう？　サイキック？　こいつは一体何者なんだ？　私は、どうも、何がなんだかわからなくて混乱していて……」
English: “Siu Tse, what are we to do now? A psychic? What in the world is this person? I confess I am so confused that I no longer understand anything...”

Japanese: 龍頭が途方に暮れた顔で僕に尋ねる。
English: The Longtou asked me helplessly.

Japanese: 「僕に訊ねられたところで、映像からわかることしかわかりませんが。……とりあえず、みんなが見た通り、相手はタイプAです。能力は、さっき世傑が言ったようにテレポーテーション。いわゆる瞬間移動ってやつでしょう。……いや、もっと正確に言うなら、空間のスワップ能力とでも表現したほうがいいのかな？」
English: “You can ask me, but I know no more than what we can see in the recording. ...For now, as everyone has observed, the adversary is a Type A. Her ability is teleportation, as Sai-kit said. What people ordinarily call instantaneous movement. ...No—more precisely, perhaps it would be better described as the ability to swap spaces.”

Japanese: 「スワップ？」
English: “Swap?”

Japanese: 龍頭は首をひねる。
English: The Longtou tilted his head.

Japanese: 「空間と空間を交換するんですよ。自分とその周囲の空間を、目標となる空間の位置を入れ替えるから、結果として瞬間移動になる」
English: “It exchanges one space for another. Her body and the space around it trade positions with whatever occupies the target space. The result is instantaneous movement.”

Japanese: 「ものがすっぱり切れてしまうのはどういうことなんだ？」
English: “Then why are objects cut cleanly apart?”

Japanese: 「入れ替えが起きた場所と、入れ替えが起きずにその場に残ったものとの間で切断が起こるんです。……いまの映像で言うと……もう一度、コマ送りでお願い。……いや、もうちょっと前から。そうそう……」
