English: “The cut occurs along the boundary between the space that changed places and anything left behind. ...Using the recording we just saw... Please take us through it frame by frame again. ...No, begin a little earlier. Yes, there...”

Japanese: 画面に田尻が断裂する瞬間の映像を表示させながら、僕は説明をする。
English: I explained while the screen displayed the instant Tajiri came apart.

Japanese: 「ここに田尻が立っているでしょう？　このとき女はおそらくこの画面の外、天井辺りに居たはずです。そこから、この田尻の胴体のあたりに能力を使う。……女の身体とその周囲の空間はこちらに移動し、かわりに田尻の身体が天井付近に移動するけれど、女が小さかったため、手足は移動せずにこの場に残る……そして、画面から消えた胴体は天井付近に移動して居るわけだから、続く映像で画面の上から振ってくる。これがバラバラ死体の製造方法ですね。実に素晴らしい」
English: “Tajiri is standing here, you see? At this point the woman was probably outside the frame, somewhere near the ceiling. From there, she used the ability upon the area around Tajiri’s torso. ...Her body and the space surrounding it moved here. Tajiri’s body moved near the ceiling in exchange, but because the woman was smaller than he was, his arms and legs did not move and remained behind. ...The torso that vanished from the frame had moved near the ceiling, and so, in the following images, it falls back into view from above. And that is how you make a dismembered corpse. Truly magnificent.”

Japanese: 僕はそこで黙って一同を振り返ったが、彼らは何も言わずにただ画面を見つめているので、僕は話を続けることにした。
English: I fell silent and looked around at the others. They merely stared at the screen without speaking, so I decided to continue.

Japanese: 「しかし、こいつはやっかいなヤツだよ。……次はもうちょっと前まで映像を遡ってもらって……ほらこの場面、画面の左端に、黒いのが一瞬映るでしょ？　これ、女の服の端じゃないかな？　女は外からこのロビーに飛び込んだあと、一旦部屋の天井付近にジャンプしてるんだ。そして、そこから田尻を攻撃している。そしてすぐにその場から消えた。画面で確認出来るだけでも四回能力を使っている」
English: “This one is trouble. ...Now take the recording a little farther back. Look at this instant. Something black appears for a moment at the left edge of the screen, doesn’t it? Could that be the hem of her clothes? After entering the lobby from outside, she made one jump to a position near the ceiling. From there, she attacked Tajiri, then vanished again at once. We can confirm at least four uses of her ability from the recording alone.”

Japanese: 「……短い時間に連続して使用出来るなんて、凄い能力ね」
English: “...An extraordinary ability, if she can use it repeatedly in so short a time.”

Japanese: 世傑が感心したように言う。
English: Sai-kit sounded impressed.

Japanese: 「確かにそれもそうだけれど、攻撃の前にわざわざ一回移動を挟んでいるのが秀逸だよ。部屋に入ってきてのんびり相手を確認してから攻撃するんじゃなく、相手に攻撃されないよう、部屋に入ってすぐに細かい移動を一つ挟んでから相手の場所を確認し、攻撃してるんだ」
English: “That is true. What is more impressive, however, is that she took the trouble to make one additional move before attacking. She did not enter the room, leisurely find her target, then strike. The instant she arrived, she made one short jump to prevent anyone from attacking her, used that position to locate her target, and only then struck.”

Japanese: 「なるほど」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 「こんなの、初めての襲撃だったら使うわけないでしょ。冷静だし、どう見たってこういう襲撃に慣れたヤツだ。……こういう慣れたヤツが、どこかで待ち伏せしたりせずに本拠地に一人で乗り込んで来るってのは、とんでもない自信があるんだろうね。いやんなっちゃうよ」
English: “No one moves like that on their first raid. She is calm and unmistakably accustomed to this kind of work. ...For someone so experienced to enter an enemy headquarters alone instead of arranging an ambush elsewhere, she must have a truly preposterous degree of confidence. It is enough to make me sick.”

Japanese: 「うーん、廖から前に届いていたメールでは、街の怒りを代表するものだと名乗ったとかなんとか言っていたけれど、どうなのかしらね」
English: “Hmm. Liao’s email claimed she called herself a representative of the city’s anger, or words to that effect. What do you make of that?”

Japanese: 「まあ、適当なことを言ったんだろうと思うよ。どう見たってプロの手口だ。廖が雇ったのかねえ。……こんな化け物、廖に雇われるようなたまにも思えないけど……。もしかして、ただの偶然の一致で、廖のメールとまるっきり関係ないのかもしれないよ？　ここに来たのも、ふらりと立ち寄っただけで、べつに龍頭の命を狙ってるわけじゃないのかもしれない。だとしたら、戦わないで済むかもしれない」
English: “I assume she said whatever came to mind. This has every appearance of a professional method. Did Liao hire her? ...Then again, she doesn’t strike me as the sort of monster Liao could hire. ...Perhaps it is pure coincidence, and she has nothing whatsoever to do with his email. Perhaps she merely wandered in here with no particular intention of killing the Longtou. In that case, we might not have to fight her.”

Japanese: 「そんな偶然あるわけないでしょ」
English: “There couldn’t possibly be a coincidence like that.”

Japanese: 世傑は冷静に否定する。
English: Sai-kit calmly rejected the possibility.

Japanese: 「だよねえ」
English: “No, I suppose not.”

Japanese: 僕が考え込んでしまうと、
English: I sank into thought.

Japanese: 「女の正体について色々と思うところがあるのはわかりますが、今はその詮索をしてる場面じゃありません。相手が何者にしろ、うちのガードマンを殺害した以上、排除すべき侵入者なのは間違い有りません」
English: “I understand that you have questions about the woman’s identity, but this is not the time to pursue them. Whoever she may be, she has killed one of our guards and is therefore unquestionably an intruder to be eliminated.”

Japanese: 「そうだけどさ」
English: “Yes, but...”

Japanese: ジェフリーの指摘に、僕は肩をすくめる。
English: I shrugged at Jeffrey’s observation.

Japanese: ここまで話したところで、さっそく指示した通りに上層にいる部下達が廊下に到着したと報告が入った。
English: Just then, word arrived that the men on the upper floors had assembled in the corridor as instructed.

Japanese: 僕たちは手狭なモニタールームには入りきれずにドアの外に並んでいる彼らを確認する。
English: They could not all fit into the cramped monitor room, so we went to the door and looked over the men lined up outside.

Japanese: 彼らは総勢十五名。まだ到着していないものがもう、二、三人いるそうだ。
English: There were fifteen in all. We were told that another two or three had not yet arrived.

Japanese: 彼らの武器を調べると、ほとんどが拳銃のみを手にし、それ以外では警備担当のものが二人、小型のサブマシンガンを持っているだけだった。その他には、日本刀や青竜刀などの刃物を持って来ていたが、これは今回の敵には役に立たないだろう。倉庫にあったのは軍用のライフルが八丁で、拳銃が約三十丁、サブマシンガンが五丁。
English: An inspection of their weapons showed that almost all carried only pistols. The sole exceptions were two guards with compact submachine guns. Others had brought Japanese swords, Chinese broadswords, and similar blades, but those would be of no use against this enemy. The armory held eight military rifles, approximately thirty pistols, and five submachine guns.

Japanese: 「天下のYSの武器庫のわりにはおもちゃみたいな武器しかないんだね」
English: “For the arsenal of the mighty YS, these are remarkably toy-like weapons.”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、
English: At my words, Sai-kit replied.

Japanese: 「前は大物もたくさんあったらしいけれどねえ。ロケットランチャーなんかもずらっと揃えてたみたい。昔相手の事務所に打ち込んだ事件があったでしょ？　でも、そういうのは警察と協定を結んだときに手放したんだって。今は、街のもめ事に使うならこれで充分だしねえ……」
English: “Apparently they used to have plenty of heavy equipment. Rows of rocket launchers, even. You remember the incident when they fired one into an enemy office, don’t you? They gave up weapons like that when they reached their agreement with the police. What we have now is more than enough for disputes within the city...”

Japanese: 世傑は倉庫から持って来た拳銃の一つを懐に入れながら、
English: Sai-kit slipped one of the pistols from the armory into his coat.

Japanese: 「もっとも、たとえミサイルがあったって、正体不明の能力をもったタイプAを相手にするのは気分がよくないわね。まったくもって、何をされるのかわからない」
English: “Although even a missile would do little to improve my mood when we’re facing a Type A with an unknown ability. We have absolutely no idea what she may do.”

Japanese: そう顔を顰める。
English: He grimaced.

Japanese: 「同感だけど、お客さんの方から勝手に訊ねてきたんだから、あるものでもてなさないといけないよ」
English: “I agree. But the guest has chosen to call without an invitation, so we must entertain her with whatever we have.”

Japanese: 「こんな状況じゃフルコースをご馳走するのは無理よ？」
English: “Under these conditions, we can hardly offer her a full-course meal.”

Japanese: 「それでも満足はさせるさ。シェフの腕の見せ所だ」
English: “We will satisfy her all the same. This is the chef’s opportunity to demonstrate his art.”

Japanese: すぐに僕たちが部屋に戻って龍頭とジェフリーに状況を報告すると、彼らは彼らで今後の方策を話し合っていたようだ。
English: When we returned to the room and reported the situation to the Longtou and Jeffrey, we found that they had been discussing their own course of action.

Japanese: 「まず非戦闘員を避難させなければいけません。集まった女子供には護衛をつけ、出口へ向かって移動させます。避難ルートは、天明のレーダーを頼りにこちらから適宜指示するのがベストですね。そして残った我々が、この最上階で相手を待ち受けます。……この方針がベストでしょう」
English: “We must evacuate the noncombatants first. Give the assembled women and children an escort and move them toward the exit. Relying on Tin-ming’s radar, we can redirect them as circumstances demand. Those of us who remain will await the adversary here on the top floor. ...That would appear to be our best course.”

Japanese: 彼の問いかけに、僕は頷く。
English: I nodded in answer to his question.

Japanese: 「みんなで逃げるって手もあるわよ？」
English: “We could all run away.”

Japanese: 世傑が苦笑しながら言うが、
English: Sai-kit offered the suggestion with a bitter smile.

Japanese: 「本当はそうしたいさ。けれど、ビルには大勢住んでいる。守らなくちゃいけない人々もいる。相手の目的はまだ定かじゃないが、仕留められるなら、それがベストだ」
English: “In truth, that is what I would prefer. But a great many people live in this building, including people we are obliged to protect. We still don’t know the attacker’s purpose, but if we can kill her, that would be best.”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、
English: At my words, Sai-kit agreed.

Japanese: 「そうね。それに、小娘一人にビルを捨てて全員で逃げたら、普段威張ってるYSがって、みんなに笑われちゃうわ」
English: “Yes. And if the great YS, after all its usual swaggering, abandoned the building and fled in its entirety from one little girl, everyone would laugh at us.”

Japanese: 世傑が意見を翻して同調し、その言葉に龍頭が苦い顔をする。
English: Sai-kit reversed his position. The Longtou’s expression turned bitter at his words.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、馬明とか、ビルの外にいるメンバーには襲撃を報せたのかい？」
English: “Speaking of which, have Ma Ming and the other members outside the building been informed of the attack?”

Japanese: 「はい、最初の段階で。急行するとのことですが、間に合いはしないでしょう」
English: “Yes, at the very beginning. They intend to hurry here, but they cannot possibly arrive in time.”

Japanese: 「だろうね。それに、来ても被害者が増えるだけかもしれない」
English: “I thought not. Besides, their arrival might only increase the number of victims.”

Japanese: 僕は溜息をつき、ジェフリーがその通り部下に命じている間、手近なソファーに身を沈める。
English: I sighed and sank onto the nearest sofa while Jeffrey issued the orders we had discussed.

Japanese: 「さて、それではこの化け物をうまく迎撃する方法を考えようか。……そうだ天明、まだ相手の位置は特定出来ないかい？」
English: “Now, let us devise a way to deal with this monster. ...Tin-ming, have you still been unable to identify her position?”

Japanese: 僕が訊ねると、緊張のせいか、暑くもないのに首元がじっとりと汗ばんだ天明は首を横に振る。
English: At my question, Tin-ming shook her head. From tension, perhaps, the skin around her neck was damp with sweat even though the room was not warm.

Japanese: 「まだ下層は混乱していて、なんとも。通知は携帯電話にメールで送ったものですから、気がついていないものもいるかもしれません。……館内放送でアナウンスしますか？」
English: “The lower floors remain in confusion, so we cannot say. We sent the evacuation notice by email to their mobile phones, and some may not have seen it. ...Should we make an announcement over the building’s system?”

Japanese: 「それはやめとこう。相手にも聞かれてしまうからね。こっちが対応してるってことをはっきり知られたくない。……なるべく多くの人が無事に逃げられればいいんだけれどね……」
English: “No. The attacker would hear it too. I would rather not make it clear that we are responding to her presence. ...I only hope as many people as possible can escape safely...”

Japanese: 下層にいるのはYSのメンバーだけではない。ビル内に店舗を構え、メンバー相手に営業を行うクリーニング屋、料理店、子供達に勉強を教える教師など……彼らの多くはこういった非常事態には慣れていないだろうし、スムーズな行動も期待は出来ない。YSのメンバーが誘導に当たっているはずだが、それでも、彼らがビルから去るのには、相当な時間がかかるだろう。
English: The people on the lower floors were not limited to YS members. There were dry cleaners, restaurants, tutors who taught the children, and other businesses within the tower that served the organization’s people. Most would be unaccustomed to an emergency of this kind, and we could not expect them to move smoothly. YS members should have been guiding them, but even so, their departure from the building would take considerable time.

Japanese: それよりも、あの女が中層に足を踏み入れて、それを天明たちが発見する方が先かもしれない。
English: The woman might set foot upon the middle floors, allowing Tin-ming and Tin-cheung to discover her, before that evacuation was complete.

Japanese: 僕がソファーに座って考えている間、部屋の他の人々は女が殺す場面を繰り返し眺めて、あれこれと話し合っている。
English: While I sat upon the sofa and considered the problem, the others replayed the woman’s killing again and again and debated what they saw.

Japanese: 「……世傑君。この映像のスピードで連続的に瞬間移動してくる相手に銃弾を命中させることは可能ですか？」
English: “...Sai-kit, could you strike an adversary with a bullet if she teleported repeatedly at the speed shown in this recording?”

Japanese: 「とても自信がないわ」
English: “I’m not remotely confident.”

Japanese: ジェフリーの質問に、彼は首を横に振る。
English: Sai-kit shook his head at Jeffrey’s question.

Japanese: 「そうですか。だとすれば、相手からの攻撃を防ぐのは不可能に近いということになりますね。……なら、こちらから攻撃する方が良いのでしょう。幸い、こちらには監視カメラと、天明たちの人間レーダーという優れた目があります。これを利用して先制攻撃するのが最善でしょうか……小謝、どう思います？」
English: “I see. Then defending against her attack would be nearly impossible. ...Perhaps it would be better for us to attack first. Fortunately, the surveillance cameras and Tin-ming and Tin-cheung’s human radar give us excellent eyes. Would our best course be to use them for a preemptive strike? ...What do you think, Siu Tse?”

Japanese: 「まあそうなんだけど、瞬間移動する相手に先制攻撃の機会を作るのが難しい」
English: “That is true. But creating an opportunity for a preemptive strike against someone who can teleport will be difficult.”

Japanese: 「それは確かに」
English: “Indeed.”

Japanese: 先に攻撃出来るなら、それは確かに最良の手段かもしれない。しかし、いくら天明のレーダーがあっても、壁も天井も無視して移動する相手に先制攻撃を加えるのは、不可能とは言わないが非常に困難だ。外部から直接上層にテレポーテーションして来ずに、一階ロビーに姿を現した点からすると、敵の能力はそう遠くまで移動出来るものではないのかもしれないが、映像で見せたような短いジャンプで連続して上に移動してきたら、到底追いつけるものではない。
English: If we could attack first, it might indeed be the best method. Yet even with Tin-ming’s radar, launching the first strike against an enemy who passed through walls and ceilings would be exceedingly difficult, if not impossible. The fact that she had appeared in the first-floor lobby instead of teleporting directly into the upper stories from outside might indicate that her ability could not carry her very far. But if she ascended through a rapid succession of short jumps like those we had seen in the recording, we could never catch her.

Japanese: しかも、中途半端な形で遭遇すれば、それこそ銃で狙いを付けるよりも早く、一瞬にしてこちらが殺されてしまうのだ。
English: And if we encountered her before we were fully prepared, she would kill us in an instant, before we could even bring a gun to bear.

Japanese: 「まあ、タイプAの能力は使うと疲労するものらしいから、そう無制限に連続で瞬間移動出来るとは限らないけど。でも個人差があるからね。この相手が一回能力を使うごとにどの程度消耗するかなんて、現段階ではまったくわからない」
English: “Then again, using a Type A ability apparently causes fatigue, so she may not be able to teleport repeatedly without limit. But that varies from one person to another. At present, we have no idea how much each use of her ability exhausts this particular adversary.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ、どうするのよ」
English: “Then what are we going to do?”

Japanese: 「そうせかすなよ。慎みて軽速なるなかれ」
English: “Don’t hurry me. Be cautious; do not play hastily.”

Japanese: 「孫子かなにか？」
English: “Is that Sun Tzu or something?”

Japanese: 「囲碁の格言。僕もいま一番良い方法を考えているんだ」
English: “A Go proverb. I am trying to discover our best move.”

Japanese: 「……ねえ、どうせここに来るのは直通エレベーターと非常階段しかないんだし、そこに何人か先回りさせておいたほうが良くないかしら？　ここで廊下に待機させているのは、無駄のような気がするのよ」
English: “...Listen. The only ways up here are the express elevator and the emergency stairs. Wouldn’t it be better to send a few people ahead to cover them? Keeping everyone waiting in this corridor feels like a waste.”

Japanese: 世傑もやはり危機を感じているらしく、いつも以上に緊迫した面持ちだった。
English: Sai-kit plainly sensed the danger as well. His expression was more tense than usual.

Japanese: 「それは分かるけど、何の策もなくエレベーターや非常階段みたいな場所で待ち受けて、この相手を上手く仕留められる気がしない」
English: “I understand your point, but I doubt we can kill this opponent merely by waiting at an elevator or emergency stairwell without a plan.”

Japanese: 「いや、世傑の言うことは一理あります」
English: “No. There is merit in Sai-kit’s suggestion.”

Japanese: 黙って聞いていたジェフリーが口を挟んだ。
English: Jeffrey, who had listened in silence, interjected.

Japanese: 「幸い、ライフルがいくつかあります。どこか見通しのいい通路に使えるやつを配置して、相手の視界の外からの狙撃を行わせましょう」
English: “Fortunately, we have several rifles. Let us position men proficient with them at the end of a corridor with a clear line of sight and have them fire from beyond the adversary’s view.”

Japanese: タイプAに対して、ライフルなどの距離をおいて相手を一方的に殺害出来る武器を使用するというのは、いつの場合でもきわめて有効だ。
English: Against a Type A, a weapon such as a rifle, which permitted the wielder to kill from a distance without allowing a reply, was exceptionally effective in almost any situation.

Japanese: 「悪くはないけれど……」
English: “It is not a bad idea, but...”

Japanese: 今回の場合、もっと他に良い方法があるような気がする。
English: In this instance, I felt that some better method existed.

Japanese: しかし、漠然とした感覚のようなもので、うまく言葉にすることが出来なかった。
English: It was nothing more than a vague impression, however, and I could not put it properly into words.

Japanese: 「誰か、ライフルの扱いに特に自信があるものを五人くらい選んで……」
English: “Choose approximately five men who are particularly confident with a rifle and...”

Japanese: 僕の言葉を待たず、ジェフリーが部下に言いかけたところで、
English: Without waiting for me, Jeffrey had begun to give the order when—
“Ah—just now...”

Japanese: 天明と天祥の姉妹が声を揃えた。
English: Tin-ming and Tin-cheung had spoken in unison.

Japanese: 「どうした？　何かあったか？」
English: “What is it? Did something happen?”

Japanese: ジェフリーが鋭く訊ねると、天明が説明をする。
English: At Jeffrey’s sharp question, Tin-ming explained.

Japanese: 「か、下層で避難中の集団に変化がありました。二階のロビー付近の通路で、それまでスムーズに移動していた集団が突然パニックを起こしています」
English: “T-there was a change in one of the groups evacuating below. Near the second-floor lobby, a group that had been moving smoothly through the corridor suddenly fell into panic.”

Japanese: 「襲撃を受けたのか？」
English: “Were they attacked?”

Japanese: 僕はそう訊ねる。
English: I asked her.

Japanese: 「そのようですが……だれか死んだかどうかは、混乱のせいで、正確に判別することが出来ません……」
English: “It appears so... But with the confusion, we cannot determine precisely whether anyone has died...”

Japanese: 「正確な場所は？」
English: “Where, exactly?”

Japanese: 「おそらく、２１２号室周辺の廊下だと思います」
English: “I believe it is the corridor near Room 212.”

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは頷き、
English: Jeffrey nodded.

Japanese: 「その辺りなら、監視カメラの映像があるはずです。切り換えを頼む」
English: “There should be a surveillance camera covering that area. Change the feed.”

Japanese: 「はい」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: ジェフリーの命令の前からすでにその行動に取りかかっていたらしく、画面はすぐに切り替わる。
English: The surveillance operator appeared to have begun even before Jeffrey gave the order, for the picture changed at once.

Japanese: 案の定、その廊下も血にまみれていた。
English: As expected, that corridor too was covered in blood.

Japanese: 床には先ほどの田尻と同じようなバラバラ死体が散らばり、その血だまりのなかに黒衣の少女が立っている。
English: Dismembered bodies like Tajiri’s were scattered across the floor, and the girl in black stood amid their blood.

Japanese: 「画面に映ってる遺体は男二人と、女一人分だけだな。この場所にいたのはこれだけ？」
English: “I can see parts belonging to two men and one woman. Were those the only people there?”

Japanese: バラバラ死体の手足の数をかぞえてから僕はそう訊ねる。
English: I asked after counting the arms and legs among the scattered remains.

Japanese: 「いえ、十人程度はいました。一つ現場にのこった生命以外は、みな離れたようです」
English: “No. There were approximately ten. Except for one life remaining at the scene, all the others have moved away.”

Japanese: 「出会った相手を皆殺しにするってわけでもないんだね。やろうと思えば出来るんだろうけど」
English: “Then she does not necessarily kill everyone she encounters. I imagine she could if she wished.”

Japanese: 死体の上に立ち、廊下の向こうがわ……おそらく家族が逃げていった方向をぼんやりとながめている少女の後ろ姿を見ながら、僕はそう呟く。
English: I murmured the observation while watching the girl’s back as she stood upon the bodies and stared vacantly down the corridor—probably in the direction the family members had fled.

Japanese: そこでモニタールームの電話が鳴った。すぐに部下の一人がとると、今まさに襲撃を受けた家族からのものだったので、通話をスピーカーに切り換える。
English: The monitor-room telephone rang. One of the men answered at once. The caller belonged to the family group that had just been attacked, and he switched the call to the speaker.

Japanese: 『きゅ、きゅうにっ、血をふいて倒れてっ……』
English: ‘S-suddenly, they sprayed blood and fell—’

Japanese: 動揺に取り乱す女の声が、生々しい当事者の感覚をモニタールームの静まりかえった空間に呼び起こす。
English: The frantic woman’s voice brought the raw immediacy of the event into the silent monitor room.

Japanese: 今回襲撃を受けたのは、下層に住むYSメンバーの家族達だったらしい。避難途中で不幸にも敵に遭遇し、命を落としてしまったのだ。
English: The group attacked this time appeared to have consisted of the families of YS members living on the lower floors. They had encountered the enemy during their evacuation, and some had lost their lives in the attack.

Japanese: ジェフリーはそれをなだめつつ、彼女に別の退避ルートを指示するよう部下に命じた。
English: Jeffrey soothed the caller while ordering a subordinate to direct her toward another evacuation route.

Japanese: そのやりとりをしている間にも、画面上の少女には動きがある。
English: Even as he did so, the girl on the screen began to move.

Japanese: 彼女は血だまりから抜け出すと、廊下になすりつけるようにして裸足の足の裏の血を拭い、そして袖で顔にかかった返り血を拭き取るなどという行為をしていたのだが、不意に床の上に膝をついて、うなだれた。
English: She stepped out of the pool of blood, wiped the soles of her bare feet against the corridor floor as though smearing it there, and used her sleeve to clean the spattered blood from her face. Then, without warning, she sank to her knees and bowed her head.

Japanese: 「ど、どうしたんだ？　具合でも悪くなったのか？　腹痛とか……」
English: “W-what is wrong with her? Has she become ill? A stomachache, perhaps...”

Japanese: もちろん龍頭は期待してそう言ったのだろうけれども、声の響きが体調を心配しているようにも聞こえておかしかった。
English: Naturally, the Longtou must have asked in hope. Yet his tone also made him sound concerned for her health, which was amusing.

Japanese: 「これ、祈っているのよ」
English: “She is praying.”

Japanese: 世傑が言うとおり、胸の前で手を組み、唇を小さく動かしている少女の様子は、神に向かって祈りを捧げているようにも見えた。
English: As Sai-kit said, the girl’s clasped hands and faintly moving lips made it appear that she was offering a prayer to a god.

Japanese: 「懺悔の祈りでもしてるのかな。殺人マシーンじみた手際のよさで人を殺しておいて、信心深いもんだな」
English: “A prayer of repentance, perhaps? She kills with the efficiency of a machine, yet she is remarkably devout.”

Japanese: 僕がそう呟くと、世傑は呆れたように溜息をつき、
English: At my murmur, Sai-kit gave an exasperated sigh.

Japanese: 「あら、小謝も案外不勉強ね。これが人間ってものよ。どんな人間だって、どんなに慣れたって、心に何か特別な支えがなければ殺人なんて続けていけないわ」
English: “My, Siu Tse, you are unexpectedly ignorant. This is what human beings are. No matter who they are or how accustomed they become, no one can continue killing without something special to cling to.”

Japanese: 「それは体験談かい？」
English: “Do you speak from experience?”

Japanese: 「そうよ」
English: “I do.”

Japanese: 「案外ヒューマニストなんだね」
English: “You are more of a humanist than I expected.”

Japanese: 「当然だわ。人を殺せば誰でもそうなる」
English: “Naturally. Killing does that to everyone.”

Japanese: 断言する世傑に対して僕は苦笑し、
English: Sai-kit said it flatly, and I gave a wry smile.

Japanese: 「どういう事情があるにしろ、相手を殺すたびに神だかなんだかにのんびり祈りを捧げてくれるんなら、僕らにとってはありがたい話だね」
English: “Whatever her circumstances, if she takes her time praying to some god or other every time she kills, that is excellent news for us.”

Japanese: そう話し合う僕らをよそに、ジェフリーと龍頭も言葉を交わす。
English: While we talked, Jeffrey and the Longtou exchanged words of their own.

Japanese: 「とにかく、これはチャンスですね。誰か近くに武器を持ったものはいないか？　今なら無防備です。攻撃をするチャンスでしょう」
English: “In any event, this is an opportunity. Is there anyone armed nearby? She is defenseless now. This is our chance to attack.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは早速部下に命じて手配するが、しかし、奇襲を加える時間はないようだった。
English: Jeffrey immediately ordered his men to arrange it, but there appeared to be no time for a surprise attack.

Japanese: 画面のなかの少女は祈りをやめ、立ち上がっていた。そしてぴょんと跳躍すると、空中で消えてしまうのである。
English: The girl on the screen had ended her prayer and risen. She gave a little jump and vanished in midair.

Japanese: 「天明」
English: “Tin-ming.”

Japanese: 僕が短くその名を呼ぶ。
English: I called her name curtly.

Japanese: 「廊下の生命反応は消えて、西方向に新しい反応があらわれました。ロビー付近に移動したと思われます」
English: “The life response in the corridor has disappeared, and a new response has appeared to the west. I believe she moved near the lobby.”

Japanese: その言葉を受けて、モニターを操作する部下は、誰かの指示を待つまでもなく画面を切り換える。
English: At those words, the man operating the monitors changed the feed without waiting for anyone’s command.

Japanese: 田尻が殺された部屋の真上に当たる二階ロビーのカメラは、四つ並ぶエレベーターのドアを見下ろす形で設置されていた。
English: The camera in the second-floor lobby, directly above the room where Tajiri had been killed, looked down upon four elevator doors standing in a row.

Japanese: 少女は画面端からとことこと歩いてきて、そのドアの並ぶ前に立つと、ぴょんと飛び、そして姿を消した。黄姉妹のレーダーによると、エレベータールーム内部で目まぐるしく移動をしたようだ。そしてまた、監視カメラの映し出す風景のなかに現れる。
English: The girl pattered into view from the edge of the screen and stopped before the doors. She jumped, then vanished. According to the Wong sisters’ radar, she moved about the inside of the elevator room at a dizzying pace before reappearing on camera.

Japanese: ビルの警備システムをチェックしていた部下の報告によると、彼女はエレベーターのケーブルを切断し、使えなくしたらしい。
English: A subordinate inspecting the building’s security systems reported that she appeared to have severed the elevator cables, disabling them.

Japanese: 「我々を逃がさないというつもりか」
English: “Does she intend to prevent our escape?”

Japanese: 龍頭が渋い顔で言うのを、
English: The Longtou grimaced as he said it.

Japanese: 「まあ、非常階段もあるけどね」
English: “We still have the emergency stairs.”

Japanese: 世傑がまぜっかえす。
English: Sai-kit could not resist the rejoinder.

Japanese: 「とりあえず、こいつの用件は最上層にある僕らだってのははっきりしたね。それならそうと言ってくれればいいのに」
English: “At least we now know she came for us on the upper floors. She could have simply said so.”

Japanese: 少女はエレベーターの前を少しうろうろした後、また軽くジャンプをして、瞬間移動をした。今度は二つ上の階へと移動したようだ。
English: The girl wandered for a moment before the elevators, then gave another light jump and teleported. This time she appeared to have moved two floors upward.

Japanese: どうも、計画性があるのかないのかよくわからない。移動の仕方を見ていると無駄が多く、ビルの構造などをあらかじめ把握して来たわけでもなさそうだ。
English: I could not decide whether she had a plan. Her movements were remarkably inefficient, and it did not appear that she had studied the building’s structure in advance.

Japanese: エレベーターを破壊したのも、あらかじめそうと決めてきたわけではなく、目の前にあったからなんとなく破壊したように思える。最初から使用不可能にするつもりなら、一階ロビーで田尻を殺傷した時点でそうしていたはずだ。
English: Even the destruction of the elevators looked less like a predetermined objective than something she had done because they happened to be in front of her. Had she intended from the beginning to make them unusable, she should have done so when she attacked Tajiri in the first-floor lobby.

Japanese: 家族と出会った時も、中途半端に殺しているが、あれも意味がわからない。戦闘力がある男だけを狙ったようにも見えるが、本当に警戒するなら女だからといって他を逃がすのは甘いし、戦闘したくないなら最初から避けるのも容易なはずだ。
English: Nor could I understand why she had killed only some of the family group she encountered. She appeared to have targeted the men capable of fighting. Yet if she were truly cautious, sparing the others merely because they were women would be naive. If she wished to avoid combat, she could easily have avoided the entire group from the beginning.

Japanese: 戦い方だけは手慣れているが、行動はどうも行き当たりばったりだ。
English: Her fighting was practiced; everything else she did seemed improvised.

Japanese: 慣れてはいても、所詮小娘ということなのだろうか？　戦闘能力が高すぎるから、綿密に計画を立てたりしないでもやってこれたのかもしれない。
English: Perhaps, for all her experience, she was merely a young girl. Or perhaps her ability was so overwhelming that she had never needed to plan in detail.

Japanese: 「少し迷っているのかどうか、うろうろしてはいますが、どうやらこっちへ向かおうとはしているようですね」
English: “She is wandering a little, perhaps because she is lost, but she does appear to be attempting to come toward us.”

Japanese: 天明が少女の位置を報告するのを聞きながら、ジェフリーはそう呟く。
English: Jeffrey murmured the observation as he listened to Tin-ming report the girl’s position.

Japanese: 「この子、随分のんびりしてるわね。アタシたちが襲撃に気がついてないとでも思ってるのかしら？　人間レーダーがいるなんて知らないでしょうし」
English: “This child is taking her time. Does she imagine we haven’t noticed the attack? I suppose she wouldn’t know that we have human radar.”

Japanese: 世傑が首をひねる。
English: Sai-kit tilted his head.

Japanese: 「普通のビルだったらそう思うかもしれないけど、ここは僕らの本拠地なんだよ？　監視カメラにもばっちり映ってるし、いくらなんでもそこまで何も考えていないとは……」
English: “She might believe that in an ordinary building, but this is our headquarters. The surveillance cameras have captured her perfectly. Surely she cannot be quite that thoughtless...”

Japanese: 「ないとは言い切れないわ。だって子供なのよ」
English: “We cannot rule it out. She is a child.”

Japanese: 「ただの子供だと思うのは危険だと思うけどなあ」
English: “It would be dangerous to assume she is an ordinary child.”

Japanese: 僕もそこはどうも自信がなかったが、
English: I was not entirely sure of that myself, but—

Japanese: 「ともあれ、相手の目的が僕らならばやりやすい。家族を下ろすなら、今がタイミングかな？　ジェフリー、そう思わない？」
English: “In any case, if we are her objective, that simplifies matters. This may be the moment to take the families downstairs. Don’t you agree, Jeffrey?”

Japanese: 「同感です」
English: “I do.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは頷き、龍頭の許可を得ると、早速その指示を出した。
English: Jeffrey nodded. Once he had obtained the Longtou’s permission, he immediately issued the order.

Japanese: 相手は下層からエレベーターを使わずに、徒歩と瞬間移動を交えながら階を上がってきている。
English: The adversary was ascending from the lower floors through a combination of walking and teleportation, without using the elevators.

Japanese: 上層で待機している家族達はエレベーターで降りられる一番低い階の十五階までまず降りる。そこからさらに下まで降りるエレベーターは破壊されてしまったから、そこから下は少女とはなるべく離れた階段を使って降りることになる。
English: The families waiting above would first take the elevator down to the lowest floor it could reach, the fifteenth. The elevators continuing lower had been destroyed. From there, they would have to descend by whichever stairwell kept them farthest from the girl.

Japanese: 少女は行ったり来たりしながら進んでいるから正確な予測は難しいが、エレベーターを降りきって、そしてさらに一階か二階降りたあたりですれ違うことになるだろう。そこで出会ってしまえば凄惨なことになるかもしれないが、エレベーターさえ降りきってしまえば、ビルの構造を知り、黄姉妹の目がある我々がうまくやりすごせる公算が高い。
English: Her back-and-forth progress made a precise prediction difficult, but we would likely cross her level after the families had left the elevator and descended another one or two floors. Encountering her then could be appalling. Once clear of the elevator, however, our knowledge of the building and the Wong sisters’ sight would give us a strong chance of avoiding her.

Japanese: 準備が整ったところで、
English: Once the preparations were complete,

Japanese: 「よし、じゃあ、龍頭とジェフリーは天明達を連れてみんなを誘導してくれないかな？」
English: “Good. Longtou, Jeffrey, would you take Tin-ming and Tin-cheung and direct everyone?”

Japanese: と僕は言った。
English: I said.

Japanese: ジェフリーが露骨に顔を顰めるのを無視して、言葉を続ける。
English: Ignoring Jeffrey’s open frown, I continued.

Japanese: 「ここは僕と世傑が受け持つ。それで、あのタイプＡを迎え撃つ」
English: “Sai-kit and I will hold this position and face the Type A.”

Japanese: 「小謝」
English: “Siu Tse.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは苦々しく僕を咎める。
English: Jeffrey rebuked me bitterly.

Japanese: 「言いたいことはわかる。でも、それが一番成功率が高い配置なんだ。龍頭を危険から遠ざけなくちゃいけない」
English: “I know what you mean to say. But this deployment gives us the highest probability of success. We must keep the Longtou out of danger.”

Japanese: 「アンタはいいけど、勝手に居残り組に入れられたアタシの意見は？」
English: “Fine for you. What about my opinion, when you’ve decided I’m staying behind without even asking me?”

Japanese: そこで世傑が口を挟むが、
English: Sai-kit interjected.

Japanese: 「きみは僕の部下じゃないか」
English: “You are my subordinate, aren’t you?”

Japanese: 僕が言うと、いやそうに顔にしわを浮かべる。
English: At my answer, he grimaced in distaste.

Japanese: 「今回ばかりはその意見を通すわけには行きません。個人的な手柄なら、もう劉建志の件で充分です。自重してください」
English: “On this occasion, I cannot possibly allow you to prevail. You won more than enough personal distinction in the matter of Ryu Kenshi. Exercise some restraint.”

Japanese: 「そうだとも」
English: “Precisely.”

Japanese: 龍頭が珍しく語気を強くして同調する。
English: For once, the Longtou added his support in a forceful tone.

Japanese: 「形式としていまは私が龍頭の座を務めさせて貰っているが、本当の後継者はお前なのだぞ。お前こそ、みなとともに避難しなくてはならないのだ」
English: “Formally, I have been allowed to serve as Longtou for the present. But you are the true successor. You, more than anyone, must evacuate with the others.”

Japanese: 彼は僕をまっすぐと見つめる。
English: He looked directly into my eyes.

Japanese: 「逆に私は、形式的でも龍頭である以上は、部下を捨てて逃ることなど出来ない。ここに残る」
English: “Conversely, formal or not, I am the Longtou. I cannot abandon my subordinates and run. I will remain here.”

Japanese: 「いや、龍頭も小謝と一緒に避難してください」
English: “No. Longtou, you will evacuate with Siu Tse.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはぴしゃりと言う。
English: Jeffrey said it sharply.

Japanese: 「しかし、私は……」
English: “But I...”

Japanese: 龍頭はなおも何か言いたげだった、ジェフリーはそれを遮って、
English: The Longtou still appeared to have something to say, but Jeffrey interrupted him.

Japanese: 「ここには私が残ります」
English: “I will remain.”

Japanese: そう断言した。
English: He declared it.

Japanese: 「何を言ってるんだ。相手は未知のタイプＡなんだよ？　ここは僕じゃないと……」
English: “What are you saying? The adversary is an unknown Type A. This is a task that requires me—”

Japanese: 僕のスタイルからすると、こういう場面では絶対に譲るわけにはいかないのだが、
English: By nature, I could never yield in a situation like this, but—

Japanese: 「小謝、それはいかん。お前こそが義勝の希望なのだ」
English: “Siu Tse, that will not do. You are the hope of Yisheng.”

Japanese: 他ならぬ龍頭からそう言われると、抗弁がしにくい。
English: Coming from the Longtou himself, the words made protest difficult.

Japanese: 彼は自分の口ではっきりと、自分がたんなる繋ぎであり僕が真の後継者であると語っている。彼だってこの業界ではそれなりの立場がある人間なのだ。先代の血縁とはいえ、この間まで街を出て好き勝手やっていた僕に、そこまで言う、その心情は察するに余り有った。
English: He had stated plainly, in his own voice, that he was merely a bridge and I the true successor. He, too, was a man of considerable standing in this world. Even if I was a blood relative of the former Longtou, I had been living outside the city and doing precisely as I pleased until only days ago. I could more than imagine what it cost him to go so far.

Japanese: 僕は思わず黙ってしまう。
English: I fell silent despite myself.

Japanese: 「何でもいいから、早くきめてよ！　自分が残る、自分が残るって言い争ってるうちに、家族は逃げ遅れて、結局全員で居残ることになるわ？」
English: “I don’t care which of you stays. Decide quickly! If you keep arguing that you will stay and you will stay, the families will miss their chance to escape and we will all end up staying.”

Japanese: 世傑が茶化すのももっともだ。
English: Sai-kit’s mockery was justified.

Japanese: 「ここは私が決定します。私にはその権利があります。抗命は許しません」
English: “I will decide this matter. I have the authority to do so. I will tolerate no disobedience.”

Japanese: ジェフリーは有無を言わさぬ調子で言った。
English: Jeffrey’s tone admitted no argument.

Japanese: 「小謝、策があるなら、それをここで言うのです。私がそれを実行しましょう」
English: “Siu Tse, if you have a plan, explain it here. I will execute it.”

Japanese: 「しかしこれは……」
English: “But this...”

Japanese: ジェフリーは僕の言葉を最後まで聞かない。
English: Jeffrey did not permit me to finish.

Japanese: 「小謝は、自分の作戦は自分で実行すれば、作戦が外れて失敗したときでも、自分の命で責任が取れると考えているのではありませんか？　そんな幼い考え方は捨てなさい。あなたはこれから龍頭になるのです。自分の考えた方針で、部下が危険にさらされることは、この先何度もあるでしょう。そのたびに自分が現場に赴くつもりですか？　あなたにどれだけ自信があるのか知りませんが、すべての作戦が成功するわけじゃないでしょう。そんなことをしていれば、すぐに死にますよ」
English: “Do you imagine that by personally executing your own plan, you can pay for its failure with your own life? Abandon that childish mode of thought. You will be the Longtou in the future. Time and again, your decisions will expose your subordinates to danger. Do you mean to go into the field yourself on every occasion? I do not know how great your confidence may be, but not every plan will succeed. If you behave that way, you will soon be dead.”

Japanese: 随分はっきりと言う。
English: He was remarkably blunt.

Japanese: その物言いに驚いていると、彼はさらに続ける。
English: Surprised by how bluntly he had put it, I listened as he continued.

Japanese: 「本音を言うと、私は皆が言うほどあなたを評価していません。しかしあなたは先代の決めた後継者なのです。皆そう思っているから、あなたを優先して逃がそうとしている」
English: “To speak frankly, I do not esteem you as highly as everyone else appears to. But you are the successor chosen by the former Longtou. Everyone believes that, and for that reason, they are attempting to secure your escape before their own.”

Japanese: そしてじっと僕を見つめる。
English: He stared steadily at me.

Japanese: 「気分を害しましたか？」
English: “Have I offended you?”

Japanese: 「そりゃ害するよ。僕にも感情ってものがある。でも、ジェフリーがそう思ってるのは知ってたから、今更だよ」
English: “Of course you have. I have feelings too. But I already knew what you thought of me, so it hardly comes as news.”

Japanese: 「そうですか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 「どう思われてたって、僕は自分が持ってるものでやるしかないからね。……それより、いまあんたは、なんだか撃退出来ずに死ぬのが決まってるような言い方だったけれど……」
English: “Whatever anyone thinks of me, I can only work with what I’ve got. ...More importantly, you just spoke as though it had already been decided that you would fail and die...”

Japanese: 僕は溜息をついて、
English: I sighed.

Japanese: 「僕が残れば僕らは必ず勝つだろう。だけど、あんたらはどうだろうね。そこまで言うなら譲るが、やるからには確実に成功させてもらう。そのための僕の意見は受け入れてもらう。僕は未来のリーダーなんだろう？」
English: “If I stayed, we would certainly win. But whether you can do the same is another question. If you insist so strongly, I will yield. But once you undertake it, I expect certain success, and you will follow my advice toward that end. I am to be the future leader, am I not?”

Japanese: 言うと、ジェフリーが少し笑ったのがしゃくに障った。
English: Jeffrey smiled slightly when I said it, which irritated me.

Japanese: だから僕はさらに「あんな写真がばらまかれたから死にたいのかもしれないが、死ねないからね」と付け足そうと思ったけれども、さすがに可哀想なのでやめた。
English: I almost added, ‘Those photographs may have made you wish to die, but I will not permit it.’ In the end, pity stayed my tongue.

Japanese: ジェフリーに僕の考えた撃退案を伝えて、女子供達と共に移動を開始した。
English: I explained my proposed defense to Jeffrey, then began moving with the women and children.

Japanese: 僕に同行するのは龍頭マイケル・ツェー、レイレイ、馬世傑、黄天明と天祥の姉妹。ジェフリーは十名の部下と共に最上階に残った。避難する家族のなかにはジェフリーの妻もおり、別れ際に抱擁をかわした。
English: My party consisted of the Longtou, Michael Tse; Leilei; Ma Sai-kit; and the sisters Wong Tin-ming and Wong Tin-cheung. Jeffrey remained on the top floor with ten men. His wife was among the evacuating families, and the two embraced before parting.

Japanese: 避難する女子供達には今このビル内で起きていることをつまびらかに伝えてはいないが、この状況からただごとでないことは察しているようだった。しかし、その多くが幹部の家族ということだけあって、誰かを捕まえて質問攻めにするということもなく、むずがったり落ち着きのない子供達をなだめ、我々の指示を守ってくれた。
English: We had not informed the women and children of precisely what was happening inside the building, but the circumstances told them that it was no ordinary matter. Most belonged to the families of officers, and none cornered us with questions. They soothed the restless children and the ones beginning to complain, and obeyed our instructions.

Japanese: 高速エレベーターで中層の十五階まではすんなり降りることが出来た。黄姉妹のレーダーによると、相手は十二階付近にいる。ここで遭遇すれば、僕らは身を守るすべがない。一応銃を構えてはいるが、映像で見たような速度で瞬間移動を繰り返されれば弾は命中することなく、一方的にやられるだろう。
English: The express elevator carried us smoothly down through the middle stories to the fifteenth floor. According to the Wong sisters’ radar, the adversary was near the twelfth. If we encountered her here, we had no means of defending ourselves. We held our guns ready, but if she teleported repeatedly at the speed shown in the recording, not one bullet would strike her and we would be slaughtered without reply.

Japanese: ここまで相手は階段を使わず瞬間移動で階を上っている。何階か上るごとに、北側の階段と東側の階段の方を警戒するそぶりを魅せる。そしてその他に、少しその辺りをうろうろと歩るきまわったり、動きを止めてじっとしていたりする。ビルから脱出しようとするものを警戒しているつもりなのかもしれないが、相変わらず不規則で挙動不審だ。
English: Until now, she had ascended by teleportation without using the stairs. After climbing several floors, she would display an interest in the north and east stairwells. At other times, she wandered about the vicinity or stopped and remained entirely still. Perhaps she meant to watch for anyone attempting to escape the building, but her behavior remained irregular and suspicious.

Japanese: だからその移動先を正確に読むのは難しいが、十五階に到着した時点で直線距離はそれなりに開いている。
English: That made her destination difficult to predict precisely, but by the time we reached the fifteenth floor, a fair straight-line distance separated us.

Japanese: ここまで相手は長距離の瞬間移動は見せていなかったので、おそらく安全距離は保たれているだろう。
English: She had demonstrated no long-distance teleportation to this point, so we had probably preserved a safe distance.

Japanese: 我々は、おそらく彼女が見落としていると思われる西側の階段を使って一階まで降りることにした。
English: We decided to descend to the first floor by the western stairs, which she appeared to have overlooked.

Japanese: 十五階の階段を降りるのは女子供の体力では難しかったが、僕の想定では、一番下まで降りる必要はなく、どこかの段階で少女が最上層に辿り着き、そこでジェフリー達に処理される筈だった。
English: Fifteen floors of stairs would be difficult for the women and children. By my calculation, however, we would not need to reach the bottom. At some point along the way, the girl should reach the top floors and be disposed of by Jeffrey’s party.

Japanese: エレベーターから階段までの移動は、ひどく緊張する時間となる。
English: The walk from the elevator to the stairs was excruciatingly tense.

Japanese: 子供の混じった集団の移動はもともと遅いものだが、少女と出会った場合の無力さを知っている僕らにとってはより一層遅く感じられた。
English: A group containing children moved slowly under ordinary conditions. To those of us who understood how helpless we would be if we encountered the girl, the group seemed slower still.

Japanese: 「あっ」
English: “Ah.”

Japanese: と天明が声をあげた時はぎくりとした。
English: Tin-ming’s cry made me start.

Japanese: 「相手は上ではなく、こちらの方向へ、瞬間移動をしました」
English: “The adversary teleported toward us, not upward.”

Japanese: まさか何らかの方法で、我々に気がついたのか？　と肝を冷やしたが、次の移動で彼女は上の階へと飛び、ほっと胸をなで下ろす。
English: A chill passed through me at the thought that she might somehow have noticed us. Her next movement carried her to the floor above, however, and I breathed a sigh of relief.

Japanese: 「まったく、女の気まぐれに振り回されるってのはいやなものね」
English: “Nothing is more unpleasant than being jerked around by a woman’s whims.”

Japanese: さすがの世傑も冷や汗をかきながらそう言った。
English: Even Sai-kit broke into a cold sweat as he spoke.

Japanese: そして僕達は階段まで辿り着く。少女はさっきのようにエレベーターを破壊してから、北側階段を警戒しながら最上層へ向かっているようだった。
English: Then we reached the stairs. The girl appeared to have destroyed the elevator as before, after which she continued toward the highest floors while watching the northern stairwell.

Japanese: 我々の方はひとまず危機を脱したと言って良いだろう。ここから先は焦って駆け出して転び落ちたりしないよう、慎重に降りて行けばいいだけだ。
English: It was reasonable to say that we had escaped the immediate danger. From here, we needed only descend with care, without rushing and tumbling down the stairs.

Japanese: 僕たちはジェフリー達と常に連絡を取りながら移動している。ここで僕は、
English: We maintained constant contact with Jeffrey’s party as we moved. At that point, I said to him,

Japanese: 「相手の警戒はまったくなってない。素晴らしくガバガバだよ。まだ全員で逃げるっていう手段が残っているけどどうする？　本当はね、こんな奇襲とまともに戦うなんて愚かな作戦なんだ。可能ならば戦わずに逃げるべきだ」
English: “Her vigilance is nonexistent. Her movements are magnificently full of openings. We still have the option of everyone escaping. What do you think? The truth is, meeting a surprise attack like this head-on is a foolish plan. If flight is possible, we ought to flee without fighting.”

Japanese: 中層から上へ向かう階段は少なく、二つしかない。エレベーターは壊され、北側は警戒されているが、しかし天明の報告からすると南側の階段の側には近づいていない。そこを通れば最上層にいるものたちも脱出することが出来るだろう。
English: Few stairs connected the middle and upper stories; there were only two. The elevator had been destroyed and the northern stairs were under observation, but Tin-ming’s reports placed the girl nowhere near the southern stairs. The men on the top floors could escape by that route.

Japanese: 黄姉妹のレーダーがなければ二分の一の賭けを強制させられることになるが、幸い我々は迷うことなく正解を選ぶことが出来る。
English: Without the Wong sisters’ radar, we would have been forced into a fifty-fifty gamble. Fortunately, we could select the correct path without hesitation.

Japanese: 「ＹＳの本拠地に乗り込んだ者を、手ぶらで帰しては世間の笑いものです」
English: “If we let someone who attacked YS headquarters walk away scot-free, the world will laugh at us.”

Japanese: ジェフリーはきっぱりと断言する。
English: Jeffrey was adamant.

Japanese: 「私個人が笑いものになるのとはわけが違う」
English: “That is altogether different from the world laughing at me personally.”

Japanese: 珍しく自嘲の冗談を言うあたり、余裕があるのか、逆に緊張しすぎているのか。
English: It was rare for him to make a joke at his own expense. Perhaps he was calm; perhaps he was too tense.

Japanese: 「僕は自分個人が笑いものになる方がいやだけど」
English: “Personally, I dislike being laughed at far more.”

Japanese: ともあれ、ジェフリーは僕の作戦を実行するつもりでいるようだった。
English: In any event, Jeffrey appeared intent upon carrying out my plan.

Japanese: ――僕が考えついたのは、作戦というような立派なものでもない、ごく簡単でシンプルなやり方だった。
English: What I had devised hardly deserved to be called a plan. It was an exceedingly simple method.

Japanese: 相手はものすごい能力を持っていて、もしかしたら未知の能力もあるのかもしれないけれども、相手を感知することにおいては普通の人間とかわらない。それは、田尻を殺す映像で相手を捕捉するために手間をかけていることからもはっきりしている。
English: The adversary possessed a tremendous ability and might possess other abilities still unknown to us. Yet her means of detecting others was no different from that of an ordinary person. The trouble she had taken to locate Tajiri before killing him made that much clear.

Japanese: そして目的は、あくまでも廖のメールを信用するならばだが、龍頭の命である。メールが出鱈目だとしても、最上層を目指しているようだからＹＳの幹部に用があるに違いない。とすれば、執務室に行くのはまず間違いないだろう。
English: And if Liao’s email was to be believed, her purpose was the Longtou’s life. Even if the email was nonsense, she was plainly climbing toward the uppermost floors and therefore must have business with the officers of YS. She would almost certainly visit the office.

Japanese: だから執務室に隠れて彼女を待ち伏せする。
English: They would hide inside the office and ambush her.

Japanese: 執務室の内部には監視カメラはないが、みなから集めた携帯端末を部屋の各所に置いて監視カメラ代わりにする。物陰に隠れるものはその携帯端末のカメラに映った映像を自分の端末で受信すれば、一切自分の姿をさらすことなく部屋の状況を知ることが出来る。
English: There was no surveillance camera in the office, but mobile devices collected from the others could be placed throughout the room to serve in their stead. Each person concealed behind cover could receive the images from those cameras on his own device, learning everything in the room without exposing himself at all.

Japanese: 部屋に入ってきたら、まず一人が少女を射撃する。これでうまく仕留めれば被害者ゼロだが、そうはいかないかも知れない。そのための対策が、今回の作戦の肝要な部分だ。
English: When the girl entered, the first man would shoot her. Ideally, that would kill her with no casualties on our side. It might not. The preparation for that possibility was the crucial part of the plan.

Japanese: 少女の攻撃方法というのは、非常に強力だが、最大の弱点がある。
English: Her method of attack was tremendously powerful, but it had one great weakness.

Japanese: それは、攻撃した後の彼女自身の居場所を予測するのが容易だという点だ。
English: Her position after an attack was easy to predict.

Japanese: 彼女の攻撃は瞬間移動で対象のいる場所に移動するということでしか成立しない。つまり、もし最初の射撃が失敗し、少女がその第一の射撃者を攻撃するとなれば、彼がいた場所に少女がいるということだ。
English: She could attack only by teleporting into the space occupied by her target. In other words, if the first shot missed and she attacked the first shooter, the girl would then occupy the position where he had stood.

Japanese: 移動先がわかっているのだから、あらかじめ照準を合わせておくことが出来る。
English: Because her destination was known, another shooter could aim there in advance.

Japanese: 第二の射撃者は、第一の射撃者が攻撃を行うのと同時に、物陰から彼に狙いを付けておく。そうしておけば、もし第一の射撃シャガ失敗して敵の攻撃を受けてしまっても、あらためて照準をあわせる必要はなく、ただ微調整をして引き金を引くだけで弾が敵に向かって飛んでゆく。これを回避するのは難しい。
English: The second shooter would take aim at the first from cover at the instant the first man attacked. Then, even if the first shot missed and the enemy struck him, the second shooter would not need to acquire a new target. He would make a minute correction and pull the trigger, sending the bullet into her. It would be difficult to evade.

Japanese: これを、第二、第三、第四と繰り返してゆく。まあ、相手はどこかのタイミングで逃げるだろうが、こちらに撃退する能力があるのを見せるだけでも意味がある。
English: The process would repeat with a second man, then a third and fourth. The adversary would probably flee at some point, but even demonstrating that we could repel her would be worthwhile.

Japanese: 重要なのは相手に見破られずに射撃者を配置することと、指示通りのタイミングでアクションを起こすことの二点だ。これさえクリア出来れば、相手が無傷で部屋を出て行くのは非常に難しいだろう。
English: Two points were essential: placing the shooters without permitting the adversary to discover them, and ensuring that each man acted at exactly the instructed moment. If those conditions were met, she would find it exceedingly difficult to leave the room unharmed.

Japanese: 人が死ぬことを前提としているので、出来れば最初の射撃者が相手を仕留め、僕の小細工が登場することもなくけりがついて欲しいものだ。
English: The plan assumed that people would die. I hoped, if possible, that the first shooter would kill her and settle the affair before my stratagem ever had to come into play.

Japanese: この考えを披露したときは、さすがにジェフリーの顔色が変わった。
English: When I revealed the idea, even Jeffrey’s complexion changed.

Japanese: 「仲間を囮にするようなかたちになるわけですな」
English: “Then our comrades would, in effect, serve as decoys.”

Japanese: 「最悪そうなるね」
English: “At worst, yes.”

Japanese: 「なるほど……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: ジェフリーは腕組みをして考え始める。
English: Jeffrey folded his arms and began to think.

Japanese: 「考えてみたのだけどね、相手が不規則に移動する以上、拳銃やサブマシンガンで倒すのは非常に難しい。爆弾や毒ガスでもあればまた違うんだがね。だから繰り返すけど、今の状況なら相手をせずに逃げるのが一番なんだよ」
English: “I have considered the matter. As long as she moves unpredictably, killing her with pistols or submachine guns will be exceedingly difficult. A bomb or poison gas would change matters. So I repeat: under present conditions, the best course is escape without engagement.”

Japanese: 「それは出来ません」
English: “We cannot do that.”

Japanese: 「なら、勇気と胆力を発揮してもらわなきゃならない。目の前で盟友が断裂するのを見ながら冷静に行動するんだ。僕はこのメンバーがどういう資質の持ち主なのかしらないから、そのあたりはジェフリーが判断してくれ」
English: “Then the men must demonstrate courage and strength of nerve. They must act calmly while they watch their comrades being torn apart before them. I don’t know the dispositions of the men with you, so I will leave that judgment to you.”

Japanese: 僕の言葉からやや間を開けて、ジェフリーは答えた。
English: Jeffrey waited a moment after my words before answering.

Japanese: 「いや、やりましょう。我々にならば可能です」
English: “No. We will do it. We can.”

Japanese: こわばってはいるが、彼は確かに微笑みを浮かべていた。
English: His face was rigid, but he was unmistakably smiling.

Japanese: 「義勝らしい勇敢な作戦ですよ。面白い」
English: “It is a brave plan, worthy of Yisheng. I find it interesting.”

Japanese: 「そういう考え方は好きじゃないな。正常じゃない」
English: “I dislike that mode of thought. It is not sane.”

Japanese: 僕が思わずそう言ってしまうと、
English: The words escaped me involuntarily.

Japanese: 「我々のいる世界が正常だと、いつから思い違いをしているんですか？　これは先が思いやられる。我々には命よりも大事なものがあるのです」
English: “When did you fall into the error of believing our world was sane? This bodes poorly for your future. There are things we value more highly than life.”

Japanese: さて、そのジェフリーは現在すでに配置を終えている。特に射撃に慣れ、勇気に秀でたものを五人選び、射撃者として現場に配置した。みな興奮剤の『ピーク』を通常の倍量飲んで精神をギンギンに研ぎ澄ませている。
English: Jeffrey had now completed his preparations. He selected five men with particular experience of gunfire and exceptional courage, and placed them at the scene as shooters. Each had taken twice the usual dose of the stimulant Peak, leaving his nerves razor-sharp.

Japanese: あとの五人はモニタールームで我々から送られてくる天明の情報を受けつつ、監視カメラの映像をチェックしており、いよいよとなったら彼らも物陰に隠れる。ジェフリーもモニタールームにいて、その瞬間には物陰に隠れて現場のものたちに指示を出す。
English: The other five remained in the monitor room, receiving Tin-ming’s information from us while they watched the camera feeds. When the time came, they too would conceal themselves. Jeffrey was also in the monitor room. At that point, he would take cover and issue instructions to the men on the scene.

Japanese: 「むっつりと黙り込んじゃって、やっぱり心配？」
English: “You’ve gone so grim and silent. Are you worried after all?”

Japanese: 階段を降りていると、世傑が怪訝な顔をする。
English: Sai-kit looked at me quizzically as we descended the stairs.

Japanese: 「こんな時にぺちゃくちゃと喋るものじゃない」
English: “This is hardly the moment for idle chatter.”

Japanese: 「でも、何か考え込んでいたでしょう？」
English: “But you were lost in thought, weren’t you?”

Japanese: 「まあね。でも、心配というのとはちょっと違うよ。こんな大人数でぞろぞろ薄暗い階段を降りていると、可笑しくなっちゃってね。ジェフリーは女の子一人を殺すために執務室で待ち構えている。女の子の方も、お菓子でも食べてりゃいいのに、何が楽しいのかわざわざギャングのビルに人殺しにやって来た。生命なんてものは、放っておくだけでも勝手に寿命で滅んでしまうような儚いものなのに、みんなくだらないことできりきり舞いして、しかも真剣だって言うんだから、何かのギャグみたいでさ……」
English: “Yes, but I would not quite call it worry. Watching this whole crowd trudge down a dim stairwell together struck me as funny. Jeffrey is lying in wait in the office to kill one girl. She could be eating sweets somewhere, but instead she came all the way to a gang’s headquarters to kill people—whatever she finds so enjoyable about that. Life is fragile enough to expire of old age all on its own if you leave it alone, yet everyone is running themselves ragged over this nonsense, all of them deadly serious. It feels like some kind of joke...”

Japanese: 「何急に達観したようなこと言ってるのよ。そんなんじゃ困るわ」
English: “Why have you suddenly started talking like an enlightened sage? That attitude will not do at all.”

Japanese: 「全くその通りだ。でも、ときどき、無性に笑っちゃいたくなるんだよ」
English: “Entirely true. But at times I feel an overwhelming desire to laugh.”

Japanese: 僕の言葉に、世傑は苦い顔をして黙り込む。
English: Sai-kit fell silent with a bitter expression.

Japanese: 「大丈夫。僕は人格的には問題があるかもしれないが、心は今も冷静だよ。動揺もなにもしていない」
English: “Don’t worry. My character may have its defects, but my mind remains perfectly calm. I am not shaken in the least.”

Japanese: 「そうだとありがたいわね」
English: “I hope so.”

Japanese: 世傑は溜息をつく。
English: Sai-kit sighed.

Japanese: 僕たちは階段を降り続ける。女子供の体力をいたわりながらの移動はまったくもって遅い。一方、侵入者はうろうろと無駄な動きをしながらの移動だが、早かった。
English: We continued down the stairs. Accommodating the stamina of the women and children made our progress maddeningly slow. The intruder wandered wastefully, but moved fast.

Japanese: 僕らがやっと七階まで降りてきたところで、侵入者はジェフリー達のすぐ下の階に辿り着く。
English: We had only just reached the seventh floor when she arrived directly below Jeffrey’s position.

Japanese: ここからあと一階瞬間移動すれば執務室に現れることも可能だ。ジェフリー達はもう身を隠していて、僕らが相手の位置を伝えると、小さく抑えたかすれ声で返事が返ってきた。
English: One more upward teleportation could bring her into the office. Jeffrey’s party was already concealed. When we reported the adversary’s position, a faint, hoarse whisper came back.

Japanese: いよいよその瞬間が近づいて来ている。
English: The moment had finally drawn near.

Japanese: 僕は手元の端末の画面に集中した。
English: I focused on the screen of the device in my hand.

Japanese: ジェフリーが部屋に仕掛けた端末の数は六つ。それらの映像は僕の端末にも送られており、様々な角度からとらえた執務室の映像が画面に分割表示されている。
English: Jeffrey had placed six devices throughout the room. Their feeds were transmitted to mine as well, and its split screen showed the office from several angles.

Japanese: 画面上には誰も映っていない。部屋には普段は置かれていない家具やらが持ち込まれており、そのどこかに五人の刺客が潜んでいるはずだが、僕の目からも、どこにいるのかはわからなかった。
English: Not one person was visible. Furniture not ordinarily present had been brought into the room, and five shooters should have been concealed somewhere among it, but even my eyes could not locate them.

Japanese: 少なくとも、隠れるという点においては完璧だ。その上で、ちゃんと作戦が機能するように配置されているかどうかというのが気になったが、そればかりは実際に相手が部屋にやって来るまで知りようがなかった。そして何よりも、射撃者達が作戦通りに実行できるかどうか。配置さえ正しければ、後はあらかじめ決まった場所に狙いを定め、少女がその先に現れた瞬間に引き金を引くだけの簡単な作業となるが、緊迫した場面で、タイプAの異常な力で味方の身体が断裂するのを目の当たりにしながら混乱なく実行できるものなのか。
English: In terms of concealment, at least, the preparations were perfect. Whether they had been placed correctly for the plan to function was another matter, but one we could not know until the adversary entered. Most important of all was whether the shooters could execute the plan as instructed. Provided their positions were correct, the remaining work was simple: aim at a predetermined point, then pull the trigger the instant the girl appeared there. But could they do so without confusion amid such tension, while watching the unnatural power of a Type A tear their comrades apart before their eyes?

Japanese: 経験豊かで勇気のある者を残したが、僕にとっては未知数だ。
English: We had left behind men of experience and courage, but I had no way to know how they would perform.

Japanese: その瞬間は唐突に訪れた。
English: The moment arrived without warning.

Japanese: それまで誰もいなかった執務室の窓際、床から一メートルくらいの高さの場所に、ふっと少女が現れたかと思うと、すぐに消え、同時に右手の壁側に現れる。そしてそのまま絨毯の上に着地した。
English: Near the window of the previously empty office, approximately one meter above the floor, the girl appeared and vanished in an instant. At the same time she materialized beside the wall on the right, then landed upon the carpet.

Japanese: 映像でも見せた、細かい移動を挟みながら状況を把握する彼女のやり方だ。
English: It was the same method shown in the recording: making short jumps while she assessed the situation.

Japanese: 部屋に降り立った彼女は、左右をきょろきょろと確認する。部屋に誰もいないことをどう思っているのか。フードで顔の上半分が隠れているため、うかがい知ることが出来ない。
English: Once upon the floor, she looked rapidly to the left and right. I could not know what she made of the empty room. The hood concealed the upper half of her face.

Japanese: 彼女は周囲を警戒しながら、部屋の奥中央に置かれた龍頭の椅子に近づく。そこの椅子のヘッドレスト部分には意味ありげに帽子が被せられている。
English: Watching her surroundings, she approached the Longtou’s chair in the center of the room’s far end. A hat had been placed conspicuously upon its headrest.

Japanese: 「そろそろね」
English: “Any moment now.”

Japanese: 隣から画面をのぞき込んでいた世傑が言い、僕は頷く。
English: said Sai-kit, peering at the screen beside me. I nodded.

Japanese: 二歩、三歩、少女が歩いたが襲撃者はあらわれない。ジェフリーがどのタイミングで指示を出すのか、僕は聞いていない。あるいは最初の射撃者に、そのタイミングはゆだねられているのかも知れない。
English: The girl took two steps, then three, but no shot came. I had not asked at what moment Jeffrey intended to give the order. Perhaps the first shooter had been entrusted with the timing himself.

Japanese: 少女は無人の部屋のなかをきょろきょろと見回す。さすがに警戒はしているようだ。
English: The girl surveyed the empty room. At least she appeared to be on her guard.

Japanese: そして少女は椅子の上に置かれた帽子に視線をやる。いかにも意味ありげに置かれたその帽子に、やはりひときわ強い警戒心を抱いているらしい。テーブルの端に置いてあったグラスを手に取り、それに投げつける。
English: Then her eyes fell upon the hat on the chair. The conspicuously placed hat seemed to make her particularly wary. She picked up a glass from the edge of the table and hurled it at the hat.

Japanese: 命中し、帽子が落ちる。
English: It struck, and the hat fell.

Japanese: それだけだ。
English: Nothing else occurred.

Japanese: もうすぐ彼女は瞬間移動を使って部屋から逃げてしまうだろうが、まだ最初の射撃者は攻撃をしない。彼女が狙撃しやすい場所にいないのか、それとも、怖じ気づいたのかもしれない。それならそれでかまわない。自信がないのに無理に攻撃をするよりも、ここはやりすごして次のチャンスを狙うという手もある。
English: She would probably teleport out of the room very soon, yet the first shooter did not attack. Perhaps she was not standing where he could shoot her easily. Perhaps he had lost his nerve. That too was acceptable. If he lacked confidence, letting this chance pass and waiting for another opportunity would be better than forcing an attack.

Japanese: ここで彼らが攻撃をしないのなら、少女はまたビルを降りてくるだろう。ならば、僕たちはもう少し階段を降りる速度を上げなくてはいけない……。
English: If the men did not attack here, the girl would descend through the building again. In that case, we would need to increase our own pace down the stairs...

Japanese: 僕がその方向でこれからの方針を考え始めた時だった。
English: I had just begun planning on that basis when it happened.

Japanese: 端末から、連続的な銃声が鳴り響く。
English: A succession of gunshots thundered from my device.

Japanese: 画面に射撃者の姿は現れない。隠れたままサブマシンガンで発砲したらしい。これが命中したのか、どうか。
English: The shooter did not appear in any image. He had evidently fired the submachine gun without emerging from concealment. Had he hit her?

Japanese: 端末を分割した小さな画面でも、ぱっと肩の辺りで血がはじけたのが見える。
English: Even on one of the small split-screen panes, I saw blood burst near her shoulder.

Japanese: フルオートのサブマシンガンは引き金を引いているかぎり弾薬が空になるまで連続して銃弾を撃ち出すことが出来るが、射撃精度を維持するためには三、四発程度をひとつのセットとして引き金をそのたびに戻しながら射撃するのが望ましい。今回の射撃者もそれを心得ていて、最初の三発を発射したあと一旦区切ってから、次の射撃を開始する。しかし、二回目の銃声が鳴るのとほとんど同時に少女の姿は消えている。
English: A fully automatic submachine gun continued firing until its ammunition was exhausted for as long as the trigger remained depressed. To preserve accuracy, however, one should fire bursts of three or four rounds, releasing the trigger between them. This shooter understood the principle. After discharging the first three rounds, he paused before beginning a second burst. Yet the girl vanished almost exactly as those second shots sounded.

Japanese: 六つの画面のあちこちに、チラチラと少女の姿が映る。移動を繰り返しながら、相手の位置を探っているのだ。
English: Her figure flickered across the six screens. She was repeating short movements as she searched for her adversary’s position.

Japanese: 奇襲を受け、負傷しているにもかかわらず、部屋から逃げずに相手を見つけて攻撃しようとしている辺り、好戦的な相手だ。
English: She had been surprised and wounded, yet sought to locate and attack the shooter instead of fleeing the room. She was evidently an aggressive opponent.

Japanese: 射撃者は、その状態でもまだ冷静さを維持しているのはさすがだった。パニックになると引き金を引きっぱなしにしてあっという間に弾倉を空にしてしまうものだろうが、一瞬でも少女が見えたところに向かって、銃を構え、短く引き金を引く。
English: The shooter displayed admirable composure even then. Panic would presumably have made a man hold the trigger down and empty the magazine in an instant. Whenever he caught the briefest sight of the girl, he raised the gun and fired a short burst.

Japanese: しかし、空中を移動しながら飛び回る相手を狙撃するのは不可能だった。
English: But it was impossible to hit a target leaping through the air by teleportation.

Japanese: この射撃で、少女はどこから撃たれているか、その場所を把握した。相手のいる場所に少女はジャンプする。
English: Those shots told the girl where the shooter was. She jumped into the space he occupied.

Japanese: 少女がそれまでいた空中に、棚の一部と男の上半身があらわれる。そして、画面手前の棚がガラガラと崩れた。最初の射撃者はそこにいたのだろう。そして、射撃者の上半身が床に落下するよりも早く、第二の射撃者による銃声。
English: Part of a cabinet and the upper half of a man appeared in the air where she had been. The cabinet in the foreground collapsed with a clatter. That must have been the first shooter’s hiding place. Before his upper body could strike the floor, the second shooter opened fire.

Japanese: ほぼベストのタイミングで放たれた銃弾は少女足の辺りに命中したようだったが、致命傷には至らない。今度は少女も相手の発砲が見えたらしく、一度空中への瞬間移動を挟んだだけで、すぐに第二の射撃者の頭部を空に浮かせることになる。
English: The bullet was fired at nearly the best possible instant and appeared to strike the girl’s leg, but it was not fatal. This time she appeared to see the gun’s muzzle flash. After only one intervening teleportation into the air, she sent the second shooter’s head floating upward.

Japanese: しかし、二発の銃弾を身体に受けたのは相当の痛手だったらしく、第二の射撃者の首なし遺体の側で、小さく蹲る。
English: The two bullets in her body had evidently done considerable harm. Beside the second shooter’s headless body, she curled into a tight crouch.

Japanese: 蹲ってしまったことで、第三の射撃者の射線から外れてしまったのかもしれない。或いは、死角を保ちながら撃つのに良い場所が見つからなかったために、最初からそういう手はずで考えていたのか。とにかく、三人目は自らカーテンの裏から飛び出して、少女を射撃したのだ。
English: Perhaps crouching carried her out of the third shooter’s line of fire. Or perhaps he had been unable to find a position from which he could fire while remaining behind cover, and this had been the plan from the beginning. Whatever the reason, the third man leaped from behind a curtain and fired at the girl himself.

Japanese: これが最初から予定の行動で、そのとおり実行してるのだとしたら、なかなか勇気のある行動だ。いや、正直言ってここまでの次点で相当僕の想像を上回る勇敢さを見せている。
English: If that had been prescribed from the beginning and he was executing the plan exactly, it was an impressively courageous act. Indeed, by this point, they had already shown bravery far beyond anything I had imagined.

Japanese: 「あっ」
English: “Ah.”

Japanese: と僕が思わず声をあげたのは、同時にもう一人、ソファーの裏から飛び出してしまったのだ。
English: The cry escaped me because another man leaped from behind the sofa at the same time.

Japanese: 「だめだ、いけない」
English: “No. Don’t.”

Japanese: 思わず言葉が漏れる。
English: The words left my mouth involuntarily.

Japanese: 二人同時に攻撃すればなんとかなるという相手でもない。それより、一人ずつでも物陰から一方的に射撃をしていった方が確実だ。こんなふうに飛び出してはいけない。仲間が一人ずつやられてゆくのに焦りを感じたのかもしれない。引き金をひきっぱなしで、銃弾をばらまきながら最後の一人は現れた。
English: Two people attacking at once would not overwhelm an adversary of this kind. It was more reliable to have each man fire upon her unseen, one after another. They should not have rushed out like this. Perhaps watching their companions fall one by one had made them impatient. The final man appeared while holding down his trigger and spraying bullets.

Japanese: そう思ったその直後に、僕が危惧していた光景が画面の上に展開される。
English: The sight I had feared unfolded upon the screen in the very next instant.

Japanese: 姿を現した二人は、ほとんど同時に少女の移動によって切断される。
English: The girl’s movement severed both exposed men almost simultaneously.

Japanese: そして少女の姿も消え、画面のなかに残ったのは盛大にぶちまけられた四人分の死体であった。銃弾や少女の移動攻撃によって破損した家具と、人の手足や内臓が混じり合うように床の上にばらまかれている。見ているだけで生臭い血のにおいがしそうだ。
English: Then she too vanished. All that remained in the image were the remains of four bodies strewn everywhere. Furniture broken by bullets and the girl’s moving attacks lay across the floor among limbs and viscera, all mixed together. The image alone seemed to carry the raw smell of blood.

Japanese: 「どこへ行った？」
English: “Where did she go?”

Japanese: 僕は天明に訊く。
English: I asked Tin-ming.

Japanese: 「に、西へ１０メートル程度移動し、そこでじっとしています！」
English: “S-she moved approximately ten meters west and has remained entirely still!”

Japanese: 彼は悲痛な顔でそう言った。
English: She delivered the report with anguish on her face.

Japanese: 「休憩室ね」
English: “The private lounge.”

Japanese: 世傑が言うとおり、おそらく相手がいるのは龍頭のためのベッドなどが置かれた部屋だろう。
English: As Sai-kit said, the adversary was probably in the room containing a bed for the Longtou.

Japanese: 「ジェフリー。申し訳ないが僕の作戦は失敗だ。きみたちはそこに隠れたまま待機。我々はこのままビルを離脱する。相手も多分逃げるだろう。今回は痛み分けというところで手を打とう。そして、死んだ部下達の家族には充分な保証金を出すんだ」
English: “Jeffrey. I am sorry, but my plan has failed. Remain hidden where you are and wait. We will continue out of the building. The adversary will probably flee as well. We will accept a draw on this occasion. And the families of the men who died are to receive ample compensation.”

Japanese: こちらの会話が聞こえているはずのジェフリーに、そう呼びかける。
English: I called to Jeffrey, who should have been able to hear us.

Japanese: 『いえ、我々はこれから攻撃に向かいます。このグランドタワーを襲撃した者を、生きて帰す訳にはいきません』
English: ‘No. We are about to attack. We cannot let anyone who attacks Grand Tower leave alive.’

Japanese: 「無理をするな。きみたちはよくやった。ジェフリーが言うとおり、みな勇敢だった。胸を張って帰って来てくれ」
English: “Don’t overreach. You have done well. As you said, every one of the men was brave. Come back with your heads high.”

Japanese: 『そうは行きません』
English: ‘We cannot.’

Japanese: 「駄目だ！　帰ってくるんだ！」
English: “No! Come back!”

Japanese: 僕は怒鳴った。
English: I shouted.

Japanese: そう答えるだろうことはなんとなく予期していた。
English: Some part of me had anticipated his answer.

Japanese: そして、その彼を説得するには、ごちゃごちゃ理屈を言うよりも、感情を見せることが必要に思えた。それでも意見を翻してくれる見込みは薄いが。
English: And I thought that if I meant to persuade him, I must show emotion rather than argue him in circles. The prospect that even this would change his mind was slight.

Japanese: 「ここで深追いするのは愚かな考えだ。何も生まない」
English: “Pursuing her any farther is foolish. It will accomplish nothing.”

Japanese: 『相手は負傷しています。そして居場所もわかっている。この状態で怯えて隠れていろと？』
English: ‘The adversary is wounded. We know her position. And you would have us cower in hiding under those conditions?’

Japanese: 「そうだ。くだらないメンツなんか、犬にでも食わせておけばいい」
English: “Yes. Throw your worthless pride to the dogs.”

Japanese: 『あなたはこの世界のことを全くわかっていない。……休憩室ですね？　相手が移動したら、また連絡をしてください』
English: ‘You understand nothing of this world. ...The private lounge, you said? Inform us if the adversary moves again.’

Japanese: それから先は、僕が何を呼びかけてもジェフリーは返事をしなかった。
English: From that point onward, Jeffrey gave no answer, no matter what I said.

Japanese: 「ち、父たちも、移動をはじめました」
English: “M-my father and the others have begun to move.”

Japanese: 天明が狼狽を押し殺しながらそう報告する。
English: Tin-ming suppressed her panic as she delivered the report.

Japanese: 「そうか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 僕は言って、端末をポケットにいれた。
English: I put the device into my pocket.

Japanese: ジェフリーは自分の部下を死に追いやった以上、たとえ自殺行為でも、自分が責任をとらなければならないと考えたのだろうか？　それとも、本当に勝算があるのか。僕にはちょっとわからない。
English: Having sent his subordinates to their deaths, did Jeffrey believe that he was obliged to accept responsibility himself, even if doing so was suicidal? Or did he truly believe he could win? I could not tell.

Japanese: 「我々は移動速度を上げる。みな、足元に気をつけながら急いでくれ」
English: “We are increasing our pace. Hurry, everyone, but watch your footing.”

Japanese: 僕たちはガタガタと跫音を立てながら階段を降り進める。
English: Our footsteps clattered as we continued down the stairs.

Japanese: 天明は逐一、最上階での生命の位置や数の変化を報告し、そして僕らが三階に辿り着いた辺りで、最上階に置いてきたすべての仲間が死に絶え、少女だけが残ったことをうわずった声で耳打ちした。
English: Tin-ming reported every change in the position and number of lives upon the top floor. When we reached approximately the third floor, she whispered in a high, strained voice that every comrade we had left above was dead and only the girl remained.

Japanese: 「ご苦労」
English: “Good work.”

Japanese: 僕が天明をねぎらうと、
English: When I thanked Tin-ming, the Longtou spoke.

Japanese: 「小謝」
English: “Siu Tse.”

Japanese: 龍頭が不安げに僕を見る。
English: He looked at me anxiously.

Japanese: 僕は彼に頷きを返す。
English: I answered him with a nod.

Japanese: 「そうか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 察して、下唇を噛んだ。
English: Understanding, he bit his lower lip.

Japanese: 「一体、何があったんですか？」
English: “What in the world happened?”

Japanese: 声をかけたのはレイレイだった。その向こうにはジェフリーの妻がいて、こちらをじっと見ている。
English: The question came from Leilei. Beyond her stood Jeffrey’s wife, watching us without looking away.

Japanese: 「あとで説明する。今は先を急ぐんだ」
English: “We will explain later. For now, keep moving.”

Japanese: 口ごもる龍頭のかわりに僕がこたえた。ジェフリーの妻は何も言わない。彼女にも他の家族同様何も説明をしていないが、僕らの態度ですべてを察したのだろう。
English: I answered in place of the Longtou, who could not find his words. We had explained nothing to Jeffrey’s wife, just as we had told the other families nothing, but our manner must have allowed her to understand what had happened.

Japanese: 目が合うと、顔をこわばらせる。
English: When our eyes met, her face stiffened.

Japanese: 「龍頭」
English: “Longtou.”

Japanese: 僕は脚を止めて俯く彼に声をかけると、顔を上げる。
English: I addressed the Longtou, who had stopped and bowed his head. He looked up.

Japanese: 「あなたはみんなを連れて、ビルの外まで逃がしてください。僕らは少し引き返して十五階で迎え撃ちます」
English: “Take everyone outside the building. We will go back a short distance and meet the adversary on the fifteenth floor.”

Japanese: 「しかし、今ジェフリーはそのやり方で……」
English: “But Jeffrey just used the same method, and...”

Japanese: 「彼は無理に追い回したから失敗しました。僕は待ち伏せして、可能なら攻撃をします。危険なら何もしません」
English: “He failed because he chased after her recklessly. I will set an ambush and attack if the opportunity arises. If it becomes dangerous, I will do nothing.”

Japanese: 「小謝。さっきも言ったように、お前を危険にさらすわけには……」
English: “Siu Tse. As I said before, we cannot expose you to danger...”

Japanese: 「今はそんな状況ではありません。ジェフリーが言ったように、相手が消耗している以上、今がチャンスなのは確かです」
English: “Circumstances have changed. As Jeffrey said, the adversary has been worn down. This is unquestionably our opportunity.”

Japanese: 僕の言葉に、龍頭はうんと頷こうとしない。ただ苦い顔で僕を見つめている。
English: The Longtou would not agree. He merely stared at me with a bitter expression.

Japanese: 「……ジェフリーがいなくなった以上、僕が唯一の補佐役のはずです。僕の意見に従ってください。レイレイ、龍頭を頼むよ」
English: “...Now that Jeffrey is gone, I should be your sole adviser. Follow my counsel. Leilei, take care of the Longtou.”

Japanese: 渋る龍頭に家族と共に下に行かせ、僕は世傑と黄姉妹、そして三人の部下を借りて降りて来た階段を上り始めた。
English: I made the reluctant Longtou continue downstairs with the families. Then I took Sai-kit, the Wong sisters, and three subordinates with me and began climbing the stairs we had just descended.

Japanese: 「大丈夫？　むきになってない？」
English: “Are you all right? You aren’t letting this become personal?”

Japanese: 隣を行く世傑が、不安げに訊ねる。
English: Sai-kit walked beside me and asked anxiously.

Japanese: 「僕は至って冷静だよ。自分でも恐ろしいほどだ」
English: “I am entirely calm. Frighteningly so, even to myself.”

Japanese: 僕は自分の銃に弾丸が装填されているのを確認しながらこたえる。
English: I answered while checking that my gun was loaded.

Japanese: 「あの当たり方からすると、手当てをしない限り相手は出血で消耗し続けるはずだ。ジェフリー達のやり方は無謀だったが、それを処理するのに相手も大分能力を使った。相手はどこかに逃げて治療を受けることを優先するだろう。そこを不意打ちする。相手は思考能力や注意力も落ちているだろうしね。……観察して、想定よりも消耗がないようなら接触を避けて撤退する」
English: “Judging by where the bullets struck, she should continue losing blood and weakening unless she receives treatment. Jeffrey’s method was reckless, but dealing with it also forced her to use her ability a great deal. She will probably make escaping somewhere to obtain treatment her priority. We will take her by surprise then. Her judgment and attention should be impaired as well. ...We will observe her. If she appears less exhausted than expected, we will withdraw without contact.”

Japanese: 「それならいいけど。でも……」
English: “If that is truly what you mean. But...”

Japanese: 世傑が言いかけたのを、天明が遮る。
English: Tin-ming interrupted Sai-kit before he could continue.

Japanese: 「小謝、相手が移動を開始しました！」
English: “Siu Tse, the adversary has begun moving!”

Japanese: 冷静でないのはむしろこの黄姉妹だろう。父が死んだショックで二人とも、その顔を青ざめさせてはいるが、復讐の念は強いのか、さっきとは違う感情のこもった声でそう伝える。
English: If anyone had lost composure, it was more likely the Wong sisters. The shock of their father’s death had left both faces pallid. Perhaps their desire for revenge was powerful, for Tin-ming’s report now carried an emotion absent from her earlier voice.

Japanese: 「北側の方へゆっくり移動して……あっ……」
English: “She is moving slowly toward the north... Ah...”

Japanese: 「どうした？」
English: “What happened?”

Japanese: 「……見失いました」
English: “...We lost her.”
“What?”

Japanese: 「ビルの外に瞬間移動したんです！　それで、そのまま連続して瞬間移動し、あれよあれよと地上まで辿り着いて、そのまま人混みのなかへ……そこで見失いました。すみません……」
English: “She teleported outside the building! Then she continued teleporting in rapid succession, reached the ground before we knew it, and entered the crowd... We lost her there. I’m sorry...”

Japanese: 天明はくやしげに下唇を噛む。彼女の肩は震えている。もし彼女に普通の人間のように目があったら、涙をこぼしていたかもしれない。
English: Tin-ming bit her lower lip in frustration. Her shoulders trembled. Had she possessed eyes like an ordinary person, she might have been shedding tears.

Japanese: 「謝る必要はないよ。それは仕方がないことだ」
English: “There is no need to apologize. It couldn’t be helped.”

Japanese: 僕は溜息をつき、階段を上る足を止める。一同もそれに習う。
English: I sighed and stopped climbing. Everyone else followed my example.

Japanese: そうだ。相手は瞬間移動を連続して使うことが出来るのだ。わざわざビルの中を伝って降りる必要などない。
English: Of course. The adversary could teleport repeatedly. She had no reason to make her way down through the building.

Japanese: なぜ襲うときは、同じように空中を連続移動して直接最上階を狙わなかったのか？　どうしてわざわざ正面から攻撃して、ビル全体を制圧しようとしたのか？
English: Then why, when she attacked, had she not made the same succession of movements through the air and gone directly to the highest floor? Why had she attacked from the front and taken the trouble to try to take control of the entire building?

Japanese: 考えようとしたが、急に気の抜けたような感じになってしまって、うまく考えられない。
English: I tried to think, but suddenly felt drained and could not make my thoughts work.

Japanese: ……とにかく、僕は、相手を逃がしてしまったのだ。部下達を好き放題殺し、ジェフリーを殺した相手を。
English: ...In any event, I had allowed her to escape. The person who had killed my subordinates at will, and killed Jeffrey.

Japanese: 僕は階段の段の上に腰をおろす。
English: I sat down on one of the steps.

Japanese: 「大丈夫？」
English: “Are you all right?”

Japanese: 世傑がそう声をかける。
English: Sai-kit asked.

Japanese: 「ねえ世傑。僕は悪ガキどものリーダーをしていたが、一度も奇襲をうけて負けたことがない。それは恥だと思っている。奇襲をまともに受けてしまうことも、不利な状況のまま戦ってしまう判断力も情けない。ジェフリーが語った価値観はやっぱり理解出来ないし、この死に方は恥じるべきものだと感じるよ」
English: “Listen, Sai-kit. I led a band of delinquents, but I never once let an ambush defeat me. I find this shameful. Being caught squarely by a surprise attack is pathetic, and so is choosing to fight while the odds are against you. I still cannot understand the values Jeffrey described. I believe there is shame in dying this way.”
“Siu Tse...”

Japanese: 「今後僕が龍頭になるとしたら、こんな奇襲は絶対に受けない」
English: “If I become the Longtou in the future, I will never permit an ambush like this to reach us.”

Japanese: 僕は溜息をつき、
English: I sighed.

Japanese: 「悪いけど、ほんの少しだけ休ませてくれないか？　なんだか、ひどく疲れたんだ」
English: “I’m sorry, but could you let me rest for just a moment? I’m terribly tired.”

Japanese: ビルから退避したすべてのものに、襲撃者が去ったことを伝え、僕は世傑や龍頭と共に戦場となった最上階に戻る。
English: We informed everyone evacuated from the building that the attacker was gone. Then the Longtou, Sai-kit, and I returned to the top floor that had become a battlefield.

Japanese: 執務室は映像で見た通りの血の海が広がり、そして隣の休憩室も同様だった。
English: As in the recording, a sea of blood filled the office. The private lounge beside it was the same.

Japanese: 壁には銃弾によって穿たれた穴がいくつかあり、世傑は無言でそれに指先で触れていた。
English: Bullets had punched several holes in the walls. Sai-kit touched them silently with his fingertips.

Japanese: 休憩室に転がる遺体も、瞬間移動によって切断されている。ジェフリーは頭のてっぺんから右脇の下にかけて楕円を描くような形で切断されていた。彼の握る銃の弾丸は二発使われていた。他の遺体が持つ銃も、一、二発は消費されているのを見ると、一方的に返り討ちにされたのではなく、それなりに戦闘の形をとることは出来たようだ。
English: The bodies scattered through the private lounge had also been severed by teleportation. Jeffrey had been cut along an oval running from the crown of his head to beneath his right arm. Two rounds were missing from the gun he still held. The weapons carried by the other bodies had also discharged one or two rounds. It appeared that they had achieved something resembling a battle, rather than being cut down entirely without reply.

Japanese: 父の遺体に直面した黄姉妹は、両手の平で顔を覆った。目などないはずだが、においや雰囲気が生々しく状況を伝えたのだろう。その肩は細かく震えている。
English: Confronted with their father’s body, the Wong sisters covered their faces with both hands. They had no eyes, but the smell and atmosphere must have communicated the scene with terrible immediacy. Their shoulders trembled faintly.

Japanese: やがて龍頭が馬明と共に到着した。
English: In time, the Longtou arrived with Ma Ming.

Japanese: 馬明は顔を真っ赤にして怒ったが、何も言わなかった。普段はうるさいほど饒舌なくせに。
English: Ma Ming’s face reddened with fury, but he said nothing. Ordinarily, he was almost oppressively talkative.

Japanese: そして、黙って僕を見ていた。言いたいことがあるのなら言えばいい。
English: He merely stared at me in silence. If he had something to say, he should say it.

Japanese: 「エレベーターはすぐには直らないそうだ。遺体は人力で下ろし、丁重に埋葬しよう」
English: “I am told the elevators cannot be repaired quickly. We will carry the bodies down by hand and bury them with due respect.”

Japanese: 龍頭は沈鬱な表情でそう言った。
English: The Longtou spoke with a somber expression.

Japanese: 僕は彼に、ジェフリーの役割に自分を就けるよう提案した。すると彼は、ゆっくり首を横に振る。
English: I proposed that he appoint me to Jeffrey’s position. He slowly shook his head.

Japanese: 「小謝には、次の龍頭になって貰いたい」
English: “I want Siu Tse to become the next Longtou.”

Japanese: ここにやって来るまでにその考えを固めていたらしく、有無を言わせぬ態度だ。
English: He appeared to have settled upon the decision before coming here. His manner admitted no objection.

Japanese: 「私にはこの混乱のなかで龍頭を続けてゆく能力がない。ウォン君が死んでしまったいまはなおさらだ」
English: “I lack the ability to continue as Longtou amid this confusion. All the more so now that Wong is dead.”

Japanese: そして龍頭の証しである杯を取り出すと、
English: He produced the cup that symbolized the office of Longtou.

Japanese: 「これを持つのは、小謝が一番相応しい」
English: “Siu Tse is the one most worthy to carry it.”

Japanese: 僕に向かって差し出す。
English: He held it out to me.

Japanese: 「近いうちに、儀式を行おう。私のときのように盛大な宴を用意することが出来ないのが申し訳ないが……」
English: “We will hold the ceremony soon. I am sorry that we cannot prepare a grand banquet like the one for my succession...”

Japanese: 僕は首を振り、その杯を受け取った。
English: I shook my head and accepted the cup.

Japanese: 龍頭マイケル・ツェーの名で通達された劉建志の処刑はYS内に衝撃を与えた。
English: The execution of Ryu Kenshi, announced in the name of Longtou Michael Tse, sent a shock through YS.

Japanese: その直後にグランドタワーで行われた幹部の定例会食には、みなこわばった顔であらわれた。
English: Every attendee arrived at the regular officers’ dinner in Grand Tower with a tense expression.

Japanese: クリスが行っていたのと同様、食事の後に重要な話し合いが行われるのだが、食事は無言で行われ、だれひとり口をきかないという異常事態だった。
English: As Chris had done, they held their important discussions after the meal. That evening, however, the meal passed in an unnatural silence, without a single person speaking.

Japanese: そして続く会合では、まず龍頭が型どおりの報告を行ったあと、ジェフリーの口からあらためて劉建志の処刑について説明が行われた。
English: At the meeting that followed, the Longtou first delivered the customary reports. Jeffrey then gave a fresh explanation of Ryu Kenshi’s execution.

Japanese: 彼がくどくどと話すまでもなく、劉建志の常軌を逸した行動は死に相当する罪であり、YSのルールに従えばその決定自体は誰にも否定出来ない筈だった。
English: There should have been no need for him to belabor the point. Ryu Kenshi’s aberrant conduct constituted a crime punishable by death, and under the rules of YS, no one should have been able to dispute the decision itself.

Japanese: しかし、これを公然と批判したのは廖志明だ。
English: Yet Liao Chi-ming openly condemned it.

Japanese: 「幹部クラスの人間に対する処刑は、幹部の合議で決めるべきだ。劉建志君は若輩者とは言え、自分のファミリーを持つ幹部の一人だ。今回のやり方は執行部の暴走としか言いようがない」
English: “The execution of an officer should be decided through collective deliberation among the officers. Ryu Kenshi may have been young, but he was an officer with a family of his own. There is no other name for this but the executive running out of control.”

Japanese: 彼は憤りをあらわにしてそう言った。
English: He spoke with open indignation.

Japanese: 実際のところ彼が劉建志にそこまで肩入れする理由は見当たらなかったし、その怒りが演技か本当の心から出たものかはその場に居る誰も判別がつかなかった。おそらく本人自身も区別がついていないだろう。彼のように演技的に生きて来た人間は、顔の表情だけでなく、感情そのものまで自分に都合のよいように動かしてしまうものだ。
English: In truth, there was no evident reason for him to feel so strongly about Ryu Kenshi, and no one present could tell whether his anger was a performance or arose from the heart. Liao himself probably could not distinguish between the two. A man who had spent his life performing as he had could bend not only his expression, but emotion itself, to whatever served him best.

Japanese: そして、劉建志のことを話したあとはその部下たちのことにふれ、YSを破門されて路頭に迷うしかなくなった彼らを引き取ると宣言した。
English: After speaking about Ryu Kenshi, he turned to the man’s subordinates and announced that he would take them in now that their expulsion from YS had left them with nowhere to go.

Japanese: 劉建志のファミリーの構成員は、ほとんどがクリスが貸した香港派の人員で、それが元の場所に戻ると劉のチンピラ仲間のようなものしか残らなかったが、ジェフリーはこうした廖の態度自体を問題視した。
English: Most of the members of Ryu Kenshi’s family had been lent to him by Chris from the Hong Kong faction. Once they returned, little remained but Ryu’s old band of street toughs. Jeffrey nevertheless regarded Liao’s conduct itself as a problem.

Japanese: 「今回の処置は龍頭の決定です。あなたの立場を軽んじるわけではありませんが、こうした処罰の権限は龍頭に委任されているはずです」
English: “This was done by order of the Longtou. I do not mean to disregard your position, but authority over such punishments has been delegated to the Longtou.”

Japanese: 「はっ、笑わせる」
English: “Ha! Don’t make me laugh.”

Japanese: 廖志明は聞き入れなかった。
English: Liao Chi-ming refused to listen.

Japanese: 「すべての言葉は龍頭の名で出ているが、実際に指示を下しているのは。ジェフリー・ウォン、きみだろう？　きみは龍頭を傀儡とし、組織を私物化している。相談役といえども、明らかに越権行為じゃないか？　掟がどうこうと口うるさく言うが、きみこそYSの掟を乱すものではないか？」
English: “Every proclamation is issued in the Longtou’s name, but the person actually giving the orders is—you, Jeffrey Wong. Isn’t that right? You have made the Longtou your puppet and appropriated this organization for yourself. Even as chief adviser, you are plainly exceeding your authority. You never stop lecturing us about the code, but aren’t you the one disrupting the code of YS?”

Japanese: 廖とジェフリーのやりとりを、他の面々は静かに黙って聞いている。
English: The others listened to the exchange between Liao and Jeffrey in silence.

Japanese: 彼らのうち誰がどちらにつくつもりなのか、まだ品定めをしている最中なのか、それとも自分が新たな勢力となるつもりなのか、本人以外にはうかがい知る余地はなかった。
English: Whether they meant to side with one man or the other, were still sizing both men up, or intended to emerge as a new force in their own right—no one but the individuals themselves could know.

Japanese: 「それは龍頭への侮辱ですよ」
English: “That is an insult to the Longtou.”

Japanese: 「何が龍頭だ。先代の意志は尊重するが、みろ、この場においてただうろたえているだけではないか。マイケルどのは悪い人間ではないが、盟主たる器ではないのではないか？」
English: “What Longtou? I respect the wishes of our predecessor, but look at him. All he does here is flounder. Lord Michael may not be a bad man, but is he truly fit to lead this alliance?”

Japanese: 「問題発言です。口を謹んでください」
English: “That remark is unacceptable. Watch your tongue.”
