English: According to Hayashi’s recollection, Tse Leung conducted himself with unwavering confidence from beginning to end and faced whatever occurred without flinching.

Japanese: 亮が廖志明に交渉を試みるのは事前に聞かされていたが、林氏が期待していたのは、もちろん交渉が決裂して廖志明が殺されることである。廖の部下に囲まれたこのマンションからどう脱出するかといった課題や、公然と廖を裏切ってしまってこれからどうやって生きるのかといった不安など、考えるべきことは多かった筈だが、林氏はどうしようもない憎しみにかられ、ただひたすら廖志明の死だけを願っていたのだ。
English: Hayashi had been told beforehand that Leung intended to negotiate with Liao Chi-ming. What he expected, of course, was for the negotiations to collapse and Liao to be killed. He had plenty else to think about: how they would escape an apartment building surrounded by Liao’s men, or how he and his lover could live after openly betraying the man. But Hayashi said that his hatred had overwhelmed him, leaving him able to wish for nothing but Liao Chi-ming’s death.

Japanese: しかし、実際膝を抱え蹲る廖志明を見てしまったあとでは、その気持も雲散霧消したと言う。
English: Yet once he actually saw Liao crouching there and clutching his knee, Hayashi later said, the feeling dissolved altogether.

Japanese: 氏も不良少年であったわけで、喧嘩などは見慣れていたが、人が人を銃で撃つその場面を目の当たりにしたのは初めてで、その衝撃は大きかった。
English: Hayashi himself had been a delinquent and was familiar with fistfights, but this was the first time he had seen one person shoot another. The shock was immense.

Japanese: 事前に亮との打ち合わせをしたとおり、押さえつけて注射を打つところまではなんとかやり遂げたが、それが限界だ。
English: As arranged with Leung beforehand, he somehow managed to hold Liao down and administer the injection. That was the limit of what he could bear.

Japanese: 傷つく廖に同情したというわけでもないが、足から血をダラダラ流しながら、薬の効果によってとろんとした目つきをした彼の姿を見たとき、自分でも予期しなかった恐怖が心にわき起こって、もうその場にいられなくなったと言う。
English: It was not that he felt sympathy for the wounded Liao. But when he saw blood pouring from the man’s leg and his eyes glazed by the medicine, an entirely unexpected fear welled up inside him. He could no longer remain there, Hayashi later recalled.

Japanese: 「これから僕は一つ提案をする。あんたにとってもけして損とは言えない話だ」
English: “I am about to make you a proposal. It is not a bad deal for you, either.”

Japanese: 亮はそう言って、話を切り出した。
English: With these words, Leung opened the discussion.

Japanese: 「さっき言ったとおり、僕はもうすぐ第三代龍頭になる。だからあんたに龍頭の地位を譲ることは出来ないが、かわりに僕の後見人という立場を用意する」
English: “As I told you, I will soon become the third Longtou. I cannot yield that position to you. In its place, however, I will offer you the position of my guardian.”

Japanese: 廖はこの言葉で、例の蛇に似た顔にひきつり笑いを浮かべる。
English: At this, Liao twisted his snakelike face into a smile.

Japanese: 「私がお前の後見人？　銃弾をあびせ、訳の分からぬ薬を打って、そんなもの後見人に対する仕打ちではないだろう」
English: “I am to be your guardian? You shoot me, inject me with some incomprehensible drug, and call that any way to treat a guardian?”

Japanese: そのあざけりの態度に、亮は表情一つ変えず言葉を続ける。
English: Leung continued without the slightest change of expression at the mockery.

Japanese: 「龍頭の後見人となれば、格としては僕よりも上であるし、あんたにとっては何も恥ずかしいことじゃない。もちろん、仕事は何もしなくて良い。……いや、この街ではもうどういった仕事をする必要もないんだ。あんたは第一線を退いて街の外で暮らすんだ。あんたの組織は僕らが引き継いで、これまでの活動を行ってもらう」
English: “As guardian to the Longtou, you would stand above even me in formal rank. There would be nothing shameful in it for you. Naturally, you would have no work to perform. ...No, there would no longer be any need for you to conduct business of any kind in this city. You would retire from the front line and live outside Y District. We would take over your organization and have its members continue their present activities.”

Japanese: 「私は街から追放で、組織は解体して義勝に吸収するということか」
English: “You mean to exile me from the city, dismantle my organization, and absorb it into Yisheng?”

Japanese: 薬が本来の効き目を発揮し、落ち着きを取り戻したのか、廖の顔つきには鋭さが戻る。
English: Whether because the medicine had taken its intended effect or because he had recovered his composure, the sharpness returned to Liao’s face.

Japanese: 「馬鹿を言っちゃいけない」
English: “Do not talk such nonsense.”

Japanese: さすがにこういった場合の廖志明は迫力のある表情をするものだ。しかも、こんな絶望的な状況でも微塵もそれを感じさせない態度で、端で見ている林の背をぞくりとさせるものがあった。林はこうした組織のボスというものを間近に見るのは初めてだったが、なるほど伊達ではないのだと不本意ながら納得せざるをえなかった。
English: Liao Chi-ming could be genuinely intimidating at a moment like this. Even in so desperate a position, his manner betrayed none of it, and a chill ran down Hayashi’s back as he watched from the edge of the room. He had never seen the head of an organization at such close range. Against his will, he understood that the man’s position was no empty title.

Japanese: が、最も近くで正面に座った亮は何も感じなかったようだ。
English: Yet Leung, seated directly before Liao, appeared to Hayashi to feel nothing at all.

Japanese: 「そうかな？　最大限の敬意を払った条件なんだがね」
English: “Is that so? I believed I had offered you the most respectful terms possible.”

Japanese: 彼はさらりと言う。
English: He spoke lightly.

Japanese: 「このままあんたを殺したっていいんだ。しかし、まがりなりにもあんたは初代……つまり僕の父に対しては従順だったし、最大の協力者でもあった。だからこうして、ありえない厚遇を提案している」
English: “I could simply kill you now. But for all your faults, you were loyal to the first Longtou—my father—and were his greatest collaborator. That is why I have come here to offer you unheard-of generosity.”

Japanese: 「ふん、わかったわかった。こうなっては是非もなし。後見人になってやるから、もう帰ってくれ。早く治療をしなくては、おれは失血で死んでしまう」
English: “Hmph. Very well, very well. There is nothing to be done now. I will become your guardian, so go home. Unless I receive treatment quickly, I will bleed to death.”

Japanese: そして廖は、シッシッと、手を振って犬でも追い払うような仕草をする。
English: Liao waved his hand as though shooing away a dog.

Japanese: それに対して亮は、胸元から携帯端末を取り出すと、指先で操作をし、その画面を廖に見えるように置く。
English: In answer, Leung removed a mobile device from his breast pocket, tapped at the screen, and set it where Liao could see.

Japanese: その画面には生体認証を促すメッセージが表示されている。廖志明が親指を画面に押し当て、口頭で暗証番号を言えば、銀行のメニューに入り、手続きが行えるというものだ。
English: A message on the screen requested biometric authentication. If Liao Chi-ming pressed his thumb to it and spoke his PIN aloud, the device would open the banking menu and allow the necessary procedures.

Japanese: 「承諾するのなら、あんたの個人資産を抑えさせて貰う。すべてが終わったら返還する」
English: “If you accept, I will take control of your personal assets. They will be returned once everything is finished.”

Japanese: 差し出された画面を前に、廖は口ごもる。
English: Faced with the screen waiting for his authentication, Liao faltered.

Japanese: 「はやくしてくれないか？　失血死がこわいんだろう？」
English: “Would you hurry? You are frightened of bleeding to death, aren’t you?”

Japanese: 亮が促すのに、廖は苦笑し、
English: At Leung’s urging, Liao gave a strained smile.

Japanese: 「そんなことをしなくても大丈夫。私は嘘をついたりはしないよ」
English: “There is no need for that. I would never tell a lie.”

Japanese: 「どうしても認証したくないんだね？」
English: “You are determined not to authenticate it?”

Japanese: 「今日はそういう気分ではないんだ」
English: “I don’t feel like doing so today.”

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 亮はあっさりと端末を引っ込め、
English: Leung withdrew the device without protest.

Japanese: 「こんな状況でも、僕らを騙そうとするあんたの度胸に個人的には敬服するが、まあ客観的には賢明とは言えないね」
English: “Personally, I admire the nerve it takes to deceive us even in your present circumstances. Objectively, however, I cannot call it wise.”

Japanese: 「ふざけるなっ！　だれが組織を手放して隠居などするか！」
English: “Do not mock me! Who would surrender his organization and retire?”

Japanese: 突然廖は吼えた。目の前で大声をあげられた亮は顔を顰め、
English: Liao suddenly roared. Leung frowned as the man shouted in his face.

Japanese: 「うるさいな」
English: “You’re loud.”

Japanese: 「殺すなら殺せ！　しかし、お前達が私達と争って勝てると思うなよ。そもそも、私を殺してここから無事に帰れるかどうか……」
English: “Kill me if you mean to! But do not imagine that you can defeat us in a conflict. To begin with, even if you kill me, do you truly think you can leave here alive...?”

Japanese: 「あんたをここで殺したって、大した争いにはならないよ。……あんたは本当に、自分の部下が、自分の死後も戦ってくれると思っているのかい？」
English: “Killing you here would hardly produce any great conflict. ...Do you truly believe that your subordinates will continue fighting after your death?”

Japanese: 亮はあきれたように溜息をつく。
English: Leung sighed in exasperation.

Japanese: 「あんたの組織は確かに巨大だが、僕らと争いたがっているのはあんただけだ。あんたが死んだら、僕はジェフリーの件を公表し、組織の掟通りの処罰をしたことを宣言してから、きみの幹部たちに交渉をもちかけるつもりだ。すべてがすべてとは言わないが、大半はほどほどのところで和解してくれるだろう。我々と協力すれば、これまでより儲けられるのは彼らにもすぐ理解出来る。……あんたが知っているとおり、あんたの部下はみな非常に優秀で合理的で賢明だ。無意味な抗争よりビジネスを優先するだろうね」
English: “Your organization is certainly enormous, but you are the only one who wants to fight us. If you die, I will make your responsibility for Jeffrey public and declare that you were punished according to the organization’s rules. Then I will approach your officers and negotiate. I won’t claim that every last one will agree, but the majority will accept a reasonable settlement. They will soon understand that cooperation with us will earn them more than before. ...As you know, your subordinates are uniformly capable, rational, and intelligent. They will place business above a pointless war.”

Japanese: 廖は反論をせずに、睨み付けている。ここで言い返さないということは、彼もその態度とは裏腹に亮と同じ見解を持っているということだろう。
English: Liao offered no rebuttal, but only glared. His silence suggested that beneath his defiance, he shared Leung’s view.

Japanese: 「だからあんたが本当に僕らに勝つつもりだったら、自分の身だけは最優先で守るべきだったのさ。くだらない女遊びは自重してね。……僕らの方から手を出すはずがないと、なめてたのかな？　僕らが、もっとあんたたちのことを恐れていると思っていた？　……その辺はやっぱり、結局ただの商売人上がりで、弱いモノだけを相手に暴力を使ってきた甘えなんだろうね。父から組織を受け継ぎ、市民を脅しながら生きてきたあんたは、対等に近い実力と、暴力的な性格の両方を持つ相手と戦ったことがない」
English: “If you truly meant to defeat us, your own safety should have been your highest priority. You should have restrained yourself from this foolish womanizing. ...Did you look down upon us because you thought we would never strike first? Did you imagine we were more afraid of you? ...I suppose that, in the end, is the complacency of a mere merchant who has only ever used violence against the weak. You inherited an organization from your father and lived by threatening ordinary citizens. You have never fought anyone nearly as strong as you and just as willing to use violence.”

Japanese: 淡々と語る亮を、廖はあざ笑い、
English: Liao sneered at Leung’s measured speech.

Japanese: 「お前は何もわかっていない。たとえばお前の父親のクリス・ツェーならば、平気な顔で普段と同じように振る舞ったろう。それが本当の支配者になるものの振る舞いというものだ」
English: “You understand nothing. Your father Chris Tse, for example, would have kept a perfectly calm face and behaved no differently than on any other day. That is the conduct of a true ruler.”

Japanese: 「……父さんの真似をしたつもりかい？」
English: “...You meant to imitate my father?”

Japanese: 「まあね。……しかし、残念ながら私にはお前の父親ほどの器量はなかったようだ。だからこんな結果になった。だが、こんな暗殺者のまねごとをしているお前は、さらにそれ以下のようだな」
English: “I did. ...Regrettably, it seems I was not a man of your father’s caliber, and this was the result. But you, playing at assassin in this fashion, appear to be lesser still.”

Japanese: 「非合理で古くさい考え方だ。……そんなだから、僕は最初からあんたたちに負ける気は全然しなかったんだよ。ただね、どういう形で収めるかについては随分悩んだ」
English: “That is an irrational and antiquated way of thinking. ...It is precisely why I never thought for a moment that I would lose to people like you. I did spend a long time deciding how best to settle this.”

Japanese: 彼は机に置かれたままの龍頭の杯を見つめながら話している。
English: He spoke while staring at the Longtou’s cup where it remained upon the table.

Japanese: 林氏はなぜ彼がこの場面で目をそらしているのか、不自然に思ったが、理由を思いつくよりも早く亮は次の言葉を口にする。
English: Hayashi found it strange that Leung should look away at this particular moment. Before he could think of a reason, Leung spoke again.

Japanese: 「それでまあ、可能ならば円満解決がベストだと思ってね」
English: “And so, if possible, I decided an amicable resolution would be best.”

Japanese: 「銃弾で傷つけ、脅迫しながら円満解決とは笑わせてくれる」
English: “You shoot and threaten me, then speak of an amicable resolution. How very amusing.”

Japanese: 「廖志明、拗ねてる場合じゃないよ。いまあんたは正しい判断を下さなければならない。なに、難しいことじゃない。あんたの両肩に乗っているそいつがスイカじゃなければ、それを使えばいいだけの話だ」
English: “Liao Chi-ming, this is no time to sulk. You have to make the correct decision now. It isn’t difficult. If that thing between your shoulders isn’t a watermelon, you need only use it.”

Japanese: 亮は呆れて溜息をついた。
English: Leung sighed in exasperation.

Japanese: 「あんたは優秀だったが、もう終わった人間だ。自分の組織が戦えない状態になっていることに気づかず戦争を仕掛けようとした判断は愚劣としか言いようがない。立て直せると考えてるようだが、もう無理だ。だけれど、僕にはそれが出来る。僕の支配下に収まれば、あんたの作った組織も戦える集団として蘇るだろう」
English: “You were a capable man, but your time is over. You failed to realize that your organization was in no condition to fight, yet you tried to start a war. The decision can only be called foolish. You appear to believe you can rebuild it, but you cannot. I can. Under my rule, the organization you created can be restored as a fighting force.”

Japanese: 廖は何も言わずににらみ返している。
English: Liao said nothing and returned his glare.

Japanese: 「あんたに、僕に協力するチャンスをやろうと言っているんだ。僕はあんたの組織を吸収したら、その後は、他のファミリーも取り込むつもりだ。大体、一つの組織のなかで、香港人だの、客家人だの、ブラジル人だの、別々に固まっているのは効率的ではないからね。くだらない分断がなくなれば、YSはもっと強くて巨大な組織になる」
English: “I am offering you a chance to cooperate with me. Once I absorb your organization, I intend to bring the other families into the fold as well. It is hardly efficient for people from Hong Kong, Hakka people, Brazilians, and every other group to cluster separately within a single organization. Once those pointless divisions disappear, YS will become both larger and stronger.”

Japanese: 「そう上手くいくと思うなよ」
English: “Do not imagine it will go so smoothly.”

Japanese: 廖は吐き捨てるように言う。
English: Liao spat the words.

Japanese: 「うまくいくさ」
English: “It will.”

Japanese: 亮は目を細め、
English: Leung narrowed his eyes.

Japanese: 「すべてのファミリ－は一旦解散して、新しいYSの部下となるんだ。その時には、もちろん、香港派というのも消えてなくなっているし、義勝なんていう古くさい名前を口にするやつもいないだろう」
English: “Every family will first dissolve, and its members will become subordinates of a new YS. Naturally, by then the Hong Kong faction will have vanished as well, and no one will utter an antiquated name like Yisheng.”

Japanese: そう言った時、世傑も驚きの目で亮を見た。彼も事前に知らされていない内容だったのだろう。
English: At those words, even Sai-kit looked at Leung in surprise. Evidently, he too had not been informed of the plan beforehand.

Japanese: 「新しいYSには、出身地によるどんな優劣もない」
English: “In the new YS, no place of origin will stand above another.”

Japanese: 「机上の空論だな。血と土地というものは人間の深い部分に根ざしたものだ」
English: “An armchair fantasy. Blood and land are rooted in the deepest parts of human beings.”

Japanese: 廖は苦々しく呟く。
English: Liao muttered bitterly.

Japanese: 「あんたたちにとってはそうかもしれない。だけど、世代はかわる。これからは、僕らのような、Y地区で生まれた人間達がこの街を仕切ってゆくんだ。行ったこともない土地の名前に縛られて行動するのは馬鹿馬鹿しい話さ」
English: “Perhaps that is true for your generation. But generations change. From now on, people like us—people born in Y District—will govern this city. It is absurd to let the name of a land one has never visited dictate one’s actions.”

Japanese: 亮は机の上の龍頭の杯の位置をすこし動かし、
English: Leung shifted the position of the Longtou’s cup slightly upon the table.

Japanese: 「そして僕は、この街のあちこちにわだかまっているくだらないものを排除する。別に健全で綺麗な街にしようってんじゃない。……僕はちょっと計算してみたんだが、暗闇通りの平均的な娼婦一人あたり、業者三人を養っている。この業者ってののうち、二人は売春の利益になるようなことは何もしないで金をたかるだけの穀潰しだ。だから見ろよ。暗闇通りには、真っ昼間から肩で風を切って歩き、金をばらまくように使う連中がわんさかいるんだぜ。そして売春婦たちは病気だの暴力だので、平均六年で死ぬ。育てられなかった子供の死体はその辺にゴミのように捨てられる。一方、穀潰しどもはどんどん肥え太る。それがこの街の良さだと言う人間もいるが、僕には我慢がならないのさ」
English: “And I will remove the pointless things festering throughout this city. I don’t mean to make it wholesome and clean. ...I did a little calculation. The average prostitute on Darkness Street supports three middlemen. Of those three, two do nothing useful for the sex trade. They merely extort money—parasites. Look around you. Darkness Street teems with men who swagger about in broad daylight and spend money as though throwing it away. Meanwhile, disease or violence kills the prostitutes after an average of six years. The bodies of children they cannot raise are discarded nearby like refuse, while the parasites grow fatter and fatter. Some say that is what makes this city so fine. I find it intolerable.”

Japanese: 「私には興味のない話だな」
English: “The subject does not interest me.”

Japanese: 「そうだろう。まあ、あんたには何も伝わらないと思いながら、話してみたのさ」
English: “I thought nothing I said would reach you. I decided to say it anyway.”

Japanese: 「くだらん！」
English: “Enough of this nonsense!”

Japanese: 廖は不快を隠しもせずに顔を歪め、
English: Liao’s face twisted with undisguised displeasure.

Japanese: 「……いろいろとご託を並べたが、お前は私を撃って、無理矢理茶飲み話をしに来たのか？　だとすれば大したジョークだな！　くだらんことを言うのなら、私を殺してみろ！　そして、お前が言うように、私の部下が降伏するか、試してみれば良い。さあ殺せ！　その後に、お前も死ぬことになるのだからな！」
English: “...You have delivered a great many sermons, but did you shoot me and force your way in here merely to have a pleasant chat? If so, that is quite the joke. If you have nothing but nonsense to say, try killing me! Then you can discover whether my subordinates surrender as you claim. Come, kill me! You will die afterward in any case!”

Japanese: 「いくら傷ついているとはいえ、がっかりさせないで欲しいもんだ。どうしても僕らに季節外れのスイカジュースを作らせたいらしい……」
English: “Wounded or not, I would rather you did not disappoint me. Apparently, you are determined to make us prepare some out-of-season watermelon juice...”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめて溜息をつくと、
English: Leung shrugged and sighed.

Japanese: 「……というわけで、次はきみと話そうか。トーマス・リャオ」
English: “...With that settled, shall I speak with you next, Thomas Liao?”

Japanese: 「トミーだって？」
English: “Tommy?”

Japanese: 声をあげたのは、馬世傑だ。
English: Ma Sai-kit was the one who cried out.

Japanese: 「そうとも」
English: “That’s right.”

Japanese: 亮はこともなげに答える。
English: Leung answered as though it were nothing.

Japanese: 「どこに彼がいるのよ？」
English: “Where is he, then?”

Japanese: 世傑は部屋を見回す。彼の目には、亮が言うような人物は映らない。
English: Sai-kit looked around the room. He saw no sign of the person Leung had named.

Japanese: 「お客さんは、大分前からもう来て、話を聞いているぜ」
English: “Our guests arrived some time ago. They’ve been listening all along.”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめ、
English: Leung shrugged.

Japanese: 「おい小僧。トミーがこの部屋にいるというのか？」
English: “Listen, boy. Are you saying Tommy is inside this room?”

Japanese: 廖が顰める。
English: Liao frowned.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。僕はさっきからずっとそれに気がついていた。トミー、早く姿を現せよ。話をしようじゃないか」
English: “I am. I have known he was here for some time. Tommy, show yourself already. Let us have a conversation.”

Japanese: 「嘘だ。お前は何をでたらめを言っている。トミーなど、この部屋のどこにもいない」
English: “That is a lie. What nonsense are you spouting? Tommy is nowhere in this room.”

Japanese: 廖のその言葉に、亮は溜息をついて、
English: Leung sighed at Liao’s words.

Japanese: 「……本名は李小玉」
English: “Her real name is Li Xiaoyu.”

Japanese: と、静かに語り始めた。
English: He began speaking quietly.

Japanese: 「２５年前にボーダーエリアに住む夫婦の元に生まれた。三才の時に街の者との諍いで両親を殺される。十二才の時にエリアを出て、暗闇通りの空き家に住み着き窃盗を繰り返すが、ある時ヤミ金事務所に盗みに入った時に捕まり、リンチを受けて殺されるところをトーマス・リャオに救われ、彼のボディガードとなる」
English: “She was born twenty-five years ago to a couple living in the Border Area. When she was three, her parents were killed in a dispute with people from the city. At twelve, she left the Area and occupied an abandoned house on Darkness Street, where she repeatedly committed theft. One day, she was caught breaking into a loan shark’s office. Thomas Liao saved her when they were about to beat her to death, and she became his bodyguard.”

Japanese: そこで廖の顔をチラとみると、彼は落ち着きをなくし、黙り込んでいる。
English: Leung glanced at Liao. The man had lost his composure and fallen silent.

Japanese: 「アイスと偽名を名乗ったその女はタイプAだ。そのA能力は、けして誰にも気づかれずに行動すること。彼女が能力を使えば、堂々と部屋のドアを開け、中に入っても僕らは自分の目や耳でそれを認識することが出来ない。……素晴らしい能力だが、万能ではない。多分、物理的に姿を消すのではなく、人間の心をいじる力なんだろ。だから、その能力で人間の感覚を欺くことが出来ても、機械の目はごまかせない。例えば監視カメラが相手では意味がないし、他には……」
English: “The woman using the alias Ice is a Type A. Her ability allows her to act without anyone ever noticing her. When she uses it, she can openly enter through a room’s door, and we cannot recognize her presence with our own eyes or ears. ...It is a magnificent ability, but not an omnipotent one. I doubt she physically vanishes. More likely, her power interferes with the human mind. It may deceive human senses, but it cannot deceive a machine’s eye. A surveillance camera, for example, can still record her. And then there are...”

Japanese: 亮は目の前の龍頭の杯を持ち上げ、
English: Leung lifted the Longtou’s cup before him.

Japanese: 「よく磨かれた金属にも、その姿がばっちり映り込んでしまうのさ」
English: “Highly polished metal surfaces. Her image appears in them perfectly clearly.”

Japanese: 「それは……」
English: “That...”

Japanese: 動揺を見せる廖をよそ目に、亮は誰もいないはずの空間に向かって言う。
English: Ignoring Liao’s agitation, Leung addressed a space that should have held no one.

Japanese: 「もう姿を出せよ。アイス……それと、トーマス・リャオ。天明が、ビルの側にあった二つの生命が突然消えたって報告した時からね、君らがここに来るのは分かっていたんだ」
English: “Show yourselves. Ice... and Thomas Liao. I knew you were coming from the moment Tin-ming reported that two life signs beside the building had suddenly disappeared.”

Japanese: その言葉が部屋に響き、そして皆が固唾を飲んで見守るしばしの沈黙のあと、
English: His words echoed through the room. Everyone held their breath and watched through the brief silence that followed.

Japanese: 「な、な、なんで……あっ」
English: “H-how, how did you... Ah.”

Japanese: 声と共に、ふっと二人の男女が誰もいない空間に姿を現した。
English: With the voice, two figures—a man and a woman—abruptly appeared in the empty space.

Japanese: トーマスはうっかり声を出してしまったことに一瞬後悔の表情を見せたが、今はそれよりも気になることがある。
English: For an instant, Thomas looked as though he regretted letting the words escape. But he had a more pressing question.

Japanese: 「なんで小謝は、そこまで詳しくアイスのことを知ってるの？」
English: “How do you know so much about Ice, Siu Tse?”

Japanese: 「そりゃ当然調べるよ。僕が香港派の一員としてYSに加入する以上、きみやアイスは仮想の敵だからね」
English: “Naturally, I investigated. Once I joined YS as a member of the Hong Kong faction, you and Ice became potential enemies.”

Japanese: 「……ねえアイス、君の本名は李小玉っていうの？」
English: “...Ice, is your real name Li Xiaoyu?”

Japanese: トーマスはアイスを振り返る。
English: Thomas looked toward Ice.

Japanese: アイスは警戒に満ちた目でじっと亮の顔を見つめながら頷く。
English: She nodded without taking her wary eyes from Leung’s face.

Japanese: 「僕も全然しらなかったよ」
English: “I didn’t know either.”

Japanese: トーマスは絶句した。
English: Thomas was lost for words.

Japanese: 林氏が言うには、謝亮のこうした不思議な調査力は子供の頃からのものらしい。特にミュータントについては不必要と思われる素性まで徹底的に調べる。タイプAに痛い目に遭わされたことがあったのだろう。謝亮は昔から、仲間があきれるほどY地区に住むタイプAについて詳しかった。
English: According to Mr. Hayashi, Tse Leung had possessed this uncanny ability to investigate since childhood. He was particularly thorough with mutants, pursuing even details that appeared unnecessary. Hayashi supposed that some Type A might once have caused him pain. From an early age, Leung knew more about the Type As living in Y District than even his companions thought reasonable.

Japanese: 「トミー。とりあえず、おかしな真似はしないでね」
English: “Tommy, don’t try anything strange, all right?”

Japanese: 世傑はいつの間にかもう片方の手に新たな拳銃を握っており、トーマス達に狙いをつけている。
English: At some point, a second pistol had appeared in Sai-kit’s other hand. He trained it upon Thomas and Ice.

Japanese: 「世傑、彼は大丈夫だ。銃を下ろしてくれ」
English: “Sai-kit, he is no threat. Lower the gun.”

Japanese: 亮はすぐにそう言って、世傑に銃を下げさせる。
English: Leung spoke at once and made Sai-kit lower the weapon.

Japanese: 「……なぜここに」
English: “...Why are you here?”

Japanese: 廖志明と言えども、このような形で息子と会うのはバツが悪いらしかった。
English: Even Liao Chi-ming was uncomfortable meeting his son under these circumstances.

Japanese: ここは愛人宅であるし、廖はまんまと罠にはまって銃で脅されているのである。しかも脅している相手はトーマスと幼なじみである謝亮だ。
English: He was inside his mistress’s home, caught neatly in a trap and threatened at gunpoint. Worse still, the man threatening him was Tse Leung, Thomas’s childhood friend.

Japanese: 「お父さんがどんなことをしているか知りたくって。それと、お父さんに何かあったら守ろうと……」
English: “I wanted to know what you were doing. And if anything happened, I wanted to protect you...”

Japanese: 「守れてないじゃないか」
English: “You haven’t protected me.”

Japanese: 廖は苦い顔で言う。
English: Liao spoke bitterly.

Japanese: 「来た時にはもう傷ついていて、チャンスを待っていたら、つい、姿を現しそびれちゃって……。僕らは武器も持ってこなかったし……」
English: “You were already wounded when we arrived. We waited for our chance, and then somehow we missed the moment to show ourselves... We didn’t bring any weapons, either...”

Japanese: 「駄目なやつだ」
English: “Useless fool.”

Japanese: 廖は肩を落として溜息をつく。
English: Liao’s shoulders fell as he sighed.

Japanese: 「駄目じゃないさ。何もしなかったのは正解さ。僕が見張っていたんだからね」
English: “He is not useless. Doing nothing was the correct decision. I was watching Thomas the whole time.”

Japanese: 亮の指摘を受け、廖は彼の顔を睨み付ける。
English: At Leung’s reminder, Liao glared into his face.

Japanese: 「それより、小謝、今の言葉は本当かい？　YSのなかから対立をなくして、街をよくするって」
English: “More importantly, Siu Tse, was what you just said true? Do you truly mean to end the divisions within YS and improve the city?”

Japanese: 「そのつもりだ」
English: “That is my intention.”

Japanese: 「そうしたら、路上で自分を売り物にするかわいそうな子供達や、ケモノのように扱われるかわいそうなミュータントたちもいなくなるの？」
English: “Will that mean there will be no more poor children selling themselves on the street, or poor mutants treated like animals?”

Japanese: 「いなくなりはしない。ただ彼らも生き延びるチャンスが増えるだろう」
English: “They will not disappear. But their chances of surviving may improve.”

Japanese: 言われてトーマスは考え込む。
English: Thomas fell into thought.

Japanese: 「……なあトミー、協力してくれないか？　きみたち親子が協力してくれるのなら、さっき話したとおり、僕は出来うる限りの待遇で迎え入れるつもりだ」
English: “...Tommy, will you cooperate with me? If you and your father agree to help, I mean to welcome you on the most generous terms I can offer, precisely as I explained.”

Japanese: 亮はソファーにどっしりと腰をおろしたまま、気安い口調でそう呼びかける。
English: Still seated solidly on the sofa, Leung made the appeal with easy familiarity.

Japanese: 「小謝と戦うのは、いやだな……」
English: “I don’t want to fight you, Siu Tse...”

Japanese: トーマスは俯き、顎に手を当てる。
English: Thomas lowered his head and placed a hand upon his chin.

Japanese: 「おい、トミー！　何を考えることがある！」
English: “Tommy! What is there to consider?”

Japanese: 廖は息子の思わぬ態度に慌てるが、トーマスは返事をせずに真剣な顔で考え続け、そして首を左右にふると、
English: His son’s unexpected attitude alarmed Liao. Thomas did not answer, but continued thinking with a grave expression. At length, he shook his head.

Japanese: 「父さん、僕は、小謝の言ってることの方が正しいような気がする」
English: “Father, I feel that Siu Tse is the one who is right.”

Japanese: そしてまっすぐに父を見つめた。
English: He looked directly into his father’s eyes.

Japanese: 「この街は、YSみたいな大きい組織が出来る前は、木下組が好き放題やったり、よそ者がおかしな秘密クラブを作ったりして、メチャクチャだったんでしょ？　父さんがYSのなかで変な争いを起こそうとしているのは、時代を逆戻りさせるのと同じことだと思うんだ。小謝のお父さんが秘密クラブを潰し、YSを作ったから、ファミリー同士の対立も収まり、街は前より良くなったんだ。次の段階として、YS内での垣根を取り払うというのは、すごくまっとうな考え方だと思う……。ねえ小謝、いまここでうんといえば、父さんを治療してくれるかい？」
English: “Before there was a large organization like YS, this city was in chaos, wasn’t it? The Kinoshita-gumi did whatever they pleased, and outsiders created strange secret clubs. I think your attempt to cause a conflict inside YS would amount to turning back the clock. Siu Tse’s father destroyed those secret clubs and created YS. That ended the conflicts between the families, and the city improved. Removing the barriers inside YS as the next step seems entirely reasonable to me... Siu Tse, if he says yes here and now, will you treat Father’s wound?”

Japanese: 「もちろんだとも」
English: “Of course.”

Japanese: 「おい、やめろ！　お前は、このガキがどれだけ恐ろしいことを言っているのか分かっていない。何が、血を流したくないだ！　こいつの言ったことを実行すれば、それこそすべてが混乱してしまう。まずまっさきに、こいつの仲間の義勝の連中が、反対するだろうよ！　そんなことを公に宣言した途端、こいつは最も重要な仲間に見放されるのだ」
English: “Stop, you fool! You do not understand how monstrous this boy’s proposal is. He speaks of avoiding bloodshed, but if he carries out what he described, he will throw everything into chaos. His own comrades in Yisheng will be the first to object! The moment he announces such a policy in public, his most important allies will abandon him.”

Japanese: 廖志明の言葉はトーマスにとっても一定の説得力があった。
English: Liao Chi-ming’s argument made a certain amount of sense even to Thomas.

Japanese: 実際、旧義勝が保守的だというのは広く知られており、他の組織が時代と共に他国人などを受け入れるケースが増えてきたのに対し、彼らは香港出身者以外を組織に招き入れない。
English: Old Yisheng’s conservatism was widely known. While other organizations had increasingly begun to accept people from different countries as the times changed, Yisheng admitted no one who did not come from Hong Kong.

Japanese: 余談ではあるが、それが、クリス・ツェーによって天下を取ったと言って良い香港派がのびなやむ最大の理由でもあった。
English: As an aside, this was also the greatest reason the Hong Kong faction, which had effectively conquered the city under Chris Tse, now struggled to expand.

Japanese: 「……小謝、もし、父さんの言うように、義勝の人たちが従えないと言い出したらどうするつもり？　もしくは、別のものを龍頭に仕立て上げると言い出したら……」
English: “...Siu Tse, what will you do if the people of Yisheng say they cannot obey, as Father predicts? Or if they announce that they mean to make someone else Longtou...?”

Japanese: 「トミー、YSには掟がある」
English: “Tommy, YS has rules.”

Japanese: 亮はトーマスの目をじっと見つめ、穏やかな口調で言った。
English: Leung looked steadily into Thomas’s eyes and spoke in a gentle tone.

Japanese: 「龍頭の方針に従えないのならば、そのものは追放されなければならない。自分のボスを陥れようとするならば、死を持って償わなければならない」
English: “Anyone unable to obey the Longtou’s policy must be expelled. Anyone who attempts to bring down his own boss must pay with his life.”

Japanese: 「相手が誰でも？」
English: “No matter who it is?”

Japanese: 「誰でもだ。馬明だって、世傑だって、場合によっては僕自身にだって、掟は平等に適用される」
English: “No matter who. The rules apply equally to Ma Ming, to Sai-kit, and, if the occasion arose, even to me.”

Japanese: 「……ありがとう。信じるよ。父さんが銀行の認証すればいいんだね？」
English: “...Thank you. I believe you. Father only needs to authenticate the bank account, is that right?”

Japanese: 「おい、馬鹿！」
English: “You idiot!”

Japanese: 「父さん、僕は、こんな場所に自分自身でやって来て、危険をおかして父さんと直の話し合いを求めた小謝の気持は本物だと思うんだ。対立をなくしたいって言葉を僕は信じたい」
English: “Father, Siu Tse came to a place like this in person and exposed himself to danger to seek a direct conversation with you. I believe his feelings are sincere. I want to believe him when he says that he wants to end the conflict.”

Japanese: トーマスが真剣な眼差しを向けながらきっぱりそう告げると、廖は言葉を失う。
English: Thomas delivered the words firmly, his gaze grave and unwavering. Liao could find no answer.

Japanese: 「小謝、ただひとつだけ、条件をつけてほしい」
English: “Siu Tse, I only ask that you add one condition.”

Japanese: 「なんだい？」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「僕らのファミリーがYSに吸収された後は、YSに所属する一部署になると思うんだけど、そのリーダーを僕に任せてくれないか？」
English: “Once our Family has been absorbed into YS, I imagine it will become one division within the organization. Will you entrust its leadership to me?”

Japanese: 「つまり、きみが父のあとを継ぎたいってわけか」
English: “In other words, you want to succeed your father.”

Japanese: 「形としてはそうなるけれど、ちゃんときみの部下として振る舞うよ……。もちろん、グランドタワーに暮らすし、監視してくれてかまわない」
English: “Formally, yes, but I would serve you faithfully as your subordinate... Naturally, I would live in Grand Tower, and you would be free to keep me under observation.”

Japanese: 「いままで、いくら勧めても、ファミリーを継ぎたいなんて口にしたことがなかったのに、なぜこんな場面になって……」
English: “No matter how often I encouraged you, you never once said that you wished to inherit the Family. Why, at a moment like this...?”

Japanese: 廖は呆然とした面持ちで口にする。
English: Liao spoke in a daze.

Japanese: 「それですべてが丸くおさまると思うんだ。形式上でも僕がリーダーということになれば、ファミリーのみんなは納得しやすいと思うし。……ねえ謝亮。どうかな？」
English: “I think that would settle everything neatly. Even if my leadership were only formal, it would make the Family’s members more likely to accept the arrangement. ...Tell me, Leung. What do you say?”

Japanese: 「飲もう」
English: “Agreed.”

Japanese: 「ありがとう……。きみが言う通り、世代が変わって、すべてがかわるんだと思う。フェルナンデスさんのところのアウロラだって、きっと同意してくれるはずさ。これからのY地区は、Y地区で生まれ育った人たちが作ってゆくんだ！」
English: “Thank you... Just as you said, the generations are changing, and everything will change with them. Even Aurora in Mr. Fernandes’s family is sure to agree. From now on, Y District will be built by the people born and raised in Y District!”

Japanese: 「トーマス様が生まれたのはY地区ではなく、お母様のご実家近くの病院だったはずですが……」
English: “Master Thomas, I believe you were born not in Y District, but at a hospital near your mother’s family home...”

Japanese: アイスが小声で囁くが、トーマスは無視して、
English: Ice whispered the correction. Thomas ignored her.

Japanese: 「小謝、たくさんひどいことをした僕と父さんを許しておくれ。僕はきみの部下として、YSが良くなるよう全力を尽くしたい……」
English: “Siu Tse, please forgive my father and me for all the terrible things we have done. As your subordinate, I want to devote all my strength to making YS better...”

Japanese: そう言って跪くトーマス。口をあんぐりと開け、目の前で起きていることが信じられない廖志明。そして林氏は、トーマス・リャオという人間のことはよく知らなかったが、血みどろになって息絶え絶えの父親の前でこんな話をしているということに度肝を抜かれ、謝亮や廖志明と同じような、『自分とは違う人種』なのだと感じているのだった。
English: Thomas knelt. Liao Chi-ming’s mouth hung open, unable to believe what was taking place before him. Mr. Hayashi knew little about Thomas Liao, but the sight of him speaking this way before his blood-soaked, gasping father left Hayashi thunderstruck. Like Tse Leung and Liao Chi-ming, he felt, Thomas belonged to a breed apart from himself.

Japanese: 「あっははははは！」
English: “Ah-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

Japanese: 亮は、その場に居合わせたみなが面食らうような大きな声で笑い、笑い終わると、笑い涙を指先で拭い、そして言った。
English: Leung laughed loudly enough to startle everyone present. When he had finished, he wiped a tear of laughter away with a fingertip and spoke.

Japanese: 「素晴らしい」
English: “Magnificent.”

Japanese: ――これが、廖家併合の顛末である。
English: —Such were the circumstances of the Liao Family’s annexation.

Japanese: これによってYS最大級の組織であるリャオ・ファミリーと旧義勝は統合されることになり、その事実はこれから一週間後に行われた謝亮の第三代龍頭就任の場において発表された。
English: As a result, the Liao Family, one of the largest organizations in YS, was integrated with old Yisheng. The announcement came one week later, at Tse Leung’s investiture as the third Longtou.

Japanese: このときの所信表明において、謝亮は組織全体の統合についても口にした。今現在それぞれ別個の組織として存在するギャング達をYSという一つの名のもとに吸収するというこの言葉は、大きな反響と動揺をもたらし、それによって、新しい騒動が始まることになるが、それはまた別の話である。
English: In his declaration of policy at the ceremony, Tse Leung also spoke of integrating the organization as a whole. His announcement—that the various gangs then existing as separate organizations would be absorbed under the single name YS—produced an enormous reaction and great unrest. It would give rise to a new disturbance, but that is another story.

Japanese: 就任式の後、廖志明は約束通り街を去り、トーマス・リャオはアイスと共にグランドタワーに住まいを移した。謝亮達が愛人宅で待ち伏せし、脅迫めいたやりとりで統合を決意させたという事実は伏され、一部の者しか知らない。表向きは平和的な説得により廖志明が世代交代を決意したという形だった。経緯が経緯だけに、世間の者達はにわかには信じがたかったが、謝亮就任の集まりにおいて廖志明自信が、後見人として新龍頭に祝福の言葉を述べたことで、その話題は大きくなることはなかった。
English: After the investiture, Liao Chi-ming left the city as promised, and Thomas Liao moved into Grand Tower with Ice. The fact that Leung’s group had ambushed Liao at his mistress’s apartment and coerced his decision through a threat-laden exchange was concealed and known to only a few. The public account held that peaceful persuasion had convinced Liao Chi-ming to accept the generational transition. Given the history between the parties, people found it difficult to believe at first. But when Liao himself attended Leung’s investiture and, as guardian, spoke words of blessing to the new Longtou, the matter attracted no further attention.

Japanese: 「一安心したわ」
English: “What a relief.”

Japanese: 廖が街を去ったあとに、世傑が溜息を漏らしたそうだ。
English: Sai-kit reportedly sighed after Liao left the city.

Japanese: 「小謝、もし彼らが、土壇場で裏切って来たらどうするつもりだったの？　私はかなりの確率で、廖志明が態度を豹変させてもう一波乱起こすと踏んでたんだけど」
English: “Siu Tse, what did you intend to do if they betrayed us at the very last moment? I judged there was a considerable chance that Liao Chi-ming would reverse himself and cause one final disturbance.”

Japanese: それに対し謝亮は、
English: Tse Leung answered.

Japanese: 「そうなったら受けて立つさ。言ったとおり、戦っても勝つつもりはある。……が、僕はもうあれで終わりだと確信はあった。廖は息子の発言で明らかに戦意を喪失していたし、それに、トミーが約束を破るなんて考えられないからね」
English: “Then we would have met them in battle. As I said, I intended to win even if we fought. ...But I was certain the affair had ended. Liao had plainly lost the will to fight after his son spoke. And I cannot imagine Tommy breaking a promise.”

Japanese: 「随分信じてるのね」
English: “You certainly have faith in him.”

Japanese: 「そうとも。僕は本来人を疑うのは嫌いなんだ」
English: “I do. By nature, I dislike doubting people.”

Japanese: 「あきれた」
English: “Unbelievable.”

Japanese: 亮が真顔で言ったため、世傑は何かの冗談なのか、本気で言っているのか判別がつかず、苦い顔をした。
English: Leung spoke with a perfectly serious face. Unable to determine whether the words were a joke or sincere, Sai-kit grimaced.

Japanese: 「色々あったけれども、ああいう特別な場面に居合わせるというのは、なかなか体験出来るものじゃないですねえ」
English: “A great deal happened, but it is not often that one has the opportunity to witness such an extraordinary moment.”

Japanese: 林氏は、赤子をあやしながら言った。
English: Mr. Hayashi spoke while soothing the baby.

Japanese: 先ほどまで家事をしていたはずの彼の細君も、いつの間にかその隣に座って筆者の取材風景を眺めている。
English: His wife, who had apparently been attending to the housework moments earlier, had taken a seat beside him at some point and now watched the author conduct the interview.

Japanese: 彼女はかつてエリカ・ビリンガムという名だった。今は結婚により姓を変えてハヤシエリカと名乗っている。化粧っ気がないにも関わらず、廖志明が夢中になった美貌は衰えを感じさせなかった。
English: She had once been named Erika Billingham. Marriage had changed her surname, and she was now Erika Hayashi. Even without a trace of makeup, she had lost none of the beauty that had so captivated Liao Chi-ming.

Japanese: マンションでの話し合いの後、謝亮は廖志明にエリカの解放を交渉し、彼女は晴れて自由の身となった。林氏と結婚するにあたっては父親の反対などもあり、スムーズには行かなかったそうだが、最終的には彼女を解放するために林氏が命をかけたという事実が後押しした。
English: After the discussion at the apartment, Leung negotiated Erika’s release with Liao Chi-ming, and she regained her freedom. I was told that her father’s opposition made her marriage to Mr. Hayashi anything but smooth. In the end, however, the fact that Hayashi had risked his life to free her helped win her father over.

Japanese: その後YSとのつき合いはなく、小さな喫茶店を営業して真っ当な商売を行っていたそうだが、世間はそうは見ず、なかなか苦労をしたようである。
English: The couple reportedly had no further dealings with YS. They operated a small coffee shop and earned an honest living. Society did not see them that way, however, and it appears that they endured no small hardship.

Japanese: 「珍しいものを見させてもらいましたよ。出来ればもう二度と見たくありませんが」
English: “I was shown something rare indeed. I would prefer never to see it again, if possible.”

Japanese: そう語る林氏には不良少年の境遇から、こうして平和な家庭を築き上げ、順調な人生を作り上げたという自信が見て取れた。
English: To my eyes, Mr. Hayashi spoke with the confidence of a man who had risen from delinquency, built a peaceful family, and set his life upon a secure course.

Japanese: その彼に、筆者は最後の質問をした。
English: The author asked him one final question.

Japanese: YS第三代龍頭謝亮とは、一体どういう人物なのか。
English: What kind of man was Tse Leung, third Longtou of YS?

Japanese: 街で名をはせる不良少年グループのリーダー格でありながら、街と仲間を捨てて東京で大学などに通い、そこで夢中になって研究にのめり込んでいたにもかかわらず、ひょいひょいと帰って来て父の跡を継ぎギャングのボスになる。そしてしまいにはYSの改革とY地区の発展まで宣言してしまう。
English: He had been one of the leaders of a delinquent band notorious throughout the city, only to abandon both city and comrades for a Tokyo university. There he immersed himself passionately in research—yet returned as casually as though he had merely stepped outside, succeeded his father, and became the boss of a gang. In the end, he even proclaimed the reform of YS and the development of Y District.

Japanese: その頃の筆者にはどうにも行動の理念というか、本質のようなものを見つけ出すことが出来ず、謝亮という人物をつかみかねていた。
English: At the time, the author could find no guiding principle behind his actions, nothing that seemed to reveal his essence. The man called Tse Leung remained elusive.

Japanese: 「一言で言うと、彼には感情が欠落していたんでしょうね」
English: “In a word, I suppose certain emotions were missing from him.”

Japanese: 林氏は遠い目になり、
English: Mr. Hayashi gazed into the distance.

Japanese: 「感情がまるっきりないってわけではないんです。笑ったり怒ったりはしていました。でも、もっと複雑な感情……喜怒哀楽で言うところの、喜と哀に関してはまるっきりなかったと思いますね。あいつは世界が光であふれているようにさえ思える満ち足りた気持も、すべてが真っ暗になってしまうような胸が痛むような切なさも、感じたことがないんじゃないでしょうか。だから、我々には行動理念みたいなものはわからず、一貫してないように見える。ただ、彼にだけわかる一貫性はあったんじゃないですかね。欠けた心なりに。それじゃないとあまりにも寂しすぎますから」
English: “I don’t mean that he had no emotions whatsoever. He laughed, and he became angry. But the more complicated feelings... If you divide emotion into joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure, I don’t think he possessed joy or sorrow at all. Perhaps he had never felt the fulfillment that makes the world seem flooded with light, or the aching grief that leaves everything dark. That may be why the rest of us couldn’t understand the principles behind his actions, and why he seemed inconsistent. Still, I imagine there was a consistency that only he understood, even within that incomplete heart. Otherwise, it would be altogether too lonely.”

Japanese: そう言って彼は苦笑する。
English: He gave a wry smile.

Japanese: 「あいつのことを思い出すと、何やら、昆虫のような気がするんですよ。おそろしく頭の良い昆虫。……昆虫は、敵に対して怒ったような反応をとったり、餌を見つけて食べている時など楽しそうに見えたりもしますが、でも幸福を感じたり、悲しみを感じているようには見えないじゃないですか。そういう印象なんです。私にとって、彼は」
English: “When I remember him, I somehow think of an insect. A terrifyingly intelligent insect. ...An insect may react to an enemy as though angry, or appear to enjoy itself when it finds food and eats. But it never looks as though it feels happiness or sorrow, does it? That is the impression he gave me.”

Japanese: そこで林氏は愛娘に口づけをすると、
English: Mr. Hayashi kissed his beloved daughter.

Japanese: 「でも、悪い奴ではなかったですよ。妻を無事救出し、結婚出来たのは菅原のおかげですからね。あいつがいなければ、この娘もいなかった。悪い奴ではないんです。なんだか悪口みたいなことを言ってしまいましたが、私も別にきらいじゃありません。ただちょっと変なヤツだと思うだけで……あっ、こら」
English: “But he wasn’t a bad man. I owe it to Sugawara that I rescued my wife safely and was able to marry her. Without him, this girl would never have existed. He wasn’t a bad man. I realize I’ve made it sound as though I was speaking ill of him, but I don’t dislike him. I only think he was a little strange... Ah, hey!”

Japanese: 彼は、彼の鼻の穴に指を突っ込もうとする赤子の手を、幸せに満ちあふれた笑顔を浮かべながら払いのけた。
English: Smiling with perfect happiness, he brushed away the baby’s hand as she tried to stick a finger up his nose.

Japanese: グランドタワー最上階。龍頭の執務室であるその部屋の窓からは、Y地区の主要な地域を一望することが出来る。
English: The Longtou’s office occupied the top floor of Grand Tower. From its windows, one could look out over all the principal areas of Y District.

Japanese: 滑走路通り、パラシュート通り、暗闇通り……そしてその向こうに広がる森林公園の鬱蒼と茂った木々。その木々の枝葉に隠されて、グレートホールのぽっかりとあいた穴はさすがに見ることは出来ないが。
English: Runway Street, Parachute Street, Darkness Street...and beyond them, the densely wooded expanse of Forest Park. Naturally, the gaping hole of the Great Hole could not be seen, concealed as it was beneath those spreading branches and leaves.

Japanese: 新しく龍頭となった謝亮は、その窓際に立って街を眺めていた。
English: Tse Leung, the new Longtou, stood at the window and gazed down at the city.

Japanese: すると、背後でドアがノックされ、エリー・ホワイトが入って来る。彼女は謝亮による新しい体制でも有力な幹部の一人としての地位を保っており、香港派の重要なビジネスパートナーでもあった。謝亮やその部下達が持つ銃器などの武器は、もっぱら彼女の組織が調達したもので、龍頭に就任するにあたって、YSの組織内での立場とは別の、様々な物品の売買における新たな契約を結んでいる。
English: A knock sounded at the door behind him, and Ellie White entered. She had retained her position as one of the leading officers under Leung’s new regime and remained an important business partner of the Hong Kong faction. Her organization supplied nearly all the firearms and other weapons used by Leung and his subordinates. On taking office as Longtou, he had concluded new contracts with her for trade in a range of goods, separate from her place within YS itself.

Japanese: 「あなたのお父様も、よくその場所に立って街を見下ろしていました」
English: “Your father often stood in that same place and looked down over the city.”

Japanese: エリーに言われると、この若きリーダーはフと鼻で笑う。
English: At Ellie’s words, the young leader gave a soft snort.

Japanese: 「そしてよく、この様な立場につき、こうして街を見下ろしていると、途方もない権力者になったような勘違いをしたくなると笑っておられました」
English: “And he often laughed that standing here in such a position, looking down over the city like this, tempted him to mistake himself for a man of immeasurable power.”

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 「あなたがそうして立っていると、まるでお父様の生き写しのよう」
English: “When you stand there that way, you are the very image of your father.”

Japanese: エリーは亮に歩み寄ると、その頬に触れ、じっと顔を見つめた。間近に見ると、ベールが透けて素顔が見えた。初めて見たその顔は、想像していたよりも若く美しい。そして、憂いに満ちている。
English: Ellie approached Ryo, touched his cheek, and gazed steadily into his face. At such close range, he could see her bare features through the veil. It was the first time he had seen them. She was younger and more beautiful than he had imagined—and full of sorrow.

Japanese: 「きみが僕に初代の面影を求めても、それはむなしいだけのものだ」
English: “Seeking the First Longtou’s image in me will bring you nothing but emptiness.”

Japanese: 「わかっています」
English: “I know.”

Japanese: エリーはそう呟くと亮に顔を近づけ、その唇を触れ合わせた。
English: Murmuring those words, Ellie brought her face close to Ryo’s and pressed her lips to his.

Japanese: 亮は避けるそぶりも、かといって積極的になるでもなく、ただ静かに父の愛人だったと言われている女のなすことを受け入れている。その表情は茫漠としてとらえにくく、いかなる感情も映し出さず、人間観察に優れたものであっても、彼のいまの心情をうかがい知ることは出来なかったであろう。
English: Ryo made no move to avoid her, but neither did he respond. He simply stood still and accepted the kiss from the woman said to have been his father’s lover. His expression was so vague and distant as to defy interpretation, betraying no emotion; even a keen observer of human nature could not have divined what he felt at that moment.

Japanese: エリーは顔を離すと、再び亮の顔を見つめ、何か言おうとし、しかし言葉は出ずにかわりに涙がその目の端から流れ落ちた。
English: Ellie drew back and looked into Ryo’s face once more. She tried to say something, but no words came. Tears ran instead from the corners of her eyes.

Japanese: 「うっ」
表情が泣き顔に歪み、嗚咽が漏れそうになる口元を抑える。
English: Her face twisted with grief, and she covered her mouth to stifle the sob threatening to escape.

Japanese: 「ミス・ホワイトがそんな安っぽいことをするべきではない。僕は見なかったことにするよ」
English: “Miss White should not cheapen herself this way. I will pretend I saw nothing.”

Japanese: 「ありがとうございます」
English: “Thank you.”

Japanese: エリーはそのまま足早に部屋を立ち去って行く。
English: Ellie hurried from the room without another word.

Japanese: エリー・ホワイトと言えば他のギャングのボスや、様々な男達と対等に渡り合う辣腕で知られている。それが、このような姿を見せることがあるとは、誰も想像がつかないに違いない。
English: Ellie White was renowned as a formidable woman, one who dealt with gang bosses and every sort of man on equal terms. No one could possibly have imagined her revealing herself this way.

Japanese: 亮は深いため息をつき、執務室の椅子に腰掛けた。これも、初代が残し、愛用した椅子である。
English: Ryo released a deep sigh and sat in the office chair. This, too, had been left behind by the First Longtou, who had used it often.

Japanese: 執務室の家具は先だってのタイプA少女の襲撃によっていくつか損なわれたが、似たようなものが調達され、同じ場所に配置されていた。誰の指図でそうなったのかしらないが、初代の作り上げたものはそのまま手つかずで残すというのがYSの、いや香港派の不文律のようなものになっている。
English: Some of the furniture had been damaged in the recent attack by the Type A girl, but similar pieces had been procured and set in the same places. Ryo did not know who had ordered it done, but preserving everything the First Longtou had created—even the arrangement of this room—had become a kind of unwritten law in YS, or at least in its Hong Kong faction.

Japanese: さらに、部屋にはジェフリー・ウォンが持ち込んだコーヒーを作るための本格的な道具も、少女の襲撃を生き残って設置されたままだった。いつのまにかすっかりYSの一員となってしまったレイレイが、行き届いた清掃によって執務室の清潔感を保っており、コーヒー道具のケースはホコリ一つなくピカピカに拭かれていたが、ジェフリーが死んで以来使うものはいなかった。
English: The room also still held the professional coffee equipment Jeffrey Wong had brought in, which had survived the girl’s attack. Leilei, who had somehow become a full-fledged member of YS, kept the office immaculate with her painstaking cleaning. The case containing the coffee equipment had been polished until it shone without a speck of dust, but no one had used it since Jeffrey died.

Japanese: そうした、死者達の持ち込んだ物が並ぶ部屋の真ん中で、謝亮が佇んでいる。
English: Tse Leung stood amid a room filled with the things the dead had brought into it.

Japanese: どことなくメランコリックに見えるうつろな表情だった。晴れて龍頭となり、ライバルであった廖ファミリーを吸収し、このY地区においてかつてないほどの強大な権力を手に入れつつある彼が、これほどつまらなそうな顔をして居るのは、部下が見たら不思議に思えるだろう。
English: His vacant expression looked vaguely melancholic. Now formally installed as Longtou, he was absorbing the rival Liao Family and acquiring power unprecedented in Y District. Any subordinate who saw him wearing such a profoundly bored expression would have found it strange.

Japanese: 「ふわぁ」
English: “Hwaaah...”

Japanese: 亮はひとつあくびをして、そしてそのまま覆い被さるように机に伏せると、寝息を立て始めた。
English: Ryo yawned once, collapsed forward over the desk, and immediately began breathing softly in sleep.

Japanese: 寝付いてすぐに、目の前の電話がけたたましい呼び出し音を立てる。
English: He had only just drifted off when the telephone before him rang shrilly.

Japanese: 亮は起きず、呼び出し音は一分ほど続いてから切れ、もう一度鳴ったがやはりとられることはなく、しまいには部下が直接部屋に入ってきた。
English: Ryo did not wake. The ringing continued for about a minute before stopping, then began again and went unanswered once more. At last, a subordinate came into the room in person.

Japanese: 「龍頭」
English: “Longtou.”

Japanese: 何度呼びかけても亮は起きず、耳元で大きな声で呼んでも起きなかったため、
English: Ryo failed to wake no matter how many times the subordinate called to him, even when he raised his voice beside Ryo’s ear.

Japanese: 「失礼します」
English: “Excuse me.”

Japanese: 揺すっても、すぐには目を覚まさない。心配になった部下が安否を確認するため、手首をとって脈を調べようとしたところで、やっと亮の目が開いた。
English: Even shaking him did not wake him at once. Growing concerned, the subordinate took his wrist to check his pulse—and only then did Ryo’s eyes finally open.

Japanese: 「すまない。うたた寝をしてしまった」
English: “Sorry. I dozed off.”

Japanese: 寝ぼけまなこのままそう言う亮に、
English: Ryo spoke while still bleary-eyed with sleep.

Japanese: 「出発の準備が出来ました」
English: “Everything is ready for your departure.”

Japanese: と、部下は言う。
English: The subordinate relayed the message.

Japanese: 「わかった。すぐ行く」
English: “All right. I’ll be there at once.”

Japanese: 亮はふらつく身体で立ち上がると、机の引き出しにしまっていた自分の携帯電話を取りだした。
English: Ryo rose unsteadily and took his cell phone from a desk drawer.

Japanese: 知らぬ間に着信をしていたらしく、通知の表示が画面に出ている。電話をかけてきたのは汐健慈朗。
English: A notification on the screen showed a call he had missed. The caller was Shio Kenjiro.

Japanese: 彼は無表情のまましばらくその名前を見つめてから、それをポケットにしまった。
English: He stared at the name for a while without expression, then put the phone in his pocket.

Japanese: 亮が向かったのは、滑走路通りの一角にある中華料理店「うまかしゅか」。文字をあてれば「馬家酒家」となるのだろう。馬明が経営する飲食店で、美食家である彼の趣味と実益をかねたサイドビジネスであった。
English: Ryo’s destination was Umakashuka, a Chinese restaurant on one corner of Runway Street. Its name would presumably be written with the characters for Ma Family Restaurant. Ma Ming owned the place as a side business combining the epicure’s pleasures with profit.

Japanese: モダンアートを思わせる黒を基調としたシックで現代的な建物の、正面にある扉には臨時休業を伝える張り紙が貼ってある。
English: A notice of temporary closure hung on the front door of its sleek, contemporary black building, reminiscent of a work of modern art.

Japanese: 黒服の部下がその扉を開けると、亮はコートのポケットに手を突っ込んだまま店内に足を踏み入れる。
English: A subordinate in a black suit opened the door, and Ryo entered with his hands thrust into the pockets of his coat.

Japanese: 店舗の地下は広めの貯蔵庫になっており、業務用冷蔵庫や、各種の棚が所狭しと並べられている。部屋の中央は少し広い作業場になっていて、そこで運び込まれた食材の荷ほどきや仕分けを行うのだが、いまはその作業台は取り払われ、かわりに一つ椅子が置かれ、そして一人の男がロープで縛り付けられていた。
English: The restaurant’s basement was a large storeroom crowded with commercial refrigerators and shelves of every kind. A somewhat broader work area in the center was ordinarily used to unpack and sort delivered ingredients. Today, its worktable had been removed. In its place stood a single chair, with a man bound to it by ropes.

Japanese: 身体には無数の打撲痕があり、土汚れが付着している。顔も同様に暴力の痕跡があり、まぶたは青黒く腫れて目を圧迫し、唇はふくれあがってその端が切れ、赤い血を滴らせている。
English: His body was covered in bruises and smeared with dirt. His face bore the same marks of violence: eyelids swollen blue-black until his eyes were nearly shut, lips bloated and split at one corner, dripping bright red blood.

Japanese: 全体的に凄惨な姿であったが、中でも目を引くのは、肘掛けに縛り付けられてた両腕だった。
English: The sight was gruesome in every respect, but most conspicuous were the arms lashed to the chair’s armrests.

Japanese: 右手はすべての指が切り落とされ、左手も、親指が切断されている。その傍らには血で濡れた中華包丁を持った部下が立っており、その足元には血まみれの指が散らばり、奇妙な芋虫のようであった。
English: Every finger had been cut from his right hand, and the thumb from his left. Beside him stood a subordinate holding a cleaver wet with blood. Severed fingers lay scattered at the man’s feet like strange caterpillars.

Japanese: 「吐いたか？」
English: “Did he talk?”

Japanese: 部屋に降りてきた亮は、その若者の姿に眉一つ動かさない。残虐行為が行われている場にそぐわない日常的な調子で、そのギラギラと光る丸い目で若者を眺めていた馬明に尋ねる。
English: Ryo had descended into the room without so much as raising an eyebrow at the young man’s condition. In a casual tone wholly out of place amid such brutality, he addressed Ma Ming, who watched the captive with round eyes gleaming brightly.

Japanese: 「吐いたとも。小謝の言う通りだった。まったく愚かしいやつらだ」
English: “He talked. You were right, Siu Tse. They really were fools.”

Japanese: 馬明は苦々しげに言った。
English: Ma Ming spoke bitterly.

Japanese: 男は謝浩俊という三十二才の人物であった。その姓から分かるとおり、謝亮とは親戚筋にあたり、旧義勝グループでは古く有力な家系だ。父の謝超亜は旧義勝の重鎮の一人である。
English: The man was Tse Ho-chun, thirty-two years old. As his surname indicated, he was a relative of Tse Leung and belonged to an old, powerful family within the former Yisheng group. His father, Tse Chiu-a, was one of that organization’s leading figures.

Japanese: この浩俊は、亮が龍頭となって二日後に仲間に対してメールを送った。
English: Two days after Ryo became Longtou, Ho-chun had sent a message to his associates.

Japanese: そこでは『にっくき客家人と手を組んだ謝亮は我らのリーダーではない』と宣言されており、亮を殺し、それにとってかわって別のリーダーを立てようというような呼びかけがされていた。
English: It declared, ‘Tse Leung, who has joined hands with the hated Hakka, is no leader of ours,’ and called upon them to kill Ryo and install another leader in his place.

Japanese: もちろんこれは許されることではなく、彼は昨夜自宅のマンションで世傑達に拘束され、このような状況に置かれることとなった。
English: Naturally, this could not be permitted. Sai-kit and his men had seized him at his apartment the previous night, and thus he found himself here.

Japanese: 「つまり、今回の件は父の超亜も協力しているということでいいんだね？」
English: “Then my understanding is that your father, Chiu-a, also cooperated in this affair. Is that correct?”

Japanese: 亮は浩俊に呼びかけるが、彼はうつむいて荒い呼吸をするだけで反応を示さない。
English: Ryo addressed Ho-chun, but the man only hung his head and breathed raggedly, offering no response.

Japanese: 亮と彼はさほど親しいわけでもないが、幼い頃から何度か顔を合わせてはいる。亮が七才の時に彼は十七才で、遊ばなくなったゲームソフトを何本か譲ってくれた思い出があった。
English: Ryo had never been particularly close to him, though they had met several times since childhood. When Ryo was seven and Ho-chun seventeen, the older boy had given him several video games he no longer played.

Japanese: 「超亜に関しても、既に捕縛の手配をしている。世傑もそちらへ向かった」
English: “Arrangements have already been made to capture Chiu-a as well. Sai-kit went there himself.”

Japanese: 何も言わない囚われの男のかわりに、馬明が口を開いた。
English: Ma Ming spoke in place of the silent captive.

Japanese: 「ご苦労」
English: “Good work.”

Japanese: 亮は懐に手を入れると、拳銃を取り出した。廖志明を撃つのにも使用した、あの音のしない銃である。
English: Ryo reached inside his coat and drew a pistol—the same soundless gun he had used to shoot Liao Chi-ming.

Japanese: 「あんたは不適切な考えを持ったが、指を六本落とされるまで口を開かなかった忍耐力には敬意を表する。本来ならば反逆者は生きたまま切り刻むというのが我々の掟だけれど、特別に楽に死なせよう。最後に何か言い残すことはあるかい？」
English: “Your ideas were ill-advised, but I respect the endurance that kept you silent until they cut off six of your fingers. Our law ordinarily demands that traitors be carved apart alive, but I will make an exception and grant you an easy death. Do you have any last words?”

Japanese: 浩俊は顔を上げ、膨れたまぶたに押しつぶされて細くなった目で亮を見る。
English: Ho-chun raised his face and looked at Ryo through the narrow slits left by his swollen eyelids.

Japanese: 「思い上がるな。……生まれる家さえ違えば、お前とおれの立場は逆だった……」
English: “Don’t get above yourself. ...If we had only been born into different families, you and I would have traded places...”

Japanese: かすれた声でそう言った。
English: His voice was hoarse.

Japanese: 「そんな感情的に物事を考えるから、こんな無茶な計画を立てて、死ぬことになるんだよ。聞かなかったことにしてやるから、もう少しマシなことを言った方が良い。あんたの妻と子に伝えよう」
English: “It is because you let emotion govern your thinking that you devised this reckless plan and wound up about to die. I will pretend I didn’t hear that, so say something better. I’ll deliver it to your wife and child.”

Japanese: そう言って次の言葉を待ったが、相手はまた顔を伏せ、与えられた機会を拒絶した。
English: He waited for the man’s next words, but Ho-chun lowered his face once more, rejecting the opportunity he had been offered.

Japanese: 亮は溜息をついてから、浩俊の頭にさっと銃口で狙いを付けると、ためらいもなくあっさりと引き金を引く。浩俊は頭から血を吹いて絶命をする。
English: Ryo sighed, swiftly trained the muzzle on Ho-chun’s head, and pulled the trigger without hesitation or ceremony. Blood burst from Ho-chun’s head, and he died instantly.

Japanese: 馬明が合図をすると、部下達があらわれ、部屋の後片付けをはじめた。浩俊の遺体を黒いファスナー付きの袋にいれ、床についた血を拭い、切断された指や、銃弾によってはじき飛んだ肉や骨のかけらはちりとりに集められてゴミ袋へ捨てられた。
English: At a signal from Ma Ming, subordinates appeared and began to clean the room. They placed Ho-chun’s body in a black zippered bag, wiped the blood from the floor, and swept the severed fingers and fragments of flesh and bone blown free by the bullet into a dustpan, then emptied it into a garbage bag.

Japanese: 「思ったより早く蹴りがついた。いまから仕込みをすれば、夜からの営業開始に間に合うぞ」
English: “That settled matters sooner than I expected. If we begin the preparations now, we can open for dinner.”

Japanese: 馬明は自ら椅子や作業台の位置を戻しながら、そう言った。
English: Ma Ming spoke while personally restoring the chair and worktable to their proper places.

Japanese: 「……しかし、どうしてこんな愚かな計画を立てたのか。たとえ小謝を殺せたとしても、その後どうにかなるわけでもあるまいに」
English: “...Still, why did they devise such a foolish plan? Even if they managed to kill you, Siu Tse, they could hardly have expected matters to go their way afterward.”

Japanese: 「浩俊が仲間に送った文面の通りの理由だよ。僕が客家人たちを受け入れたのが気にいらなかったのさ」
English: “The reason is precisely what Ho-chun wrote in his message. He resented my acceptance of the Hakka.”

Japanese: 亮は片隅の蛇口で、手をジャブジャブと洗いながらそう答える。
English: Ryo answered while vigorously washing his hands at a faucet in one corner.

Japanese: 「どうも、言葉通りだとは思えない。だって、彼らはそういうタイプではなかったろう」
English: “I find it difficult to believe he truly meant that. They were never that sort, were they?”

Japanese: 旧義勝のなかには、ほとんど宗教的といっていいほどに他地域の出身者を憎み、普段から嫌悪感をあらわにしている連中がいるが、謝超亜・浩俊の親子はかつてそういったそぶりを見せなかった。
English: Some members of the former Yisheng harbored an almost religious hatred of people from other regions and openly displayed their disgust as a matter of course. Tse Chiu-a and Ho-chun, however, had never behaved that way in the past.

Japanese: 「言わなかっただけで、実際は切実な問題があったんだ。単純に言えば、彼らは客家人に対して借金がある」
English: “They simply never said it aloud. In reality, they faced a pressing problem. Put simply, they owed money to Hakka creditors.”

Japanese: 親子はかつて飲食店にボディガード代などを支払わせて自分達の収入にしていたが、最近はうまくいかず、経済状態が逼迫している。そこで自分達で商売を行おうとしたところことごとく失敗し、負債だけが残った。
English: Father and son had once extorted protection money and similar payments from restaurants for their income. Lately, that business had gone poorly and their financial circumstances had grown desperate. They attempted to establish businesses of their own, failed at every one, and were left with nothing but debt.

Japanese: 彼らはギャングとしての本領を発揮し、支払いを拒絶したが、困った業者は債権を売った。
English: They put their talents as gangsters to use by refusing to pay. The businesses they had left unpaid responded by selling the debts.

Japanese: 「そこで債権を買ったのが、客家人の金貸しだってわけさ」
English: “And the buyers were Hakka moneylenders.”

Japanese: 親子はその後も支払いを拒否し続けた。そして、客家人たちも龍頭の親戚である親子との面倒をさけ、いままで大事にすることなくやって来た。
English: Father and son continued to refuse payment afterward. The Hakka, for their part, wished to avoid trouble with relatives of the Longtou and had allowed the matter to rest without making an issue of it.

Japanese: が、客家人がこれからは同じ組織の同志となり、廖志明が謝亮の後見人となってしまった以上、このような関係を続けることは出来ない。
English: But now that the Hakka would become comrades within the same organization and Liao Chi-ming had become Tse Leung’s guardian, that relationship could not continue.

Japanese: 旧義勝の掟では、仲間同士での取引は契約通りに公平に行わなければいけないことになっており、そして謝亮は、今後は客家人も香港人と全くおなじ扱いをすると公言したのだ。
English: The laws of the old Yisheng required all transactions between comrades to be conducted fairly and according to contract. And Tse Leung had publicly declared that the Hakka would henceforth receive precisely the same treatment as the Hong Kongers.

Japanese: 掟通り借金を返せば親子の経済が立ちゆかなくなるし、返さなければ組織の掟に従って処罰される。どちらでも絶体絶命だ。
English: Repaying the debt as the law required would ruin the family’s finances; refusing would bring punishment under that same law. Either way, they were trapped.

Japanese: 「だから客家人を受け入れるわけにはいかなかった。追放し、出来ればその後で客家人と戦争したかったのかもしれないね。そうすれば借金はチャラになる」
English: “That was why they could not permit the Hakka to join us. They may have hoped to drive them out, then go to war against them if possible. The war would have wiped the debt clean.”

Japanese: 「なるほど。……しかし、早い段階で察知出来て良かったな。気づかなければ、もっと同調者が増えて、大騒ぎになっていたかもしれん。客家人を受け入れたくない人間は多いからな。正直言って、おれだって素直に納得が出来たわけではないんだぞ。ジェフリーのこともあるしな。……まったく、よくもまあ大事になるまえに火種を消せたものだ」
English: “I see. ...But it is fortunate we detected them so soon. If we had not, they might have gained more sympathizers and caused a great disturbance. There are many who do not want the Hakka among us. To be honest, I haven’t accepted it without reservations myself, especially after what happened to Jeffrey. ...But somehow, you extinguished the spark before it became a fire.”

Japanese: 馬明はしきりに危機的状況だったことを強調する。
English: Ma Ming repeatedly emphasized how dangerous the situation had been.

Japanese: それに対し、亮は何も言わなかった。
English: Ryo said nothing in reply.

Japanese: しかし、実際のところ彼は今回の親子の裏切りは予想していた。事前に監視も強化しており、早い段階で発見されるのは当然のことだったのだ。
English: In truth, however, he had anticipated the betrayal by father and son. He had strengthened surveillance in advance, so the plot’s early discovery was only to be expected.

Japanese: 亮は組織に加入が決まった直後、補佐としての仕事をジェフリーに任せっきりにして、頻繁に旧義勝の人たちと会い、その帳簿を提出させてまで情報収集をした。それは現在も継続して行っており、香港人たちの金の流れや、置かれている状況については誰よりも熟知している。
English: Immediately after it was decided he would join the organization, Ryo had left nearly all of his formal duties as an aide for Jeffrey to handle and met frequently with members of old Yisheng, going so far as to make them submit their account books while he gathered information. That effort continued even now. No one knew the flow of money among the Hong Kongers or the circumstances in which they found themselves better than he did.

Japanese: こうなった場合に謝親子が裏切るというのは、彼ら自身がそれを思いつくよりも先に、亮には予想出来たことだったのだ。驚くべきことは何もない。
English: Ryo had foreseen that Chiu-a and his son would betray him under these circumstances before the men themselves conceived the idea. There was nothing in it to surprise him.

Japanese: 一方馬明は純粋に驚いているのだが、彼に対して亮はそうした種明かしを何もせず、
English: Ma Ming, on the other hand, was genuinely surprised. Ryo offered him none of that explanation.

Japanese: 「まあ、僕にはわかっていたんだよ」
English: “Well, I knew.”

Japanese: めんどくさそうに言うと、洗い終わった自分の手のにおいを嗅ぎ、
English: He answered as though the whole matter were a nuisance, then lifted his freshly washed hands to his nose.

Japanese: 「まだ硝煙の匂いがする」
English: “They still smell of gunpowder.”

Japanese: と顔を顰めた。
English: He grimaced.

Japanese: 「兄貴はタイプAで、壁の向こうを見通す特別の目があった。息子のお前はノーマルで何の超能力もないが、父と同じように人には見えないものを見通す力があるようだ」
English: “Your father was a Type A, with special eyes that saw through walls. You, his son, are a Normal without a single psychic power, yet it appears you share his gift for seeing what no one else can.”

Japanese: 馬明は濡れた手をぼんやり見つめている亮にタオルを手渡す。
English: Ma Ming handed a towel to Ryo, who was staring absently at his wet hands.

Japanese: 「そんなんじゃないさ。僕は普通のことしかできない。ただ妥当なものを積み重ねてるだけだよ。僕に言わせればみなが目の前のものさえ見てない……いや、見ようとしないだけなんだ。まともな相手が出て来たら僕も苦戦するだろう」
English: “It is nothing of the kind. I can only do ordinary things. I merely build one reasonable conclusion upon another. As I see it, everyone else fails to notice what lies before their eyes... No, they refuse to look. If I ever face a competent opponent, I will struggle too.”

Japanese: 「いやあ、そうじゃないだろう」
English: “No, that cannot be all.”

Japanese: 馬明は感心したように溜息をついた。
English: Ma Ming sighed in admiration.

Japanese: 「しかし、廖志明を屈服させるなんて想像も出来なかった。殺すしか解決法がないと思っていたのに、実質完全なかたちで敗北させることが出来たなんて。……やっぱりお前はおれが見込んだとおり、才能がある。あの変態馬鹿息子までも、大人しく従っているじゃないか。あいつがここまで何も問題を起こさないなんて想像出来なかったことだ。もっとも、あいつを信じてはいかんぞ。何を考えているかわからんやつで、裏切りはお手の物だからな」
English: “Still, I never imagined you could bring Liao Chi-ming to heel. I thought killing him was the only solution, yet you defeated him completely in every practical respect. ...Just as I believed, you have talent. Even that perverted idiot son of mine is behaving himself and obeying you. I never imagined he could go so long without causing trouble. Do not trust him, mind you. No one can tell what he is thinking, and betrayal is second nature to him.”

Japanese: 馬明は息子の世傑に対してはいつも手厳しい。
English: Ma Ming was invariably severe toward his son, Sai-kit.

Japanese: 「裏切りで死ぬようなら、それは僕の考えが足りなかったというだけのことさ」
English: “If a betrayal kills me, it will only mean I failed to think far enough.”

Japanese: 「ふん、素直じゃないな。まあいい、おれはとにかく、お前がその気になってくれてうれしいぞ。あれだけ、ギャングはくだらないと馬鹿にしてたお前が、こんなに真剣に仕事に取り組むとはな」
English: “Hmph. You can never be honest with yourself. Never mind. I am simply glad you have finally chosen to take this seriously. After all the contempt you showed us, calling gangsters ridiculous, I never thought you would devote yourself to the work this earnestly.”

Japanese: 「いまだってべつに好きじゃないさ。こんな野蛮な世界」
English: “I still don’t like it. This barbaric world.”

Japanese: 亮は目を細め、どこかうつろな表情を一瞬見せると、それを打ち消すように笑い、
English: Ryo narrowed his eyes. A hollow expression crossed his face for a moment, then he smiled as though to erase it.

Japanese: 「ただ、やるからには最低限の仕事くらいは果たしたいだけだよ。僕はなんだっていつだってそうさ」
English: “But if I am to do it, I want to do at least the bare minimum the job requires. That is how I have always approached everything.”

Japanese: 「ねえ見て、トミー。あと一週間くらいで生まれるんだって。もう出て来る寸前なのよ？」
English: “Look, Tommy. They say the baby will be born in about a week. It’s nearly ready to come out.”

Japanese: 馬美美は幸福に満ちた笑顔を浮かべて、はちきれんばかりにふくれた腹をさすった。
English: Ma Meimei rubbed her belly, swollen almost to bursting, with a smile full of happiness.

Japanese: 「わあ、すごいねえ！　でも信じられないな。美美が本当にお母さんになっちゃうなんて」
English: “Wow, that’s incredible! I still can’t believe you’re truly about to become a mother, Meimei.”

Japanese: トーマス・リャオは母となる喜びを素直に分かち合うような笑顔を浮かべる。
English: Thomas smiled, sharing her happiness at becoming a mother without reservation.

Japanese: 「ねえ、触ってみてよ。なかで赤ちゃんが動くのわかるのよ」
English: “Here, touch it. You can feel the baby moving inside.”

Japanese: 「え、あっ、そんなっ……」
English: “What? Ah, I couldn’t possibly...”

Japanese: 美美が手を取ると、トーマスは露骨にうろたえる。
English: When Meimei took his hand, Thomas became visibly flustered.

Japanese: 「何赤くなってるの？」
English: “Why are you blushing?”

Japanese: 「だって、そんな、女の人のお腹にさわるなんて」
English: “Because—touching a woman’s stomach like that...”

Japanese: 「あら、変に意識しちゃって。いやらしいわねえ。あ、私、おっぱいも大きくなったのよ。こっち触ってみる？」
English: “Oh, you’re making it strange all by yourself. What a dirty mind. My breasts have grown too, you know. Would you like to touch those instead?”

Japanese: 「うう、僕をばかにして。……ねえ聞いてよ。小謝、美美の赤ちゃん、もうすぐ生まれるんだって」
English: “Ooh, don’t make fun of me. ...Listen, Siu Tse. Meimei says her baby is almost here.”

Japanese: トーマスは困って遠くの謝亮に助けを求めるが、
English: At a loss, Thomas appealed for help to Ryo, sitting some distance away.

Japanese: 「そりゃよかった」
English: “That’s good.”

Japanese: 亮は椅子に腰掛けたまま茶を飲むだけで、立ち上がろうともしない。
English: Ryo merely drank his tea without rising from his chair.

Japanese: 彼が飲んでいるのは最近美美が健康のために取り寄せているというマコモを使ったお茶で、身体にはいいのかもしれないが飲みにくくて仕方がない。
English: It was tea made from makomo, which Meimei had recently begun ordering for its supposed health benefits. It might be good for him, but it was almost impossible to drink.

Japanese: 渋い顔で、少しずつ喉の奥に流し込んでいる。
English: With a sour expression, he poured it little by little down his throat.

Japanese: 『うまかしゅか』の地下での出来事のあと、馬明に誘われてこの家にやって来たのがまずかった。その庭ではなぜか美美とトーマスが茶を飲んで話し込んでおり、その上馬明は急用が入って出かけていったので、なし崩し的に美美たちに合流することとなる。
English: Coming to this house at Ma Ming’s invitation after the incident in Umakashuka’s basement had been a mistake. For some reason, Meimei and Thomas were already sitting in the garden deep in conversation over tea. Then urgent business called Ma Ming away, and Ryo found himself swept into joining them by default.

Japanese: 一応龍頭である自分を置き去りにして私用で出かけるなどふざけていると、亮は馬明に対して思ってみたりもした。
English: Ryo did find himself thinking that Ma Ming had some nerve abandoning him—the Longtou, after all—and running off on private business.

Japanese: それにしても、亮からすれば、いくら客家人と和解が成立したとはいえ、経緯を考えれば複雑なものがあってしかるべきだろう。正確な経緯を知らない美美はともかく、トーマスの頭にもそのあたりの葛藤はないようなのが理解しがたい。
English: More puzzling to him was Thomas. Whatever reconciliation had been reached with the Hakka, the history between them ought to have left him with complicated feelings. Meimei did not know the full course of events, but Thomas showed no sign that such conflict had even entered his mind.

Japanese: 亮とて彼に私利私欲が薄いのは理解していたが、父親が負傷してもその姿勢を崩さないというのは、一種の狂人ではないのか。
English: Ryo understood that the man possessed little self-interest, but to maintain that attitude even after his father was wounded—did that not make him a kind of madman?

Japanese: ――いや、僕はどうも言葉が悪い。聖人とか、道徳者と言い直すべきか。
English: —No, my choice of words is poor. I ought to call him a saint, or a virtuous man.

Japanese: トーマスと美美のやりとりを眺めながら亮はそんなことを考えている。
English: Ryo entertained these thoughts as he watched the exchange between Thomas and Meimei.

Japanese: 「トミー、そんなので大丈夫なの？　あなたもえらくなったのにねえ。まったく、あなたがお父さんの跡を継いだなんて、とても信じられない」
English: “Are you sure you’re up to this, Tommy? You’ve become such an important man yourself. I still can’t believe you took over from your father.”

Japanese: 「僕も信じられないよ。でも、さっきも言ったようにね、やるからには恥ずかしくないリーダーになろうと思う。僕らはこに日本の法的には良くない存在かもしれないけれど、世間的には街にいる沢山の移民やミュータント達自体が良くない存在って言われてるんだ。彼らの代表者として、そして部下やYSのみんなの幸せのためにも、僕は必要なことをしなくちゃいけない」
English: “Neither can I. But as I was saying, if I am to do it, I intend to become a leader I needn’t be ashamed of. Our very existence here in Japan may not be acceptable under the law, but society treats the many immigrants and mutants living in this city as though their existence were unacceptable too. As their representative—and for the happiness of my subordinates and everyone in YS—I must do what needs to be done.”

Japanese: トミーは自分の言葉に、真顔でこくこくと頷く。
English: Tommy nodded gravely along with his own words.

Japanese: 「そうだよね、小謝……いや、龍頭」
English: “Isn’t that right, Siu Tse...? No, Longtou.”

Japanese: 「どうだろうね」
English: “Who can say?”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめる。
English: Ryo shrugged.

Japanese: 「バカねトミー。小謝は、こういうところで仕事の話はしたくないのよ」
English: “Don’t be silly, Tommy. Siu Tse doesn’t want to discuss work in a place like this.”

Japanese: 「べつにそういうわけでもないけどさ。……それより、今日は二人だけで何を話し込んでいたんだ？」
English: “It isn’t that. ...More importantly, what were the two of you discussing here alone today?”

Japanese: 「……ちょっと、人生についての深い話をね」
English: “...The deeper questions of life.”

Japanese: トーマスが格好をつけてそう言うと、
English: Thomas attempted to deliver the words with dignity.

Japanese: 「安心しなさいよ。不適切なことはなにもないから」
English: “You can relax. Nothing improper happened.”

Japanese: それを台無しにするように、美美が冗談を言う。
English: Meimei ruined the effect with a joke.

Japanese: 「あ、当たり前だよ！　いい旦那さんがいて、これから子供が生まれるっていうのにそんな……」
English: “O-of course not! You have a wonderful husband, and you’re about to have his child, so I would never...”

Japanese: トーマスがしどろもどろになったところで、美美は使用人に呼ばれ、部屋を出て行った。
English: While Thomas floundered for words, a servant summoned Meimei and she left the room.

Japanese: そして、トーマスと二人、その場に取り残される。
English: That left Ryo there alone with Thomas.

Japanese: 第三代龍頭と、客家人リーダーとして二人きりになるのは、これが初めての機会であった。
English: It was their first opportunity to meet privately as the third Longtou and the leader of the Hakka.

Japanese: 「まったく困っちゃうよ。彼女ったらあんなことばかり言って」
English: “She is impossible. Always saying things like that.”

Japanese: トーマスは溜息をつく、
English: Thomas sighed.

Japanese: 「でも、真面目な話をするとねえ、小謝。僕は、この立場でどうしたらいいのか、それですごく悩んでいるんだよ。だから考えることが多くて……」
English: “But to speak seriously, Siu Tse, I am terribly uncertain about what I ought to do in this position. It leaves me with so much to think about...”

Japanese: そして神妙な顔でそう切り出した。
English: His expression grew solemn as he began.

Japanese: 「この街を変えなくちゃいけないとは、すごく前から思ってるんだけど、あちこちに問題ばかりでどう解決したらいいのか……そうだ、小謝は知ってる？」
English: “I’ve believed for a very long time that this city must change, but there are problems in every direction, and I don’t know how to solve them... Oh, Siu Tse, have you heard?”

Japanese: 「何を」
English: “Heard what?”

Japanese: 「この街には、タイプBの人たちの地下組織があるんだってね。三人のお爺さんがリーダーを率いて、街のいろんなタイプBの人たちが隠れて所属している……」
English: “Apparently, there is an underground organization of Type Bs in this city, headed by three old men, with Type Bs all across the city belonging to it in secret...”

Japanese: 「『老人達』のことか」
English: “You mean the ‘Elders’?”

Japanese: 「そう。僕の部下の言うところによるとね、彼らの活動がね、最近活発なんだって」
English: “Yes. According to my subordinates, their activity has increased recently.”

Japanese: 「どういうこと？」
English: “In what way?”

Japanese: 「あ、小謝も知らなかったんだ。うれしいなあ。小謝より僕のほうが詳しいことがあるなんて」
English: “Oh, so even you didn’t know, Siu Tse. How wonderful. To think I know something you don’t.”

Japanese: 「さっさと話せよ」
English: “Get on with it.”

Japanese: 亮が眉間にしわを寄せてうながすと、
English: Ryo frowned and prompted him to continue.

Japanese: 「う、うん」
English: “Y-yes.”

Japanese: トミーは咳払いをして、
English: Tommy cleared his throat.

Japanese: 「彼らは知っての通り、この街で唯一麻薬を売り買いしている組織だけれど、新しい薬を盛大に売り出し始めたらしいんだ。なんでも、タイプBにとって特別な効き目があるという……」
English: “As you know, theirs is the only organization buying and selling narcotics in this city. Apparently, they’ve begun aggressively marketing a new drug—one said to have a special effect upon Type Bs...”

Japanese: 「タイプBにって……『ローズ』みたいな？」
English: “For Type Bs...? Like Rose?”

Japanese: 新しい薬と聞いて、亮の目つきがにわかに鋭くなる。
English: At the words ‘new drug,’ Ryo’s eyes abruptly sharpened.

Japanese: 「いや、それを改良した新しい薬で、なんでも『ネオ・ローズ』というらしい」
English: “No. It is said to be a new, improved form of Rose. I hear they call it ‘Neo Rose.’”

Japanese: 「まさか、いや、そんな筈は……」
English: “It can’t be. No, that isn’t possible...”

Japanese: 「知ってるの？」
English: “You’ve heard of it?”

Japanese: 「噂ではね。それが本物ならば、確かにタイプBの人生を変えうる薬だ。タイプBの発作を抑え、その優れた能力だけを生かすことが出来る。副作用も少ない。タイプBにとっては夢の薬だよ。が、夢は夢のまま、実在しないと考えた方がいい。世間でネオ・ローズといって売り出しているのは、大抵ローズに混ぜ物をしたまがい物だよ。今回もきっとそうだろう。『老人達』も、あこぎな商売に乗り出したものだね」
English: “Only from rumors. If it were genuine, it could certainly change the lives of Type Bs. It is said to suppress their episodes, allowing them to retain only their enhanced abilities, and to have few side effects. For a Type B, it would be a dream drug. But it is wisest to assume that dream remains a dream and the drug does not exist. Nearly everything sold on the streets as Neo Rose is adulterated Rose, a counterfeit. I expect the same is true this time. It seems the ‘Elders’ have entered a particularly crooked line of business.”

Japanese: 「偽物なのかな？　巷では本当によく効くって噂をきくけど……」
English: “You believe it’s counterfeit? The rumors on the street say it works remarkably well...”

Japanese: 「完全に否定はしないけど、十中八九ありえないな。ただ、そうやっておおっぴらに商売を始めたというのは興味深い。彼らはこの街で麻薬利権を独占しているが、ここしばらくはずっと控えめにやっていたからな」
English: “I won’t deny the possibility absolutely, but nine times out of ten, it isn’t true. It is interesting, however, that they’ve begun trading so openly. They monopolize the narcotics trade in this city, but for some time now they have kept their business quiet.”

Japanese: 亮は腕組みをして考え込む。
English: Ryo folded his arms and sank into thought.

Japanese: 「彼らはどういうつもりなんだろう？」
English: “What are they trying to accomplish?”

Japanese: 「YSなんか眼中にないってことは確実だな。初代が死んでから、ほとんど僕らを無視している」
English: “At the very least, it is clear that YS no longer concerns them. Since the First Longtou died, they have all but ignored us.”

Japanese: 「そうか。でも、何にしても、僕はうまく手を組んでいくべきだと思うな。……僕が何か言わなくても、小謝はよく考えているんだろうとは思うけど、でも、タイプBの人たちは、敵ではなく味方なんだ。彼らの秘密結社に入っているほとんどの人は、ギャングでもなんでもない、街で普通に暮らすタイプBなんだし。僕らはまず彼らを助けてあげなくちゃいけないんだよ」
English: “I see. Whatever the case, I think we should find a way to cooperate with them. ...I am sure you’ve considered the matter thoroughly without my advice, Siu Tse, but Type Bs are our allies, not our enemies. Most of the people in their secret society aren’t gangsters at all. They are ordinary Type Bs living in this city. Our first duty should be to help them.”

Japanese: 「トミー、僕は彼らを不当に扱うつもりはないが、とりたてて優遇するつもりもないんだよ」
English: “Tommy, I don’t intend to treat them unjustly, but neither do I intend to give them preferential treatment.”

Japanese: 「本当に？　だって、向こうには小謝の親友の見土道夫って人もいるんでしょ？」
English: “Truly? But isn’t your close friend Michio Mido with them?”

Japanese: トーマスは尋ねかけるが、亮はこたえない。
English: Thomas asked, but Ryo did not answer.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、見土道夫ってさ、このまま老人達の後継者としてタイプBのリーダーになるって、大分前から噂になってるけど、本当にそうなのかい？　」
English: “Come to think of it, people have been saying for a long time that Michio Mido will succeed the Elders and become the leader of the Type Bs. Is that true?”

Japanese: 「知らないよ」
English: “I don’t know.”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめて答える。
English: Ryo answered with a shrug.

Japanese: 「もしなったら、いいね。だって、幼なじみ同士なら、きっとうまくやれるでしょ？　YSと彼らはもっと友好的にやるべきだと思うんだ」
English: “I hope it happens. If the two of you are childhood friends, surely you’ll be able to work well together. YS and their organization ought to be on friendlier terms.”

Japanese: 「……そう簡単にはいかないさ」
English: “...It won’t be so simple.”

Japanese: 「でも、廖家と謝家だってこうして一つになれたんだから」
English: “But even the Liao and Tse families have managed to become one.”

Japanese: 「また別の問題がある。……それに、確かに僕は出来るだけ流血の少ない方法を選ぶといったが、全く血を流さずに済むとは言っていない」
English: “That presents different problems. ...And while I did say I would choose the course involving the least bloodshed, I never said we could avoid blood entirely.”

Japanese: 「どういうこと？」
English: “What do you mean?”

Japanese: 「何かを変えるということは、必然的に犠牲が伴う」
English: “Change inevitably demands sacrifice.”

Japanese: 亮は、いまさっき馬明の店の地下で行われたことを、トーマスに伝えてはいなかった。
English: Ryo had not told Thomas what had just occurred in the basement of Ma Ming’s restaurant.

Japanese: 彼らの謀反は、現在では執行部のなかでもさらにごく一部しか知らない。すべてにけりがついてから、その経緯と結末を公表する手はずになっている。
English: Even within the leadership, only a very few people yet knew of the rebellion. Once everything had been settled, they intended to make both the circumstances and the outcome public.

Japanese: いま謝亮がこうして語っているのも、この謀反人の処刑を前提にしたものに違いない。
English: Ryo’s present words, too, must have assumed that the rebels would be executed.

Japanese: 「これからも人死には出るだろう。きみのところは、きみの協力によって事なきを得たが、あの時きみがここにいなかったら、僕らは殺し合いをしていて、きみの父さんは死に、きみやアイスも死んでいたはずだ。僕はそういうつもりだったから、アイスのこともよく調べたんだ。尊大に思えるかもしれないが、僕の率直な感想だ」
English: “More people will die. Your family escaped disaster through your cooperation, but had you not been here then, we would have killed one another. Your father would be dead, and you and Ice would be dead as well. That was my intention, which is why I investigated Ice so thoroughly. It may sound arrogant, but that is my honest assessment.”

Japanese: 「……きっと、小謝の言う通りなんだろうね」
English: “...I am sure you’re right, Siu Tse.”

Japanese: トーマスは素直に頷く。自分たちの死を口にされても動揺が見られないのは、彼も同じ意見を持っていたから自然に受け入られたのだろうが、しかしこうまで言われて侮辱と受け取るでもなく平然としているのはやはり彼の人間性なのだろう。
English: Thomas nodded readily. He showed no distress at hearing the prospect of their deaths stated aloud, presumably because he shared Ryo’s assessment and accepted it as natural. But that he remained composed without taking offense even when Ryo put it so starkly was surely a reflection of the man’s character.

Japanese: 「アイスについては、僕も知らないようなことばかりで、本当に驚いた」
English: “Nearly everything you knew about Ice was new to me. I was truly amazed.”

Japanese: トーマスは感心したように溜息をつく。
English: Thomas sighed in admiration.

Japanese: 「僕は必要ならば何を敵に回すことも恐れていない。トミーは気にいらないかもしれないが、それが僕のやりかただ。もちろん、きみはきみの考えがあるだろうから、奴隷になって従うことはない。気にいらないなら、それを言って貰ってかまわない。むしろ言うべきだ」
English: “I am not afraid to turn anyone or anything against me when necessity demands it. You may dislike that, Tommy, but it is my way. Naturally, you have ideas of your own, so you need not obey me as a slave. If you object, you are free to say so. In fact, you should.”

Japanese: 「気にいらないとか、そういうことじゃないんだ。ただ、戸惑っていて……」
English: “It isn’t that I object. I am simply confused...”

Japanese: 「そうか。でも、そんなことで一々戸惑う必要はないんだよ。きみは今まで通り、自分の理想について発言しつづけてくれればいい。僕もそれを期待している」
English: “I see. But there is no need to get hung up on every such thing. Continue to speak for your ideals just as you always have. I expect that of you.”

Japanese: 「小謝……きみが何を言わんとしているのか、僕には理解出来ないよ」
English: “Siu Tse... I don’t understand what you’re trying to tell me.”

Japanese: 言いながら、トーマスは戸惑いを見せる。それは、言葉の内容よりも、亮の態度によって引き起こされた動揺だった。
English: Thomas’s confusion showed as he spoke. It arose less from the substance of Ryo’s words than from the way Ryo delivered them.

Japanese: 雰囲気が前と違う。だれか、彼の知らない人物がそこにいるような気がしたのだ。
English: Something in the atmosphere had changed. Thomas felt as though someone he did not know stood before him.

Japanese: どこか気怠げに話す亮の目の奥には、トーマスがかつて見たことがない陰がある。かつて見たような……それは、あのクリス・ツェーの瞳にあったものだろうか？
English: In the depths of Ryo’s eyes as he spoke with that languid air lay a shadow Thomas had never seen before. Or had he seen it once...? Had something like it lain in the eyes of Chris Tse?

Japanese: 壁の向こうを見通すサイキックであったクリス・ツェーの瞳は邪眼だの魔眼だのと言われたが、能力とは別に、率直に見つめられると汗がとまらなくなるような不思議な雰囲気があった。いまの亮もそれと似ているようだが、どこか根本的に違っているようにも思えた。親子だと思うから、似てるように感じるのか。
English: Chris Tse had been a psychic capable of seeing through walls, and people called his eyes wicked or demonic. Yet apart from that ability, they possessed a strange quality that could leave a man sweating uncontrollably when Chris looked straight at him. Ryo’s eyes now appeared similar, yet fundamentally different in some way. Did Thomas imagine the resemblance only because they were father and son?

Japanese: この奇妙な違和感を、トーマスは内心で気のせいだと打ち消しつつ、
English: Thomas dismissed the peculiar discomfort as his imagination and continued.

Japanese: 「とにかくね、老人達が活発になったって話を僕がしたのはね、この街には、僕らのYSの他にもいろんな底の知れないものが一杯あって、そういうのが、どうも、最近動きが活発になってるって言いたかったんだ。小謝のお父さんの死によって、僕たちだけじゃなく、いろんなものが変わろうとしているのかもしれないって伝えたくってさ」
English: “In any case, my point in telling you that the Elders have become active was that many fathomless things exist in this city besides YS, and lately, those things all seem to be stirring. I wanted to tell you that your father’s death may be changing more than our organization. It may have set all sorts of things in motion.”

Japanese: 「それはわかった。僕も気にとめておこう。それでこの話は終わりだ。……そう言えばトミー、全く別の話だけれど、きみに一つ聞きたいことがあったんだ」
English: “I understand. I’ll bear it in mind. That is enough about that. ...By the way, Tommy, on a wholly different matter, there is something I’ve wanted to ask you.”

Japanese: 「何でも聞いてよ。僕だって結構色々知ってるんだから」
English: “Ask me anything. I know more than you might think.”

Japanese: トーマスは胸を張る。
English: Thomas puffed out his chest.

Japanese: 「それは頼もしいな。じゃあはっきり聞くけれど」
English: “How reassuring. Then I’ll ask plainly.”
“What is it?”
