English: The exterior guards had run toward the front, leaving the area deserted. The five men in black approached the service gate, shot apart the lock on the door beside it, and entered the grounds.

Japanese: 「はいってすぐのところで清掃員が片付けをしている。武装はしていないようだ。おれが先行するから続け。発砲はするな」
English: “A cleaner is finishing up just inside. She doesn’t appear to be armed. I’ll go first; follow me. Do not fire.”

Japanese: クリスが呟くと、他のメンバーは頷く。
English: Chris murmured the instructions, and the other members nodded.

Japanese: クリスは建物の裏側にあるドアのノブを慎重に捻って、そのなかに身体を滑り込ませる。
English: He carefully turned the knob of a door behind the building and slipped inside.

Japanese: その部屋には彼が前もって伝えていたとおり、作業服を着た清掃係らしい中年女がゴミ袋の口を縛っていた。
English: As Chris had warned them, a middle-aged woman who appeared to be a cleaner stood in the room, tying shut a garbage bag. She wore work clothes.

Japanese: 「ひっ」
English: “Eek!”

Japanese: なだれ込んできた黒衣の五人の姿を見て、女は顔を歪める。
English: The woman’s face twisted at the sight of five black-clad men flooding into the room.

Japanese: 「動くな。抵抗したら撃つ」
English: “Don’t move. Resist, and we’ll shoot.”

Japanese: 「いっ、命だけは……」
English: “P-please, spare my life...”

Japanese: 「安心しろ。大人しく従えば命までは奪わない」
English: “Don’t worry. Do as you’re told, and we won’t kill you.”

Japanese: クリスが銃で脅しつけ、残りのメンバーで清掃員を縛り上げると、その口に黒いガムテープを貼った。
English: Chris held her at gunpoint while the other members bound her, then sealed her mouth with black duct tape.

Japanese: 下働きの人間は地域の一般市民がほとんどなので、余裕があるかぎりは極力殺害しないというのが今回の方針だった。客も、女子供にも、同様に死傷者を出さないようにする。
English: Most menial workers were ordinary residents of the district, so the policy for this operation was to avoid killing them whenever circumstances allowed. The same applied to customers, women, and children: casualties were to be prevented.

Japanese: 武器を持った人間と、抵抗する人間、それとマネージャークラス以上の職員は問答無用で射殺する。職員の役職は、バラをかたどった胸のバッジを見れば判別がつく。
English: Anyone carrying a weapon, anyone who resisted, and any employee of managerial rank or above would be shot without discussion. The employee’s rank could be identified by the rose-shaped badge on the chest.

Japanese: クリス達の行くルートは、ちょうど、この間アサヒことベルーハを逃がすときに使った経路を遡ったものとなる。裏階段を使って十階のプラチナフロアまで上がり、そこから別の階段で一つ上の階に行けば管理職たちのビジネスフロアになる。
English: The route taken by Chris’s party exactly retraced the one he and Tachikawa had used not long before to help Asahi—Belukha—escape. They would use the rear staircase to climb to the Platinum floor on the tenth story, then take a different staircase up one more level to the business floor occupied by management.

Japanese: 最重要ターゲットのロジャー・アダムス達は今そこに集まっているはずだ。
English: Roger Adams and the other highest-priority targets should now have been gathered there.

Japanese: 裏階段を上っていると、馬明達の暴れる銃声の音と、女の悲鳴などが壁越しに聞こえてくる。そのたびにクリスは振り向き、彼にしか見えない壁の向こうの状態を確認する。馬明達も順調に作戦をこなしているようだった。
English: As they climbed the rear stairs, the rampage of gunfire from Ma Ming’s men and the screams of women reached them through the walls. Each time, Chris looked back and inspected conditions beyond the wall, visible to him alone. Ma Ming’s group appeared to be proceeding smoothly as well.

Japanese: 十階を階段で駆け上がるのはそれなりに労が要る。急がなければいけないが、駆け足になれば息が切れてしまう。焦らず黙々と昇っていると、太刀川の身体はじっとりと汗ばみ、目出し帽の下で群れて不快だった。
English: Running up ten floors demanded considerable effort. They needed to hurry, but a full sprint would leave them breathless. As they climbed steadily without panicking, sweat dampened Tachikawa’s body. The balaclava grew hot and clammy around his head.

Japanese: こうした場におけるクリスというのはほとんど万能の働きを発揮する。四階を過ぎたところでふと立ち止まり、上の階のドアに向かって発砲をした。銃はサプレッサーをつけているとはいえ、音が消えるわけではなく、銃声が階段中に響き渡る。
English: In circumstances of this kind, Chris displayed an almost superhuman competence. Just after passing the fourth floor, he abruptly stopped and fired at the door on the floor above. The suppressor did not eliminate the sound, and the shots rang throughout the stairwell.

Japanese: 銃を撃ち終わるとクリスは駆け上がって、驚く仲間達に得意げにドアを開いてみせた。その先には、拳銃を握った二人の男が頭を撃ち抜かれて倒れている。
English: Once he finished firing, Chris ran up and proudly opened the door for his startled companions. Beyond it lay two men with handguns in their fists and bullets through their heads.

Japanese: 万事この調子であり、自分で発見し自分で処理をする。他の面々は彼の後をついてその指示に従うだけでほとんど何もする必要がなかった。
English: Everything proceeded in this fashion: Chris discovered every threat and dealt with it himself. The others needed to do almost nothing but follow him and obey his instructions.

Japanese: 一方、ローズ・クラブ側は完全に混乱していた。
English: The Rose Club, meanwhile, had descended into complete confusion.

Japanese: その日の会議に参加していたのは六人。オーナー社長であるロジャー・アダムスの他も、組織の役員ばかりであった。
English: Six people attended the meeting that day. Apart from Roger Adams, the owner and president, every participant was an officer of the organization.

Japanese: その日の定例会議は、出席者にあくびが目立つようなゆるんだ空気のなか、最近の芳しくない収支報告について議論が行われていた。といっても、YSの妨害活動が原因であるのだが、それに対処するのは木下組であり、ローズ・クラブ側で出来ることはない。決定的な対処法がないのはみなわかっているのだ。
English: The regular meeting had been discussing the recent unfavorable financial reports in an atmosphere so lax that the participants openly yawned. The cause, of course, was YS’s campaign of obstruction. Dealing with YS fell to the Kinoshita-gumi, leaving nothing the Rose Club itself could do. Everyone knew there was no decisive remedy available to them.

Japanese: その停滞した雰囲気を破って、血相を変えたチーフマネージャーが飛び込んで来た。
English: A chief manager with a bloodless face burst into the room, shattering the stagnant atmosphere.

Japanese: 「しゅっ、襲撃です！」
English: “W-we’re under attack!”

Japanese: 彼はしどろもどろになりながら、正面受付が突破され、武装した集団が施設内に流れ込んだことを伝えた。
English: Stumbling over his words, he reported that armed men had broken through the front reception and were pouring into the facility.

Japanese: 一同に動揺に走るなか、ロジャー・アダムスは落ち着いていた。
English: Disturbance swept through the assembled officers, but Roger Adams remained calm.

Japanese: 金色の髪と青い瞳を持ち、長身をグレーのスーツに包んでいる。顔立ちは整っており、表情には屈折したところがなく、黙っていても温厚な印象を人に与える。テレビドラマに出演するのならば、正義の医者か弁護士といった役柄が相応しいだろう。少なくとも、とても臓器移植の違法コーディネーターあがりの、変態クラブオーナーには見えない。
English: He was a tall man with golden hair and blue eyes, dressed in a gray suit. His features were handsome, and there was nothing twisted or guarded in his expression; even in silence, he gave an impression of gentleness. Were he cast in a television drama, he would have suited the role of a virtuous doctor or lawyer. At the very least, he looked nothing like an illegal organ-transplant coordinator turned owner of a perverse club.

Japanese: 「あのYSの連中かい？」
English: “Is this the work of those people from YS?”

Japanese: アダムスは穏やかにそう訊ねた。
English: Adams put the question gently.

Japanese: 「わかりませんが、おそらく……。軍隊のようなものものしい銃器で武装しています」
English: “We don’t know, but probably... They’re armed with military-grade weapons.”

Japanese: 「それは困った」
English: “That is unfortunate.”

Japanese: アダムスはふうと溜息をつく。
English: Adams released a long breath.

Japanese: 「彼らはフロアになだれ込んで、従業員を、しゃっ、射殺して……」
English: “They’ve flooded the floors and sh-shot the employees...”

Japanese: 「わかった、わかった。少し黙って落ち着きたまえ」
English: “I understand. Now be quiet for a moment and compose yourself.”

Japanese: アダムスは手をあげて、チーフマネージャーに口を閉じるよう促す。
English: Adams raised a hand, prompting the chief manager to close his mouth.

Japanese: 「木下組の予想は外れたみたいですね」
English: “It appears the Kinoshita-gumi’s prediction was mistaken.”

Japanese: 彼は動揺する役員たちに向かってそう肩をすくめた。
English: He shrugged as he addressed the shaken officers.

Japanese: ローズ・クラブは再三YSへの具体的な対処を求めたが、木下組は、彼らがこのような実力行使に出ることはないと動かなかったのだ。
English: The Rose Club had repeatedly asked the Kinoshita-gumi to take concrete measures against YS, but the group refused to act, insisting that YS would never resort to direct force of this kind.

Japanese: ――YSは木下組を恐れ、出来れば交渉で決着をつけたいと思っている。今までY地区の連中は常にそのような態度であったし、武闘派と知られているクリス・ツェーも木下組に対してはそこまで強硬な手段をとったことがない。
English: —YS feared the Kinoshita-gumi and hoped, if possible, to reach a negotiated settlement. The people of Y District had always adopted that posture, and even Chris Tse, famous for his readiness to fight, had never taken such forceful action against the Kinoshita-gumi.

Japanese: その予測が木下組の判断の根拠だった。
English: That forecast had formed the basis of the Kinoshita-gumi’s judgment.

Japanese: 「みなさん、彼らの目的はなんだと思いますか？」
English: “Ladies and gentlemen, what do you believe they want?”

Japanese: 慌てふためく役員達に、一人落ち着きを保つアダムスはそう訊ねた。
English: Alone in retaining his calm, Adams put the question to the panicking officers.

Japanese: こんな火急の時に悠長に質問をしている彼に、役員達は戸惑いの視線を向ける。
English: They stared at him in confusion for posing it so leisurely amid a crisis.

Japanese: 「おそらく我々経営陣の命でしょう。今日を狙ったのも、こうして役員が集まる日だからです。ここから逃げた方が良いですね」
English: “Most likely, the lives of the management. They chose today because it is the day the officers gather here. We should escape.”

Japanese: そしてアダムスは立ち上がり、チーフマネージャーに呼びかける。
English: Adams rose and addressed the chief manager.

Japanese: 「きみ、武器を持っているものを集めて、みなさんを逃がしてやってくれないか？　監視カメラの映像を良く見て、敵と遭遇しないよう道を選ぶんだ」
English: “Gather everyone carrying a weapon and help these people escape. Watch the surveillance feeds carefully and choose a route that will keep you from encountering the enemy.”

Japanese: 「オ、オーナーは？」
English: “What about you, sir?”

Japanese: 「僕はここに残る。彼らが一番欲しい命は、僕だろうからね……。ほら、早く！　早く行動をしないと、手遅れになる！」
English: “I will remain here. The life they want most is probably mine. ...Now go! If you don’t act immediately, it will be too late!”

Japanese: アダムスはそう言って、他の人々に今すぐ部屋を出るように促した。その言葉で役員達にもスイッチが入ったようで、彼らは恐怖に駆られるままにドタバタとドアから出て行った。
English: Adams urged the others to leave the room at once. His words appeared to flip a switch within the officers. Driven by terror, they tumbled noisily through the door.

Japanese: そして部屋には一人アダムスだけが残される。
English: Adams alone remained in the room.

Japanese: 彼は暗い表情で椅子に座り直すと、
English: He sat once more in his chair, his expression dark.

Japanese: 「まあ、もう誰も助からないだろうが」
English: “Though I doubt anyone will escape now.”

Japanese: 一人呟き、煙草に火をつけた。
English: He murmured the words to himself and lit a cigarette.

Japanese: その一本を吸い終わらないうちに、開きっぱなしにしたドアから銃を持った黒ずくめの五人が部屋に入ってくる。先頭の男が自分に銃口を向けて来るのを見ながら、彼は強く吸って煙草の残りを燃焼させ、灰皿に潰した。
English: Before he could finish it, five black-clad men carrying guns entered through the door he had left open. Watching the man in front aim at him, Adams inhaled deeply enough to burn away the remainder of the cigarette, then crushed it in the ashtray.

Japanese: 「お前がロジャー・アダムスだな？」
English: “You’re Roger Adams?”

Japanese: 相手の声はうわずっていないし、早口でもなく、落ち着いたものだった。
English: The other man’s voice was neither shrill nor hurried, but calm.

Japanese: 「そうだ。きみが誰なのか誰か教えてくれるかな？」
English: “I am. Would someone kindly tell me who you are?”

Japanese: その言葉に応じて、相手は覆面をはぎ取り、床に投げ捨てた。
English: In answer, the man tore away his mask and threw it upon the floor.

Japanese: 下からは汗ばんだ男の顔があらわれ、その三つの目でアダムスを睨み付ける。
English: A sweating male face emerged beneath it, glaring at Adams with three eyes.

Japanese: 「リーダー自らお出ましとは勇ましいね。しかし、きみがいたんじゃ、やっぱり誰も逃げることは出来なかったかな」
English: “How brave of the leader himself to appear. Still, with you here, I suppose no one could escape after all.”

Japanese: アダムスは目を細めながらそう言った。
English: Adams narrowed his eyes as he spoke.

Japanese: 「この部屋からあたふたと出て行ったお仲間のことなら、一足先に地獄で待ってるぜ」
English: “If you mean the friends who scurried out of this room, they’ve gone ahead to wait for you in hell.”

Japanese: クリス・ツェーの構える銃口はアダムスの顔面に狙いがつけられている。引き金にかかった指がほんの少し動けば、46mmの弾丸がいくつも飛び出し彼の頭部を『トムとジェリー』に出て来るチーズのように穴だらけにするだろう。
English: The muzzle in Chris Tse’s hands pointed at Adams’s face. If the finger upon the trigger moved by the smallest degree, a stream of 4.6 mm rounds would punch his head full of holes like a wheel of cheese in Tom and Jerry.

Japanese: しかしアダムスは汗一つかかず、涼しい顔でクリスに語りかける。
English: Adams did not shed a single bead of sweat. With perfect composure, he addressed Chris.

Japanese: 「きみは自分がしていることがわかっているのかい？　僕を殺したって、人の欲望を殺せるわけじゃない。このクラブがなくなっても、また別のところに同じような施設が出来るだけだろう。もう、そういう世の中になってしまってるんだよ。結局、誰かがこの汚れ仕事を引き受けなきゃいけないんだ。それなら僕でいい。……自分で言うのもなんだがね、僕は私利私欲が全くないし、働いている女の子や男の子たちにも出来る限りよくしてやっている。こんな経営者は他にいないだろう？　僕がいなくなれば、世の中はもっと悪くなる」
English: “Do you understand what you are doing? Killing me cannot kill human desire. If this club disappears, another facility of the same kind will simply be built elsewhere. That is the world we live in now. Ultimately, someone must undertake this dirty work. It might as well be me. ...If you will forgive me saying so, I possess no selfish motive whatsoever, and I treat the girls and boys working here as well as I possibly can. Where will you find another proprietor like me? Without me, the world will grow worse.”

Japanese: 「そんなのはおれには関係ないね。この街のガキに手を出すやつがいなくなりゃ、あとはどうだっていいんだ」
English: “That’s no concern of mine. So long as no one touches the kids in this city, the rest can go to hell.”

Japanese: 「なるほど。まあね、それも一つの考え方だ。近しい人を何よりも優先するというのは、それはそれで理にかなった正しい感じ方だと思う」
English: “I see. Well, that too is one possible view. Placing the people close to you above all others is, in its fashion, a rational and proper way to feel.”

Japanese: アダムスがあっさりと認めたので、クリスは若干拍子抜けしたようだった。
English: Chris appeared somewhat deflated when Adams accepted the point so readily.

Japanese: 「ひとつ、聞いてもいいですか？」
English: “May I ask you one question?”

Japanese: 黒覆面の一人が声をあげる。彼だけは、この襲撃者のなかでただ一人、小さな拳銃しか持っていない。
English: One of the masked men spoke. Alone among the attackers, he carried only a small handgun.

Japanese: 「あなたは血を飲ませて何人もの女性を不死身にしたそうですが、あれはなんなのですか？　科学ですか？　それとも、サイキックの力ですか？」
English: “I am told that you gave several women your blood to drink and made them immortal. What was that? Science? Or a psychic power?”

Japanese: 「それは言えないな。それに、きみたちが知る必要もないことだ」
English: “I cannot tell you. Nor is it anything you need to know.”

Japanese: そう言って、アダムスは微笑を浮かべた。
English: Adams smiled faintly.

Japanese: 「ああ、今感情が動きましたね。これは……悲しみだ。どうして悲しむんですか？　それに何か、いとおしむような気持が混ざっている。あなたと不死の間に、どんな関係があるんです？」
English: “Ah, your emotions moved just now. This is... sadness. Why are you sad? There is something like tenderness mixed into it as well. What relationship do you have with immortality?”

Japanese: 問われるとアダムスはわずかに動揺を見せたが、何も言わなかった。ただ黙って、発言者の目をじっと見つめている。彼はその時ふと気がついた。その男の目出し帽からのぞく目のうち、向かって右側の目に、二つの瞳があることに。
English: The question produced a slight disturbance in Adams, but he said nothing. He merely stared into the speaker’s eyes. At that moment, he noticed something: of the eyes exposed by the man’s balaclava, the one on Adams’s right contained two pupils.

Japanese: 「ドクター、ラインをオフにしな。『その瞬間』にシンクロしたままでいたら、気が狂っちまうぜ」
English: “Doctor, turn off the line. If you stay synchronized with ‘that moment,’ it’ll drive you insane.”

Japanese: クリスが忠告すると、その男――太刀川はがっかりしたように溜息をつき、視線をアダムスの目からそらした。
English: At Chris’s warning, the man—Tachikawa—sighed in disappointment and looked away from Adams’s eyes.

Japanese: 「クリス・ツェー、きみはこれから……」
English: “Chris Tse, from this moment you will...”

Japanese: アダムスが口を開きなにか言おうとしたが、その言葉が終わる前に、彼の鼻から上は何発もの銃弾によって吹き飛ばされた。彼は言いかけた唇のかたちのまま仰向けにのけぞり、そして椅子ごと後ろに倒れる。
English: Adams opened his mouth and attempted to continue, but before the sentence ended, multiple bullets blew away everything above his nose. With his lips still holding the shape of the interrupted words, he arched backward, then toppled with the chair.

Japanese: 「ドクター確認してくれ」
English: “Doctor, examine him.”

Japanese: クリスは倒れて動かなくなったアダムスの身体から目をそらさないでそう言った。
English: Chris gave the instruction without taking his eyes from Adams’s fallen, motionless body.

Japanese: 太刀川は頷き、その身体の側にかがみ込むと、手首に触れて脈をとり、胸に耳を当てて心音を聞き取り、そして破壊された頭部をじっと観察する。そのまま三分ほど過ぎただろうか。
English: Tachikawa nodded and crouched beside the corpse. He touched the wrist and took its pulse, placed an ear to the chest and listened for a heartbeat, then closely observed the destroyed head. Perhaps three minutes passed.

Japanese: 「再生している様子は全くないですね。死体現象がはじまっています」
English: “There is no sign of regeneration whatsoever. Postmortem changes have begun.”

Japanese: そう言って、すっと立ち上がった。
English: He rose smoothly to his feet.

Japanese: 「そうか、意外だな。てっきりこいつも不死身になっているのかと思ったんだが」
English: “Is that so? I’m surprised. I was certain he had made himself immortal too.”

Japanese: クリスはどうにも解せないらしく、アダムスの死体を爪先で蹴飛ばす。しかし、やはりそれは無反応であった。
English: Still unable to make sense of it, Chris kicked Adams’s corpse with the toe of his boot. It remained unresponsive.

Japanese: この部屋に追い詰められてからのロジャー・アダムスの態度はあまりに平然としていて、慌てる様子もなかったから彼はそんな風に考えたのだ。
English: Roger Adams had behaved with such complete ease after being cornered in the room, without the slightest sign of panic, that Chris had formed that conclusion.

Japanese: 「よくわからないやつだったが、まあ、おかげで手間が減って助かる。不死身だったらどうやって死なそうかと思っていたんだ」
English: “I never did understand him, but this saves us a lot of trouble. I was wondering how we’d manage to kill him if he was immortal.”

Japanese: クリスは仲間に振り返って苦笑すると、床に落ちた目出し帽を拾い、一旦被りかけたが途中で思いとどまり、ズボンのポケットにしまった。
English: Chris turned to his companions with a wry smile. He picked up the balaclava from the floor and began to put it on, then changed his mind halfway through and stuffed it into his trouser pocket.

Japanese: 「さて、我々の作戦は予定通り終了だ。じゃあ合流地点に移動するか」
English: “Our operation is complete according to plan. Let’s move to the rendezvous point.”

Japanese: そしてまだじっと死体を見つめている太刀川を促し部屋を出たところで、クリスはポケットから携帯電話を取り出した。
English: He prompted Tachikawa, who still stood staring at the body, and led the party from the room. Outside, Chris took his mobile phone from his pocket.

Japanese: 見ると、携帯電話は馬明からの通話着信で細かく振動している。
English: The phone vibrated rapidly with an incoming call from Ma Ming.

Japanese: 「どうした？」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 『兄貴、そっちは大丈夫か？』
English: “Boss, are things all right over there?”

Japanese: 「ああ。今から合流地点に向かうところだ。そっちは何かあったのか？」
English: “Yes. We’re about to head for the rendezvous point. Did something happen on your end?”

Japanese: 『こっちもプラチナフロアの制圧が終わったところなんだが、予想外の光景に出くわしちまって……』
English: “We’ve just finished securing the Platinum floor, but we ran into something we didn’t expect...”

Japanese: 「予想外？」
English: “Something unexpected?”

Japanese: 言いながら、クリスは足元に視線をやる。彼の額の第三の目は、床の向こうにある下のフロアを見通しているのだろう。
English: As he spoke, Chris lowered his eyes toward the floor. The third eye in his forehead was presumably looking through it to the floor below.

Japanese: 『言われたとおり、肩に三日月のタトゥーがあるやつらはうちらで保護しようとしたんだよ。それで見取り図にある、例の場所に来たんだが……』
English: “Just as you said, we tried to protect everyone with a crescent tattoo on her shoulder. Then we came to that place on the floor plan...”

Japanese: ベルーハから聞いた三日月の女の待機所は、計画の段階で見取り図にマークをつけて特に重要な場所としてあった。
English: Belukha had told them about the waiting room for the women marked with crescents. During the planning stage, they had marked it on the floor plan as a location of particular importance.

Japanese: クリスはその図を頭に思い浮かべながら、そちらに視線をやる。
English: With the floor plan in mind, Chris directed his gaze toward the room.

Japanese: 『その部屋に足を踏み入れたら……』
English: “When we stepped inside...”

Japanese: 「わかった。今から行く」
English: “I understand. We’re coming now.”

Japanese: クリスは最後まで聞かずに通話を切った。その表情はさっきまでとはうってかわって硬いものとなっている。
English: Chris ended the call without hearing the rest. His expression had become hard, utterly transformed from moments before.

Japanese: 彼は馬明から説明されるまでもなく、その光景を自分の目で見てしまったのだ。
English: Before Ma Ming could explain it, Chris had seen the scene with his own eyes.

Japanese: クリスはポケットに携帯電話をしまうと、不安げにこちらを見ている太刀川たちに向き直った。
English: He returned the phone to his pocket and faced Tachikawa and the others, who watched him anxiously.

Japanese: 「予定変更だ。プラチナフロアに向かう」
English: “Change of plan. We’re going to the Platinum floor.”

Japanese: その言葉で一同は察し、無言で頷いた。
English: The party understood from those words and nodded in silence.

Japanese: 女達の待機所は、階段を降りると空中回廊を歩いて、この間初めてアサヒと太刀川が出会ったあの場所より先に進み、さらに右の薄暗い通路に入った突き当たりの部屋である。
English: To reach the women’s waiting room, they descended the stairs, crossed the elevated corridor, continued beyond the place where Asahi and Tachikawa had first met not long before, then entered a dim passage on the right. The room stood at its far end.

Japanese: 久しぶりにやって来たその場所は、壁には無数の銃痕が残り、床には血みどろの従業員や流れ弾に当たった女の死体が転がり、カーテンは破れ、戦闘の痕跡を生々しく残していた。一行は死体をまたぎながら進む。
English: The place to which they now returned bore vivid traces of the battle. Countless bullet scars marked the walls. Blood-soaked employees and women struck by stray rounds lay dead upon the floor, and the curtains hung torn. The party stepped over the bodies as it advanced.

Japanese: 目的の部屋のドアは開きっぱなしになっており、先頭のクリスが最初にそのなかに入ると、太刀川は二番目に部屋に足を踏み入れた。
English: The door to their destination stood open. Chris entered first, and Tachikawa stepped into the room immediately behind him.

Japanese: 「これは……」
English: “This is...”

Japanese: ここに来るまでのクリスの表情と態度でおおよその想像はついていたが、実際目の当たりにするとさすがに驚かないわけにはいかなかった。
English: Chris’s expression and manner on the way had allowed Tachikawa to imagine the scene in broad outline. Confronting it with his own eyes shocked him nevertheless.

Japanese: プラチナフロアの待機所は、客室に劣らぬくらい豪華な作りになっている。天井には金の飾りがついたシャンデリアがぶら下がり、足元には上質の絨毯が敷き詰められている。その上に、下着のように露出の多いドレスを身に纏った女達が、折り重なるように倒れていた。太刀川が以前に見たショーと同じ、子供のように幼い女も、成熟した者も、肌が黒い者も、白い者も、あるいは白目を剥き、苦悶の表情を浮かべ、ぴくりとも動かない。女だけではない。割合は少ないが、美少年や美男児の姿もそのなかにまざっている。
English: The waiting room on the Platinum floor had been constructed as luxuriously as any guest room. A chandelier with golden decorations hung from the ceiling, and a fine carpet covered the floor. Upon it, women wearing revealing dresses scarcely more substantial than underwear had collapsed over one another. Just as in the show Tachikawa had once witnessed, some were as young as children and others mature, some dark-skinned and others pale. Some showed the whites of their eyes; some wore expressions of agony. None moved. Nor were all of them female. Fewer in number, beautiful boys and young men lay among them.

Japanese: 先に到着した馬明とその部下達は、その女達を爪先や銃口でつついたりしながら、生存者の確認を行っていた。
English: Ma Ming and the subordinates who had arrived first were prodding the women with their toes and gun barrels as they searched for survivors.

Japanese: 「駄目かい」
English: “No good?”

Japanese: クリスが、しかめっつらでしゃがみこみ、遺体の顔を眺めていた馬明にそう尋ねる。
English: Chris addressed Ma Ming, who crouched with a scowl to inspect the face of one body.

Japanese: 「どうやらそうらしい」
English: “It looks that way.”

Japanese: 馬明は立ち上がってかぶりを振る。
English: Ma Ming rose and shook his head.

Japanese: 「他の女たちは？」
English: “What about the other women?”

Japanese: 「もう移動させた。今頃階段を降りているはずだよ」
English: “We moved them already. They should be going down the stairs by now.”

Japanese: 「そうか。しかし、おかしいな。どいつも三日月のマークがついているのに……」
English: “I see. But this makes no sense. Every one of them has the crescent mark...”

Japanese: クリスはドレスから剥き出しになった女たちの肩を見ながら首を捻った。男の遺体のシャツをめくってみると、やはりそこにも三日月のマークがある。
English: Chris tilted his head as he studied the women’s shoulders, exposed by their dresses. When he lifted the shirt of one male body, he found a crescent mark there as well.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、ベルーハは『三日月』から不死身の力を奪う薬があると言っていたな。それを使ったのか？」
English: “Come to think of it, Belukha said there was a drug that stripped the Crescents of their immortality. Did they use it?”

Japanese: クリスは太刀川の姿を探す。彼は床に這いつくばるようにして、死体の状態を確認していた。
English: Chris looked for Tachikawa. The doctor was almost crawling over the floor as he examined the bodies.

Japanese: 「ドクター、どう思う？」
English: “What do you think, Doctor?”

Japanese: 「どの遺体も、腕に静脈注射の痕跡があります。なにかの薬品で殺害された可能性が高いですね」
English: “Every body bears the mark of an intravenous injection on the arm. There is a strong possibility that some drug was used to kill them.”

Japanese: 言葉は冷静を装っていたが、声には動揺があらわれていた。
English: His words were outwardly calm, but the disturbance showed in his voice.

Japanese: 「わざわざ三日月の女ばかり集めて……。そうだ、馬明、ここに来るまでに戦った従業員で、銃で撃ったのに起き上がってくるようなやつはいなかったか？」
English: “They went out of their way to gather only women with crescents... Wait. Ma Ming, among the employees you fought on the way here, did any of them rise again after being shot?”

Japanese: 「いや、特にそう言うのはいませんでしたね」
English: “No, nothing of the kind.”

Japanese: 「こっちもだ。不死身なのは、商売用の女だけなのかねえ。やはり、儀式は相当なリスクが伴うのだろうか。……馬明、このフロアをもう一度調べてくれないか」
English: “We saw none either. Are only the women used for business made immortal? Perhaps the ritual carries considerable risk after all. ...Ma Ming, search this floor once more.”

Japanese: クリスは顔をあげて馬明にそう指示した。
English: Chris raised his face and issued the instruction.

Japanese: 「了解。……一班の者は、おれについてこい！」
English: “Understood. ...First squad, come with me!”

Japanese: 馬明が部下をまとめて部屋を出て行こうとしたとき、
English: Ma Ming was gathering his subordinates and beginning to leave when a voice rose behind him.

Japanese: 「この女、まだ息があります！」
English: “This woman is still breathing!”

Japanese: 遺体を調べていた部下の一人がそう声をあげた。それを受けて、太刀川はすぐに立ち上がって駈け寄る。
English: The shout came from a subordinate examining the bodies. Tachikawa immediately stood and ran toward him.

Japanese: そして部下を押しのけ、女の顔をのぞき込むと、そのからだがこわばり凍り付いた。
English: He pushed the man aside and looked into the woman’s face. His body stiffened and froze.

Japanese: 「お、おおお……」
English: “O-ohhh...”

Japanese: 動けなくなった太刀川の唇の間からうめき声が漏れる。
English: A groan escaped between Tachikawa’s immobilized lips.

Japanese: 普段冷静沈着な『ドクター』の、見たこともない異常な感情の揺らぎは、まるで何か神経性の発作のようにさえ見えた。その場に居合わせた一同は戸惑いを浮かべる。
English: No one present had ever witnessed such a violent emotional upheaval in the ordinarily composed Doctor. It almost resembled some form of nervous seizure. The entire party stared in bewilderment.

Japanese: 「ドクター……」
English: “Doctor...”

Japanese: 部下の一人が彼の肩を叩くが、太刀川は微動だにしない。
English: One subordinate touched him on the shoulder, but Tachikawa did not move by the smallest degree.

Japanese: 一人落ち着いているクリスは手を上げて、ドクターから離れるよう無言で指示を出す。
English: Chris alone remained calm. He raised a hand and silently directed the others away from the Doctor.

Japanese: 「もしかして、これは例の？」
English: “Could this be the one you mentioned?”

Japanese: 女をまたいでやって来た馬明が耳に囁くと、クリスは頷く。
English: Ma Ming stepped over a woman and whispered in Chris’s ear. Chris nodded.

Japanese: 「ミアオ……」
English: “Miao...”

Japanese: 太刀川は喉の奥から絞り出すようにその名を口にした。そして彼女の肩の三日月の刻印を見て顔を顰める。
English: Tachikawa forced the name from the depths of his throat. When he saw the crescent branded upon her shoulder, his face tightened.

Japanese: そう、そこに倒れていたのは彼が長年探し求めていたその女だったのである。
English: Yes—the woman lying there was the very one he had sought for so many years.

Japanese: 夢にまで見たその肉体は、以前とちっとも変わらず美しかったが、その命が尽きようとしているのは明白だった。
English: The body he had seen even in his dreams remained every bit as beautiful as before, but it was plainly on the verge of death.

Japanese: 女は確かにまだ息がある。微かに呼吸をし、弱々しい脈拍も感じ取れた。しかしその肌は血の気が失せて蒼白になっている。
English: The woman was certainly still alive. She breathed faintly, and a feeble pulse could be felt. Yet all color had drained from her skin, leaving it deathly pale.

Japanese: 太刀川はその手を取って裏返し、その内側を見た。そこにも注射のあとがある。太刀川は唇を噛んだ。
English: Tachikawa took her hand, turned it over, and examined the inside. There, too, was the mark of a needle. He bit his lip.

Japanese: 「ミアオ、私だ……」
English: “Miao, it’s me...”

Japanese: 彼はミアオを抱きかかえ、その焦点の定まらない目に自分の顔を見せつけようとしたところで、まだ帽子をかぶったままなのに気がつき、荒々しい手つきではぎ取り、投げ捨てる。
English: He gathered Miao into his arms and tried to bring his face before her unfocused eyes. Only then did he realize he was still wearing the balaclava. He tore it off with a savage motion and flung it aside.

Japanese: 「私だ、太刀川だ……わかるか？」
English: “It’s me. Tachikawa... Do you recognize me?”

Japanese: 首筋をそっと撫でながらそう呟くと、ミアオは首をわずかに持ち上げて、ゆらゆらと定まらない視点を彼の顔にあわせようと動かす。
English: He murmured the words while gently stroking the side of her neck. Miao lifted her head a fraction and moved her wandering gaze in an effort to bring his face into focus.

Japanese: 「タチカワ……さん……」
English: “Mr. Tachikawa...”

Japanese: かすれる声でそう呟くと、うすく微笑した。
English: She whispered in a rasping voice, then smiled faintly.

Japanese: 「……久しぶり……」
English: “...It’s been a long time...”

Japanese: 「ああ、久しぶりだ。本当に……久しぶりだ……」
English: “Yes, it has. Such a... very long time...”

Japanese: 言葉につまり、太刀川の目に涙の塊が浮かぶ。
English: His words caught in his throat, and great tears welled in his eyes.

Japanese: 「駄目だ、これじゃぼやけてしまって、お前の目が見えない……」
English: “No, this won’t do. Everything’s blurred—I can’t see your eyes...”

Japanese: 太刀川は袖口で涙をぬぐい取った。
English: Tachikawa wiped the tears away with his cuff.

Japanese: ミアオは苦悶に顔を歪め、身体を引きつらせる。その強く閉ざしたまぶたにしわが浮かぶ。
English: Miao’s face twisted in agony, and her body convulsed. Furrows formed across her tightly shut eyelids.

Japanese: 「苦しいか？　大丈夫だ。もう心配いらない。私は医師だ」
English: “Does it hurt? It’s all right. You have nothing more to fear. I am a doctor.”

Japanese: 太刀川はそう励まし、ミアオの身体を抱き寄せる。彼女の華奢な身体は腕の中にすっぽりとおさまり、その痙攣が彼女の生を実感させる。
English: Tachikawa drew Miao’s body close as he reassured her. Her slender frame fit entirely within his arms, and its convulsions made the life within her palpable.

Japanese: やがて彼女の身体のひきつりが収まった。
English: In time, the spasms subsided.

Japanese: 不安になって太刀川は身体を離し、彼女の顔を見た。ミアオは目を閉じているが、先ほどの苦痛の表情は消え、穏やかに微笑んでいる。
English: Growing anxious, Tachikawa drew back and looked at her face. Miao’s eyes were closed, but the agony had vanished from her features. She wore a tranquil smile.

Japanese: 「……そうだね……タチカワさんは、優秀だから……」
English: “...That’s right... You’re an excellent doctor...”

Japanese: 「そうだ。おれは同期の誰よりも優秀だった。だから安心していい。お前は助かるんだ」
English: “I am. I was better than anyone else in my class. So you can rest easy. I’m going to save you.”
“...I see.”

Japanese: ミアオはそう呟いた。
English: Miao whispered the words.

Japanese: しかし、穏やかでいられたのは一瞬だった。すぐに彼女の顔には苦しみがもどり、その手足に、これほど弱った人間のものとは思えない力が入る。
English: Her peace lasted only an instant. Pain swiftly returned to her face, and a strength inconceivable in one so weakened flooded her limbs.

Japanese: 「あっ……あああっ！」
English: “Ah... Aaaagh!”

Japanese: 開いた口の奥から、人のものとは思えない声があがる。
English: From the depths of her open mouth rose a cry that scarcely seemed human.

Japanese: 太刀川はその目を見ようとしたが、彼女のまぶたはぴったりと閉ざされていた。
English: Tachikawa tried to look into her eyes, but her lids remained sealed tight.

Japanese: 「ミアオ、目を開けろ！　開けてくれ！」
English: “Miao, open your eyes! Please, open them!”

Japanese: 「あ、あ、ああっ！」
English: “Ah... Ah... Aaaagh!”

Japanese: 太刀川の叫び声はもう彼女の耳には届かない。
English: Tachikawa’s cries no longer reached her ears.

Japanese: 「おれにも、わけてくれ！　お前の感情をっ！」
English: “Share them with me—your feelings!”

Japanese: 太刀川は咄嗟に片手を伸ばし、指先を彼女のまぶたにあてがって、むりやり目を開かせる。
English: Acting on impulse, Tachikawa extended one hand, set his fingertips against her lids, and forced her eyes open.

Japanese: 「やめろっドクター！　何をしている！　何を見ようとしている！」
English: “Stop, Doctor! What are you doing? What are you trying to see?”

Japanese: クリスは叫んだ。
English: Chris shouted.

Japanese: 「黙れクリスっ！」
English: “Be quiet, Chris!”

Japanese: 太刀川の空気が震えるほどのすさまじい怒声で、駈け寄ろうとしたクリスの足が止まる。
English: Tachikawa’s furious roar seemed to shake the very air. It stopped Chris in his tracks as he began to run toward them.

Japanese: 「うあっ……あああっ……」
English: “Uagh... Aaaagh...”

Japanese: ミアオは口からよだれを垂れ流しながら、手足をばたつかせ、そして太刀川にしがみつく。
English: Drool streaming from her mouth, Miao thrashed her limbs and clung to Tachikawa.

Japanese: しがみつかれたどうにかしてその目を開かせようとする。
English: Tachikawa struggled to make her open her eyes.

Japanese: 「目をっ、目を開けてくれっ！」
English: “Your eyes—open your eyes!”

Japanese: やっとその声が届いたのか、ミアオの目は大きく見開らかれた。太刀川はほとんどキスをするように顔を近づけ、彼女の目と自分の眼球が二つある目をくっつきそうなくらい接近させる。
English: Perhaps his voice finally reached her, for Miao’s eyes opened wide. Tachikawa brought his face so close that he might almost have been kissing her, until his double-pupiled eye seemed on the verge of touching hers.

Japanese: すると、太刀川の全身も硬くこわばり、ぷるぷると震え始めた。
English: Then Tachikawa’s entire body went rigid and began to tremble.

Japanese: 「あああああああっ……」
English: “Aaaaaaaaaagh...”

Japanese: そして、彼の口からも、ミアオとそっくりの苦しみの声が漏れる。
English: From his mouth came a cry of agony almost identical to Miao’s.

Japanese: 「馬鹿野郎っ！」
English: “You damn fool!”

Japanese: ついに近づいたクリスがその肩をつかんだが、太刀川は乱暴に振り払う。しかしその拍子でミアオの身体が離れ、彼女は床に仰向けに倒れた。太刀川はその上に覆い被さるような姿勢をとると、ミアオの顔を両手で挟むように固定し、その目をじっと見つめる。
English: Chris finally reached him and seized his shoulder, but Tachikawa violently shook him off. The motion tore Miao’s body from him, and she fell onto her back. Tachikawa bent over her, fixed her face between his hands, and stared into her eyes.

Japanese: ミアオの感情と、太刀川の感情が完全に一体化する。
English: Miao’s emotions and Tachikawa’s merged completely.

Japanese: 「あっ……ああっ……」
ミアオが身体をびくりと痙攣させると、太刀川も同じように痙攣し、ミアオの全身から力がぬけてぐったりと倒れ込むと、太刀川も脱力してそのまま彼女の上に倒れた。
English: Miao’s body jerked in a spasm, and Tachikawa convulsed with her. The strength left her whole body and she collapsed limply; Tachikawa likewise went slack and fell on top of her.

Japanese: 「おい！　ドクター！」
English: “Hey! Doctor!”

Japanese: クリスは太刀川の身体を掴んで引き起こす。首はぐらぐらと揺れ、目は見開き、口からは泡を拭いている。下のミアオも同様だった。
English: Chris seized Tachikawa and hauled him upright. His head lolled, his eyes stood open, and he was foaming at the mouth. Miao beneath him was in the same condition.

Japanese: 「マジかよ……」
English: “You’ve got to be kidding...”

Japanese: クリスは太刀川の胸に耳を当てる。すると、そこには心音がある。ほっとして、次はミアオの胸に耳を当てると、そこには何の音もない。電池の切れた時計に耳を当てたかのように何も聞こえない。
English: Chris put his ear to Tachikawa’s chest and heard a heartbeat. With a breath of relief, he listened next at Miao’s chest. There was nothing. It was as silent as a clock whose battery had died.

Japanese: 太刀川はまだ生きているが、ミアオはもう死んでいた。不死を殺す薬を打たれていたのだとしたら、蘇ることもないだろう。
English: Tachikawa still lived, but Miao was dead. If she had been injected with the drug that killed immortals, she probably would not revive.

Japanese: クリスは目を剥いたままのミアオのまぶたを閉じてやってから立ち上がった。
English: Chris closed the lids over Miao’s staring eyes, then stood.

Japanese: 生きている人間の精神に、死ぬ瞬間の人間の心が流れ込んだらどうなるのだろうか？　太刀川がそれを身をもって試したということになる。
English: What would happen if the mind of a person at the instant of death flowed into the mind of someone still living? Tachikawa had tested the question with his own body.

Japanese: 彼は他人の感情と自分の感情が入り交じってしまう自分の能力が、自分にとってどれだけリスクがあるものなのかよく理解していた。だから、能力を用いるときも非常に慎重で、クリスの仕事を手伝う時も、対象の感情に引きずり込まれないよう、必要な瞬間を選んでピンポイントで能力を使っていた。あからさまに落ち着きを失っている相手には、けして能力を使おうとしなかった。彼自身も、人より強い精神力を持っていた。それでも、仕事の後は情緒が不安定になって精神安定剤などを服用していたのをクリスは知っている。
English: He understood very well how much danger his ability—mingling another person’s emotions with his own—posed to him. He had therefore always used it with extreme care. Even when assisting Chris in his work, he chose the exact instant he needed and employed the power only at that single point, taking care not to be pulled into his subject’s emotions. He never attempted to use it on anyone who had plainly lost composure. He appeared to possess greater mental strength than most. Even so, Chris knew that his emotions would become unstable after a job and that he took tranquilizers and similar medication.

Japanese: 「無茶をしやがる……」
English: “What a reckless thing to do...”

Japanese: ぐったりと倒れたまま起き上がろうとしない太刀川を見下ろしながらクリスはそう呟いた。
English: Chris whispered as he looked down at Tachikawa, who lay limp and made no attempt to rise.

Japanese: 「おいドクター！　おい！」
English: “Hey, Doctor! Hey!”

Japanese: 馬明が彼の頬を手のひらではたくが、反応をしめさない。
English: Ma Ming slapped his cheek with an open hand, but Tachikawa showed no response.

Japanese: 「はあ……大変なことになったな……」
English: “Damn... This is a real mess...”

Japanese: 馬明は溜息をつくと、太刀川の身体を引き起こし、その身体を背負い、立ち上がった。
English: Ma Ming sighed, pulled Tachikawa’s body upright, hoisted him onto his back, and stood.

Japanese: 「これじゃ、死体を背負ってるのとかわらない」
English: “I might as well be carrying a corpse.”

Japanese: 自分の背中の上で、ぶらぶらと自然に太刀川の手足が揺れるのを見て馬明は顔を顰めた。
English: Ma Ming frowned as Tachikawa’s limbs swung freely against his back.

Japanese: 「兄貴、もう予定時間を大分過ぎてるよ。撤収しよう」
English: “Big Brother, we’re already well past the scheduled time. Let’s pull out.”

Japanese: その問いに、クリスは頷き、
English: Chris nodded in answer.

Japanese: 「わかった。その前に、ちょっとだけ確認させてくれ」
English: “All right. Just let me check one last thing first.”

Japanese: そう言って、千里眼でフロアを見回す。ジェフリーの子供達のように瞬間的に付近の人間を察知する能力ではなく、どこを見るか意識的に調整しなければいけない力であるから、ざっと見回したくらいでは見落としもあるだろうが、ゆっくりしている時間もない。警察はおそらく来ないだろうが、木下組の救援が来るかも知れない。
English: With that, he surveyed the floor using his clairvoyant eye. Unlike Jeffrey’s children, whose power allowed them to detect nearby people in an instant, Chris had to consciously direct his attention toward whatever place he wished to see. A cursory search could therefore miss something, but they had no time to conduct a thorough one. The police were unlikely to come, though reinforcements from the Kinoshita-gumi might.

Japanese: 今の装備なら負ける相手ではないが、意味のない戦いは避けたかった。
English: Their present equipment would make such opponents no threat, but he wished to avoid a pointless battle.

Japanese: 「よし、切り上げよう」
English: “Good. Let’s finish here.”

Japanese: そして撤収の準備に取りかかると、今度はジェフリーから連絡があった。
English: As they began preparing to withdraw, a report came from Jeffrey.

Japanese: それによると、一階で火災が発生したらしい。義勝のメンバーが制圧したときには何事もなかった場所が火元だというから、あとで誰かが火をつけたのだろう。火事は猛烈な勢いで広がりつつあるから、早急に退去すべきだという意見をジェフリーは述べた。
English: A fire had apparently broken out on the first floor. Its source was a location where nothing had been amiss when Yisheng’s men secured it, suggesting that someone had set the blaze afterward. Jeffrey advised them to leave at once, as the fire was spreading with tremendous speed.

Japanese: クリスとしてもそれには異論がない。部下たちに事態を伝えると、自ら先導して降り始めた。
English: Chris had no objection. He informed his subordinates and began leading the way down himself.

Japanese: 来る時に使った裏階段は炎に巻かれ、煙がもくもくと階下からのぼってきており使えない。エレベーターに乗ったら、途中でチカチカと電灯が瞬いて、消える。同時にエレベーターも停止する。ドアをこじ開けて外に出たら建物の中全体が真っ暗になっていた。炎によって電気設備が壊れたのだろう。
English: The rear stairway they had used on the way in was engulfed in flame and unusable, with dense smoke billowing up from below. They entered the elevator, but partway down its lights flickered and went out. The car stopped at the same instant. When they forced the doors open and emerged, the entire building was dark. The fire had probably destroyed the electrical equipment.

Japanese: 回廊の手すりにつかまって、吹き抜けから下を見ると、煙があがって来てとても目を開けていられない。一階のホールも燃えているのだ。
English: Clinging to the gallery railing, they looked down through the atrium, but rising smoke made it impossible to keep their eyes open. The first-floor hall was burning as well.

Japanese: 炎が下から上へと移動する速度は速い。特に巨大な吹き抜けを持つこの建物ならば瞬く間に全体が炎に包まれるだろう。
English: Flames climbed from lower floors to higher ones with terrible speed. In a building with an enormous atrium such as this, the whole structure would be enveloped in fire in the blink of an eye.

Japanese: 普通なら絶体絶命の状況かもしれないが、クリスの目はこういう場合でも役に立つ。
English: Under ordinary circumstances, they might have been trapped with no hope of escape, but Chris’s eye was useful even in a situation like this.

Japanese: 煙と炎を壁一枚、ドア一枚隔てて、紙一重のルートで進み、その途中で逃げ損ねた女を拾う余裕さえみせながら、無事に脱出をした。
English: They followed a route separated from smoke and flame by no more than a single wall or door, even finding the leisure to rescue a woman who had failed to escape along the way, and emerged safely from the building.

Japanese: 来る時に縛った清掃員も助けてやりたかったが、火元がそちらの方向だったので助けることが出来なかったことだけがクリスの心残りだ。
English: Chris’s sole regret was that he could not rescue the cleaner they had bound on the way in. The fire had started in that direction, making it impossible to reach her.

Japanese: 最初の襲撃で馬明たちが破壊した受付を乗り越え外に出ると、Ｙ地区特有の雨がしとしと降っている。建物の方を見ると、すでに上の方の窓からも炎の赤い舌が噴き出していた。この程度の雨では、炎の勢いの方が上回るだろう。
English: They climbed over the reception desk Ma Ming’s men had destroyed in the initial assault and stepped outside into the gentle rain peculiar to Y District. When they looked back, red tongues of flame were already bursting from windows high above. Such light rain could never overcome the force of the fire.

Japanese: クリスがふと振り返ると、建物から脱出したものたちが呆然と炎を眺めている姿が目に映った。プレイ中に追い出された半裸の客や女がいれば、きらびやかなドレス姿の女も、作業着を着た下働きの従業員も、そして武装したクリスの部下たちも、さまざまな立場のものが、さまざまな格好をして、しかし同じような無心の表情で炎を見上げている。彼らすべての瞳に、小さな赤い炎が映っている。
English: Chris happened to turn and saw those who had escaped standing dumbstruck before the flames. There were half-naked patrons and women driven out in the middle of play, women in brilliant dresses, low-ranking employees in work clothes, and Chris’s armed subordinates. People of every station, dressed in every fashion, all gazed upward with the same vacant expression. A tiny red flame was reflected in every eye.

Japanese: クリスにとって、この光景は終生忘れ得ないものとなった。
English: For Chris, it became a sight he would remember until the end of his life.

Japanese: それから四日後、教会通りから一本路地に入った小さな診療所のベッドで太刀川は目を覚ました。
English: Four days later, Tachikawa woke in a bed at a small clinic one alley off Church Street.

Japanese: 彼は金具の塗装があちこちはげて錆が浮かんだベッドの上で、腕が点滴に繋がれ、おむつをはかされ、尿道には排尿用のカテーテルが差し込まれている自分を発見する。
English: He found himself lying upon a bed whose metal fittings had lost their paint in places and begun to rust, one arm connected to an intravenous drip, a diaper around his waist, and a urinary catheter inserted into his urethra.

Japanese: 部屋をざっと見回すと、古い木造建築で、柱の木材は経年によって茶色く変色し、白い壁紙はその端が剥がれかけていた。窓が開いていて、その向こうにこの街では珍しい青い空と白い雲がみえる。ときどき風がそよいで、窓に吊された風鈴が音を立てる。
English: A quick look around revealed an old wooden building. Age had stained the timber pillars brown, and the edges of the white wallpaper had begun to peel. The window stood open, showing blue sky and white clouds of a kind seldom seen in this city. Now and then a breeze stirred the wind chime hanging there and set it ringing.

Japanese: 小学生時代に田舎の祖父母の家をなんとなく思い出されるようなレトロな光景で、太刀川は、ここ何年もの暗い出来事が、すべて少年の自分が見た長い長い悪夢だったような錯覚さえおこしそうだ。
English: The nostalgic scene vaguely reminded him of his grandparents’ country home when he was in elementary school. Tachikawa could almost succumb to the illusion that all the dark events of the past several years had been nothing more than a long, long nightmare dreamed by his boyhood self.

Japanese: そうして本物の自分はあの薄くて畳のかたさが背中にこたえる寝床の中で目を覚まし、祖母が焼いてくれたしょっぱいタラコと、キノコと豆腐の入った味噌汁で、白米をこれでもかというほど沢山食べるのだ。その日を、どんなやりかたで目一杯楽しんでやろうかと計画を練りながら。
English: His real self would awaken in that thin bed, the hardness of the tatami pressing against his back, then eat bowl upon bowl of white rice with the salty cod roe his grandmother had grilled and miso soup full of mushrooms and tofu—all while making plans to wring every possible pleasure from the day ahead.

Japanese: 「ミアオ……」
English: “Miao...”

Japanese: 少年時代の記憶に思いをはせていたはずなのに、ふと口から漏れたのは全く関係ない別の名だった。
English: Though his thoughts had been wandering through childhood memories, the name that suddenly escaped his lips belonged to something else entirely.

Japanese: 太刀川はそんな自分に驚きつつ、そして最後の瞬間の少し前に見せた彼女の微笑みが脳裏に浮かんだ。そうするともう、とめどもなく思い出が彼の感情を埋め尽くし、それは涙となって流れ出た。
English: Tachikawa surprised himself. Then he remembered the smile she had shown shortly before the end. Memory after memory flooded in, filled his heart, and spilled from him as tears.

Japanese: 泣き終わるのを見計らうように中年の看護師が姿を現し、太刀川は彼女にクリスを呼ぶよう頼んだ。
English: A middle-aged nurse appeared as though she had waited for his weeping to end. Tachikawa asked her to summon Chris.

Japanese: 「もう起きないんじゃないかと心配したぜ」
English: “I was starting to worry you’d never wake up.”

Japanese: クリスは冗談めかして笑う。
English: Chris laughed as though making a joke.

Japanese: 「さっき看護師の方に聞きました。私は四日も眠り込んでいたのですね」
English: “The nurse just told me. I was asleep for four whole days, wasn’t I?”

Japanese: 「そうだよ。まったく、気が気じゃなかったぜ。……あとそうだ、ここのやつらは口が固い。ドクターの身体のこととかは、誰にも言う心配がないから安心しなよ」
English: “That’s right. Honestly, I was worried sick. ...Oh, and the people here know how to keep their mouths shut. You don’t have to worry about anyone learning about your body or anything else.”

Japanese: 「そうですか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 太刀川はそう言って目を細めた。
English: Tachikawa narrowed his eyes as he spoke.

Japanese: 「しかし、無茶苦茶するなあ。あんなの、誰だって危険だってわかるぜ。本当に二度と目が覚めなくてもおかしくなかったんじゃないか？」
English: “But that was completely insane. Anyone could tell how dangerous it was. You really might never have woken up again, you know?”

Japanese: おどけるクリスの様子に、太刀川は薄く苦笑して、
English: Tachikawa gave a faint, wry smile at Chris’s bantering manner.

Japanese: 「確かに後先考えずに行動してしまいましたが、でも、やって良かったと感じています」
English: “It is true that I acted without thinking of the consequences. Nevertheless, I am glad I did it.”

Japanese: 「まあ、満足出来たのならいいけどさ……」
English: “Well, if you’re satisfied, I suppose that’s what matters...”

Japanese: クリスは口ではそう言うが、顔は納得出来ない様子だった。
English: Chris said the words, but his face showed that he was not convinced.

Japanese: 気を遣ってその顔の方をみないように視線をそらしている太刀川は、彼の表情に気づかぬまま言葉を続ける。
English: Tachikawa had considerately averted his eyes and did not notice the expression as he continued.

Japanese: 「私は極限状態の精神を恐れ、今までシンクロしないようにして来たんですよ。でも、今回はじめてそれをやりました。そしたら、とても不思議な感覚が生まれたんですよ」
English: “I have always feared minds in extreme states and avoided synchronizing with them. This was the first time I ever attempted it. And when I did, an extremely strange sensation arose.”

Japanese: 「不思議な感覚？」
English: “A strange sensation?”

Japanese: 「それは、ただ死に行く人の心だからというだけじゃ説明がつかない。彼女がタイプBだったせいもあるのでしょう……とても独特で不思議な世界で、体験したことのないものでした。その余韻として、しこりのようなものが心に残っているんです。今でも。……いや、しこりというより、彼女の魂が私の心のなかに存在しているような。……わかりますか？」
English: “It cannot be explained merely by the fact that it was the mind of someone dying. Perhaps Miao’s being a Type B also played a part... It was a unique and mysterious world, unlike anything I had ever experienced. The experience has left something like a knot within my mind. Even now. ...No, rather than a knot, it feels almost as though her soul exists inside my mind. ...Do you understand?”

Japanese: 「わかるような……わからないような……。いや、やっぱり全然わからないな！」
English: “I think I do... and then I think I don’t... No, I don’t understand at all!”

Japanese: クリスはそう言って苦笑する。
English: Chris said it with a wry smile.

Japanese: 「そうですか、残念ですね。でも、とにかくこれはとても重要なもののような気がするんですよ。何か新しい価値観を与えてくれそうな……。あの世界の向こうには、とても穏やかで平和な……満ち足りた……そんなものがあるような気がします。もしかしたら逆に酷くおそろしいものかもしれませんが」
English: “I see. That is unfortunate. In any event, I feel as though this is something extremely important. As though it might give me some new way of seeing the world... I have the sense that beyond that world lies something extraordinarily tranquil and peaceful... something complete. Though it may be something terrible and frightening instead.”

Japanese: そこで一旦切って彼の顔を見ると、肩をすくめて、「わからない」というジェスチャーをとってみせる。
English: He paused there and looked at Chris, who shrugged in a gesture of incomprehension.

Japanese: 「とにかく、私は今までこの能力を疎ましく思ったりしたものですが、おかげで、今はそんな風には感じません。サイキックとして生まれて、人の心を分かち合う力を与えられて、幸運だと素直に思えます」
English: “In any event, there were times when I resented this ability in the past, but thanks to what happened, I no longer feel that way. I can honestly consider myself fortunate to have been born a psychic and given the power to share another person’s heart.”

Japanese: 「そうか、それは良かった。……とにかく、本当に良かったよ！　目を覚ましてくれてさ。その調子ですぐに元気になって、バリバリ働いてもらわなくちゃな！　これからＹＳはどんどん大きくなる。それと同時に、おれとドクターの仕事もスケールがでかくなって行くだろう。もう誰にも馬鹿にさせない。地を這い回るチンピラじゃないんだ。そして、この新しい世界でやっていくためにはあんたの力が必要だ。おれ、ドクターのためにどんなポストがいいのか、考えておいたんだぜ？」
English: “I see. That’s good. ...In any case, I’m just glad you woke up! You’ll have to get well at once and come work yourself to the bone! YS is going to keep growing, and the work you and I do will grow in scale right along with it. We won’t let anyone look down on us again. We’re not petty thugs crawling through the dirt. And I need your power if we’re going to make our way in this new world. I’ve already been thinking about the best position for you, Doctor. Want to hear?”

Japanese: 「そうですか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 太刀川は申し訳なさそうに顔を歪めて、
English: Tachikawa winced apologetically.

Japanese: 「それはとても光栄です。しかし、その話、請けることは出来ません」
English: “I am greatly honored. But I cannot accept.”

Japanese: 「どうしてだい？」
English: “Why not?”

Japanese: 「また、医者に戻ろうと思うんです。だから、こういった仕事はもう出来ません」
English: “I intend to become a doctor again. That means I can no longer do this kind of work.”

Japanese: 「そうか。……それじゃあ、おれも引き留めるわけにもいかねえな。残念だけどさ……」
English: “I see. ...Then I guess I can’t try to stop you. Much as I hate to lose you...”

Japanese: クリスは何か言いたそうだったが、言わず、頭をボリボリと乱暴に掻いた。
English: Chris appeared to have something more to say, but left it unspoken and scrubbed roughly at his scalp.

Japanese: 「そう遠くへ行くわけじゃありませんよ。街の外れにタイプＢ専用の古い病院があったでしょう？　あそこで働けないかなと思って」
English: “I will not be going far. There was an old hospital reserved for Type Bs on the outskirts of the city, wasn’t there? I thought I might see whether they would let me work there.”

Japanese: 「えっ『タイプＢ収容所』のことか？　あんなところで働くなんて、気が知れない。だって、患者は頭のイカレたタイプＢばっかりなんだぜ？　何が楽しくって、そんなことを」
English: “What, the ‘Type B Internment Center’? I can’t imagine why anyone would want to work in a place like that. The patients are all Type Bs who are out of their minds, aren’t they? What could possibly be enjoyable about—”

Japanese: 「私は今まで発症したタイプＢの目を見たことがありません。怖かったからです。でも、今は違う。彼らの心を見てみたい。きっとそこに、ミアオが残してくれた宿題に対する手がかりがあるはずなのです」
English: “Until now, I have never looked into the eyes of a Type B whose symptoms had manifested. I was afraid. But that has changed. I want to look into their hearts. I am certain that somewhere within them lies a clue to the task Miao left me.”

Japanese: 「理解出来ねえな……」
English: “I don’t understand you...”

Japanese: クリスははあと溜息をついて、
English: Chris let out a long sigh.

Japanese: 「まあ、理解は出来ないが、あんたらしいぜ。なんたって、一度は医者の立場を捨ててギャングの手伝いをした男だからな」
English: “Well, I may not understand, but it certainly sounds like you. After all, you’re a man who once abandoned his position as a doctor to help a gang.”

Japanese: 残念そうに言うと、口を歪めて複雑な笑いを浮かべた。
English: He spoke regretfully, then twisted his mouth into a conflicted smile.

Japanese: 「ありがとうクリス。おかげで貴重な体験が出来ました」
English: “Thank you, Chris. You have given me an invaluable experience.”

Japanese: 「こちらこそ、ドクター。あんたがいなきゃ、こんな成功はなかった」
English: “And thank you, Doctor. We never could have achieved this without you.”

Japanese: そう言ってから、クリスは鼻を啜り、
English: After speaking, Chris sniffed.

Japanese: 「……あの帰りに雨に打たれてから少し風邪気味でね。おまけに、ひどい眠気で、どこでもかまわず眠っちまうんだ」
English: “...I’ve had a bit of a cold since I got soaked in the rain on the way back. And I’ve been terribly sleepy on top of it. I keep dozing off wherever I happen to be.”

Japanese: 「大丈夫ですか？　医者には診てもらいましたか？」
English: “Are you all right? Have you seen a doctor?”

Japanese: 「どうってことないさ」
English: “It’s nothing.”

Japanese: クリスはふざけたような笑みをみせて、
English: Chris gave a playful smile.

Japanese: 「まあ、気持はわかった。今後は他人として振る舞うよ。ギャングとつき合いがあるとなっちゃ、医者の仕事に差し支えるだろうからな。でも、いつでも帰って来ていいんだぜ？　なんたって、ＹＳは半分あんたが作ったようなものなんだから」
English: “Well, I understand what you want. From now on, we’ll act like strangers. Being associated with a gang would interfere with your work as a doctor, after all. But you can always come back, you hear? YS is practically half your creation.”

Japanese: 「ありがとう」
English: “Thank you.”

Japanese: 太刀川は一言だけそう返した。
English: That was Tachikawa’s only reply.

Japanese: クリスも、もうそれ以上は余計な言葉は口にせず、
English: Chris said nothing further.

Japanese: 「お大事に」
English: “Take care.”

Japanese: 最後に一言そう言い、病室を出て行った。
English: With that last remark, he left the hospital room.

Japanese: ドアがパタンと音を立ててしまったあと、太刀川は目を閉じ、そしてすぐにすやすやと寝息を立て始めた。
English: After the door closed with a soft click, Tachikawa shut his eyes and was soon breathing softly in sleep.

Japanese: ――これ以降二人が顔を合わせることはなく、次に彼らが出会うのは十五年もの長い月日が流れたあと、クリスが病に倒れ、死の床についてからだった。
English: —The two would not see one another again until fifteen long years had passed, when Chris fell ill and lay upon his deathbed.

Japanese: グランドタワー三十五階。第三代龍頭謝亮（ツェー・ルオン）と同じフロアに執務室を与えられたトーマス・リャオはパソコンの数字を前に、閉口しきっていた。
English: Thomas Liao had been given an office on the thirty-fifth floor of Grand Tower, the same floor occupied by Tse Leung, third Longtou of YS. Now he sat before the figures on his computer, utterly at a loss.

Japanese: 難しい顔をして、唸ったり、溜息をついたり、首を捻ったりしており、その様子を彼のボディガード兼秘書であるアイスが心配そうに見守っている。
English: His face was grave. He groaned, sighed, and tilted his head this way and that, while Ice—his bodyguard and secretary—watched with concern.

Japanese: 謝亮の新体制になって、父親廖志明のファミリーは執行部に吸収され、トーマス自身も執行部に所属する幹部として組織の一部に組み込まれた。しかし現状実態はトーマスが父の業務を引き継ぎ、旧廖ファミリーのリーダーとして執務に当たっている。
English: Under Tse Leung’s new regime, his father Liao Chi-ming’s Family had been absorbed into the executive body, while Thomas himself had been incorporated into the organization as an officer of that body. In practical terms, however, Thomas had inherited his father’s duties and continued to work as leader of the former Liao Family.

Japanese: 彼が今脂汗をかき、苦しみながら眺めている数字の羅列はファミリーの月間収支報告だった。そこには、直接経営するヤミ金業者や飲食店の売り上げや支出、一般店舗から徴収したみかじめ料など、金銭に関するありとあらゆる数字がまとめられている。
English: The rows of figures he now studied in torment, beads of greasy sweat standing on his brow, belonged to the Family’s monthly financial report. They compiled every conceivable number pertaining to money: the income and expenditures of directly operated loan sharks and restaurants, the protection money collected from ordinary shops, and much more besides.

Japanese: この数字の見方は、父の代からの秘書である李（リー）という男から説明を受けてはいるのだが、リーダーとしてこの数字をどう理解し、組織運営に反映させていいのかさっぱりわからず、ひたすら苦しんでいるのである。
English: A man named Lee, who had served as secretary since his father’s time, had explained how to read the figures. Thomas nevertheless had no idea how a leader was supposed to interpret them or put them to use in running the organization. He could only sit there and suffer.

Japanese: 彼は学校の授業でも、数字を扱う教科は不得意で、数学の試験の時間は真っ赤な顔で空欄ばかりのテスト用紙を眺めて過ごしていたのである。数字に対しては、ほとんどアレルギーのような苦手意識があった。
English: Even in school, Thomas had been poor at subjects involving numbers. During mathematics examinations, he would spend the entire period staring red-faced at an answer sheet covered in blanks. He was practically allergic to numbers.

Japanese: 「あの、李さんもそれとなく確認しておけばいいとおっしゃっていたし、そんなにむきになって理解しようとしなくても良いのではないのでしょうか？」
English: “Mr. Lee did say that it would be enough for you to give them a general review. Perhaps you need not be quite so determined to understand every detail?”

Japanese: 見るに見かねたアイスがそう提案するが、トーマスは首を横に振る。
English: Unable to watch any longer, Ice offered the suggestion. Thomas shook his head.

Japanese: 「父さんはこういう数字を沢山見て、ずばずばとリーダーシップを発揮していたんでしょう？　それならば、僕も出来る限りやらなくちゃ」
English: “Father looked at lots of figures like these and exercised decisive leadership, didn’t he? Then I have to do everything I can as well.”

Japanese: 「お父様は元々商売をなさっていて、こうした数字の扱いには精通していらっしゃったわけですから。トーマス様はお父様とは違うのですし、それはみな理解していますから、トーマス様なりのやり方でいいのではないかと……」
English: “Your father was originally a businessman and thoroughly familiar with figures of this kind. You are a different person, Master Thomas, and everyone understands that. I believe it would be entirely proper for you to do things in your own way...”

Japanese: そう言われても、やはりトーマスには素直に受け入れるわけには行かないが、しかし、やりなれないことをして既に疲労困憊だった。
English: Even put that way, Thomas could not simply accept the advice. Yet the unfamiliar work had already exhausted him.

Japanese: コーヒーカップのすっかり冷めた珈琲を飲み、溜息をついて、椅子ごとくるりとアイスに振り返る。
English: He drank the coffee that had gone completely cold in his cup, sighed, then spun his chair around to face Ice.

Japanese: 「こういう数字って、他のギャングのボスたちも見たりしているの？」
English: “Do the bosses of the other gangs look at figures like these too?”

Japanese: 「ある程度は会計係から報告があると思いますが、こんな細かい数字を一々チェックするところはまずあり得ないと思います」
English: “I imagine they receive reports from their accountants to some extent, but I very much doubt that any of them inspects such detailed figures one by one.”

Japanese: 「そうか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: トーマスは安心したように溜息をつく。
English: Thomas released a sigh of relief.

Japanese: 「あ、でも、確か謝亮様はわざわざ細かい書類を作らせて、全部目を通したとか……」
English: “Ah, though as I recall, Master Tse Leung went to the trouble of having detailed documents prepared and read through all of them...”

Japanese: 「ああ、小謝はそこまでやってるのか。さすがだね……」
English: “Oh, Siu Tse goes that far too? Impressive...”

Japanese: 「トーマス様、もう謝亮様のことは『小謝』と呼ばずに、『龍頭』と呼ぶのではなかったのですか？」
English: “Master Thomas, had you not decided that you would stop calling Master Tse Leung ‘Siu Tse’ and address him as ‘Longtou’?”

Japanese: 「そうだった！　どうしても忘れちゃう。……まあ、とにかく、龍頭がそこまでやっているのなら、僕だって自分でもうちょっとやらないといけないね」
English: “That’s right! I can’t help forgetting. ...Well, in any case, if the Longtou does that much, I have to do a little more myself too.”

Japanese: 「謝亮様とトーマス様も違ってもいいではないですか」
English: “Surely there is no harm in Master Tse Leung and Master Thomas doing things differently.”

Japanese: 「そうはいかないよ！　アイスだって笑っちゃうだろうけど、僕は一応彼をライバルだと思ってるんだからね。お互いを高め合う関係で居たいんだ。彼はそうは思ってないだろうけどさ」
English: “That won’t do! You may laugh at me, Ice, but I do consider him my rival, after a fashion. I want us to help one another improve. Though I doubt he thinks the same of me.”

Japanese: 「私は笑ったりはしません」
English: “I would never laugh at you.”

Japanese: 「そうか。ありがとう」
English: “I see. Thank you.”

Japanese: トーマスは苦い顔をしながらも、またモニターの方を向くが、数字の羅列が目に入った途端頭がクラクラとする。
English: Still wearing a pained expression, Thomas faced the monitor once more. The instant the rows of figures entered his eyes, his head began to spin.

Japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと休憩……」
English: “I-I need a little break...”

Japanese: 彼は椅子を立ち、気分転換に窓の外を眺めるが、三十五階からの眺めは高所恐怖症のトーマスには、やはり頭をクラクラとさせる要素でしかなかった。
English: He rose from his chair and looked out the window for a change of pace. But for Thomas, who was afraid of heights, the view from the thirty-fifth floor only made his head spin all over again.

Japanese: 顔を真っ青にしながら椅子に座り、頭を抱える。
English: His face deathly pale, he sat again and clutched his head.

Japanese: 「トーマス様、だ、大丈夫ですか？」
English: “M-Master Thomas, are you all right?”

Japanese: 「大丈夫だよ。大丈夫……あ、そうだアイス……」
English: “I’m fine. Fine... Oh, that’s right, Ice...”

Japanese: トーマスは顔を上げて、
English: Thomas raised his face.

Japanese: 「あのベトナム料理屋のタンさんの娘さんが、独立してスイーツの屋台をはじめたんだって。結構評判いいらしいから、ちょっと視察に行かないか？」
English: “I heard Mr. Tan’s daughter from that Vietnamese restaurant has struck out on her own and opened a dessert stall. It seems to have a very good reputation. Why don’t we go conduct an inspection?”

Japanese: 「視察……ですか？」
English: “An inspection...?”

Japanese: 急に生き返ったような生き生きとした表情で語りかけるトーマスに、アイスは若干驚きを浮かべつつ応えた。
English: Ice answered with mild surprise at the sight of Thomas suddenly animated, as though he had sprung back to life.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。視察だよ。数字も大事だけれど、自分の傘下のお店が、どんな美味しいものを作ってるか、この目と舌で確認するのも大事な仕事だよね。さあ、そうと決まれば今すぐ行こう！」
English: “That’s right—an inspection. Figures are important, but surely it’s also a vital part of my work to use my own eyes and tongue to learn what delicious things the shops in my care are making. Now that we’ve settled that, let’s go at once!”

Japanese: 「あ、は、はい」
English: “Ah... Y-yes.”

Japanese: トーマスは戸惑うアイスの手を掴むと、その丸っこい身体を鞠のように弾ませながら、小走りで部屋を出た。
English: Thomas seized the bewildered Ice by the hand and trotted from the room, his round body bouncing like a rubber ball.

Japanese: 「外出なさるのなら、李さんか誰かに連絡をしないと……」
English: “If you are going out, we ought to inform Mr. Lee or someone else...”

Japanese: 「良いって良いって、ちょっとの時間だし、出る時に駐車場の人に言っておけば大丈夫だから」
English: “It’s fine, it’s fine. We’ll only be gone a little while. I’ll tell the people in the parking garage on our way out.”

Japanese: 「しかし、また李さんが怒りますよ」
English: “But Mr. Lee will be angry with you again.”

Japanese: アイスはあきれ顔でそう言った。
English: Ice said it with an exasperated expression.

Japanese: つい先日も、今のように視察と行って街に出かけたきり、暗闇通りの子供達と夕方まで遊び惚け、あの白髪の老人にいつものしかめっつらで小言を言われたばかりなのである。
English: Only a few days earlier, Thomas had likewise gone into the city on an ‘inspection,’ then lost track of time playing with the children of Darkness Street until evening. He had only just been scolded by the white-haired old man, wearing his customary scowl.

Japanese: 「いいんだよ。これもが僕の仕事なんだから」
English: “It’s all right. This is part of my work too.”

Japanese: トーマスは全く気にすることなく笑っている。
English: Thomas laughed, entirely unconcerned.

Japanese: 最上階から一階まで降りるには、十五階で一度エレベーターを乗り換えなくてはいけないのがこのビルのややこしいところだ。
English: One of the complications of this building was that a journey from the top floor to the first required changing elevators once on the fifteenth floor.

Japanese: その乗り換えのところで、二人は思わぬ人物に出くわした。
English: At that transfer point, the two encountered people they had not expected to see.

Japanese: 三人の屈強な男に囲まれるように、二人の若い女が立っている。彼らはエレベーターを待っており、こちらに背を向けてドアの上の階表示を見上げていた。
English: Two young women stood surrounded by three powerfully built men. Waiting for the elevator, they had their backs turned as they looked up at the floor indicator above the doors.

Japanese: 「やあ」
English: “Hello.”

Japanese: トーマスは気さくに声をかける。
English: Thomas greeted them casually.

Japanese: 振り向いた二人の褐色の肌をした美女は、フェルナンデス家の娘、長女アウロラと三女リタだった。こうして近づくと二人とも香水の良いにおいがした。トーマスはその臭いにあてられながら、内心で（アイスも負けないくらい美人なんだから何かつければいいのに）と思った。
English: The two beautiful, brown-skinned women who turned were daughters of the Fernandes Family: Aurora, the eldest, and Rita, the youngest. Up close, both smelled pleasantly of perfume. Half overwhelmed by the scent, Thomas thought, (Ice is every bit as beautiful. She ought to wear something herself.)

Japanese: まわりの男たちはフェルナンデス・ファミリーのメンバーで、彼女たちのボディガードだろう。
English: The men around them were presumably Fernandes Family members serving as their bodyguards.

Japanese: 「こんにちは、今日は小謝にでも用事があったの？」
English: “Hello. Did you have some business with Siu Tse today?”

Japanese: トーマスはいつも通りのニコニコとした円満な笑みで、この子供の頃からのつき合いである二人の女にそう言った。
English: Wearing his usual amiable smile, Thomas addressed the two women he had known since childhood.

Japanese: しかし、相手は虫の居所が良くないようだった。
English: They, however, appeared to be in a very poor humor.

Japanese: 「そうよ。断りに来たの」
English: “We did. We came to refuse him.”

Japanese: アウロラはぴりぴりとした苛立たしげな態度であった。
English: Aurora’s manner bristled with irritation.

Japanese: その隣のリタも、いつも以上におどおどとして落ち着きがない。
English: Rita beside her was even more nervous and restless than usual.

Japanese: 「断るって？　何を？」
English: “Refuse what?”

Japanese: 「結婚よ」
English: “Marriage.”

Japanese: 「誰の結婚？」
English: “Whose marriage?”

Japanese: 「もう大分前のことだけど、トミーは知らなかったの？　小謝はリタに結婚を申し込んでいたのよ」
English: “It was some time ago now, but didn’t you know, Tommy? Siu Tse asked Rita to marry him.”

Japanese: 「えーっ！」
English: “What?”

Japanese: トーマスは目を丸くして、辺りをはばからない大きな声で叫んでしまう。
English: Thomas’s eyes widened, and he shouted loudly without regard for anyone around them.

Japanese: 「小謝が？　きみに？」
English: “Siu Tse? You?”
“Y-yes...”

Japanese: リタは気まずそうに頷く。
English: Rita nodded awkwardly.

Japanese: 「ちっとも知らなかった。驚いたなあ……。アイスは知ってた？」
English: “I had no idea. What a surprise... Did you know, Ice?”

Japanese: アイスは無言で首を横に振る。
English: Ice silently shook her head.

Japanese: 「そうだよね。しかし、アウロラはなんでそんなに怒ってるんだい？　別にプロポーズされたって、怒るようなことじゃないでしょう。もしかして、リタがすごくいやだったの？　小謝のことが嫌いだとか？　全然そうは見えなかったけど……」
English: “I thought not. But why are you so angry, Aurora? There’s no reason to be angry merely because he proposed, is there? Did Rita hate the idea that much? Does she dislike Siu Tse? It never looked that way to me...”

Japanese: リタは俯いたまま応えようとしない。
English: Rita kept her face lowered and made no attempt to answer.

Japanese: 「トミー、小謝はね、リタを利用しようとしてるだけなのよ？」
English: “Tommy, Siu Tse is only trying to use Rita.”

Japanese: かわりにアウロラがその美しく整えられた眉をしかめながら言う。
English: Aurora spoke in her place, drawing together her beautifully shaped eyebrows.

Japanese: 「あいつはいま、YSに所属してるファミリーを全部自分の部下にしようとしてるでしょ？　うちのお父さんは絶対反対だし、私たちだってそんなの我慢がならないわ。だから、リタを騙してそこから取り入ろうとしたの。リタがあいつのことを好きなの知って、気持を踏みにじったのよ！」
English: “He’s trying to bring every Family in YS under his command now, isn’t he? Father will never accept that, and neither will we. So he tried to deceive Rita and use her to gain a foothold. He knew she was in love with him, and he trampled all over her feelings!”

Japanese: 「リタ、きみは彼のことが好きだったの？　それに、取り入るだなんて、そんな言い方は……」
English: “Rita, were you in love with him? And gaining a foothold—surely you don’t have to put it that way...”

Japanese: トーマスはアウロラの言葉に驚きつつそう訊ねた。
English: Thomas asked the question in surprise at Aurora’s words.

Japanese: 「トミー、私は……」
English: “Tommy, I...”

Japanese: リタが何か言いかけたが、アウロラが遮った。
English: Rita began to speak, but Aurora cut her off.

Japanese: 「他に言いようがないわ。卑怯なやり方よ。小謝は変わってしまったわ。こんな冷酷なやつだとは思わなかった。彼が龍頭になってからしたことって、やりかたに反対する仲間をどんどん追放したり、殺したり、YSの昔からのルールを変えたり、そんなことばっかり！　これからこの街はどうなってしまうの？」
English: “There’s no other way to put it. It was cowardly. Siu Tse has changed. I never knew he could be so cold-blooded. Since becoming Longtou, all he’s done is expel or kill comrades who oppose his methods and rewrite the old rules of YS! What is going to happen to this city?”

Japanese: アウロラはそう吐き捨てて、舌打ちをする。
English: Aurora spat out the words and clicked her tongue.

Japanese: 「アウロラの言い分もよくわかるけど、小謝は小謝で、色々考えてやってるんだと思うよ……」
English: “I understand your position, Aurora. But I think Siu Tse has reasons of his own for what he’s doing...”

Japanese: トーマスは悲しげな表情でそう言った。
English: Thomas spoke with a sorrowful expression.

Japanese: 心優しい彼にすれば、事情がどうあれアウロラがこんな風に謝亮のことを憎々しく罵っているという状況が耐えがたいものであった。
English: Kindhearted as he was, Thomas could not bear to hear Aurora speak of Tse Leung with such bitter hatred, whatever the circumstances.

Japanese: 「自分のことしか考えてないわ。ねえ、トミー、大体なんであなたはそんなヘラヘラとしていられるの？」
English: “He only thinks of himself. And Tommy, why are you able to stand there grinning like a fool?”

Japanese: アウロラがずいと顔を近づける。
English: Aurora thrust her face toward him.

Japanese: 「え、僕が？」
English: “What, me?”

Japanese: トーマスは若干のけぞりながらそうこたえる。
English: Thomas leaned back slightly as he answered.

Japanese: 「そうよ。お父さんがあんな目に遭わされて、自分のファミリーは全部小謝たちに奪われて、それで平気で居られるのが信じられない」
English: “Yes, you. After what he did to your father—after Siu Tse’s people took your entire Family away from you—I can’t believe you can act as though nothing happened.”

Japanese: 「と、父さんは小謝の考えに納得して、相談役として身を引いただけで……」
English: “F-Father came to understand Siu Tse’s thinking and simply stepped back into an advisory role...”

Japanese: 目をそらして言い訳をしようとするトーマスを、アウロラは許さない。
English: Aurora did not permit Thomas, who had averted his eyes, to escape into excuses.

Japanese: 「そんなの嘘だってみんな知ってるわよ。脅迫されたんでしょ？　なんで怒らないの？　それでもあなた男なの？」
English: “Everyone knows that’s a lie. He was threatened, wasn’t he? Why aren’t you angry? Are you even a man?”

Japanese: 「元々は、父さんが発端だったんだし……それに、ぼ、僕は……」
English: “Father was the one who started it... And b-besides, I...”

Japanese: トーマスは顔を上げてアウロラの視線を正面から見つめ返すと、
English: Thomas raised his face and met Aurora’s eyes directly.

Japanese: 「小謝の考え方もわかるんだ。アウロラが言うような、自分のことばかり考えているってわけじゃないと思う。もう少し、信じたらどうだろう？　いろいろ言われてるけど、僕の部下たちもすごく良くして貰ってるし、思った以上に義勝の人達と連携がとれてる。彼はきっとアウロラのことだってちゃんと考えていると思う。リタを悲しませるつもりだってなかったと思う。もちろん、結婚のことは僕からはどうこう言える話じゃないけど……」
English: “I understand Siu Tse’s way of thinking too. I don’t believe he considers only himself, the way you say. Couldn’t you place a little more trust in him? Whatever people may say, my subordinates have been treated very well, and they’re cooperating with the old Yisheng people much better than I expected. I’m sure he has thought carefully about your position too. I don’t believe he ever intended to hurt Rita. Of course, their marriage isn’t a matter on which I have any right to speak...”

Japanese: 「まあ、すっかり洗脳されてるのね」
English: “Well. He’s thoroughly brainwashed you.”

Japanese: アウロラは驚いて目を丸くすると、
English: Aurora’s eyes widened in surprise.

Japanese: 「それなら、あなたとも話すことはなさそうね。残念だわ」
English: “Then it seems I have nothing to discuss with you either. How unfortunate.”

Japanese: 溜息をつき首を左右に振る。
English: She sighed and shook her head.

Japanese: 「リタ、行きましょう」
English: “Rita, let’s go.”

Japanese: そして彼女たちは、とっくにドアが開いているエレベーターに乗り込んだ。
English: The women stepped into the elevator, whose doors had long since opened.

Japanese: 「さようならトミー。きっと近いうちにこの街はYSが出来る前みたいな混乱に戻ってしまうけど、あなたとは敵にならないよう願ってるわ」
English: “Goodbye, Tommy. I’m sure this city will soon return to the chaos it knew before YS was created, but I hope you and I will not become enemies.”

Japanese: 硬い表情でそう告げると、ドアは閉まり、エレベーターは降りていった。
English: With that hard-faced farewell, the elevator doors closed on the two women and carried them down.

Japanese: 残されたトーマスは溜息をついてから、
English: Thomas, left behind, sighed.

Japanese: 「僕らも降りるつもりだったのに、閉め出されちゃったね」
English: “We meant to go down too, but they shut us out.”

Japanese: と苦笑を浮かべた。
English: He gave a wry smile.

Japanese: 「せっかくだから、ちょっと小謝と話してから出かけようか？」
English: “Since we’re here, why don’t we speak with Siu Tse before we go out?”

Japanese: 「はい」
English: “Very well.”

Japanese: そして二人は来た道を引き返す。
English: The two retraced their steps.

Japanese: 「確かにね、アウロラの言い分は理解出来るんだ」
English: “I really do understand Aurora’s position.”

Japanese: トーマスは歩きながら、先ほど書類と格闘していた時の情けない顔とは別人のような真面目な表情でそう言った。
English: As he walked, Thomas spoke with a serious expression utterly unlike the pathetic face he had worn while wrestling with the documents.

Japanese: 「フェルナンデス・ファミリーは昔から独立独歩だったものね。YSは連盟という形だから参加出来ていたけれど、それでもやっぱりずっと執行部の干渉は許さないで来た。……彼らはあくまでも同じ出身地の仲間を守るための組織でいたいだけで、本当のギャングにはなりたくなかったんだよ。だから、小謝がやろうとしている、今までのグループを解体して地域や民族の壁を取り払った組織にしようっていうのは絶対に受けいれらない」
English: “The Fernandes Family has always followed its own independent course. They could participate in YS because it took the form of a federation, but even then, they never permitted interference from the executive body. ...They only want to remain an organization that protects people from the same homeland. They never wished to become a true gang. That means they can never accept Siu Tse’s attempt to dismantle the existing groups and build an organization without regional or ethnic barriers.”

Japanese: トーマスはまっすぐ前だけを見ながら歩いている。隣を歩くアイスは、その真剣な横顔をチラチラと見ていた。
English: Thomas walked with his eyes fixed straight ahead. Beside him, Ice repeatedly stole glances at his earnest profile.

Japanese: 「でも、結婚は悪くないと思うんだけどな……。政略結婚ってアウロラは言うけれどさ、本当に愛情はないのかな？　正直、小謝がどう考えてるかはわからないけど、リタはきっとどんな形でも結婚が出来たらまんざらでもないかって気がするし、それが不幸だとも限らないと思うんだけど……アイスはどう思う？」
English: “Still, I don’t think marriage would necessarily be bad... Aurora calls it a political marriage, but is there truly no affection in it? To be honest, I don’t know what Siu Tse thinks. But I have a feeling Rita might not be entirely opposed to marrying him, whatever form it took, and that it would not necessarily make her unhappy... What do you think, Ice?”

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 意外な話題を振られてアイスは戸惑いを見せる。
English: Caught off guard by the unexpected subject, Ice showed her bewilderment.

Japanese: 「……私は、そういう男女の機微はちょっとわかりかねます……」
English: “...I am afraid I know very little about such subtleties between men and women...”

Japanese: 亮の執務室につくと、彼の他に秘書兼身のまわりの世話役のレイレイと、見知らぬはげ頭の中年男がいた。亮はシャツ姿で部屋の中央に立ち、男は手に持ったメジャーで身体の各部位を測っている。
English: When they reached Leung’s office, they found Leilei, his secretary and personal attendant, along with an unfamiliar bald man of middle age. Leung stood in the center of the room in his shirtsleeves while the man used a measuring tape on various parts of his body.

Japanese: 「話があったんだけど、今、忙しいみたいだね」
English: “There was something I wanted to discuss, but you seem busy.”

Japanese: その部屋の様子にトーマスが引き返そうとすると、
English: Thomas began to withdraw at the sight.

Japanese: 「いや、このまま話してくれてもかまわないよ」
English: “No, I don’t mind speaking like this.”

Japanese: 身体を計られながら亮はそう答える。
English: Leung answered while the measurements continued.

Japanese: 「スーツを新調しようと思ってね。僕はそのあたりの吊るしで選んでも良かったんだが、馬明はどうしてもオーダーメイドじゃなければいけないと言い張って」
English: “I thought I would have a new suit made. I would have been perfectly satisfied choosing something ready-made, but Ma Ming insisted that nothing less than bespoke would do.”

Japanese: 「そうなんだ」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 男は今は亮の後ろにまわってその肩幅を測っているところだった。
English: The man had now moved behind Leung and was measuring the breadth of his shoulders.

Japanese: 「いや、さっきね、アウロラたちとそこで会って、少し話したんだけど……」
English: “Well, I ran into Aurora and Rita just now, and we spoke for a moment...”

Japanese: トーマスはその男をチラチラと気にしながら言う。外部の人間の前で話してもかまわないのだろうかと、彼は考えていた。
English: Thomas kept glancing toward the man as he spoke, wondering whether they ought to discuss the matter in front of an outsider.

Japanese: 「気にしないで良いよ。この人は父さんの頃から服をお願いしている人で……僕とはそう親しくはないけれど、余計な話をよそで漏らすことの意味をよく知っている人ではあると思う」
English: “You needn’t concern yourself. This gentleman has made clothes for us since Father’s time... I can’t say he and I are particularly close, but I believe he understands perfectly well what it would mean to repeat careless talk elsewhere.”

Japanese: トーマスの気持をくみ取って亮がそう言うと、仕立屋は苦笑する。
English: Leung read Thomas’s concern and offered the explanation. The tailor gave a wry smile.

Japanese: 「なんとつれない。龍頭の小さい頃の服も、作らせて頂いたじゃないですか」
English: “How terribly distant. I had the honor of making clothes for the Longtou when you were a little boy, did I not?”

Japanese: 「これは失礼した。まあ、僕を殺したいやつはそこらじゅうにいるから、つい、ね」
English: “My apologies. Well, people who wish to kill me are everywhere, so the habit comes naturally.”

Japanese: 亮の言う通り、つい先日も彼の暗殺計画が露見したばかりである。
English: Just as Leung said, another plot to assassinate him had come to light only days earlier.

Japanese: 最近彼は執行部配下の構成員の増員を行ったのだが、その時旧義勝とは別の香港人グループを吸収した。このグループはYSが出来る以前に義勝と犬猿のなかだった人々で、今は数人しかいない小さな組織である。
English: He had recently increased the membership under the executive body, absorbing in the process a Hong Kong group outside old Yisheng. Before YS was created, its members and Yisheng had been bitter enemies. By now it was a tiny organization with only a few people remaining.

Japanese: その他、異国人なども多く採用した。
English: He had also recruited many foreigners.

Japanese: これが旧義勝の反謝亮派とも言うべき老人たちの不興を買い、その一人が暗殺者を送り込んだのである。
English: This displeased the old men who might be called the anti-Leung faction within old Yisheng, and one of them sent an assassin.

Japanese: 事前に察知していた謝亮の手配により暗殺者はグランドタワーの内部で射殺されたが、謝亮が第三代龍頭となってから、実に三回目の暗殺事件である。そのうち二回は義勝内部からのものであり、残り一回は暗闇通りに住むタイプBの若者が謝亮を殺せば自分が龍頭になれるという妄想にとりつかれて起こしたものだった。彼は元々はYSの構成員で、ダリオ・ボネットの部下であった。発症して発砲事件を起こしたために除名になった人物である。
English: Through arrangements made by Leung, who detected the plan in advance, the assassin was shot dead inside Grand Tower. It was already the third assassination incident since Leung became the third Longtou. Two had originated within Yisheng. The remaining attempt was committed by a young Type B man from Darkness Street, possessed by the delusion that killing Leung would make him Longtou. He had once belonged to YS as a subordinate of Dario Bonetto, but had been expelled after his symptoms manifested and he caused a shooting incident.

Japanese: ただ、こうした敵対組織の吸収や異国人の採用は父親のクリス・ツェーも何度か行っているもので、このような反発は不当というべきなのだが、そうはいかないのが人間の感情というものなのだろう。
English: Chris Tse himself had absorbed hostile organizations and recruited foreigners on several occasions, so resentment of this kind might fairly have been called unjust. Human emotion, however, rarely submitted to such fairness.

Japanese: 「父さんがやれば許せても、僕が同じことをやったらはらわたが煮えくりかえる連中がいる。それと、父さんみたいな千里眼ではなく、僕みたいな実績も超能力もない若造なら簡単に殺してとってかわれると考えている連中もいる。……まあ、そのうち静かになるさ」
English: “There are people who could forgive Father for something, but boil with rage if I do precisely the same. There are also people who think that a young nobody like me, without Father’s clairvoyance or any achievements or psychic power of my own, can easily be killed and replaced. ...They’ll quiet down eventually.”

Japanese: 馬明が新しい龍頭を受け入れない人々が存在することに腹を立てて怒鳴り散らしたとき、亮はそう笑った。
English: Leung had laughed and said this when Ma Ming raged at the existence of people who refused to accept the new Longtou.

Japanese: エリー・ホワイトは新しい龍頭を積極的に支持しているが、それ以外のフェルナンデス、ボネット、壬生屋などの本心ははっきりしない。彼らも、廖志明のようにクリスが死んで自分のチャンスが巡ってきたと考えているという具合に、疑おうと思えばいくらでも疑うことが出来る状況だ。
English: Ellie White actively supported the new Longtou, but the true feelings of Fernandes, Bonetto, Mibuya, and the others remained unclear. If one chose to be suspicious, there was no end to the possibilities: perhaps, like Liao Chi-ming, they believed Chris’s death had finally brought them their opportunity.

Japanese: さらに、この間廖志明の銅像を破壊し、グランドタワーを一人で血の海に変えたテレポート少女もまだ居場所が見つかっていない。
English: Moreover, the teleporting girl who had recently destroyed Liao Chi-ming’s statue and single-handedly turned Grand Tower into a sea of blood had still not been found.

Japanese: トーマスなどからすればとても生きた心地がしないような生活に思えるのだが、亮は睡眠不足でクマを作るわけでもなく、食欲不振になるでもなく、血色のいい肌つやをしている。
English: To Thomas, such a life seemed scarcely endurable. Yet Leung neither developed dark rings from lack of sleep nor lost his appetite. His skin remained healthy and full of color.

Japanese: 「ねえ小謝、リタに結婚を申し込んだというのは本当なのかい？」
English: “Tell me, Siu Tse. Is it true that you asked Rita to marry you?”

Japanese: トーマスはさっき『小謝』と呼ばないと言ったことをすっかり忘れてそう訊ねた。
English: Thomas asked the question, having completely forgotten his earlier promise to stop calling him Siu Tse.

Japanese: 「本当だよ」
English: “It is.”

Japanese: 「それで断られたって聞いたけれど」
English: “I heard that she refused you.”

Japanese: 「アウロラはとんでもなく怒ってたろう？　あんなに怒るところははじめて見たよ」
English: “Aurora was incredibly angry, wasn’t she? I had never seen her so furious.”

Japanese: 亮はそう言って肩をすくめる。
English: Leung spoke with a shrug.

Japanese: 「そりゃもう、すごい勢いで。政略結婚なんかでリタの気持を踏みにじって許せないって。いますぐにでもフェルナンデス・ファミリーがYSを離脱するような言い方だった」
English: “Oh, she was furious. She said she couldn’t forgive you for trampling on Rita’s feelings with a political marriage. She spoke as though the Fernandes Family might leave YS at any moment.”

Japanese: トーマスの言葉に、亮は溜息をつく。
English: At Thomas’s words, Leung sighed.

Japanese: 「どうしてリタに結婚を申し込んだんだい？　彼女を利用しようとしたのかい？」
English: “Why did you ask Rita to marry you? Were you trying to use her?”

Japanese: 「利用と言うのは言い方がわるいな。丸くおさめるにはそれが一番だと彼女に説明したし、理解してくれていると思う。それに、僕だってもし妻になってくれるならば、その判断に見合ったものを彼女に提供するつもりだったんだ」
English: “‘Use’ is an unpleasant way to put it. I explained to her that it was the best way to settle matters amicably, and I believe she understood. And if she had agreed to become my wife, I intended to offer her something worthy of that decision.”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめる。
English: Leung shrugged.

Japanese: 「上手くいくかどうかはそれほど確信があったわけじゃないけれど、もし成立すれば円満解決だから切り出す価値はあると思ったんだ。……だけど、結果としては僕の判断が甘かった。アウロラがそこまで反対するとはね。リタが僕とくっついて跡を継ぐのがどうしてそんなにいやなんだろう？　アウロラ自身が後継者になりたかったのだろうか？　そうは見えなかったんだが」
English: “I was never particularly certain it would succeed, but if it did, the problem would be resolved peacefully. I thought it worth proposing. ...In the end, though, my judgment was naive. I never imagined Aurora would oppose it so strongly. Why does she hate the idea of Rita ending up with me and succeeding their father? Did Aurora want to become the successor herself? It never appeared that way.”

Japanese: 「た、多分そういう問題じゃないと思うけど。もっと、人情的な部分じゃないかな……。ほら、リタは小謝に気があったような感じだったし……」
English: “I-I don’t think that’s the problem. It’s probably something more personal... Rita did seem to have feelings for you, after all...”

Japanese: トーマスが苦い顔をすると、
English: Thomas grimaced.

Japanese: 「龍頭も、意外と駄目なところあるんですね」
English: “Even the Longtou has some unexpected weaknesses.”

Japanese: アイスがその耳に囁いた。
English: Ice whispered into his ear.

Japanese: 「まあどうでもいいいや。とにかく、結局アウロラが組織を継ぐのかな？　だとしたら先行きが心配だよ。僕らじゃなくて、フェルナンデス・ファミリーのね。彼らにとって一番いい選択肢を用意してあげたつもりなのに」
English: “Well, never mind that. In any case, will Aurora inherit the organization after all? If so, I’m concerned about the future—not ours, but the Fernandes Family’s. I thought I had presented them with the best option available.”

Japanese: 身体を計り終わって、レイレイが亮にジャケットを着せる。彼は部屋の正面にある龍頭用の椅子に腰掛け足を組んだ。黒い革靴の爪先がピカピカと光っている。
English: Once the measurements were finished, Leilei helped Leung into his jacket. He sat in the Longtou’s chair at the front of the room and crossed his legs. The toes of his black leather shoes gleamed.

Japanese: 「離脱したいなら僕に止めることは出来ない。もともとそういう約束で彼らはYSに参加しているんだ」
English: “If they wish to withdraw, I cannot stop them. They entered YS under an agreement that permits precisely that.”

Japanese: 「もし彼らが離れても、抗争にはならないよね？」
English: “Even if they leave, it won’t mean war, will it?”

Japanese: トーマスは心配をあらわにしてそう訊ねる。
English: Thomas asked the question with open concern.

Japanese: 「そう願いたいけれど、先のことはわからない」
English: “I hope not, but no one knows the future.”

Japanese: 「でも、もし敵になったらアウロラたちとも戦うの？」
English: “But if they do become enemies, will you fight Aurora and the others?”

Japanese: 「今の時点でその質問に答えるのは難しいが……」
English: “It is difficult to answer that question at this stage...”

Japanese: 亮は背もたれに身体を伸ばし、
English: Leung settled back against the chair.

Japanese: 「YSの仕事を手伝うようになってから今日まで、街で醜態をさらすバカやら、僕を暗殺しようとするヤツが現れるやらで、僕は十三人殺した。そのなかには血の繋がった親戚もいるし、子供もいる。それが必要ならば、誰が相手だって戦いをためらう例外にはならないんだ。……トミー、きみ以外はみんなそのことを知ってる。もちろんアウロラだってそうだ」
English: “From the day I began helping with YS work until today, idiots have made spectacles of themselves in the city and people have attempted to assassinate me. I have killed thirteen people. Some were my blood relatives, and one was a child. If fighting is necessary, there is no one I would make an exception for or hesitate to confront. ...Everyone but you knows that, Tommy. Aurora included.”

Japanese: 「ごめん、小謝……」
English: “I’m sorry, Siu Tse...”

Japanese: 「あやまる必要はないよ。それがきみの良いところでもあるし……それに、本当はきみのような感じ方をするのが人間としては正常なんだ」
English: “There is no need to apologize. It is one of your good qualities... And in truth, yours is the normal way for a human being to feel.”

Japanese: 亮はそう言って、意味ありげな微笑を浮かべた。
English: Leung gave an enigmatic smile.

Japanese: 「それに、僕だってむざむざ無意味な抗争をするつもりはないよ。僕らとフェルナンデス・ファミリーが戦えば、他の組織につけいる隙を与えるだけだ。木下組だってまた色気が出て来るだろう。すくなくとも僕からふっかけることはしない。むこうがどう考えているかは知らないが。……まあ、もし戦いになっても僕らが確実に勝つけどね」
