English: “Besides, I have no intention of stumbling into a pointless conflict. If we fight the Fernandes Family, we’ll merely leave an opening for other organizations to exploit. Even the Kinoshita-gumi may begin to entertain ambitions here again. I will not be the one to start a fight, at the very least. I don’t know what they intend. ...Though if war does come, we will certainly win.”

Japanese: 仕立屋が頭を一つ下げて部屋を出て行く。彼はそれに頷きを返してから、
English: The tailor bowed and left the room. Leung acknowledged him with a nod, then continued.

Japanese: 「トミー、きみはそのままで居てくれ。そして僕のことを信じて欲しい。僕は毎日の仕事に手応えを感じている。きっと最終的には全部僕の思った通りになるだろうし、それはきみにとっても悪い結論ではないはずだ。このYSは、今までよりもっと強く巨大な、そして素晴らしい組織になるよ」
English: “Tommy, I want you to remain exactly as you are. And I want you to trust me. Every day, I feel that my work is bearing fruit. In the end, I am sure everything will turn out as I intend, and the result should not be a bad one for you either. This YS will become stronger and greater than ever before—a magnificent organization.”

Japanese: 「……小謝、僕は、子供の時からこれまで一度もきみを疑おうなんて思ったことはないよ」
English: “...Siu Tse, not once since we were children have I ever considered doubting you.”

Japanese: そして謝亮はこれから別の人間と会う予定があるとのことで、トーマスとアイスの二人はそのまま部屋を辞した。
English: Leung had another appointment, so Thomas and Ice took their leave.

Japanese: 「いやあ、ミスターリャオがわざわざ足を運んでくれるなんて、うれしいですねえ」
English: “Well! I’m so pleased that Mr. Liao came all this way to visit.”

Japanese: ベトナム料理屋店主タンの娘は、顏一杯に人なつこい笑顔を浮かべている。
English: The daughter of Mr. Tan, owner of the Vietnamese restaurant, wore a warm smile across her whole face.

Japanese: 彼女の屋台は元々おでんか何かの中古屋台を買い取って改造したものらしく、下のリヤカー部分も、上の木造の屋台本体も、錆が浮いたり日光で変色したりで年季を感じさせられた。
English: Her stall appeared to be a secondhand oden cart or something similar that she had bought and remodeled. Both the handcart beneath and the wooden stall above showed their age, spotted with rust and faded by sunlight.

Japanese: 評判だけあって買い求める客が列を作り、近くでは彼女の商品を持った客があちこちに座って食べている。
English: True to its reputation, the stall had attracted a line of customers. All around it, others sat eating what they had bought from her.

Japanese: トーマスとアイスは彼女の申し出を断って列に並んで買い求めたが、食べる場所は彼女の懇願じみた要望に従って、作業スペースとして使っていたテーブルを片付けて使わせて貰っている。
English: Thomas and Ice declined her offer of special treatment and waited in line to make their purchases. At her almost pleading insistence, however, they ate at a table she cleared for them from the work area.

Japanese: 彼女が販売しているのは『チェー』と呼ばれるもので、あんこやフルーツにココナッツミルクをかけた、あんみつやぜんざいのようなスイーツだった。ベトナムでは有名な食べ物で、温かいものも冷たいものもあるらしい。
English: She sold a dessert called chè: sweet bean paste and fruit topped with coconut milk, something like anmitsu or zenzai. It was apparently famous in Vietnam and could be served either hot or cold.

Japanese: 彼女の屋台は小さいながらも数多くの具材を用意してあり、珍しいものからオーソドックスなものまで客の好みで選べるが、人気があるのは柱に貼られた紙に書かれている彼女おすすめの組み合わせだ。『ダナンの恋人たちの語らい』だとか『メコン河に落ちる黄昏』だとか、具材の内容がまったく想像出来ない名前がついている。
English: Small though the stall was, she had prepared a great many ingredients, allowing customers to choose everything from the familiar to the unusual. The most popular selections, however, were her recommended combinations, written on sheets of paper pasted to a pillar. They bore names that revealed nothing whatsoever about their contents, such as ‘Sweet Nothings Between Lovers in Da Nang’ and ‘Twilight Falling on the Mekong.’

Japanese: ベトナムの地名がおりこまれているが、本人はY地区生まれY地区育ちでベトナムには行ったことがないそうである。
English: The names incorporated Vietnamese places, though the woman herself had apparently been born and raised in Y District and had never visited Vietnam.

Japanese: 透明のプラスチックコップにカラフルな具材が積み重ねられ、白いココナッツミルクで満たされた様子は、見た目も華やかで美しい。
English: Layers of colorful ingredients filled transparent plastic cups, all bathed in white coconut milk, making them look bright and beautiful.

Japanese: この陽気な食べ物を前に、アイスとトーマスは暗い顔で佇んでいる。
English: Before this cheerful food, Ice and Thomas sat wearing gloomy faces.

Japanese: 「どうしました？　お口にあわなかったですか？」
English: “Is something wrong? Was it not to your taste?”

Japanese: 店主が心配して訊ねるのに、トーマスは愛想笑いを浮かべて首を横に振る。
English: When the proprietor asked in concern, Thomas put on an amiable smile and shook his head.

Japanese: 「とっても美味しいよ。ただちょっと僕は考え事があるんだ。あと、この子は普段からあんまり笑わないから気にしないでくれ」
English: “It’s absolutely delicious. I simply have something on my mind. And this girl rarely smiles at the best of times, so please don’t worry about her.”

Japanese: 客が待っているから戻るよう伝えると、店主は渋々作業を再開する。
English: He told her to return to the waiting customers, and she reluctantly resumed her work.

Japanese: 実際スイーツは美味であったし、店主に誤解されたくはなかったが、トーマスはなかなか気持を切り換えることが出来なかった。
English: The dessert truly was delicious, and Thomas had no wish for the proprietor to misunderstand. Even so, he found it difficult to change his mood.

Japanese: 「なんだか、最近の小謝は少し怖い気がしない？」
English: “Don’t you feel Siu Tse has been a little frightening lately?”

Japanese: トーマスは辺りをはばかって小声でそう囁く。
English: Mindful of those around them, Thomas whispered the question.

Japanese: 「そうですか？　私は、初めて会った時から常にいつ会っても恐ろしいと感じていますが」
English: “Do you think so? I have found him frightening at every encounter since the first time we met.”

Japanese: 「確かに、あのマンションの時の小謝はすごかったけど……」
English: “Admittedly, Siu Tse was formidable that day at the apartment, but...”

Japanese: トーマスがそう言うと、アイスは僅かに顔を歪めた。
English: At Thomas’s words, Ice’s face tightened by the smallest degree.

Japanese: 廖志明の愛人のマンションで能力を亮に見破られたことは、普段自分の能力で主人を守り切ると宣言している彼女にとってはあまり思い出したくない記憶だった。
English: Leung’s discovery of her ability at Liao Chi-ming’s mistress’s apartment was not a memory she cared to revisit. Ice ordinarily declared that her power would enable her to protect her master under any circumstances.

Japanese: トーマスはそんな彼女の態度に気づく様子もなく、
English: Thomas showed no sign of noticing her response.

Japanese: 「まあ、気のせいかもしれないね。……何かが変わったわけじゃなくて、立場がそう感じさせているのかもしれない。だとしたら、前と同じように接してあげなくちゃ駄目だな。やたらとまわりの人に恐れられるというのは、きっと寂しいだろうし」
English: “Well, perhaps I’m imagining it. ...Perhaps nothing about him has changed, and his position merely makes me feel that way. If so, I must be certain to treat him just as I did before. It must be lonely to have everyone around you constantly afraid.”

Japanese: アイスには、自分の暗殺計画を初めて報告された時でさえ顔色一つ変えなかった亮がそんなことを寂しがるようには思えなかったが、優しい主人のためにその意見を口にはしなかった。
English: Ice found it difficult to imagine that Leung, who had not so much as changed expression upon first learning of a plot to assassinate him, could be lonely for such a reason. For the sake of her kind master, however, she left the opinion unspoken.

Japanese: 食べ終わり、礼を言って立ち去ろうとすると、娘はトーマスにまだ温かい紙袋を押しつけた。
English: When they finished eating, thanked her, and prepared to leave, the woman pressed a warm paper bag into Thomas’s hands.

Japanese: 「揚げたてのバインザンです。あとで召し上がってください」
English: “These are freshly fried bánh rán. Please enjoy them later.”

Japanese: その屋台ではチェーの他にもフライヤーで団子を揚げて売っているが、その揚げたてを詰めてくれたのだと言う。
English: In addition to chè, the stall used a fryer to prepare and sell balls of dough. She had apparently filled the bag with a batch fresh from the oil.

Japanese: 「払うよ。いくらなの？」
English: “I’ll pay. How much are they?”

Japanese: 「いいんですよ。あなたにはこれから頑張って貰わないといけないんですから。龍頭様も若くてかっこいい人になったし、何か変わるんじゃないかってみんな期待してるんですよ」
English: “They’re free. We need you to work hard for us from now on. The new Longtou is young and handsome too, and everyone is hoping that things might change.”

Japanese: 「わかった。ありがとう。協力してくれる街のみんなのために頑張るよ」
English: “All right. Thank you. I’ll work hard for everyone in the city who supports us.”

Japanese: トーマスはそう言って、自らその紙袋を受け取った。
English: Thomas accepted the paper bag himself.

Japanese: 「これ、ひとつ小謝……龍頭にもあげておくよ。きっと喜ぶと思うよ。彼は意外とこういう食べ物好きだからね」
English: “I’ll save one for Siu Tse... for the Longtou. I’m sure he’ll be pleased. He has a surprising fondness for this sort of food.”

Japanese: 「い、いや！　とんでもないです！　それは恐れ多くて……」
English: “N-no! Certainly not! I could never presume...”

Japanese: 急に慌てる娘を見て、トーマスは自分も一応幹部なのになと思わぬでもなかったが、そのことについては特に何も言わずにその場をあとにした。
English: The woman’s sudden panic did make Thomas think that he was an officer too, after a fashion. He said nothing about it and left.

Japanese: その日は空はどんよりと曇り、風が強く、少し肌寒かったが滑走路通りはいつも通りの活気に満ちあふれている。
English: The sky that day was dark with cloud, the wind strong and the air slightly cold. Runway Street nevertheless overflowed with its usual vitality.

Japanese: この街の裏側では、クリスの死に伴う世代交代以後、ぴりぴりとした雰囲気が全体を覆っているが、表通りを見る限りではまるきり影響を感じられなかった。もっとも、滑走路通りにはよその地域から参入した人々の店舗なども多く、かつてのように、誰もが裏社会との関わりを持っているわけではない。
English: Since the generational transition brought by Chris’s death, a tense atmosphere had covered the city’s underworld. On the main street, however, none of that tension could be felt. Admittedly, Runway Street held many businesses operated by newcomers from other regions, and not everyone possessed ties to the underworld as they once had.

Japanese: YSという絶対的な組織が生まれたことで、この街は、これでもだいぶ平和になったのだ。そして外から客も店も集まって来て、この繁栄を産んだ。これ街の住民にとっても多くの利益を生み出したが、反面割を食った住民も少なくなかった。Y地区の移民同士は年と共に少しずつ混ざり合ってきたものの、こうした新しくやって来た者たちと古い住民とのトラブルは増えている。
English: The birth of a dominant organization called YS had made the city considerably more peaceful. Customers and businesses gathered from outside and created its present prosperity. That prosperity benefited many residents, but there were also many who received the worst of the bargain. The city’s immigrant communities had gradually mingled over the years, yet conflict between newcomers of this kind and older residents was increasing.

Japanese: トーマスは積極的に街に出て、人々の声を聞いていた。
English: Thomas went actively into the city and listened to what its people had to say.

Japanese: 彼の廖ファミリーは、街の発展によって明らかに利益を伸ばした側だったので、当然彼の感覚では誰もがこの現在の栄華を歓迎していると思っていただけに、そうではない者たちが多くいると知ったのは新しい発見だった。
English: His own Liao Family had clearly profited from the city’s development. Thomas had naturally assumed from his perspective that everyone welcomed its present prosperity, and discovering how many did not came as a revelation.

Japanese: そして、YSについても様々な評判を聞いた。
English: He also heard a wide variety of opinions about YS.

Japanese: YSの幹部の一人と言えばこの街では相当地位の高いギャングであり、龍頭が街の王だとすれば、諸侯くらいの地位はある。しかしトーマスの温厚な人柄のせいか、アイス一人を引き連れるだけという身軽な姿のためか、彼が訊ねると皆忌憚のない意見を語ってくれた。
English: An officer of YS occupied an extremely high station in this city. If the Longtou was its king, an officer might be one of its feudal lords. Perhaps because of Thomas’s gentle personality, or because he traveled lightly with Ice alone, everyone offered a candid opinion when he asked.

Japanese: たとえば彼の父の廖志明や、他の諸侯であるダリオ・ボネットや壬生屋タカシではそうはいかないだろう。彼らはみな高級な車を乗り回し、武装したボディガードで身のまわりを堅め、人々は目もあわさぬように震え上がる。
English: The same could hardly have been said of his father Liao Chi-ming or of other such lords as Dario Bonetto and Takashi Mibuya. All of them drove expensive cars and surrounded themselves with armed bodyguards. People trembled before them and took care not even to meet their eyes.

Japanese: 「僕からすると、いまのＹＳの評判はそんなに悪くないんだよね」
English: “From what I have seen, YS’s reputation isn’t particularly bad at present.”

Japanese: トーマスはアイスを相手にそう語る。
English: Thomas shared his thoughts with Ice.

Japanese: 「元々さあ、ＹＳで人気があるのって、小謝のお父さんだけだったじゃない？　そりゃ、あのひとは残酷な殺人事件とか起こして恐れられてはいたけれど、住民に対しては寛容だったからね。クリスマスなんて、スラムの住民のために炊き出しとかしてたでしょう？　アイスも知ってるでしょ」
English: “Originally, the only popular person in YS was Siu Tse’s father, wasn’t he? Certainly, people feared him for the cruel murders he committed, but he was generous toward the residents. At Christmas, he used to serve meals for the people in the slums. You know that too, don’t you, Ice?”

Japanese: 「知ってます。よく子供が列を作ってるところとか見ました」
English: “I do. I often saw the children standing in line.”

Japanese: 「でしょう？　フェルナンデスさんのところも同じような活動はしていたけど、あの人の場合は南米出身の人達以外には結構冷淡だったから、異教徒でも異国人にでも分け隔てなく与えたクリスさんみたいな人気はないよね。そして、僕の見るところ、街の人達は小謝にもお父さんと同じような印象を抱いているんだよ」
English: “Exactly. Mr. Fernandes did similar work, but he could be quite cold toward anyone who wasn’t South American. He was never as popular as Mr. Chris, who gave without distinction to people of every faith and nationality. And from what I’ve seen, the people of the city have formed much the same impression of Siu Tse as they held of his father.”

Japanese: 「そ、それはちょっと」
English: “I-I am not sure about that.”

Japanese: 余りにも亮のことが好きなトーマスの贔屓目ではないか、とアイスは主人を窘める。
English: Ice warned her master that his excessive fondness for Leung might simply be coloring his judgment.

Japanese: 「確かに大好きだけど、そうじゃないんだって。だって、今はもう劉建志が殺されたのは、市民に対して乱暴を働いたからだって、今では街の誰もが知っているんだよ？　龍頭になってから、YS内の派閥をなくしていくと宣言したのもすごく好感度が高い」
English: “I certainly love him, but that isn’t it. By now, everyone in the city knows that Ryu Kenshi was killed because he committed violence against civilians. And his declaration as Longtou that he would eliminate the factions within YS was extremely well received.”

Japanese: 「まあ、確かにそれは」
English: “Well, that much is true.”

Japanese: 「それとは逆に、女性を売り買いする壬生屋さんとか、どうしても過去の暗殺屋のイメージがつきまとうボネットさんはメチャクチャ不人気だったでしょう？　小謝には彼らをなんとかしてくれるんだなって、期待感されてるところもある。それにね……」
English: “By contrast, Mr. Mibuya, who buys and sells women, and Mr. Bonetto, who can never escape his old image as an assassin, were terribly unpopular. Part of what people expect of Siu Tse is that he’ll do something about men like them. And then...”

Japanese: 「まだあるんですか？」
English: “There is more?”

Japanese: 「うん」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: トーマスは頷き、
English: Thomas nodded.

Japanese: 「小謝が子供の頃、よその子供と同じように裏通りを走り回っていたというのもプラスだよね。親近感があるし、かつて一緒に遊んだ仲間たちが、この街には沢山存在するから。親近感と言えば、お父さんみたいに人間離れをした容姿をもつサイキックじゃなくて、ノーマルの若者だっていうのも重要だよ。それになんといっても美形！　女の子の人気はとんでもないことになってる」
English: “The fact that Siu Tse ran through the back streets like any other child when he was young works in his favor as well. It makes him familiar, and a great many people who once played with him still live here. Speaking of familiarity, it also matters that he is a young Normal, not a psychic with an otherworldly appearance like his father’s. And above all, he’s beautiful! His popularity among the girls is extraordinary.”

Japanese: 「はあ」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 「だから、YSのなかでは孤立していたけれど、街では多くの人に期待されているんじゃないかな」
English: “That’s why I think that although he was isolated within YS, many people in the city have placed their hopes in him.”

Japanese: 「確かにそうかもしれません」
English: “That may indeed be true.”

Japanese: アイスもむげに否定するつもりはないのだけれど、主人が亮に入れ込んでいるのを常々心配しているだけに、つい苦言を言うような形になってしまう。
English: Ice had no wish to deny the idea out of hand. Yet she was always concerned by her master’s devotion to Leung and consequently found herself offering criticism.

Japanese: 「でも、それが実態に沿った期待なのか、単に初代の君臨が長かったために生まれたストレスの裏返しなのかは判別がつかないところですよ」
English: “But it is difficult to tell whether those hopes correspond to reality, or merely represent a reaction against the strain produced by the first Longtou’s lengthy reign.”

Japanese: 「そうだけどさあ……」
English: “That’s true, but...”

Japanese: 「それに、その期待の一部は、今の娘さんのように、トーマス様にも向けられているはずです」
English: “Moreover, some portion of those hopes must be directed toward you as well, Master Thomas, just as that young woman demonstrated.”

Japanese: 「そうだね」
English: “That’s true.”

Japanese: トーマスは考え込んで、
English: Thomas fell into thought.

Japanese: 「ねえアイス、そりゃ僕たちはギャングだし、いくら力があったって社会からすれば寄生虫みたいなものなのかもしれないけど、まだまだこの街には僕らのような存在が必要だと思うよ。この街にはここでしか生きていけない人が沢山いるし、法律や警察は彼らを守ってはくれないんだもの」
English: “Tell me, Ice. We may be gangsters, and however powerful we become, society may still see us as little more than parasites. But I believe this city still needs people like us. Many people can live nowhere but here, and neither the law nor the police will protect them.”

Japanese: 少し暗くなりはじめ、電光看板に明かりが点り始める。ネオンの照り返しで顔に色がついたトーマスは、人混みを眺めながらそう言った。
English: The light had begun to fade, and electric signs flickered to life. Neon reflections colored Thomas’s face as he looked over the crowd and spoke.

Japanese: 「小謝もきっとそういうことを考えていると思う。そしてアウロラ達もきっと……。だから、話し合えばちゃんとわかると思うんだ」
English: “I’m sure Siu Tse is thinking about those things too. And Aurora and the others must be as well... That’s why I believe they can come to understand one another if they talk.”

Japanese: そしてアイスの顔をまっすぐ見つめるが、彼女は何も応えない。
English: He looked directly into Ice’s face, but she offered no answer.

Japanese: 彼女がこういうときに同意の言葉を口にしないで黙っているということは、違う意見なのだということをトーマスは知っている。
English: Thomas knew that when Ice declined to voice agreement and remained silent in circumstances like these, it meant that her opinion differed.

Japanese: 「アイス、きっときみは小謝のことをあんまり信用していなくて……」
English: “Ice, perhaps you don’t place very much trust in Siu Tse...”

Japanese: トーマスが言いかけたとき、誰かが彼の太ももの辺りにぶつかった。
English: As Thomas began the sentence, someone collided with his thigh.

Japanese: それは、フードのついた裾の長い服を着た子供で、前を見ずに歩いていたらしく、道路の上にひっくり返る。
English: It was a child wearing a long, hooded garment. Apparently walking without looking ahead, the child tumbled backward onto the road.

Japanese: その子供は手さげ袋を持っていて、転んだ拍子にその中に入っていた玉ねぎやらリンゴやらがいくつも飛び出しコロコロと散らばってゆく。
English: The child had been carrying a shopping bag. The fall sent onions, apples, and other items spilling out to roll in every direction.

Japanese: 「あっ、ごめんっ！」
English: “Oh! I’m sorry!”

Japanese: 倒れた子供を助けようか、野菜を拾おうか、トーマスは一瞬硬直してしまう。
English: For one instant, Thomas froze, unable to decide whether to help the fallen child or collect the vegetables.

Japanese: そうしているアイスはさっと子供の手を引いて立たせ、次に遠くへ転がろうとする野菜を回収にかかる。
English: While he stood there, Ice swiftly pulled the child upright by one hand, then began collecting the vegetables before they could roll farther away.

Japanese: 「ぼ、僕も」
English: “I-I’ll help too.”

Japanese: アイスに続いて野菜を拾おうと中腰になると、
English: He bent to help Ice gather the vegetables.

Japanese: 「大丈夫です。トーマス様はその子を見ていてください」
English: “That is not necessary. Please watch the child, Master Thomas.”

Japanese: 彼女がそう言ったので、大人しくそれに従った。
English: At her instruction, he obediently complied.

Japanese: 「どこか痛くない？」
English: “Does anything hurt?”

Japanese: 子供はフードを目深に被っている。トーマスがしゃがんでその顔を見ようとしたら、俯いてそのフードで顔を隠すような仕草をした。
English: The child wore the hood pulled low. When Thomas crouched to look at the child’s face, the child bowed still lower and hid behind the hood.

Japanese: 『怪我とかしてないかな？』
English: “Are you hurt anywhere?”

Japanese: 最初の言葉は日本語で、次に英語で尋ねたが、やはり子供は返事をしない。それから中国語で語りかけてみるが、それもやはり反応しない。
English: Thomas had asked first in Japanese and then in English, but the child answered neither. He tried Chinese next, with the same lack of response.

Japanese: 「今あのお姉さんが全部拾ってくれるから、待っててね」
English: “That lady is picking everything up for you. Just wait here.”

Japanese: アイスは手早く玉ねぎなどを拾っている。通行人も手伝ってくれて、すぐに袋から転がり出たものはすべて回収された。トーマスはアイスと、拾ってくれた通行人達に礼を言うと、拾った野菜をはたいて埃を払う仕草をしてから、子供が持っている手提げ袋のなかに一つずつ入れる。
English: Ice gathered the onions and the rest with practiced speed. Passersby helped as well, and everything that had rolled from the bag was soon recovered. Thomas thanked Ice and the people who had assisted, brushed the dust from each piece of produce, then returned them one by one to the child’s shopping bag.

Japanese: 子供はその間、一言も口をきかずに俯いたままで、トーマスが全部の野菜を戻すと頭一つ下げずに駆け去っていった。
English: Throughout the process, the child remained silent with head bowed. The moment Thomas had returned every vegetable, the child ran away without so much as a nod of thanks.

Japanese: 「どこの子かな？　怪我してなければいいけど……」
English: “I wonder where that child came from. I hope the child wasn’t hurt...”

Japanese: 去ってゆく子供の背中を心配そうに眺めながら彼はそう呟いた。
English: Thomas murmured as he watched the child’s retreating back with concern.

Japanese: 「あの子、ボーダーエリアの子供です」
English: “That child was from the Border Area.”

Japanese: アイスは無感情な声で言った。
English: Ice spoke without emotion.

Japanese: 「身体を隠すぶかぶかの服を着ていましたよね。あれ、ボーダーエリアの人が良く着る服なんです」
English: “You noticed the loose clothing that concealed the body? People from the Border Area often dress that way.”

Japanese: 「……きみはボーダーエリアの出身だって、小謝が言ってたね」
English: “...Siu Tse told me that you came from the Border Area too.”

Japanese: あの時亮は、トーマスも知らなかったアイスの出身地の話をした。気にしてはいたが、そのことについて今までトーマスは訊ねなかった。
English: That day, Leung had spoken of Ice’s birthplace, something even Thomas had not known. The matter had remained on his mind, but he had never asked her about it.

Japanese: グレートホールを中心とした汚染地帯とY地区の主要繁華街の境界であるため、その地域は『ボーダーエリア』或いは単に『ボーダー』と呼ばれている。
English: Because it formed the border between the contaminated region surrounding Great Hole and the principal commercial districts of Y District, the neighborhood was called the Border Area, or simply the Border.

Japanese: そのあたりは昔は基地ではなく住宅街であったが、グレートホールの出現と汚染の発生により住民が退去し、廃墟となっていた。今そこには、街の中心地に住むことが出来ないタイプAたちが、崩れた壁に板を張ったり、コンクリートで塗り固めながら暮らしている。彼らの多くは特質変異により醜く崩れた肉体を持っていた。
English: It had once been a residential neighborhood rather than part of the base. The appearance of Great Hole and the contamination, however, drove out its residents and left it in ruins. Type As unable to live in the city center occupied it now, patching holes in crumbling walls with boards or filling them with concrete as they made their homes. Many possessed bodies grotesquely disfigured by trait mutations.

Japanese: 彼らは外部の人間とは必要最低限しか交渉せず、独自のルールや宗教を持ち、静かに暮らしている。
English: They dealt with outsiders only when absolutely necessary, observed rules and religions of their own, and lived quietly.

Japanese: 彼らのなかには優れた能力を持った者も存在するという噂があり、実際、昔とある小さなギャング組織が彼らを利用しようと干渉したときに、ボスとその家族が全員不審死するという事件があり、その犯人は見つかることがなかった。
English: Rumor held that some among them possessed extraordinary powers. There had, in fact, once been an incident in which a small gang tried to interfere with the community and exploit its residents, after which the boss and his entire family died under mysterious circumstances. The culprit was never found.

Japanese: Y地区のギャング達ともお互いに関わり合うことがなく、溝平B団地こと『ヘドロ団地』と並んで、外部の人間が立ち入らない閉ざされたエリアとして知られていた。
English: The community and the gangs of Y District avoided all involvement with one another. Along with Mizohira B Housing Complex, otherwise known as the Sludge Housing Complex, the Border was famous as a closed area outsiders never entered.

Japanese: 「私も、小さな時はああいう服を着ていました」
English: “When I was small, I wore clothes like that too.”

Japanese: アイスは淡々と言った。
English: Ice spoke dispassionately.

Japanese: 「きみの生まれた場所なんだね。……どんな街だったんだい？」
English: “It’s where you were born, then. ...What kind of place was it?”

Japanese: 「街の人が思っているような神秘的な場所でもなく、タイプAといってもほとんど使えるような能力を持った人もいません。ただとても静かで、平和でした。……Y地区は他で生きられない者が生きてゆく街だとおっしゃいましたが、醜い姿のために、そこでさえも生きられなくなった者たちを受け入れる場所です。一度そこへやって来ると、もう誰も出て行こうとはしません。醜い自分の姿から目をそらし、傷をなめ合うようにして一生をそこで暮らすのです。そこは化け物たちの楽園なんです。私もその一人でした」
English: “It is not the mysterious place people in the city imagine. Although the residents are Type As, almost none possess useful abilities. It was simply very quiet and peaceful. ...You said that Y District is a city where people who can live nowhere else survive. The Border accepts those whose ugly forms have made even this city uninhabitable. Once someone comes there, no one ever attempts to leave. They turn their eyes from their own ugliness and spend their whole lives licking one another’s wounds. It is a paradise for monsters. I was one of them.”

Japanese: アイスが自分のことを喋るのは初めてで、トーマスは驚きながらその横顔を見つめた。
English: This was the first time Ice had spoken about herself. Thomas studied her profile in surprise.

Japanese: 彼女はそうして見られていることに気づいているはずだが、何の反応もせずにまっすぐ前だけを見ている。
English: She must have noticed his gaze, but showed no response and continued looking directly ahead.

Japanese: 「でもきみはそこを出た」
English: “But you left.”

Japanese: トーマスの言葉に、アイスは下唇を噛む。それくらいの表情の変化でも、彼女にしては珍しいことだ。
English: At Thomas’s words, Ice bit her lower lip. Even so slight a change of expression was rare for her.

Japanese: トーマスもそれ以上は何も訊ねない。亮があの時言った言葉を思い出していた。
English: Thomas asked nothing further. He remembered what Leung had said that day.

Japanese: 『……本名は李小玉。２５年前にボーダーエリアに住む夫婦の元に生まれた。三才の時に街の者との諍いで両親を殺される。十二才の時にエリアを出て、暗闇通りの空き家に住み着き窃盗を繰り返すが、ある時ヤミ金事務所に盗みに入った時に捕まり、リンチを受けて殺されるところをトーマス・リャオに救われ、彼のボディガードとなる』
English: ‘She was born twenty-five years ago to a married couple living in the Border Area. When she was three, her parents were killed in a dispute with people from the city. At twelve, she left the Area and occupied an abandoned house on Darkness Street, where she repeatedly committed theft. One day, she was caught breaking into a loan shark’s office. Thomas Liao saved her when they were about to beat her to death, and she became his bodyguard.’

Japanese: 「僕が思うに、化け物っていうのは、ちょっと人と姿が違うだけの人間をさすために使う言葉じゃない。どんな人間の心にも住み着いている、えたいの知れない存在のことを呼ぶ時に使うんだ。それにとりつかれた人間は、ときに本来の人格とはまったく違う生き物に化けてしまう」
English: “As I see it, ‘monster’ isn’t a word for a human being who merely looks a little different from other people. It names an unknowable presence that lives in every human heart. When it possesses someone, they may turn into a creature utterly unlike their original self.”

Japanese: トーマスはアイスの手を握りしめる。
English: Thomas clasped Ice’s hand.

Japanese: 「この街にはそうして取り憑かれてしまった人々があふれている。彼らは悪人ではなくて、人格を奪われているだけなんだ。僕たちの仕事は、それと向き合い、時に飼い慣らして使いこなすことが必要なんだよ。……行こうアイス。僕はここで生きてゆくには、まだあまりにも未熟だ。もっといろんな人を会って、もっと賢くならなきゃいけない」
English: “This city is overflowing with people who have been possessed in that way. They aren’t evil. Their personalities have merely been stolen from them. Our work requires us to confront that presence—and at times to tame it and make use of it. ...Come, Ice. I’m still far too immature to live in this city. I need to meet all kinds of people and become much wiser.”

Japanese: 彼はそう言うと、手を掴んだまま歩き始めた。
English: With that, he began to walk, still holding her hand.

Japanese: クリス・ツェーが死んでも、週に一度、大幹部達が集まって食事と会議を行う定例会食は続いている。
English: Even after Chris Tse’s death, the regular dinners at which the senior officers gathered once each week for a meal and a meeting continued.

Japanese: 絶え間なく冗談を口にしていたクリスに比べて、謝亮の主催する定例会は淡々と必要最低限の報告を行い合うだけの静かなものだった。
English: Chris had kept up a constant stream of jokes. By contrast, the meetings hosted by Tse Leung were quiet affairs where the participants did little more than exchange the minimum necessary reports.

Japanese: それは謝亮の人柄もあったろうが、もちろん、彼が龍頭就任時に宣言した、すべてのファミリーを統合するという計画に対する反応でもある。
English: Leung’s personality may have played a part, but so did the participants’ response to the plan he had announced upon becoming Longtou: the integration of every Family.

Japanese: 会食のメンバーは、クリス存命時のものから少し顔ぶれが変わっている。死亡したジェフリー・ウォンと処刑された劉建志はいなくなり、追放された廖志明のかわりにトーマス・リャオが参加し、あとはジョゼ・フェルナンデス、壬生屋タカシ、ダリオ・ボネット、エリー・ホワイト、そして馬明。
English: The composition of the dinners had changed somewhat since Chris was alive. Jeffrey Wong was dead and Ryu Kenshi had been executed; Thomas Liao now attended in place of the exiled Liao Chi-ming. The others were José Fernandes, Takashi Mibuya, Dario Bonetto, Ellie White, and Ma Ming.

Japanese: 現状このなかで明確に亮の統合計画を支持するものはトーマスだけだ。エリーも亮という個人については支持を表明していたが、こと統合に関しては難色を示している。
English: At present, Thomas alone among them clearly supported Leung’s plan for integration. Ellie had expressed her support for Leung personally, but even she showed reluctance where integration itself was concerned.

Japanese: その日もみな積極的に話そうとはせず、報告が終わってしまうと、ナイフやフォークのカチャカチャとした音ばかりが響いた。
English: That day, too, no one spoke willingly. Once the reports ended, little could be heard but the clatter of knives and forks.

Japanese: この雰囲気を打ち破ったのは、ジョゼ・フェルナンデスだった。
English: José Fernandes was the one who broke the atmosphere.

Japanese: 「龍頭、それからみなども、今日の会食の最後に、一つ、私の方から伝えたいことがあるのだが」
English: “Longtou, and all of you as well: before today’s dinner ends, there is one matter I wish to tell you.”

Japanese: 会食が終わりに近づき、みなの前にデザートが運ばれてから、彼はそう言った。
English: He spoke as the dinner approached its end, once dessert had been brought to the table.

Japanese: 「発言してもかまわないか？」
English: “May I?”

Japanese: 「もちろん」
English: “Of course.”

Japanese: と亮は言った。
English: Leung gave his permission.

Japanese: このとき部屋全体の空気が張り詰めたが、誰よりも緊張していたのはトーマスだったろう。明らかに落ち着きを失って、亮とフェルナンデスの間で視線を行ったり来たりさせている。
English: The air throughout the room drew taut. Thomas was probably more nervous than anyone. Plainly unable to compose himself, he looked back and forth between Leung and Fernandes.

Japanese: 「我々のファミリーは、YSの連合から外させて貰う」
English: “My Family will withdraw from the YS federation.”

Japanese: 皆が注目するなか、フェルナンデスははっきりとした声でそう宣言した。
English: Under every eye, Fernandes made the declaration in a clear voice.

Japanese: 「元々この組織は、ローズ・クラブを潰し、木下組から街を守るために生まれたものだ。その役割を果たした時点で本来の役割は終わっている。あの時自ら戦ってくれた初代龍頭への恩があったから今日までともに歩んできたが、彼が死んだ今、もうその必要もない」
English: “This organization was created to destroy the Rose Club and protect the city from the Kinoshita-gumi. Once it fulfilled that purpose, its original role had ended. Our debt to the first Longtou, who fought for us himself in those days, has kept us at your side until today. Now that he is dead, there is no longer any need.”

Japanese: 覚悟していたとは言え、実際その言葉を聞くと、トーマスはYS崩壊の序曲が流れはじめたような思いがして背筋が冷たくなった。
English: Thomas had expected this. Yet hearing the words nevertheless sent a chill down his back, as though the overture to the collapse of YS had begun to play.

Japanese: 「小謝のやろうとしていることには賛同出来ない。合理化だの融和だのと言えば聞こえがいいが、それぞれの組織のなかにある絆や繋がりを解体しようとしているだけだ。私は同郷の仲間達の生活を守らなくてはならない。これ以上は協力出来ない」
English: “I cannot support what Siu Tse is attempting. ‘Rationalization’ and ‘reconciliation’ may sound pleasant, but all he is doing is dismantling the bonds within each organization. I must protect the lives of my comrades from our homeland. I can cooperate no further.”

Japanese: 「ミスター・フェルナンデスらしくもない。それはあまりにも軽率ではありませんか？」
English: “That is unlike you, Mr. Fernandes. Are you not being rather rash?”

Japanese: 苦笑交じりにそう言ったのは、出席者で唯一の女性であるエリー・ホワイトであった。
English: The only woman present, Ellie White, spoke with a faint, wry smile.

Japanese: 「軽率とは、どういうことかな？」
English: “What do you mean by rash?”

Japanese: フェルナンデスは猛禽類のようにぎょろりとした目を動かし、エリーを睨み付ける。
English: Fernandes shifted his bulging, raptor-like eyes and glared at Ellie.

Japanese: 並の女であったら震え上がってしまうような恐ろしい顔つきであったが、しかしその黒衣の女性は平然とヴェールの下の口元に微笑を浮かべたままだ。
English: The terrifying face would have made an ordinary woman tremble. The woman in black remained perfectly calm, a smile still visible beneath her veil.

Japanese: 「失礼ですが、YSと離れたらあなたは立ちゆきませんよ？　今は、YSを結成したあの頃とは違います。街は大きく発展し、変化しました。しかし残念ながらあなたのファミリーはとりのこされ、変化に適応出来ていない。その結果、規模は大きいが、それに経済力が追いつかなくなっている。YSを離れ、我々との連携がなくなれば苦しい状況に陥るのではないですか？」
English: “Forgive me, but you cannot sustain yourself apart from YS. The city is no longer what it was when we formed the federation. It has undergone tremendous growth and change. Unfortunately, your Family has been left behind and failed to adapt. As a result, its economic power has not kept pace with its size. If you leave YS and lose your cooperative ties with us, will you not find yourself in considerable difficulty?”

Japanese: 「ふん、何やら私情を感じるね。いや、女の執念かな？」
English: “Hmph. I sense something personal in this. Or should I call it a woman’s vindictiveness?”

Japanese: 独り言のようにそう言ってせせら笑ったのは壬生屋タカシであった。
English: Takashi Mibuya delivered the sneering remark almost to himself.

Japanese: エリーはその発言が聞こえなかったかのように無視し、フェルナンデスの方を向いてその答えを待っている。
English: Ellie ignored him as though she had heard nothing. She continued facing Fernandes and waited for his answer.

Japanese: 彼は口をへの字に結んだまま、黙っている。
English: His mouth set in a downward curve, Fernandes remained silent.

Japanese: エリーの指摘は間違ってはいない。街の経済が発展し、あの武闘派で知られた旧義勝のメンバー達も今はさまざまなビジネスに手を広げている。一方フェルナンデスはただ暴力だけを持つだけの、移民たちの守護者的なあり方を変えず、リャオ・ファミリーの経営する飲食店に用心棒を派遣したり、ヤミ金の取り立てを代行したりといったかたちで協力関係を結ぶことで利益を上げている。これらがなくなれば、別の食い扶持を探す必要に迫られるだろう。
English: Ellie’s observation was not mistaken. The city’s economy had developed, and even the members of old Yisheng, once famous as militant fighters, had now spread into a variety of businesses. Fernandes, by contrast, had never changed his Family’s role as protectors of immigrants, armed with nothing but violence. It profited through cooperative arrangements such as providing guards for restaurants operated by the Liao Family or collecting debts for its loan sharks. If those opportunities disappeared, the Family would be forced to find another source of livelihood.

Japanese: 「また当時のように暴力を使って一稼ぎしますか？　しかし、この街であまり手荒なことをするならば、私たちと対立せざるを得ないでしょう。その覚悟はおありで？」
English: “Will you return to earning money through violence as you did in those days? But if you resort to heavy-handed violence in this city, we will have no choice but to oppose you. Are you prepared for that?”

Japanese: エリーはさらに追求する。
English: Ellie pressed him further.

Japanese: 「心配してくれるのは結構だが、それは余計なお世話と言うものだ。確かに我々は経済的に弱いかもしれないが、金が欲しいからと言ってプライドを譲り渡せというような話ならば、なおさら従うわけにはいかない」
English: “Your concern is appreciated, but it is also unwelcome interference. We may indeed be weak economically. But if you mean that our desire for money should compel us to surrender our pride, that only gives us still greater reason to refuse.”

Japanese: フェルナンデスは毅然としてその言葉をはねのける。
English: Fernandes firmly rejected the argument.

Japanese: そこで、意外な方向から彼の決定を支持する声があった。
English: Then support for his decision arrived from an unexpected direction.

Japanese: 「ミス・ホワイト、これは、それほど危機的な話ではないんだよ」
English: “Miss White, this is not such a dire matter.”

Japanese: そう言ったのは亮である。
English: The speaker was Leung.

Japanese: 「彼は争いをしたいわけじゃない。ただ仲間思いなだけなんだよ。彼は故郷からの難民などもたくさん面倒を見ているからね。YSに吸収されたら過去のような手厚い保護が出来なくなると心配してる。そうでしょう、フェルナンデスさん？」
English: “He does not want conflict. He simply cares for his comrades. He looks after a great many refugees from his homeland, after all. He worries that absorption into YS would leave him unable to protect them as generously as he has in the past. Isn’t that so, Mr. Fernandes?”

Japanese: 亮の言葉に、フェルナンデスは何も言わず、しわだらけのむっつりした顔で黙り込んでいる。その沈黙は、不本意ながらの肯定を意味していると考えるべきだろう。
English: Fernandes made no reply, but sat in silence with his wrinkled face set in a sullen expression. It was probably best to interpret that silence as reluctant agreement.

Japanese: 「私だって、離脱したからといって、即座に関係を絶とうなんて思ってはいない。あくまでも独立した組織同士として、これまでどおりの提携が出来ればと考えている。……それでどうだろう？　あなただって、別に、いまここで我々と絶交するつもりではないと思うのだけれど」
English: “Nor do I intend to sever our relationship the instant you withdraw. I hope we can continue cooperating just as before, but as independent organizations. ...What do you say? I do not imagine that you intend to break with us here and now.”

Japanese: 「もちろんだ。私としても、好き好んで対立を求めているわけではない」
English: “Of course not. I have no desire to seek conflict for its own sake.”

Japanese: 「私としては非常に残念だけれども……しかし、判断自体は尊重する。龍頭である私に組織の決定権があるように、あなたにも自分の組織の行き先を決める権利がある」
English: “I find the decision extremely regrettable... but I respect it. Just as I, as Longtou, possess the right to decide the course of my organization, you possess the right to determine the future of your own.”

Japanese: 「感謝する」
English: “You have my gratitude.”

Japanese: フェルナンデスがそしてデザートを残し退室した。
English: Fernandes then left the room with his dessert unfinished.

Japanese: このやりとりは同室した面々に少なからず衝撃を与えた。
English: The exchange came as a considerable shock to the others in the room.

Japanese: 統合に従えないことを理由にフェルナンデスは離脱を宣言し、龍頭はそれを全く引き留めず、それどころか、方針に従えないのならば出て行く他ないと断言をしたのである。態度を保留するかたちであった他の幹部達も、判断を迫られている。
English: Fernandes had declared that he would withdraw because he could not accept integration. The Longtou made no attempt whatsoever to stop him—indeed, he had stated outright that if Fernandes could not obey the policy, he had no choice but to leave. The other officers, who had withheld their own decisions, were now being forced to choose.

Japanese: それ以降会食が解散されるまで誰もフェルナンデスの離脱について話題にはしなかったが、みなそれを強く意識しているのは明白だった。
English: No one raised the subject of Fernandes’s withdrawal before the dinner disbanded, but it was plain that everyone remained acutely conscious of it.

Japanese: 会食が終わった後、馬明はフェルナンデスの離脱を全く咎めなかったことを心配したが、亮は一笑に付すばかりであった。
English: After the dinner, Ma Ming expressed concern that Leung had not reproached Fernandes at all for withdrawing. Leung merely laughed the matter aside.

Japanese: 「彼は惜しいが、どうせ引き留めたところで離脱するのはわかっていたからね。それならはっきりさせた方が良い。これで少し状況が動くはずだ」
English: “He is a regrettable loss, but I knew he would withdraw no matter how I tried to stop him. Better to make matters clear. This should set the situation in motion.”

Japanese: 果たして事態は彼の言う通りになった。
English: Events did indeed unfold as he had said.

Japanese: 翌日には壬生屋タカシが執務室を訪れて、統合に賛成すると言い出した。その代わり、トーマスと同じように今の立場を保証して貰いたいとのこと。
English: The following day, Takashi Mibuya visited Leung’s office and announced his support for integration. In exchange, he wanted his present position guaranteed in the same manner as Thomas’s.

Japanese: 同席していた馬明は驚いた。
English: Ma Ming, who was present, stared in surprise.

Japanese: 「まさか、あいつが来るとは思わなかった！」
English: “I never expected him to come!”

Japanese: 壬生屋が退室すると、目を丸くして声をあげる。
English: Ma Ming exclaimed with rounded eyes after Mibuya left the room.

Japanese: 「どうして？」
English: “Why?”

Japanese: 亮は机に肘をつき、馬明に問い返す。
English: Leung rested his elbows on the desk and returned the question.

Japanese: 「だって、壬生屋は処刑された劉建志の親友だろう？　我々に憎しみを持っていたっておかしくないじゃないか」
English: “Mibuya was close friends with Ryu Kenshi, the man we executed. It would be perfectly natural for him to hate us.”

Japanese: 「彼はそんな風には考えないよ。合理的な人間だからね。処刑されるようなへまをした劉建志が愚かだとしか思いやしない。むしろ、ライバルの一人が減ったと喜ぶくらいだろう」
English: “He doesn’t think that way. He is a rational man. He would simply consider Ryu Kenshi a fool for blundering badly enough to be executed. If anything, he is probably pleased to have one fewer rival.”

Japanese: 亮は苦笑しながらそう言った。
English: Leung spoke with a wry smile.

Japanese: 「でも、僕もやっぱり不思議な気がするよ。あんなに反対していたのに……」
English: “I still find it strange too. He was so strongly opposed before...”

Japanese: その場にいたトーマスも驚きをもってそう首をひねる。
English: Thomas, who had also been present, tilted his head in surprise.

Japanese: 「別に不思議なことはないよ」
English: “There is nothing strange about it.”

Japanese: 亮はこともなげに言う。
English: Leung spoke as though it were obvious.

Japanese: 「壬生屋タカシは統合に反対していたが、あれはただのポーズなんだよ。ごねて僕らから条件を引き出したかっただけだ。最初からYSを出るつもりなんかない」
English: “Takashi Mibuya opposed integration, but that was nothing but posturing. He only meant to dig in his heels until he extracted concessions from us. He never intended to leave YS.”

Japanese: 「どうしてそう思う？」
English: “Why do you think that?”

Japanese: 馬明は腑に落ちない顔で問う。
English: Ma Ming asked, plainly unconvinced.

Japanese: 「YSを出たら彼は売春組織のオーナーに戻るだけだからね。女衒、女衒と軽く見られるのを嫌っている彼にその選択肢は選べない。彼の目標はYSの中で少しでも地位を高めることだが、僕を殺してとってかわるのは現実的じゃない。仮に殺せたとしても、壬生屋って名前が嫌われていて誰もついてこないのを理解している。だから、龍頭である僕が交渉に応じるつもりがないことを示せば、誰よりも早くかけつけて媚を売り、少しでもいい地位を確保したくなるはずさ」
English: “If he leaves YS, he goes back to being nothing more than the owner of a prostitution business. He cannot choose that when he despises being dismissed as a common pimp. His ambition is to raise his position within YS as high as he can, but killing and replacing me is not a realistic course. Even if he succeeded in killing me, he understands that the Mibuya name is hated and no one would follow him. So the moment I show him I have no intention of negotiating, he’ll be the first to come running, flatter me, and try to secure the best position he can.”

Japanese: 「なるほど」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: そこで馬明は納得して頷く。
English: Ma Ming finally nodded in understanding.

Japanese: 「しかし、小謝は、最初からこうなることがわかっていたみたいだな。もしかして、だから、フェルナンデスの娘を嫁に貰おうなどということを企てて、決裂させたのか？」
English: “Still, Siu Tse, you sound as though you knew from the beginning that this would happen. You didn’t devise that scheme to marry Fernandes’s daughter because you wanted the proposal to collapse, did you?”

Japanese: 「まさか」
English: “Certainly not.”

Japanese: 亮は肩をすくめる。
English: Leung shrugged.

Japanese: 「どっちにしたって壬生屋はどうせ統合されるわけだから、わざわざそんな手間をかけたりはしないよ。あの結婚がうまく行った方が本当は良かったんだ。だって、どう考えたってフェルナンデスが一番厄介な問題だからね。だから、苦労しなくちゃいけないのはこれからさ」
English: “Mibuya was going to accept integration in any case. I would never go to such trouble for that. I truly wanted the marriage to succeed. No matter how you look at the matter, Fernandes is the most difficult problem of all. That means the real work begins now.”

Japanese: 彼はそう言うと、わざとらしく溜息をついて見せた。
English: He followed the words with a deliberately theatrical sigh.

Japanese: しかし、実際にはこの後謝亮がジョゼ・フェルナンデスの対応で頭を悩ませることにはならなかった。
English: In reality, however, Leung would not, in fact, have to agonize over what to do about José Fernandes.

Japanese: なぜならば、それから数日後にジョゼ・フェルナンデスは死んでしまうからである。
English: Only a few days later, José Fernandes would be dead.

Japanese: それは一本の電話から始まった。
English: It began with a single telephone call.

Japanese: まだ夜も明けぬ午前四時。ベッドで眠りこけていた亮は電話の呼び出し音で目を覚ました。久しぶりのリタ・フェルナンデスからの通話着信を、一体なんの用かと出てみると、感情の乱れたとりとめのない言葉がスピーカーから溢れ出た。
English: At four in the morning, before the first light of dawn, the ringing phone woke Leung from a deep sleep. The call was from Rita Fernandes, from whom he had not heard in some time. He answered, wondering what she could want, and a flood of rambling words, disordered by emotion, poured from the speaker.

Japanese: 『小謝っ！　お父さんとお姉ちゃんが……ああ……、どうして……』
English: ‘Siu Tse! Father and my sister... Ah... Why...?’

Japanese: リタは完全に動揺し、半分泣きながら何かを訴えている。落ち着かせながら話を聞くと、彼女は屋敷に居て、どうも襲撃に遭ったらしい。謝亮はどこかに身を隠して動かぬよう伝えてベッドから飛び起きた。
English: Rita was completely distraught, attempting through her sobs to tell him something. Leung calmed her enough to learn that she was at the family residence and that it had apparently been attacked. He told her to hide somewhere and remain still, then leapt out of bed.

Japanese: 双花紅根の馬世傑をたたき起こし、すぐに動かせる数名を連れてグランドタワーを出る。
English: He roused Double Flower Red Pole Ma Sai-kit and left Grand Tower with the handful of men he could mobilize at once.

Japanese: その日は土砂降りで、真っ黒い空から滝のような雨がアスファルトを叩きつけていた。
English: Rain fell in torrents that day, pouring from the pitch-black sky like a waterfall and hammering the asphalt.

Japanese: 屋敷に到着すると、フェルナンデスの部下達が先に到着していて建物に入ろうとする亮の行き先を阻む。
English: When they reached the residence, Fernandes’s subordinates had already arrived. They barred Leung’s party from entering the building.

Japanese: 「我々は、もうYSの一員ではありませんから。お引き取りください」
English: “We are no longer members of YS. Please leave.”

Japanese: ポロシャツを着て、浅黒い肌をした口ひげの男が亮達の前に立ちはだかった。彼はその場で一番立場の高い者らしく、近くのものに指示を出しながら、亮達の対応に当たっている。
English: A dark-skinned, mustachioed man in a polo shirt blocked their way. Apparently the senior person present, he issued instructions to those around him while dealing with Leung’s group.

Japanese: その男と雨に打たれながら押し問答をしていると、寝間着姿のリタが現れ、
English: They were arguing back and forth with the man beneath the rain when Rita appeared in her nightclothes.

Japanese: 「私が呼んだのです！　お願いします、通してあげてください！」
English: “I called them! Please, let them through!”

Japanese: と叫んだので亮達はやっとその現場に足を踏み入れることが出来た。
English: Only after she shouted this did Leung and the others gain access.

Japanese: 屋敷のなかも、銃を持った男達が歩き回り、ポルトガル語で言葉を交わしている。リタは電話の時よりは落ち着いていたが、亮の顔を見ると張り詰めていたものが切れてしまったらしく、説明しかけたところでボロボロと涙を流し泣き崩れてしまった。
English: Inside the residence, too, armed men walked the halls and exchanged words in Portuguese. Rita was calmer than she had been on the phone, but the sight of Leung’s face seemed to break the tension holding her together. She had scarcely begun her explanation when tears streamed down her face and she collapsed in grief.

Japanese: そして喋れなくなってしまった彼女のかわりに、さきほど亮達を入り口のところで押しとどめた口ひげの男が説明した。
English: The mustachioed man who had stopped Leung’s party at the entrance gave the explanation in her place.

Japanese: 今夜、フェルナンデスたちは家族集まってリビングルームで話し合いをしていたらしい。それは夜更けまで続き、リタは眠くなって寝室に戻った。これが結果として彼女の命を救うことになる。
English: The Fernandes family had apparently gathered in the living room that night for a discussion. It continued until late, when Rita grew sleepy and returned to her bedroom. In the end, that decision saved her life.

Japanese: 襲撃は午前四時頃に行われた。覆面をかぶって武装した４、５人がに襲来し、入り口の守衛を撃ち殺すとそのまま屋敷の敷地内に入り、庭に回ってそこから直接リビングルームを襲った。そこには二人のボディガードが居たが突然の襲撃には対応出来なかった。そしてフェルナンデスと二人の娘、そして使用人の若い女と中年の男が殺害された。
English: The attack occurred at approximately four in the morning. Four or five masked and armed people arrived, shot dead the guard at the entrance, entered the grounds, went around to the garden, and attacked the living room directly from there. Two bodyguards were present there, but could not respond to the sudden attack. Fernandes and two of his daughters were killed, along with a young female servant and a middle-aged male servant.

Japanese: リタが騒音で起きてリビングに足を踏み入れた時にはすでに襲撃者は去っており、その現場から亮に連絡したのがさっきの電話であったらしい。一方、リタと同様体調不良で自室で休んでいたもう一人の使用人も何を逃れ、こちらは口ひげの男に報告をしたのだそうだ。
English: By the time the noise woke Rita and she entered the living room, the attackers had already left. The telephone call had apparently been placed to Leung from that scene. Another servant, who like Rita had been resting in a private room because of illness, likewise escaped the attack and reported it to the mustachioed man.

Japanese: 説明が終わるころにはリタも気を取り直していた。口ひげの男はリタの精神状態を心配して現場にはもう行くべきでないと反対したが、リタはそれを聞かず、自ら先頭に立って亮達を現場となったリビングルームに案内した。
English: By the time the explanation ended, Rita had regained her composure. Concerned for her mental state, the mustachioed man argued that she should not return to the scene, but Rita ignored him and personally led Leung’s group to the living room where the attack had occurred.

Japanese: そこに足を踏み入れ、部屋の照明のスイッチを入れると、説明から想像される通りの光景が目の前に広がった。
English: They entered and switched on the lights. The scene before them was exactly what the report had led them to expect.

Japanese: 庭へ続く全面ガラス張りのサッシは銃弾によって破壊され、強い雨が吹き込んで毛足の長い絨毯を濡らしている。暗い庭には飼い犬が撃たれて死んでいるのが見えた。
English: Gunfire had destroyed the floor-to-ceiling glass doors leading to the garden. Strong rain blew through the opening and soaked the deep-pile carpet. In the dark garden, they could see the family dog lying dead from a gunshot.

Japanese: 部屋のなかの壁もソファーも、あらゆるものは穴だらけになるか、完全に打ち壊されて原型をとどめていなかった。
English: Inside the room, the walls, the sofas, and everything else had either been riddled with holes or destroyed beyond recognition.

Japanese: 床には血液や肉の塊が飛び散り、部屋全体を血なまぐさくしている。
English: Blood and lumps of flesh lay scattered across the floor, filling the entire room with the reek of blood.

Japanese: そして部屋の中央には毛布をかぶせられて盛り上がりがある。世傑が近づいて端をめくると、犠牲者の遺体が胸の上で手を組むかたちで並べられていた。フェルナンデスの部下たちがいたましい姿で倒れていた主人たちをこのように整えたのだと言う。
English: At the center of the room was a mound covered by a blanket. Sai-kit approached and lifted one edge. The victims’ bodies had been arranged side by side with their hands folded upon their chests. Fernandes’s subordinates had apparently arranged their masters’ bodies this way after finding them where they had fallen.

Japanese: 犠牲者は、ジョゼ・フェルナンデス、アウロラ・フェルナンデス、アナ・クララ・フェルナンデス。いずれも亮が子供の頃からよく知っている人々だ。
English: The victims were José Fernandes, Aurora Fernandes, and Ana Clara Fernandes. Leung had known all three well since childhood.

Japanese: 使用人達の遺体はさほどでもなかったが、フェルナンデスの家族はどれも大量の銃弾を受けて損傷が激しかった。特に頭部は原形がないほどに破壊されており、アウロラなどはとれかけた下あごが首と皮一枚で繋がっているだけでそこから上は完全に失われている。あの街中に知れ渡った美貌は、この部屋に散らばる無数の赤い塊になってしまったのだろう。
English: The servants’ bodies were not as badly damaged, but every member of the Fernandes family had been struck by an enormous number of bullets. Their heads in particular had been destroyed beyond recognition. Aurora’s lower jaw hung from her neck by a single strip of skin, and everything above it was gone. The beauty once famous throughout the city had presumably become the countless red fragments scattered across the room.

Japanese: 「あまり慣れてない人間の犯行ね。きっと、家族にひどく恨みがある連中よ」
English: “This looks like the work of amateurs. Whoever did it must have held an extraordinary grudge against the family.”

Japanese: 毛布をかけ直してから世傑はそう言った。
English: Sai-kit replaced the blanket as he spoke.

Japanese: 「大した戦闘にもならない一方的な殺戮の筈なのに、あまりにも散らかし過ぎだもの。興奮しすぎて頭の中が真っ白になったのかしらね？　弾をそこらじゅうにプレゼントしてるわ」
English: “It should have been a one-sided massacre with hardly any fighting, but they made far too much of a mess. Perhaps they became so excited that their minds went blank. They sprayed bullets all over the place like presents.”

Japanese: 彼はそっけなく言ったが、今日の被害者は幼い頃からつき合いのある人間たちであった。普段なら絶え間なく冗談を口にする彼も、この屋敷に到着してから一度も軽口を叩いていない。
English: He spoke curtly, but he had known that day’s victims since childhood. Though ordinarily unceasing in his jokes, he had not made a single flippant remark since reaching the residence.

Japanese: 先ほどまで泣いていたリタは、亮の隣に立ち、さきほど世傑が毛布をめくったときも目をそらさず気丈に家族の姿を見た。顔は血の気が引いて蒼白だったが、襲撃者に対する怒りが表情にあらわれていた。
English: Rita, who had been weeping moments earlier, stood beside Leung. When Sai-kit lifted the blanket, she did not avert her eyes, but steadfastly looked upon her family. Her face was drained white, yet anger toward the attackers showed in her expression.

Japanese: 亮は感情のうかがい知れない鈍い表情をしている。そしてふとしゃがみ込み、毛布をめくって死者たちの姿をもう一度確認してから立ち上がると、リタの顔を見る。
English: Leung wore a dull, heavy expression from which no emotion could be read. Abruptly he crouched, lifted the blanket, and inspected the dead once more. Then he stood and looked into Rita’s face.

Japanese: その時の彼の目は、リタの身体に鳥肌が立つほどであった。
English: The look in his eyes at that moment sent goosebumps over Rita’s skin.

Japanese: 「この件は、僕たちも追う」
English: “We will pursue this as well.”

Japanese: ぽつりと一言だけ言い、あとは相手の返事も聞かず、仲間と共にその場を後にした。
English: He offered only those few words. Without waiting for an answer, he left the scene with his companions.

Japanese: フェルナンデス殺害のニュースは関係者によって隠蔽されメディアに取り上げられることはなかったが、どこから漏れたのか、たちまちY地区じゅうで噂となった。
English: Those involved kept the Fernandes murders out of the media, but somehow the news leaked. In no time at all, it had become the subject of rumor throughout Y District.

Japanese: 故人はY地区を代表するギャングの一人であり、二人の娘もこの街では美女の例えとして持ち出されるほどの有名人である。それが無惨に殺害されたとなれば、隠し通せるはずもなかった。
English: The dead man had been one of the foremost gangsters in Y District, and his two daughters were so famous that people invoked them as bywords for beauty in the city. Once such figures had been brutally murdered, there could be no concealing it.

Japanese: そしてその犯人が見つかっていないとなれば様々な憶測が飛び交うのも当然だが、いくつも生まれた陰謀説のなかで、もっとも信憑性が高く、多くの人々が信じたのが謝亮犯人説だろう。
English: With the culprits still at large, speculation naturally ran wild. Of all the conspiracy theories that arose, the theory people considered most credible, and the one most widely believed, was probably that Tse Leung had done it.

Japanese: 何と言ってもフェルナンデス・ファミリーがYSを離脱した直後の事件である。身内の粛清などで過激な活動が目立つ亮がその第一犯人として疑われるのは無理のない話で、事情に暗いものも通じたものも、彼の陰謀であるのは間違いないと断言するものが多かった。
English: After all, the incident had occurred immediately after the Fernandes Family withdrew from YS. Leung had drawn attention through the violence of his internal purges, so it was hardly surprising that suspicion fell upon him first. People ignorant of the circumstances and people familiar with them alike confidently declared that it had to be his conspiracy.

Japanese: その噂は街の無責任な市民の間だけでなく、裏社会の人間達、もっと言えばYSのメンバーでさえそう信じているものが少なくない。
English: The belief was not confined to irresponsible citizens gossiping in the streets. It had spread through the underworld, and more than a few members of YS itself shared it.

Japanese: 彼らは事件直後に亮が現場へ急行し、そして犯人の捜索を行っていることは知っていたが、それでもこの狡猾な龍頭ならやりかねないと信じているようだった。
English: They knew that Leung had rushed to the scene immediately after the incident and was searching for the culprits. Even so, they seemed to believe that such a cunning Longtou was perfectly capable of it.

Japanese: 「やっぱり、あれをやったのは龍頭ですよね？」
English: “It was the Longtou who did it, wasn’t it?”

Japanese: トーマスも、部下の、しかも幹部クラスの人間にそう訊ねられた時には驚く他なかった。
English: Thomas could only stare when one of his own subordinates—and an officer at that—asked him the question.

Japanese: 彼はそんなわけがないと噂を否定したが、部下は信じようとしない。それどころか、
English: He denied the rumor, insisting that it could not possibly be true. His subordinate refused to believe him. Worse still, the man continued:

Japanese: 「龍頭を信じちゃ駄目ですよ。あれは今までのボスとは違って非情そのものです。用無しになったり、邪魔になればすぐに消そうとする人物のようです。フェルナンデスの件もそうです。今のうちに独立した方がいいんじゃないですか？　ボスが本気で説得すれば、飲まざるを得ないんじゃないですか。そして、他の華僑達と連合して新しい組織を作りましょう。この街にはYSとは違う華僑だけの組織が必要です」
English: “You can’t trust the Longtou. That man is nothing like our previous bosses. He’s ruthlessness itself. The moment someone is no longer useful—or simply gets in his way—he seems ready to make them disappear. Just look at the Fernandes affair. Shouldn’t we declare our independence while we still can? If you negotiated in earnest, Boss, he’d have no choice but to accept it. Then we could join forces with the other overseas Chinese and create a new organization. This city needs an organization exclusively for Chinese people, separate from YS.”

Japanese: そう独立までを進められる始末であった。
English: Thomas had even found himself being urged to declare independence.

Japanese: まあ、このことがなくてもトーマスの部下にも吸収に否定的で、もう一度リャオ・ファミリーの独立を希望するものは何人か存在する。
English: The incident aside, several of his subordinates had opposed their absorption from the beginning and wanted the Liao Family to recover its independence.

Japanese: トーマスはこうやって独立を口に出されるたびに、内心閉口しつつも、亮に協力することの意味と必然性を説明するのだった。
English: Whenever one of them spoke of independence, Thomas would suppress his private exasperation and explain why cooperating with Leung was both meaningful and necessary.

Japanese: ただ、そうして亮の潔白を主張するトーマスでさえも、完全にその可能性は存在しないかと言われれば、否定しきれないものがあった。だが、そんな風に思ってしまったときは慌ててその考えを否定し、亮を疑ってしまった自分を恥じるのだ。確かに彼は必要があれば戦うと言っていたが、本当に、幼なじみのアウロラや、アナ・クララを襲わせるとは考えられない。
English: Yet even Thomas, for all his insistence upon Leung’s innocence, could not completely dismiss the possibility when forced to consider it. Whenever the thought occurred to him, he would hastily reject it and feel ashamed that he had doubted Leung at all. Leung had certainly said that he would fight if necessary. But Thomas could not believe he would truly order an attack upon Aurora and Ana Clara, his own childhood friends.

Japanese: 襲撃犯はすぐに特定された。
English: The attackers were soon identified.

Japanese: 名前はミゲル。ブラジル出身の二十三才のタイプBで、かつてはフェルナンデスの世話になっていたが、組織の決まり事が守れず除名。滑走路通りをうろついて観光客を狙ったスリやひったくりでその日暮らしをしている男だ。
English: One was named Miguel, a twenty-three-year-old Type B from Brazil. The Fernandes Family had once looked after him, but his inability to obey its rules led to his expulsion. Since then, he had lived from one day to the next around Runway Street, picking pockets and snatching bags from tourists.

Japanese: そんな彼が、なぜかサブマシンガンを入手して、酒場で自慢をしていたという情報が入ったのである。
English: Then information arrived that Miguel had somehow obtained a submachine gun and had been boasting about it in a bar.

Japanese: 馬世傑が仲間と共に彼が寝床としているパラシュート通りの簡易宿泊所を訪ねると、麻薬を使い、ベッドの上でぐにゃぐにゃになって笑っている姿で発見された。荷物の中からは銃と血のついた札束が見つかり、即刻グランドタワーに連行されることになる。
English: Ma Sai-kit and several companions visited the cheap lodging house on Parachute Street where he slept. They found him high on drugs, sprawled limply across his bed and laughing. A gun and a bundle of bloodstained bills lay among his belongings. He was taken to Grand Tower at once.

Japanese: ミゲルは臆病な小心者で、窓のない暗い部屋で椅子に縛り付けると、薬剤や拷問をしなくとも、少し脅しただけでぺらぺらと喋り出し、フェルナンデス一家殺人事件の全容が明らかになった。
English: Miguel was a timid coward. Once he had been tied to a chair in a dark, windowless room, no drugs or torture were required. A little intimidation was enough to make him talk freely, and the full story of the Fernandes Family murders came to light.

Japanese: 主犯はダヴィという二十一才の若者である。タイプBで、少年のころに発症しており時々幻覚に襲われることがあった。そのためトラブルが多く、故郷を追われ、あちこちを彷徨い、フェルナンデスという面倒見の良い親分がいるとききつけこの街にやって来たのが去年のことだ。
English: The ringleader was a twenty-one-year-old named Davi. He was a Type B whose symptoms had manifested during adolescence, and he sometimes suffered hallucinations. The resulting trouble drove him from his hometown. He wandered from place to place until he heard of a generous boss named Fernandes and came to this city the previous year.

Japanese: そこでダヴィは境遇に同情したフェルナンデスによって非常に親切な扱いを受け、屋敷に居候させて貰いながら彼の紹介した仕事場で働くことになった。しかし、どの仕事場でも彼は長続きしなかった。理由は症状だけでなく、盗癖があり、店や同僚のものを盗んでしまうからだった。
English: Fernandes sympathized with Davi’s circumstances and treated him with extraordinary kindness, allowing him to stay at the mansion while arranging employment for him. But Davi never lasted long in any workplace. His symptoms were not the only reason: he was also a habitual thief who stole from shops and coworkers.

Japanese: このことが知れてもフェルナンデスは家から追い出したりしようとはせず、彼の更正を期待して説教をしたり、彼のために労力を割いたがそれは報われなかった。結局ダヴィ自身がその生活に嫌気がさし、何も言わずに姿を消した。
English: Even after learning the truth, Fernandes did not attempt to throw Davi out. He lectured the young man in hope of reforming him and expended considerable effort on his behalf, but none of it bore fruit. In the end, Davi himself grew tired of that life and vanished without a word.

Japanese: そして街でこそ泥などをする生活を送り、同じような境遇のミゲルと知り合った。
English: He returned to a life of petty theft in the city and met Miguel, whose circumstances resembled his own.

Japanese: ダヴィはミゲルに対し、よくフェルナンデスのことを語ったが、いずれも嫉妬と憎悪に塗れたものであった。
English: Davi often spoke to Miguel about Fernandes. Every such account was steeped in envy and hatred.

Japanese: フェルナンデス家の豊かな財産、美しく仲の良い娘達との幸福な家庭、どんな命令にも従う忠実な部下と、彼らから得る尊敬、そしてタイプBの苦しみとは無縁なノーマルであること。それらはいずれも、ダヴィが渇望してもけして手に入れられることがなかったものである。
English: The Fernandes Family’s wealth. Fernandes’s happy home with his beautiful, close-knit daughters. His loyal subordinates, who obeyed every command, and the respect they accorded him. His existence as a Normal untouched by the suffering of Type Bs. Davi desperately craved all of it, yet none would ever be his.

Japanese: この屈折した憎悪が具体的な犯行計画に変わるのに、そう長い時間はかからなかった。武器を買い、泥棒仲間をさらに二人加え、着々と準備が進められた。目的はファミリーの殺害と、金品の奪取。屋敷で居候していたダヴィは、金がどこにあって、どのようなルートなら襲撃が成功しやすいかを知っていた。
English: It did not take long for that twisted hatred to become a concrete plan. Davi bought weapons, recruited two more companions from among his fellow thieves, and advanced his preparations methodically. Their objectives were to kill the Family and steal its valuables. Having lived in the mansion, Davi knew where the money was kept and which route would give the attack its best chance of success.

Japanese: そしてあの夜、計画は実行に移されたのである。
English: That night, they put the plan into action.

Japanese: 四人は泥棒が専門で、殺人などの経験がなく、興奮剤を注射してから計画を実行したが、みな無我夢中だった。本当ならば屋敷の各部屋をまわって家族の全員を殺しきる筈だったが、深夜にもかかわらずにフェルナンデス一家はリビングルームに集まっていて、そこでリタ以外の全員を一片に殺せてしまったので、その場に長く留まるのが怖くなった。そこで彼らはリタの殺害を断念すると、金庫を破壊して金を盗み、現場から逃げ出したのである。
English: All four men were thieves by trade and had no experience of murder. They injected themselves with stimulants before carrying out the plan, but once it began, each acted in a frenzy. They had intended to visit every room in the mansion and kill the entire family. Despite the late hour, however, the Fernandes family was gathered in the living room, allowing the attackers to kill everyone except Rita at once. Afraid to remain any longer, they abandoned the search for her, broke open the safe, stole the money, and fled.

Japanese: その後は奪ったものを分配してバラバラになったので、他の実行犯がどうしているかはミゲルも知らなかった。
English: Afterward, they divided the proceeds and went their separate ways. Miguel did not know what had become of the other participants.

Japanese: この報告を受け、謝亮は残りの実行犯の捕縛を世傑に命じた。
English: Upon receiving the report, Tse Leung ordered Sai-kit to capture the remaining attackers.

Japanese: 共犯者の一人、ペドロはカジノで遊んでいるところを発見、素手で抵抗したが体術の達人である世傑にはかなわず瞬く間に失神させられ、グランドタワーに運ばれる。
English: One accomplice, Pedro, was found gambling in a casino. He resisted with his bare hands, but was no match for Sai-kit’s mastery of hand-to-hand combat. Sai-kit rendered him unconscious in moments and had him transported to Grand Tower.

Japanese: もう一人、ジョアンは売春宿から出て来たところで遭遇、銃撃戦になりその場で死亡させてしまうが、遺体として回収される。
English: Another, João, was encountered as he left a brothel. A gunfight followed, and he was killed at the scene. His body was recovered.

Japanese: そして主犯者のダヴィは暗闇通りで見つかったところから一旦は逃げることに成功したが、その後街から脱出しようと試みたところで、黄天明、天祥の人間レーダー姉妹に発見される。世傑に銃を突きつけると大人しく降伏し、グランドタワーに連行される。
English: Davi, the ringleader, initially escaped after being located on Darkness Street. When he later attempted to flee the city, however, the human-radar sisters Wong Tin-ming and Wong Tin-cheung discovered him. Sai-kit held him at gunpoint; Davi surrendered without resistance and was taken to Grand Tower.

Japanese: 彼らは龍頭である謝亮自らによる尋問を受け、フェルナンデス一家殺害に関与したことが明らかになると、フェルナンデス・ファミリーに身柄を引き渡されることになった。
English: The prisoners were interrogated by Tse Leung, the Longtou, in person. Once their participation in the Fernandes Family murders had been established, it was decided that they would be transferred into the custody of the Fernandes Family.

Japanese: ジョゼ・フェルナンデス亡きあとのファミリーは、一時的な措置としてあの口ひげの幹部――エンゾ・アラーニャ・エ・シウバが指揮を執っている。彼は他の幹部やリタとの協議の末、最大の罪を犯したものに行われる。この街では伝統的な手法で彼らを処刑することに決定した。
English: After José Fernandes’s death, the mustachioed officer Enzo Aranha e Silva had assumed command of the Family as a temporary measure. After consulting the other officers and Rita, he decided that the prisoners would be executed by a traditional method reserved in this city for those guilty of the gravest crimes.

Japanese: 三人は赤く熱した鉄の棒を用いた暴行によって痛めつけられ、やがて死亡が確認されると鉈によって首を切断される。こうして出来上がった斬首死体は、既に死んでいるジョアンのものとあわせ、暗闇通りの路上に放置されることになった。
English: The three men were beaten with red-hot iron bars. Once their deaths had been confirmed, their heads were severed with a machete. The resulting decapitated corpses were left upon Darkness Street together with João’s body.

Japanese: ワゴン車で運んできた遺体をアスファルトの上に蹴り落とす場面には謝亮も同行し、襲撃犯の無惨な最後を見届けた。
English: Tse Leung accompanied the party as they brought the bodies in a van and kicked them out onto the asphalt. He watched the attackers’ grisly end through to its conclusion.

Japanese: 遺体の胴体はうつぶせに並べられ、切り取られた頭部はその背中の上に置かれる。
English: The torsos were laid face down in a row, with each severed head placed upon its owner’s back.

Japanese: ギリギリまで冷静を保ってこの設置作業を見守っていたリタも、去る間際には我慢が出来なくなり、涙を流しながら遺体に石を投げつけた。
English: Rita maintained her composure almost until the work of arranging them had ended. As they were about to leave, however, she could endure it no longer. Weeping, she hurled stones at the bodies.

Japanese: こうして一件が落着すると、リタが父の跡を継いで新しいボスに就任し、エンゾのサポートを受けながらファミリーを率いてゆくことが決定した。
English: With the affair thus brought to a close, it was decided that Rita would succeed her father as the new boss and lead the Family with Enzo’s support.

Japanese: 暗闇通りからほど近く、一見すると何の変哲もないその民家こそが、Y地区中のタイプBたちが加盟しているという秘密結社『八龍会』の本拠地だ。
English: Not far from Darkness Street stood an utterly unremarkable private house. It was, in fact, the headquarters of the Eight Dragons Society, the secret organization said to count Type Bs throughout Y District among its members.

Japanese: 何かの祝い事の日には近所のタイプBの子供が集まってパーティを行ったり、平日の昼間にタイプBのカウンセラーや主婦達が集まって彼らならではの悩み事を打ち明け合ったり、明るく健康的な活動の反面、夜にはギャング組織の幹部などがとりまきを引き連れて出入りしたりもしている。そしてタイプBたちに、症状を和らげる薬物を、合法非合法限らずに安く販売もする。
English: On holidays, neighborhood Type B children gathered there for parties. On weekday afternoons, Type B counselors and housewives met to share problems particular to their condition. Yet for all those cheerful and wholesome activities, gang officers and their entourages also came and went at night. The Society sold Type Bs drugs that eased their symptoms at low prices, whether those substances were legal or illegal.

Japanese: その家の主は三人の老人で、東洋人、黒人、白人とそれぞれ違った人種であり、三人の間に上下はない。
English: The house belonged to three old men—one East Asian, one Black, and one white man. None held authority over the others.

Japanese: 裏社会での表看板がYSであり、その龍頭である謝亮だとするならば、裏社会のさらに裏の支配者と言えばこの三人になるだろう。この街ではあらゆる組織にタイプBが入り込んでおり、彼らはそれに強い影響力を持っている。
English: If YS and its Longtou, Tse Leung, represented the public face of the underworld, then these three might be called the rulers of the world behind the underworld. Type Bs had entered organizations throughout the city, and the elders exerted powerful influence over them.

Japanese: フェルナンデス一家が殺害されてから数日後のことである。昼下がり、この三人はのんびりと麻雀に興じていた。屋敷に遊びに来たゲストなどもよく使う古い全自動卓は、来客のない時でも三人によって酷使され、塗装のあちこちに剥げなどが目立つ。
English: It was several days after the Fernandes Family murders. In the middle of the afternoon, the three men were leisurely playing mahjong. Guests to the house often used the old automatic table, but the elders worked it hard even when no visitors were present, and its finish had worn away in places.

Japanese: 彼らの遊んでいるルールは、一般的によく知られている四人で遊ぶものではなく、三麻（サンマ）とよばれる三人麻雀であった。しかも一局ごとに点数を精算するタイプのルールを採用している。
English: They were not playing the familiar four-player game, but three-player mahjong, or sanma. Their rules also called for settling the score after every hand.

Japanese: 点数が高く、しかも早くなりやすい刺激的なルールで、よく遊ばれている半荘制のように大きな区切りがないからいつまでも遊んでいられる。老人たちはこのルールを非常に好んでおり、滅多に四人打ちでは遊ばない。
English: It was an exciting form of the game in which high scores came easily and hands ended quickly. Unlike the common hanchan format, it provided no large natural break, allowing play to continue indefinitely. The old men greatly preferred these rules and rarely played with four people.

Japanese: 現に今日も、見土道夫がいるのに、彼を見学させたまま三人でゲームを繰り返している。
English: Indeed, even with Michio Mido present today, they had left him to watch while the three of them played hand after hand.

Japanese: 「道夫、お前はまだやくたいもない饅頭売りをしているのかい？」
English: “Michio, are you still peddling those worthless little buns?”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは牌を一枚取り、そのまま卓の上に捨てるという動作をしながら言った。
English: Mr. Chen asked the question as he drew a tile and discarded it upon the table in one uninterrupted motion.

Japanese: 彼はリーチをしており、あとはあがるための牌を持って来るか、他のメンツが捨てるのを待つだけである。
English: He had declared riichi. All that remained was to draw his winning tile or wait for one of the others to discard it.

Japanese: 「やくたいもないって言い方はないでしょう」
English: “You don’t have to call them worthless.”

Japanese: 「そうは言っても、なかなか成果が出ていないようじゃないか」
English: “But you still don’t seem to be achieving much.”

Japanese: 三人の牌を取り、捨てるテンポは早く、すぐにミスター・チェンの手番が回ってくる。
English: The three men drew and discarded at a rapid tempo. Mr. Chen’s turn soon came around again.

Japanese: 「これからですよ。これから。やっと目処がついてきたところなんですから」
English: “It’s still early. Early. Things are finally starting to take shape.”

Japanese: 「ふん、いつも同じことばかり言っていますね」
English: “Hmph. You say the same thing every time.”

Japanese: 白い顔のミスター・スミスは持って来た牌を見て、手を止める。そしてミスター・チェンが捨てた牌の列を眺めている。
English: The white-faced Mr. Smith stopped when he saw the tile he had drawn. He studied the row of tiles Mr. Chen had discarded.

Japanese: 「遅いよ。下手な考え休むに似たりね」
English: “You’re slow. Second-rate thinking is no better than sleeping.”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンがそう煽ると、彼は眉間に皺を寄せ、
English: Mr. Chen’s taunt drew a crease between Smith’s brows.

Japanese: 「これは通るはずだヨ」
English: “This tile ought to be safe.”

Japanese: 悩んだ末に結局掴んだ牌を捨てた。
English: After all that hesitation, Smith discarded the tile he had drawn.

Japanese: それは何事もなかったようで、次のミスター・アーノルドが卓の上の牌に手を伸ばす。
English: Nothing happened. The next player, Mr. Arnold, reached toward the tiles upon the table.

Japanese: 「YSは世代交代をして、フェルナンデスのところも娘があとを継いだ。そろそろお前にも、重要な役割についてほしいと私たちは思っているんだよ」
English: “YS has passed to a new generation, and the Fernandes girl has succeeded her father. We think it is time for you to assume an important role as well.”

Japanese: アーノルドは言うと、持って来た牌を自分の手の牌と取り替えて卓の上に横向きに並べ、自分の引き出しから赤丸ひとつが印字された点棒を一本放り投げる。
English: As Arnold spoke, he exchanged the tile he had drawn for one in his hand, set the discarded tile sideways upon the table, and tossed a thousand-point stick from his drawer.

Japanese: 「リーチ」
English: “Riichi.”

Japanese: 「あいやー、それはあまりにも強気な追っかけだよ。困ったね」
English: “Aiyah! Chasing my riichi with a hand that aggressive? Now I’m in trouble.”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは苦笑しながら牌をとる。
English: Mr. Chen drew a tile with a rueful smile.

Japanese: 「カミラと、ジョン、そしてお前の三人で幹部になるんだ。我々の後継者としてな。この組織は、黒、白、黄色という三人でバランス良くやっていかなきゃいけない。そうでなければ、この街に住む様々な肌の色のタイプBが、気後れなく参加することは出来ないからな」
English: “Camilla, John, and you will become the three officers—our successors. The organization needs three people, Black, white, and Asian, to maintain its balance. Otherwise, Type Bs of every color who live in this city will not be able to join without hesitation.”

Japanese: ミスター・アーノルドは傍らのサイドテーブルに置いたコーヒーカップを手に取るとそう言った。
English: Mr. Arnold picked up the coffee cup on the side table beside him as he spoke.

Japanese: 「……そりゃ、手伝いくらいはしますが、そんなに本格的には出来ませんよ。何度も言ってますが」
English: “...I’ll help out, but I can’t commit myself to anything that serious. I’ve told you that many times.”

Japanese: 道夫が困って頭を掻くと、
English: Michio scratched his head in discomfort.

Japanese: 「ロン！」
English: “Ron!”

Japanese: 鋭く発声したのは、ミスター・スミスであった。
English: The sharp call came from Mr. Smith.

Japanese: 「おー、テンパイしていたのか！　しかも倍満！」
English: “Oh! You were in tenpai? And it’s baiman!”

Japanese: スミスが倒した手牌を見て、その思ったよりも高い得点に頭を抱えたのは振り込む形となったミスター・チェンである。
English: When Smith laid down his hand, the score was far higher than Mr. Chen had expected. Chen, who had dealt into it, clutched his head.

Japanese: 「降りても良かったし、手代わりを待っても良かったんですが、高いやつを出してくれましたからね。これで今日は私のトップですか？」
English: “I could have folded or waited for my hand to change, but you dealt into such a valuable hand. Does that put me in first place for the day?”

Japanese: 普段通りの無表情でスミスはそう言った。
English: Smith said it with his usual expressionless face.

Japanese: 「何、これからよ」
English: “Nonsense. I’m only getting started.”

Japanese: チェンは舌打ちをして牌を崩した。
English: Chen clicked his tongue and broke apart his hand.

Japanese: 三人は両手を伸ばして今使った牌をじゃらじゃらと卓の中央のくぼみへ落とし込む。そうしてボタンを押すと、新しい牌がすぐゲームを開始できるように二段の列となってせり上がってくるのが全自動卓というものなのだが、何度押しても動かない。
English: All three men reached forward and swept the used tiles with a clatter into the hollow at the center of the table. Ordinarily, pressing a button would cause new tiles to rise in two-tiered walls, ready for the next hand. But no matter how many times they pressed, the table did not move.

Japanese: 「また故障！　三日前に修理して貰ったばかりなのに！」
English: “Broken again! We only had it repaired three days ago!”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは顔を真っ赤にして卓の端を手のひらで叩く。
English: Face flushed crimson, Mr. Chen slapped the edge of the table with his palm.

Japanese: 「今日はもうやめよう。私はすこし疲れた」
English: “Let us stop for today. I am a little tired.”

Japanese: ミスター・アーノルドはコーヒーを飲みながら醒めた表情で言う。
English: Mr. Arnold said it coolly as he drank his coffee.

Japanese: 「アナタはプラスでもマイナスでもないからそれでいいだろうけれど、私はこれでは引っ込みつかないよ……」
English: “Easy for you to say when you’ve broken even. I can’t possibly leave things like this...”

Japanese: 「頭が熱くなったままじゃ負けが込むだけだ。それに、どうやってやる？　手積みでは面倒で仕方がない」
English: “You’ll only lose more while your head is hot. Besides, how would we play? Building the walls by hand would be intolerably tedious.”

Japanese: 「勝ったから言うわけではないですが、私ももう十分でし。また修理が終わったらやればいいじゃないですか」
English: “It isn’t because I won, but I’ve had enough too. We can play again once the table is repaired.”

Japanese: 二人に諭されると、ミスター・チェンは渋々引き下がる他なかった。
English: With both men urging him to stop, Mr. Chen had no choice but to retreat grudgingly.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、そういうことで、おれもコンタ一人に店番させてるから、そろそろ……」
English: “Well, if that settles it, I left Konta alone to mind the shop, so I should probably be going...”

Japanese: このタイミングに道夫はそう言って席を外そうとしたのだが、
English: Michio attempted to use the opportunity to excuse himself.

Japanese: 「いや、お前には残って貰う。会って貰いたい人間がいるのでな」
English: “No. You will remain. There is someone we want you to meet.”

Japanese: ミスター・アーノルドが釘を刺すので、浮かしかけた腰をまた降ろす。
English: Mr. Arnold’s warning forced Michio to sit back down just as he had begun to rise.

Japanese: 「『またか』って顔をしているね。そうなんだよ、またなんだ。すまないね」
English: “Your face says, ‘Again?’ Yes, again. I am sorry.”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは苦笑して言った。
English: Mr. Chen spoke with a rueful smile.

Japanese: まったく、道夫からすればうんざりするようなやり方である。
English: Michio was thoroughly sick of their methods.

Japanese: はじめから人と会うと言って呼んだら来ないのがわかっているから、顔を見たいだの、体調がよろしくなくて不安だの、別の理由をつけて呼び出し、人とあわせるのだ。道夫はわかっていても、この手の誘い文句には弱い。
English: They knew that he would refuse if told from the beginning that they wanted him to meet someone. Instead, they claimed to miss his face or said that one of them felt unwell and was worried, luring him there for some unrelated reason before presenting the visitor. Even when Michio recognized the trick, such appeals to his concern remained his weakness.

Japanese: 可愛い女の子がこういう理由を使うならまだしも、なんだって食えない爺さんどもにこんなことを言われて来てしまうのか、自分でもそう思いはするのだが。
English: He could have understood allowing a pretty girl to coax him with excuses like those. Why did he keep falling for them when they came from these wily old men? He often wondered the same thing himself.

Japanese: そうして、ここのところ何度も人と会わされている。相手は滑走路通りの商業ビルのオーナーやら、ギャングのお偉いさんやら、銀行の頭取やら様々な社会的地位を持つ人間だ。
English: They had introduced him to people repeatedly of late: the owner of a commercial building on Runway Street, a senior gang figure, the president of a bank, and others who occupied all manner of social positions.

Japanese: 道夫だけでなく若い三人でどうこうと、老人たちは言うが、こうして引っ張り出されるのは道夫ばかりであり、どうしても腑に落ちない。
English: The old men spoke of all three younger successors, not Michio alone. Yet he was invariably the one dragged out for these meetings, a discrepancy he could not understand.

Japanese: 今日もまたどこぞの名士さまに引き合わされるのかと思うとうんざりする。
English: The prospect of being introduced to yet another local dignitary today filled him with dread.

Japanese: 早々と諦めてしまった老人たちをよそに、故障してしまった麻雀卓を隙間からのぞいたり、ドライバーで中をつついたりしてどうにか治らないかと試行錯誤していると、はたしてその人物がやって来た。
English: While the old men promptly abandoned the table, Michio peered into gaps in the broken table and prodded its innards with a screwdriver, trying one thing after another in hopes of repairing it. As he worked, the anticipated visitor arrived.

Japanese: 幾人ものボディガードを引き連れて屋敷の玄関をくぐったのは、誰あろう、YSの第三代龍頭謝亮であった。高級なスーツを身につけ、屈強な男達に囲まれた姿はどこからどう見ても若きマフィアの頭目であり、道夫としてもうかつに声をかけにくい雰囲気があった。
English: The man who crossed the threshold with a procession of bodyguards was none other than Tse Leung, third Longtou of YS. In his expensive suit, surrounded by powerfully built men, he looked every inch the young head of a mafia organization. Even Michio found him difficult to approach casually.

Japanese: 亮の方も、道夫を横目でちらりと見ただけで何も言わない。
English: Leung merely glanced at Michio from the corner of his eye and said nothing.

Japanese: 「やあ、よく来てくれたね」
English: “Ah, thank you for coming.”

Japanese: 彼らを部屋に招き入れると、ミスター・チェンは目を細めた。
English: Mr. Chen narrowed his eyes as he invited the party into the room.

Japanese: 「若き龍頭どのと、そちらに居るのは馬君のところの倅さんだね。最近随分活躍しているそうじゃないか。若い人が出て来ると頼もしいねえ」
English: “Our young Longtou—and the fellow beside you must be Mr. Ma’s son. I hear he has been doing remarkable work lately. It is most reassuring to see young people stepping forward.”

Japanese: 丸いテーブルを挟んで、三人の老人と謝亮が向かい合って座っている。それを取り囲むように馬世傑と双方のボディガードが立っていた。いつもの客よりお互いが連れている人間が多く、緊張感がある。
English: The three elders sat facing Tse Leung across the round table. Ma Sai-kit and the bodyguards from both sides stood around them. Each party had brought more people than the elders’ usual visitors, lending the room an air of tension.

Japanese: 道夫はすこし離れたところに椅子を置いて状況を見守りながら、その不思議な緊張感に首を捻っていた。
English: Michio placed his chair at a slight distance and watched. The strange tension left him puzzled.

Japanese: 最近は饅頭屋の活動に力を入れていて、裏社会の動きをあまり知らない。フェルナンデス一家の殺害や、その犯人の遺体が路上に晒されたことなどは聞いているが、詳細な事情は聞いていない。八龍会の動きに関しては、老人たちは極端な秘密主義なので親切に道夫に説明することはなかった。どこで何をしているのかわからない。
English: He had recently devoted himself to the Great Hole Bun business and knew little of current movements in the underworld. He had heard about the Fernandes Family murders and the display of the culprits’ bodies in the street, but not the circumstances in any detail. As for the Eight Dragons Society, the elders were fanatically secretive and never took the trouble to explain its activities to Michio. He had no idea where they went or what they did.

Japanese: 「一体何のつもりで私たちを呼んだ？　何か釈明でもしてもらえるのかな」
English: “Why did you summon us? Do you intend to offer some explanation?”

Japanese: 亮の態度は最初からトゲトゲしかった。
English: Leung’s manner was hostile from the first word.

Japanese: 「ほっほっほ、何を釈明しろと」
English: “Ho ho ho. Explain what?”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは真っ白い口ひげを撫でながらそう笑う。
English: Mr. Chen laughed as he stroked his snow-white mustache.

Japanese: 道夫は知らなかったが、このとき八龍会はY地区中の有力者達にYSを非難する通達文を送りつけていた。
English: Michio did not know it, but by then the Eight Dragons Society had circulated a notice denouncing YS among influential figures throughout Y District.

Japanese: その内容は、フェルナンデス一家の殺害事件についてである。
English: The notice concerned the Fernandes Family murders.

Japanese: もとより謝亮の陰謀説があるこの事件だが、その噂は犯人達が死亡した後も消えることがなかった。余りにも早く殺人犯が見つかったことから、謝亮のでっちあげた真犯人を隠す替え玉、あるいはYSに雇われて彼らが犯行を行ったという説も生まれた。
English: The theory that Tse Leung had conspired to arrange the killings had existed from the beginning, and the death of the perpetrators did not put the rumor to rest. Their discovery had come so quickly that new theories arose: that the men were scapegoats planted by Leung to conceal the true culprits, or that YS had hired them to commit the murders.

Japanese: 八龍会の声明は、それらの陰謀説を前提とした形での非難であった。
English: The Eight Dragons Society framed its denunciation around those conspiracy theories.

Japanese: 犯人達はいずれもタイプBであり、しかも発症して精神が不安定な状態にある。YSはこれらにつけ込んで、彼らを利用した。タイプBを守る立場の八龍会としては到底これを容認することが出来ない。
English: The notice alleged that all the perpetrators were symptomatic Type Bs whose minds were unstable, and that YS had preyed upon their condition and used them. It presented the Eight Dragons Society as unable to tolerate such conduct in its role as protector of Type Bs.

Japanese: この街はタイプBを含めたミュータントとノーマルが協力して支え合っている街であり、このような非人道的な行いをする龍頭謝亮は到底許されるものではない。
English: Mutants, including Type Bs, and Normals sustained this city through mutual cooperation. A Longtou such as Tse Leung, who committed an act so inhumane, could never be forgiven.

Japanese: というのが八龍会の言い分である。
English: Such was the Eight Dragons Society’s position.

Japanese: 「面白いことを言う。釈明するならばアナタの方でしょう？」
English: “What an interesting thing to say. Surely you are the one who owes an explanation?”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは笑顔を絶やさずに言う。
English: Mr. Chen’s smile never wavered.

Japanese: 「馬鹿馬鹿しい」
English: “Absurd.”

Japanese: 「考えてみたらどうですか？　YSから離脱した途端に襲撃者が現れ、そしてすぐにそれが発症したタイプBだと判明する。これはあまりに出来すぎています」
English: “Consider the sequence. Attackers appeared the moment the Fernandes Family withdrew from YS, and almost immediately they were identified as symptomatic Type Bs. It is all much too convenient.”

Japanese: ミスター・スミスは不機嫌そうに言う。
English: Mr. Smith spoke with evident displeasure.

Japanese: 「ただの作り話だね。そういう話でいいなら、私はもっと面白い話を知ってるよ」
English: “That is merely a story. If stories are all we need, I know a more interesting one.”

Japanese: 亮はうっすらと意地の悪い笑みを浮かべた。
English: A faint, malicious smile appeared upon Leung’s lips.

Japanese: 「犯人達が死んだ後我々も少し調査をしたのだけれど、面白いことがわかったんだ」
English: “We continued investigating for a little while after the culprits died, and we learned something interesting.”

Japanese: 「面白いこと？」
English: “Something interesting?”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンが問い返す。
English: Mr. Chen repeated the phrase as a question.

Japanese: 「そう、彼らは確かにフェルナンデスの屋敷から金を盗んだが、それだけじゃ計算が合わない。事件のあとに。それじゃ支払えないくらい豪遊しているんだ。計画前に、武器を買うのさえ借金しなければならないようなすかんぴんどもが、どこにお金を隠していたんだろうねえ」
English: “Yes. They certainly stole money from the Fernandes mansion, but the figures do not add up. After the incident, they went on a spree far beyond what that money could have funded. These penniless men had to borrow even to buy weapons before the attack. Where could they possibly have been hiding so much money?”

Japanese: 「何が言いたい」
English: “What are you suggesting?”

Japanese: ミスター・アーノルドは額にしわをよせて訊ねた。
English: Mr. Arnold asked with a furrowed brow.

Japanese: 「誰かが彼らにフェルナンデス襲撃を依頼して、その報酬を受け取った。それが誰かっていうのはまだわからないが、彼らの部屋からは白い薬が大量に見つかった。このY地区で麻薬を扱っている組織はひとつしかない。そして、その組織はつい最近とんでもない新薬を仕入れて町中の会員にばらまいているそうだ」
English: “Someone hired them to attack Fernandes and paid them for it. We do not yet know who. But a large quantity of a white drug was found in their rooms. Only one organization handles narcotics in Y District, and I hear that very organization recently obtained an extraordinary new drug and distributed it among its members throughout the city.”

Japanese: 亮は風邪でもひいているのか、鼻を啜る仕草をして、
English: Perhaps Leung had caught a cold; he sniffed, then continued.

Japanese: 「タイプBを利用するってさっきあんたは言ったけれども、それにかけちゃもっと歴史の古い組織がこの街には存在すると思うんだがね？」
English: “You spoke a moment ago about exploiting Type Bs. I seem to recall that this city contains an organization with a much longer history of doing precisely that.”

Japanese: 「これは驚いた！　我々を疑っているんだネ？」
English: “What a surprise! You suspect us?”

Japanese: 「作り話でいいなら、そういう話もあるってことさ。こちらの方が現実味があると思わないかい？」
English: “If we are trading invented stories, that is another one we could tell. Does it not strike you as the more plausible version?”

Japanese: 「そんなの、ただの憶測じゃないか。この街のタイプBは多かれ少なかれ我々と関わりを持っているものがほとんどだ。我々はどんなタイプBも拒まないからネ」
English: “That is nothing but speculation. Nearly every Type B in the city has some connection to us, in one way or another. We reject no Type B.”

Japanese: ミスター・チェンは呆れて顔をしかめる。
English: Mr. Chen frowned in exasperation.

Japanese: 「何だっていいさ。ただ、裏があるなら徹底的にやるつもりだ。フェルナンデスの連中もこの世界で生きるからにはあんな死に方も覚悟していただろうが、離脱したとはいえYSの功労者だからね。主謀者は実行犯どものように路上でウジ虫の餌になるだろう」
English: “Call it whatever you please. If there is something behind this, I intend to follow it all the way to the end. The Fernandes people lived in our world and must have known they could die that way, but despite their withdrawal, they were veterans who had served YS well. Whoever planned this will end as food for maggots in the street, just like the men who carried it out.”

Japanese: 「威勢のいいことだな」
