Remembering his behavior at the restaurant only strengthened that impression. Surely he showed his feelings that openly only when he was with her. Ever since childhood, Ryo had behaved differently toward her than he did in public. The man she saw at the restaurant had been no different from the boy who showed that side of himself to her alone.

Japanese: ギャングになったことを気にして、ばかみたい。
English: Worrying because he had become a gangster—how ridiculous.

Japanese: ベッドのなかで彼女はいつもそう呟く。
English: She always murmured the words to herself in bed.

Japanese: 人でなしで残酷なギャングのボスと、素性の知れない化け物なんて、お似合いじゃないか。
English: A heartless, brutal gang boss and a monster of unknown origin. They were perfect for one another.

Japanese: きっといつか収まるべきところに収まるのだろうと考える。もし収まるところが自分の想像と違っていても、それはそれで仕方ない。その時は悲しめば良いだけだ。将来悲しむのを恐れて何も期待しないというのは、あまりにも愚かしい。
English: Surely, one day, things would settle where they belonged. If that place differed from the one she imagined, so be it. She could grieve when the time came. Refusing to hope for anything because she feared some future sorrow would be far too foolish.

Japanese: そうやって自分の考えを確認しながら、眠りにつくのだ。
English: Reaffirming her thoughts in this way, she fell asleep.

Japanese: その日、松子は日が傾きかける頃に出勤した。その日のシフトは夜勤だった。彼女の施設では夜勤者は十七時から翌朝九時までが勤務時間となっており、途中三時間の仮眠休憩が与えられており、各階二人ずつの職員が交互に休む。
English: That day, Matsuko arrived for work as the sun began to sink. She was assigned to the night shift. At her facility, the night shift ran from five in the afternoon until nine the next morning, with a three-hour nap break. Two members of staff were assigned to each floor and took their breaks in turn.

Japanese: タイプBの子供は突発的な行動を起こすことが多いので、その階に出勤している職員全員が眠ってしまって起きている者が誰もいなくなるような時間は作ってはいけないことになっている。
English: Type B children were prone to sudden and unpredictable behavior. The rules therefore forbade any period when every member of staff on a floor was asleep and no one remained awake.

Japanese: 松子は始業三十分前の十六時半には出勤しており、その日も普段と変わらぬ時間に、一階にある職員室の自席についていた。
English: Matsuko arrived at four thirty, half an hour before the beginning of her shift, and took her usual seat in the staff room on the first floor.

Japanese: 「今日は一階だっけ？」
English: “You’re on the first floor today, right?”

Japanese: 机の上の整理をしているとハシモトが話しかけてくる。
English: As Matsuko tidied her desk, Hashimoto spoke to her.

Japanese: 「そうです。タグチさんと一緒です」
English: “Yes. I’m working with Taguchi.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ今日はこき使われちゃうねー」
English: “Then you’ll get worked to the bone today.”

Japanese: 「ハシモトさんは日勤でしたか？」
English: “Were you on the day shift, Ms. Hashimoto?”

Japanese: 「ううん、早番。だから、もう帰らせて貰うわ。今日はねー、デートなの」
English: “No, the early shift. So I get to go home now. I have a date today.”

Japanese: 「ああ、この間言っていた人と」
English: “Oh, with the man you mentioned before.”

Japanese: 「そう！　はっきりしない男なんだけどねー。今日こそビシッと言わせてやるわ。絶対あたしのこと好きなんだから」
English: “That’s right! He’s terribly indecisive, but today I’m going to get a straight answer out of him. I know he likes me.”

Japanese: 「アハハ、楽しそうですね」
English: “Ahaha. You sound excited.”

Japanese: 「そうよ。あなたも仕事ばっかりしてないで遊ばなきゃ」
English: “I am. You can’t spend all your time working. You need to enjoy yourself too.”

Japanese: 「いやあ、私はべつに……」
English: “Oh, I don’t really...”

Japanese: 「やっぱり、見土さんとつき合ってるのね？」
English: “So you are dating Mr. Mido after all?”

Japanese: 松子は愛想笑いをしながら話をはぐらかすと、今日は自分の予定で夢中になっているハシモトはいつもほどしつこくなく話題を切り上げ、別の職員を捕まえて同じようなことを話し始めた。
English: Matsuko laughed politely and evaded the subject. Preoccupied with her own plans today, Hashimoto gave up more quickly than usual, caught another colleague, and began telling her much the same things.

Japanese: 一人になった松子は、肩をすくめて笑ってから、小さく溜息をつく。
English: Left alone, Matsuko shrugged with a smile, then gave a quiet sigh.

Japanese: 時間になると申し送りがはじまる。
English: When the hour arrived, the shift handoff began.

Japanese: 松子は児童たちの居住棟の一階に行き、そこの職員室で日勤者からの報告を受けた。
English: Matsuko went to the staff room on the first floor of the children’s residence and received the day shift’s report.

Japanese: 施設内では少し前から風邪が流行っていたが、やっと収束に向かいつつあり、今日は熱発者もなく五名ほどが少し咳込むだけだと言う。十歳の児童に朝から金眼現象が出ており、朝に薬を飲ませたが落ち着かず、イライラしっぱなしなので観察が必要とのことだった。その他細々とした生活のなかでの変化や、一日に起きたことを聞き、重要なことはメモに取る。
English: A cold had been spreading through the facility for some time but was finally subsiding. No one had developed a fever today, and only five children still coughed a little. One ten-year-old had exhibited the golden-eye phenomenon since morning. Medication had failed to calm the child, who remained irritable and would require observation. Matsuko listened to the other minor changes and events of daily life and made notes of the important points.

Japanese: 夜勤者の仕事のはじまりはいつもドタバタとしている。
English: The beginning of a night shift was always frantic.

Japanese: 門限になっても帰って来ない児童を探したり、自分勝手に遊んだり喧嘩をしたりする児童たちに席に座って食事を食べさせ、いやがる児童に歯磨きをさせたり、入浴をさせたり、薬の時間にはこっそり捨ててしまう児童を見張ったり、そして障碍のある児童の世話をしたり。
English: They searched for children who failed to return by curfew; made children who wanted only to play as they pleased or fight with one another sit and eat their meals; made reluctant children brush their teeth and bathe; watched those who secretly threw away their medicine when the hour came; and cared for children with disabilities.

Japanese: 夜勤者が出勤してから遅番が帰るまでの時間帯は職員の数が最も多くなるが、いくら手があっても足りない。
English: The interval between the night shift’s arrival and the late shift’s departure put more staff on duty than at any other time, yet there were never enough hands.

Japanese: 児童をうまく叱れるベテランの職員がいるとそうでもないのだ。しかし今夜のように若く優しい職員ばかりだとなかなか大人しく従ってはくれない。松子は声をからして叱るが、思春期を迎えた男の子などはかえって面白がるくらいのものだ。甘く見られているのである。
English: Things were easier when an experienced worker knew how to discipline the children. But on a night like this, when the staff were all young and gentle, the children did not readily obey. Matsuko scolded until her voice went hoarse, but adolescent boys found even that amusing. They did not take her seriously.

Japanese: その点、死んだリョウカは子供の扱いがうまかった。子供たちと打ち解けて心を開かせながらも、叱るときは恐ろしく、子供たちはみな彼女を尊敬し、恐れていた。そのような扱いをされるのは所長など一部のベテランと彼女くらいだった。
English: The late Ryuka had excelled at handling children. She won their trust and got them to open their hearts, yet was terrifying when she scolded them. Every child respected and feared her. Only the director and a few veteran employees commanded the same response.

Japanese: そしてリョウカは若い分、ベテランたちよりも子供たちと距離が近く、姉のような雰囲気があった。距離があまりにも近すぎて職員として行き過ぎてしまうこともあり、所長から叱られることもあったが、そう言った面も含めて松子は彼女を見習っていた。死んだ後、その思いは一層強くなった。
English: Being young, Ryuka had also been closer to the children than the veterans were, with something of an elder sister about her. At times she became too close and exceeded the proper bounds of a member of staff, earning a reprimand from the director. Matsuko had admired even that part of her example. Since Ryuka’s death, the feeling had only grown stronger.

Japanese: リョウカさんが生きていたら、どうしたろう？　そんな風に考えて、一人首をひねったりもする。
English: What would Ms. Ryuka have done if she were alive? Matsuko sometimes tilted her head and considered the question alone.

Japanese: 消灯時間を過ぎるとやっと一段落がつく。夜勤者たちは大体この時間に食事をとるのだが、それでもしばしば眠れない児童が訪ねて来て食事を中断させられることも少なくない。この日も自宅で作って来た弁当をもそもそと食べていると、トントンとドアを叩くものがあった。
English: Once lights-out had passed, things finally settled down. The night staff generally ate at this hour, though children unable to sleep often came to visit and interrupted their meal. This night, as Matsuko picked quietly at the boxed meal she had prepared at home, someone tapped upon the door.

Japanese: 「あ、私が出ます」
English: “I’ll answer it.”

Japanese: 同僚のタナベにそう言ってドアを開けると、三人の女子児童が立っている。
English: She said this to her colleague Tanabe, then opened the door to find three girls standing outside.

Japanese: 「どうしたの？」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「汐さん、テレビが見たいの」
English: “Ms. Shio, we want to watch television.”

Japanese: 「テレビ？」
English: “Television?”

Japanese: 学校で話題になっている深夜番組があるのだと言う。
English: There was apparently a late-night program everyone at school was discussing.

Japanese: 松子がどうしてもダメだと言うと、児童たちは「汐さんのケチ」と捨て台詞を残して去って言った。
English: When Matsuko insisted that they absolutely could not watch it, the children left her with the parting shot, “You’re so stingy, Ms. Shio.”

Japanese: 「もっとピシっと言いなさいよ。そんなんだから舐められるのよ」
English: “You need to be firmer. They walk all over you because you talk like that.”

Japanese: 席に戻ってくるとタナベはそう言って苦い顔をした。
English: When Matsuko returned to her seat, Tanabe made this remark with a sour expression.

Japanese: 「そうなんですけど、でも、テレビくらい好きに見せてあげたいなって気持ちもあって、なかなか言えないんですよね」
English: “I know. But part of me wants to let them watch as much television as they like, so I find it difficult to say.”

Japanese: 松子は困り顔で溜息をつく。
English: Matsuko sighed, looking troubled.

Japanese: 「そんなこと気にしないでいいのよ。どこの家庭だって、親はそう言うわ。ルールはルールなんだから、それを崩したらだめ。どうしても見たいなら隠れてコソコソ見たらいいのよ。そういうものよ。あなただって子供の頃、そうやってこっそり何かすることはあったでしょ？」
English: “Don’t worry about that. Parents say the same thing in every household. Rules are rules, and you can’t start bending them. If they want to watch so badly, they can sneak around behind your back. That’s how it works. You must have done something in secret when you were a child too, mustn’t you?”

Japanese: タナベの夕食は出勤途中にコンビニエンスストアで購入したスパゲッティナポリタンだった。電子レンジで温めたそれは、部屋中にケチャップの甘い香りを漂わせている。
English: Tanabe’s dinner was a serving of spaghetti Napolitan purchased at a convenience store on her way to work. Heated in the microwave, it filled the room with the sweet aroma of ketchup.

Japanese: 「ええ、まあ」
English: “Yes, I suppose.”

Japanese: 松子は深夜番組を見たり、なにか不良行為をしたということはなかったけれども、食べるのが面倒でなんでもミキサーにかけて飲んでいたことを思い出しながらそう頷いた。
English: Matsuko had never stayed up to watch late-night television or engaged in any delinquent behavior, but she nodded as she remembered how, finding food troublesome, she used to put everything through a blender and drink it.

Japanese: 大人になって振り返ると、自分はけして威張れるようなものではない、おかしな子供だったのである。
English: Looking back as an adult, she had been a peculiar child—hardly one she could boast about.

Japanese: 「なんだか、自分が出来ていなかったことで子供を怒るのは疲れますね。そうしなきゃいけないとはわかっているんですけど」
English: “It is tiring to scold children for things I failed to do myself. I understand that I have to, though.”

Japanese: そう言って肩をすくめた。
English: She spoke with a shrug.

Japanese: 「そんなの気にしないでいいのよ。私なんか、うちのチビの前ではなんでも出来る完全無欠の人間みたいに振る舞ってるんだから。そうじゃないとやっていけないわ」
English: “You don’t need to worry about that. In front of my little ones, I behave as though I’m some flawless human being who can do anything. It’s the only way to manage.”

Japanese: 今年三十歳になるタナベの家には五歳と二歳の子供がいる。彼女が仕事に出ている間は夫が面倒を見ていた。夫は複数の言語を操るベトナム人で、留学生としてやって来て将来を嘱望されたエリートだったらしい。それがどういうわけかY地区に流れ着き、今は近所の飲食店のメニューを他の言語に変換したりといった翻訳業のような仕事をしている。ただしあまり熱心でなく、収入が心許ない。
English: Tanabe, who would turn thirty that year, had two children, aged five and two. Her husband cared for them while she worked. He was Vietnamese and spoke several languages. Apparently, he had come to Japan as an international student and been considered an elite with a promising future. Somehow he had drifted into Y District and now did something like translation work, rendering the menus of nearby restaurants into other languages. He was not particularly diligent, however, and his income was unreliable.

Japanese: 彼女と夜勤に入るとその愚痴を延々と聞かされるのがいつものことであった。
English: Whenever Matsuko shared a night shift with Tanabe, she could expect to hear those complaints without end.

Japanese: しかし、夫の怠惰を批判する彼女も腰が重いタイプで、夜勤になるとパートナーに仕事を押しつけてばかりいるのであまり評判はよくない。
English: Yet Tanabe, for all her criticism of her husband’s laziness, was slow to stir herself. On night shifts she pushed most of the work upon her partner and was not very well regarded.

Japanese: ただ一旦動けばテキパキと片付ける方で、子供たちへの愛情も強く、松子は特別苦手というわけではなかった。
English: Once she did begin, however, she worked quickly and efficiently. She also loved the children deeply, and Matsuko did not especially dislike her.

Japanese: 児童たちが寝入ってしまうと定時の見回りをするくらいで、あとは重要な仕事はない。
English: After the children had fallen asleep, the only remaining important duty was the scheduled patrol.

Japanese: 人によっては日勤時に残った仕事を片付けたり、資格の勉強をしたり、携帯電話でゲームをやったり、事務所の掃除をはじめたり、時間の使い方はひとそれぞれだが、女性ばかりのこの職場はおしゃべりに費やされることが多かった。
English: Some people used the time to finish work left over from a day shift, study for qualifications, play games on their phones, or begin cleaning the office. Everyone spent it differently, but in this workplace of almost entirely women, it was often given over to conversation.

Japanese: タナベもそのタイプだが、今日は夫への悪口ではなく、最近職員の間でよく話題になるあるニュースについての話だった。
English: Tanabe belonged to that sort. Today, however, she spoke not about her husband but about a recent item of news much discussed among the staff.

Japanese: 「結局建物を取り壊して、更地にしちゃうんだって」
English: “In the end, they’re going to demolish the building and clear the entire site.”

Japanese: 彼女が言っているのは、つい一週間ほど前に襲撃された、巻河原病院のことである。
English: She meant National Makigawara Hospital, which had been attacked about a week earlier.

Japanese: 松子は今度一緒に作ろうと約束した折り紙を、予習のために本を見て折りながらその相手をしている。
English: Matsuko listened while consulting a book and practicing the origami she had promised to make with the children next time.

Japanese: 「それで、他の場所に同じような病院つくるらしいわよ。でも、どこに建てるのかしらね。今時どこだって、タイプBの専門病院なんかいやがるでしょう」
English: “They’ll apparently build another hospital like it somewhere else. But where? These days, no one wants a hospital specializing in Type B patients nearby.”

Japanese: 松子は意見を述べずに困ったような顔をして黙っている。
English: Matsuko offered no opinion, merely falling silent with a troubled expression.

Japanese: 「あの夜に診て下さるサングラスの先生も、あの病院に勤めていらっしゃったんでしょ？　ご無事だったのかしら」
English: “The doctor in sunglasses who used to see us at night worked at that hospital too, didn’t he? I wonder if he’s safe.”

Japanese: タナベはしかめっ面で言い、
English: Tanabe frowned as she spoke.

Japanese: 「でも、本当にびっくりする事件が起きたものねえ。世の中おかしくなってきたと思わない？　昔みたいな大抗争が起きるなら、引っ越そうかしら……と言っても、他に行くところもないんだけど」
English: “But what an astonishing thing to happen. Don’t you think the world is going mad? If another great gang war starts like the ones in the old days, perhaps I should move away... Not that I have anywhere else to go.”

Japanese: そう溜息をつく。
English: She sighed.

Japanese: 病院を襲撃したのは八龍解放軍という、八龍会が作った新しい組織であることはもう公然の秘密として街の住民の間では知られていた。
English: The city’s residents already treated it as an open secret that the hospital had been attacked by the Hachiryu Liberation Army, a new organization created by the Hachiryukai.

Japanese: 「そう言えば、あの、よくうちに来てた饅頭屋さんがあの解放軍だかのリーダーになったんでしょ？　そんな乱暴な人には見えなかったのにねえ。というか、タイプBだって知らなかったわ」
English: “Come to think of it, that bun vendor who used to visit us all the time became the leader of the liberation army or whatever it is, didn’t he? He never looked so violent. I didn’t even know he was a Type B.”

Japanese: 彼女の言葉に、松子はぎくりとして折り紙を折る手が止まる。
English: At her words, Matsuko started, and the hands folding the paper went still.

Japanese: 女性の職場は噂の伝わりが早い。自分がその饅頭屋と知り合いであるということはハシモトなどは知っていることだし、自分がいない間に職員室で話題になっているのではないかと思っている。
English: Rumors traveled quickly in a workplace full of women. Hashimoto and others knew that Matsuko was acquainted with the bun vendor. She suspected they might have discussed it in the staff room while she was absent.

Japanese: 「そうなんですか。驚きですねえ」
English: “Is that so? How surprising.”

Japanese: いつそのことを訊かれるのか。訊かれたら誤魔化すのも気が重いなあと、内心おだやかではなかったが、タナベの態度を見る限り彼女はそのことを知らないようだった。
English: When would they ask her? The thought of evading the question weighed upon her, and inwardly she was far from calm. From Tanabe’s manner, however, it appeared that she did not know.

Japanese: 「まったく怖いわねえ。あの人たちって、入院してたタイプBの人たちを解放するっていって襲ったんでしょ？　タイプＢのアルバイトに何かしたとかで、レストランを壊したりもしたって聞いたわよ。だとしたら、うちもタイプBの子供を自由にしろって襲われたりしない？」
English: “It’s terrifying. Those people attacked the hospital to liberate the Type Bs held there, didn’t they? I also heard they wrecked a restaurant because of something it did to a Type B employee. In that case, might they attack us and demand that we set the Type B children free?”

Japanese: 「さあ、どうでしょうか……」
English: “I’m not sure...”

Japanese: 「そう考えると、もうちょっと門限を緩めてあげたりしないとダメかしら？」
English: “Should we loosen the curfew a little, then?”

Japanese: タナベは真顔で首をかしげる。
English: Tanabe tilted her head with a perfectly serious expression.

Japanese: 「それはあんまり関係ないような気がしますが」
English: “I don’t think that has much to do with it.”

Japanese: 「そうお？　でも、怖いわねえ」
English: “You don’t? Still, it’s frightening.”

Japanese: 夜が更け、そろそろ職員の一人が仮眠に入る時間が近づいていた。
English: The night deepened, and the time for one member of staff to begin her sleeping break was drawing near.

Japanese: どちらが先に眠りにつくか相談しはじめたところで、ピンポンとインターフォンが音を立てた。
English: Just as they began discussing who would sleep first, the intercom chimed.

Japanese: 施設の正面玄関に取り付けられたインターフォンは、普段は管理棟の事務室に繋がっているが夜はこちらの一階職員室でもとれるようになっている。
English: The intercom at the facility’s main entrance ordinarily connected to the administration office, but at night the staff room on the first floor could answer it as well.

Japanese: こんな夜中にはほとんど鳴ることはないが、たまに鳴った時には義父母に引き取られたはずの子供が虐待されて戻ってきたり、のっぴきならない用事であるため、音が鳴ると共に二人は緊張して顔を見合わせる。
English: It almost never rang so late. On the rare occasions it did, however, the reason might be that a child placed with foster parents had suffered abuse and returned, or some other emergency. The moment it sounded, the two women tensed and exchanged glances.

Japanese: すぐに松子がガタリと音を立てて椅子を立ち上がると、パネルの前に立った。
English: Matsuko immediately rose from her chair with a clatter and stood before the panel.

Japanese: モニターには、白黒のカメラ映像が映し出されており、心細げな表情をする黒いロングコートを着た白人女性がそこにいるのが確認された。
English: The monochrome camera image on the monitor showed a white woman in a long black coat, wearing a forlorn expression.

Japanese: 松子は通話ボタンを押す。
English: Matsuko pressed the talk button.

Japanese: 「はい、もしもし」
English: “Hello?”

Japanese: 声をかけると、イギリス訛りの英語で返事がきた。
English: When she addressed the visitor, the reply came in English with a British accent.

Japanese: 『あの、すみません……。なかに入れて欲しいんです』
English: “Excuse me... I would like you to let me inside.”

Japanese: その顔には彼女のこれまでの人生における苦悩を物語るように細かい皺がいくつも刻み込まれ、頬がこけ落ちている。見ようによってはまるで老婆のようにも見える。松子の目には一見四十歳くらいに見えたが、もしかしたらもう少し若いかもしれない。
English: Her face was etched with fine lines that seemed to speak of a lifetime’s hardships, and her cheeks were hollow. From some angles, she appeared almost elderly. To Matsuko she looked about forty at first glance, though she might have been somewhat younger.

Japanese: 『ここに、私の子供がいると聞きまして、どうしても会いたくて……』
English: “I was told that my child is here. I simply must see them...”

Japanese: 「すみません。この時間にお通しすることは出来ないんです。明日になってから改めていらしてはいただけませんか？」
English: “I’m sorry. We cannot admit you at this hour. Would you please come again tomorrow?”

Japanese: 松子は相手の表情をよく観察しながら英語で言う。
English: Matsuko spoke in English, carefully observing the woman’s expression.

Japanese: こんな夜中に、そのような用件で訪れるのはいかにも不審だ。薬物中毒のせいで存在しない自分の子を探し求めて施設を訪れた女が過去にいたと、先輩職員から聞いたことがあった。それは暗闇通りの娼婦で、いないと言っても聞き入れず、事務所で暴れて大変な目に遭ったそうだ。
English: The request was suspicious in the extreme at this time of night. A senior colleague had once told her about a woman who came to the facility searching for a nonexistent child while under the influence of drugs. She had been a prostitute from Darkness Street, and when told the child was not there, she refused to listen and caused a terrible disturbance in the office.

Japanese: 『非常識なのはわかっています。でも、どうしても、どうしても今夜でなければならないんです。どうか、特別に開けていただけませんか？　一目見て、少し会話をするだけでいいんです。そうしたら私は満足して帰りますから』
English: “I understand that this is unreasonable. But I must—it absolutely must be tonight. Please, could you make a special exception and open the door? One glimpse and a few words would be enough. Then I will be satisfied and leave.”

Japanese: 目は金色ではない。口調はしっかりしている。正気のように見えるが、しかし、話している内容がどうにも信用しきれない。
English: Her eyes were not golden. Her speech was coherent. She appeared sane, yet Matsuko could not quite believe what she was saying.

Japanese: 「子供たちはもう眠っています。こんな時間に起こして、会って頂くわけにはいかないんですよ」
English: “The children are already asleep. We cannot wake one of them at this hour and ask them to meet you.”

Japanese: 『じゃあ、職員のかただけでも会って、お話だけでも聞いて下さい』
English: “Then please, at least meet with me yourselves and hear what I have to say.”

Japanese: 「申し訳ありません。それは出来ないんです」
English: “I’m sorry. We cannot do that.”

Japanese: 『どうか、どうかお慈悲を……』
English: “Please. Please, have mercy...”

Japanese: そして女はすすり泣きをはじめる。
English: Then the woman began to sob.

Japanese: 松子は戸惑って顔を曇らせる。
English: Matsuko’s face clouded with uncertainty.

Japanese: 「なんだって？」
English: “What did she say?”

Japanese: 振り返ると、タナベが眉間にしわを浮かべてこちらを見ていた。
English: Matsuko looked back. Tanabe was watching her with a deep furrow between her brows.

Japanese: 夫は語学に堪能だが彼女自身は日本語以外は理解が出来ない。
English: Her husband was fluent in several languages, but Tanabe herself understood only Japanese.

Japanese: 「ここにお子さんがいるからどうしても会いたいと。こんな時間だからとお断りしたんですが、そうしたら、話だけでも聞いてくれないかとおっしゃって……」
English: “She says her child is here and she has to see them. I told her we couldn’t admit her at this hour, and then she asked whether we would at least hear her story...”

Japanese: 「えーっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: タナベは思い切り顔を顰めると、
English: Tanabe grimaced openly.

Japanese: 「非常識よ。ほっときなさい」
English: “That is completely unreasonable. Ignore her.”

Japanese: 「はあ」
「こんな時間にそんな対応は出来ないわ」
English: “We can’t deal with something like that at this hour.”

Japanese: 「でも、何か特別な事情があるかもしれませんし……」
English: “But she might have some extraordinary reason...”

Japanese: 「まあ、汐さんは話を聞こうっていうの？」
English: “You don’t mean to hear her out, do you, Ms. Shio?”

Japanese: 「いや、そうじゃありませんけれど、本当にここにお子さんがいて、今しかチャンスがなくて二度と会えないとなったら、お母さんも子供さんもどう思うのかなって……」
English: “No, that isn’t what I mean. But if her child truly is here, and this is her only chance to meet before they can never see each other again, I wonder how both the mother and the child would feel...”

Japanese: ただ困惑したまま態度をはっきりしない松子に対してタナベは首を左右に振り、
English: Matsuko remained irresolute, nothing but confusion upon her face. Tanabe shook her head.

Japanese: 「どんな事情があったって関係ないの。それに、本当に今しか会えないのなら会わない方が良いわ。そんな言い方をしているなら引き取るってわけでもないでしょうし、お互いつらいだけでしょう」
English: “Her reasons don’t matter. And if this truly is her only chance, then it would be better not to meet. She doesn’t sound as though she intends to take the child with her. They would only cause each other pain.”

Japanese: 「そうかもしれません」
English: “Perhaps you’re right.”

Japanese: 「大体、誰のお母さんだって言うの？」
English: “Who does she even claim is her child?”

Japanese: 「聞きましょうか？」
English: “Shall I ask?”

Japanese: 「いや、いいわ聞かないで。もう一回、帰るよう言って頂戴」
English: “No, don’t. Tell her again that she has to leave.”

Japanese: 「はい、わかりました」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: 松子は浮かない顔でまたパネルに向かう。
English: With a dispirited expression, Matsuko turned back to the panel.

Japanese: タナベの言っていることは理解出来るし、間違っているとは思わない。子供を引き取る準備があるなら、こんな時間にこんな風に訪れるはずもないからだ。そもそも、彼女自身引き取るなんてことは口にせず会って帰るだけだと言っている。
English: She understood Tanabe’s reasoning and did not believe it mistaken. If the woman was prepared to take the child home, she would not have come at such an hour or in such a manner. Indeed, the woman herself had said nothing about doing so, only that she would meet the child and leave.

Japanese: しかし、自分だったらどうだろう？　もし実の親が訪れて、一度だけ会って会話が出来るとなったら、やはり会いたいのではないだろうか？
English: But what would Matsuko do? If a biological parent came to her and offered a single meeting, a single conversation, would she not want it after all?

Japanese: 松子は割り切れない思いを感じながら通話ボタンを押した。
English: Unable to settle the feeling, Matsuko pressed the talk button.

Japanese: そして、どうしても今日会うことは不可能であるともう一度説明し、一度帰って出直すよう伝える。すると女は取り乱し、
English: She explained once more that a meeting today was impossible and asked the woman to leave and return another time. The woman became distraught.

Japanese: 『出直すことなんか出来ないんです！　それならば、ここで待てる限り待たせて頂きます。どうか、どうかお慈悲を……』
English: “I cannot return another time! Then I will wait here as long as I am able. Please, please, have mercy...”

Japanese: カメラに顔を近づけ、画面一杯にその涙で濡れた顔を映しながら泣き声で言った。
English: She brought her face close to the camera, filling the screen with her tear-soaked features as she pleaded through sobs.

Japanese: 松子は通話を切り、席に戻る。
English: Matsuko ended the call and returned to her seat.

Japanese: そして無言で折り紙をはじめるが、どうも集中出来ず、本を見ているのに間違えてしまう。
English: She resumed the origami in silence, but could not concentrate. Even with the book before her, she made mistakes.

Japanese: タナベが先に仮眠を取る。一人になった松子はあれこれと考えてしまう。何かすることはないかと探して、所長から勧められた資格を取るための参考書などを本棚から取り出して目を通すが、一向に頭に内容が入って来ない。
English: Tanabe took the first sleeping break. Alone, Matsuko could not stop thinking. She searched for something to do and took from the shelf a study guide for one of the qualifications the director had recommended. She could not absorb a word.

Japanese: そしてついインターフォンのパネルの前に立ち、カメラの映像を表示させてしまう。すると、むこうの塀に寄りかかるようにしてさっきの女が蹲っているのが見える。本当に待っているのだ。
English: At last she found herself standing before the intercom panel and displaying the camera image. The woman from earlier was crouched against the wall on the other side. She truly was waiting.

Japanese: 松子は胸が苦しくなって画面を消す。
English: Matsuko felt a pain in her chest and switched off the screen.

Japanese: これが母の愛というものなのだろうか？
English: Was this a mother’s love?

Japanese: 松子には親子の愛情というものがわからない。汐健慈朗に対して尊敬も愛着もあるが彼は本当の親ではないし、彼女自身もそのことをよく知っている。この感情が、普通の親子と同じものなのかどうか自信がない。
English: Matsuko did not understand the love between a parent and child. She respected Kenjiro Shio and felt affection for him, but he was not her real parent, and she knew it well. She had no confidence that her feelings were the same as those of an ordinary parent and child.

Japanese: Ｙ地区の子供たちは歪な家庭が多く、親子の感情関係というものは千差万別だった。それでも親と子の繋がりは特別なものがあると言う。亮が母親の面倒を見て、そして街が嫌いだと出て行って大学まで通っていたのにわざわざ帰って来て龍頭になったのも親子の繋がりだろう。松子にはうまく理解出来なかった。この仕事を行うようになってさらに多くの子供と親を見るようになり、なおさらよくわからなくなった。
English: Many children in Y District came from fractured families, and feelings and relationships between parents and children took countless forms. Even so, people said there was something special in the bond between parent and child. Ryo had cared for his mother; though he hated the city, left it, and even attended university elsewhere, he had deliberately returned to become Longtou. That too must have been the parent-child bond. Matsuko could not properly understand it. Working here had shown her more children and parents than ever, and left her understanding it less.

Japanese: ただその繋がりは、感情は、人間にとってとても重要で美しいものだと言う。その美しさを知らない自分は何かが欠けているに違いない。
English: All she knew was that people called the bond, and the feelings within it, profoundly important and beautiful. Something had to be missing from her if she did not know that beauty.

Japanese: そう感じるからこそ、他人の親子の繋がりを、少しでもとりもってやりたいという思いがある。
English: Precisely because she felt that way, she wanted to help bring other parents and children together whenever she could.

Japanese: このまま帰らせてしまって、本当にいいのだろうか？
English: Was it truly right to send the woman home like this?

Japanese: 一時間ほど過ぎて、タナベが不機嫌な顔で仮眠室から出て来た。
English: About an hour passed before Tanabe emerged from the sleeping room with a disgruntled expression.

Japanese: 「さっきの人、どう？　帰った？」
English: “What about that woman from earlier? Did she leave?”

Japanese: 松子と目が合うとぶっきらぼうにそう訊ねる。
English: Meeting Matsuko’s eyes, she asked the question brusquely.

Japanese: 「いえ、まだ門の前に……」
English: “No. She’s still outside the gate...”

Japanese: 「そう」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: タナベは言って、目をゴシゴシと擦る。
English: Tanabe rubbed her eyes vigorously.

Japanese: 彼女も外で待つあの女のことが気になっていて、眠れなかったのかもしれないと松子は思った。
English: Perhaps she too had been unable to sleep because she was thinking about the woman waiting outside, Matsuko thought.

Japanese: 「あの、タナベさん。話だけでも聞かせてくれませんか。私が応接室で対応しますから、タナベさんはその間ここにいてください。今日私は仮眠はいらないので……」
English: “Um, Ms. Tanabe. Could we at least hear her story? I’ll speak with her in the reception room, and you can stay here in the meantime. I don’t need a sleeping break tonight...”

Japanese: 「そう言うと思ったわ」
English: “I knew you would say that.”

Japanese: タナベは肩をすくめると、
English: Tanabe shrugged.

Japanese: 「わかった。そうしましょう」
English: “All right. Let’s do that.”

Japanese: 「ありがとうございます！」
English: “Thank you!”

Japanese: 「ただし、私も一緒に行くわ。上の階の人に連絡だけしておけば、ここは少しくらいあけても大丈夫よ」
English: “But I’m coming with you. As long as we notify the people upstairs, we can leave this room empty for a little while.”

Japanese: タナベはそう言ってから、あくびをかみ殺した。
English: After saying this, Tanabe stifled a yawn.

Japanese: 松子が門を内側から開けると、女はすぐに気がついて立ち上がる。
English: When Matsuko opened the gate from inside, the woman noticed at once and stood.

Japanese: 「入ってください。お話だけ伺います」
English: “Please come in. We will hear what you have to say, nothing more.”

Japanese: 松子の言葉に女は小走りで駈け寄ってくると、
English: At Matsuko’s words, the woman trotted toward her.

Japanese: 「ありがとうございます。ありがとうございます」
English: “Thank you. Thank you so much.”

Japanese: 震える両手で松子の手を取って泣いた。
English: She took Matsuko’s hand between her trembling hands and wept.

Japanese: 管理棟の応接室に通し、お茶を出す。
English: They showed her into the reception room of the administration building and served tea.

Japanese: 「すみません。無理を言ってしまって。本当に今日しかないもので」
English: “I’m sorry for asking the impossible. It truly had to be today.”

Japanese: 女は恐縮して、日本人の風習にあわせるように頭を下げて礼をする。
English: Abashed, the woman bowed in thanks, following Japanese custom.

Japanese: もう泣いてはおらず、朗らかな笑みが顔に浮かんでいた。
English: She had stopped crying, and a cheerful smile now lit her face.

Japanese: 「子供とはもう何年も会っていないんです。でも、お陰でこうして会うことが出来ました。あなたが今日ここにいてくれたからです。別の日だったらあなたもいなかったし、私は子供に会うことが出来ませんでした」
English: “I haven’t seen my child for years. But thanks to you, I can finally do so. It is because you are here today. On any other day you would not have been here, and I could not have seen my child.”

Japanese: 女の口調は自然と明るく、早口になっていた。
English: The woman’s voice brightened, and her words came faster.

Japanese: 「いえ、そんな」
「子供の名前を聞いた？」
English: “Did you ask the child’s name?”

Japanese: 恐縮する松子の横で、二人の英語による会話が聞き取れないタナベが囁く。
English: Beside the abashed Matsuko, Tanabe whispered. She could not follow their conversation in English.

Japanese: 松子は頷き、
English: Matsuko nodded.

Japanese: 「あの、それでお子さんの名前を教えて頂けませんか？」
English: “Would you please tell us your child’s name?”

Japanese: 「ああ、そうですね！　まだその名前を言っていませんでしたね。私のその生き別れになった娘の名前を。いくらあなたといえども、言わなきゃわからないですものね」
English: “Oh, of course! I haven’t said the name yet, have I? The name of the daughter from whom I was separated. Even you could not know unless I told you.”

Japanese: 女は上機嫌だ。いくらなんでも上機嫌過ぎるようにも見える。ほとんどはしゃいでいると言ってもいい。
English: The woman was in high spirits—far too high, perhaps. One could almost call her giddy.

Japanese: こんなに嬉しいものなのだろうかと、松子は違和感を覚えた。
English: Could a person truly be this delighted? Matsuko felt a flicker of unease.

Japanese: 「ええ、名前を言っていただかないと、お連れ出来ませんし、会うことも出来ません」
English: “Yes. Unless you tell us her name, we cannot bring her here or let you meet her.”

Japanese: 「おほほ」
English: “Ohoho.”

Japanese: 女は唇の両端をつり上げて笑うと、まっすぐ松子の目を見つめながら言う。
English: The woman raised both corners of her mouth in a smile and stared directly into Matsuko’s eyes.

Japanese: 「もう誰かを連れて来る必要はないのです。だって、もう目的は果たされているんですから。わかりませんか？　マツコ・シオ」
English: “There is no need to bring anyone here. My purpose has already been fulfilled. Do you not understand, Matsuko Shio?”

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 言葉の内容もそうだが、急に名前を呼ばれたことにも驚いた。まだ名乗っていないのだ。
English: Matsuko was startled not only by the meaning of the words, but by the sudden use of her name. She had not introduced herself.

Japanese: 驚き何か訊ねようと言葉を探す松子の前で、女はさっと手をあげる。
English: As Matsuko searched for a question, the woman swiftly raised one hand.

Japanese: 常にタイプＢの覚醒状態である松子の反射神経は常人より鋭かったが、それでも気づいたときには、女の手のなかの黒光りする拳銃が顔面に突きつけられている。
English: Matsuko’s reflexes, perpetually in a Type B awakened state, were sharper than an ordinary person’s. Even so, by the time she realized what was happening, the gleaming black handgun in the woman’s hand was pressed to her face.

Japanese: 「ひっ」
English: “Eek.”

Japanese: タナベは小さく悲鳴を上げて凍り付き、松子は無言で目を細める。
English: Tanabe gave a tiny scream and froze. Matsuko narrowed her eyes without a word.

Japanese: 「そう、誰かを連れて来る必要はありません。だって、私どもの娘は今ここにいるのですもの」
English: “Yes, there is no need to bring anyone here. Our daughter is already present.”

Japanese: そう言ったかと思うと、女の顔が蠢きはじめる。
English: No sooner had the woman spoken than her face began to writhe.

Japanese: それはまるでクレイアニメーションのようにぐにゃぐにゃと形を変え、やがて全く別人の姿をそこに作り出す。
English: It warped and changed shape like a figure in clay animation, until an entirely different person had been molded in her place.

Japanese: 「あなたは……」
English: “You’re...”

Japanese: 「久しぶりだね。元気そうだ」
English: “It has been some time. You look well.”

Japanese: そう笑ったのは以前彼女の前でアレクセイと名乗った青年――黒髪の殺人鬼コシチェイであった。
English: The young man smiling at her was the black-haired killer Koschei, who had called himself Alexei when they met before.

Japanese: （やってしまった）
English: (I’ve made a terrible mistake.)

Japanese: 自分が引き入れた相手がとんでもないモンスターであったことに気がついた松子は下唇を噛む。
English: Realizing that she had invited a monstrous danger inside, Matsuko bit her lower lip.

Japanese: その隣ではタナベが目の前で起きたことが信じられず、まるで彫像のようにそこに固まって身動きひとつしない。
English: Beside her, Tanabe could not believe what had happened before her eyes. She stood as motionless as a statue.

Japanese: 「いやあ、ずっと会いたかったんだがね。とにかく忙しくてその暇がなかったんだ。……しかし、このあたりは警報器が多いねえ。おかげで能力が使えなくて、入れて貰うのにこんな面倒な手を使わなくちゃいけなかった。まあ警報器なんか無視してもいいんだが、そうなると用件を手早く済まさなくちゃいけなくなる。急かされるのは好きじゃないんだ。門を開けてくれたのは賢明な判断だよ。そうしなければ、その乱暴な手段を使わなくちゃいけなくなるところだった」
English: “I have wanted to see you for a long time, but I’ve been so terribly busy that I never had the chance. ...There are a remarkable number of alarms around here. They kept me from using my ability, so I had to resort to this tiresome performance to make you let me inside. I could simply have ignored the alarms, but then I would have had to finish my business quickly. I dislike being rushed. Opening the gate was a wise decision. Otherwise, I would have been forced to use that more violent method.”

Japanese: アレクセイは紅い唇の隙間から白い歯を見せながらそう言葉を吐き出した。
English: Alexei delivered the words through white teeth visible between his red lips.

Japanese: 彼がわざわざここに来て何やら意味深な言葉を投げかけている。このコシチェイという人物は自分にとってただならぬ存在であることを補強する重要な場面のはずだが、松子の頭をその時支配していたのは隣のタナベを、そしてこの施設の人たちをどうやって守るかということだった。
English: He had gone to the trouble of coming here and was making cryptic insinuations. This should have been an important moment, further confirming that Koschei was profoundly connected to Matsuko’s own history. Yet the thoughts occupying her mind were how to protect Tanabe beside her, and everyone else in the facility.

Japanese: 目の前にいるのが非常に危険な人物であることは自分の体験だけでなく、路地などからも聞いている。主に自分の好みの女性をさらって残虐に殺す快楽型の連続殺人犯ではあるが、必要とあれば路地の恋人や堂島刑事にそうしたように、排除することも厭わない。
English: Her own experience had taught her that the man before her was extremely dangerous, as had the accounts of Roji and others. They described a serial killer who took pleasure in abducting women he found attractive and murdering them brutally. When expedient, however, he was equally willing to eliminate obstacles, as he had done with Roji’s lover and Detective Dojima.

Japanese: 「ここに何をしに来たんですか？」
English: “Why have you come here?”

Japanese: 松子は相手の目をじっと見つめながらそう訊ねた。
English: Matsuko asked while staring into his eyes.

Japanese: 「きみに会いに来たのさ。……しかし、大きくなったものだ。それにとても美人だ。目がくりくりしているのは少しロジャーに似ているな」
English: “To see you. ...How you’ve grown. You are very beautiful too. Those large, round eyes look a little like Roger’s.”

Japanese: 「し、知り合いなの？」
English: “D-do you know him?”

Japanese: タナベは緊張で裏返った声で松子にそう訊ねる。
English: Tanabe asked Matsuko, her voice pitched high with tension.

Japanese: 先ほどからアレクセイは日本語で話しており、彼女にも理解することが出来ていた。
English: Alexei had spoken Japanese since the transformation, allowing her to understand him.

Japanese: 「……知り合いというか……」
English: “...I wouldn’t exactly say we know each other...”

Japanese: 松子は言葉を濁したが、
English: Matsuko hedged, but Alexei interrupted.

Japanese: 「はじめまして。おれはアレクセイ。そこの彼女とは知り合いでね。どう説明したら良いのかな……ああそうだ、リュウカって子を殺したのはおれなんだよ」
English: “A pleasure to meet you. I’m Alexei. The young lady and I are acquainted. How should I explain it...? Ah, yes. I’m the man who killed the girl named Ryuka.”

Japanese: 「ひええっ」
English: “Eee!”

Japanese: タナベは完全に動揺してしまっている。この状態では走って逃げろと指示したとしても腰が抜けて立てないかもしれない。
English: Tanabe was completely distraught. In this condition, even if Matsuko ordered her to run, her legs might fail beneath her.

Japanese: どうやって彼女に冷静さを取り戻そう。
English: How could she restore the woman’s composure?

Japanese: 松子は横目でちらりとこの先輩職員を眺めながら考えた。
English: Matsuko considered the problem as she stole a glance at her senior colleague.

Japanese: 絶対に家に帰さなくてはならない。そこには二人の子供と、愛する夫が待っているんだ。
English: She had to send Tanabe home alive. Her two children and beloved husband were waiting there.

Japanese: 「私に用があるのなら、二人きりで話をしませんか？　大事な用件なら、他の人がいない場所の方がいいでしょう」
English: “If you have business with me, why don’t we speak alone? If it is important, somewhere more private would be better.”

Japanese: 「必要ないよ。大丈夫。彼女が聞いてくれたってかまわない」
English: “There is no need. It’s all right. I don’t mind if she hears us.”

Japanese: 彼が手を振って否定するのを見て、松子は苦い顔をする。
English: Alexei dismissed the suggestion with a wave of his hand, and Matsuko’s expression soured.

Japanese: さっきもタナベの前でその必要もないのに自分が殺人犯だと名乗った。タナベに何を聞かれてもかまわない、という態度は、松子にとっては不吉なものでしかない。
English: He had already identified himself as a killer before Tanabe without any need to do so. His indifference to what she heard could only be an ominous sign.

Japanese: 「あのマンションできみのちからを見た時は驚いた。はじめはクラブの女の生き残りか何かかと思ったよ。でも少し調べたらすぐにわかった。……きみはいま汐健慈朗の娘として生活しているそうだね」
English: “I was surprised when I saw your power in that apartment. At first, I thought you might be one of the club’s surviving women. But a little investigation made the answer clear at once. ...I hear that you now live as the daughter of Kenjiro Shio.”

Japanese: アレクセイは銃をこちらに向けたまま、もう片方の手でカップをつかみお茶を一口飲む。
English: Keeping the gun trained upon Matsuko, Alexei used his other hand to take the cup and sip the tea.

Japanese: 「いいね。なかなかうまいグリーンティーだ……」
English: “Good. Quite a pleasant green tea...”

Japanese: 独り言のようにそう呟いてから、
English: After murmuring this as though to himself, he continued.

Japanese: 「それを知っていたときピンと来たよ。きみは知っているか？　彼は昔ローズクラブのゴミ処理をしていたんだ。きっと、ゴミからきみを拾って育て上げたに違いない。大体、彼には妻も恋人もいないし、預かるような親戚の子だっていないんだ。契約を結ぶときよく調べたから知っている。何も持たない人間だったのさ。だからへんな正義感にとらわれることもないだろうと信用して仕事を任せたのだが、まさかこんなことになるとはね」
English: “When I learned that, I knew at once. Did you know? He once handled the garbage disposal for Rose Club. He must have found you among the rubbish and raised you. After all, he had neither wife nor lover, nor any relative’s child he might have taken in. I know because we investigated him thoroughly before entering into the contract. He had no one. That was why we trusted him with the work: there was no risk of some strange sense of justice taking hold of him. To think it would end this way.”

Japanese: 「さっき、私のことを娘と言いましたが……」
English: “You called me your daughter just now...”

Japanese: 「そうだよ。きみはこのコシチェイのなかにいるとある女の娘なんだよ。さっきからそいつは非常に会いたがっているがね。……どうしようかとじいさんが思案中さ」
English: “Yes. You are the daughter of a certain woman inside Koschei. She has been desperate to see you ever since we arrived. ...The old man is still deciding what to do about that.”

Japanese: アレクセイは肩をすくめる。
English: Alexei shrugged.

Japanese: その言葉は松子が探し求めた真実を告げるものだったが、不思議と心には何も響かない。彼女はそんな自分に微かな戸惑いを覚えた。
English: His words claimed to reveal the truth Matsuko had sought, yet strangely, they stirred nothing within her. That absence troubled her faintly.

Japanese: かわりに隣のタナベが大きく驚き、松子の顔とアレクセイの顔を交互に見る。
English: Tanabe, by contrast, was visibly shocked. Her gaze moved back and forth between Matsuko and Alexei.

Japanese: 「きみはおれのことを覚えていないかい？　小さい頃、会っているはずなんだがなあ」
English: “Don’t you remember me? We should have met when you were very small.”

Japanese: 「覚えてないですね。あなたのことなんか」
English: “No. I don’t remember you at all.”

Japanese: 「そうかい。残念なことだなあ。あの時三歳だったきみを生きたままバラバラにして、ゴミ袋に詰めてやったのはおれなんだぜ？　アハハハ」
English: “I see. What a pity. When you were three years old, I cut you apart alive and packed you into a garbage bag. Ahahaha.”

Japanese: アレクセイは乾いた声で笑う。
English: Alexei laughed in a dry voice.

Japanese: 松子はただ黙って相手を見つめている。
English: Matsuko merely stared at him in silence.

Japanese: 「蘇らないようしっかり薬を使ったはずなんだがね。どうしてまだ生きていたのか。バラバラに切断してしまったのが良くなかったのかな？　薬の効きが良くない破片があったのかもしれない。あれは『仕事』だから楽しんではいけないって、ヘスの爺さんの言うことは正しかったんだろうね。でも、そうはいかないじゃないか？　小さなきみはとても可愛かったんだ。それに手をつけないなんて、そんな勿体ないことは出来ない。あまりにも愛がない」
English: “I was certain I used enough of the drug to keep you from reviving. Why were you still alive? Perhaps cutting you into pieces was a mistake. One of the fragments may not have received enough of the drug. Old Hess may have been right when he said I shouldn’t enjoy it, because it was ‘work.’ But how could I help myself? You were so adorable when you were small. I couldn’t possibly leave you untouched. What a waste that would have been. There would be no love in that.”

Japanese: 「どうしてここに来たんですか？　私に用があるなら、私の家に来ればよかったじゃないですか。こんな場所で、職場の人たちを巻き込んで……」
English: “Why have you come here? If you had business with me, you could have come to my home. Why involve the people at my workplace...?”

Japanese: 「今夜きみが自宅にいたならそうしたよ。場所はどこだって良かったんだ。時間が大事だったんだよ。さっきキャシーがきみに言ったのは嘘じゃない。今夜か、それか明後日くらいしか時間がとれなくてね。何しろいまおれは本当に多忙で、まったくいやになっちまう」
English: “If you had been home tonight, I would have. The place did not matter. The time did. What Cathy told you earlier was no lie. Tonight and perhaps the day after tomorrow were my only openings. I truly am terribly busy at present. It has become quite intolerable.”

Japanese: アレクセイは大げさに肩をすくめて溜息をつく。
English: Alexei shrugged theatrically and sighed.

Japanese: 「こういうときみはまたおれがどこかで女を殺してると思うんだろうね。世間ってのはまったくそういうもんさ。しかし、そうじゃない。社会を変えるとか、なんとか……まあ一種の社会奉仕みたいなもんだね。おれには全く理解出来ないが……。きみはどうだ？　権力だとか、支配だとか、くだらないと思わないか？　金なんか、うまいワインを飲めて、いい音楽を聴いて、楽しく一日を過ごせるだけあればいい。たまには恋もしてね。人生ってそれ以上は何も必要ないと思わないか？」
English: “I expect you assume that, when I say busy, I mean I have been killing women somewhere again. That is how society sees me. But no. Changing society, or some such thing... a form of public service, you might call it. I understand none of it. ...What about you? Do you not find power and dominion ridiculous? One needs only enough money to drink good wine, listen to good music, and spend each day pleasantly. To fall in love from time to time. Do you not agree that life requires nothing more?”

Japanese: 「あなたはわざわざ人生の話をしに来たんですか？」
English: “Did you come all this way to discuss life?”

Japanese: 「いや、そうじゃない。そうじゃないんが……最近はどうも感傷的になっていけないね。うふふ、何かと面倒なことが多いのさ」
English: “No, that isn’t it. It isn’t, but... I have been growing altogether too sentimental lately. Hehe. There are so many tiresome complications.”

Japanese: アレクセイは肩をゆすって笑う。
English: Alexei laughed, his shoulders shaking.

Japanese: その態度に、松子は何か投げやりで支離滅裂なものを感じた。もっとも、シリアルキラーというものは本来そのような性質があるのかもしれないが。
English: Matsuko sensed something disjointed and self-abandoning in his manner. Perhaps, she thought, serial killers were inherently like that.

Japanese: 喋っている間になんとか銃口がそれて隙を作ってくれないかと観察していたが、こんな話をしていながらもアレクセイの銃口はピタリと松子の顔面に向いたままだった。前に会った時に痛手を負わされたのを覚えていて、警戒はしているのだろう。
English: She watched in the hope that the muzzle might drift and expose an opening while he talked. Yet despite the loose conversation, Alexei kept it trained precisely upon Matsuko’s face. He must remember how badly she had hurt him at their last meeting and remain on his guard.

Japanese: 「そう、ひとつ聞きたいことがあるんだ。いいかな？」
English: “Yes, there is one thing I would like to ask. May I?”

Japanese: 「なんですか」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「路地邦昭って知ってるね？　ツノの生えた大男だよ」
English: “You know Kuniaki Roji, don’t you? The large man with horns.”

Japanese: この質問にはどう答えるのが正解なのか？
English: What was the correct answer to that question?

Japanese: 松子は迷ったが、あまり長く逡巡しているわけにはいかない。アレクセイは笑っていない目でこちらの表情を観察している。露骨に迷えばこちらの返答の内容にかかわらず相手に情報を渡すことになるだろう。
English: Matsuko hesitated, but could not deliberate for long. Alexei watched her expression with eyes that did not smile. If she displayed her uncertainty openly, the reaction itself would give him information, no matter how she answered.

Japanese: 「ろじさん……ですか？」
English: “Roji...?”

Japanese: 「そう」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: 「ツノの生えた人なら街で見かけたことがありますが……」
English: “I have seen a man with horns around the city...”

Japanese: 「ふむ」
English: “Hmm.”

Japanese: アレクセイは小さく首をかしげる。
English: Alexei tilted his head slightly.

Japanese: ある程度は情報を隠すことに成功したのかもしれない。そうだとしたら、路地がここに匿われていたことも知らないのだろう。ということは、思ったよりこちらの事情に詳しくないのかもしれないと、松子は推測した。
English: Perhaps she had succeeded in concealing some of the truth. If so, he might not know that Roji had been sheltered here. That would mean he knew less about their circumstances than she had feared, Matsuko inferred.

Japanese: 「先日久しぶりに会ったんだが、彼、死なないんだよ」
English: “I saw him for the first time in quite a while the other day, and the man does not die.”

Japanese: 「死なない？」
English: “He doesn’t die?”

Japanese: 「彼に即死になる致命傷を与えたはずなんだが、起き上った。彼はいつの間にか我々と同じ体質になっていたんだよ。前は違ったように見えたがね。それとも気づかないだけで前からそうだったのか……。だからきみが関与しているのかと思ったのだが」
English: “I inflicted what should have been an instantly fatal wound, but he rose again. At some point, he had acquired the same constitution as us. He appeared different before—or perhaps he was always that way and I failed to notice. ...I wondered whether you might be involved.”

Japanese: ついに路地と交戦をしたということを知り、松子は内心でドキリとした。
English: Learning at last that Roji had fought him made Matsuko’s heart jolt.

Japanese: 彼がここにいるということは、彼の復讐は果たされなかったのだろう。とすると、彼はどうなったのか？
English: If Alexei was here, Roji’s revenge could not have succeeded. Then what had become of him?

Japanese: 松子は驚きと不安で鼓動が早くなるのを押し隠しつつ、
English: Matsuko suppressed her racing heart and concealed her surprise and fear.

Japanese: 「そうなんですか。そのことと、私が何か関係あるんですか？」
English: “Is that so? What does it have to do with me?”

Japanese: 「きみは知らないのか？」
English: “You don’t know?”

Japanese: 「何をですか？」
English: “What do you mean?”

Japanese: アレクセイが言っているのは、血を分け与えれば相手を不死に出来る能力のことだと松子は察していたが、表情には出さずとぼけて見せた。
English: Matsuko understood that he meant her ability to make another person immortal by sharing her blood. She pretended ignorance without allowing it to show in her face.

Japanese: 「そうか。まあいい。あと……そうだな」
English: “I see. No matter. One more thing...”

Japanese: アレクセイが考えたところで、横のタナベがこちらを見ていることに松子は気がついた。
English: As Alexei considered, Matsuko noticed Tanabe looking at her from the side.

Japanese: 「汐さんあなたって……」
English: “Ms. Shio, what are you...?”

Japanese: いまここで聞かされたことは彼女にとっては驚きの連続だろう。これが施設内で広まれば松子の今までの生活は崩壊してしまうかもしれない。
English: Everything she had heard here must have been one shock after another. If it spread throughout the facility, the life Matsuko had lived until now might collapse.

Japanese: そんな予感を感じてはいたが、今はそれを心配している状況ではない。
English: She felt that presentiment, but this was no time to worry about it.

Japanese: 「後で話します」
English: “I’ll explain later.”

Japanese: 小さくそう返事をして、またアレクセイに視線を戻した。
English: She answered quietly and returned her gaze to Alexei.

Japanese: 彼は私たち二人をこの場で殺害するつもりだろう。そうでなければこんな話し方をするはずがない。
English: He means to kill us both here. Otherwise, he would never speak like this.

Japanese: 思えば、エリー・ホワイトの家でローズ・クラブの顛末を聞いた時点で想像するべきだった。コシチェイが三日月の女たちを殺害してから脱出したのは、この不死身の血を外に出したくなかったからだろう。だとすれば、自分を襲いに来ることをもっと具体的な問題として想定出来たはずだ。
English: In retrospect, Matsuko should have anticipated it when she heard the story of Rose Club at Ellie White’s home. Koschei must have killed the Crescent women before escaping because he did not want their immortal blood to reach the outside world. If so, she should have treated the possibility of his coming for her as a concrete danger.

Japanese: しかし、今更悔いても仕方がない。とにかく、彼が私に対して話すことがなくなり、最後の仕事に取りかかる前になんとかしなくては……。
English: Regret was useless now. She had to act before he ran out of things to tell her and began his final ‘work.’

Japanese: 松子は焦っていた。機会をうかがうよりも、自分のタイプBとしての運動能力に賭けて無理矢理こちらから行動を起こした方が良いのか？　それとも、ここは待つべきなのか。どちらとも決断出来ていない今の状態が一番悪いのはわかっているのだが。亮だったらどう判断しただろう？　子供の頃喧嘩に巻き込まれたときは、いつも亮が正しく判断をしてくれたのに。
English: Matsuko was growing desperate. Rather than wait for an opening, should she gamble upon her physical abilities as a Type B and force the issue herself? Or should she wait? She understood that the worst possible state was this one, in which she could decide upon neither. What would Ryo have done? When they were swept into fights as children, Ryo had always made the correct decision.

Japanese: とにかく人死にを出してはならない。タナベも、他の誰一人この殺人鬼に手をかけさせてはいけない。そして自分も生き延びるのだ。
English: Whatever happened, no one could die. She would not allow this murderer to lay a hand on Tanabe or anyone else. And Matsuko herself would survive.

Japanese: 少し前だったら自分の命を希薄に感じていたかもしれない。でも今は違う。
English: Not long ago, her own life might have felt insubstantial to her. It was different now.

Japanese: ――私にはまだやることがある。やっと最近自分の命の価値がわかったんだ。
English: —There are still things I must do. Only recently have I finally understood the value of my life.

Japanese: 目の前の男は自分を殺す方法を知っているだろうけれど、むざむざとそれを成功させてはいけない。全員が無事でこの夜を乗り越えるんだ。
English: The man before her presumably knew how to kill her, but she would not meekly let him succeed. Every one of them would come through this night unharmed.

Japanese: 覚悟を決める松子の目に強い意志の光があらわれている。たがアレクセイはそれに気がつかなかった。
English: A strong light of resolve entered Matsuko’s eyes. Alexei did not notice it.

Japanese: 「よし、じゃあ次の質問だ。きみは……」
English: “Very well. My next question. Do you—”

Japanese: 彼がそう言いかけた時だ。
English: He broke off.

Japanese: 「うっ」
English: “Urgh.”

Japanese: アレクセイは急に目を大きく見開いて、そしてガクリと俯く。何か発作でも起きたかのように身体が揺れ、銃口がぶれた。
English: Alexei’s eyes suddenly opened wide, then his head dropped. His body shuddered as though in the grip of some seizure, and the muzzle wavered.

Japanese: 松子はその隙を見逃さなかった。立ち上がりながらさっと手を伸ばし、相手の銃を掴む。
English: Matsuko did not miss the opening. She rose as she darted out a hand and seized his gun.

Japanese: 「お、お前っ……」
苦悶で皺だらけにした表情でアレクセイは松子を睨み付けた。その時引き金を引いたようだが、銃口は既に松子の身体からは大きく外れており、壁に掛かった創立者の顔写真を撃ち抜く。
English: Alexei glared at her through features contorted with agony. He appeared to pull the trigger, but the muzzle had already swung far from Matsuko’s body. The bullet pierced a framed photograph of the facility’s founder on the wall.

Japanese: 松子は掴んだ拳銃をアレクセイの手の甲の方にねじりあげる。すると引き金にかかったままのアレクセイの一差し指が、トリガーガードに締め上げられる形になって、パキッと割り箸を折ったような乾いた音がする。
English: Matsuko twisted the gun she held upward toward the back of Alexei’s hand. His forefinger, still hooked around the trigger, was crushed against the trigger guard. A dry crack sounded, like a pair of chopsticks snapping.

Japanese: 「くっ」
アレクセイは苦痛に顔を歪める。一差し指の骨が折れたのだ。
English: Alexei’s face contorted in pain. The bone in his forefinger had broken.

Japanese: 松子はもう片方の手で、拳銃を握る彼の手首を握りしめ、そのまま彼の腕を関節と逆向きにねじる。痛みから逃れるにはその回転に逆らわずに松子の手の動きに従うしかない。そうなれば、彼の身体は完全に松子の制圧下に置かれるはずだった。
English: With her other hand, Matsuko gripped the wrist of the hand that held the gun and twisted his arm against the natural direction of the joint. To escape the pain, he would have to follow the rotation of her hands rather than resist it. Then his body would be entirely under her control.

Japanese: これは子供の頃亮から教わった護身術だった。使うのは久しぶりだが、身体はまだ覚えている。
English: Ryo had taught her this method of self-defense when they were children. It had been a long time since she had used it, but her body still remembered.

Japanese: しかしアレクセイは松子の腹の辺りを蹴って力任せに腕を引き抜く。肘や肩から鈍い音がし、彼はそのまま後に転がった。テーブルの上から転がり落ちたカップが音を立てて床ではじける。
English: Alexei kicked Matsuko in the abdomen and wrenched his arm free by brute force. Dull sounds came from his elbow and shoulder as he rolled backward. A cup tumbled from the table and burst upon the floor.

Japanese: 「ぐあっ……うっ……」
English: “Gwaa... Urgh...”

Japanese: アレクセイは床の上で折れた腕の痛みにのたうちまわりながらも、銃は手放さない。
English: Writhing on the floor in pain from the broken arm, Alexei still refused to release the gun.

Japanese: しりもちを付いた松子は立ち上がり、攻撃しようとしたが、彼は無事な方の手で銃を掴んで銃口で彼女を制す。絶体絶命の状況で、彼は躊躇せずにすぐに引き金に指をかけるが、しかしまた発作のように身体が揺れた。
English: Matsuko rose from where she had landed and tried to attack. He seized the gun with his uninjured hand and held her at bay with the muzzle. Even in this desperate condition, he did not hesitate to put his finger to the trigger. Then his body shuddered again as though in another seizure.

Japanese: そして彼はその姿を変えた。
English: And his form changed.

Japanese: 「はあ……はあ……」
English: “Ahh... ahh...”

Japanese: 肩を揺らしてそこで荒い呼吸をするのは、長い黒髪の女性であった。
English: The person standing there, shoulders heaving with ragged breaths, was a woman with long black hair.

Japanese: 彼女はゆらりと立ち上がり、そして手の中の銃を見ると、床に投げ捨てた。
English: She rose unsteadily. When she saw the gun in her hand, she threw it onto the floor.

Japanese: 「くっ」
変身しても怪我は残るようで、折れた方の腕を動かそうとして顔を顰める。
English: The injuries appeared to persist across transformations. She tried to move the broken arm and grimaced.

Japanese: そして彼女は顔を上げて、こちらを見た。彼女は東洋人で、三十になるかならないかといった年齢の美しい女だった。
English: Then she raised her face and looked at Matsuko. She was a beautiful East Asian woman, perhaps just under or just over thirty.

Japanese: 「ああ……ミシェル……」
English: “Oh... Michelle...”

Japanese: そう呟くと、女の目に涙が溢れた。
English: As she murmured the name, tears filled the woman’s eyes.

Japanese: 新たに現れたコシチェイの三番目の姿を松子は呆然と眺めている。
English: Matsuko stared blankly at this third form of Koschei that had newly appeared.

Japanese: 「ミシェル……あなたが生きていたなんて……」
English: “Michelle... You’re alive...”

Japanese: 女は顔中を涙で濡らしながらゆらりと松子に近づく。松子は警戒してその分下がる。
English: Her face drenched in tears, the woman swayed toward Matsuko. Matsuko retreated the same distance, remaining on guard.

Japanese: 「どうか触らせて頂戴……お母さん、もう一度あなたに会えるなんて、夢にも思わなかった……」
English: “Please, let me touch you... Your mother never dreamed she would see you again...”

Japanese: 「……お母さん？」
English: “...My mother?”

Japanese: 「そうよ。……私があなたを産んだの。守ってあげられなくてゴメンね……」
English: “Yes. ...I gave birth to you. I’m sorry I couldn’t protect you...”

Japanese: 女は松子に向かって手を伸ばす。松子はそれを避けて駆け足で女の後にまわりこみ、銃を拾う。
English: The woman reached out toward Matsuko. Matsuko dodged the hand, darted around behind her, and picked up the gun.

Japanese: 「いいわ。それで私を撃ちなさい。そうしたら、すぐに私の上着のポケットから注射器を取り出してそれを私の身体に打つの。そうすれば、二度と生き返ることはないわ」
English: “Good. Shoot me with it. Then take the syringe from my coat pocket at once and inject it into my body. If you do, I will never come back to life.”

Japanese: 女は松子を追うことを諦め、そう言った。
English: The woman abandoned her attempt to follow Matsuko and gave the instruction instead.

Japanese: 「どうしてそんなことを教えてくれるんですか？」
English: “Why are you telling me how?”

Japanese: 松子は両手で銃を構えながら訊ねる。
English: Matsuko asked while holding the gun in both hands.

Japanese: 冷静な顔をしていたが、心臓の鼓動が早まり、じっとりとしたおかしな汗を掻いていた。
English: Her face remained calm, but her heart raced and her skin was slick with unnatural sweat.

Japanese: 目の前の女は母親だと名乗っている。松子の直感はそれは真実であると告げていた。しかし自分たちに脅威を与えようとしているコシチェイの一部であることも間違いないのだ。
English: The woman before her claimed to be her mother. Matsuko’s intuition told her it was true. Yet the woman was undeniably also one part of Koschei, who had come here to threaten them.

Japanese: 「ミシェル、私はあなたを守ろうとしたの。愛するロジャーとの間に出来たあなたを。……でもみんなは肉親を持つことを許さなかった。そして、この殺人鬼に命じてあなたを殺させたのよ……うるさいわ！　もうあなたの言葉なんか聞かない！」
English: “Michelle, I tried to protect you—the child I bore with my beloved Roger. ...But the others would not permit us to have families. They ordered this murderer to kill you... Be quiet! I won’t listen to you anymore!”

Japanese: 彼女は急にそっぽを向くと、誰もいない空間にそう怒鳴った。
English: She suddenly turned aside and shouted into empty space.

Japanese: そしてすぐに松子の方を向くと、頭痛に耐えるように頭を抑え、顔を顰めながら言う。
English: She immediately faced Matsuko again, clutched her head as though enduring a headache, and spoke through a grimace.

Japanese: 「ミシェル。……残念だけどあまり時間がないみたい。早く私を撃ちなさい。みんなが、私を引きずりおろそうとしている」
English: “Michelle... I’m sorry, but it seems I have very little time. Shoot me quickly. They are trying to drag me down.”

Japanese: 松子は今すぐ女の言う通り今すぐ引き金を引くべきだと頭では理解していたが、指がどうしても動かず、銃口が震えた。
English: Matsuko understood rationally that she should pull the trigger at once, exactly as the woman asked. But her finger would not move, and the muzzle trembled.

Japanese: 「……あなたは今、私を助けてくれたんですか？」
English: “...Did you just save me?”

Japanese: 唾液がなくなってカラカラに乾いた口でそう言った。
English: Her mouth was parched as she forced out the words.

Japanese: 「早く……早く撃ちなさい……」
English: “Hurry... Shoot me...”

Japanese: 女は頭を抱えたままゆらりと揺らめいた。また、別に誰かに変身しようとしているのだ。
English: Still holding her head, the woman swayed unsteadily. She was beginning to transform into someone else again.

Japanese: 松子は下唇を噛み、銃を構え直す。そして、その照準を女の胸の辺りに当てる。
English: Matsuko bit her lower lip and readied the gun once more. She set her sights upon the woman’s chest.

Japanese: 母だと名乗るその女は顔を顰め、喘ぐように口で呼吸をしていた。
English: The woman who called herself Matsuko’s mother grimaced and breathed through her mouth in gasps.

Japanese: ――この人がくれたこのチャンスを無駄にしてはいけない。大体、私はこんな人全然知らないじゃないか！
English: —I must not waste the chance this woman has given me. I don’t even know her!

Japanese: 松子は心中で自分に向かってそう叫んだが、引き金にかけた一差し指はまるで誰か他人のものになってしまったかのように動かない。
English: Matsuko screamed the words inwardly, but the forefinger upon the trigger would not move, as though it belonged to someone else.
“Hurry...”

Japanese: 女はまぶたをぎゅっと閉じ、涙を流している。彼女も平気なわけじゃない。撃たれる恐怖を感じてなお、そう言っているのだ。
English: The woman squeezed her eyes shut and wept. This was not easy for her either. She was afraid of being shot, yet continued to ask for it.

Japanese: 松子は肩をふるわせながら銃を彼女に向けている。落ち着くために、口を開き、音が聞こえるくらい深く呼吸をする。
English: Matsuko held the gun upon her with trembling shoulders. Trying to calm herself, she opened her mouth and drew a breath deep enough to be heard.

Japanese: そして、人差し指を引こうとしたが、やはりどうしても動いてくれない。
English: She tried to pull her forefinger back, but still it refused to move.

Japanese: 松子のはだらりと拳銃をおろした。
English: Matsuko’s arms sagged, lowering the gun.

Japanese: 「だめだ……撃てない。撃てないよお母さん……」
English: “I can’t... I can’t shoot you, Mom...”

Japanese: 松子の言葉で女はハッと目を開き、顔をあげる。
English: At Matsuko’s words, the woman’s eyes flew open and she raised her face.

Japanese: そしてその涙で曇った目で、彼女は目の前の愛娘が自分と同じように涙を流しているのを見た。
English: Through eyes clouded with tears, she saw the beloved daughter before her weeping just as she was.

Japanese: 「ミシェル……いまお母さんて……」
English: “Michelle... Did you just call me Mom...?”

Japanese: 言いかけたところで、彼女は頭を抑えて前のめりに倒れた。
English: Before she could finish, she clutched her head and pitched forward.

Japanese: 「お母さんっ！」
English: “Mom!”

Japanese: 松子はほとんど無意識に倒れる母に駈け寄り、そして目の前で立ち止まった。
English: Almost without thought, Matsuko rushed toward her falling mother, then stopped directly before her.

Japanese: 女の身体はみるみるうちに膨れ上がり、服が内側から押し上げられパンパンに表面が張っている。
English: The woman’s body swelled before her eyes. Her clothing was thrust outward from within, its surface drawn taut.

Japanese: また変身が始まっているのだ。
English: Another transformation had begun.

Japanese: しかしこれはなんと禍々しい能力なのだろう。人間が、人格も体格も全く違う別の人間に入れ替ってしまうとは。路地から話には聞いていたが、こうして目の当たりにしても信じることが出来ない。まるで夢を見ているようだ。
English: What an ominous power it was. One human being could change places with a completely different one, with another personality and physique. Matsuko had heard it from Roji, yet even seeing it before her eyes, she could not believe it. It was like a dream.

Japanese: ――サイキックとは、或いは夜明けに見る支離滅裂な悪夢を現実の世界に呼び出す能力なのかもしれない。
English: —Perhaps psychic power was the ability to summon the disjointed nightmare before dawn into the waking world.

Japanese: 「くっ」
松子は我を取り戻し、銃を構える。もう躊躇している暇はない。相手の銃を向けると、目をつぶって引き金にかけた一差し指に力を込めた。
English: Matsuko recovered herself and raised the gun. There was no longer time to hesitate. Pointing it at her opponent, she closed her eyes and squeezed the trigger.

Japanese: この時コシチェイが持っていたのは、独自ルートで入手した中国製の拳銃だった。
English: The gun Koschei possessed at this time was a Chinese-made pistol obtained through an independent route.

Japanese: エリー・ホワイトが密輸しているものよりも大分質が劣る。パーツ製造の精度が低く、しばしばトラブルが発生し、病院襲撃の際も故障する銃が見られた。
English: It was considerably inferior to the weapons Ellie White smuggled. Its parts were manufactured with poor precision and frequently malfunctioned; some guns had failed during the attack upon the hospital as well.

Japanese: この時もそれが起こった。
English: It happened again now.

Japanese: 引き金が固く、松子の力でもビクともしない。動転して二度、三度引いたが同じことだ。
English: The trigger was so rigid that not even Matsuko’s strength could move it. Distraught, she pulled a second time, then a third. The result remained the same.

Japanese: 排莢がうまくいかず、拳銃のなかで先ほど撃った弾の薬莢が詰まっている。これではいくら引き金を引こうとしたところで弾は発射されない。
English: The spent casing from the previous shot had failed to eject and was lodged inside the pistol. No matter how often she pulled the trigger, it could not fire.

Japanese: 松子は銃器には疎く、もちろんそんなことは知るよしもない。突然のトラブルに呆然としていると、何か黒いものが視界を覆った。
English: Matsuko knew little about firearms and naturally had no way of understanding any of this. She stared blankly at the sudden problem, and something black filled her vision.

Japanese: 次の瞬間、彼女は咄嗟に手をあげて守ったが、そのまま身体が空中に吹き飛ばされた。
English: In the next instant, she instinctively raised a hand to defend herself, but her body was sent flying through the air.

Japanese: 変身を終えたコシチェイは、筋骨隆々たる大男になっており、立ち上がりながらその拳を横薙ぎにして、手の甲の部分――いわゆる裏拳で殴りつけたのだ。
English: Koschei had completed the transformation into a huge, powerfully muscled man. As he stood, he swept one fist sideways and struck her with the back of his hand—a backfist.

Japanese: これによって松子の身体はピンボールの玉のようにはじけ飛び、背後にあった棚に激突し、それを壊した。戸に使われていたガラスが砕け散り、パラパラと松子の身体に降り注ぐ。
English: Matsuko’s body ricocheted like a pinball, struck the cabinet behind her, and destroyed it. Glass in its doors shattered, raining down upon her in a shower.

Japanese: 「汐さんっ！」
English: “Ms. Shio!”

Japanese: タナベが叫ぶ。
English: Tanabe screamed.

Japanese: 松子の意識は危ういところで繋ぎ止められていた。痛みに顔を顰めながら薄目をあけると、部屋の向こう側に山のような巨体を持つ大男が立っているのが見えた。膨れ上がった筋肉で服は破れ、ほとんど全裸のようになっている。彼はこちらに横顔を向けながら、毛むくじゃらの身体にまとわりつくぼろきれとなった服を指先で引きちぎっていた。
English: Matsuko barely clung to consciousness. Wincing, she cracked open her eyes and saw a man with a mountainous body standing across the room. His swollen muscles had torn his clothes until he was nearly naked. With his face turned partly toward her, he used his fingertips to rip away the tatters clinging to his hairy body.

Japanese: 相手とは少し距離がある。腕の一振りで部屋の端から端へはじき飛ばされたのだ。化け物じみた腕力である。衝撃を受けた右手が動かない。こちらは骨折しただろう。そして、肩も脱臼したのかやたらと痛む。背中にはガラスの破片が突き刺さっているのか、こちらも全面がやけどを負ったような痛みがする。
English: There was some distance between them. One swing of his arm had flung her from one end of the room to the other. His strength was monstrous. Her right hand would not move after taking the impact; the bones were likely broken. Her shoulder too hurt intensely, perhaps dislocated. Shards of glass seemed embedded in her back, whose entire surface burned as though scalded.

Japanese: 銃はどこかへ落としたらしく手の中になかった。いや、たとえあったとしても故障したままじゃ役に立たない。
English: The gun had fallen somewhere and was no longer in her hand. Even if she had retained it, the malfunction would have made it useless.

Japanese: この相手にどう対処するか？
English: How could she deal with this opponent?

Japanese: 相手は明らかに自分よりパワーがある。アレクセイを相手にするようにはいかない。まだこちらの身体は動くようだが、素手でやりあったら到底分があるとは思えない。
English: He was plainly more powerful than she was. She could not fight him as she had Alexei. Her body still seemed capable of movement, but she could not imagine gaining any advantage in an unarmed struggle.

Japanese: 松子は目を閉じ、そして手だけを動かして手のひらのなかに沢山のガラスの破片を集めた。
English: Matsuko closed her eyes and moved only her hand, gathering a large number of glass fragments in her palm.

Japanese: こちらが目を開けたとき、相手はよそを見ていた。意識を失ったふりをすれば信じるだろう。そうしたら、きっととどめをさしに来るはずだ。タナベが怯えてすすり泣く声がするが、彼女よりこちらを優先するだろう。
English: Before she closed them, the man had been looking elsewhere. If she pretended to be unconscious, he would believe it. Then he would surely come closer to finish her. She could hear Tanabe sobbing in fear, but he would prioritize Matsuko.

Japanese: あの男がある程度近づいたところで、この手のなかのガラスの破片を顔面に投げつけ、目潰しをする。そうして怯んだ隙に起き上がってタナベのところに駆けつけ、彼女を抱えて逃げる。
English: Once the man drew near enough, she would hurl the glass into his face and blind him. While he recoiled, she would rise, rush to Tanabe, carry her, and escape.

Japanese: ――とにかく、一旦体制を立て直すことが必要だ。
English: —First of all, she had to regroup.

Japanese: 松子は目を閉じながら、意識を聴覚に集中した。
English: Keeping her eyes closed, Matsuko concentrated upon her hearing.

Japanese: 身体に窮屈にまとわりついた布を剥がし、自由に動けるようになったコシチェイがこちらにむかって歩きはじめる。
English: Koschei finished tearing away the cloth that clung tightly to his body and began walking toward her, able to move freely now.

Japanese: その足が、部屋に散らばった様々なものを踏みつけ、ジャリジャリと音を鳴らす。
English: His feet crunched over the various objects scattered across the room.

Japanese: この跫音だけを頼りに距離を測るのだ。
English: She would judge the distance by those footsteps alone.

Japanese: 遠すぎても近すぎてもいけない。相手が避けにくい程度には近く、けれど相手の手が届かない丁度良い距離で目を開き、位置を確認したら即座に駆けつける。
English: Neither too far nor too close. She would open her eyes at the precise distance—near enough that he would find it difficult to evade her attack, but beyond the reach of his hands. The instant she confirmed his position, she would move in.

Japanese: 松子の心からは先ほどの鑑賞は消え、別人のような冷静さが支配していた。本人は気がついてはいないが、この感情の切り替えの早さこそが彼女が人とは違うところだ。
English: The sentiment that had filled Matsuko earlier was gone, replaced by a calm that made her seem another person. She herself did not realize it, but this speed in changing from one emotion to another was precisely what set her apart.

Japanese: 跫音がゆっくりと近づいてくる。それを聞きながら松子はタイミングを計る。
English: The footsteps slowly approached. Listening, Matsuko judged her moment.

Japanese: そしてもう少しというところで、音が消えた。その場で相手が立ち止まったのだ。
English: Then, just before he reached her, the sound vanished. He had stopped where he stood.

Japanese: もし相手が警戒して近づかずに何か投げつけて来ようとしているのなら、それにも対応しなくてはいけない。
English: If suspicion kept him from approaching and he meant to throw something at her, she had to be ready for that too.

Japanese: さらに一層の注意を聴覚に傾けていると、布を破る音が聞こえた。まだからだにまとわりついた衣服の残骸があったようだ。
English: She concentrated still more intensely upon her hearing and caught the sound of tearing cloth. Some remnant of his clothing must still have been wrapped around him.

Japanese: それを捨てると、相手はまた近づく。シュウシュウと空気が抜ける呼吸の音が鮮明になる。
English: After discarding it, he approached again. The hissing passage of air through his lungs became clear.

Japanese: ――ここだ。
English: —Now.

Japanese: 松子はぱっと目を見開くと目の前に迫ったその男の位置を確認し、動く方の腕を腕を振るう。
English: Matsuko’s eyes snapped open. She confirmed the position of the man looming before her and swung the arm she could still move.

Japanese: 「ぐおおっ！」
English: “Gwoaah!”

Japanese: 意識を失っていると思われた相手に至近距離で投げつけられたガラスのつぶては、いかに優れたタイプBと言えども避けることは出来ないようだ。
English: It seemed that even an exceptional Type B could not evade a handful of glass hurled from point-blank range by someone he believed to be unconscious.

Japanese: 獣のような呻き声を上げてのけぞる男の姿を横目で確認しながら松子は素早く立ち上がり、タナベの方へ駆けた。
English: The man reeled backward with an animal groan. Matsuko confirmed it in the corner of her eye, sprang to her feet, and ran to Tanabe.

Japanese: タナベは顔を涙にぐちゃぐちゃにしたまま放心してかたまっている。
English: Tanabe sat frozen in a daze, her face wet and distorted with tears.

Japanese: 松子を見ると、「汐さん……」と何か言おうとしたが、聞かずに肩に抱え上げる。背後ではガラスの破片がよほどうまく命中したらしく、コシチェイが空気が震えんばかりの大きな苦しみの声をあげていた。いま攻撃したら勝てるだろうか？　いや、たとえぼやけてでもこちらを見ることが出来れば勝ち目があるとは思えない。それよりもまずタナベを逃がしたほうがいい。
English: When she saw Matsuko, she began, “Ms. Shio...” Matsuko did not listen, but lifted her onto one shoulder. Behind them, Koschei roared in agony loudly enough to shake the air; the glass had struck exceptionally well. Could Matsuko defeat him if she attacked now? No. If he could see her at all, however indistinctly, she did not believe she had any chance. Escaping with Tanabe came first.

Japanese: 松子はコシチェイを尻目にドアを開けて廊下へ飛び出す。
English: With Koschei behind her, Matsuko opened the door and burst into the corridor.

Japanese: 廊下を走って裏口から外へ出た。空には月が浮かんでいる。建物のなかの喧噪とは裏腹に、世界はいつも通り平常運行をしていた。いや、こういった血みどろの争いも、世界の平常のなかに収まるものなのだろう。この世界は我々からするとどんなに異常と感じられるものでも当たり前のような顔で売り場に並べている。――松子は月を見ながらこの緊急の場にはおよそそぐわぬそんなことを考えながら、タナベを降ろす。
English: She ran down the corridor and left through the rear exit. The moon hung in the sky. In contrast to the chaos inside the building, the world continued its ordinary course. Or perhaps a blood-soaked struggle like this too fell within the world’s ordinary course. However abnormal something seemed to us, the world displayed it for sale with the most commonplace expression. Looking at the moon and thinking thoughts wholly unsuited to the emergency, Matsuko set Tanabe down.

Japanese: 「し、汐さん、あなた傷だらけで……」
English: “M-Ms. Shio, you’re covered in wounds...”

Japanese: 松子の顔をみてタナベが顔を顰める。
English: Tanabe grimaced at the sight of Matsuko’s face.

Japanese: 確かに彼女の言う通り、片腕はまるきり使えないし背中はガラスの破片が突き刺さって血みどろだし、そしてさっきはそれほどでもなかったが顔面も腫れ上がってほとんど片目が見えないほどに膨れ上がってなっている。その姿はまるで番町皿屋敷のお岩の如く、コメディで笑いを取るために大げさにメイクしたらこうなるのだろうかといった案配だ。
English: She was right. One arm was entirely unusable; Matsuko’s back was blood-soaked and studded with glass; and though it had not been so severe at first, her face had now swollen until one eye was almost closed. She looked like Oiwa from The Dish Mansion at Banchō, or perhaps like a performer made up with such exaggeration for a comedy.

Japanese: 「私は大丈夫です。タナベさん、ここからは一人で避難してください」
English: “I’m all right. Ms. Tanabe, you must evacuate alone from here.”

Japanese: 「一人で？」
English: “Alone?”

Japanese: 「はい。私は戻ってあいつの相手をします」
English: “Yes. I’m going back to face him.”

Japanese: 「な、何を言っているの……。一緒に逃げて、警察が来るのを待って……」
English: “Wh-what are you saying? Come with me. We can wait for the police...”

Japanese: 「それじゃだめなんです。あいつの目的は私です。私の姿が見えなくなれば、何をするか……」
English: “That won’t work. I’m his target. If I disappear, there’s no telling what he’ll do...”

Japanese: 「でも、相手はもう目が見えないでしょう？　だから安全なところで待ってればきっと」
English: “But he can’t see anymore, can he? If we wait somewhere safe, surely...”

Japanese: 「あれくらい、すぐ治ります。そういう身体なんです。あいつも、私も……」
English: “That will heal quickly. That is the kind of body he has. And so do I...”

Japanese: 松子はタナベの手を握って、
English: Matsuko took Tanabe’s hand.

Japanese: 「私も死ぬつもりはありません。どんな手を使っても生き延びます。そのためにはタナベさんの協力が必要です」
English: “I don’t intend to die either. I will survive by any means necessary. To do that, I need your cooperation.”

Japanese: 「わ、わたしが？」
English: “M-my cooperation?”

Japanese: 「ええ」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: 松子はタナベを落ち着かせるために痛みで脂汗が浮かんだ顔に微笑みを浮かべると、
English: To calm Tanabe, Matsuko forced a smile onto her pain-wracked face, slick with cold sweat.

Japanese: 「ちょっとだけなかに戻って、必要なものを持って来ます。そこに隠れて待っていて下さい」
English: “I’m going back inside just long enough to retrieve something I need. Hide there and wait for me.”

Japanese: そして立ち上がり、今出たばかりの建物のなかに引き返した。
English: Then she stood and returned to the building she had only just left.

Japanese: 一方部屋に残されたコシチェイは床の上に蹲り顔を押さえている。
English: Meanwhile, Koschei remained crouched upon the reception-room floor, holding his face.

Japanese: 右目はさほどではなかったが、左目は鋭い破片が直撃して完全に視覚を失っている。そしてとにかくひどい激痛だ。
English: The right eye was not badly injured, but a sharp fragment had struck the left and destroyed its vision completely. Above all, the pain was appalling.

Japanese: 彼は皮膚や骨の痛みには強かったがこうした急所の痛みに耐えることが出来なかった。
English: He tolerated pain in skin and bone well, but could not endure pain in a vital organ like this.

Japanese: 頭のなかではヘスによる指示がひっきりなしに飛んでいる。
English: Hess’s instructions sounded without pause inside his head.

Japanese: 『追え！　痛がる暇はないぞ！　腰抜け！』
English: “Go after her! You have no time to whimper! Coward!”

Japanese: 辛辣な言葉は、そのままヘスの彼に対する不信感を表していた。
English: The bitter words directly expressed Hess’s distrust of him.

Japanese: 彼の名前はエミール・ブラーエ 。チェコ出身のプロレスラーということになっている。プロレスラー時代に頭を打った影響で舌に麻痺があり、言葉がうまくでない。性格は粗暴で反逆的。自分が『コシチェイ』を構成する一人であることをうまく理解しておらず、頭のなかで鳴り響くヘスの声には従ったり逆らったり、不安定である。
English: His name was Emil Brahe. Publicly, he was a professional wrestler from the Czech Republic. A blow to the head during his wrestling career had paralyzed his tongue, making speech difficult. His temperament was violent and rebellious. He did not properly understand that he was one of the people who constituted ‘Koschei,’ and his response to Hess’s voice ringing within his head was unstable, veering between obedience and defiance.

Japanese: 理性に乏しく気分の赴くままに殴り、殺し、強姦し、奪う、非常な問題児で、ヘスは滅多に彼を呼び出すことはない。
English: Possessing little reason, he beat, killed, raped, and stole as his mood directed. He was an exceptionally difficult member, and Hess rarely called him forth.

Japanese: が、その肉体は頑健で、タイプBとしての身体能力増強効果も大きく、素手による戦闘能力はずば抜けていた。
English: His body, however, was exceptionally robust, and Type B enhancement had produced a tremendous effect upon his physical abilities. His capacity for unarmed combat was outstanding.

Japanese: 松子はアレクセイの身体能力を上回っており、マリアの能力では相手をバラバラにしてまた復活の可能性を残してしまうため、今回は彼が呼び出された。
English: Matsuko’s physical abilities surpassed Alexei’s, while Maria’s power would merely tear her apart and leave open the possibility of another resurrection. Emil had therefore been selected on this occasion.

Japanese: ヘスは言うことをきかぬこの男を出してしまったことを後悔しかけたが、しかし指示がなくともエミールの心は自分にこの苦痛を与えた松子への憎悪で満ちていた。
English: Hess had begun to regret calling forth a man who refused to obey, but even without orders, Emil’s mind was full of hatred for Matsuko, who had inflicted this pain upon him.

Japanese: しばらく部屋で蹲っていると持ち前の治癒力で痛みが少しずつ治まってゆく。眼球は完全に破損しており彼と言えども二日や三日では再生しないだろうが、痛み自体は耐えられるほどのものになっていた。
English: After he crouched in the room for some time, his natural healing power gradually reduced the pain. The eyeball had been destroyed completely and, even for him, would take more than two or three days to regenerate. The pain itself, however, had become bearable.

Japanese: そして彼は立ち上がり、松子の姿を探した。
English: He stood and searched for Matsuko.

Japanese: 応接室は様々なものが砕けて足元にはガラスや棚の破片などが散乱している。その上に、ポツポツと赤黒い血が部屋の電灯で照らされているのを彼は見つけた。
English: Countless things had been shattered in the reception room, leaving glass and pieces of the cabinet scattered across the floor. Among them, he found drops of dark red blood illuminated by the electric lights.

Japanese: それを追って廊下に出る。
English: He followed them into the corridor.

Japanese: 廊下は消灯しており、非常灯の緑色の明かりだけが頼りだった。それでも、一つの目をギロギロとこらせば血を辿ってゆくことが出来る。
English: The corridor lights had been extinguished, leaving only the green glow of the emergency lamps. Even so, by straining his one remaining eye, he could follow the blood.

Japanese: 血の跡は裏口の方へ続いており、それを追って歩く。全裸に近いエミールの足の裏がひたひたと音を立てる。
English: The trail continued toward the rear exit, and he walked after it. Emil’s nearly naked feet made soft, wet sounds against the floor.

Japanese: そして扉を開いた。ドアの外の地面はコンクリートで舗装されており、月明かりで黒い血液の雫が見える。しかし、ほんのドアの近くに痕跡があるだけで、どこかへ去った様子はなかった。
English: He opened the door. The ground outside was paved with concrete, and the moonlight revealed drops of black blood. Yet there were traces only near the door, with no sign that they led away.

Japanese: 困っていると、
English: As he stood at a loss,

Japanese: 『中だ。中に戻った跡があるから中を探せ』
English: “Inside. The trail shows that she went back in. Search inside.”

Japanese: 頭のなかでヘスの言葉が響き、エミールも今回はそれに従った。
English: Hess’s words echoed within his head, and this time Emil obeyed.

Japanese: 地面の痕跡を見ながら戻ると、確かに血の跡は途中で分岐しているのに気づく。
English: Following the marks upon the ground back inside, he noticed that the blood trail indeed branched partway along.

Japanese: 廊下と裏口を繋ぐ一本道ではなく、横に逸れており、その先にはドアがあった。ドアの上には職員室と書かれたプレートがあるが、彼には日本語が読めなかった。
English: It no longer followed the straight path between the corridor and rear exit, but veered to the side and ended at a door. A Japanese plate above it read STAFF ROOM, though he could not understand the words.

Japanese: 『中へ入るな。ここで脅せ。出て来なければ子供を殺すと叫ぶんだ』
English: “Do not enter. Threaten her from here. Shout that if she refuses to come out, you will kill the children.”

Japanese: 日本語が喋れないエミールに英語でそう言うようヘスは伝えた。
English: Hess told him to say the words in English, since Emil could not speak Japanese.

Japanese: しかし、怒り狂ったエミールはその言葉を守らなかった。
English: But Emil, crazed with anger, did not obey.

Japanese: 丸太のような足を振り上げ、ドアを蹴破る。鍵のかけられた引き戸は中央で二つに折れて吹っ飛ぶと、奥に並んだ机の上のものをなぎ倒して盛大な音を立てた。
English: He raised a leg like a log and kicked through the door. The locked sliding door broke in two at the center and flew inward, sweeping the objects from desks beyond it with a tremendous crash.

Japanese: 部屋のなかは廊下よりもさらに暗い。
English: The room was darker still than the corridor.

Japanese: エミールは恐れずそのなかへ足を踏み入れた。
English: Emil entered without fear.

Japanese: そこで待ち構えていた松子が襲い掛かった。
English: Matsuko, lying in wait, attacked.

Japanese: 彼女は入り口のそばの棚の上に潜んでいて、彼が部屋に足を踏み入れると同時に飛び降りたのだ。
English: She had concealed herself atop a shelf beside the entrance and jumped down the moment he stepped inside.

Japanese: その右手には白い布で包丁を縛り付けている。包丁は、職員室の奥の給湯室に常備されたものだった。普段、誰かが持って来た果物やお菓子を切り分けるために使われているそのセラミックの白い刃を振りかざし、エミールの首もとに向かって体重を込めて振り下ろす。
English: A white cloth bound a kitchen knife to her right hand. The knife was ordinarily kept in the kitchenette at the back of the staff room, where it was used to cut up fruit or sweets someone had brought in. Raising its white ceramic blade, Matsuko drove it toward Emil’s neck with all her weight.

Japanese: しかしエミールの人間離れした反射能力はその完全な不意打ちさえも通用しなかった。
English: Yet even this complete surprise attack failed against Emil’s inhuman reflexes.

Japanese: 彼は巨体に見合わぬ素早さでうしろに飛び退く。包丁の刃はどこかの肉を切り裂き、血が飛び散ったが、到底致命傷というには及ばなかった。
English: With speed that belied his huge body, he leaped backward. The blade cut into flesh somewhere and sent blood flying, but the wound was far from fatal.

Japanese: エミールは職員室の闇の中に姿勢を低くして自分を襲ってきた相手を見据える。廊下から差し込む緑の光の下に、白い包丁を持って無表情にこちらを見る松子の姿があった。折れた方の腕はだらりと下げられている。
English: Emil lowered his stance in the darkness and stared at the person who had attacked him. Beneath the green light entering from the corridor stood Matsuko, watching him without expression and holding a white knife. Her broken arm hung limply at her side.

Japanese: 最初の襲撃に失敗したが、彼女は冷静だった。感情がないと言われていた子供の頃とまったく同じ表情だった。
English: Her first attack had failed, but she remained calm. It was exactly the expression she had worn as a child, when others said she possessed no emotion.

Japanese: エミールが一息つく間も与えず、すぐに飛びかかった。身体ごと包丁を突き出す。しかしその刃はエミールに届かない。
English: Without allowing Emil even a breath, Matsuko lunged again, thrusting the knife with her entire body. The blade never reached him.

Japanese: 素早さにおいて圧倒的な差があった。
English: The difference in their speed was overwhelming.

Japanese: エミールの手は松子に見えないほどの早さで、包丁を握る手首を握った。そして次の瞬間にはくるりと捻られて、手首と肘からバキバキと骨の折れる音がした。
English: Emil’s hand moved too quickly for Matsuko to see as it seized the wrist holding the knife. In the next instant he gave it a turn, and bones cracked in her wrist and elbow.

Japanese: 松子はそれでも怯まない。頭突きの要領で頭をエミールに突き出そうとしたが、その動きも彼に咎められる。
English: Even then Matsuko did not recoil. She tried to drive her head into Emil as though delivering a headbutt, but he arrested that movement too.

Japanese: 彼のもう片方の手が、松子の白い喉を正面から掴んでいる。
English: His other hand closed around the front of Matsuko’s white throat.

Japanese: 松子の口から声が漏れる。
English: A sound escaped Matsuko’s mouth.

Japanese: その顔はやはり無表情で、恐怖も絶望も感じてはいないようだった。
English: Her face remained expressionless. She appeared to feel neither fear nor despair.

Japanese: エミールは首を掴んで振り回すと側面の壁に松子の身体をドンと押しつけてその動きを制限すると、もう片方の手で髪の毛を掴み、手前に強く引いた。
English: Holding her by the neck, Emil swung her around and slammed her body against the side wall to restrict her movement. With his other hand, he seized her hair and pulled violently toward himself.

Japanese: ゴキッと音がして松子の頸椎が砕ける。そして手足がビクリと動き、そのあと静かになった。
English: There was a hard crack as Matsuko’s cervical vertebrae shattered. Her limbs jerked once, then fell still.

Japanese: エミールはそうして髪の毛を掴んだまま頭をグリグリと回す。首の骨が完全に砕けて皮だけで繋がっている頭部はなんの抵抗もなく、手を離すとだらりとあり得ない形にぶら下がった。
English: Still gripping her hair, Emil ground her head around and around. The neck bones were completely destroyed, leaving the head connected only by skin. It moved without resistance, and when he released it, it hung limply at an impossible angle.

Japanese: その目は見開かれ、半開きになった唇の間から唾液が糸を引いて落ちる。
English: Her eyes were wide open, and a thread of saliva fell between her parted lips.

Japanese: 首を押さえた手も離すと、糸の切れた操り人形のように松子の身体は床の上に崩れ落ちた。
English: When he released her throat as well, Matsuko collapsed onto the floor like a puppet whose strings had been cut.

Japanese: 完全に息がないのを確認すると、エミールはその身体を肩に担いで応接室に戻った。
English: After confirming that she was no longer breathing, Emil lifted the body onto his shoulder and returned to the reception room.

Japanese: そして、破れた衣服のなかから『ネオ・ローズ』の薬液が入った注射器を取り出すと、松子の身体に針を突き刺した。
English: From among his torn clothes, he removed a syringe filled with a Neo Rose solution and drove the needle into Matsuko’s body.

Japanese: そのあとズボンと下着を脱がし、だらりと力のない足を掴んで松子の股を開かせると、まだ少し温かみの残る性器のなかで二回射精して、その場を立ち去った。
English: Then he removed her trousers and underwear, took hold of her limp legs, spread them, ejaculated twice inside her vagina, which still retained a little warmth, and left.

Japanese: それから十五分ほどすると、タナベがおそるおそる部屋に戻ってくる。
English: About fifteen minutes later, Tanabe cautiously returned to the room.

Japanese: 彼女は武器のつもりか、手に金属バットを構え、慎重にあたりを見回すと、変わり果てた松子の姿を見つけた。
English: She held a metal bat as an improvised weapon. Looking carefully around her, she found Matsuko’s ruined body.
