Japanese: 広美にも、それを口にしたら彼らの感情を害するだろうと想像するくらいの分別はあったので、黙っていた。
English: Hiromi possesses enough discretion to imagine that saying so aloud would hurt their feelings, and therefore remains silent.

Japanese: そして翌日、広美が出発するときがやって来た。
English: Then the day of Hiromi’s departure arrives.

Japanese: 「本当に一人で大丈夫かい？　誰か一緒について行かせようか？」
English: “Are you truly certain you’ll be all right alone? Shall I send someone with you?”

Japanese: 昨日も会話をした八龍会のそのメンバーは、一通りの説明を終えた後に心配げにそう訊ねた。
English: After finishing his explanations, the Hachiryukai member who spoke with her yesterday asks with concern.

Japanese: ろくに世間を知らない広美に、その場所までたどり着けるとはとても思えなかったのだろう。
English: He probably cannot imagine that Hiromi, who knows almost nothing of the outside world, will manage to reach the address.

Japanese: 「大丈夫です。この携帯電話の使い方も教えて貰ったし」
English: “I’ll be all right. You taught me how to use this phone.”

Japanese: 八龍会が与えてくれた携帯電話の地図アプリには実家の住所を登録してもらってある。
English: Her family address has been entered into the map application on the phone Hachiryukai gave her.

Japanese: 「それに、小さいころ電車にのった記憶はなんとなくあります。わからなかったら、駅の人に聞けば大丈夫なんですよね」
English: “And I vaguely remember riding trains when I was small. If I don’t understand something, I can ask someone at the station, can’t I?”

Japanese: 「それはそうだけど……」
English: “That is true, but...”

Japanese: 彼は浮かない顔で広美の幼さの残る顔をまじまじと見る。
English: With a troubled expression, he studies Hiromi’s still-childish face.

Japanese: 「ご家族に事前に連絡はしたほうがいいんじゃないか？」
English: “Shouldn’t you contact your family in advance?”

Japanese: 「要りません。きっと、電話をしても私が良くなったって信じてくれないです。昨日鈴木さんも信じて貰えなくて泣いてたじゃないですか。あれを見て、直接行って病気が治った姿を見て貰ったほうがいいと思ったんです。そうすれば、私がもう悪い子じゃないって、一目でわかってくれると思います」
English: “There is no need. If I call, they won’t believe that I’m better. Yesterday, Ms. Suzuki cried when her family refused to believe her. Seeing that made me think it would be better to go there and let them see me after the illness is gone. Then one look will tell them I’m not a bad child anymore.”

Japanese: 広美はそう言って微笑んだ。
English: Hiromi smiles as she speaks.

Japanese: 「そうしたらきっと、私が病気になる前の、私のことが大好きだったお父さんとお母さんに戻ってくれます」
English: “Then I’m sure the mother and father who loved me before I became ill will come back to me.”

Japanese: 相手は答えず、難しい顔で広美を見下ろしたままだ。
English: The man gives no answer. He continues looking down at Hiromi with a difficult expression.

Japanese: 「それより、私が家に帰ってから、警察とかが聞きに来たらどう言えばいいですか？　病院のこととか、みなさんのこととか、聞かれると思うんですが……」
English: “More importantly, after I go home, what should I say if the police come to question me? I think they’ll ask about the hospital and all of you...”

Japanese: 広美の言葉に相手は苦笑して、
English: The man smiles wryly at her question.

Japanese: 「そんなの、気にすることはないよ。全部ありのままを言えばいい。この街で今はじまろうとしていることは、警察には止められないんだから」
English: “You don’t need to worry about that. Tell them everything exactly as it happened. The police cannot stop what is beginning in this city.”

Japanese: 広美はそんなものかとその言葉を疑問なく受け入れた。
English: Hiromi accepts his words without question, assuming that must be how things are.

Japanese: もっとも、実際にはこの八龍会員の自信ほど、彼らに勢いがあったかといえばそれは疑問だ。
English: The later account, however, casts doubt upon whether Hachiryukai truly possessed all the momentum implied by this member’s confidence.

Japanese: ネオ・ローズの効果によって優れた身体能力を活かせるようになったタイプBたちは確かにかつての欠点を克服した存在となっていたし、Y地区のあちこちの場所に会員を潜ませている八龍会は確かに脅威には違いない。しかし、それはあくまでもこの地域内限定の話である。地域外のタイプBの秘密組織は警察の監視下にあったし、そもそも、『ネオ・ローズ』の利益を独占したい八龍会は外の地域との関係が悪化しはじめており連携が難しかった。
English: Under the effects of Neo Rose, Type Bs could indeed make use of their superior physical abilities and had overcome their former disadvantage. Hachiryukai, with members hidden throughout Y District, was unquestionably a threat. But that held true only within this region. Secret Type B organizations elsewhere were under police surveillance. Moreover, Hachiryukai’s determination to monopolize the benefits of Neo Rose had begun damaging its relationships with groups in other regions, making cooperation difficult.

Japanese: Y地区ではあまりにも警察の力は弱かったが、外はそうではないのだ。病院襲撃のようなことを地域の外で行ったならば、すぐに手痛い報復を受けていただろう。
English: The police were extraordinarily weak inside Y District. Outside it, they were not. Had Hachiryukai attempted an attack like the one upon the hospital beyond the district, it would likely have met swift and painful retaliation.

Japanese: 八龍会の幹部たちには正しい認識があったはずだが、しかし彼のような末端の会員はそこまで冷静に状況を把握しているわけではなかった。
English: Hachiryukai’s executives presumably understood this correctly. But rank-and-file members like the man before Hiromi did not necessarily grasp circumstances with the same composure.

Japanese: カミラなどが説く理想を真に受け、自分たちの力を過信していた。
English: They took the ideals preached by Camilla and others at face value and overestimated their own power.

Japanese: もちろんそれは彼らが特別に悪いと言うわけではなく、長年彼らをおびやかしていた発症の恐怖や、ノーマルに対する劣等感が、奇跡のように消えてなくなってしまったのだから当然の反応なのだろう。
English: The account does not present this as any special moral failing. The fear of onset that had threatened them for years, and their sense of inferiority toward Normals, had vanished as if by a miracle. It interprets their response as natural enough.

Japanese: 八龍会の、特に若い者たちはみな輝ける将来への期待に胸を躍らせていた。
English: The young members of Hachiryukai in particular were said to be thrilled by the promise of a shining future.

Japanese: しかしその情熱は、病院で衣食に困らない平和な生活を長年送っていた元患者たちにはあまりピンとこないものだったようだ。細井のように理解を示す人間は少なく、ほとんどが広美のように、わけのわからないことを言っていると受け止めた。
English: That passion, however, appears not to have resonated much with the former patients, who had spent years living peacefully in the hospital without worrying about food or shelter. Few understood it as Hosoi did. Most, like Hiromi, received the members’ words as incomprehensible nonsense.

Japanese: 解放さえすればみな感謝して八龍会に協力してくれると、カミラをはじめとする幹部たちは随分単純に考えていたようだが、その思惑は外れることとなる。
English: Camilla and the other executives seem to have reasoned rather simply that everyone they liberated would feel grateful and cooperate with Hachiryukai. Their expectation would not be fulfilled.

Japanese: いずれにせよ、八龍会が細かい注文をつけてこないのは広美にとっては有り難いことだった。
English: In any event, Hiromi is grateful that Hachiryukai imposes no detailed conditions upon her.

Japanese: 話が終わると早速出発の準備をした。といっても、身ひとつのまま病院から脱出してきた広美にはさしたる荷物はない。八龍会から借りた携帯電話と身につけた衣服、細々としたものを入れる小さなポシェットひとつ。現金は病院に預けていたおやつ代の五千円と、さらに一万円を八龍会が貸してくれた。広美の家族が住む街まで電車で千円ほどしか使わないが、何かあったときのためだということだ。
English: The moment their conversation ends, she begins preparing to leave. Not that Hiromi, who escaped the hospital with nothing but the clothes upon her body, has much luggage. She has the phone borrowed from Hachiryukai, the clothes she is wearing, and one small shoulder bag for odds and ends. Her cash consists of five thousand yen in snack money deposited with the hospital, plus another ten thousand yen loaned to her by Hachiryukai. The train to her family’s city will cost only about one thousand yen, but the extra is said to be for emergencies.

Japanese: そして金色に目を輝くためのカラーコンタクトをつけようとしたのだが、こういったものを目に入れたことがなく、自分だと怖くてつけられない。
English: She also tries to insert colored contacts to hide her shining golden eyes. Having never put anything like them into her eyes before, however, she is too frightened to manage it alone.

Japanese: 細井につけて貰おうと、部屋を出てその姿を探そうとしたが見つからず、近くにいた他の元患者に聞くと街に買い物をしにいったということだった。アパートに残ったのは広美と親しくないものしかいないようだった。仕方なく部屋に戻って涙をぼろぼろとこぼしながらコンタクトをつけて、部屋に細井へ別れの挨拶を書いた手紙を置いてドアを開けた。
English: Hiromi leaves the room to find Hosoi and ask for help, but cannot locate her. Another former patient nearby says Hosoi has gone shopping in the city. Everyone remaining in the apartments appears to be someone Hiromi does not know well. With no other choice, she returns to her room and inserts the contacts while tears pour down her face. She leaves Hosoi a letter of farewell, opens the door, and departs.

Japanese: 外はしくしくと静かに雨が降っている。
English: Outside, the rain falls softly, almost as though weeping.

Japanese: 透明なビニール傘をさし、敷地から出ようとしたところで、向こうから金髪の青年がやって来た。
English: Holding a transparent plastic umbrella, Hiromi is about to leave the grounds when a blond young man approaches from ahead.

Japanese: 「やあ。一人でどこへ行くんだい？」
English: “Hello. Where are you going by yourself?”

Japanese: すれ違おうというとき、相手がそう声をかけたのでビクリとして立ち止まる。
English: As she tries to pass, he calls out. Hiromi flinches to a stop.

Japanese: 「あ、あの、親のところへ帰ろうと思って……」
English: “U-um, I’m going back to my parents...”

Japanese: 黒い傘をさして立つその青年は広美からすると見上げるほどに背が高く、ギョッとしながらそう答えた。
English: The young man standing beneath a black umbrella is tall enough that Hiromi has to crane her neck to look at him. Startled, she gives her answer.

Japanese: 「そうか。それは素敵だね！　これからがきみの本当の人生だから、幸せに生きるんだよ」
English: “I see. That’s wonderful! Your real life begins now. Be happy.”

Japanese: 青年は広美の動揺を意に介さずに笑うと、手にしたビニール袋から何かを取り出して広美の手に無理矢理柔らかいものを持たせる。
English: Ignoring Hiromi’s alarm, the young man smiles, takes something from the plastic bag and presses the soft object into her palm before she can resist.

Japanese: それは透明なフィルムでパッケージされたまんじゅうだった。
English: It is a manju wrapped in transparent film.

Japanese: 「餞別だよ。おれはこれをみんなに配ろうと思ってここに来たんだ。うまいんだぜ」
English: “A farewell gift. I came here to hand these out to everyone. They’re delicious.”

Japanese: 彼はそれだけ言うと、そのままアパートの方へ歩いて行ってしまう。
English: With nothing more than that, he walks on toward the apartments.

Japanese: 広美は困惑した面持ちでその背中を眺めた後、まんじゅうをポシェットにしまって歩きはじめた。
English: Hiromi watches his back with a bewildered expression, then slips the manju into her shoulder bag and continues walking.

Japanese: その人物は解放軍のリーダー見土道夫で、病院の襲撃の時にも居たのだが、結局広美はそのことに気がつかなかった。
English: The man was Michio Mido, leader of the Liberation Army. He had also been present during the attack upon the hospital, but Hiromi never realized either fact.

Japanese: 八龍会の世話係が一番心配していたのはY地区から出るまでの道のりで、右も左もわからない世間知らずの少女では、駅に辿り着くまでに地区内の不埒ものにちょっかいを出されてしまうかもしれない。ということで、八龍会の人間が駅まで送ってくれることになっていた。
English: What worried the Hachiryukai coordinator most was Hiromi’s journey out of Y District. A sheltered girl who scarcely knew left from right might attract the attention of some scoundrel in the district before ever reaching the station. For this reason, someone from Hachiryukai had been assigned to take her there.

Japanese: アパートを出てすぐ斜め向かいにあるアパートもまた元患者たちが暮らす建物になっており、そこの管理人室を訪ねると話を聞いていた中年女性が車を出して駅まで送り届けてくれた。
English: Another apartment building diagonally across the road from Hiromi’s houses former patients as well. When she visits its manager’s office, a middle-aged woman who has been told the situation brings out her car and drives Hiromi to the station.

Japanese: その女性には広美と同じくらいの年頃の娘がいるらしく、小さな時からずっと病院で暮らしていると言うとひどく同情してくれて、ハンカチで何度も目元を拭っていた。それが運転しながらのことだったので、広美はどうにも落ち着かなかった。
English: The woman apparently has a daughter about Hiromi’s age. When Hiromi says that she has lived in the hospital since childhood, the woman is deeply moved and repeatedly wipes her eyes with a handkerchief. Since she does this while driving, Hiromi cannot relax.

Japanese: そして駅につくと、頼みもしないのに行き先を聞くとそこまでの切符を広美の代わりに買ってくれる。
English: At the station, the woman asks Hiromi’s destination and, without having been requested, buys her a ticket all the way there.

Japanese: 「帰ったら、思う存分ご両親に甘えるのよ」
English: “When you arrive, let your parents spoil you to your heart’s content.”

Japanese: 別れ際に真っ赤な目で手を握ってくるその女性に、広美はぎこちない微笑みを返した。
English: At their parting, the red-eyed woman takes Hiromi’s hand. Hiromi gives her an awkward smile in return.

Japanese: ガラガラの電車に乗り込むと、広美はさっき貰った饅頭を食べながらぼんやり窓の外を見た。
English: After boarding the nearly empty train, Hiromi eats the manju she received and gazes vaguely through the window.

Japanese: 流れゆく景色を眺めていると昔のことを思い出す。
English: The passing landscape calls back memories of long ago.

Japanese: 小さな頃、よく両親に連れられて電車で出かけたものだ。
English: When she was small, her parents often took her on outings by train.

Japanese: 広美はバンザイするような格好で、右手では母親の手を握り、左手はまだ赤ん坊だった妹をおぶった父親の手を握っている。そして満面の笑みを浮かべて、とめどもなく何かを喋っていたんだ。興奮のまま、ただでさえ幼児特有のとりとめのない言葉が、ますます本人以外にはわからないものになって、「ねえ？　ねえ？」と訊ねるたび両親は答えられずに苦笑していた。
English: Hiromi would stand like a child cheering with both arms raised, her right hand holding her mother’s and her left clasping the hand of her father, who carried her baby sister upon his back. A tremendous smile covered Hiromi’s face as she talked without end. In her excitement, the already rambling speech of a small child became still more incomprehensible to anyone but herself. Each time she demanded, ‘Right? Right?’ her parents could only smile helplessly, unable to answer.

Japanese: あれはどこへ行こうとしていたんだろう？　遊園地だったっけな。そうだ、あの時はどの乗り物よりも、どのキャラクターよりも、甘いキャラメルのかかったポップコーンを買って貰って食べるが楽しみで仕方なかった。それから白とピンクで綺麗に飾られた棒付きの飴。
English: Where had they been going that day? Was it an amusement park? Yes. More than any ride or character, she had been beside herself with anticipation for the sweet caramel-coated popcorn they would buy her. And then there was the beautifully decorated white-and-pink lollipop.

Japanese: あの頃は不安も恐ろしいものもなく、何もかも輝いて見えていたっけ。
English: In those days, she had known no anxiety and nothing frightening. Everything had seemed to shine.

Japanese: 誕生日とクリスマスもとても楽しかった。
English: Birthdays and Christmas had been wonderful too.

Japanese: 大好きな苺の乗ったケーキにローソクを立てて吹き消して、砂糖菓子で出来た人形や、メッセージの書かれたチョコレートは全部独占して、そうすると妹が泣くので半分だけ分けてあげて、母が作った骨のところを銀紙で覆って掴めるようにした鶏の唐揚げを食べて、サイダーを飲んで。
English: She would put candles into a cake topped with her beloved strawberries and blow them out; claim all the sugar figures and the chocolate plaque with its written message; give half to her little sister when that made her cry; eat the fried chicken her mother prepared, each bone wrapped in foil to make it easy to hold; and drink soda.

Japanese: 自分にそんな記憶があったのをすっかり忘れていた。病院にいるときはちっとも思い出さなかった。毎日真っ白な建物のなかで、恐ろしいものが見えて、恐ろしい声が聞こえて、調子が悪いとトイレにも行けなくなってそのあたりに粗相をしてしまったり、特別な鍵がないと脱ぐことが出来ない服を着せられたりして、でもそれが当たり前だった。
English: She had completely forgotten that such memories existed within her. Not once had she recalled them inside the hospital. Every day, inside that perfectly white building, she saw frightening things and heard frightening voices. When her condition was poor, she could not even reach the bathroom and would soil herself wherever she stood. They dressed her in clothing she could not remove without a special key. Yet all of it had felt ordinary.

Japanese: 家族のことも、ほとんど思い出すこともなかった。
English: She had scarcely remembered her family either.

Japanese: それは全部病気のせいで、今はもうそれが治った。ポシェットのなかには、二週間後にうつ薬と注射を入れて貰った。使ったらまた貰いに行って、使い続けていればもうずっと病院に戻らなくて済むそうだ。
English: That had all been the illness, and now it was cured. Inside her shoulder bag, they had placed a dose of medicine to inject two weeks later and a syringe. Once she uses it, she can return for another. They told her that if she continues using it, she will never have to return to the hospital.

Japanese: （私は、本当の自分に戻れるんだ……）
English: (I can return to my real self...)

Japanese: また学校にも行きたい。症状が頻発するようになってからいじめられるようになったが、それまでは楽しくやっていたし、学校が好きだった。嫌いな授業はなかったし、給食の時間は楽しかった。友だちと一緒に帰るのも楽しかった。この年から行ける学校はあるんだろうか？
English: She wants to attend school again. The other children had begun bullying her once her episodes became frequent, but before then, she had enjoyed herself and loved school. There had been no subject she disliked. Lunchtime was fun. Walking home with her friends was fun. Was there any school she could attend starting at her present age?

Japanese: 電車の振動が、車窓から見える景色が、彼女の心を刺激するのか。まるでパンドラの箱を開けたかのように次から次へと子供時代の記憶が飛び出してくる。
English: Perhaps the vibrations of the train and the landscape beyond the window stimulate her mind. As if she had opened Pandora’s box, memories of childhood spring forth one after another.

Japanese: めくるめく感情と記憶の奔流にほとんど目眩を感じてくらくらしているうちに、広美は目指す駅に辿り着いていた。
English: Almost dizzy beneath the dazzling torrent of emotion and memory, Hiromi finds that she has arrived at her destination.

Japanese: 家族は昔広美が住んでいた頃から引っ越していない。駅前の風景にはところどころ見覚えがあった。
English: Her family has not moved since the days when she lived with them. Parts of the neighborhood before the station look familiar.

Japanese: いつもお菓子を買って貰っていたコンビニエンスストアー。買い物のついでに季節の衣類をよく出していたクリーニング店には、あのころとほとんど変わらないきついパーマのかかった無愛想な女店員が立っている。
English: There is the convenience store where her parents always bought her sweets. At the dry cleaner where they often dropped off seasonal clothing while out shopping, the same unfriendly woman with the tight perm stands behind the counter, looking almost unchanged from those days.

Japanese: はじめは携帯の地図を頼りに歩いていたが、家に近づくにつれてもやがはれるように記憶が鮮明になり、必要がなくなった。
English: At first, Hiromi walks with the map on her phone as a guide. As she approaches her house, however, her memories sharpen as though a fog has lifted, and she no longer needs it.

Japanese: 友だちと泥遊びをした公園の前を通り過ぎ、虫を捕まえた空き地は今はマンションになっていて、その前の角を曲がる。広美は早足になり、胸の鼓動は興奮で高鳴った。
English: She passes the park where she made mud pies with her friends. The vacant lot where she caught insects has become an apartment building. She turns at the corner beyond it. Hiromi quickens her pace, her heart pounding with excitement.

Japanese: そして、記憶のなかの自分の家の前に辿り着いて立ち止まると、手に握りしめた携帯電話から『目的の場所に到着しました』というアナウンスが流れる。
English: Then she reaches the house from her memories and stops before it. From the phone clenched in her hand comes an announcement: ‘You have arrived at your destination.’

Japanese: 建物は広美の記憶とは変わっていたが、その表札にはしっかりと『UCHIDA』という文字があった。
English: The building has changed from what Hiromi remembers, but the nameplate clearly reads ‘UCHIDA.’

Japanese: 広美はゴクリと喉を鳴らして生唾を飲み込んだ。
English: Hiromi’s throat works as she swallows nervously.

Japanese: Y地区の憂鬱な曇り空に慣れた広美にとって、その青空と太陽の輝きはあまりにも鮮やかに目に沁みた。
English: After growing accustomed to the dreary overcast skies of Y District, Hiromi found the blue sky and the brilliance of the sun almost painfully vivid.

Japanese: アスファルトの上に濃い影をくっきりと作り出す強い日差しの下、彼女はそろそろと手を持ち上げて、インターフォンのボタンにその指先を触れる。
English: Beneath the fierce sunlight, which cast dense, sharp-edged shadows upon the asphalt, she slowly raised her hand and touched the tip of one finger to the intercom button.

Japanese: プラスチックの艶やかな感触を一差し指に感じる。
English: The sleek plastic pressed against her index fingertip.

Japanese: この目の前の、どこにでもある普通の一軒屋のなかに、広美にとってたったひとつの家庭がある。
English: Inside this ordinary detached house before her—one like any other—was the only family Hiromi had.

Japanese: もう何年も、全く別の生活を送ってきた彼らだが、身体に流れる血のつながりと、昔の思い出は共有しており、誰にも拭い去ることは出来ない。
English: They had lived entirely separate lives for years now, but they shared the blood in their veins and the memories of long ago, and no one could wipe those away.

Japanese: 今この指にほんの少しの力を入れるだけで、それぞれの生活を隔てて来た見えない壁が崩れ去り、お互いの生活のなかにお互いが姿を現すのだ。
English: The slightest pressure from this finger would bring down the invisible wall that had divided their lives. Each would appear once more within the life of the other.

Japanese: 広美は緊張して喉をごくりとならしたが、口の中はからからに乾いて飲み込むものはなかった。
English: Hiromi swallowed nervously, though her mouth was so dry that there was nothing to swallow.

Japanese: 風が吹き、木の葉がざわざわと擦れ合う音が聞こえる。車が通り過ぎるエンジンの音が聞こえる。
English: The wind blew, and she heard leaves rustling against one another. She heard the engine of a passing car.

Japanese: 広美は指をインターフォンから離し、溜息をついた。
English: Hiromi drew her finger away from the intercom and sighed.

Japanese: さっきまであんなに楽しみにしていたのに、いざとなると勇気が出ない。
English: She had been looking forward to this so desperately only moments before. Now that the moment had come, she could not find the courage.

Japanese: 彼女はまったく、今の家族たちの様子を知らないのだ。少し、どんな風だか見てみようと、敷地を取り囲む生け垣に沿って歩きながら家の様子をうかがった。
English: She knew nothing at all about what her family was like now. Thinking that she would take just a brief look, Hiromi walked along the hedge surrounding the property and peered toward the house.

Japanese: 側面にまわったところで背伸びをして覗き込むと、庭の光景が目に入る。
English: When she reached the side, she stood on tiptoe and looked over it. The garden came into view.

Japanese: 一畳ほどの小さな家庭菜園があって、ミニトマトが実っている。庭の隅にこんもりと小さく盛り上がった上に『クロ』と書かれた板が刺さっているのはペットの墓でもつくったんだろうか。縁側に上がるところには、サンダルが二足ならんでいる。
English: A little kitchen garden, no more than the size of one tatami mat, held miniature tomatoes. In one corner of the yard, a board marked ‘KURO’ stood upon a small mound of earth. Had they made a grave for a pet? Two pairs of sandals sat side by side below the veranda.

Japanese: そしてガラスのサッシの向こうには、リビングルームの様子が見えた。
English: Beyond the glass doors, she could see into the living room.

Japanese: はっきりした木目が浮かび上がったキャメルのフローリングに白い壁のシンプルな洋室。大きな液晶テレビ。ニスで艶光りする木製の棚の上には、写真立てが並べられている。壁に掛かった賞状は妹が学校でとったものだろうか。ここからではその文字までは読めない。
English: It was a simple Western-style room, with white walls and camel-colored flooring whose grain stood out clearly. There was a large flat-screen television. Framed photographs lined the top of a varnished wooden cabinet. Had her sister won the certificate hanging on the wall at school? Hiromi could not read the words from here.

Japanese: そして中央に設置された六人掛けのテーブルの上には、サラダの入った大きなボウルと、口のところが銀紙のようなものでパッケージされた飲み物の瓶とグラス、そして白いホールケーキがあった。
English: Upon the table set for six in the center of the room sat a large bowl of salad, glasses and a bottle whose mouth was sealed in something like silver foil, and an entire white cake.

Japanese: それを見た時広美の胸はざわついた。
English: The sight sent a restless stirring through Hiromi’s chest.

Japanese: 誰かの誕生日パーティをやろうとしているのだろうか。それは、父親か、母親か、それとも妹か。
English: Were they about to hold a birthday party for someone? Was it her father, her mother, or her sister?

Japanese: 思い出そうとしてみたけれど、今日が何日かわからない。携帯電話で確認してから、それ以前に家族の誕生日を誰一人として知らないことに気がついた。
English: She tried to remember, but she did not know the date. After checking it on her phone, she realized that she did not know the birthday of a single member of her family in the first place.

Japanese: 誰もいなかったその部屋に、奥のキッチンから一人の人物が現れた。
English: A person emerged from the kitchen at the back of the empty room.

Japanese: それは紛れもない母の姿だった。髪型を変え、少し老けて印象が変わっていたが一目でそうとわかった。
English: It was unmistakably her mother. She had changed her hairstyle and aged a little, altering her appearance, but Hiromi knew her at a glance.

Japanese: 母は両手にお盆を持ち、その上に今日の料理を盛った皿を乗せていた。
English: Her mother carried a tray in both hands, with plates laden with food for the occasion arranged upon it.

Japanese: 予期していたはずなのに、それはあまりにも突然の邂逅に感じられた。広美は心臓が止まりそうな思いをしながらとっさに姿を生け垣に隠し、その葉の隙間からなかの様子をこっそりと覗く。
English: Although Hiromi should have expected it, the encounter felt overwhelmingly sudden. Her heart nearly stopped. She ducked behind the hedge on instinct and secretly watched the room through the gaps between its leaves.

Japanese: 母はこちらに気づくことなく、皿をテーブルの上に並べている。
English: Her mother noticed nothing and began arranging the plates upon the table.

Japanese: そしてすぐにもう一人の人物が別のドアを開けて部屋のなかに入って来た。少し腹が突き出て、頭髪が寂しくなっているがそれは父だった。
English: Another person soon opened a different door and entered the room. His stomach protruded slightly and his hair had grown thin, but it was her father.

Japanese: 父は両手にリボンでラッピングされた箱を持っており、母に見せると二人で笑い合う。言葉を交わしたのちに、箱をテレビの裏に隠した。あれで、今日の主役を驚かせようと言うのだ。
English: Her father held a ribbon-wrapped box in both hands. He showed it to her mother, and the two of them laughed together. After exchanging a few words, he hid the box behind the television. They intended to surprise the guest of honor with it.

Japanese: そう、今日は妹の誕生日で、家族はそれを盛りあげるための準備をしているに違いない。
English: Yes—today must be her sister’s birthday, and the family must be preparing to celebrate.

Japanese: 父は落ち着かない様子のままソファーに座り、新聞を手に取ったり戻したりしていた。その足元にはいつのまにか部屋に入っていた小さな毛むくじゃらの犬がじゃれつき、父はそれを抱き上げる。
English: Her father sat restlessly upon the sofa, picking up the newspaper only to put it down again. A little shaggy dog that had slipped into the room at some point played around his feet, and he lifted it into his arms.

Japanese: 広美は凍り付いたようにそのガラスを隔てた絵に描いたような平和な光景に見入っていた。
English: Hiromi stood frozen, staring through the glass at a scene of perfect peace, as though it had been painted there.

Japanese: それは、広美が発症する前にこの家にあった光景だ。そして、広美が発症してからはこのように完全にくつろいだ光景はなかった。本来ならここに自分も居たのだろうか？　いや、あのまま自分がここにいたら、彼らはこのように笑う日は来なかったかもしれない。自分がいなくなることで、彼らはこの幸福を作れたのだろう。でも、今の自分なら？
English: It was the kind of scene this house had held before Hiromi’s onset. Afterward, there had never again been such perfect ease. Should she rightfully have been there among them? No. Had she remained, perhaps a day when they could smile this way would never have come. Perhaps they had created this happiness because she was gone. But what about her as she was now?

Japanese: 胸がどきどきとして、おかしな汗がこめかみを伝う。
English: Her heart pounded. A strange sweat ran down her temples.

Japanese: 母はケーキの上に小さな蝋燭を並べ、父がそれにライターで火をつける。全ての着火が終わると、部屋の電気は消され、カーテンが閉められた。そして、妹を呼ぶ父の声が聞こえる。
English: Her mother arranged small candles upon the cake, and her father lit them with a lighter. Once every flame was burning, they switched off the lights and closed the curtains. Then she heard her father call for her sister.

Japanese: 広美は閉め出されたような格好でしばらくそこに立っていたが、すぐに移動して部屋のなかを見られる場所を探す。
English: Hiromi stood there for a moment as though she had been shut out. Then she moved at once, searching for somewhere else from which she could see into the room.

Japanese: 別の壁に小さな窓があり、生け垣の土台となっているブロックの上に上れば、なんとかそこからテーブルの近くを見ることが出来た。
English: There was a small window in another wall. By climbing onto the blocks forming the hedge’s foundation, she could just manage to see the area around the table.

Japanese: そして、ちょうど自分の席に座ろうとしている妹の姿が見えた。
English: There she saw her sister, just as the girl was about to take her seat.

Japanese: 彼女は、一目でそうとわかった両親とは違い、記憶のなかよりもずっと成長して、まるで別人のようだった。街で偶然見かけてもその顔立ちだけでは気がつかないかもしれない。でも、もしかしたら、と振り返りはするだろう。
English: Unlike their parents, whom Hiromi had recognized at once, her sister had grown so much from the child in Hiromi’s memories that she seemed almost another person. Had they passed by chance upon the street, her features alone might not have been enough. Yet Hiromi might still have turned and wondered.

Japanese: なぜなら、幸せそうに目を輝かせる彼女の顔の半分には、この幸福そのものの光景にはあまりにも不似合いなみにくい焼けどのあとがあったからだ。
English: For half of that happy, shining-eyed face was covered by an ugly burn scar, grotesquely out of place amid the happiness of the scene itself.

Japanese: 「あっ」
English: “Ah—”

Japanese: 広美の身体ががくがくと震え、その拍子に足をすべらせてブロック塀から落ちてアスファルトに尻餅をつく。
English: Hiromi’s body began to shake violently. Her foot slipped from the block wall, and she fell backward onto the asphalt.

Japanese: そして立ち上がると、駆け出した。どこへ行こうというつもりもなく、とにかくこの場を離れたかった。その顔は蒼白で、引きつっていた。
English: Then she rose and ran. She had no destination in mind; she simply had to get away. Her face was bloodless and drawn tight.

Japanese: インターフォンなど押せるわけがない。自分が、あの幸せな誕生日パーティを邪魔出来るだろうか？　あのささやかな幸せを取り戻した家庭に戻れるだろうか？　あの妹の顔に消えない痣を作ったのは自分なのだ。
English: She could never press that intercom. How could she intrude upon that happy birthday party? How could she return to a family that had recovered this modest happiness? She was the one who had left that permanent scar upon her sister’s face.

Japanese: （どうして忘れていたんだろう？　どうしてなの？　戻れるわけなんかないじゃないか！）
English: (How could I have forgotten? How? Of course I can never go back!)

Japanese: 走る広美の目に涙が浮かんで丸いたまとなり、それが崩れるようにボロボロと頬の上を流れ落ちた。
English: Tears swelled into round drops as Hiromi ran, then broke loose and streamed down her cheeks.

Japanese: 家で暮らしていた最後の日々、広美は完全に別の世界の住人となっていた。
English: During her final days at home, Hiromi had become a resident of another world entirely.

Japanese: 一緒に住む二人の大人と一人の幼児は、見た目は家族にそっくりだが、その正体はまったく別の恐ろしいものだ。きっと宇宙人に違いない。いつのまにか入れ替わって、自分をいつも見張っている。そして大事なものを奪おうとしているんだ。
English: The two adults and the small child who lived with her looked exactly like her family, but beneath those appearances they were something else—something terrible. They had to be aliens. At some point they had replaced her real family and begun watching her constantly. They meant to take away everything precious to her.

Japanese: 宇宙人は火に弱いと、別の声が教えてくれる。その声はいつも優しくて、広美を肯定してくれる天使の声だから信用出来る。火を使って、宇宙人を追い出せば優しい両親と、かわいい妹が帰ってきてくれるんだ。早くあの懐かしい家族に会いたい！
English: Another voice told her that aliens were weak against fire. It was always gentle, always affirmed her, and therefore had to be the voice of an angel. She could trust it. If she used fire to drive the aliens out, her kind parents and adorable little sister would return. She wanted to see that beloved family again as soon as possible.

Japanese: 夜にこっそり起き出すと雑誌をちぎって紙切れをうずたかく山にした。広美の症状が出るようになってからライターはみな鍵付きの戸棚に仕舞われていたが、この日のために来客がハンガーにかけたジャケットからひとつ抜き取ってある。それを使って、紙くずに火をつけた。さっき父親が蝋燭に火をつけたように。メラメラと炎があがり、臭い煙が立ち上って部屋に充満する。火災警報器がけたたましい音を立てる。恍惚の表情で炎を眺めていた広美はその音でビクッと肩をふるわし、部屋を飛び出る。
English: Late at night she had crept from bed, torn apart magazines, and piled the scraps of paper high. Ever since her symptoms began, every lighter in the house had been locked in a cabinet. In preparation for this day, however, she had stolen one from the jacket a visitor left hanging by the door. She used it to set fire to the paper, just as her father had lit the candles moments ago. Flames leapt upward and foul smoke rose, filling the room. The fire alarm began to shriek. Hiromi had been gazing into the flames in ecstasy, but the sound made her shoulders jerk and sent her rushing from the room.

Japanese: 「あの音を止めて！　宇宙語で私の悪口を言っているの！」
English: “Make that noise stop! It’s saying terrible things about me in alien language!”

Japanese: 一度も思い出したことがないその光景が、ありありと広美の脳裏に蘇った。その夜すこし肌寒かったことや、隣の犬が狂ったように吠えていたことも思い出した。
English: The scene, which had never returned to her before, came back to Hiromi with perfect clarity. She even remembered that the night had been slightly cold and that the neighbor’s dog had barked like mad.

Japanese: そうだ自分は散々迷惑をかけて、その挙げ句に焼き殺そうとしたんだ。結果妹は顔に消えない痣を作った。女の子が顔にあんな痣を作って、どれだけつらい人生を送ってきたのだろうか。全て自分がやったんだ。
English: Yes. She had caused them endless misery and then, at the end of it all, tried to burn them to death. Her sister had been left with a permanent scar across her face. What kind of painful life must a girl have endured with a scar like that? Hiromi had done all of it.

Japanese: たとえ病気のせいとはいえ、言い訳出来るようなものではない。もう症状が消えましたと、何食わぬ顔で家に戻ることなんか出来るはずもない。
English: Even if illness had caused it, there was no excuse she could possibly make. She could never stroll back into the house with an innocent face and announce that her symptoms were gone.

Japanese: あの頃みたいに、妹は怯えて引きつった顔でこちらを見、両親は何かあるたびまた無茶苦茶なことをするのではないかとビクビクと怯えて暮らすことになるのだろう。
English: Her sister would look at her with the same frightened, rigid expression as before. Her parents would spend their lives cowering, afraid that every small event might drive her to do something senseless again.

Japanese: そもそも本当に症状が消えたのか？　こんな大事なことを忘れて、すっかり元通りになれると信じていただなんて、どう考えたって普通じゃない。
English: Were her symptoms truly gone in the first place? She had forgotten something this important, yet believed completely that she could simply return to how she had been. No matter how she considered it, that was not normal.

Japanese: 広美は泣きながら、やみくもに走った。
English: Hiromi ran blindly, weeping.

Japanese: それから先自分がどこをどう行動したのか覚えていない。
English: She remembered nothing of where she went or what she did afterward.

Japanese: ただ気がつけば雨でびしょ濡れになって、Y地区に居た。うなだれ、どこともわからない通りを歩いている。酔っ払った客が時々何か下品な言葉をかけてくるが、世界の果てで囁いているようで耳に入ってこない。いまの広美にとって、周囲で起きている全てのことが地球の裏側の出来事のように遠かった。
English: When awareness returned, she was drenched by rain and back in Y District. Her head hung low as she walked along a street she did not recognize. Drunken customers occasionally called something vulgar to her, but the words seemed whispered from the end of the world and never reached her ears. Everything happening around her felt as distant as an event upon the opposite side of the earth.

Japanese: 動揺はしていない。気持ちはもう大分落ち着いていた。
English: She was no longer distraught. Her emotions had already settled considerably.

Japanese: 結局、自分のことばかり考えていたんだ。相手のことを考えたり、想像したりすることが出来なかった。だから実際相手の暮らしを見るまで何も気づかなかった。
English: In the end, she had thought only of herself. She had been unable to consider the other people involved, or even imagine their lives. Not until she saw those lives for herself had she understood anything.

Japanese: 彼らの暮らしは自分とは余りに違った。病院でわがままに暮らし、そして世話してくれた人たちの血みどろの亡骸をそれほどの感情もなく踏み越え、今度は家族と元通り幸せに暮らそうだなんて、そんな都合のいいことがどうして思えよう？
English: Their lives were too different from hers. She had lived selfishly in the hospital, stepped over the blood-soaked bodies of the people who cared for her with scarcely any emotion, and then imagined that she could return to a happy life with her family as though nothing had happened. How could she ever have entertained such a convenient fantasy?

Japanese: （ああ、本当に、私は恩知らずだった）
English: (Oh, I truly was ungrateful.)

Japanese: そう、病院では本当に優しくしてもらえていたんだ。その彼らがあんな無惨に殺されて、ちょっとショックだったけれど、その程度しか悲しまないのはいくらなんでもおかしい。
English: Yes. The people at the hospital had treated her with genuine kindness. They had been slaughtered so brutally, yet she had felt only a little shock. Surely there was something wrong in grieving no more than that.

Japanese: 「ノミさん、ノミさん」
English: “Ms. No-mi, Ms. No-mi.”

Japanese: 広美はことあるごとにそう呟いて看護師の能見美紗を頼った。その名前を呼べば、つらくて怖いときでも何でもしてくれると思ったからだ。
English: Whenever anything happened, Hiromi murmured those words and turned to the nurse Misa Nomi. She believed that if she called the name, Ms. Nomi would do anything for her whenever she was suffering or afraid.

Japanese: 「ノミさん、ノミさん」
English: “Ms. No-mi, Ms. No-mi.”

Japanese: 「ノミじゃないって。の・う・み」
English: “Not No-mi. No-o-mi.”

Japanese: その日は一日中調子が悪く、ずっとその名を繰り返していた。能見はそのたびにやって来て、苦笑いをしながらそう訂正する。
English: Hiromi had been unwell all day and had repeated the name without end. Each time, Nomi came to her and corrected her with a wry smile.

Japanese: 「ノミさん、ノミさん……」
English: “Ms. No-mi, Ms. No-mi...”

Japanese: 広美はあふれでる涙を拭いながらそう訴える。現実に何かされたとか、そういうわけではないのだ。恐ろしいものが見えて、恐ろしい声が聞こえて、ただ怖くてたまらない。
English: Hiromi pleaded with her that way as she wiped away overflowing tears. No one had actually done anything to her. She saw terrifying things and heard terrifying voices, and she was simply too frightened to bear it.

Japanese: 「あのね、の・うぅぅぅぅ・み」
English: “Listen. No-oooo-mi.”

Japanese: 「ノミさん……」
English: “Ms. No-mi...”

Japanese: 能見は広美が繰り返す言葉に、溜息をついて訂正を諦めた。
English: Nomi sighed at the word Hiromi repeated and gave up correcting her.

Japanese: そうやって能見が接している間は少し落ち着くが、離れれば声が高く大きくなって、それに耐えかねた患者たちが苦情をいれる。
English: While Nomi stayed with her, Hiromi calmed a little. Whenever Nomi left, however, her voice grew higher and louder until the other patients could bear it no longer and complained.

Japanese: それを何度か繰り返していると、医師の太刀川が病室までやって来た。そうして、興奮状態の広美の目をチラリと見ると、
English: After this happened several times, Dr. Tachikawa came to the room. He gave the agitated Hiromi’s eyes a brief glance.

Japanese: 「駄目ですね。拘束の準備をしてください」
English: “No. This won’t do. Prepare the restraints.”

Japanese: と、助手の林田に指示を出した。
English: He gave the order to his assistant, Hayashida.

Japanese: そして広美は病室から観察室へつれてゆかれると、ベッドにベルトで手足を縛り付けられ、点滴の針を刺される。点滴にはタイプBの精神症状に効果があると言われている新薬が含まれている。広美は点滴を自分で引き抜いてしまうため、いつも拘束が必要だった。
English: Hiromi was taken from her room to the observation room, where her arms and legs were strapped to a bed and an IV needle inserted. The infusion contained a new drug said to be effective against psychiatric symptoms associated with Type B. Hiromi would pull out the IV herself, so she always had to be restrained.

Japanese: 広美はそうされている間、特に抵抗はしない。何度も拘束されている広美は特に拘束を嫌がる気持ちもなかったし、そもそも自分が縛られているということを理解出来る状況でもなかった。
English: Hiromi did not resist as they did this. She had been restrained so many times that she felt no particular aversion to it, and she was not in a state to understand that she was tied down in the first place.

Japanese: 観察室は患者たちの居住するスペースとは鍵の付いたドアで隔てられており、看護室のすぐ隣にある。
English: A locked door separated the observation room from the patients’ living area. It stood immediately beside the nurses’ station.

Japanese: 部屋には予備のマットレスなどが積まれているが、他にはなにもなく、静かで情報量の少ない部屋だ。そこで二時間ほど過ごすと薬の効果もあったのか大分落ち着いて来たが、太刀川の指示では明日まで点滴を続けるということだったのでそのまま観察室で一晩を過ごすことにになっている。
English: Spare mattresses and similar items were stacked inside, but otherwise the room was empty, quiet, and nearly free of stimulation. After about two hours, perhaps partly because of the medicine, Hiromi had settled considerably. Tachikawa’s instructions called for the IV to continue until the following day, however, so she was to spend the night in the observation room.

Japanese: そして、退勤間際の能見が様子を見にやって来た。彼女は汗の噴き出た広美の顔を固く絞ったひんやりとするタオルで拭い、それからおむつを確認すると便が付着していたので交換した。
English: Just before the end of her shift, Nomi came to check on her. She wiped Hiromi’s sweating face with a cool, tightly wrung towel, then checked her diaper. Finding that it was soiled, she changed it.

Japanese: 「ありがとう、ノミさん……」
English: “Thank you, Ms. No-mi...”

Japanese: 広美が言うと、
English: When Hiromi said this,

Japanese: 「大分よくなったみたいだね。よかった」
English: “You seem much better now. I’m glad.”

Japanese: 能見は嬉しそうに笑った。
English: Nomi smiled happily.

Japanese: 「ノミさん。のどかわいた。ジュースが飲みたい」
English: “Ms. No-mi. I’m thirsty. I want juice.”

Japanese: 「まあ、落ち着いたと思ったらすぐそんなこと言って。……ジュースはないから、お水でもいい？」
English: “My, the moment you calm down, you start asking for things. We don’t have juice. Would water do?”

Japanese: 広美が頷くと、能見は吸い飲みに水を入れて飲ませてくれる。
English: When Hiromi nodded, Nomi filled a feeding cup with water and helped her drink.

Japanese: 「広美ちゃん、ひとつお願いがあるんだ」
English: “Hiromi, there’s one thing I’d like you to do for me.”

Japanese: 水を飲み終わった広美の顔を見つめながら、能見は語りかけるように言った。
English: Nomi gazed into Hiromi’s face once she had finished drinking and spoke to her gently.

Japanese: 「ずっと先、私がお婆ちゃんになって、死んじゃったりしたらね。そしたらお葬式に来て、泣いてくれない？　それで、能見さんは本当に頑張って仕事をしてくれたいい人だって、嘘でもいいから褒めてほしいの」
English: “A long, long time from now, when I’ve become an old woman and I die... will you come to my funeral and cry for me? And will you tell everyone that Ms. Nomi was a good person who worked terribly hard? You can lie. I don’t mind.”

Japanese: 能見がそんなことを言うのは初めてだった。
English: Nomi had never said anything like this before.

Japanese: 広美は目をぱちくりさせて聞いている。
English: Hiromi listened, blinking in surprise.

Japanese: 「能見さんの家族はね、私がこの仕事をやるのをあんまり喜んでないの。だから、広美ちゃんが仕事頑張ってたんですよーって褒めて泣いてくれればね。ああ、あいつも立派な仕事してたんだなって思ってくれるかなって」
English: “You see, Ms. Nomi’s family isn’t very happy about her doing this work. So if you cried for me and told them, ‘She worked so hard,’ maybe they’d think, ‘Oh, so she did respectable work after all.’”

Japanese: 能見は微笑みながら言う。
English: Nomi spoke with a smile.

Japanese: 「私はこうやってみんなのために働くのは素敵な仕事だと思ってるんだけど、みんなは誤解してて……だから、分かって欲しいの」
English: “I think working for all of you this way is a wonderful job. But everyone misunderstands it... and I want them to understand.”

Japanese: そう言ってから、少し黙って広美の顔を見つめると、
English: After saying this, she fell silent for a moment and looked into Hiromi’s face.

Japanese: 「あはは、無茶なこと言ってるよね。でも、今日は私一日中広美ちゃんにつきっきりだったんだから、これくらい言わせてもらうからね」
English: “Ahaha. I’m asking something impossible, aren’t I? But I’ve spent the whole day looking after you, so let me ask this much of you.”

Japanese: 最後に広美の頭を撫でて、彼女は部屋を出て行った。
English: She stroked Hiromi’s head one last time, then left the room.

Japanese: 彼女は仕事だったから優しくしてくれたのかもしれない。でも、あんな状態になった自分のことは、家族だって見捨てたんだ。学校でもいじめられた。
English: Perhaps Nomi had been kind only because it was her job. But even Hiromi’s family had abandoned her once she became that way. At school, she had been bullied.

Japanese: 職員にはいじわるで嫌いな人もいたけれども、優しくしてくれた人もたくさん居たんだ。
English: Some members of staff had been cruel, and Hiromi had hated them. Many others, however, had treated her with kindness.

Japanese: （でも、もうみんな死んでしまった）
English: (But now they’re all dead.)

Japanese: 目を剥いて血の海に倒れていた能見の姿を思い出すと、また涙が溢れ出た。
English: When she remembered Nomi lying wide-eyed in a pool of blood, the tears spilled out once more.

Japanese: 広美はよろめくような足取りで街の外れまで歩き、病院を見た。入り口は閉鎖されて入れなくなっている。人気はなく、灰色の建物がじっと雨に打たれている。
English: Hiromi staggered to the edge of the district and found herself before the hospital. Its entrance had been sealed, and she could no longer enter. No one was there. The gray building stood motionless beneath the rain.

Japanese: それをじっと見上げてから、また街の方へ戻った。
English: After gazing up at it for some time, she turned back toward the city.

Japanese: 八龍会は何かあったら連絡をしてくれと言っていたが、今更患者の皆が暮らしているアパートに行こうとは思わない。
English: Hachiryukai had told her to contact them if anything happened, but she could no longer imagine returning to the apartments where the other patients lived.

Japanese: 病気から救ってくれるつもりだったのだろうけれど、そのためにあんなにたくさんの人を殺す必要はあったんだろうか？　そんなにいい薬があるのなら、病院の人に説明して使って貰えばよかったじゃないか。
English: Perhaps they had meant to save everyone from illness. But had that truly required killing so many people? If they possessed medicine that good, why couldn’t they have explained it to the hospital staff and asked them to use it?

Japanese: （そもそも、病気なんか治らなくたって良かったんだ。それなら、いやなことを思い出して、こんなにつらくならないで済んだのに）
English: (It would have been better if I had never been cured at all. Then I wouldn’t have remembered anything terrible, and I wouldn’t have had to suffer like this.)

Japanese: 歩き疲れた広美は塀を背に座り込んだ。そういえば、食事もとっていない。現金はいくらか残っているはずだが、買うのも食べるのも億劫だった。
English: Exhausted from walking, Hiromi sat with her back against a wall. Come to think of it, she had eaten nothing. She should still have had some cash, but buying food and eating it both felt like too much trouble.

Japanese: （このままずっと薬を貰いに行かなければ、また病気になるっていってたっけ。きっと私はそれでいいんだ。こんなにいろいろと考える頭なんかいらない。ばかのままでいればいいんだ）
English: (They said I’d become ill again if I never went back for more medicine, didn’t they? Maybe that would be best. I don’t need a head that thinks about all these things. I should stay stupid.)

Japanese: 広美はめそめそと失われたもののことばかりを考えた。
English: Hiromi whimpered as her thoughts circled everything she had lost.

Japanese: もう前向きに動くための一切の原動力が失われていた。
English: She had lost every impulse that might have moved her forward.

Japanese: そこに、一人の人物が声をかけたのだ。
English: It was then that someone spoke to her.

Japanese: 「おいどうした。お嬢ちゃん、こんなところで座り込んでいたら風邪をひくぜ」
English: “Hey, what’s wrong? Little lady, you’ll catch your death sitting out here.”

Japanese: 顔を上げるとひげ面の白人男性が酒臭い息を漂わせている。
English: When she raised her face, a bearded white man stood over her, his breath reeking of alcohol.

Japanese: 彼女が今座っているのは暗黒通りの片隅だった。Y地区でももっともたちの悪い地域のひとつに、こんな無防備な姿でへたり込んでいることを広美自身は知らなかった。そもそも他人を警戒するという習慣自体が彼女には薄かった。
English: Hiromi was sitting in a corner of Darkness Street. She did not know that she had collapsed utterly defenseless in one of the worst parts of Y District. The habit of guarding herself against other people had scarcely developed in her at all.

Japanese: 「いいんです。風邪なんかひいたって。死にたいくらいだもの」
English: “I don’t care. I don’t care if I catch cold. I want to die anyway.”

Japanese: 「そうか。それは邪魔をしたな」
English: “I see. Sorry to disturb you.”

Japanese: 男は案外あっさりとしたもので、それだけで引き下がると目の前を去っていった。
English: The man withdrew with surprising ease. Having said no more than that, he walked away.

Japanese: 広美はまた顔を伏せる。すると、目の前でまた跫音が聞こえた。さっきの男が帰って来たのかと思ったが、そうではなかった。
English: Hiromi lowered her head once more. Soon she heard footsteps before her. She thought the first man had returned, but it was someone else.

Japanese: 「ほら、立てよ」
English: “Come on. Get up.”

Japanese: 不意に、ぐいと腕を捕まれた。
English: Without warning, a hand seized her arm and pulled.

Japanese: 見ると髪の毛を金色に染めた背の高い男が自分の腕を掴んでいる。広美は突然のことで声が出ない。男の身体は服の上からわかるほど分厚い筋肉がついている。広美はタイプBであり、ネオ・ローズによってその力が解放されてはいた。それでも、もともとが病院で育ったひょろひょろの身体であり、今は衰弱してもいる。確かにみかけよりはずっと力が強かったがとても目の前の男の腕力にはかなわなかった。そして何より、全力を振り絞れるような気力が失われている。
English: A tall man with dyed blond hair was gripping her. The shock left Hiromi unable to speak. His body was packed with thick muscle visible even through his clothing. Hiromi was Type B, and Neo Rose had released her strength. Yet she had begun as a frail girl raised in a hospital, and now she was weak with exhaustion besides. She was certainly much stronger than she looked, but no match for the man’s raw power. More importantly, she no longer possessed the will to summon her full strength.

Japanese: 声を出そうとすると、その丸太のような腕がとんで広美の頬を殴った。
English: When she tried to speak, his loglike arm lashed out and struck her cheek.

Japanese: 「声を出したら殺すぞ」
English: “Make a sound and I’ll kill you.”

Japanese: 男はそう吐き捨てて、無理矢理腕を引っ張って広美を立たせると、ぐいぐいと引っ張りながら歩きはじめる。
English: The man spat out the threat. He hauled Hiromi to her feet by the arm and began walking, dragging her forcefully after him.

Japanese: そして近くの狭い路地に入ると、もう人通りもなく彼らを見咎めるものものいなかった。
English: Once he turned into a narrow alley nearby, there were no longer any passersby to notice, much less intervene.

Japanese: いかに世情にうとい広美でも、自分が恐ろしい窮地に陥っているのははっきりとわかった。ここは病院ではないし、家族ももう自分のことを守ってはくれない。自力では抵抗するすべはないだろう。殴られてチカチカとする視界で状況を見ながらそう思った。
English: However ignorant Hiromi might have been of the world, she understood clearly that she was in terrible danger. This was not the hospital, and her family would no longer protect her. She could see no means of resisting him herself. Through vision still flashing from the blow, she took stock of the situation and reached that conclusion.

Japanese: 人間は完全に自分が無力であることを悟ったとき、逆らうことをやめる。従順にふるまうことで相手に刺激を与えることを避け、少しでも苦痛を減らしてしのごうとする本能だろう。動物でも突然無抵抗になってしまうものもいる。広美もこのときそんな心理が働いて、諦めと同時に抵抗をやめ、男に引かれるまま歩いた。しかし、この本能は一体どの程度の意味があるものなのだろう。無抵抗になった動物はそのまま捕食者に食われるものだし、今回の広美の場合もあまり良い判断だったとは言えない。
English: When people realize that they are completely powerless, they may cease resisting. Perhaps submission is an instinct: by avoiding any further provocation, they try to endure with as little pain as possible. Some animals, too, suddenly become passive. Something of the kind appears to have happened within Hiromi. At the same moment that she surrendered hope, she stopped resisting and walked wherever the man pulled her. Yet how useful can such an instinct truly be? A passive animal may simply be eaten by its predator, and in Hiromi’s case, submission was hardly a sound decision.

Japanese: 相手の男はこの近くに住み、日雇いで肉体労働を行っているものだが、このように女性を強引に連れ去っては乱暴をするのを常習していた。考える能力が足りない彼は、脅した女が従順になるのを見て「女は殴られるのが好きだ」とごく自然に信じていた。女がどんなに逆らっても、殴りつけて、脅して、そうすれば自分を好きになる。恐怖から逃れるために男のために愛想笑いをし、進んで喜ぶことをし、好意があるような態度をとっているなど想像もしなかった。
English: Later accounts describe the man as a nearby resident who performed day labor and habitually abducted women this way before assaulting them. His reasoning was poor, and when a woman became submissive under threat, he took it as perfectly natural proof that women liked being struck. However fiercely a woman resisted, he believed that if he hit and threatened her, she would come to love him. It never occurred to him that she might smile, please him of her own apparent accord, and feign affection only to escape her fear.

Japanese: このY地区においては彼のような人間が特別少ないというわけではない。また現実に、こうした行為を繰り返した結果女の方も男に依存心が生まれ、そのまま結婚してしまうというような救いのない例もある。人間の精神の仕組みの悲しさというべきものだろう。
English: By accounts of Y District at the time, men like him were not especially rare. There were even hopeless cases in which repeated abuse led a woman to depend upon her abuser and ultimately marry him. One might call it a sorrow born of the workings of the human mind.

Japanese: だから男はこの時も自分を疑いはしなかった。広美の態度の軟化を見て、てっきり受け入れられたと感じ、
English: The man therefore appears to have entertained no doubt on this occasion. Seeing Hiromi’s manner soften, he assumed that she had accepted him.

Japanese: 「心配するな。すぐにお前もおれのことを好きになる」
English: “Don’t worry. You’ll like me soon enough.”

Japanese: と言ったのは、嘘でも脅しでもない思ったままの言葉だったのである。
English: The words expressed exactly what he thought. They were neither a lie nor a threat.

Japanese: さて、このままあと十数メートル歩けば彼の住まいに辿り着く。もしそれに連れ込まれていたら、広美はこの街ではごくありふれた不幸を体験することになっていただろう。彼女の不幸続きの人生においてはそうなっても何も不自然はなかったが、今回は奇跡的な幸運が訪れた。
English: A little more than a dozen meters would have brought them to his home. Had he taken her inside, Hiromi would presumably have suffered a misfortune all too common in this district. Nothing in her long succession of unhappiness would have made such an end seem strange. This time, however, extraordinary luck intervened.

Japanese: 「ちょっと待ちな」
English: “Hold it right there.”

Japanese: と声をかけたのは、さきほどの白人男性だった。
English: The speaker was the white man from moments before.

Japanese: やはり心配になって引き返したところで引きずられてゆく広美を見つけたのだろう。
English: Perhaps concern had drawn him back, and he had found Hiromi being dragged away.

Japanese: 「なんだお前」
English: “Who the hell are you?”

Japanese: こちらの男はドスを聞かせた声で相手を威圧した。
English: The blond man lowered his voice, trying to intimidate him.

Japanese: 相手の白人は何がおかしいのかやたらとニヤニヤしている。
English: The white man grinned as though he found something hilarious.

Japanese: 「その子はおれが先約ずみなんだ。返してもらうぜ」
English: “I had a prior claim on the girl. Give her back.”

Japanese: 彼はそう言ったが、こちらは訊ねておきながらもとより会話をするつもりはなかったようだ。
English: He gave this answer, but the blond man had apparently never intended to hold a conversation despite asking the question.

Japanese: その言葉が終わるのも待たずに、またその太い腕を振り回して相手に襲い掛かる。
English: Without waiting for the white man to finish, he swung that thick arm and attacked.

Japanese: 相手の白人もけしてひ弱というわけではなかったが、こちらのゴリラのような男に比べれば大分見劣りする。見た目だけなら到底勝てる見込みはなさそうだが、結果は見た目通りにはならなかった。
English: The white man was by no means frail, but beside this gorilla of a man he looked far less imposing. Judged by appearances alone, he had no chance. Appearances proved deceptive.

Japanese: 二人が近づいた瞬間、ゴツッと鈍い音がして、崩れ落ちたのはこちらの男の方だった。すぐそばにいた広美にも何が起きたのかわからない。筋肉のかたまりのような男が、白目をむいてひっくりかえっている。
English: The instant they came together, there was a dull crack. It was the blond man who collapsed. Even Hiromi, standing immediately beside them, had not seen what happened. The mountain of muscle lay flat upon his back, the whites of his eyes showing.

Japanese: 「おっと、死んではいないよな」
English: “Whoops. I didn’t kill him, did I?”

Japanese: 白人は倒れた男に息があるのを確認してから、その身体を引きずって雨の当たらない場所に運ぶ。
English: The white man checked that the fallen man was breathing, then dragged him somewhere out of the rain.

Japanese: 広美はへたりこんだままその作業を見ていて、逃げるという気持ちも起きなかった。彼女に人並みの警戒心があったなら、ここで逃げるべきだったろう。新しく現れた人物が、彼女にとって信頼出来るものであるという保証などどこにもないのだ。
English: Hiromi remained sitting where she had fallen and watched the work, never thinking to flee. Had she possessed an ordinary degree of caution, this would have been the moment to escape. Nothing guaranteed that the newcomer was someone she could trust.

Japanese: 白人は広美の前に戻ってくると、手を差し伸べた。
English: The white man returned to Hiromi and extended his hand.

Japanese: 広美は一瞬戸惑ったが、結局その手を握る。
English: She hesitated for a moment, but finally took it.

Japanese: 白人は映画で見るようなキザな動作で広美を立たせると、
English: With a showy gesture like something from a movie, the white man helped Hiromi to her feet.

Japanese: 「お嬢ちゃんツイてるな。おれは普段ならこういった真似はしないんだぜ。キリがないし、それにとても冷酷なんだ。たくさんひどいことをしてきた。でも今日は特別だ。ちょっと誰かに優しくしたい気分だったのさ。どういうわけか、おれは月に一度くらいそういう日があってね。……そう怯えることはない。安心しな、きっちりとパパとママがいるあったかいところへ送ってやるぜ」
English: “You’re lucky, little lady. Normally I don’t do things like this. There’d be no end to it, and besides, I’m a very cold man. I’ve done plenty of terrible things. Today’s an exception. I felt like being nice to somebody. For some reason, I have a day like that about once a month. So don’t look so frightened. Relax. I’ll see you safely back someplace warm, with a proper mommy and daddy waiting.”

Japanese: 結果として、広美は本当に幸運だったのだろう。男は笑い、そしてエリオット・ネスと名乗った。
English: In the end, perhaps Hiromi truly had been fortunate. The man smiled and introduced himself as Eliot Ness.

Japanese: 広美はその名前の意味がわからない。ただ俯くと、また涙を流す。家族のあの光景を見てから、沢山の涙を流したはずだがまだ枯れ果ててはいないのだ。
English: Hiromi did not understand the significance of the name. She merely hung her head, and tears began to fall again. She had cried so much since seeing her family, yet the supply within her had not run dry.

Japanese: 「私には、戻るところなんか、ない……」
English: “I... don’t have anywhere to go back to.”

Japanese: 震える声でそう言うと、声をあげて泣き出した。
English: The words trembled from her, and then she began to sob aloud.

Japanese: さて、このエリオットと名乗った人物は、勿論廖志明のボディガードを務めていたあのエリオットである。
English: This man who called himself Elliott was, of course, the same Elliott who had served as Liao Chi-ming’s bodyguard.

Japanese: アメリカ海兵隊で優秀な成績を収め、国内でテロ事件に関与したのちに、タイプB系のテロ組織『ブラッド』の軍事教官をつとめ、自らも戦闘員として活動をしてきたといういかにも恐ろしげな経歴を持つ彼であるが、暗闇通りの片隅で朝から晩まで酒を飲む酔っ払いでしかなかった。以前サイキックであるマリアには後れをとったものの、その経験と実績はよく知られており、八龍会をはじめとして様々な組織から仕事を依頼されたが、この頃は全て断ってあてのない生活をしている。
English: His reported history was formidable: an excellent record in the United States Marine Corps, involvement in a domestic terrorist incident, then service as a military instructor and combatant for the Type B terrorist organization Blood. At this point, however, he was merely a drunk who spent his days drinking in a corner of Darkness Street. Although the psychic Maria had once bested him, his experience and record were well known. Hachiryukai and various other organizations offered him work, but during this period he declined every approach and lived without purpose.

Japanese: 自堕落な生活ですっかり腕はさび付き、それが露見するのを恐れてこのように仕事から逃げ回っているのだ、などと陰で囁かれたりもする。その一方で彼をこの街で最も強力な個人であると評価するものも少なくない。
English: People whispered that a life of dissipation had rusted his skills away completely, and that fear of exposure was the reason he avoided work. At the same time, more than a few observers considered him the most powerful individual in the district.

Japanese: 実戦経験が豊富で元々優秀な兵士である彼は、さらにその優れたタイプB能力が軍隊の特殊訓練によって鍛えられ、『ネオ・ローズ』などを使用しなくともその力を発揮出来た。
English: Already an exceptional soldier with extensive combat experience, Elliott had further honed his Type B ability through specialized military training and could exercise its power without Neo Rose or any similar drug.

Japanese: 彼が得意なのは戦闘だけではなかった。頭脳もまた人並みより優れていた。
English: Combat was not his only strength. He was intellectually gifted as well.

Japanese: 記憶力にすぐれ、いくつもの暗号を難なく使いこなした。言語の習得も早く、ヨーロッパの言葉だけでなく、中国語や日本語もすぐに使えるようになった。人の嘘を見破ったり、自分が嘘をつくのがうまかった。痛みに強く、どんな困難にも耐えた。急な状況の変化にも、冷静に素早く適応することが出来た。テロリストとして必要なものは全て備えていたといって良い。
English: He possessed an excellent memory and handled several codes without difficulty. Languages came quickly to him; he soon acquired not only European languages, but Chinese and Japanese as well. He was skilled both at detecting lies and telling them. He endured pain and every form of hardship. To sudden changes in circumstances, he adapted swiftly and calmly. One might fairly say that he possessed every quality required of a terrorist.

Japanese: こうした彼の能力は、タイプBやサイキックがひしめくこのY地区でも傑出したもので、後に勃発した抗争において遺憾なく発揮され街の全ての住人の知るものとなるのだが、それはこの物語が終わって数年が過ぎた後のことであり、この稿では扱わない。
English: Even in Y District, crowded as it was with Type Bs and psychics, these abilities were exceptional. He would display them fully in a conflict that erupted later, until every resident of the district knew his name. That, however, occurred several years after the conclusion of this story and falls outside the scope of the present account.

Japanese: とにかく、この時期のエリオットはそのありあまった能力をたまに酒場でのいざこざに用いる程度のもので、重要な場面には一切姿を現さず、街の表舞台からは完全に見捨てられた存在であった。
English: At this time, in any event, Elliott spent his surplus of ability on nothing more than the occasional barroom disturbance. He appeared in none of the important events, and the public life of the district had discarded him completely.

Japanese: そうして世捨て人のように暮らしていた時期のエリオットが唯一Y地区の運命に関与する事件の発端こそが、この内田広美との邂逅であった。
English: His meeting with Hiromi Uchida was the beginning of the one affair through which Elliott, during these years of near-reclusion, became involved in Y District’s fate.

Japanese: しかし、彼がこの時行き場がなく雨の下泣く内田広美を拾ったのは、彼とすれば珍しい行動であった。
English: Yet taking in a homeless Hiromi as she wept beneath the rain was unusual behavior for him.

Japanese: 彼は自らを冷酷だと広美に伝えたが、その言葉はあながち嘘ではない。
English: Elliott had described himself to Hiromi as coldhearted, and the description was not entirely false.

Japanese: 下卑た冗談を口にし、女をからかう姿なども目撃されていたが、実際には女を買うこともほとんどなく、自分の生活に立ち入らせることもなかったようである。
English: He had been seen making vulgar jokes and teasing women, but apparently rarely paid for sex or allowed a woman into his private life.

Japanese: 社会の裏側で長年活動を続けてきた彼にとって、女というものはしばしば組織に利用され、思わぬ危機を招く警戒すべき対象であった。
English: After long years spent upon the hidden side of society, he had learned to treat women warily: organizations often used them, and through them an unforeseen crisis might arrive.

Japanese: 彼は現在名を隠し素性を捨てて生活をしているが、その正体を知ればこれまでの経歴で得た情報を知りたがったり、或いは憎み殺意を抱く者はいくらでも現れるはずだ。
English: He was now living under a hidden name, having discarded his former identity. Were that identity discovered, any number of people might appear—some seeking information acquired over the course of his career, others driven by hatred and a desire to kill him.

Japanese: そんな彼にとって、異性は容易に近づけるべきものではなかったのである。そして生来情の薄い方で、異性と関わることの喜びよりも、面倒という気持ちの方が先に立つタイプの男だ。『ブラッド』に所属していた頃、任務のために敵対組織の支配する地域に潜入したことがあり、その時現地の女と知り合い共に生活をしたのだが、任務終了時にはその女を殺害してから街を出ている。
English: For Elliott, then, the opposite sex was not something he could safely allow close. Accounts also portray him as cold by nature, a man in whom the prospect of trouble arose sooner than any pleasure in intimacy. During his time with Blood, he once infiltrated territory controlled by an enemy organization. There he met a local woman and lived with her, but when the mission ended, he killed her before leaving the city.

Japanese: まだ若く、テロリストとして毎日のように人殺しをしていた時期のことであり、今となっては多少彼の心境にも変化があるのかもしれないが、そうだとしても見知らぬ少女を理由もなく救うというのは彼にしては考えられない。
English: He had still been young then, killing people almost daily as a terrorist. Perhaps his feelings had changed somewhat since. Even if they had, however, rescuing a strange girl for no reason remained all but inconceivable behavior from him.

Japanese: しかしこの突飛な行動が、Y地区の勢力図に少なからず影響を与える結果になるのだから世の中というのは数奇なものである。
English: And yet this unexpected act would affect the balance of power within Y District to no small degree. The world follows strange courses.

Japanese: もし彼がここで広美を助けなければ、この街の運命は変わっていただろうか？　……いや、現実として起きたことに対して『もし』を考えるほど意味のないことはない。どんな些細なことでも、そこに至るには膨大な原因があり、全てが必然で出来て居居る。つまり、ここで彼が広美を助けたのも気まぐれのようでいて、誰にも変えることが出来ない確固とした根拠が積み重なった末の行動なのである。
English: Would the district’s fate have changed had he not saved Hiromi here? No—nothing is more meaningless than asking ‘what if’ of an event that has already occurred. However minor an event may seem, an immense accumulation of causes was required to produce it, and every part of that accumulation was inevitable. What looked like Elliott’s whim was therefore an action built upon foundations so firm that no one could have changed it.

Japanese: だから我々人間は既に起きてしまった事実には謙虚になり、まだ見ぬ未来に対しては大胆になるべきなのだ。
English: By that reasoning, we human beings ought to meet accomplished fact with humility and the unseen future with boldness.

Japanese: さて、泣きじゃくる広美はエリオットに誘われるまま彼の住まいへと向かった。
English: Hiromi, still sobbing, went with Elliott to his home.

Japanese: 日が暮れるころに辿り着いた彼のマンションは、廖志明に与えられた場所に引き続き住んでいるものだったが、到底それほど長く暮らしているとは思えないほどに物が少なかった。
English: Around sunset, they reached the apartment Liao Chi-ming had given Elliott, where he still lived. It held so few possessions that no one would have guessed he had occupied it for so long.

Japanese: つい先日、この街にやって来たばかりだと言われても信用してしまいそうなくらいだ。越してきた時から備え付けられていたベッドや机や椅子などの調度品以外のものを全て集めても旅行鞄ひとつに収まってしまいそうに思える。
English: One could easily have believed that he had arrived in the district only days ago. Aside from the bed, desk, chairs, and other furnishings present when he moved in, everything he owned appeared capable of fitting into a single suitcase.

Japanese: 3DKの間取りのうち、寝室とダイニングのテーブルまわり以外はまるきり使っていないようで、残り二つの部屋には白い埃がつもっていた。
English: Of the apartment’s three rooms and dining kitchen, he seemed to use only the bedroom and the space around the dining table. White dust covered the other two rooms.

Japanese: 「わるいが掃除してくれるか」
English: “Sorry, but would you clean this?”

Japanese: 呆然とする広美に、エリオットは掃除機を押しつけてぶっきらぼうにそう言った。
English: Elliott thrust a vacuum cleaner into the bewildered Hiromi’s hands and spoke brusquely.

Japanese: 掃除機は病院での掃除にも使われていて、広美は触ったことがなかったが職員がいじっていたのを見て覚えている。部屋の埃を全て吸い取り終わるとエリオットが毛布を持ってやって来た。
English: The hospital staff had used vacuum cleaners, and although Hiromi had never touched one herself, she remembered watching them operate it. Once she had removed all the dust from the room, Elliott appeared with a blanket.

Japanese: 広美はてっきりそれを使って寝ろということかと思ったが、
English: Hiromi assumed he meant her to sleep under it, but he said,

Japanese: 「今シーツをかえたからお前はベッドを使え。おれは今晩はこっちで寝る」
English: “I just changed the sheets, so you take the bed. I’ll sleep in here tonight.”

Japanese: と、部屋のなかにその茶色の毛布を乱暴に投げ出した。
English: He tossed the brown blanket roughly into the room.

Japanese: 「大分濡れてるな。むこうにバスルームがあるからシャワーを使うといい。服は洗濯機にいれてボタンを押せば明日には乾いている。朝になったらそれを着てここを出るんだ」
English: “You’re soaked. There’s a bathroom over there, so take a shower. Put your clothes in the washing machine and press the button. They’ll be dry tomorrow. In the morning, put them on and leave.”

Japanese: 「は、はい」
English: “Y-yes.”

Japanese: 「今ピザを頼んだ。シャワーから出て来る頃には届いているだろう。今日はそれを食って寝るんだ」
English: “I just ordered pizza. It ought to arrive by the time you’re out of the shower. Eat that and get some sleep.”

Japanese: それからバスルームに案内されてシャワーの使い方と、新しいタオルの場所を教わった。長年人の指示に従って生活することに慣れていた広美は従順に頷いて聞いていた。
English: He took her to the bathroom and explained how to use the shower and where to find a fresh towel. Long years of living under other people’s instructions had accustomed Hiromi to obedience, and she listened with docile nods.

Japanese: そして彼が出て行くと言われたとおりに服を脱ぎ、それを洗濯機に入れてボタンを押す。ドラム式の洗濯機のなかで水の音がしはじめて、思わず驚く。ドアについた透明な窓に顔を近づけ、中に水がたまってゆくのをしばらく眺めてから、バスルームに移動した。
English: Once he left, she undressed as instructed, put her clothing into the washing machine, and pressed the button. The sound of water beginning to fill the front-loading drum startled her. For some time, she held her face close to the transparent door and watched the water accumulate within. Then she moved to the shower.

Japanese: これが病院を出てから初めての入浴だ。
English: It was her first bath since leaving the hospital.

Japanese: 鑑の前のプラスチックの椅子に腰掛けると目の前に大きな鏡があり、全裸の自分と向かい合わせられた。幼い頃より発達してまるで大人のような身体になっているのに今更ながら驚く。症状が出ている間もその成長を見ていたはずだが、目の前にあったのにまるで認識していなかったから、間をすっとばして急にこの身体が現れたような気がした。
English: When she sat upon the plastic stool before the large mirror, she found herself confronted with her own naked body. Only now did it astonish her that the body had developed since childhood until it looked almost adult. She must have watched it growing even while her symptoms were present, but she had scarcely perceived what stood before her eyes. It felt as though the intervening years had been skipped and this body had appeared all at once.

Japanese: （ちゃんと洗えるかな……）
English: (Will I be able to wash myself properly...?)

Japanese: シャワーのお湯の温度を指先で確認しながら、広美は不安だった。
English: Hiromi tested the shower’s temperature with her fingertips, full of anxiety.

Japanese: 病院にいるときはいつも職員に身体も頭も洗って貰っていた。病院に来る前は母親が洗っていた。さらにその前の、症状が出る前は自分で洗っていたときもあるような気がするが、もう大分昔のことだ。
English: At the hospital, a member of staff had always washed both her body and her hair. Before she entered the hospital, her mother had washed her. Before even that, prior to the onset of her symptoms, she felt that she might sometimes have washed herself—but that was very long ago.

Japanese: ここには職員も母親もいない。職員は死んでしまったし、母親はもう会うことが出来ない。それを思うと涙が溢れ出てまた泣いてしまいそうだったが下唇を噛んで堪えた。
English: There were no staff members here, and no mother. The staff were dead. She could never see her mother again. The thought brought tears surging up and nearly made her cry once more, but she bit her lower lip and held them back.

Japanese: バスルームを出てタオルで身体を拭くときになって、髪の毛にまだ泡がついているのに気がついた。その他にも本人は気がつかなかったがボディソープとシャンプーを間違って使ったりもしていた。しかし、それ以外のことはおおむねミスもなく入浴をすませることが出来た。
English: Only after leaving the shower and beginning to dry herself did she notice that suds still remained in her hair. She also confused the body wash and shampoo without realizing it. Aside from these mistakes, however, she managed the rest of the bath without serious trouble.

Japanese: エリオットが用意してくれた着替えは白無地のＴシャツと、綿で出来たベージュのズボンだった。彼が普段身につけているものらしく、いずれのあまりにも大きく、ズボンの裾を何度も折り返さなくてはならなかった。
English: Elliott had left her a plain white T-shirt and beige cotton pants. They appeared to be clothes he ordinarily wore, and both were far too large. She had to roll up the cuffs of the pants several times.

Japanese: 下着はなくあちこちがすうすうとしていたが、思春期を病院で過ごした広美は女性的な羞恥心に疎く、なんとも思わなかった。
English: There was no underwear, leaving her exposed to every draft. Having spent adolescence in the hospital, however, Hiromi possessed little of the modesty expected of a young woman and thought nothing of it.

Japanese: バスルームを出るとダイニングのテーブルの上にはピザがもう届いている。エリオットの姿が見えなかったが、広美のたてた物音を聞きつけたのか向こうの部屋からやって来た。手にはウィスキーの入ったグラスがあり、その顔は赤く染まっていた。
English: When she emerged from the bathroom, the pizza was already waiting upon the dining table. Elliott was nowhere in sight, but perhaps he heard the noise she made, for he soon came from the other room. He held a glass of whiskey, and his face was flushed red.

Japanese: 「冷めないうちに食いなよ。ピザが嫌いってことはないんだろ？」
English: “Eat before it gets cold. You don’t hate pizza, do you?”

Japanese: 広美は頷き、テーブルについた。
English: Hiromi shook her head and sat at the table.

Japanese: 勝手に開けていいのかわからずに座ったままじっとしていたが、エリオットは酒を飲んでぼんやりと携帯電話をいじるだけで何もしない。
English: Unsure whether she was permitted to open the box, she remained motionless in her seat. Elliott merely drank and idly played with his phone, doing nothing.

Japanese: おずおずと手を伸ばして見たけれども彼に咎められる様子はなかったので、そのまま蓋を開いた。
English: She reached out hesitantly. When he gave no sign of reproach, she opened the lid.

Japanese: ケチャップとチーズの香りが漂い、大きめの四角いピザがそこにあった。
English: The scents of ketchup and cheese drifted up from a large square pizza.

Japanese: それほど空腹を覚えてはいなかったが、病院でも指示をされればその通り食事をしていた広美は機械的に手を動かして、チーズの糸を引くピザを一切れとった。そして一口囓って飲み込むと、自分でも思っていなかったほどの食欲があとからあとから沸いて来た。
English: She had not felt especially hungry. At the hospital, however, Hiromi had always eaten mechanically whenever instructed, and habit set her hand moving now. She took one slice, trailing strings of cheese, bit into it, and swallowed. Only then did an appetite greater than she had imagined surge up, wave after wave.

Japanese: 今日一日様々なことがあって心は傷ついていたが、彼女の身体は若く生命力に満ち溢れており、疲労したぶんだけ栄養を求めていたのだ。
English: The events of the day had wounded her heart, but her body was young and full of life, demanding the nourishment required by its exhaustion.

Japanese: 「食べないんですか？」
English: “Aren’t you going to eat?”

Japanese: 瞬く間に半分ほど食べてしまった広美は、気を遣ってエリオットに訊ねた。
English: After devouring nearly half the pizza in moments, Hiromi remembered her manners and asked Elliott.

Japanese: 「おれは夜は酒だけでいいんだよ。最近はろくにトレーニングもしていないし、太って仕方ない。しかし、えらい食いっぷりだな」
English: “Liquor is enough for me at night. I hardly train anymore, and I can’t stop getting fat. You can really put it away, though.”

Japanese: 携帯をいじっていたはずのエリオットは、いつの間にか広美の食べる様子に目を奪われており、呆れたように言った。
English: Though Elliott had seemed occupied with his phone, at some point Hiromi’s eating captured his attention. He sounded astonished.

Japanese: 「美味しくって……」
English: “It’s so good...”

Japanese: さっきまで泣いていたのにこんなに食べている姿を見せてしまって、恥ずかしく俯いた拍子にげっぷが出てしまったのでなおさら恥ずかしい思いをした。ピザと一緒に置いてあったペットボトルのコーラの炭酸が悪さをしたのだろう。
English: She lowered her head in embarrassment at being seen eating so much after all her tears, only to belch and embarrass herself still further. The carbonation in the bottle of cola that came with the pizza was presumably to blame.

Japanese: ピザもコーラも、病院ではほとんど口にする機会がなかったものだ。
English: Pizza and cola were both things she had scarcely ever tasted at the hospital.

Japanese: 「さっき戻るところがないと言っていたな。お前さんにもいろいろあるんだろうが、詳しい事情は聞かないぜ。お互いその方がいいだろう。さっき言った通り、一晩寝たら明日の朝ここを出て行くんだ。だから、それまでにどうするか決めておくんだな」
English: “You said you had nowhere to go back to. I’m sure you’ve got your reasons, but I won’t ask. Better for both of us that way. Like I said, once you’ve slept for the night, you’re leaving tomorrow morning. Decide what you’ll do before then.”

Japanese: エリオットはニコリともしないでそう言った。広美を連れて来たことを後悔した、というわけでもないようだが言葉通りこれ以上の深入りをするつもりはなさそうな冷淡な表情をしている。
English: Elliott said this without the faintest smile. He did not appear to regret bringing Hiromi home, but his expression was cold and suggested that, true to his words, he meant to involve himself no further.

Japanese: 「はい、わかりました」
English: “Yes. I understand.”

Japanese: もとより広美にも世話になろうという思いがあったわけでもなく、自然にそう答えて頷く。
English: Hiromi had never intended to depend upon him in the first place, and so she answered and nodded without hesitation.

Japanese: この態度には、エリオットの方が若干拍子抜けをしたようだった。
English: Her response appeared to take Elliott slightly aback.

Japanese: 一般的に言って不幸な状況にある少女に突き放すような言葉を投げかければ、すがりつこうとするか、暗い表情を見せるかしそうなものだが、広美はどちらでもなくあまりにもあっさりとしている。そしてまたピザに手を伸ばしはじめたのである。
English: One might ordinarily expect a girl in unhappy circumstances to cling to him or at least look stricken when met with such rejection. Hiromi did neither. She accepted it with astonishing ease and reached for another slice of pizza.

Japanese: エリオットは溜息をつき、
English: Elliott sighed.

Japanese: 「どんなときでも食えるときにたくさん食うってのは、生き延びるやつの条件だ。お前さんはきっと長生きするぜ」
English: “Being able to eat your fill whenever you get the chance—that’s one condition for surviving. I bet you’ll live a long time.”

Japanese: そう言って、部屋を去っていった。
English: With that, he left the room.

Japanese: そのあとも一人で食べ続けた広美は結局全てをたいらげた。残ったゴミを捨てようと、箱をもってうろうろとしたが部屋の片隅のくず入れにはサイズが小さくて、一旦は折りたたんで無理に突っ込んだものの、とりやめて引っ張り出すと捨てるのを諦めテーブルの上に放置したまま寝室に引っ込んだ。
English: Alone, Hiromi continued eating until she had finished everything. She picked up the box and wandered around in search of somewhere to discard it, but it was too large for the wastebasket in the corner. She folded it and forced it inside, changed her mind, pulled it out again, then abandoned the effort and left the box upon the table before retiring to the bedroom.

Japanese: さて、先に部屋に戻っていたエリオットである。
English: Elliott, meanwhile, had returned to his room first.

Japanese: 明かりを消した暗い部屋で横になっていたが眠れず、仕方なく瓶から直で寝酒のつもりで飲んでいたウィスキーも空になってしまった。
English: He lay in the darkness with the light off, unable to sleep. At last even the bottle of whiskey he had been drinking directly as a nightcap ran empty.

Japanese: マンションに若い女を連れて来るのは久しぶりのことだったが、彼はそのことを少しも意識していない。どころか、広美のことさえ考えていない。彼は、彼女を拾う原因となった事件のことを考えていた。
English: It had been a long time since he had brought a young woman to his apartment, but this fact did not occupy his mind in the least. Nor, indeed, was he thinking about Hiromi herself. His thoughts were with the chain of events that had caused him to take her in.

Japanese: それはひとつの事件ではない。いくつもの出来事が連鎖してひとつのイメージを作り出している。
English: It was not one event. Many incidents linked together to form a single image.

Japanese: かつて『ブラッド』で仕事をしていたとき、彼は多くの人間を手にかけた。そのなかには子供や女も少なくはない。
English: While working for Blood, he had killed many people. Women and children had by no means been rare among them.

Japanese: たとえばタイプBの子供がある差別的な扱いによって命を落としたとする。一般的なタイプBの市民団体などは抗議の声をあげ、とりまく環境の変化を訴える。一方『ブラッド』は施政者の家族をむごたらしく殺害することで抗議の手段とする。
English: Suppose, for example, that discriminatory treatment caused the death of a Type B child. An ordinary Type B civil-rights group might protest and call for changes to the conditions surrounding them. Blood made its protest by slaughtering the responsible official’s family.

Japanese: この有名なテロ組織は、特定の国家や民族によるものではない。その支援者はタイプBだけではなく、リベラルな思想を持つノーマルなども多く含まれている。富裕者は金銭によって、学者などの知識人は思想を理論化し、有名人はメッセージを発信するかたちで組織を支援する。そのメンバーは公開されていないが、組織の上部にいるのはみな地位のある人間であるという。彼らは純粋な平等の思想を掲げているが、それだけでなく、支援をすることで一定の恩恵を組織から受け取っているという。
English: The famous terrorist organization belonged to no particular nation or ethnic group. Its supporters reportedly included not only Type Bs, but many Normals with liberal beliefs. The wealthy gave money; scholars and other intellectuals supplied theory; celebrities sent out its message. Its membership was not public, but those at its highest levels were said to be people of standing. They proclaimed a pure ideal of equality, while reports also held that their support purchased particular benefits from the organization.

Japanese: たとえば、前述の家族を殺された施政者は、実は『ブラッド』を支援するある政治家の政敵であったというのはただの偶然だろうか？
English: For example: was it truly coincidence that the official whose family had been murdered was the political enemy of a politician who supported Blood?

Japanese: その能力によって重宝され、上層部の事情を知ることとなったエリオットはその構造に疑問を持っていたが、彼は自分の考えの一切を口にせず淡々と仕事を続けた。
English: Elliott’s abilities made him valuable and brought him close enough to learn how the leadership actually operated. He had doubts about the structure, yet voiced none of them and continued performing his work with perfect composure.

Japanese: ぬいぐるみを抱えて震える幼子の首を絞め、手のひらのなかにその頸動脈の拍動が止まるのを感じる瞬間も、顔色ひとつかえなかった。
English: He did not so much as change color when he strangled a small child trembling around a stuffed animal and felt the pulse of the carotid artery beneath his palm cease.

Japanese: くだらない仕事だと思っていた。かつて若き兵士だった頃はタイプBの理想に燃え、その結果軍を追われることになったが、『ブラッド』に対してはただ自分の技術を高く買ってくれる相手という以外なんの感情もなかった。タイプBをとりまくいかなる感情的な議論も、彼の身体を通り過ぎるだけで心には何も残さなかった。そして、任務委において自分の両手がいかにおぞましい行為をしようとも、何も感じなかったのだ。
English: He considered the work pointless. As a young soldier, he had burned with ideals for Type Bs and been expelled from the military as a result. Toward Blood, however, he felt nothing beyond recognition that it paid highly for his skills. Every emotional argument surrounding Type Bs passed through his body without leaving anything in his heart. No matter how appalling the acts his hands performed during a mission, he felt nothing.

Japanese: その時は。
English: At the time.

Japanese: そしてしばらくは自分がそんなことをしたという事実もほとんど忘れかけていた。
English: For a while, he nearly forgot that he had done any of it.

Japanese: 組織を抜けた今となっても、罪悪感などは特に感じていない。あれは単なる仕事であったし、子供と言えども時間が経てばすぐに大人になるだけの『まだ小さい人間』でしかなく、世間がよく天使やなにかに例えたりするような感覚は彼にはなかった。
English: Even now, after leaving the organization, he felt no particular guilt. It had merely been work. A child, in his understanding, was only ‘a person who is still small’ and would soon grow into an adult. He possessed none of the instinct by which people so often likened children to angels.

Japanese: しかし、どういうわけだろう。時々、子供たちを殺す夢を見るのだ。
English: Yet for some reason, he sometimes dreamed of killing the children.

Japanese: そこに現れる被害者は子供だけではない。腹の出た妊婦。妻をかばう病気の男。命乞いをする老婆。彼が様々な仕事で殺害したもののうち、いずれも弱く善良な人々である。彼はもう一度そのあわれな人々を現実と同じやり方で殺してゆく。次から次へと場面が変わって、果てしなく。ただそれだけの夢だ。
English: Children were not the only victims who appeared. A pregnant woman with a swollen belly. A sick man shielding his wife. An old woman begging for her life. All were weak and decent people whom he had killed in the course of various assignments. He murdered those pitiable people again, exactly as he had in reality. Scene followed scene without end. That was all the dream contained.

Japanese: 彼はその夢を見ても何も感じない。悲しくも苦しくもない。……しかし、目が覚めるとひどく気怠いのに気がつく。
English: He felt nothing while dreaming it. Neither sorrow nor pain. And yet, when he woke, he found himself terribly listless.

Japanese: そしていつもよりほんの少し酒の味が薄く感じられ、ほんの少し酔い方が悪い。
English: His liquor tasted the slightest bit thinner than usual, and the drunk it produced felt the slightest bit worse.

Japanese: 色もくすんで見え、テーブルに飾られた花を嗅いでも、音楽を聴いてもいつもより薄い。
English: Colors seemed dull. Whether he smelled the flowers arranged upon a table or listened to music, every sensation was fainter than usual.

Japanese: まるで、全ての感覚に灰色のフィルターがかかってしまったように。
English: It was as though a gray filter had fallen across every sense.

Japanese: それで困るというわけでもないが、すっきりしない一日だった。その時雨のなかでうなだれている広美を見つけた。その横顔に、ふと殺してきた女や子供の顔が重なって、気づけば話しかけていた。
English: It did not cause him any particular trouble, but the day never felt right. Then he saw Hiromi standing beneath the rain with her head bowed. For an instant, her profile overlapped the faces of women and children he had killed. Before he knew what he was doing, he had spoken to her.

Japanese: 今は毛布のなかで、今度は夢ではなくはっきりと自分の意志でその場面を思い出している。別に動揺はしない。ただ乾いた感じがするだけだ。
English: Now, beneath the blanket, he recalled those scenes clearly and by his own will rather than through a dream. They did not disturb him. He felt only dry inside.

Japanese: 殺し合いの場で心に深い傷を負って使い物にならなくなる人間を何人も見てきた。唇を震わせ、真っ青な顔で、あからさまにおかしくなるやつもいたが、本人にはなんの自覚もなく、一見するとまわりからもわからないが、話してみると確かに壊れているという人間もいた。
English: He had seen many people take wounds in battle that left them unable to function. Some trembled at the lips and turned deathly pale, plainly deranged. Others were unaware of any change, and nothing appeared wrong from the outside, yet conversation revealed that something in them had certainly broken.

Japanese: おれも知らないうちに、どこかおかしくなっているのかもしれないな。
English: (Maybe something in me has gone wrong without my knowing it.)

Japanese: 心のなかでそう呟いてみた。そうだとしても、別に悲しくもなかった。
English: He murmured the thought inwardly. Even if it were true, he did not find it sad.

Japanese: その回想に導かれるように、昔のさまざまな情景が脳裏に浮かび上がってくる。自分を愛してくれた女。彼女も結局自分で殺すことになった。仲間の一人が情報を売っていて、泣いて命乞いしているのを証拠の撮影をしながらもう片方の手に握った銃で手足から撃ち抜いていった。砂漠のキャンプで、まだ幼さの残る子供たちに戦い方を教えた。毎日同じテントで眠り、同じ食事をした。
English: Led onward by the recollection, scene after scene from long ago rose into his mind. A woman who had loved him; in the end, he had killed her himself. A comrade who sold information and begged for his life; Elliott filmed the evidence while using the gun in his other hand to shoot him through the arms and legs one by one. Children still marked by youth, whom he taught to fight at a camp in the desert. Every night they had slept in the same tent and eaten the same food.

Japanese: いつの間にか眠りについており、そして物音で目が覚めた。
English: At some point he fell asleep, and a noise woke him.

Japanese: 回想のせいですっかり当時の感覚に戻っていた彼は、反射的に当時いつも枕元に置いていた銃の場所に手を伸ばし、虚しく空を探ることになる。
English: The memories had returned him so thoroughly to the sensations of that time that his hand darted by reflex toward the place where he had always kept a gun beside his pillow, only to search empty air.

Japanese: そしてすぐに今自分はそんなに神経を張り詰めて生活する必要がないことを思い出し、同時にドアを開けて立っている広美を見つけた。彼女はエリオットの大きなシャツのなかで身体を泳がせている。
English: He quickly remembered that his present life required no such constant tension. At the same moment, he saw Hiromi standing in the open doorway, her body nearly lost inside Elliott’s enormous shirt.

Japanese: 「どうした？」
English: “What is it?”

Japanese: 「お腹がすいて……」
English: “I’m hungry...”

Japanese: 「冷蔵庫に何か入ってる。何でも使っていいから適当に食え」
English: “There’s something in the refrigerator. Use whatever you like and make yourself something.”

Japanese: 「冷蔵庫に？」
English: “In the refrigerator?”

Japanese: 「卵かベーコンがあったかな。目玉焼きくらいつくれるだろ。キッチンにフライパンは出したままになっていたはずだ」
English: “I think there are eggs or bacon. You can at least fry an egg, can’t you? The frying pan should still be out in the kitchen.”

Japanese: さすがのエリオットも昨日は飲み過ぎてしまったらしく、喋ると頭がズキズキと痛んで顔を顰める。
English: Apparently even Elliott had drunk too much the night before. Speaking made his head throb, and he grimaced.

Japanese: 「食ったら好きなところへ行け。挨拶はいらないからな。おれはもう少し眠る」
English: “Once you’ve eaten, go wherever you like. No need to say goodbye. I’m sleeping a little longer.”

Japanese: エリオットはぶっきらぼうに言うと、またごろりと横になって毛布にくるまった。
English: Elliott spoke brusquely, rolled over, and wrapped himself in the blanket again.

Japanese: そしてもう一度眠りについた。
English: Then he returned to sleep.

Japanese: 次に目が覚めたのは、喉の渇きによってだった。
English: The next thing to wake him was thirst.

Japanese: 起き上がるとまだ頭痛がし、腹のあたりはまるで内臓が腐ったかのような不快感が残っている。毎日飲んでいるエリオットにとって二日酔いは少なくないが、今日はいつもよりきつい。
English: His head still ached when he sat up, and his stomach felt as foul as though the organs within had begun to rot. Hangovers were nothing unusual for a man who drank every day, but this one was worse than most.

Japanese: 普段ならこのまま出かけて迎え酒と行くところだが、今日は何よりもまず水を飲みたかった。
English: Ordinarily, he would have gone out and met it with another drink. Today, more than anything, he wanted water first.

Japanese: そして部屋を出たところで彼は焦げ臭いにおいを感じる。キッチンの方から音がする。
English: When he left the room, he smelled something burning. Noises came from the kitchen.

Japanese: 広美はまだ帰っていなかったのか。それとも、自分が思っているほど長い二度寝ではなかったのか。
English: Had Hiromi not left yet? Or had he slept less the second time than he imagined?

Japanese: 痛む頭を抱えながらキッチンに向かうと、予想していない光景にでくわした。
English: Clutching his aching head, Elliott went to the kitchen and encountered something he had not anticipated.

Japanese: エリオットはちっとも知らなかったが、たとえ目玉焼きといえども広美に料理など出来るはずもない。それどころか、火を扱わせてもらえず、実家にいたときもコンロのそばに近づくことさえ許されなかった彼女には、見よう見まねで調理を見た記憶もない。病院のテレビでは時々調理シーンなども流れていたはずだが、知能が落ちてテレビの内容も理解出来なかった彼女は画面に興味を持つこともなかった。
English: Elliott had no way of knowing it, but Hiromi could no more fry an egg than prepare any other food. She had never been permitted to handle fire. Even at home, she had been forbidden to approach the stove, leaving her with no memory of learning by watching others. Cooking scenes must occasionally have appeared upon the hospital television, but when her diminished understanding prevented her from following the programs, she had shown no interest in the screen.

Japanese: つまり、大変なことになっていたのである。
English: In short, a disaster had occurred.

Japanese: 卵はパックがそのまま冷蔵庫に入っていたはずだが、ほとんど割るのに失敗して、三つほどが床の上で潰れ、残りのいくつかは流しに飲み込まれたようだ。ボウルにどうにか二つの卵が入っているようだが、黄身はやぶけ、細かい殻の破片が混ざっている。
English: A full carton of eggs had been in the refrigerator. Hiromi failed to crack nearly all of them. Three lay smashed across the floor, and several more appeared to have vanished down the sink. She had somehow deposited two in a bowl, but their yolks were broken and small fragments of shell floated throughout.
