Japanese: 辺りはシンとして誰もいない。私の呼吸の音だけがきこえる。はあはあと、私はこんなに荒い呼吸をしているのか。
English: The place was utterly still and empty. I could hear only my own breathing. Panting, ragged breaths—was I really breathing that hard?

Japanese: 目の前にシャッターがあった。しっかりと閉ざされている。もし私が元気ならば、こんなのタイプBの力でこじ開けてしまえるのに、今はちょっと無理そうだ。
English: A shutter stood before me, firmly closed. If I had been well, I could have forced something like this open with Type B strength. At the moment, that seemed rather impossible.

Japanese: 他に出口はないか。
English: Was there another way out?

Japanese: 見回すために頭をふるだけで、脳がゆれてもの凄く気分が悪くなる。
English: Simply turning my head to look around made my brain shift inside my skull and sent a violent wave of nausea through me.

Japanese: ここから出られればいいのに。
English: If only I could get out of here.

Japanese: もともと私たちには手を使わずに物を動かす力があった。見えない透明人間を想像して、それに何かを触れさせると、本当に実体があるものが触れたかのように動かすことが出来るんだ。
English: We had always possessed the power to move objects without using our hands. If I imagined an invisible person and had her touch something, I could move it exactly as though a real, solid body had done so.

Japanese: 私はなんとなくそれをやってみた。
English: Without any particular expectation, I tried it.

Japanese: 自分の姿と全く同じ透明人間がシャッターの下に指をかけ、そして引っ張り上げる。
English: An invisible person identical to me hooked her fingers beneath the shutter and pulled upward.

Japanese: すると、本当に出来てしまった。
English: And it actually worked.

Japanese: シャッターのあちこちから金属のきしむもの凄い音がして、まるでアルミホイルを握りつぶしたみたいに、しわだらけになりながらシャッターがめくり上がり、そして外の太陽の光がその隙間から差し込んだ。
English: Metal shrieked from every part of the shutter. It wrinkled and crumpled like a sheet of aluminum foil being crushed in a fist as it peeled upward, and sunlight streamed through the opening beneath it.

Japanese: あれ？　どうして出来るんだろう？
English: What? Why could I do that?

Japanese: そしてふと思い出して見ると、私は自分がどっちなのか、はっきり自覚できていないことに気がついた。
English: Then, when I tried to remember, I realized that I had no clear awareness of which one I was.

Japanese: さっき撃たれた場面では、両方が撃たれて血が飛び散る場面が映像として記憶に残っているけれど、どちらも客観的に見た感じの映像だ。頭がぼんやりしているから、本当の記憶と想像ががごっちゃになっているのかもしれない。
English: My memory of the shooting showed both of us being struck and blood flying from our bodies, but both images seemed to be viewed objectively from outside. Perhaps my hazy mind had mixed real memory together with imagination.

Japanese: 昔のことを思い出そうとしても、二人が並んで何かをしている映像ばかりで、どっちがどっちかわからない。そもそも、私たちはいつも一緒だったから、違う思い出なんかないんだ。トイレとかは別々だったけど、トイレに入ってる自分の姿を思い出しても、どっちだかわからないな。
English: When I tried to remember the past, all I saw were images of the two of us doing things side by side. I could not tell which was which. We had always been together, so we scarcely possessed any separate memories in the first place. We did use the toilet separately, but even when I pictured myself in there, I could not say which one I was.

Japanese: 私は何か自分の顔が映るものがないか探して、近くの資材の金属パーツがよく磨かれているのを見つけた。そこに顔を映すと、目が金色になっている。私がタイプBなのは間違いない。
English: I searched for something that would reflect my face and found a well-polished metal component among the materials nearby. In its surface, I saw that my eyes had turned gold. There was no question that I was a Type B.

Japanese: タイプBで、そしてサイキックも使えて……これじゃもうどっちがどっちかわからない。顔を見たって、区別がつきやしないんだ。
English: A Type B, yet capable of using psychic power as well... Now I truly could not tell which of us I was. Even looking at my face offered no distinction.

Japanese: もしかしたら、ここにいるのは私じゃなくて、やっぱり『私たち』なのかもしれない。きっとそうなんだろう。そのような気がする。そもそも、そのほうがしっくりとくる。私じゃなくて、私たちのほうが。
English: Perhaps the one here was not me after all, but ‘us.’ That was probably it. It felt right. ‘Us’ fit better than ‘me.’

Japanese: とにかく、出口が出来た。
English: In any event, we had made an exit.

Japanese: 私たちはそこから出ることにした。
English: We decided to leave through it.

Japanese: 身をかがめてくぐったところで、ふと振り返った。
English: After ducking beneath the opening, we happened to look back.

Japanese: 半分めくれたシートからはみ出した私たちの死体が見える。あれはこのまま置いていっていいのだろうか？
English: Our corpse protruded from beneath the half-peeled-back sheet. Was it all right simply to leave that there?

Japanese: 置いていったら、好きなようにメチャクチャにされてしまう。
English: If we did, people would do anything they liked to it and ruin it completely.

Japanese: ああでも、それでいいのか。私たちはもう死んで、アレを利用しなくなったんだし。誰かが利用してくれるならそれは、省エネっていうか、エコっていうか、無駄のないことだ。
English: Ah, but perhaps that was fine. We were already dead and no longer had any use for it. If someone else could make use of it, that was energy-efficient—or ecological—or at least not wasteful.

Japanese: 私たちは前を向いて歩き出す。
English: We faced forward and began to walk.

Japanese: 明るい太陽が背中をやわらかく温めて、うつむき加減になったアスファルトにくっきりとした私たちの影を落とす。
English: The bright sun warmed our back gently and cast our sharply defined shadow on the asphalt beneath our lowered gaze.

Japanese: 虫の羽音のようなざわめきはずっと聞こえている。
English: The murmur like insect wings continued without pause.

Japanese: とにかくお腹が空いた。
English: More importantly, we were starving.

Japanese: 頭のなかもお腹のなかも空っぽで、ほとんどなんにも考えていなかったけれど、子供の時から街をうろついていたせいですっかり地理は身体に染み込んでいて、気づいたら私たちは『シンディーマート』という大きな看板のかかった店の前にいた。
English: Our mind and stomach were both empty, and we were scarcely thinking at all. Yet after wandering the city since childhood, its geography was ingrained in our body. Before we knew it, we stood in front of a store beneath a large sign reading CINDY MART.

Japanese: 私たちが小さな頃はコンビニみたいな小さな店舗で、薬と、お菓子や保存食料品などを売っていたけれど、今は真っ黒なアスファルトの敷かれた広い駐車場と、真夜中でもまわりが明るくなるくらい強烈な照明で広い店内を照らしている大きな店となって、薬も生鮮食品もそれぞれの専門店と同じくらい豊富に扱うようになっている。
English: When we were little, it had been a tiny shop like a convenience store, selling medicine, sweets, preserved foods, and the like. Now it had become a large establishment, with a broad parking lot paved in jet-black asphalt and powerful lights that illuminated its spacious interior brightly enough to light the neighborhood even at midnight. Its selections of medicine and fresh food rivaled those of specialty stores.

Japanese: この街のお店らしく、輸入食品も多くて、私たちはここでよくクッキーだとかお菓子を買っていた。そしてそれを食べながら、この辺りを歩いていたんだ。
English: Like so many stores in this city, it carried a great many imported foods. We often bought cookies and other sweets here, then ate them as we walked around the neighborhood.

Japanese: マットを踏むとガラスのドアが音もなく開く。入り口のところにあったカートを押して食品コーナーの方へ歩く私たちを、通り過ぎる客がジロジロと見る。
English: When we stepped upon the mat, the glass doors opened soundlessly. We took a cart from the entrance and pushed it toward the food section while the customers we passed stared openly at us.

Japanese: そう言えば私たちの胸は血みどろに汚れていたんだ。
English: Come to think of it, our chest was soaked in blood.

Japanese: 顔もきっと同じように血と誇りで汚れているに違いない。
English: Our face must have been similarly caked with blood and dust.

Japanese: 髪の毛を手のひらで触ってみると、血液でかたまって手ぐしが通らなかった。
English: When we ran a palm over our hair, the blood had hardened it so completely that our fingers would not pass through.

Japanese: すごい格好だな。……別にいいか。
English: We were quite a sight. ...Well, never mind.

Japanese: 食品コーナーには業務用の食材も沢山おいてある。私たちは身体の求めるまま、必要なものをカゴに放り込んだ。
English: The food section carried a great many bulk ingredients as well. Obeying the demands of our body, we loaded the cart with everything we needed.

Japanese: 丸のままのハムを二本、牛乳を四リットル、オリーブオイルを一瓶、キャベツを三個、生卵を五パック、ニンジンとピーマンを一袋、フランスパンを三本、レンジで温めるご飯を5パック、冷凍のアジの干物を六枚、コーラのペットボトルを一本、チョコレートを八枚……。そしてそろそろ怪しいはずなので生理用品を買った。カートに積み上げていたけれど、どうやっても乗らなくなったので仕方なくレジへ向かう。
English: Two whole hams; four liters of milk; one bottle of olive oil; three heads of cabbage; five cartons of raw eggs; one bag of carrots and bell peppers; three baguettes; five packages of microwave rice; six frozen dried horse mackerel; one bottle of cola; eight bars of chocolate... And since our period was probably due soon, we bought sanitary products as well. We piled everything upon the cart until absolutely nothing more would fit, then reluctantly made our way to the register.

Japanese: レジのところには太っちょで髭を生やしたおじさんの店員さんが携帯電話をいじっていた。
English: A fat, bearded middle-aged clerk stood at the register, fiddling with his mobile phone.

Japanese: 「すみません」
English: “Excuse me.”

Japanese: 声をかけると、顔を上げて露骨に顔を顰める。
English: When we called to him, he looked up and frowned openly.

Japanese: 「これを下さい」
English: “We would like to buy these.”

Japanese: 「こんなに？」
English: “All of that?”

Japanese: 「そうです。これ全部です」
English: “Yes. Everything here.”

Japanese: 「怪我してるのかい？　顔色も死人みたいにあおっちろいじゃないか。それに、目がギンギラに金色になってる。そんなんじゃ売れないよ」
English: “Are you hurt? You’re pale as a corpse, and your eyes are shining bright gold. I can’t sell to someone like that.”

Japanese: 店員さんはレジを打とうとしないで、えらそうに腕組みをしている。
English: The clerk folded his arms self-importantly and made no move to operate the register.

Japanese: 「お金を払いますから売ってください」
English: “We will pay. Please sell them to us.”

Japanese: 私たちは無視して財布を取り出そうとしたけれど、財布が見つからない。
English: Ignoring him, we reached for our wallet. It was not there.

Japanese: 上着のポケットに確かに入れていたはずなのに。きっと八龍会の人たちに抜き取られたんだろう。
English: We had unquestionably put it in the pocket of our jacket. The people from Hachiryukai must have taken it.

Japanese: 「ほら、金も持ってないじゃないか。もう帰ってくれ。商品はおれが戻しておくから。……まったく、面倒くさい」
English: “See? You don’t even have any money. Go home. I’ll put all this back. ...Honestly, what a nuisance.”

Japanese: 身につけた服のポケットを上からポンポンと叩いていると店員さんは舌打ちをする。
English: As we patted each pocket of our clothing, the clerk clicked his tongue.

Japanese: 「お金はないみたいです。でも食べ物が必要なんです」
English: “It appears we have no money. But we need food.”

Japanese: 「そんなのおれの知ったことじゃないよ。おうちに帰ってお父さんかお母さんに頼んで買って貰うんだね」
English: “That’s no concern of mine. Go home and ask your father or mother to buy it for you.”

Japanese: 「お金は払いません。カートはちょっと邪魔なので、袋詰めしてください」
English: “We will not pay, then. The cart is rather cumbersome, so please put everything into bags.”

Japanese: 「話が全然通じないな。これだから金目は……」
English: “You don’t understand a word I’m saying. This is why Gold-Eyes are...”

Japanese: 店員さんは私たちに見せつけるように、さっきよりも大きく舌打ちをして、
English: The clerk clicked his tongue even more loudly than before, plainly making a show of it for us.

Japanese: 「お前じゃ話にならない。保護者はいるのかい？　その連絡先を……」
English: “There’s no talking to you. Do you have a guardian? Give me their contact—”

Japanese: 「いません。はやく袋詰めしてください。とてもだるくて……」
English: “We do not. Please hurry and bag everything. We feel terribly weak...”

Japanese: 「冗談じゃないよ！」
English: “You must be joking!”

Japanese: 店員さんは顔を真っ赤にして私たちを睨み付ける。
English: The clerk’s face went crimson as he glared at us.

Japanese: 「さっさと出て行くんだ。そうでなければ警察を呼ぶぞ？　それとも、病院にしてやろうか……」
English: “Get out of here at once, or I’ll call the police. Or would you rather I called a hospital...?”

Japanese: 店員さんはカウンターの後ろにある電話の受話器を握りしめた。
English: The clerk seized the telephone receiver behind the counter.

Japanese: その時、私たちにだけ聞こえる虫の羽音と人の声は一層大きくなった。
English: At that moment, the wingbeats and human voices that only we could hear grew louder still.

Japanese: 「ああもう、うるさいっ！」
English: “Oh, be quiet!”

Japanese: すると店内のどこに設置してあったのかエスパー探知機特有のあのけたたましい警報が鳴り響き、店員さんの背後にあった煙草の棚がベキッと乾いた音を立てて、並べてあった煙草のカートンごと潰れる。
English: The piercing alarm peculiar to psychic detectors erupted from somewhere in the store. Behind the clerk, a cigarette shelf buckled with a dry crack, crushing the cartons arranged upon it.

Japanese: 私たちはこんなところで能力なんか使うつもりじゃなかったのに。イライラしてついやってしまった。
English: We had not meant to use our power in a place like this. Irritation had made us do it without thinking.

Japanese: 店員さんは目を丸くしながら、割れて鋭い破片を剥き出しにしている棚を振り返る。
English: His eyes round, the clerk turned to stare at the shattered shelf and the sharp fragments now jutting from it.

Japanese: 「店員さん、こちらを見て私たちの話を聞いて下さい」
English: “Sir, please look at us and listen to what we have to say.”

Japanese: 頭痛のするこめかみを抑えながら私たちはなるべく冷静に店員さんに言う。
English: Pressing a hand to our aching temple, we addressed the clerk as calmly as we could.

Japanese: 背中におかしな冷や汗をかいている。変な興奮が、胸をドキドキとさせ、息をハアハアとさせる。
English: A strange, cold sweat covered our back. An inexplicable excitement set our heart pounding and left us panting for breath.

Japanese: 店員さんも私たちと同じように冷や汗をかきながらこちらを振り向いた。
English: Sweating just as we were, the clerk turned back toward us.

Japanese: しばらくこめかみを抑えていると、段々頭痛が治まり、耳鳴りも小さくなった。そのかわり、なんともいえない気だるさが身体にのしかかる。
English: After we held our temple for a while, the headache gradually subsided and the tinnitus diminished. In its place, an indescribable weariness settled heavily upon our body.

Japanese: 今私たちの身体と心は、なんて不安定なんだろう。まるで波の上にいるみたいだ。
English: How unstable our body and mind were. It was like being tossed upon a wave.

Japanese: 「このハム何で出来ているか知ってますか？」
English: “Do you know what this ham is made from?”

Japanese: 私たちは億劫な手を上げてカートの上のハムを指さした。
English: With a leaden hand, we pointed to the ham atop the cart.

Japanese: 「これは豚ですよね。私たちは、たくさんの豚を繁殖させ、工場みたいな狭い場所に閉じ込めて育て、殺してその肉をとっています。なんでかっていうと、私たちより豚が弱いからです。私たちは豚の他にもいろんな生き物を産ませたり殺したり食べたりしていますが、みんな納得してるわけじゃなくて、弱いから意志なんか関係ないんです」
English: “It is made from pigs, isn’t it? We breed great numbers of pigs, raise them confined in cramped places like factories, then kill them for their meat. Do you know why? Because pigs are weaker than we are. We breed, kill, and eat all sorts of living creatures besides pigs. They do not all consent to it. They are weak, so their wishes do not matter.”

Japanese: 私たちが喋っている後で、何かいろんなものが割れたり、倒れたりしたみたいで、もの凄い音がして、もの凄い悲鳴が聞こえる。
English: Behind us as we spoke, all manner of things seemed to break and topple. There were tremendous crashes and terrible screams.

Japanese: 私たちはわざとそんなのをやったわけじゃないけど、でも本当にイライラしてるから、きっと私たちのせいなんだろう。
English: We were not doing it deliberately, but we truly were irritated, so it was probably our fault.

Japanese: 「だから、本当だったら私たちはあなたの意志なんか無視して、あなたを殺して奪って行くのが自然なのかもしれません。でも、私たちは出来れば誰も殺したくないんです。それに、袋詰めも面倒そうだし……」
English: “By that logic, it might be natural for us to ignore your will, kill you, and take what we want. But we would prefer not to kill anyone. Besides, putting all of this into bags looks rather troublesome...”

Japanese: 店員さんはうっかり青白い顔になってしまっていて、その震える手をカウンターの下にのばす。彼は多分ものすごく必死で、素早くその動作を行っているんだろうけど、なんだかスローモーションみたいにゆっくり見えておかしい。
English: The clerk had inadvertently gone deathly pale. He reached a trembling hand beneath the counter. He must have been moving with desperate speed, but to us the whole motion looked strangely like slow motion.

Japanese: カウンターの下から取り出したのはショットガンだ。強盗撃退用のその武器を、私たちに向ける。
English: What he produced from beneath the counter was a shotgun, a weapon kept for robbers. He pointed it directly at us.

Japanese: そして何か言おうと唇を開く。その拍子に唾液の飛沫がたまになってくるくる回転しながら飛んで行くのが見える。
English: He opened his lips to say something. As he did, we saw droplets of saliva fly from his mouth, turning slowly through the air.

Japanese: 「おい、お前……」
English: “Listen, you...”

Japanese: 今度は私たちはちゃんと意識して力を使った。
English: This time, we used our power consciously.

Japanese: すると、ショットガンの銃身がぐにゃりと飴細工のように曲がる。
English: The shotgun barrel bent limply like soft candy.

Japanese: 店員さんはあんぐりと口をひらいて言いかけた言葉を飲み込む。
English: The clerk’s mouth fell open, and he swallowed the words he had begun to speak.

Japanese: 硬直して動かなくなった店員さんに私たちは言った。
English: We addressed the rigid, motionless man.

Japanese: 「ねえ、暴力はやめましょうよ。私たちはお互い賢くて素晴らしい人間なんだから、言葉を使ってコミュニケーションがとれるじゃないですか。それで解決したほうが素敵だと思いませんか？　どうします？　……なんだか、私たち、こうやって考えるのも喋るのもだんだんダルくなって来たんですけど」
English: “Come now, let us stop this violence. We are all intelligent, wonderful human beings, so we can communicate through language. Wouldn’t it be nicer to settle matters that way? What do you say? ...Although thinking and speaking like this are gradually becoming rather exhausting for us.”

Japanese: そして私たちは溜息をついた。
English: Then we sighed.

Japanese: 店員さんはとても丁寧に袋詰めをしてくれた。
English: The clerk bagged everything with the utmost care.

Japanese: 大きめのレジ袋が六つ、食材でパンパンに膨らんでいる。カートで駐車場の端まで運んで、そこでタクシーを止め運転手さんの手を借りてトランクや後部座席に積み込んだ。
English: Six large shopping bags bulged with food. We pushed them in the cart to the edge of the parking lot, hailed a taxi there, and enlisted the driver’s help to load them into the trunk and back seat.

Japanese: そしてコシチェイが隠れ家にいていたあの洋館まで運んで貰った。支払いは、シンディマートのレジから拝借したお金を使った。
English: We had him take us to the old mansion where Koschei had been staying. We paid the fare with money borrowed from Cindy Mart’s register.

Japanese: このあたりのエスパー探知機はエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスが取り外してある。私たちは誰の目も気にすることなく、能力をつかって透明人間に六つの袋を運ばせた。
English: Yevgeny Ilyich Hess had removed the psychic detectors around this area. With no need to concern ourselves with watching eyes, we used our power and made the invisible person carry all six bags.

Japanese: 財布をとられていたけれど鍵は奪われておらず、それで玄関のドアを開けた。
English: Our wallet had been taken, but not our key, so we used it to open the front door.

Japanese: そうして私たち三人が暮らしていたその建物にやっと帰って来ると、身体の疲労が一片に襲ってきてもうそれ以上一歩も歩く気がしなかった。
English: When we finally returned to the building where the three of us had lived, exhaustion descended upon our body all at once. We had no desire to take another step.

Japanese: ドアから入ったすぐのところにへたり込むと、その場で袋の中のものをその辺りにまき散らして、手づかみで食事をはじめた。
English: We sank to the floor just inside the door, emptied the bags around us where we sat, and began eating with our hands.

Japanese: 牛乳をパックの口を破ってごくごくと飲む。牛乳がこぼれて胸元を汚したけれどいまさら気にしてなんかいられない。
English: We tore open the top of a carton and gulped down the milk. It spilled across our chest, but at that point we could hardly care.

Japanese: そして、ラップを剥がしてキャベツを洗わないまま剥がして口につめこみ、そしてまるごとのハムを包んである網のようなものを破ってからかじりつき、オリーブオイルを瓶に直接口をつけて流し込む。
English: We stripped the wrapping from a cabbage, tore off its leaves without washing them, and stuffed them into our mouth. Then we ripped through the netting around one of the whole hams and bit into it, and finally pressed our lips directly to the bottle of olive oil and poured it down our throat.

Japanese: それらが喉の奥を通り過ぎて胃に辿り着くと、食欲のわりには内臓の方はまだそんなに充分に機能していないみたいだった。ものすごい勢いで逆流して、私たちはうわっとその場に詰め込んだばかりのものを口から吐き出してしまう。
English: Once all of it passed down our throat and reached our stomach, it appeared that despite our appetite, our organs were not yet functioning well enough. Everything surged back with incredible force, and with a cry, we vomited what we had just crammed into our mouth all over the floor.

Japanese: もったいないことをした。これじゃ、身体が回復しない。
English: What a waste. At this rate, our body would never recover.

Japanese: 私たちはもう一度同じように牛乳を飲み、キャベツをつめこみ、ハムを囓り、オリーブオイルを飲む。また吐き気がしたけれど、今度はちゃんと心の準備していたから吐くことはなかった。
English: We drank milk again, stuffed cabbage into our mouth, gnawed at the ham, and swallowed olive oil. Nausea returned, but this time we had prepared ourselves and did not vomit.

Japanese: 両手で口を押さえ、下からせり上がって来たものを無理矢理飲み込む。そうすると、やっと内臓が我を取り戻してくれたようで消化を開始してくれた。
English: We covered our mouth with both hands and forced down everything rising from below. At last, our organs seemed to regain their senses and began digesting the food.

Japanese: 一旦内臓が動き出すと、食べたものが身体に取り込まれて行く不思議な恍惚感が心を支配する。
English: Once our organs began working, a strange ecstasy took possession of our mind as the food was absorbed into our body.

Japanese: 私たちは生卵の空を割って立て続けに三つ飲み込み、ピーマンを種もヘタもとらずにそのままむさぼり、咀嚼もあいまいなまま牛乳で流し込んだ。
English: We cracked three raw eggs and swallowed them in rapid succession. We devoured a bell pepper without removing either seeds or stem, scarcely chewed it, and washed it down with milk.

Japanese: 顔も服も食べ物でドロドロに汚しながら食べ続け、途中で途轍もなく眠くなったので少しまどろみ、起きたら食べ、そしたまた眠り、尿意で目が覚めてトイレで済ませてから戻ってくるとまた食べた。そうしている間に、窓が明るくなったり暗くなったりしていた。
English: We continued eating, smearing our face and clothes with food. Partway through, we became impossibly sleepy and dozed for a while. When we woke, we ate; then we slept again. The need to urinate woke us, so we went to the toilet, returned, and resumed eating. As this continued, the windows brightened and darkened around us.

Japanese: 何日過ぎたのかわからない。三日くらいだと思う。もしかしたら五日くらい過ぎたのかな？　目が覚めると、すっかり身体が軽くなって、気分がよくなっているのを感じた。
English: We did not know how many days had passed. Perhaps three. Or could it have been five? When we woke, our body felt wonderfully light, and we felt well.

Japanese: 全身が血と埃と食べ物で汚れて悪臭を放っている。バスルームに言って石けんでよく全身を洗い、ムダ毛を処理して、そしてバスタブに張った湯につかると生まれ変わったような気持ちになった。
English: Our entire body was filthy with blood, dust, and food, and gave off a foul odor. We went to the bathroom, washed ourselves thoroughly with soap, removed our unwanted body hair, and sank into a tub of hot water. It felt as though we had been born anew.

Japanese: 文字通り、本当に生まれ変わったようだ。銃で撃たれた場所はもう塞がって痕跡がなく、少し耳鳴りや幻聴はするけれども、身体の隅々まで力が行き渡って充実した気分だった。
English: Quite literally, we truly seemed to have been reborn. The place where the bullet struck had closed without leaving a trace. There was still some tinnitus and we could still hear voices, but power filled every corner of our body, leaving us brimming with energy.

Japanese: 鏡を見ると、瞳は相変わらず金色のままだ。
English: When we looked into the mirror, our eyes remained gold.

Japanese: 松子やコシチェイのように、興奮しなくてもずっと金色のままでいられるようになったのだろう。
English: Perhaps, like Matsuko and Koschei, they had become permanently gold even when we were not excited.

Japanese: あるいは発症しているのかな？
English: Or had our symptoms manifested?

Japanese: でも、発症したらもっとありえない幻覚が見えて、わけのわからない世界に囚われるんじゃないかしら？
English: But if they had, shouldn’t we be seeing even more impossible hallucinations and become trapped in some incomprehensible world?

Japanese: そうなってないから発症はしてないないと思うんだけど、でも、ああいうのってきっと自覚が出来ないものだから自信がない。
English: Since nothing like that had happened, we did not think our symptoms had manifested. Then again, it was surely the kind of thing one could not recognize in oneself, so we were not certain.

Japanese: まあ、すがすがしい気持ちなのは間違いないのだから、どっちでもいいんだろう。
English: Well, there was no doubt that we felt refreshed. The distinction probably did not matter.

Japanese: とにかく、これからのことを考えなくちゃいけない。
English: In any event, we had to decide what to do next.

Japanese: 私たちは片方が死んで、コシチェイは行方不明だ。
English: One of us was dead, and Koschei was missing.

Japanese: 私たちはいまタイプBの身体能力と、タイプAの念動力の両方が使える。
English: We could now use both the physical powers of a Type B and the psychokinesis of a Type A.

Japanese: あと、念動力は前よりもずっと強い力が使えるようにになったらしい。
English: Our psychokinesis also appeared to have grown far stronger than before.

Japanese: だって、そうじゃなければ倉庫のシャッターをこじ開けたり、シンディマートで鉄砲の銃身を曲げたり出来るはずがないもの。あの時は頭が朦朧としていてそうした力の変化に全く気がつかなかったけれども、今思うとあきらかにおかしい。
English: Otherwise, we could never have forced open the warehouse shutter or bent the shotgun barrel at Cindy Mart. Our mind had been so clouded at the time that we never noticed the change in our power, but in retrospect it was clearly extraordinary.

Japanese: 私たちの透明人間の腕力は、大体私たちと同じくらいの腕力だった。前はノーマルだったからノーマルなりの力しか出せなかったけど、今はタイプBとしての力がそのまま透明人間にも反映されているんだと思う。いや、それ以上なのかな？　あんな鉄の棒をひん曲げるなんて、前も金眼になっても出来ることじゃなかったし……腕力も強化されているのかしら？
English: The invisible person’s physical strength had always been roughly equal to our own. We had been Normal before, so it could exert only a Normal person’s strength. Perhaps our present Type B strength was now reflected in it directly. Or was it even stronger? We could not have bent an iron bar like that before, even with our eyes gold... Had our physical strength been enhanced as well?

Japanese: なんにしろ、私たちの力はこれまでとは別物だということだ。
English: Whatever the case, our power had become something altogether different.

Japanese: これなら、見土道夫とやりあっても負けないのかな？　そうだとしたら、行動の幅が大分広がる……。
English: Could we fight Michio Mido now without losing? If so, we had far more options...

Japanese: これから何をするか考えよう。
English: We considered what to do next.

Japanese: コシチェイは多分八龍会に捕獲されている。あの人たちはコシチェイの正体や、その能力をどの程度詳しく知っているのか……。正確にはわからないけれど、多分コシチェイを本当に殺す方法を詳しく知ってるということはないと思う。
English: Koschei had probably been captured by Hachiryukai. How much did those people know about his true identity and abilities? We could not be sure, but they probably did not possess detailed knowledge of how to kill him for good.

Japanese: それに、いくら痛めつけても死なないのなら、彼らにはうってつけだろう。
English: And if he would not die no matter how badly they hurt him, he was perfectly suited to their purposes.

Japanese: だって、八龍会の人たちは『ネオ・ローズ』の作り方を知らないんだもの。どこかに閉じ込めて、拷問だとか、色々なことをして聞き出そうとするんじゃないかな？　私たちだったらそうする。何て言ったって『ネオ・ローズ』が彼らの生命線なのは明白なのだから。あれがなければ、YSと戦うことも、この街をタイプBのものにすることも出来やしない。
English: After all, the people of Hachiryukai did not know how to make Neo Rose. Wouldn’t they imprison him somewhere and use torture and every other means they could devise to make him tell them? We would. Neo Rose was plainly their lifeline. Without it, they could neither fight YS nor make this city belong to the Type Bs.

Japanese: コシチェイの服が残っていた。白いロングＴシャツは袖をまくればいい。黒いズボンは裾を切った。それを身につけながら考えた。
English: Koschei’s clothes were still here. We could roll up the sleeves of the long white T-shirt. We cut the black trouser legs short. As we dressed, we continued to think.

Japanese: 頭はすっきりとして、調子がいい。あんな傷を負っていたのにすごい。休養と、補給をすればこんなに回復出来るんだ、いまの私たちの身体は。
English: Our mind was clear, and we felt well. The recovery was astonishing after injuries like ours. With rest and replenishment, this body of ours could heal that completely.

Japanese: ――それにしても、このタイミングで八龍会が裏切ってくるとは。
English: —Even so, for Hachiryukai to betray us at precisely this moment...

Japanese: エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスも警戒してはいたんだ。レシピを独占している以上、あの人たちに快く思われることはないって。でも、八龍会も今はYSを相手にしたり、難しい時期だし、何かあるとしてももっと先だと思ってた。
English: Yevgeny Ilyich Hess had been wary of them. As long as he monopolized the formula, he knew they would resent him. But Hachiryukai was already contending with YS, and this was a difficult time for them. Even if something happened, we had expected it much later.

Japanese: それが、今やって来るなんて。
English: For it to happen now...

Japanese: レシピもわからないのに、襲われたエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスが不死身じゃなくて、本当に死んじゃったらどうするつもりなんだろう？　ネオ・ローズがなければ解放軍も維持出来ないし、完全に終わりになっちゃうのに。
English: What had they intended to do if Yevgeny Ilyich Hess was not immortal and truly died in their attack, when they did not even know the formula? Without Neo Rose, they could not maintain the Liberation Army. It would all be completely over.

Japanese: 何か情報を掴んでいたのあ。……それとも、あんまり頭がよくないのかな？
English: Had they obtained some information? ...Or were they simply not very intelligent?

Japanese: まあそれはいいか。
English: Well, that did not matter.

Japanese: 私たちが目指すのは、あのコシチェイの救出。そのために、情報を集めなくちゃ。そもそも、生きてるって私たちが勝手に思い込んでるだけで、無事かどうかってことすらわからない。ここで私たちがのんきに食べて寝ている間、八龍会が何をしたのか探らなきゃいけない。携帯電話も没収されてしまったみたいでなくなった。調べる手段は限られている。
English: Our objective was to rescue Koschei. To do so, we needed information. For all we knew, our belief that he was alive was merely an assumption; we did not even know whether he was safe. We had to discover what Hachiryukai had done while we took our time eating and sleeping here. Our mobile phone appeared to have been confiscated as well. The means available to us were limited.

Japanese: そして、結局シンプルなやりかたを使うことにした。
English: In the end, we chose a simple method.

Japanese: 夕方になってから私たちは建物を出る。目指すは暗闇通り。女の人と遊ぶ店ばかりが有名なその通りには、飲み屋さんも沢山建ち並んでいる。そのすぐ近くの、薄暗い人の入りにくい路地には地元の人間しか行かないような小さな店がいくつかあって、八龍会の人たちがよく集まる店もそこにあることも知っている。
English: We left the building that evening and made for Darkness Street. The street was famous primarily for establishments offering female company, but it was also lined with bars. Nearby, in dim alleys that discouraged strangers, stood several small places patronized almost exclusively by locals. We knew that members of Hachiryukai often gathered at one of them.

Japanese: はじめはその近くの暗がりに潜んで、八龍会の誰かが出て来るのを待っていた。出て来たら、その人を拉致して話を聞こうと思ったんだ。だけど、じっと待つというのはどうにも性にあわない。
English: At first, we hid in the darkness nearby and waited for someone from Hachiryukai to emerge. Once someone did, we intended to abduct him and make him talk. Sitting and waiting, however, was not in our nature.

Japanese: こんな小さな店なら、どうせ大した人数もいないだろう。
English: A little establishment like this could hardly contain very many people.

Japanese: ということで、私たちは待ちきれなくなって正面のドアを開いた。
English: And so, unable to wait any longer, we opened the front door.

Japanese: この街にはいろんな異国の雰囲気を模して売り出す飲食店が多いけれど、そこはとりたてて個性のない店だ。強いて言えばイギリス風のパブに似ているのかもしれない。薄暗い店内にはテーブル席とカウンターがあり、お酒とおつまみを提供している。単に食事のために来るのもOKらしい。実際に店内に入るのは初めてだけれど、カレーなんかも美味しいという話だ。
English: Many restaurants in this city traded on the atmosphere of one foreign country or another, but this one had no particular character. At most, it might have resembled a British pub. The dim interior held tables and a counter, and offered alcohol and bar snacks. Apparently it was fine to come only for a meal. This was our first time inside, but we had heard that the curry was good.

Japanese: 店内に足を踏み入れた私たちを、カウンターでドリンクを作っている白いワイシャツ姿のひげもじゃの店員さんが見る。愛想のない人で、いらっしゃいとも何とも言わない。そして、私たちの素性にも気がつかなかったらしく、
English: As we entered, a shaggy-bearded clerk in a white dress shirt looked up from mixing drinks behind the counter. He was an unfriendly man who offered neither welcome nor greeting. Nor did he appear to recognize us.

Japanese: 「カウンター席へどうぞ」
English: “Please take a seat at the counter.”

Japanese: とだけ素っ気なく声をかけた。
English: That was all he said, and he said it flatly.

Japanese: 今私たちは変装のつもりで屋敷にあった帽子と眼鏡をつけている。眼鏡はエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスが使っているもので、きつい度が入っているからレンズを通すとぼやけて見えた。私たちはそれをずり下げて、レンズの上から店内を見回す。
English: As our attempt at a disguise, we wore a hat and glasses found in the mansion. The glasses belonged to Yevgeny Ilyich Hess. Their powerful prescription made everything blur when we looked through the lenses, so we slid them down our nose and surveyed the room over their upper rims.

Japanese: 店内は賑わっていて、男たちが酒を酌み交わし、談笑している。そのうちの半分くらいは目が金色に輝いている。ということは、多分ネオ・ローズの使用者だろう。
English: The place was lively, with men drinking together and chatting. Roughly half of them had eyes shining gold. They were probably users of Neo Rose.

Japanese: ここにいるのはほとんど八龍会の人間だろうし、その辺の誰かに話しかければいいのだろうけれど、誰に訊くのが一番いいんだろう。一番えらそうにしている人がいいのかな？
English: Almost everyone here likely belonged to Hachiryukai, and we could presumably question any one of them. But who would be best? Perhaps whoever looked the most important?

Japanese: 入り口の側で立ったまま物色していると、
English: As we stood beside the entrance searching the room, a voice called to us.

Japanese: 「お姉ちゃん」
English: “Hey, sweetheart.”

Japanese: 無精髭を生やした男がアルコールで真っ赤にそまった顔にだらしない笑顔を浮かべて私たちに話しかけてくる。
English: An unshaven man with a face flushed scarlet by alcohol addressed us through a sloppy grin.

Japanese: 「誰か、人探しか？　まだ来てないんじゃないのか。それなら一緒に飲んで待とうじゃないか」
English: “Looking for someone? Doesn’t seem like they’ve arrived yet. Why don’t you have a drink with me while you wait?”

Japanese: 酒臭い息を浴びせてくるのから顔を背けると、胸に小さなバッジが光っているのが目に入った。
English: We turned our face from his liquor-soaked breath and noticed a small badge gleaming upon his chest.

Japanese: 「あなた、解放軍の人？」
English: “Are you with the Liberation Army?”

Japanese: 「おお、そうとも。よくわかったな。今をときめく八龍解放軍のフルカワショウジと言えばおれのことだ」
English: “I certainly am. Well spotted. When people speak of Shoji Furukawa of the celebrated Hachiryu Liberation Army, they mean me.”

Japanese: 自慢げに言うけれど、そんな名前は聞いたことがない。
English: He said it proudly, but we had never heard the name.

Japanese: 「偉い人なの？」
English: “Are you important?”

Japanese: 「えらいとも。病院襲撃のときも、フェルナンデスをやったときも、大活躍したんだぜ。隊長のカミラって知ってるだろ？　今でこそえらそうにしてるが、最初は臆病でひどいもんだった。病院襲撃のときにピシっと言ってやったのがおれさ」
English: “Of course I am. I played a major part in the hospital attack and when we got Fernandes. You know our commander, Camilla, don’t you? She puts on airs now, but she was a terrible coward at first. I’m the one who set her straight during the hospital attack.”

Japanese: 「ふーん」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 「信じてないのか？　じゃあ、おれがどんな風に活躍してたか詳しく話してやろう。丁度今も、向こうの席でみんなに話してやっていたところでな……」
English: “You don’t believe me? Then I’ll tell you exactly what I did. I was just telling everyone at that table over there the whole story...”

Japanese: フルカワショウジは私たちの肩に手を回す。酒臭さが呼んでもいないのに向こうから近寄ってきたので私たちは顔を背ける。
English: Shoji Furukawa put an arm around our shoulders. The reek of alcohol approached without invitation, and we turned our face away.

Japanese: 倉庫には見土道夫もいた。つまり、私たちを襲ったのは八龍解放軍に間違いないということだ。
English: Michio Mido had been at the warehouse. That meant there was no question that the people who attacked us belonged to the Hachiryu Liberation Army.

Japanese: 「信じるよ。私たちも解放軍の人に会いたかったんだ」
English: “We believe you. We wanted to meet someone from the Liberation Army ourselves.”

Japanese: 「そうか。それなら話が早い。じゃあ、この店じゃなくて二人きりで少し話でもするか」
English: “Then that makes things easy. Why don’t the two of us leave this place and talk in private?”

Japanese: 男はそう言って、店の奥の裏口を顎で示す。あそこから出ると確か狭い裏路地に抜けて、連れ込み宿が建ち並ぶ通りに出るんだ。
English: As he spoke, the man indicated the rear exit with his chin. If memory served, it opened into a narrow back alley leading to a street lined with love hotels.

Japanese: 「わかったよ」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: 「とびっきりの面白い話があるんだ」
English: “I’ve got a particularly entertaining story for you.”

Japanese: 「それは楽しみだね」
English: “We look forward to it.”

Japanese: そして混雑する店内を通り抜け、裏口へ出ようとしたんだけれども、その途中で呼び止められた。
English: We began making our way through the crowded establishment toward the rear exit. Before we reached it, however, someone called us to a stop.

Japanese: 「あっ、お前は！」
English: “Ah! You!”

Japanese: トイレから出て来た男とすれ違おうとしたら、その男は私たちの顔を見て大きな声を出したのだ。
English: As we were about to pass a man emerging from the toilet, he saw our face and shouted.

Japanese: 「間違いない、あの時の！」
English: “There’s no mistake! You’re the one from before!”

Japanese: あの時とはどの時だろう？
English: Which time did he mean?

Japanese: きょとんとしてその顔を見上げると、そうだ、この人はあの時倉庫にいたやつじゃないか。
English: We looked up at his face in blank confusion. Then we remembered. This man had been in the warehouse.

Japanese: 確か名前をシミズと言ったはずだ。
English: His name had been Shimizu, if memory served.

Japanese: ネオ・ローズの管理をする八龍会側の人間で、コシチェイのビジネスパートナーだ。
English: He was Hachiryukai’s representative in the management of Neo Rose and Koschei’s business partner.

Japanese: 「おい、そんなやつ放っておいていこうぜ」
English: “Hey, forget that bastard. Let’s go.”

Japanese: フルカワショウジが肩に手を置くのを私たちは振り払ってシミズに向き直る。
English: We brushed Shoji Furukawa’s hand from our shoulder and turned to face Shimizu.

Japanese: 「あんた、あの時倉庫にいた人だね。私たちをはめたんだ」
English: “You were there at the warehouse. You set us up.”

Japanese: 「おい、どうやって生き返ったんだ？　確かに胸を撃たれて死んだはずだ。おれは、ちゃんと心臓が止まってるのを確認したんだぞ？」
English: “How the hell did you come back to life? You were shot in the chest. You were dead—I checked that your heart had stopped myself!”

Japanese: シミズは顔を真っ青にして金切り声をあげる。
English: Shimizu’s face went white as he shrieked the words.

Japanese: 「おい、どういうことだよ？　知り合いなのか？」
English: “Hey, what’s this about? You know each other?”

Japanese: フルカワショウジは怪訝な顔で言う。
English: Shoji Furukawa spoke with a puzzled expression.

Japanese: 「ごめん、あなたとの話は後にする。先にこの人に話を聞く」
English: “Sorry. We will hear your story later. First, we need to speak with this man.”

Japanese: 「あぁっ？」
English: “Huh?”

Japanese: フルカワショウジは顔を思い切り歪めて大声を張り上げ、すごんでみせる。
English: Shoji Furukawa contorted his face, bellowed, and did his best to look menacing.

Japanese: 子供のときから不思議なんだけど、この手の人たちはどうしてこんなに即座に怒ることが出来るんだろう？　この、ちょっといやなことがあっただけで即座に沸騰して目一杯威圧的な行動をとる、という技術はみなどこで学ぶんだろうか。威圧のしかたも大体同じような感じだもの。そういう学校があるのかな？
English: We had wondered about people like him since childhood. How could they become angry so instantly? Where did they all learn the trick of boiling over at the slightest displeasure and immediately behaving with the maximum possible menace? Even their methods of intimidation were broadly alike. Was there a school that taught it?

Japanese: 「うるさいなあ」
English: “You’re very loud.”

Japanese: 私たちはフルカワショウジに言って、その胸を透明人間の手でどんと突き飛ばす。
English: We said it to Shoji Furukawa, then shoved him sharply in the chest with the invisible person’s hand.

Japanese: 「えっ、えっ……」
English: “What? What...?”

Japanese: フルカワショウジは数歩うしろによろけながら目を丸くしている。
English: Shoji Furukawa staggered several steps backward, his eyes wide.

Japanese: 「シミズ、あなたは見土道夫と組んでエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスと私たちのもう片方を穴だらけにしたんだ」
English: “Shimizu, you joined forces with Michio Mido and shot Yevgeny Ilyich Hess and the other half of us full of holes.”

Japanese: そんなに怒ってはいないつもりだったけれど、こうして実行犯の一人を目の当たりにすると腹が立った。
English: We had not thought ourselves especially angry. Now that one of the people who had carried it out stood before us, however, rage began to rise.

Japanese: 「知ってることを全部話してもらうからね」
English: “You are going to tell us everything you know.”

Japanese: 「くっ！」
English: “Damn it!”

Japanese: シミズは懐に手を入れると、拳銃を取り出す。
English: Shimizu reached into his coat and drew a handgun.

Japanese: 『ネオ・ローズ』で発症をコントロールされている彼はノーマルよりは動きが速いが、私たちからすればそれほどではない。
English: With his symptoms controlled by Neo Rose, he moved faster than a Normal, but not especially fast from our perspective.

Japanese: 私たちは力を使って、その銃を抜いた右手を外側にねじる。
English: Using our power, we wrenched his gun hand outward.

Japanese: 「ぐあっ」
English: “Gah!”

Japanese: 思わず唸るはシミズ。
English: Shimizu groaned despite himself.

Japanese: 銃口をそらすだけのつもりが、力が入りすぎて捻った拍子に彼の肘と手首からパキッポキッと乾いた音が鳴った。
English: We had intended only to turn the muzzle aside. We used too much force, and his elbow and wrist answered our twist with sharp, dry cracks.

Japanese: 「うっ、あああっ……」
English: “Ngh—aaagh...”

Japanese: その手から銃が落ちるのを、私たちは屈んで拾い上げる。
English: The gun fell from his hand. We crouched and picked it up.

Japanese: シミズが取り出したのはリボルバー式のかっこいい拳銃だ。この街の人は弾を沢山撃ちたがるからオートマチックの拳銃ばっかり使うけど、私たちは昔から映画とかでよくみるこっちの方が断然好きだ。
English: Shimizu had drawn a cool revolver. People in this city liked to fire a great many rounds and therefore used automatic pistols almost exclusively. We had always preferred revolvers by far, having so often seen them in films.

Japanese: 「おいっ！　何をしている！　お前は何者だッ！」
English: “Hey! What are you doing? Who the hell are you?”

Japanese: フルカワショウジがそう叫ぶ。
English: Shoji Furukawa shouted the question.

Japanese: それで気がついたのだけれど、店内にたくさんいるお客さんたちはみな私たちとシミズに注目している。みんなが一片に黙ってしまったから、店内に流れるどこかで聞いたことのある古いロックの曲がよく聞こえる。
English: Only then did we notice that the many customers in the bar were watching Shimizu and us. They had all fallen silent at once, making the familiar old rock song playing inside remarkably clear.

Japanese: 「私たちは灰上」
English: “We are Haigami.”

Japanese: 自分を見つめるいくつもの金色の目を見渡しながら私たちは言った。
English: We spoke while surveying the many golden eyes fixed upon us.

Japanese: 「あなたたちが利用して裏切ったエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスの友だちだよ」
English: “We are friends of Yevgeny Ilyich Hess, whom you used and then betrayed.”
“Hess...”

Japanese: 「ヘスだと……」
English: “Did she say Hess...?”

Japanese: 私たちの言葉で、お客さんたちの何人かがざわつきはじめる。
English: Our words set several of the patrons murmuring.

Japanese: 「あなたたちに、私たちのもう一人は殺された。でもそれはどうでもいい。あの臭いお爺さんの話をきかせて。知りたいことを全部教えてくれたら何もしないわ」
English: “You killed the other one of us. But that does not matter. Tell us about that stinking old man. If you tell us everything we wish to know, we will do nothing to you.”

Japanese: 「何もしないだってさ」
English: “She says she won’t do anything.”

Japanese: 「へ、多少超能力が使えるのかもしれないが、ずいぶんと大きく出たもんだ」
English: “Heh. Maybe you can use a little psychic power, but that’s some mighty big talk.”

Japanese: 人混みのなかから笑い声が漏れる。
English: Laughter leaked from within the crowd.

Japanese: 「もし私たちの邪魔をするのなら、その時は……」
English: “If you interfere with us, then...”

Japanese: 言いかけたとき、右手の人混みから誰かが飛び出してくる。
English: Before we could finish, someone sprang from the crowd to our right.

Japanese: 金色の目を光らせて手を伸ばしたその人が狙ったのは、私たちが握っている拳銃だ。身体能力には自信があるらしく、思ったより速い動きで拳銃を捕まれてしまう。
English: The golden-eyed man reached for the handgun in our grasp. Evidently confident in his physical abilities, he moved faster than expected and caught hold of it.

Japanese: 腕力は私たちより強い。銃口は彼の力で無理矢理天井を向けさせられる。引き金を引いてももう誰にも当たらない。
English: He was physically stronger than we were. By sheer force, he turned the muzzle toward the ceiling. Even if we pulled the trigger now, we could hit no one.

Japanese: 「へっ」
English: “Heh.”

Japanese: そして勝ち誇った表情を浮かべたその男の頭を、私たちは捻った。
English: We twisted the triumphant man’s head.

Japanese: バキッとひときわ大きな音を立ててその人の首はほとんど真後ろを向く。そして糸が切れた人形のように全身から力が抜けて、彼は床の上に倒れた。
English: With an exceptionally loud crack, his neck turned almost completely backward. All strength left his body like a puppet whose strings had been cut, and he collapsed upon the floor.

Japanese: 「これを……」
English: “Look at—”

Japanese: 私たちが言おうとしたとき、今度は左手のほうの暗闇で一瞬何か光り、パンと音がした。誰かが拳銃を撃ったのだ。
English: As we began to speak, something flashed for an instant in the darkness to our left. A sharp report followed. Someone had fired a handgun.

Japanese: 私たちの右胸に穴が空き、喉の奥から血が這い上ってくる。
English: A hole opened in the right side of our chest, and blood crept up the back of our throat.

Japanese: 目をこらすと銃を握ってこちらをニヤニヤとして見ている男の顔が見えたので、その首も捻った。
English: Peering into the darkness, we made out the grinning face of a man holding a gun. We twisted his neck as well.

Japanese: そして同じように骨の砕ける音を立てて、男はその場に倒れる。
English: His bones broke with the same sound, and the man fell where he stood.

Japanese: 私たちは喉からせり上がって来た血をそのままべしゃっと床の上に吐いてから言った。
English: We spat the blood rising through our throat onto the floor with a wet splatter, then spoke.

Japanese: 「これを見ろっ！　死んだ人たちを！　もう生き返らないんだぞ！　二度と酒も飲めないし、笑うこともない。永久にだ！　それでも私たちに逆らう理由なんかあるのか？　私たちは話を聞きたいだけなんだ……。どうしてもって言うなら相手になるよ。でも、胸を撃ったって、頭を撃ったって無駄だよ。私たちは死にはしないんだから。邪魔をするならみんな殺してあげる」
English: “Look at this! Look at the people who died! They will never live again. They will never drink or laugh again. Never! What possible reason could you have to resist us? We only want to ask you questions... If you insist, we will fight you. But shooting us in the chest or the head is useless. We will not die. If you interfere, we will kill every one of you.”

Japanese: 言っているうちにまた血がのぼってきたので、それも吐いた。
English: As we spoke, more blood climbed our throat, and we spat that out as well.

Japanese: それで私たちを見ているものたちの空気が変わったような気がする。私たちに対して怯えている。みんながみんな好戦的な性格ってわけじゃないんだろう。普通の人もたくさんいるんだ。
English: The atmosphere among the people watching us seemed to change. They were afraid. They could not all be eager for combat. Many of them must have been ordinary people.

Japanese: フルカワショウジも顔を真っ青にして、壁に背をこすりつけるようにして立っている。さっきはもう少し近くにいたのに。怖くて後ろに下がっちゃったのかな。
English: Shoji Furukawa had gone deathly pale and stood with his back pressed hard against the wall. He had been closer a moment ago. Had fear made him retreat?

Japanese: シミズも痛む腕を押さえ、顔にもの凄い量の脂汗を流し、唇を震わせ、私たちを見ている。
English: Shimizu clutched his injured arm. Greasy sweat poured down his face, and his lips trembled as he stared at us.

Japanese: 人に怯えた目で見られるのは、子供の時から慣れている。
English: People had looked upon us with frightened eyes ever since we were children. We were accustomed to it.

Japanese: 私たちはちょっとほっとした。いくら撃たれて死なないと言っても、痛いことは痛いし、頭でも撃たれれば多分倒れて意識を失って復活まで時間がかかるだろうし、いいことなんかないので、諦めてくれるならそれはそれで嬉しい。それに、人を殺すのは好きじゃないんだ。こんなのを喜んでやるアレクセイはどうかしている。死体なんか、どう考えたって生きている人間よりつまらないのに。
English: We felt somewhat relieved. Even if a bullet could not kill us, it still hurt. A shot to the head would probably knock us down and render us unconscious, and resurrection would take time. None of that would do us any good, so we were glad enough if they meant to give up. Besides, we did not like killing people. There was something wrong with Alexei for doing this with pleasure. However one looked at it, a corpse was far less interesting than a living person.

Japanese: でも、今自分がこの人数のタイプBとやってどれくらい戦えるんだろう？　ちょっと興味はある。だけど、さすがに試そうとは思わない。
English: Still, we were a little curious about how well we could fight this many Type Bs at once. We had no intention of actually testing it.

Japanese: 「じゃあ質問をさせてもらうよ。本当に、私たちは質問するだけなんだからね。それだけのことを従ってくれれば最初から暴力なんかふるわなかったし、誰も死ななかったのに、まったく馬鹿みたい。ここに残ったみんなはもっと賢明なことを祈るわ」
English: “Now, allow us to ask our questions. We truly mean to do nothing more than ask. If you had cooperated in that one respect from the beginning, we would never have used violence and no one would have died. What utter stupidity. We hope everyone still alive will prove wiser.”

Japanese: 私たちはそして、激痛で震えているシミズを見た。それだけで、彼は怯えてびくっとする。
English: Then we looked at Shimizu, who was trembling with intense pain. That alone made him flinch in terror.

Japanese: 「まずシミズさん。あの日のことを教えて。あなたたちは最初から私たちを罠にかけるつもりだったの？」
English: “Let us begin with you, Mr. Shimizu. Tell us about that day. Were you planning to trap us from the beginning?”

Japanese: シミズは首をガクガクと痙攣させるように頷く。
English: Shimizu nodded so violently that his head seemed to convulse.

Japanese: 「あ、あのヘスだけをやるつもりだったんだ。あんたたちがついて来るとは知らなかったから、予定とは違ったが……」
English: “W-we only meant to get Hess. We didn’t know you were coming with him, so that part wasn’t in the plan...”

Japanese: 「主謀者は見土道夫？」
English: “Was Michio Mido the ringleader?”

Japanese: 「誰かはわからないが、解放軍の幹部で相談して決めたらしい」
English: “I don’t know who started it, but apparently the officers of the Liberation Army discussed it and made the decision.”

Japanese: 「幹部って、具体的に誰？」
English: “Which officers, specifically?”

Japanese: 「見土さん、ノーサムさん、田中さんの三人だと思う。その場におれがいたわけじゃないからわからないが……」
English: “I think it was Mr. Mido, Ms. Northam, and Mr. Tanaka. I wasn’t there myself, so I don’t know for sure...”

Japanese: 「なんで裏切ったの？　まだ協力してやったほうがいいんじゃないかと思うんだけど？」
English: “Why did you betray him? It seems to us that continuing to cooperate would have served you better.”

Japanese: 「なんでも、ヘスには変身能力やら、恐ろしいサイキック能力があるから危険だって……」
English: “They said Hess was dangerous—that he had the power to transform and some terrifying psychic ability...”

Japanese: 「なるほど、その辺りのことも知ってたわけだね」
English: “I see. So you knew about those things as well.”

Japanese: だとすれば話はわかりやすい。サイキックが必要以上に恐れられ、信用されないというのはよくあることだ。
English: If so, the situation was simple enough to understand. Psychics were often feared beyond reason and distrusted.

Japanese: それにしても、エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスは自分の能力は八龍会には知られていないとうそぶいていたけれど、やっぱりバレてたんじゃないか。偉そうなことばかり言っているけれど、本当に駄目なお爺さんだ。ボケてるのか、それとも発症しちゃってるんじゃないの？　真に受けて損した。
English: Still, Yevgeny Ilyich Hess had boasted that Hachiryukai knew nothing of his abilities. They had found him out after all. For someone who did nothing but speak grandly, he truly was a hopeless old man. Was he senile, or had his symptoms manifested? We had wasted our time taking him seriously.

Japanese: 「でも、あの見土道夫があんな卑怯な手を使うとはね。隊長になって随分成長したじゃないか。今度会った時、ちゃんと仕返しをしないと……」
English: “But for Michio Mido to use such a cowardly method... He has grown considerably since becoming commander. We will have to repay him properly the next time we meet.”

Japanese: 「あんた、知らないのか？」
English: “You don’t know?”

Japanese: 横合いからお爺ちゃんがそう言葉を挟んだ。
English: An old man interjected from beside us.

Japanese: 「道夫君にはもう会うことは出来んぞ」
English: “You won’t be able to see Michio again.”

Japanese: 「八龍会解放軍の隊長がどれだけ偉いのか知らないけど、向こうがどう思ったって勝手に会いに行くよ」
English: “We don’t know how important the commander of the Hachiryu Liberation Army may be, but we will go and see him whether he likes it or not.”

Japanese: 「そうじゃない。彼は死んだんだ」
English: “That isn’t what I mean. He’s dead.”

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 「大騒ぎになったのに、知らなかったのかい？」
English: “It caused an enormous commotion. You didn’t know?”

Japanese: 「ここ数日、全然情報を仕入れてないんだよ。順を追って話してちょうだい。嘘を言ったらあとでひどいよ」
English: “We have received no information at all for the past several days. Tell us everything in order. If you lie, things will go very badly for you later.”

Japanese: 私たちはそう言って睨み付けると、お爺ちゃんはしわがれた声で訥々と説明してくれた。
English: We glared at him as we spoke. In a hoarse voice, the old man haltingly explained.

Japanese: 「なんだか、状況が急変してるんだね……」
English: “So much has changed so quickly...”

Japanese: 私たちが身体を治すために洋館に閉じこもっている間、八龍会を取り巻く状況は随分と変化していた。
English: While we secluded ourselves in the mansion to heal, everything around Hachiryukai had changed enormously.

Japanese: まず、私たちがあの倉庫に行った日に、見土道夫がクーデターを起こしてあの有名な三人のお爺さんたちを追い出していたことさえ知らなかった。
English: We had not even known that on the day we went to the warehouse, Michio Mido had staged a coup and driven out those three famous elders.

Japanese: その足で見土道夫は私たちと戦ってお爺さんたちの次に邪魔なエフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスを倒し、そして自分が名実ともに八龍会のリーダーになった。
English: Without pausing, Michio Mido had then fought us and defeated Yevgeny Ilyich Hess, the next greatest obstacle after the elders. He had become the leader of Hachiryukai in both name and fact.

Japanese: しかしそれもつかの間、ボスとなった見土道夫のお披露目会で、殺されてしまったんだという。やったのは一人の女の子で、花束に銃を隠して撃ったとのことだ。
English: His rule had been brief. Apparently he was killed at the reception where he was introduced as the new leader. A girl had concealed a gun inside a bouquet and shot him.

Japanese: 「その女の子って何者？」
English: “Who was that girl?”

Japanese: 「道夫君がたちが解放した病院の入院患者だったらしい。でも、どうしてかはわからない。まだ捕まっていないんだ」
English: “Apparently she was a patient at the hospital Michio and the others liberated. But no one knows why she did it. They still haven’t caught her.”

Japanese: 「……そう、そうなんだ。見土道夫が死んだんだ」
English: “...I see. I see. Michio Mido is dead.”

Japanese: あの見土道夫が死んだ。見土道夫が死んだんだ。
English: Michio Mido—the Michio Mido—was dead. Michio Mido had died.

Japanese: 「あっははは！　ばっかじゃないの？　解放とか言って余計なお世話をしてやった相手に殺されたって？　子供の時からいっつも、街のためとか、みんなのためとかくっさいこと言ってたのに、同じタイプBに殺されたって？　あっはははは！」
English: “Ah-ha-ha-ha! What an idiot! He went meddling where he wasn’t wanted in the name of ‘liberation,’ and the person he helped killed him? Ever since we were children, he never stopped spouting that nauseating talk about the city and everyone else—and another Type B killed him? Ah-ha-ha-ha-ha!”

Japanese: 私たちはなんだか笑いが止まらなかった。
English: For some reason, we could not stop laughing.

Japanese: 笑いすぎて目からにじんだ涙を拭い、
English: We wiped away the tears that had gathered in our eyes from laughing too hard.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、見土道夫が死んで解放軍はだれが隊長になったの？」
English: “Then who became commander of the Liberation Army after Michio Mido died?”

Japanese: 「カ、カミラって子が、隊長になったようだよ」
English: “A-a girl named Camilla seems to have become commander.”

Japanese: お爺ちゃんは私たちの態度に動揺しながら答える。
English: The old man answered, visibly unsettled by our manner.

Japanese: 「そう。じゃあ今はカミラ・ノーサムが八龍会のリーダーってわけね。……それじゃあ、最後の質問をするよ」
English: “I see. Then Camilla Northam is now the leader of Hachiryukai. ...In that case, we will ask our final question.”

Japanese: またシミズの方を見ると彼はまたビクッと身体を震わせる。どれだけ恐れているんだろう？
English: When we looked toward Shimizu again, his body gave another frightened jerk. How terrified could one person be?

Japanese: 「エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスはどこ？　死んだなんて言わないでね。あいつは死なないってわかってるんだから。どこかにいるんでしょう？」
English: “Where is Yevgeny Ilyich Hess? Do not tell us he died. We know that man cannot die. He must be somewhere.”

Japanese: 「そ、それは知らないっ」
English: “I-I don’t know!”

Japanese: シミズは首をぶんぶんと左右に振る。
English: Shimizu shook his head violently from side to side.

Japanese: 「隠したり、嘘をつこうもんなら……」
English: “If we catch you hiding anything or trying to lie...”

Japanese: 「ほっ、本当にしらないんだっ！」
English: “I-I truly don’t know!”

Japanese: シミズは金切り声をあげて両手で頭を抱え込む。
English: Shimizu shrieked and clutched his head in both hands.

Japanese: どうも嘘をついている様子じゃない。
English: He did not appear to be lying.

Japanese: 「誰か！　このなかに知ってる人はいないの？　ここが一番知りたかったことなんだよ？　もし誰も知らないって言うなら、ここに来た意味がないんだから。本当に誰も知らないのなら……ああもうっ！　うるさいなあ！」
English: “Does anyone here know? This was the one thing we most needed to learn. If no one knows, then coming here was meaningless. If no one truly knows... Oh, enough! Be quiet!”

Japanese: また虫の羽音の耳鳴りがしてきたので、私たちは音の方向をどなりつけてから、
English: The tinnitus like insect wings had returned. We shouted in the direction of the sound, then continued.

Japanese: 「とにかく、何も知らないのなら、みんなは何の役にも立たないってことでしょ？　私たちは一人殺されてるってことは、みんなと敵同士なんだよね？　役に立たない敵なんか、ここで一人残らず……」
English: “In any event, if none of you knows anything, then none of you is of any use. One of us was killed, which makes you our enemies, doesn’t it? There is no reason to leave useless enemies alive, so we might as well kill every last—”

Japanese: 「しっ、知ってる！」
English: “I-I know!”

Japanese: 声をあげたのは列の後ろの方にいた、まだ十代くらいの男の子だった。
English: The voice belonged to a boy still in his teens who stood near the back of the group.

Japanese: 「東陽町の工場だよ！　あそこに地下室があるから、そこに閉じ込めるって……」
English: “The Toyocho factory! It has a basement. They said they were going to lock him up there...”

Japanese: 私たちはその発言をした男の子をじっと見つめる。
English: We stared fixedly at the boy who had spoken.

Japanese: 彼は汗だくになって唇を震わせていた。
English: Sweat drenched him, and his lips were trembling.

Japanese: 「ほっ、本当だよ！　おれはパラシュート通りのチャーリーだ。もし嘘だったら、おれの家に来て殺してくれたってかまわない。だから、ここにいる人をこれ以上殺さないでっ」
English: “I-it’s true! I’m Charlie from Parachute Street. If I’m lying, you can come to my house and kill me. So please don’t kill anyone else here!”

Japanese: チャーリーと名乗った少年は言うだけ言うと、肩をふるわせて荒い呼吸をしている。
English: Having blurted out everything he had to say, the boy who called himself Charlie stood with his shoulders shaking and his breath coming hard.

Japanese: 「そう」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 私たちは彼をじっと見つめながら言った。
English: We spoke while continuing to stare at him.

Japanese: 「信じるよ。チャーリー」
English: “We believe you, Charlie.”

Japanese: この言葉で、チャーリーは腰が抜けたのか近くの机にもたれかかる。
English: At those words, Charlie’s legs appeared to give way, and he leaned heavily against a nearby table.

Japanese: 「じゃあ私たちの用件は終わり。思ったより被害が少なくてよかった。それじゃあこれで……あ、フルカワシュウジ」
English: “Then our business is finished. We are glad there was less damage than expected. We will be going... Ah, Shoji Furukawa.”

Japanese: 私たちはすっかり大人しくなってしまったそのひげ面の男の名前を呼ぶ。
English: We called the name of the bearded man, who had become completely docile.

Japanese: 「さっき言ってた、とびっきりの面白い話ってなに？」
English: “What was that particularly entertaining story you mentioned?”

Japanese: 「も、もういいよ」
English: “N-never mind.”

Japanese: フルカワシュウジは慌てて首を横に振る。
English: Shoji Furukawa hurriedly shook his head.

Japanese: 「そう。じゃあね。みんなさよなら」
English: “Very well. Good-bye, then. Farewell, everyone.”

Japanese: そして私たちはそのまま裏口から店を出た。
English: With that, we left the establishment through the rear exit.

Japanese: 『東陽町の工場』の場所は私たちも知っている。
English: We knew where the place called ‘the Toyocho factory’ was.

Japanese: エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスはネオ・ローズの管理には本当に神経質で、しょっちゅうそのことばかり話していた。そこは普通の民家を改造した場所で、四台の製剤機を稼働させパッケージまで行っているそうだ。
English: Yevgeny Ilyich Hess had been truly obsessive about the management of Neo Rose and talked about little else. The facility was apparently an ordinary house converted to hold four pharmaceutical formulation machines, where even the finished product was packaged.

Japanese: 地下があるとは知らなかったけれど、きっとあるんだろう。あそこは八龍会の本部からもそう遠くないし、周りもタイプBの八龍会のメンバーばかりだからあのお爺さんを閉じ込めるには丁度良いのかもしれない。
English: We had not known there was a basement, but evidently there was. The place stood fairly close to Hachiryukai’s headquarters and was surrounded by Type B members of the organization. Perhaps it was ideally situated for imprisoning the old man.

Japanese: うまくマリアの力を使えば自力でも脱出は簡単だろうけど、そうでないならば、きっと、ネオ・ローズのレシピを聞き出すためにひどい拷問を受けてるんだろうな。あいつはいくら拷問されても死ぬことがないから、さぞかし苦しいだろう。
English: If he used Maria’s power effectively, he could probably escape on his own. If not, he was surely being subjected to terrible torture to extract the Neo Rose formula. Nothing they did could kill him, so he must be suffering greatly.

Japanese: あの偉そうなお爺ちゃんが苦しんでいるところを想像すると、可哀想な気もするけれど、ざまあみろという気もする。きらいってわけじゃないけれど。
English: Imagining that arrogant old man in pain made us feel a little sorry for him and a little pleased that he had gotten what he deserved. It was not as though we hated him.

Japanese: バーの人たちは、私たちが去った後に八龍会に連絡したろうか？　だとすれば、解放軍の人たちが待ち構えているんだろうな。
English: Would the people in the bar have contacted Hachiryukai after we left? If so, members of the Liberation Army would presumably be waiting for us.

Japanese: 見土道夫がいなくなって、私たちと対抗出来る人はいるのかな？
English: With Michio Mido gone, did anyone remain who could oppose us?

Japanese: それにしても、結局一生一度も見土道夫に勝てないまま死なれてしまった。子供の頃はよく喧嘩をして負けて泣かされて「お前らなんか一生おれに勝てないんだからやめとけ」とよく馬鹿にされたけれど、その通りになってしまった。今ならきっと私たちが勝つのに　随分つまらない死に方をしたものだ。いや、人間なんかそんなものなんだろう。もしあの不死の血がなければ、私たちは両方ともあそこで命を落としていたんだ。
English: In the end, Michio Mido had died before we could beat him even once in our entire lives. As children, we fought him frequently. He always beat us until we cried and mocked us: ‘You’ll never beat me as long as you live, so give it up.’ He had turned out to be right. We would surely win now. What a remarkably dull way for him to die. No—perhaps that was simply what human beings were. Without that immortal blood, both of us would have lost our lives in the warehouse.

Japanese: ああ、いつもならこんなとき二人で何か感想を言い合えるのに、今は心の中で延々と呟くことしか出来ないんだな。私たちのもう一方はどこへ行ったのか。本当に消えてなくなったのか？　それまで存在していたものが、消えてなくなるなんてありえるんだろうか。みんな近くにいるような気がするよ。私たちのもう片方も、お兄ちゃんも、お父さんも、お母さんも。
English: Ah, at a time like this, the two of us would ordinarily have traded our thoughts. Now we could do nothing but murmur on and on inside our mind. Where had the other one of us gone? Had she truly vanished? Could something that had existed simply disappear? It felt as though everyone were nearby: the other half of us, our brother, our father, and our mother.

Japanese: それにしても、羽音がうるさい。人のブツブツがうるさい。あんまり寂しいから、このブツブツと会話をしようか？
English: Even so, those wingbeats were loud. The human muttering was loud. Since we were so lonely, should we try conversing with it?

Japanese: そして私たちはその工場の近くまでやって来た。
English: We arrived near the factory.

Japanese: 工場とはいっても、知らなければどうってことのないごくありふれた民家である。辺りはもうすっかり真っ暗だけれど、その窓には明かりが灯っていた。
English: Despite the name, it was an utterly ordinary house that no one would have found remarkable without knowing its purpose. The neighborhood was now completely dark, but light shone from its windows.

Japanese: まだ作業中なのか、それとも、連絡を受けて私たちを待ち受けているのか。
English: Were they still working, or had someone warned them and they were waiting for us?

Japanese: 私たちは近くの建物の塀から屋根へと飛び移り、上から侵入することにした。
English: We leaped from the wall of a nearby building to its roof and decided to enter from above.

Japanese: 明かりが灯っているのは一階だけで、二階は暗い。敷地内には人影がない。窓にはレースのカーテンが掛かってなかが見にくくなっているけれど、昼はともかくこう暗いと内側から照らせばある程度は見える。でも、何か動いている様子はない。強化された私たちの聴覚にも物音は聞き取れない。ということはつまり、少なくとも作業はしていないということだ。
English: Only the first floor was lit; the second was dark. There was no one visible anywhere on the grounds. Lace curtains obscured the windows, but at night the lit interior was partly visible through them. Nothing appeared to be moving. Even our enhanced hearing detected no sound. At the very least, no one was working.

Japanese: エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスの話によれば、たしかここは庭には侵入を防ぐセキュリティシステムが張り巡らされているはずだ。
English: According to Yevgeny Ilyich Hess, the grounds ought to be protected by a security system intended to prevent intrusion.

Japanese: 私たちはそれを避けるため、塀を蹴って工場の屋根に飛び移る。そして屋根を伝ってぐるりと窓のなかを確認しながら移動するけれど、やはり人気がない。
English: To avoid it, we kicked off the wall and leaped onto the factory roof. We followed the roof around the house, examining each window, but still found no trace of anyone.

Japanese: ベランダに入るとガラス戸がある。
English: A glass door opened onto the balcony.

Japanese: 子供の時、よくこういうガラス戸を破って中に入った。友だちはサムターンの近くガラスを割って鍵を開けていた。サッシとガラスの隙間にドライバーを差し込むと音もなくガラスにひびが入るので、それを何回か繰り返すと静かにガラスが割れる。田中紺太がやたらと上手だった。そして見土道夫は右手の力を使ってもっと静かに開けることが出来た。
English: As children, we had often broken through doors like this to get inside. Our friends would shatter the glass beside the thumbturn and unlock them. Inserting a screwdriver between the sash and glass created a silent crack; repeating the process several times allowed the glass to be broken quietly. Konta Tanaka had been exceptionally good at it. Michio Mido could use the power of his right hand to open one even more quietly.

Japanese: でも私たちはそんなことせずに、もっと上手に開けられる。
English: We had no need to do any of that. We could open it more elegantly.

Japanese: まずガラスに顔をぺったりくっつける。すると、部屋の奥の壁にセキュリティシステムのパネルが見える。念動力を使ってパスコードを入力し、まずセキュリティを解除しようとしたのだが、いくらボタンを押しても画面が何も変わらない。
English: First, we pressed our face flat against the glass. A security-system panel was visible upon the far wall. We tried using psychokinesis to enter the passcode and disable the system, but no matter how many buttons we pressed, the screen did not change.

Japanese: 何度かためしてみて、そして最初から解除されていることに気がついた。帰るときにセットしわすれたのだろうか？　いくらなんでも不用心だ。
English: After several attempts, we realized that it had been disabled from the beginning. Had they forgotten to arm it when leaving? That would have been careless beyond belief.

Japanese: とにかく、防犯設備が作動していないのならあとは鍵を開けるだけだ。
English: In any event, with the security equipment inactive, we needed only to unlock the door.

Japanese: それに関してはなんてことはない。
English: That was nothing at all.

Japanese: 念動力でガラス戸のサムターンをくるりと回せば何も壊さずに部屋に入ることが出来る。
English: We used psychokinesis to turn the thumbturn on the glass door and entered the room without breaking anything.

Japanese: 部屋のなかはシンとしている。
English: The room was silent.

Japanese: 二階は元の住宅設備の家具がそのままで、革張りのソファーや大きなテレビが置かれ、壁には名画の複製がかかっている。元の住人がどんな人だったかはわからないけれど、この街でこういった暮らしが出来るのはそれなりに裕福なうちに入る。ギャング関係か、商売人か。
English: The second floor retained the house’s original furnishings. Leather sofas and a large television stood there, and reproductions of famous paintings hung upon the walls. We did not know what sort of people the former residents had been, but anyone able to live this way in this city would have counted as reasonably wealthy. Perhaps they had belonged to a gang, or owned a business.

Japanese: 電灯が消えていて暗く、窓からうっすらと差し込む外の明かりを頼りに進む。
English: The lights were out. We moved forward by the faint exterior light filtering through the windows.

Japanese: 階段のところの壁にそっと身を寄せて下の様子をうかがうけれども、やはりそちらにも人の気配がない。
English: We gently pressed ourselves to the wall beside the stairs and watched the floor below. There was no sign of anyone there either.

Japanese: セキュリティがそのままなのといい、電気がつけっぱなしなのといい、何か異変を感じさせる。それとも、普段からここはこんなにいい加減なんだろうか？　そりゃ発症したタイプBばっかりならそれくらい杜撰でもおかしくないけれど、みんな薬でしゃっきりしているはずなのにそれは考えにくい。
English: The inactive security system and lights left burning suggested that something unusual had happened. Or was the place always managed this carelessly? If it were staffed entirely by Type Bs whose symptoms had manifested, such negligence might have been unsurprising. They should all have been clearheaded on medication, however, so that seemed unlikely.

Japanese: 不審に思いながらソロソロ階段を降りると、自分の予感が当たったのを知った。
English: With our suspicion growing, we crept down the stairs and discovered that our intuition had been correct.

Japanese: 蛍光灯に煌々と照らされた部屋は、まるで空き巣にあった後のような有様だった。棚や引き出しは開け放たれ、書類のようなものがまるで見当たらない。パソコンがあったとおぼしき机の上には、引っこ抜かれたケーブルだけが残されている。
English: The room, brilliantly lit by fluorescent lamps, looked as though it had been burglarized. Shelves and drawers stood open. Not a single document remained. Only yanked-out cables lay upon the desk where a computer appeared to have stood.

Japanese: そして壁には銃弾の痕。
English: And there were bullet marks upon the walls.

Japanese: しかし血液などは床の上に流れていない……ということは交戦はしなかったんだろうか？　侵入した何者かはここで威嚇射撃を行い、作業員たちを脅しながら工場の書類などを持ち去ったんだ。
English: There was no blood on the floor... Perhaps no one had fought. It looked as though whoever entered had fired warning shots here, threatened the workers, and carried away the factory’s documents.

Japanese: 八龍会の全員が戦闘要員ではないとはいっても、警備員などはいたろうし、抵抗もせずに従わせるのは簡単ではない。
English: Not every member of Hachiryukai was a combatant, but there must at least have been guards. Forcing everyone to comply without resistance could not have been easy.

Japanese: つまり、相手は抵抗する気力がなくなるほどのもの……身内の過激派による造反か、それか、YSかな？　……YSのような気がする。クーデターが起きたり、新しいリーダーである見土道夫が死んだりして、八龍会はきっとゴタゴタしているだろうし、その状況を菅原亮が利用しない筈がない。
English: In other words, the intruders had been so formidable that resistance seemed hopeless. Had radical insiders rebelled? Or had this been YS? ...We suspected YS. Hachiryukai must have been in turmoil after the coup and the death of its new leader, Michio Mido. Ryo Sugawara would never fail to exploit such circumstances.

Japanese: 壁際に四台並んだ製剤機はまだそのままだ。これは大きいから運び出せずに、後で取りに来るつもりなのかもしれない。そう言えばまだ辺りには硝煙のにおいが立ちこめている。それほど時間が経っていないのだろう。
English: The four pharmaceutical formulation machines lined up against the wall remained in place. Perhaps they had been too large to remove immediately, and the intruders intended to return for them. Come to think of it, the smell of gunpowder still hung heavily in the air. Not much time could have passed.

Japanese: それはともかく、あの生意気なお爺さんはどこにいるのか。
English: That aside, where was the insolent old man?

Japanese: 何の音もしないのがやっぱり気になるが、考えていても仕方がない。邸内を散策すると、キッチンの横に地下へ降りる階段を見つけた。そしてその階段は血で汚れている。
English: The continued silence troubled us, but there was no purpose in thinking without acting. As we searched the house, we discovered a staircase beside the kitchen leading underground. Blood stained its steps.

Japanese: ぽつぽつとこぼれ落ちた血の雫を、靴で踏みにじったようなあとだった。
English: It looked as though someone’s shoes had trampled through the scattered drops of blood.

Japanese: それを見た時点でこの先にあるものが大体想像が付いたが、確認するために階段を降りる。
English: The sight gave us a fair idea of what lay ahead, but we descended to confirm it.

Japanese: 分厚いドアを開けると、むっと血の臭いがした。部屋のなかは真っ暗で、ドアの側で小さなランプが点灯しているスイッチを押す。
English: When we opened the heavy door, the thick smell of blood met us. The room was completely dark. We pressed a switch beside the door whose small indicator lamp was glowing.

Japanese: 地下室は本来ホームシアターとして使われていたものらしく、壁際には大きなスクリーンモニターがあり、部屋の四方には本格なスピーカーセットが設置されていた。
English: The basement appeared originally to have been a home theater. A large projection screen stood against one wall, and a professional speaker system had been installed around all four sides of the room.

Japanese: おそらく昔は部屋の中央にソファーか何か、ゆっくりくつろいで鑑賞するための家具が置かれていたんだろうけれど、今はそこには不格好な鋼鉄のベッドが置かれている。タイプB用の頑丈なやつだ。そして、時ほどかれた拘束用の鎖がその上に落ちている。
English: In the past, a sofa or some other furniture for watching in comfort had probably occupied the center. Now an ungainly steel bed stood there instead—a heavy-duty model intended for Type Bs. Loosened restraint chains lay atop it.

Japanese: ベッドの上は夥しい血で溢れていて、階段から続く血の跡はそこに続いていた。
English: An enormous quantity of blood covered the bed. The trail descending the stairs ended there.

Japanese: コシチェイはここで囚われ、八龍会によって拷問を受けていたに違いない。YSか、他の誰かかわからないが、襲撃者は彼も連れ出したんだろう。襲撃者が誰かによって、彼の運命は大きく変わる。
English: Koschei must have been imprisoned and tortured here by Hachiryukai. Whether the attackers belonged to YS or some other force, they had probably taken him as well. His fate would differ enormously depending upon who they were.

Japanese: とにかく、ここに目指す人物がいないとなればもう長居をする必要はない。
English: In any event, with the person we sought no longer here, there was no reason to remain.

Japanese: 階段をのぼり、そして玄関から外に出たところで思わぬ人物に出くわした。
English: We climbed the stairs and left through the front entrance. Outside, we encountered someone unexpected.

Japanese: 「田中紺太！」
English: “Konta Tanaka!”

Japanese: 「は、はいがみっ！？」
English: “H-Haigami!?”

Japanese: 丁度入り口から入ろうとしていたのは、三人ほど仲間を率いている田中紺太だった。
English: The person about to enter was Konta Tanaka, leading three or so companions.

Japanese: 「ど、どうしてここに？」
English: “W-why are you here?”

Japanese: その反応からすると、酒場の誰かから私たちの情報を聞きつけてやって来たというわけではないようだ。
English: Judging by his reaction, he had not come after hearing about us from someone at the bar.

Japanese: 「あなたたちがさらったあのお爺ちゃんを連れ戻しに来たんだよ。……ちょっと、遅かったみたいだけど」
English: “We came to recover the old man you abducted. ...It appears we were a little late.”

Japanese: 「やっ、やる気かっ？」
English: “A-are you looking for a fight?”

Japanese: 「あなたと喧嘩する気はないわ。意味がないし」
English: “We have no intention of fighting you. It would be meaningless.”

Japanese: 「そ、そうか……。なんでお前が生きているかわからんが、なんだか、悪いことをしたな……」
English: “I-I see... I don’t understand why you’re alive, but... we did something terrible to you.”

Japanese: 田中紺太は冷や汗を袖で拭いつつ、
English: Konta Tanaka wiped the cold sweat from his face with his sleeve.

Japanese: 「おれたちも好きでやったわけじゃないんだ。あの爺さんは、どうしても危険だったから……」
English: “We didn’t do it because we wanted to. That old man was simply too dangerous...”

Japanese: 「言い訳はしないで。思い出すと、殺したくなるから」
English: “Do not make excuses. Remembering it makes us want to kill you.”

Japanese: 「そ、そうだよな。……中はどうなってる？」
English: “R-right. ...What’s it like inside?”

Japanese: 「自分の目で見たら」
English: “See for yourself.”

Japanese: 言って私たちは彼に道を譲る。彼の部下たちは警戒心を露わにするが、田中紺太は気にせずずかずかと足を進めていって、部屋の惨状を見ると溜息をつく。
English: We stepped aside to let him pass. His subordinates displayed open wariness, but Konta Tanaka ignored them and strode inside. When he saw the devastation, he sighed.

Japanese: 「地下室にとじこめていたお爺ちゃんもいなくなってるよ」
English: “The old man you imprisoned in the basement is gone too.”

Japanese: 「そうらしいな。やつらはヘスも連れて行ったと報告が入っている」
English: “Apparently so. We received a report that they took Hess with them.”

Japanese: 「やったのはYS？」
English: “Was it YS?”

Japanese: 私たちの問いに、田中紺太は頷きを返した。
English: Konta Tanaka nodded in answer.

Japanese: だとすると、ちょっと面倒だ。YSは『コシチェイ』のことをどれくらい知っているのか……もしかしたら、八龍会よりも詳しいかもしれない。
English: That made the situation somewhat troublesome. How much did YS know about ‘Koschei’? Perhaps more than Hachiryukai did.

Japanese: コシチェイはグランドタワーを襲ったり、汐松子を襲ったりしている。菅原亮は徹底的に調べ上げただろう。YSは警察と繋がりがあるし、そういった面からも情報は入りやすいはずだ。
English: Koschei had attacked Grand Tower and Matsuko Shio. Ryo Sugawara would have investigated him exhaustively. YS had connections to the police, which should make information easier to obtain from that direction as well.

Japanese: しかも、菅原亮はコシチェイのような『不死身』の人間には誰よりも詳しい。汐松子とずっと一緒にいて、よく調べていたんだから。
English: Moreover, Ryo Sugawara knew more than anyone about ‘immortal’ people like Koschei. He had spent all that time beside Matsuko Shio and studied her closely.

Japanese: 「状況はわかったわ。じゃあね、田中紺太」
English: “We understand the situation. Good-bye, Konta Tanaka.”

Japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと待ってくれ」
English: “W-wait a moment.”

Japanese: そう言ってその場をあとにしようとすると、彼は引きとめた。
English: When we began to leave, he called us back.

Japanese: 「灰上、お前はこれからどうするんだ？　姉妹の復讐をするのか？」
English: “Haigami, what are you going to do now? Take revenge for what happened to the two of you?”

Japanese: 「復讐はしないわ。死んだ人間はもういないのよ。そのために何かをするなんてばかみたいでしょ。私たちは、お爺ちゃんを連れ戻す」
English: “We will not seek revenge. A dead person no longer exists. Doing something for their sake would be ridiculous, wouldn’t it? We are going to bring back the old man.”

Japanese: 「おれも道夫君もどうしてもわからなかったんだよ。なんで、お前がヘスと一緒にいるんだ？」
English: “Neither Michio nor I could ever understand. Why are you with Hess?”

Japanese: 「理由なんかないわ。なんだかとっても気になるんだよ。……じゃあね」
English: “There is no reason. For some reason, we simply cannot stop thinking about him. ...Good-bye.”

Japanese: そしてもう一度歩きかけて、私たちはふと思い出して振り返った。
English: We started away again, then suddenly remembered something and looked back.

Japanese: 「YSと戦うのはやめなさい。あなたたち八龍会は絶対勝てないわ。リーダーもヘスの薬も失った以上、あなたたちは無力な存在に逆戻りなんだからね」
English: “Stop fighting YS. You people in Hachiryukai can never win. Now that you have lost both your leader and Hess’s drug, you have returned to being powerless.”

Japanese: 「え、えらそうに！　お前こそ、あの爺さんを連れ戻すって言ったって出来ることなんかないだろう？」
English: “H-how high and mighty! You say you’ll bring that old man back, but there’s nothing you can do either!”

Japanese: 彼はむきになって言い返す。
English: He retorted heatedly.

Japanese: 「あるわ。私たち、交渉の材料を持ってるの」
English: “Yes, there is. We have something to bargain with.”

Japanese: それだけ言うと、あとはもううしろを振り返らずに小走りで家を出た。
English: Having said only that, we jogged away from the house without looking back again.

Japanese: その頃は今よりもはっきりとした四季があって、六月も終わりになればすっかり蒸し暑く、Y地区の裏通りはどこもかしこも用水路のヘドロから漂う腐敗臭がにおっている。
English: The seasons were more distinct in those days. By the end of June, the weather had become thoroughly hot and humid, and every back street in Y District reeked of rot rising from the sludge in its drainage channels.

Japanese: 貧しいものたちの子供はほとんど半裸で、裾や襟の伸びきったTシャツを埃だらけにし、白い歯を剥き出しにしてサッカーやら喧嘩やらに明け暮れていた。豊かなものたちの子供は洗いたてのきれいな服を着て、はじめは日陰からそれを眺めているがいつのまにか彼らと混じって埃だらけになり、同じように笑うのだった。
English: The children of the poor went almost half-naked. They wore T-shirts with hems and collars stretched out of shape and filthy with dust, baring white teeth as they devoted their days to soccer and fighting. The children of wealthier families began in freshly washed clothes, watching from the shade. Before anyone noticed, they too had joined the others, become covered in dust, and begun laughing in precisely the same way.

Japanese: いつの時代でもどの場所でも子供たちはグループを作るものだが、その頃のY地区の子供たちは地域や人種ごとにチームを作り、大人さながらに街の覇権をかけて争いあっていた。いやむしろ、YSが街を支配するようになってからギャング同士の抗争はめっきり減少していたため、大人以上の熾烈な争いだったと言えるかもしれない。
English: Children form groups in every age and place. In Y District at the time, they formed teams by neighborhood and race and fought over mastery of the city like adults. Indeed, since gang conflicts had declined sharply after YS came to dominate the city, one might say that the children’s struggles were fiercer than those of the adults.

Japanese: 子供たちの勢力争いは数年で大人になってゆくため世代交代が早い。サイキックである劉建志が暗闇通りの不良少年を束ねて一大グループを築いていたのが第一世代だとしたら、彼らの世代は第三世代と言えるだろう。
English: Because children grew into adults within a few years, power among them passed quickly from one generation to the next. If the period when the psychic Ryu Kenshi united the delinquents of Darkness Street into one enormous group was called the First Generation, theirs might be called the Third.

Japanese: 彼ら以降こうした少年同士のグループ争いはほとんどなくなるから、最後の世代といっていいかもしれない。
English: Conflicts between groups of boys virtually disappeared after them. In that sense, they might also be called the final generation.

Japanese: 彼らというのは、後に八龍会の代表となる見土道夫や、YSの第三代龍頭となる菅原亮たちのことである。
English: ‘They’ were Michio Mido, who would later represent Hachiryukai, Ryo Sugawara, who would become the third Longtou of YS, and the children around them.

Japanese: 劉建志がYSの一員となって自分のチームを解散した時点までが第一世代で、その後小さなグループがいくつも乱立していたのが第二世代だった。彼らの多くはギャングと結びつき、いかに有力なバックをつけるかをお互いに競い合った。
English: The First Generation ended when Ryu Kenshi joined YS and disbanded his team. The period that followed, when numerous small groups sprang up side by side, was the Second Generation. Many attached themselves to adult gangs and competed to secure the most powerful patrons.

Japanese: その頃は丁度『ローズ』のレシピが公開され、世界中で流行しはじめた時期で、後には悪魔の薬と呼ばれることになるこの薬は、タイプBには奇跡の薬として、その他の若者たちにはイージーなドラッグとして流行の兆しを見せ始めていた。
English: This was precisely when the formula for Rose was made public and the drug began spreading around the world. It would later be called a devil’s drug. To Type Bs, however, it appeared a miracle medicine; among other young people, it showed signs of becoming fashionable as an easy recreational drug.

Japanese: 第二世代の不良少年たちはこの『ローズ』と最も深く関わった少年たちだろう。ギャングたちとのつき合いのなかで、これを仲間に売って小銭稼ぎをしていた。買う方としても深く関わり、中毒者となってしまったものも多い。その結果、大人たちにていよく労働力や性を搾取され、命を落とすものも少なくなかった。
English: The delinquents of the Second Generation were probably the children most deeply involved with Rose. Through their associations with gangs, they sold it to their friends for pocket money. Many were equally involved as buyers and became addicted. Adults then found it convenient to exploit their labor and sexuality, and no small number reportedly lost their lives.

Japanese: 第三世代はそうした状況のなか、近所の子供が集まった遊び仲間の輪から生まれた。
English: Amid those conditions, the Third Generation grew out of circles of neighborhood children who had first gathered simply to play.

Japanese: 彼らは団結力が強く、集団の力でこの街にドラッグを流行らせた元凶と言っても良い第二世代の少年たちを駆逐していった。そのとき中心的な役割を果たしたのが、わずか十四才で暗闇通りの子供たちのリーダーとなった見土道夫だった。
English: Their bonds were strong. Through collective strength, they drove out the boys of the Second Generation, who could fairly be blamed for spreading drugs among the children of the city. At the center of that effort stood Michio Mido, who became leader of the children of Darkness Street at only fourteen.

Japanese: タイプBの身体能力とタイプAの超能力を兼ね揃えた、この孤児の少年は八龍会の老人たちに引きとられ、その頃はある日本人大工の頭領の家に預けられ、普段はその現場で手伝いをしていた。
English: The orphan possessed both the physical abilities of a Type B and the psychic power of a Type A. The elders of Hachiryukai had taken him in and placed him with a Japanese master carpenter, whom he ordinarily assisted at job sites.

Japanese: 荒くれ者の肉体労働者たちのなかで暮らした彼は喧嘩が滅法強く、同年代はもとより、大人と戦っても一歩もひけをとらなかった。
English: Living among rough manual laborers made him exceptionally strong in a fight. Not only boys his own age, but even adults could not force him to give ground.

Japanese: 当時暗闇通りはヤンという十八才の少年が率いるグループが仕切っていた。第二世代にあたる彼らはギャングと組んで売春組織を作っており、近くの少女たちを騙したり脅したりして不当に働かせていた。
English: Darkness Street was then controlled by a group led by an eighteen-year-old boy named Yang. Members of the Second Generation, they had joined with a gang to organize prostitution, deceiving or threatening girls from the neighborhood and exploiting their work.

Japanese: この被害にあった少女が幼なじみに相談した。これが見土道夫少年であり、彼は遊び仲間たちと組んで暗闇通りでヤンのグループを見かけるたびに襲って叩きのめした。その結果ヤンたちは道夫の姿を見かけると逃げ回るようになり、その姿は子供たちの物笑いの種となる。
English: One girl who suffered at their hands consulted a childhood friend: the young Michio Mido. Together with his playmates, Michio attacked and thrashed Yang’s group whenever he found them on Darkness Street. Eventually, Yang and his companions fled whenever Michio appeared, making themselves objects of ridicule among the other children.

Japanese: すっかり評判の落ちたヤンたちを恐れるものはなく、少女を集められなくなった。起死回生を狙って空き地に道夫たちを呼び出し決闘をするも、そこでも散々な目にあって敗北し、結果、ギャングたちも離れ、ヤンのグループは消滅することになる。
English: With their reputation destroyed, no one feared Yang’s group, and they could no longer recruit girls. Hoping to reverse their fortunes, they summoned Michio and his friends to a vacant lot for a duel. They suffered another wretched defeat. Their adult gang patrons abandoned them, and Yang’s group disappeared.

Japanese: その後ヤンは一時道夫の子分のような立場でチームに混じっていたが、やがてチームを抜けて飲食店に就職、そこで心を入れ替えてコツコツと働き、今はタイ人の妻と結婚して四人もの子を持つ親になっているがそれはずっと後の話である。
English: For a time afterward, Yang served as a subordinate in Michio’s team. He eventually left and found work at a restaurant. There, he changed his ways and worked steadily. Today he is married to a Thai woman and has become the father of four children—but all that lay far in the future.

Japanese: とにかく、これがきっかけで道夫は暗闇通りの少年たちのリーダーとなり、第三世代が始まったのである。
English: In any event, the affair made Michio the leader of the boys of Darkness Street and marked the beginning of the Third Generation.

Japanese: 「ねえ帰ろうよ道夫君。たった二人で、見つかったらどうすんのさ」
English: “Come on, Michio. Let’s go home. There are only two of us. What are we going to do if they find us?”

Japanese: 地元の住民が夕食の材料を買い求めて行き来するパラシュート通り。人の間をすり抜けて歩いている田中紺太は不安げにキョロキョロと辺りを見回しながら先を行く背の高い少年にそう呼びかけた。
English: Local residents moved along Parachute Street in search of ingredients for dinner. Weaving between them, Konta Tanaka looked nervously in every direction and called to the tall boy walking ahead.

Japanese: 「帰るなら一人で帰ってもいいんだぜ？」
English: “If you want to go home, you can go by yourself.”

Japanese: その少年……見土道夫は不敵に笑ってそう応える。
English: The boy—Michio Mido—answered with a fearless smile.

Japanese: 染めたての金色の髪の毛は赤みがかった太陽の光を反射してキラキラと光っていた。
English: His freshly dyed golden hair reflected the reddish sunlight and glittered brightly.

Japanese: 「そういうわけにはいかないよ……。ここを歩くなら、せめて、みんなを呼ぼうよ」
English: “I can’t do that... If we’re going to walk around here, we should at least call everyone else.”

Japanese: このパラシュート通りは彼らの縄張りではなく、別の少年グループが本拠地としている。別に取り立てて緊張関係にあるというわけではなかったが、この頃のY地区の不良少年の社会ではよそのグループの縄張りには勝手に足を踏み入れないことが不文律のようになっており、それを破ったことがきっかけに喧嘩になることも少なくない。
English: Parachute Street was not their territory. Another group of boys made its base there. Relations between the two groups were not especially tense, but among the young delinquents of Y District, entering another group’s territory without permission had become an unwritten taboo. Doing so frequently started fights.

Japanese: 紺太は口は達者だが、喧嘩には自信がなかった。彼も一応タイプＢではあるが、傾向値が低くよほど興奮してもほとんど金眼にならない上に、なっても身体能力はさほど変わらない。平均的なノーマル相手でもこてんぱんに負かされるくらいだ。
English: Konta was quick with words but had little confidence in a fight. He was technically a Type B, yet his tendency value was low. Even intense excitement almost never turned his eyes gold, and when it did, his physical abilities changed very little. An average Normal could beat him soundly.

Japanese: さらに今日は新しい黒いシャツをおろしたばかりで、汚したくないという事情もある。
English: Moreover, he was wearing a brand-new black shirt for the first time that day and did not want it dirtied.

Japanese: 母親の売春に客引きとして手伝っている彼はそこから歩合で小遣いを貰っており、他の暗闇通りの子供に比べればずっと裕福だとはいえ、好きなものを好きなだけ買えるほどの金を持っているわけではなかった。
English: He helped find customers for his mother and received a fee for each one as spending money. That gave him considerably more pocket money than most children on Darkness Street, but hardly enough to buy anything he wanted whenever he pleased.

Japanese: 「いいんだよ。これは偵察なんだ。殴り込みじゃない」
English: “It’ll be fine. This is reconnaissance, not a raid.”

Japanese: 「こんなに目立つ偵察ってないよ」
English: “Nobody has ever done reconnaissance this conspicuously.”

Japanese: 紺太が呆れる通りだ。
English: Konta was entirely right to be exasperated.

Japanese: 道夫はTシャツの半袖を肩までめくり上げ、その年の少年にしては逞しい両腕を露出しているが、右の方は肘から先が真っ黒に染まっている。
English: Michio had rolled the short sleeves of his T-shirt up to his shoulders, exposing arms unusually robust for a boy his age. The right one, however, was black from the elbow down.

Japanese: それは何かの塗料を使ったような普通の黒さではなく、何かまるきり別の物質のような、なんの光も反射しない完全な黒だった。
English: It was not the ordinary black produced by pigment. The arm reflected no light whatsoever. Its perfect black made it appear to be made of an entirely different substance.

Japanese: これを見れば誰でも彼がその身に異形の呪いをうけたタイプAであることを一目で理解し、そして少しこの地域の事情に詳しければ彼が最近少年たちの間でよく話題になる見土道夫だと気がつくだろう。
English: Anyone who saw it would understand at once that he was a Type A cursed with a misshapen form. Anyone with even a little knowledge of the neighborhood would also recognize him as Michio Mido, lately much discussed among the local boys.

Japanese: すぐ先日も、北街のブロイアーという喧嘩の強いことで知られる年上の少年に決闘を挑んで勝ちを収め、その縄張りを手に入れている。
English: Only days before, he had challenged and defeated Breuer, an older boy from North Town famed for his strength in fights, and taken his territory.

Japanese: その時に出来た青あざが彼の頬にはあり、切れた唇の端にはかさぶたが出来てた。
