English: A bruise from the fight remained upon his cheek, and a scab had formed at the corner of his split lip.

Japanese: 「だって、どんなやつか見てみたいじゃないか。その菅原亮ってやつはおれたちと同い年なんだろ？」
English: “I want to see what he’s like. This Ryo Sugawara is our age, isn’t he?”

Japanese: そう、彼が今日この場所へ足を踏み入れたのは、パラシュート通りを縄張りにする少年グループのリーダー、菅原亮に会うためであった。
English: That was why Michio had entered this neighborhood today: to meet Ryo Sugawara, leader of the boys whose territory was Parachute Street.

Japanese: パラシュート通りは滑走路通りほどではないが賑やかで人の多い地域である。住んでいるものたち人種も多様で、少し歩いただけで雰囲気がコロコロと変わり、いくつもの国を渡り歩いているような気持ちになる場所であった。
English: Parachute Street was not quite as busy as Runway Street, but it remained a lively, crowded neighborhood. Its residents came from a wide variety of races. Within a short walk, the atmosphere changed again and again, making one feel as though one had traveled through several countries.

Japanese: またＹＳの力が及びにくく、小さなギャングがいくつも根城としているため、その子供などがそれぞれ威張って歩いているが、なかなかグループというものが出来にくい。事実、それまでこれといったグループはなかった。だから滑走路通りの連中がしょっちゅうちょっかいを出して来て、それを止める手段がなかったのである。
English: The influence of YS was also weak here, and numerous small gangs maintained bases in the area. The children affiliated with each one swaggered about, yet organizing a proper group remained difficult. In fact, no group of any consequence had existed before. The boys from Runway Street therefore harassed the neighborhood constantly, and no one had possessed the means to stop them.

Japanese: Ｙ地区のメインストリートである滑走路通にはいくつか少年グループがあったが、もっとも力が大きかったのは、引退した劉建志の弟分である周という少年がひきいていたものである。
English: Several groups of boys operated upon Runway Street, one of the main avenues of Y District. The most powerful was led by a boy named Zhou, a former junior associate of the retired Ryu Kenshi.

Japanese: 彼のグループは揃いの色のハンカチを腕に巻き付け、滑走路通りの西側を我が物顔で通りを練り歩いていた。
English: Members of his group tied matching colored handkerchiefs around their arms and swaggered through the western side of Runway Street as though it belonged to them.

Japanese: 劉のツテもあってＹＳとの関係も良好で、彼らの下請けとして飲食店のボディガードを手伝うなどというようなこともしている。小規模になりがちな第二世代のグループのなかでは最も力の大きな存在である。
English: Ryu’s connections gave them good relations with YS. As subcontractors, they even helped guard restaurants and performed similar work. Among the typically small groups of the Second Generation, theirs was the most powerful.

Japanese: これがよくパラシュート通りの方までやって来るのだが、前述のようにここで力のある少年たちはバックがギャングであることで威張ってるようなものたちだったから、ＹＳと関わりがある周には逆らえなかった。
English: They frequently came as far as Parachute Street. As noted earlier, however, the powerful boys here owed their swagger largely to the gangs behind them. They could not oppose Zhou, who had connections to YS.

Japanese: ながらく彼らに好き勝手させていたが、これを拒絶して追い払ったのが、菅原亮とその仲間たちだった。
English: For a long time, his group did as it pleased. Ryo Sugawara and his friends were the ones who finally stood up to them and drove them away.

Japanese: 菅原亮はパラシュート通りに店を開く定食屋の息子で、彼の仲間も同じように何らかの商売をしている家の子ばかりである。彼らは比較的裕福で、身体は大きいが勇気がなく、喧嘩が弱いというのが暗闇通りの少年たちの評価だったが、それが暗闇通りの少年たちでもちょっと手が出せない周たちに勝ったというのだから話題になっていた。
English: Ryo Sugawara was the son of a diner proprietor on Parachute Street. His friends all came from families that ran businesses of some kind. The boys of Darkness Street regarded them as relatively well-off and big for their age, but cowardly and weak in a fight. That boys like these had defeated Zhou’s group—a group even the boys of Darkness Street were reluctant to challenge—made them the talk of the neighborhood.

Japanese: 道夫はその同年のリーダーに興味があった。
English: Michio was interested in the leader his own age.

Japanese: 彼が今まで喧嘩の相手にしてきたのは自分より年上ばかりで、同い年で少年たちの話題になるようなものは、自分の他には亮が初めてだったからである。
English: Until then, everyone he had fought had been older than he was. Ryo was the first boy his own age, apart from Michio himself, whom children across the city were talking about.

Japanese: 「心配する気持ちはわかるが、おれがいる限りお前だけは逃がしてやるから大丈夫だ。たとえどんなに沢山の仲間を連れてこようとな。……危険な武器を持ってきたら、おれもついに生物相手にこの妖刀ムラサメの封印を解くことになるかもしれないが……」
English: “I understand why you’re worried, but as long as I’m here, I’ll make sure you escape. It doesn’t matter how many friends they bring. ...If they pull a dangerous weapon, I may finally have to break the seal upon the Cursed Blade Murasame against a living creature...”

Japanese: 道夫は格好つけた口ぶりでそう言いながら、うしろを歩く紺太に真っ黒な腕を見せつける。
English: Michio delivered the words with dramatic affectation, displaying his black arm to Konta behind him.

Japanese: 「こないだは、魔剣フェンなんとかって言ってなかったっけ？」
English: “Didn’t you call it the Demon Sword Fen-something the other day?”

Japanese: 紺太は溜息をつき、
English: Konta sighed.

Japanese: 「もしそうなったらおれだって戦うよ。馬鹿にしないでほしいね。……でも、たとえ道夫君が本気を出したってそう簡単に勝てるかな？」
English: “If that happens, I’ll fight too. Don’t insult me. ...But even if you get serious, Michio, are you sure we can win so easily?”

Japanese: 「おれを信用してないのか？」
English: “You don’t trust me?”

Japanese: 道夫は立ち止まって振り返る。
English: Michio stopped and looked back.

Japanese: 「そうじゃなくてさ。相手もサイキックかもしれないじゃん。だって、周のやつらを追い返すなんて普通じゃないよ。追い返した相手には馬鹿みたいに怪力のタイプＢも結構いたはずだぜ？　もしわけのわからない力を持ってたら、道夫君でも勝てるかどうか……」
English: “That’s not it. The other guy might be a psychic too. Driving Zhou’s people off isn’t normal. Some of them were Type Bs with ridiculous strength, weren’t they? If Sugawara has some power we don’t understand, then even you might not beat him...”

Japanese: 「フ、それならそれで面白い」
English: “Heh. That would make it all the more entertaining.”

Japanese: 道夫は目をつむり、ぐっと手を握りしめ、
English: Michio closed his eyes and clenched his fist.

Japanese: 「おれはいつも本来の力で戦うことが出来なかった。あまりにも恐ろしく強い力を授かってしまったせいだ。それでも連戦連勝してしまうこの罪深さ……。正直なところ最近勝つことに飽きてしまってね。ちょっとは楽しめるなら、これより嬉しいことはない」
English: “I have never been able to fight with my true power. The strength bestowed upon me is simply too terrifying. And yet I continue to win battle after battle—what a sinful burden... To speak honestly, I have lately grown bored with victory. Nothing could please me more than an opponent capable of providing at least some amusement.”
“I-I see...”

Japanese: 紺太は眉間にしわを寄せて複雑な表情で相槌を打つ。道夫のこういったセンスにはついていけないところがあるのだが、はっきりとそう言わないのは彼の優しいところであり、かといって表情を器用に取り繕って笑ってやれないのは彼のプライドであった。
English: Konta frowned ambivalently as he answered. There were aspects of Michio’s sensibility he could not follow. Kindness kept him from saying so plainly, while pride kept him from skillfully shaping his expression into an encouraging smile.

Japanese: 「でも、もし負けたら覚悟した方が良いよ。菅原は残酷なやつらしいからね。喧嘩のとき、ヤマザキってやつが腕や足の骨をボキボキに折られたんだけど、それを見てたおれの知り合いの話じゃ、菅原はその様子を笑いながら見てたんだってさ」
English: “But if you lose, you’d better be prepared. They say Sugawara is cruel. In that fight, a boy named Yamazaki had the bones in his arms and legs broken one after another. Someone I know who watched it told me Sugawara stood there laughing while it happened.”

Japanese: そう言われると道夫もさすがに顔をしかめたが、
English: Even Michio frowned at that.

Japanese: 「そんなひどいやつなら、やっぱり少しでも早くやっつけないといけないな」
English: “If he’s that horrible, then all the more reason to defeat him as soon as possible.”

Japanese: 消沈するどころかなおさら彼の情熱をかき立ててしまったようだった。
English: Rather than discouraging him, the story seemed only to kindle his enthusiasm further.

Japanese: パラシュート通りの端の方に「菅原食堂」と、ペンキ文字の看板が掛かったこぢんまりとした中華料理店がある。
English: Near the end of Parachute Street stood a small Chinese restaurant with a hand-painted sign reading SUGAWARA DINER.

Japanese: 道夫と紺太はその前に立ち、あまりにも堂々と路面に晒されている敵リーダーの名前をあんぐりと口を開けて眺めた。
English: Michio and Konta stood before it, mouths hanging open as they stared at the enemy leader’s name displayed so boldly to the street.

Japanese: 今は営業時間の筈だが、昼食と夕食の間の時間帯の暇な時間帯のせいか入り口の傷だらけのアルミサッシには「準備中」の札が下がっている。
English: It ought to have been open, but perhaps because this was the quiet interval between lunch and dinner, a CLOSED sign hung upon the scratched aluminum frame of the entrance.

Japanese: かといって誰もいないというわけでもないらしく、磨りガラスの向こうで何者かが動いている気配があった。
English: The diner did not seem empty. They could sense someone moving beyond the frosted glass.

Japanese: 「なかにはいろうぜ」
English: “Let’s go inside.”

Japanese: 道夫は磨りガラスを見通そうでもするかのように目をこらし、押し殺した声で隣の紺太に囁く。
English: Squinting as though he might see through the frosted glass, Michio whispered to Konta beside him.

Japanese: 「いくらなんでもそれは無茶だよ」
English: “That’s reckless even for you.”

Japanese: 紺太が慌てる一方、道夫は平然とした表情で、
English: Konta grew alarmed, while Michio remained perfectly calm.

Japanese: 「ここで看板を眺めていてもなんの偵察にもならない。……それに、ここまで来たら血が騒いで来たのさ」
English: “Staring at the sign teaches us nothing. ...Besides, now that we’ve come this far, my blood is beginning to stir.”

Japanese: 唇の端を歪めてニヤリと笑った。
English: One corner of his mouth curled into a grin.

Japanese: また道夫の病気が出たのかと紺太は思ったが、呆れる一方こういうところがこの少年の面白いところでもある。
English: There he goes again, Konta thought. Yet for all his exasperation, this was also what made Michio interesting.

Japanese: 「菅原亮ってやつに挨拶をしてやるぞ」
English: “We’re going to introduce ourselves to Ryo Sugawara.”

Japanese: もうすっかり偵察であることなど頭にないのであろうと思われる台詞を吐きながらドアに近づいてゆく道夫。紺太は仕方なくその後を追った。
English: Apparently, reconnaissance had vanished from his mind altogether. Michio approached the door, and Konta followed because he had little choice.

Japanese: そして道夫は勇ましく胸を張ってガラリと入り口の戸を開ける。
English: Then Michio threw out his chest and slid the entrance door boldly open.

Japanese: 店内はカウンター席といくつかのテーブル席がある、どこにでもあるようなごく普通の定食屋だった。建物や家具は古く所々に染みついた汚れや黄ばみがあったが掃除自体は行き届いている。
English: Inside was an utterly ordinary diner, with counter seats and several tables. The building and furniture were old, stained and yellowed in places, but the room itself had been cleaned thoroughly.

Japanese: 従業員らしきものはおらず、カウンターの向こうの調理場にも人はいない。けれど客席のテーブルに、少年と少女が向かい合っていた。少女の目の前には透明なガラスの器に盛られたバニラアイスがあり、手前の少年はこちらに背を向けながら少女の食べるところを見守っているようだった。
English: There was no employee in sight, nor anyone in the kitchen beyond the counter. A boy and girl, however, sat facing each other at one of the tables. Before the girl was a transparent glass dish of vanilla ice cream. The boy sat nearer the entrance with his back to them, apparently watching her eat.

Japanese: 二人の入った音で、二人ともこちらを見る。
English: At the sound of the two boys entering, both occupants looked toward them.

Japanese: あ、美人。
English: Oh. She’s beautiful.

Japanese: こういう場合やはり異性の方に先に視線がゆくもので、少女の顔を見た道夫と紺太はほとんど同時に同じ言葉を心のなかで呟いた。
English: In such situations, the gaze naturally went first to the opposite sex. Michio and Konta thought precisely the same words at almost precisely the same moment.

Japanese: 少女は事実整った顔立ちであった。西洋人形のようにまったく表情のない冷たい顔をしていたが、それがますます美貌を引き立てており、うぶな少年ならぞくりと背中に冷たいものを感じながらたちまち恋に落ちてしまいそうな容姿である。ただ、その目は金色に輝いており、嫌が応にも道夫たちの警戒心を呼び起こした。
English: The girl did indeed possess striking features. Her face was cold and entirely expressionless, like that of a Western doll, yet this only enhanced her beauty. An innocent boy might feel a chill run down his spine and fall in love with her at once. Her eyes, however, shone gold, inevitably awakening the visitors’ caution.

Japanese: 振り返った少年も、少女に負けず劣らずの美しい容貌を持っていた。彼はその切れ長の目でこちらを見ると怪訝な表情をした。
English: The boy who turned around was no less beautiful than the girl. He studied them through narrow eyes, his expression puzzled.

Japanese: 「お前が菅原亮だな」
English: “You’re Ryo Sugawara.”

Japanese: 目的の人物にすぐ会えた興奮を抑えつつ道夫は低い声で問うと、相手は頷く。
English: Suppressing his excitement at having found the person he sought so quickly, Michio put the question in a low voice. The other boy nodded.

Japanese: やはりこの少年が噂の菅原亮なのか。見た感じ相手に特質変異は見えず、サイキックかどうかは確認出来ない。華奢というほどではないが細身で、強そうにも見えない。
English: So this really was the Ryo Sugawara they had heard about. Michio could see no trait mutation, and therefore could not tell whether Ryo was a psychic. He was slender without quite being frail and did not look particularly strong.

Japanese: しかし道夫にとってはどこかで見覚えがある顔だった。
English: Yet Michio felt that he had seen Ryo’s face somewhere before.

Japanese: 「おれが誰かわかるか」
English: “Do you know who I am?”

Japanese: 道夫はそう言って黒い右腕を出して見せる。
English: Michio held out his black right arm for Ryo to see.

Japanese: 「見土道夫だね」
English: “Michio Mido, right?”

Japanese: 亮はこともなげに言い、
English: Ryo answered as though it were nothing remarkable.

Japanese: 「たしか孤児で八龍会に拾われていて、燕町三丁目の大工の居候になってるんだっけ？　暗闇通りのガキどものリーダーだね。ハイブリッドで、超能力は特質変異のある右腕による切断。趣味はTVアニメで、その時影響された技の名前をしょっちゅう自分の能力に借用する。隣の家に住む二つ年上の盲目の女性に片思いをしていて……」
English: “An orphan taken in by Hachiryukai, currently boarding with a carpenter in Tsubamecho 3-chome. Leader of the brats on Darkness Street. A hybrid whose psychic power is cutting through things with your trait-mutated right arm. Your hobby is TV anime, and you constantly borrow the names of whatever moves impress you for your own power. You’re in love with the blind woman two years older than you who lives next door...”

Japanese: 「しっ、知りすぎだろ！」
English: “Y-you know too much!”

Japanese: 道夫は慌てて遮る。そのうしろでは紺太が驚きを浮かべている。
English: Michio cut him off in a panic. Behind him, Konta stared in surprise.

Japanese: 「道夫君って、ルーシーさんに片思いを……」
English: “Michio, you’re in love with Lucy...?”

Japanese: 紺太のつぶやきを道夫は無視しながら、
English: Ignoring Konta’s murmur, Michio said,

Japanese: 「ふん、それだけおれのことを調べたというわけか。やっぱりお前もライバルのことが気になっていたんだな」
English: “Hmph. So you researched me that thoroughly. I knew you were interested in your rival too.”

Japanese: 「ただの風の噂だよ。……そっちの彼の噂も知ってるよ。田中紺太、あんたは……」
English: “They’re only rumors I happened to hear. ...I’ve heard about your friend too. Konta Tanaka. You—”

Japanese: 「お、おれのことはどうでもいい」
English: “N-never mind me.”

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: 彼は興味なさそうに素っ気なく答えるとまた少女の方を振り返り、
English: He answered curtly, with no sign of interest, then turned back toward the girl.

Japanese: 「松子は気にしないで食べなよ」
English: “Don’t mind them, Matsuko. Keep eating.”

Japanese: その言葉に松子と呼ばれた少女は頷き、小さなスプーンでアイスを掬って口に入れる。甘いものを目の前にした女の子の態度にしては、まるで機械仕掛けのような義務的な動作で、喜びもない顔だった。
English: The girl called Matsuko nodded, scooped up a little ice cream, and placed it in her mouth. For a girl with sweets before her, the motion was remarkably dutiful, almost mechanical. Her face showed no joy.

Japanese: 「どんな味がする？」
English: “What does it taste like?”

Japanese: 「甘くて、冷たい」
English: “Sweet and cold.”

Japanese: 少女は表情を変化させずにそう応える。
English: The girl’s expression did not change as she answered.

Japanese: 「美味しい？」
English: “Is it delicious?”

Japanese: 「……美味しいってどんな味？」
English: “...What does ‘delicious’ taste like?”

Japanese: 松子は困ったように首をかたむける。亮は残念そうに溜息をつく。
English: Matsuko tilted her head in apparent uncertainty. Ryo sighed, looking disappointed.

Japanese: 「おい」
English: “Hey.”

Japanese: 思わず二人の動作を見つめていた道夫はそこで我に返って呼びかける。
English: Michio, who had found himself watching the pair, came back to his senses and called to them.

Japanese: 「準備中の札がかかってたろ？　今はなんの料理も出せないよ。店主が昼寝をしているんだ」
English: “You saw the CLOSED sign, didn’t you? We can’t serve you anything right now. The owner is taking a nap.”

Japanese: 亮は背中を向けたままそう告げる。
English: Ryo told him this without turning around.

Japanese: 「おれは客として来たんじゃない。お前に用があって来たんだ」
English: “I didn’t come as a customer. I came because I have business with you.”

Japanese: 道夫の言葉に、亮は眉間にしわを寄せ、いかにも面倒だという態度を露わにしながら振り向いた。
English: At Michio’s words, Ryo turned around with a furrowed brow and made no effort to hide what a nuisance he found this.

Japanese: 「菅原亮。お前はパラシュート通りの悪餓鬼どものボスだ。そしておれは暗闇通りを仕切っている。これから二人でどっちが強いか決着をつけよう。そして勝った方が相手のチームを奪うんだ」
English: “Ryo Sugawara. You’re the boss of the little hellions on Parachute Street, and I run Darkness Street. You and I are going to settle which of us is stronger. The winner takes the loser’s team.”

Japanese: 亮は眉の片方をつり上げて怪訝な表情をする。しかし、驚いたのは彼だけではない。
English: Ryo raised one eyebrow, looking perplexed. But he was not the only one taken by surprise.

Japanese: 「み、道夫君、そんなの聞いてないよ。どうして偵察のはずが挨拶になって、決闘になるのさ」
English: “M-Michio, you never said anything about this! How did reconnaissance turn into an introduction and then into a duel?”

Japanese: 道夫は無情にも紺太の言葉を無視する。
English: Michio heartlessly ignored Konta’s protest.

Japanese: 「なあ菅原よ。今この街は、お前がやっつけた周みたいな、ギャングとつるんだアホが仕切ってるせいで、ろくでもないと思わないか？　おれは、こんな状況は納得出来ないんだ。それともお前はギャングが好きか？」
English: “Listen, Sugawara. Don’t you think this city is rotten right now, with idiots like Zhou running with gangs and calling the shots? I can’t accept things the way they are. Or do you like gangs?”

Japanese: 「ギャングは嫌いだ。しかしそれが関係あるのか？」
English: “I hate gangs. But what does that have to do with this?”

Japanese: 亮は冷たい視線を浴びせながら言う。
English: Ryo fixed him with a cold stare.

Japanese: 「おおありさ。おれたちは自分の遊び場を守らなきゃいけない。そのためには戦力が必要なんだよ。だからおれは今、仲間と一緒にあちこちに出向いて、いろんなボスと決闘をしたり、戦争をして仲間を増やしているところなのさ」
English: “Everything. We have to protect our playgrounds, and we need strength to do that. So my friends and I are going from place to place, challenging different bosses to duels and going to war so we can recruit more allies.”

Japanese: 「戦争とはまた大げさだな」
English: “Calling it war is a little grandiose.”

Japanese: 亮は溜息をつく。
English: Ryo sighed.

Japanese: 「そして力を蓄えたところで、つまらない連中に戦いを挑むんだ」
English: “And once we’ve built up enough strength, we’ll challenge all the good-for-nothing creeps responsible for this.”

Japanese: 「だから、僕に決闘を挑んでパラシュート通りも縄張りにしようってわけだね」
English: “So you’re challenging me to a duel because you want to claim Parachute Street as your territory too.”

Japanese: 「そうだ。おれとお前、一対一で戦うんだ。そして勝った方が負けた方のチームを吸収する。おれはこの虎の目の力も、超能力も使わない。この身体だけで戦ってやる。だからお前も素手で立ち向かってこい。男同士のプライドをかけた決闘だぜ。さあ、わかったなら今すぐ表に出ろ！」
English: “Exactly. You and me, one on one. The winner absorbs the loser’s team. I won’t use the power of my Tiger’s Eye or any psychic ability. I’ll fight you with this body alone, so you come at me bare-handed too. This is a duel with our pride as men on the line. Now that you understand, get outside!”

Japanese: 道夫は興奮して高らかに宣言をするが、亮は対象的にさも億劫そうに頭をかいてから、
English: Michio declaimed excitedly at the top of his lungs. Ryo, by contrast, scratched his head as though the entire prospect were a chore.

Japanese: 「断る。だから……」
English: “I refuse. So—”

Japanese: 言おうとしたその言葉を道夫はむきになって遮った。
English: Suddenly indignant, Michio cut him off before he could finish.

Japanese: 「おい、逃げる気か？　よく考えろ。お前が拒否すればチーム同士の戦争になる。そしたら、けが人が沢山出てやつらにつけこまれる隙を作ることに……」
English: “Are you planning to run? Think carefully. If you refuse, our teams go to war. A lot of people will get hurt, and that’ll give those gangs the opening they need to—”

Japanese: 「そうじゃない。話をきけよ」
English: “That’s not what I mean. Listen to me.”

Japanese: 亮は溜息をつくと、
English: Ryo sighed.

Japanese: 「決闘なんかしない。僕の負けでいい。お前にチームは譲るから帰ってもらおうか」
English: “I’m not going to duel you. You win. I’ll give you the team, so will you please go home?”

Japanese: 「はあ？」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 道夫は口をあんぐりと開いて問い返す。
English: Michio’s mouth fell open.

Japanese: 「いいかい？　僕は別にリーダーでもなんでもないんだ。このあたりを滑走路通りの馬鹿がうろついてムカついたから、別の馬鹿を集めて追い払っただけさ。そうしたら、馬鹿たちがおかしな感じにまつりあげてきて迷惑してる。挙げ句の果てにはお前らみたいな馬鹿が家まで押しかけてきやがった。一体この馬鹿騒ぎはなんだ？　ほっといてくれ」
English: “Listen. I’m not anybody’s leader. Some idiots from Runway Street kept wandering around here and pissing me off, so I gathered some other idiots and chased them away. Then those idiots started holding me up as something special, and it’s been nothing but trouble. And now idiots like you show up at my house. What is this whole idiotic circus? Leave me alone.”

Japanese: この菅原亮という人間がどういった人物なのかまだはっきりとは掴めないが、口調こそ穏やかだが、その言葉のなかでは仲間も敵もひっくるめて「馬鹿」と連呼するところをみると、性格が相当悪いのは間違いない。
English: They still could not say exactly what sort of person Ryo Sugawara was. Yet although his tone remained calm, he called friend and enemy alike an idiot over and over. Of one thing there could be no doubt: he had a thoroughly unpleasant personality.

Japanese: 道夫も紺太も同時にそう理解した。
English: Michio and Konta reached that conclusion at the same moment.

Japanese: 「ねえ、僕は暴力は嫌いなんだ。最低最悪の解決方法だからね。ガキとギャングは程度が低いからすぐこの原始的な解決方法に頼ろうとする。もううんざりだ」
English: “You see, I hate violence. It’s the very worst way to solve a problem. Children and gangsters are so crude that they always turn straight to this primitive solution. I’m sick of it.”

Japanese: （お前もガキじゃないか）と、道夫は心の中で呟く。
English: You’re a child too, Michio thought.

Japanese: しかし本人はそんな自覚もないようで、すまし顔で続ける。
English: Ryo seemed entirely oblivious to that fact. With an imperturbable expression, he continued.

Japanese: 「だから、お前がみんなのリーダーを引き受けてくれるならこれほど嬉しいことはない。よろこんで譲るから、それでY地区の統一するなり、大番長になるなり、好きにやってくれ」
English: “So if you’re willing to be everyone’s leader, nothing could make me happier. I’ll gladly hand it over. Unite Y District, become the Supreme Delinquent Boss, do whatever you like.”

Japanese: 「な、なんて卑怯なやつだ！」
English: “Y-you coward!”

Japanese: 道夫は言って、どんと拳で傍らの壁を叩く。すると、上の方に画鋲で貼りつけられた品書きのボール紙が揺れる。
English: Michio slammed his fist against the wall beside him. A cardboard menu pinned higher up with thumbtacks shook from the impact.

Japanese: 「見損なったぞ菅原亮！　お前には情熱がないのか！」
English: “You’ve disappointed me, Ryo Sugawara! Don’t you have any passion?”

Japanese: 「ない」
English: “No.”

Japanese: 亮は苦々しい表情で荒ぶる道夫を眺めながら、
English: Ryo regarded the raging Michio with a sour expression.

Japanese: 「お前は暴力のことを一種のスポーツみたいに考えているようだけど、僕はそんなふうには解釈できない。ひどく恐ろしいものだ。くだらない殴り合いなんかしたくないんだよ。僕は一人で好きなことについて考えていたり、この子と遊んでいた方がずっと楽しい。……そろそろ美味しいって感覚がわかってきた？」
English: “You seem to think violence is a kind of sport, but I can’t see it that way. It’s terrifying. I don’t want any part of some pointless fistfight. I have much more fun sitting by myself and thinking about things I like, or playing with her. ...Is ‘delicious’ starting to make sense yet?”

Japanese: 「ううん」
English: “No.”

Japanese: 亮の問いかけに、少女は首を左右に振る。
English: The girl shook her head in answer to Ryo’s question.

Japanese: 「そっか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 亮は残念そうに言うと、空になった少女の食器を持って立ち上がった。
English: Looking disappointed, Ryo took the girl’s empty dish and rose.

Japanese: 「おい、どこへ行く気だ」
English: “Hey. Where do you think you’re going?”

Japanese: 「食器の片付けと、それから食事の用意をしようと思ってね。僕らはまだ昼食をとっていないんだ」
English: “To put the dishes away, then get lunch started. We haven’t eaten yet.”

Japanese: 「こっちの話はまだ終わっていない」
English: “We’re not finished talking.”

Japanese: 道夫が食い下がると、亮は苛立ちを浮かべてきっと睨み、
English: When Michio persisted, Ryo’s face hardened with irritation, and he glared sharply at him.

Japanese: 「それはお前の都合だろ？　こっちにはこっちの都合がある。静かに午後を過ごしているところを土足で入ってきたお前らにここまでつき合ってやったんだから少しは譲れよ。それとも、見土道夫というやつは、偉そうな口をきくわりに最低限の礼儀も知らないのか？」
English: “That’s your business, isn’t it? We have plans of our own. You barged in on our quiet afternoon, and I’ve humored you this far, so learn to compromise a little. Or is Michio Mido the sort of person who talks big without knowing even the bare minimum of manners?”

Japanese: これまで穏やかな口調で対応していた亮の突然の怒りに、道夫は思わず気圧され、
English: Ryo had answered calmly until then. The sudden anger in his voice took Michio aback.

Japanese: 「お、おう。飯くらい好きに食えよ。その子も腹が空いているだろう」
English: “O-okay. Go ahead and eat, then. She must be hungry too.”

Japanese: 不覚にもそう返事をしてしまった。
English: Before he quite realized what he was doing, Michio had agreed.

Japanese: 「ありがとう」
English: “Thank you.”

Japanese: すると亮は微笑を残し、空の食器をカウンターに上げるとその場を去ってゆく。
English: Ryo gave him a faint smile, placed the empty dish upon the counter, and disappeared into the back.

Japanese: 道夫は想像していたのとは大分違う菅原亮という人間に戸惑い、苦い顔をする。
English: This Ryo Sugawara was nothing like the person Michio had imagined. Confused, Michio grimaced.

Japanese: 「どうする？　出直す？」
English: “What do we do? Come back another time?”

Japanese: 紺太が困って訊ねても、
English: Konta asked uncertainly.

Japanese: と生返事をするのが精一杯だった。
English: That halfhearted answer was the best Michio could manage.

Japanese: 「チームをくれるって本当かな？　そんな話って本当にあると思う？」
English: “Do you think he really means it about giving us his team? Can something like that actually happen?”

Japanese: 「嘘をついているようには思えないけれど……」
English: “He didn’t seem to be lying, but...”

Japanese: 顎に手を当てて考えていると、ふと目の前にいる松子と目が合ってしまう。
English: Michio rested a hand upon his chin and considered the matter. Then his eyes happened to meet Matsuko’s.

Japanese: アイスクリームがなくなって手持ち無沙汰になった彼女は、そこに座ったままじっと道夫たちを見つめていた。相変わらず無表情で、クスリともしない。目が金色だが雰囲気からすると発症しているわけでもなさそうだ。
English: With the ice cream gone, she had nothing to occupy her and remained in her seat, gazing steadily at the two boys. Her face was still expressionless; she did not so much as smile. Her eyes were gold, but judging from her manner, she did not appear to be symptomatic.

Japanese: かといって、さっきの亮とのやりとりは表情を見る限り普通の少女にも見えない。
English: Yet judging by her responses to Ryo during their earlier exchange, she did not seem like an ordinary girl either.

Japanese: 「お前はいったい菅原の……」
English: “What exactly are you to Sugawara...?”

Japanese: 訊ねようとしたところで、奥の戸がガラガラと開いて亮が帰って来た。
English: Michio had begun to ask when a door in the back rattled open and Ryo returned.

Japanese: 彼はその手に首を落とされ羽をむしられた一羽の鶏を掴んでいる。
English: In one hand, he carried a chicken whose head had been removed and feathers plucked.

Japanese: 「まだいたんだ」
English: “You’re still here.”

Japanese: 入り口の方で佇んでいる二人にチラと一瞬だけ視線をやってからそう言うと、そのままカウンターの内側の調理場の方に足を踏み入れて、白く大きなまな板の上にその鶏をドサリと置いた。
English: Ryo spared the boys standing near the entrance a single glance. Then he stepped behind the counter into the kitchen and set the chicken down with a heavy thump upon a large white cutting board.

Japanese: 「昨日裏でしめたんだ」
English: “I slaughtered it out back yesterday.”

Japanese: 亮は白いエプロンを着けながらそう言った。
English: Ryo spoke as he put on a white apron.

Japanese: 「お前が料理するのか？」
English: “You’re going to cook?”

Japanese: 「そうだよ。大量に出来ちゃうからどうしようかと思ってたんだけど、お前らも食ってく？　そんな時間はかからないけど」
English: “That’s right. It’ll make too much for the two of us, so I was wondering what to do with the rest. You two want some? It won’t take long.”

Japanese: 亮は手にハンドソープをつけ、蛇口の水でよく洗いながら訊ねる。
English: Ryo asked as he soaped his hands and washed them thoroughly beneath the faucet.

Japanese: 「あ、うん」
English: “Uh, sure.”

Japanese: 「じゃあそこのテーブルに座ってなよ」
English: “Then sit at that table.”

Japanese: 「す、すまん」
English: “Th-thanks.”

Japanese: 言われたとおり道夫と紺太は松子の正面に腰掛けた。
English: As directed, Michio and Konta took seats across from Matsuko.

Japanese: 亮は業務用の巨大なコンロに火をつけると、中華鍋の揚げ油を温め、その間に包丁を取り出して鶏にとりかかる。よく慣れているのか、慣れた手さばきで鶏の形をしていたものはそれぞれの部位の肉の塊に切り分けられている。
English: Ryo lit an enormous commercial stove and began heating the oil in a wok. Meanwhile, he took up a knife and set to work upon the chicken. With practiced movements, he quickly reduced what had been a whole chicken to separate cuts of meat.

Japanese: 「まるでプロみたいだ。すごいなあ」
English: “You’re like a professional. That’s amazing.”

Japanese: 紺太が背筋を伸ばして亮の手さばきに見惚れている。
English: Konta straightened his back and watched Ryo’s hands in fascination.

Japanese: 一方隣の道夫は仏頂面である。
English: Michio, sitting beside him, wore a sullen expression.

Japanese: 「おい、なんでおれたちはここで菅原亮の料理を待っているんだ？　おれはやつと戦いに来たんだぞ？」
English: “Hey. Why are we sitting here waiting for Ryo Sugawara to cook for us? I came here to fight him.”

Japanese: 「そんなのおれに言われたって困るよ。道夫君がうんって応えて座ったんだろ。……あ、良い匂いがしてきた。そういえばおれも昼食べてないんだよなあ」
English: “What do you expect me to say? You’re the one who agreed and sat down. ...Oh, it’s starting to smell good. Come to think of it, I haven’t eaten lunch either.”

Japanese: 紺太はもう道夫が語る話よりも、これからどんな料理が出来上がるかの方に完全に興味がうつっているようだ。
English: Konta’s interest appeared to have shifted entirely from Michio’s concerns to what Ryo was about to serve.

Japanese: 道夫は腕組みをして今の状況を考える。
English: Michio folded his arms and considered his present situation.

Japanese: こちらは決闘を申し込み、相手はそれを拒否するかわりにこちらの条件をのんだ。つまり、チームをくれるというのだ。ということは、もう争う理由はないということになる。対立関係ではないとすれば、ここで食事をご馳走になるのもなにもおかしくはない。
English: He had proposed a duel. Ryo had refused, but agreed to his terms instead: he would hand over the team. That left them nothing to fight about. And if they were no longer enemies, there was nothing strange about accepting a meal from him.

Japanese: そのはずなのだけれども、どうも感情が納得出来ない。こんな簡単でいいのだろうか？　自分が、そして街のちょっと悪い子供たちが青春を賭けているこの戦いが、こんなにあっさり決着していいのだろうか？
English: That was how it ought to be, yet Michio’s feelings refused to accept it. Could matters truly be this easy? Could this struggle—this struggle upon which he and the city’s mildly delinquent children had staked their youth—be decided so effortlessly?

Japanese: いや、もめ事なく決着付けばそれはそれでいい。そのはずなのだが、なんだろうこの心の収まりのつかない感じは。もしかして自分の心が求めているのは、自分が頭で考えているものとは違うのか？
English: No, an end without conflict ought to be welcome. He knew that. So what was this feeling that refused to settle within him? Could what his heart desired differ from what he thought he wanted?

Japanese: 「うーん……」
考え込んでいると、また松子と目が合った。
English: As he brooded, he met Matsuko’s eyes once again.

Japanese: 「何か用か？」
English: “Do you need something?”

Japanese: 「頭でも痛いのか？　鎮痛剤あるぞ」
English: “Does your head hurt? We have painkillers.”

Japanese: 松子は無表情だが心配してくれているようだ。
English: Matsuko remained expressionless, but she appeared to be concerned for him.

Japanese: 「いや、違うんだ……今ちょっと自分というものを見直していたんだ」
English: “No, that’s not it... I was just reevaluating the nature of my own being.”

Japanese: 「そう」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 松子は素っ気なく言い、そしてあくびをした。
English: Matsuko answered curtly, then yawned.

Japanese: 「お待たせ。大皿で悪いね」
English: “Sorry to keep you waiting. And sorry it’s all on one platter.”

Japanese: 亮は出来上がった料理を食卓の上に置く。
English: Ryo placed the finished dishes upon the table.

Japanese: 一番大きな皿に盛られているのは、鶏の上げたものに長葱のたっぷり入った茶色いあんがかかったものだ。
English: The largest plate held fried chicken covered in brown sauce loaded with scallions.

Japanese: その隣の中くらいの皿にはキュウリと茄子の漬物が盛られている。そして、一人一人にわかめと卵の入った透明なスープと白米の椀が配られた。
English: Beside it, a medium-sized plate held pickled cucumbers and eggplant. Each person also received a bowl of clear soup with wakame and egg, and another of white rice.

Japanese: 「これ、から揚げか？」
English: “Is this karaage?”

Japanese: もうすっかりここに来た理由を忘れた紺太が目を輝かせて訊ねる。
English: Having completely forgotten why he had come, Konta asked with shining eyes.

Japanese: 「油淋鶏。まあ似たようなもんだけど」
English: “Yurinchi. It’s fairly similar.”

Japanese: 「へえ、良い匂いがするな。……食っていいのか？」
English: “Oh, it smells great. ...We can really eat it?”

Japanese: 「ああ、冷めないうちに食ってくれ」
English: “Of course. Eat before it gets cold.”

Japanese: 「いただきまーす！」
English: “Let’s eat!”

Japanese: 紺太は箸を右手に、白米のよそわれた茶碗を左手に取り、真っ先に大皿の鶏に手をつける。
English: Konta took his chopsticks in his right hand and the bowl of white rice in his left, then helped himself to the chicken before anything else.

Japanese: 「いただきます」
English: “Thank you for the food.”

Japanese: 松子も丁寧に手を合わせてそう言ってから、食事をはじめる。
English: Matsuko carefully placed her hands together as she spoke, then began to eat.

Japanese: 「……食べないのか？」
English: “...Aren’t you eating?”

Japanese: そして自分も食べ始めようとした亮は、箸を目の前に置いたまま動かない道夫にそう尋ねた。
English: Ryo had been about to begin his own meal when he noticed Michio sitting motionless with his chopsticks before him.

Japanese: 「いや、もらうよ。いただきます」
English: “No, I’ll eat. Thank you for the food.”

Japanese: 道夫は複雑な表情で箸を手に取ると、小さめの油淋鶏をひとつつまみ、いつもの食卓での癖で白米の上にちょんと一度触れさせてから口に運ぶ。
English: With a complicated expression, Michio picked up his chopsticks. Following his usual habit at meals, he took one of the smaller pieces of yurinchi, touched it lightly to his white rice, and brought it to his mouth.

Japanese: 多めの長葱が入った甘酸っぱいタレが、サクサクと食感良くあがった鶏と馴染んでおり、しかも少し濃い目の味付けが白米とよくあった。
English: The sweet-and-sour sauce, loaded with scallions, blended perfectly with the crisp chicken. Its assertive seasoning went especially well with the white rice.

Japanese: 「旨い。旨いなあ」
English: “Man, this is good. Really good.”

Japanese: 隣の紺太は無邪気に褒めているが、道夫はそんな風に率直に感想を口にする気にはなれない。
English: Konta praised it with innocent delight, but Michio could not bring himself to say how he felt so openly.

Japanese: 「なあ菅原」
English: “Listen, Sugawara.”

Japanese: 相変わらず松子の食べる様子を見ながら食事をしている亮にそう声をかけた。
English: He addressed Ryo, who continued watching Matsuko between bites of his own meal.

Japanese: 「さっきの話本当か？」
English: “Did you mean what you said earlier?”
“What part?”

Japanese: 「チームを譲るって話だよ」
English: “About giving me the team.”

Japanese: 「もちろんだ。僕はそういうくだらない嘘はつかない」
English: “Of course. I don’t tell petty lies like that.”

Japanese: 「だって、そんな簡単なものじゃないだろ？」
English: “But it can’t be that simple, can it?”

Japanese: 「大丈夫。混乱せずにちゃんとお前が引き継げるように、挨拶の仕方を僕が考えておくよ。心配しなくていいよ。チョロいもんなんだからさ」
English: “It’ll be fine. I’ll decide how to introduce you so you can take over properly without any confusion. Don’t worry. It’ll be easy.”

Japanese: 亮はにこりともせずに説明をする。
English: Ryo explained this without the slightest smile.

Japanese: その冷淡な態度が道夫には理解が出来ない。
English: Michio could not understand that cold attitude.

Japanese: 「おれが簡単って言ってるのは、そういう意味じゃない。どうしてそんなに簡単に手放せるのかってことだよ。せっかくリーダーになったんだろ？」
English: “That’s not what I mean by ‘simple.’ I’m asking how you can let go of it so easily. You finally became the leader, didn’t you?”

Japanese: 「興味がないんだから仕方がない。沢山のガキどもを空き地に並べて集会でもして、ああこいつらが自分の子分なんだなあってニヤニヤすればいいのか？　それとも立場を利用して女や男を思い通りにすると満たされるのか？　世間にはそういう人間が多いのは知っているけれど、僕はゴメンだね」
English: “I’m not interested, so what else should I do? Am I supposed to line up a crowd of children in a vacant lot for a meeting, look at them, and grin, thinking, ‘So these are all my underlings’? Or should I use my position to make women and men do whatever I want and find that fulfilling? I know plenty of people in the world are like that, but count me out.”

Japanese: 「威張ったら楽しいと思うけどな……」
English: “Bossing people around sounds like fun...”

Japanese: 横で呟く紺太を無視して、道夫はさらに訊ねる。
English: Ignoring Konta’s murmur beside him, Michio pressed further.

Japanese: 「お前は、おれたちの街を良くしようとは思わないのか？　このままじゃダメだろう？」
English: “Don’t you want to make our city better? It can’t go on this way.”

Japanese: 「悪いけれど、世の中をよくするためとか、社会を変えるためとか、自分の行動に社会的意義を関連付けて価値を持たせるやりかたは全然好みじゃないんだ。僕の人生にはもっと別なテーマがある」
English: “I’m sorry, but I have no taste at all for giving my actions value by tying them to some social significance, like improving the world or changing society. My life has a different theme.”

Japanese: 「お前が何を言っているのかよくわからん」
English: “I don’t really understand what you’re saying.”

Japanese: 道夫が首を捻ると亮は眉間に皺を寄せ、
English: When Michio cocked his head, Ryo furrowed his brow.

Japanese: 「じゃあそのことはいいが、街を良くするってどういうことだ？　周みたいなやつらを一人残らず叩きのめしたって何も変わらないぞ。それとも、バックのギャングたちも相手にする気か？　ギャングを一人のこらず潰すなんて現実的じゃないし、そもそもこの街はそんなことを望んでいない。結局、世の中なんてのは、自分が望む形に勝手に変化してゆくものだ。クリス・ツェーが英雄扱いされてるけど、あれだって本人の能力というより、街の空気にのっかっただけの凧みたいなもんだよ」
English: “Fine, forget that part. But what do you mean by making the city better? You could beat every last person like Zhou and nothing would change. Or do you plan to take on the gangs behind them too? Wiping out every gangster isn’t realistic, and this city doesn’t want that in the first place. In the end, the world changes of its own accord into the form it desires. Chris Tse may be treated like a hero, but that has less to do with his abilities than with his being a kite riding the city’s prevailing wind.”

Japanese: 「やっぱりよくわからないが……とにかくおれは、自分に納得出来ないものは見過ごせないし、変えられるものは変えたいんだよ。それがそんなにおかしなことか？」
English: “I still don’t really understand... But I can’t overlook things I find unacceptable, and I want to change whatever I can. Is that so strange?”

Japanese: 「おかしいとは言わないよ。お前がそれで満足ならそうすればいい。でも僕は違うってだけだ。そもそも、この街は好きじゃない。人間の素晴らしいところや、愛らしいところを、全部台無しにしてしまうから」
English: “I wouldn’t call it strange. If it satisfies you, then do it. I’m simply different. To begin with, I don’t like this city. It ruins everything wonderful and lovable about human beings.”

Japanese: 亮は溜息をつき、
English: Ryo sighed.

Japanese: 「そもそも、何が不満なのさ。僕はお前が欲しいものをタダでくれてやると言っているんだぜ？　なのになぜそのことにこだわる」
English: “What are you dissatisfied with, anyway? I’m telling you I’ll give you what you want for free, aren’t I? So why are you so hung up on this?”

Japanese: 「それは、確かにそうなんだけれど……」
English: “Well, you’re right about that, but...”

Japanese: 「じゃあこの話はやめよう。飯がまずくなる」
English: “Then let’s stop talking about it. You’re making the food taste bad.”

Japanese: そう言って亮が食事を再開したのを見て、道夫も黙って食べ始める。
English: Ryo resumed his meal. Watching him, Michio also fell silent and began eating.

Japanese: 全員が食べ終わる頃には亮が「父さん」と呼ぶこの店の主人が起きてきて、無言で調理場に入り道具の準備を始めた。
English: By the time everyone had finished, the owner of the diner, whom Ryo called Father, had awakened. He entered the kitchen without a word and began setting up his equipment.

Japanese: もうすぐ店を開けるというので、道夫と紺太は食器の片付けをして、店を出る。
English: The diner was about to open. Michio and Konta cleared their dishes, then went outside.

Japanese: 外は大分日が傾き、オレンジ色が町並みを染めていた。
English: The sun now hung much lower, staining the cityscape orange.

Japanese: 「なあ、おれ本当にお前のチームもらったのか？」
English: “Hey. Is your team really mine now?”

Japanese: 道夫がそう訊ねると、
English: Michio asked.

Japanese: 「そうだよ。じゃあね」
English: “That’s right. See you.”

Japanese: 亮はそっけなく言い、
English: Ryo answered curtly.

Japanese: 「さよなら」
English: “Goodbye.”

Japanese: その隣で松子も無表情に手を振る。
English: Beside him, Matsuko also waved without changing her expression.

Japanese: 道夫はやはりまだ納得がいっていなかったが、
English: Michio was still far from satisfied.

Japanese: 「ごちそうさま！」
English: “Thanks for the meal!”

Japanese: 紺太が満足げにそう挨拶をすると、
English: Konta called out with satisfaction.

Japanese: 「どうも、ごちそうさまでした……」
English: “Uh, thank you very much for the meal...”

Japanese: つられてそう言ってしまった。
English: Before he knew it, Michio had followed Konta’s example.

Japanese: 「良かったね。喧嘩しないで済んで」
English: “Good thing we didn’t have to fight.”

Japanese: 二人で並んで暗闇通りへの道を歩いていると、紺太がそう話しかけてくる。
English: As they walked side by side toward Darkness Street, Konta spoke to him.

Japanese: 「やっぱ、納得出来ない！」
English: “I still can’t accept it!”

Japanese: 道夫が思わず大きな声を出してしまうと、すぐそばで娼婦に交渉していた紳士が怪訝な顔で振り返る。
English: Michio cried out before he could stop himself. A gentleman negotiating with a prostitute nearby turned and gave him a puzzled look.

Japanese: この辺りは暗闇通りのような大きな通りでは商売が出来ない、個人経営の女や、わけありの女が路上に立って直接客と交渉をしている場所だった。
English: The neighborhood catered to independent sex workers and women whose circumstances kept them from doing business on major thoroughfares such as Darkness Street. They stood along the road and negotiated directly with customers.

Japanese: 「どうしてあいつはあんな素っ気ないんだ？　情熱がないのか？」
English: “Why does he act so indifferent about everything? Doesn’t he have any passion?”

Japanese: さまざまな肌の色をした女が立つこの狭い路地は観光客にとっては刺激的なものだろうが、小さな時から見慣れた道夫たちにとっては当たり前の光景で、肌の露出が多い女たちに目もくれずに道夫はそう嘆く。
English: Women of many different skin colors stood along the narrow alley. Tourists might find the sight stimulating, but Michio and Konta had known it since early childhood, and to them it was entirely ordinary. Paying no attention to the women’s revealing clothes, Michio continued his lament.

Japanese: 「……まあ人は色々だよ。いいじゃない。あいつのことは忘れて次行こう、次。道夫君には、大きな夢があるんだからさ……」
English: “...People are different. There’s nothing wrong with that. Forget about him and move on to the next one. You’ve got a big dream, Michio...”

Japanese: 紺太はそうなだめるが、
English: Konta tried to soothe him.

Japanese: 「いーや、納得出来ないね！」
English: “No! I can’t accept it!”

Japanese: やはり道夫は大きな声で否定する。
English: Michio rejected the suggestion just as loudly as before.

Japanese: 「ああ、道夫じゃないか。どうだい、遊んでいかないかい？」
English: “Oh, if it isn’t Michio. Want to have some fun?”

Japanese: 顔見知りの女が声をかけるが、興奮する道夫の耳には届かない。
English: A woman he knew called to him, but Michio was too worked up to hear her.

Japanese: 「どうして決闘を挑んだ相手にあんな対応が出来るんだ！　そしてチキンまでご馳走するなんてどういうことだ！　おれは食ってしまった！」
English: “How can anyone act that way toward a person who challenged him to a duel? And then he even treated us to chicken! What was that supposed to mean? I ate it!”

Japanese: 「おれなんか、お母さんの分まで包んでもらっちゃったよ」
English: “He even wrapped up some for me to take home to my mother.”

Japanese: 紺太は言って苦笑する。げっぷをすると、まだあのタレのにおいがした。
English: Konta spoke with a wry smile. When he burped, he could still smell the sauce.

Japanese: 「そうだ、なんということだろう！　しかも丁寧に、ごちそうさまでしたと言ってしまった！」
English: “Exactly! The horror! I even thanked him politely for the meal!”

Japanese: 道夫は恋に悩むウェルテルのように大げさな仕草で頭をかかえた。
English: Michio clutched his head in the extravagant manner of Werther tormented by love.

Japanese: 「道夫君は悪ぶってるけど意外と礼儀正しいからね」
English: “You act tough, but you’re surprisingly well mannered.”

Japanese: すっかり満足した紺太は穏やかにそう言う。
English: Now entirely content, Konta spoke mildly.

Japanese: 「しかも旨かった！　つまりこれは、やつに負けてしまったということだ！」
English: “And it was good! Which means I lost to him!”

Japanese: 「どうしてそうなるのさ」
English: “How does that follow?”

Japanese: 思わず笑ってしまう紺太の顔を道夫は立ち止まってじっと見つめ、
English: Konta could not help laughing. Michio stopped and stared intently at him.

Japanese: 「コンタ、おれはこのままじゃ引き下がれない。次こそちゃんとやつと決着をつける！」
English: “Konta, I can’t back down like this. Next time, I’ll settle matters with him properly!”

Japanese: 「次って？　チームは譲ってくれるって言ったんだから決着つける理由がないじゃないか」
English: “Next time? He said he’d give you the team, so there’s nothing left to settle.”

Japanese: 「これじゃすっきりしない。ただで譲られるなんておれのプライドの問題だよ」
English: “This doesn’t feel right. Having it handed to me for nothing wounds my pride.”

Japanese: 道夫は舌打ちをすると、また歩きはじめる。
English: Michio clicked his tongue and began walking again.

Japanese: 「……でも、美味しい料理ご馳走になっちゃったんだよ？」
English: “...But he treated us to that delicious meal.”

Japanese: 紺太は慌てて追いかける。
English: Konta hurried after him.

Japanese: 「あ、コンタ、今日お前の母さんは仕事しないのか？」
English: “Oh, Konta. Isn’t your mother working today?”

Japanese: すれ違おうとした常連客が気がついてそう声をかけるのに、「あ、今日は休んでるんで」と紺太はそう答えてから、
English: A regular customer about to pass them noticed Konta and called out. ‘Oh, she’s taking the day off,’ Konta answered before turning back to Michio.

Japanese: 「あんな親切にしてもらったのに、どうして喧嘩したいのさ」
English: “After he was so kind to us, why do you still want to fight him?”

Japanese: 「それとこれとは別だ」
English: “That’s a separate matter.”

Japanese: 道夫は仏頂面のまま首を振る。
English: Michio shook his head, still sullen.

Japanese: 「おれ、菅原亮ってそんなに悪い奴じゃないような気がするな……」
English: “I don’t think Ryo Sugawara is such a bad person...”

Japanese: 「なんだよ。お前、すっかりヤツに手懐けられてるじゃんか。安上がりなやつだな」
English: “What? He’s already got you eating out of his hand. You’re easy to buy.”

Japanese: 「い、いや、それは……」
English: “N-no, that’s not...”

Japanese: しどろもどろになる紺太を横目でチラと見てから、道夫は親指の爪を忌々しげに噛み、
English: Michio glanced sidelong at the stammering Konta, then bit his thumbnail in frustration.

Japanese: 「菅原亮……おそろしいヤツだぜ。くそ、新しい作戦を考えなきゃな」
English: “Ryo Sugawara... He’s a terrifying opponent. Damn it. I’ll have to devise a new strategy.”

Japanese: そう呟き、さらに足を早めたのである。
English: With that mutter, he quickened his pace still further.

Japanese: 燕町三丁目の大きな松がある屋敷と言えば、木村修吾の家として近所のものにはよく知られていた。
English: In Tsubamecho 3-chome, everyone knew the estate with the great pine as the home of Shugo Kimura.

Japanese: 木村は酒癖が悪いところを除けば他に欠点もない優れた大工で、彼に頼めばまず間違いがないと付近では評判だった。ひっきりなしに仕事が舞い込んでいたが、しかし生活振りはさほど派手とは言えなかった。
English: Except for his behavior when drunk, Kimura was an excellent carpenter with no other notable flaw. Locals said you could not go wrong hiring him. Work came without cease, yet his way of life was anything but extravagant.

Japanese: というのは金がないものからは金をとらず、かわりに安酒の一杯でもかまわないというような性質の人間であったため、ほとんど一銭にもならない仕事ともいえぬ雑用ばかりに追われていたからだ。
English: He refused payment from those who had no money and was perfectly happy to accept a glass of cheap liquor instead. As a result, he remained perpetually occupied with odd jobs that scarcely qualified as work and earned him virtually nothing.

Japanese: 彼はいつも連絡を受けるといつでも道具を持ってひょいひょいと一人で出かけてスラム街のボロ家にあがりこみ、雨漏りを直したり、外れたドアを取り付け、その報酬として臭い密造酒を浴びるほど飲んで真っ赤な顔で帰って来るというのが彼のよくある一日である。
English: Whenever word reached him, he gathered his tools and set off alone with a light step. He entered decrepit houses in the slums, repaired leaking roofs, rehung doors that had come loose, then accepted foul bootleg liquor in payment, drank it by the bucketful, and returned with his face bright red. Such was a typical day for Kimura.

Japanese: 酒の上での失敗も多く、暴力沙汰なども数えきれぬほど起こしていたが、こうした憎めない人柄のせいか人々に愛されていた。ただ、細君はずいぶんと影で泣いたようで、豪放磊落で知られた木村も終生この妻には頭が上がらなかったと言う。
English: Drink brought him no shortage of failures, including more violent incidents than anyone could count. Yet perhaps because there was something impossible to hate in his character, the people loved him. His wife, however, reportedly shed many tears in private. Kimura was famous for his bold, openhearted nature, but until the end of his life, she was the one person he could never defy.

Japanese: こうした木村の性格は、当時彼の家で居候をしていた見土道夫にも大きな影響を与えたのは間違いがない。乱暴であるところや、弱いものに対する愛情、それから愛嬌のある人柄など、彼の性格の基礎となる部分に影響を与えたのは間違いないだろうが、当時二人で一緒にいると仕草や話し癖などもまるでそっくり同じだったという話だから、実の親子よりも親密だったというその関係性が目に浮かぶようだ。
English: There can be no doubt that Kimura’s character greatly influenced Michio Mido, who was then boarding at his home. Kimura’s roughness, his affection for the weak, and his easy charm almost certainly helped form the foundations of Michio’s own personality. It was also said that when the two were together, even their gestures and habits of speech looked exactly alike. Their relationship was reportedly closer than that of a biological father and son, and the resemblance makes it easy to picture why.

Japanese: 幼い頃に母親を殴っていた孤児だというようなイメージから、愛情に恵まれなかった情緒欠落の人物として見土道夫をとらえ、だから成長したのちに八龍解放軍のような組織のリーダーになって過激な事件を起こして道を誤らせたという評価もあるが、それは彼の人間像を正しく捉えたものではないように思う。
English: Because Michio was an orphan who had struck his mother as a young child, some have portrayed him as emotionally deficient and deprived of love. They argue that this was why he later lost his way, becoming leader of an organization like the Hachiryu Liberation Army and causing violent incidents. That judgment does not appear to capture the man correctly.

Japanese: 少なくとも木村家に引き取られてから彼が酒による内臓疾患で病死するまでは、愛情に恵まれた生活を送っていたのだ。
English: At the very least, from the time the Kimura family took him in until Kimura died of alcohol-related organ disease, Michio lived surrounded by affection.

Japanese: 事実、その時期道夫はかなり真剣に大工になることを考えていた。
English: Indeed, during this period, Michio quite seriously considered becoming a carpenter.

Japanese: 道夫は八龍会の老人たちによってこの時既に八龍会幹部になることが約束されており、だから木村も特別彼に技術を教えるようなことはなかったのだが、道夫は自発的に大工になるための修業を行っている。
English: By then, the elders of Hachiryukai had already promised that Michio would become one of its senior members. Kimura therefore made no special effort to teach him the craft, but Michio trained for a carpenter’s life of his own accord.

Japanese: その日も、朝晴れているとみるや庭に出て、その辺りに転がっていた材木の切れ端を使って工作に精を出していた。彼の真っ黒な右手に秘められた能力は、熟練した職人の木村もうらやむほどの優れたもので、手を当てて念じるだけですっぱりとあらかじめ引いたライン通りに切断される。どんな柔らかい材料でも、固い材料でも、ひとつまみの木くずを出すこともなく、そして断面はまるでかんなをかけたようになめらかだった。
English: That day, too, the morning sky was clear, so Michio went into the garden and devoted himself to making something from scraps of lumber lying nearby. The power hidden within his pitch-black right hand was enough to make even a seasoned craftsman like Kimura envious. Michio needed only to place his hand upon the material and will it so, and it parted cleanly along the line he had drawn. However soft or hard the material, the cut produced not a speck of sawdust, and the exposed surface was as smooth as though it had been planed.

Japanese: もし道夫が本当に職人への道を歩んでいたら、比類のない仕事を成し遂げていただろう。
English: Had Michio truly followed the path of a craftsman, he would surely have accomplished work without equal.

Japanese: そうして彼は設計図を確認しながら、材木を道具もなくスパスパと細かく切り分けていた。そしてそれを見守るのは、そっくり同じ姿をした二人の少女だった。
English: Consulting his plans, he continued slicing the lumber into small pieces without tools. Two girls identical in appearance watched him work.

Japanese: 「見土道夫、それつまんないからもうやめなよ」
English: “Michio Mido, that’s boring. Stop already.”

Japanese: 「滑走路通りに遊びに行こう？」
English: “Come play on Runway Street with us.”

Japanese: 縁側に座って足をブラブラさせながら、しきりに文句を言っているのは灰上璃映子と灰上江梨子。ヘドロ団地に住むこの双子は道夫よりも三つ年下だった。
English: The girls sitting on the veranda, swinging their legs and complaining insistently, were Rieko and Eriko Haigami. The twins lived in the Sludge Housing Complex and were three years younger than Michio.

Japanese: 道夫もはじめは無視して黙々と作業をしていたが、あまりにもしつこいのでとうとう音を上げた。
English: At first, Michio ignored them and worked in silence. At last, their persistence wore him down.

Japanese: 「何でおまえら、おれの邪魔してるんだよ。遊びに行きたいなら二人で行けばいいだろ。それか、団地の子なんだから、団地の誰かを誘えばいいじゃないか」
English: “Why are you two bothering me? If you want to play, go by yourselves. Or invite someone from the housing complex. You live there, don’t you?”

Japanese: 道夫は睨み付けて抗議をしたが、双子はやっと自分たちへ注意が向いたという点しか見ず、その言葉は完全に無視をした。
English: Michio glared as he protested. The twins noticed only that they had finally won his attention and ignored every word he said.

Japanese: 「ねえ見てよ見土道夫。このブローチかわいいでしょ？」
English: “Look, Michio Mido. Isn’t this brooch pretty?”

Japanese: 「私たちの大好きな薔薇の形しているの。お兄ちゃんが送ってくれたんだよ？」
English: “It’s shaped like a rose, our favorite flower. Our brother sent it to us.”

Japanese: 双子はそうはしゃいで、自分たちの胸で太陽を照り返して真っ赤に輝く花をかたどったおそろいのブローチを見せる。
English: Chattering excitedly, the twins displayed the matching brooches upon their chests: flowers that reflected the sun and shone a brilliant red.

Japanese: 「うん、よく似合ってるよ」
English: “Yes. They suit you.”

Japanese: 不満げな表情ながらもそう応えてしまうのが道夫であった。
English: Michio answered despite still looking displeased.

Japanese: 姉はタイプA、妹はタイプBの双子は能力を使って度を過ぎた悪戯を繰り返し、孤児ながらも後見人が悪名高いヘドロ団地の大物だということで、こんなに幼いながらも有名な悪童として周囲の人間に疎まれていた。
English: The elder twin was a Type A and the younger a Type B. They repeatedly used their abilities for pranks that went much too far. Although they were orphans, their guardian was a notorious power in the Sludge Housing Complex. Thus, despite their youth, the twins were widely disliked as infamous little terrors.

Japanese: そんなこの双子は普段は同年代の子供なども少しでも気にいらない相手は容赦なくいじめているのだが、一度、それを通りかかった道夫に窘められたことがある。
English: They ordinarily bullied any child their age who displeased them in the slightest, showing no mercy. On one occasion, however, Michio had happened by and reprimanded them.

Japanese: 双子はいつものように注意をした道夫に反発して攻撃を加えたが、タイプAとタイプB両方の性質を持ち合わせた上に、年上で基礎となる身体能力も遥かに高い道夫には叶わなかった。こてんぱんに叩きのめされ、能力者が能力を使ってノーマルをいじめることがいかに悪いことか、卑怯なことか、正座をさせてこんこんと説教をしたのである。
English: As usual, the twins attacked the person who dared correct them. But Michio possessed both Type A and Type B qualities, was older, and had far greater physical ability to begin with. They were no match for him. After thrashing them soundly, Michio made them kneel formally and lectured them at length on how wrong and cowardly it was for people with abilities to use them against Normals.

Japanese: やりたい放題やって来た双子が他人に怒られるのは実の親が死んで以来はじめてのことである。
English: It was the first time anyone had scolded the twins since the death of their biological parents.

Japanese: 結局二人で大泣きして謝り、子分となることを誓ったのだが、なぜかそれ以来道夫になついて、用事もなく遊びに来ては彼をからかっている。もちろん、二人で泣いたことなど完全に忘れた様子である。
English: In the end, they both wept, apologized, and swore to become his subordinates. For some reason, they had been attached to Michio ever since. They visited for no reason other than to tease him—evidently having forgotten entirely that they had ever cried.

Japanese: 何だかんだで甘くしてしまうのが悪いのだ、と道夫もわかっているが、自分と同じように両親がなく、能力者である双子の心情は理解出来るので、むげに扱うことも出来ない。
English: Michio knew that indulging them despite everything was part of the problem. But the twins had lost their parents as he had, and they too possessed abilities. He could understand something of how they felt and could not treat them coldly.

Japanese: 「私たちには、こうやって大事にしてくれるお兄ちゃんがいるんだからねー」
English: “We have a brother who treasures us like this, you know.”

Japanese: 「頭のおかしいお母さんが死んじゃって、本当に誰も家族がいない見土道夫とは違うんだからねー」
English: “We’re not like Michio Mido, whose crazy mother died and who has absolutely no family at all.”

Japanese: もっとも、このように容赦のない言葉を投げかけてくるときは、さすがの道夫ももういっぺん殴ってやろうかと思わぬではないのだが。
English: Admittedly, when they flung such merciless words at him, even Michio sometimes considered giving them one more beating.

Japanese: 「お兄ちゃんはすごいんだよ。立派なところで働いていてね、いつもおもちゃとかお小遣いを送ってくれるんだ」
English: “Our brother is amazing. He works someplace important, and he’s always sending us toys and spending money.”

Japanese: 「今度はゲーム機買ってくれるんだよ。見土道夫はゲーム機買ってくれるようなひといる？」
English: “He’s buying us a game console next. Is there anyone who’ll buy a game console for you, Michio Mido?”

Japanese: 「いいんだよ。ゲームなんかやらないから」
English: “I don’t care. I don’t play games.”

Japanese: 道夫は言って口を尖らせる。
English: Michio thrust out his lower lip as he spoke.

Japanese: 実際のところは、友達で最新のゲームを買ったなどと言う話を聞くと真っ先に駆けつける程度には好きなのであるが。
English: In truth, Michio liked games well enough to race to a friend’s house the moment he heard they had bought the newest one.

Japanese: 「まあでも良かったな。届いたら、ちゃんとお兄さんに丁寧なお礼しなきゃだめだぞ」
English: “Well, I’m glad for you. When it arrives, make sure you thank your brother properly.”

Japanese: 「わかってるよそんなの」
English: “We already know that.”

Japanese: 「大きなお世話だわ」
English: “Mind your own business.”

Japanese: 双子は喜怒哀楽が激しく、突発的で、急に頬を膨らましてむくれてしまう。
English: The twins’ emotions were intense and impulsive. In an instant, their cheeks puffed up with indignation.

Japanese: 全く相手にしていられないということで、道夫は溜息をついて作業を再開しようとしたのだが、
English: Deciding they were impossible to deal with, Michio sighed and tried to resume his work.

Japanese: 「ねえ見土道夫、菅原亮と決闘するってほんと？」
English: “Hey, Michio Mido. Is it true you’re going to duel Ryo Sugawara?”

Japanese: 「一対一でやるんでしょ？」
English: “You’re fighting him one on one, aren’t you?”

Japanese: 意外なことを訊いてきたのでまた手を止める。
English: The unexpected question stopped Michio’s hands once more.

Japanese: 「どこで聞いたんだ？」
English: “Where did you hear that?”

Japanese: 「田中紺太が言ってた」
English: “Konta Tanaka told us.”

Japanese: 「明日って話だけれど」
English: “He said it’s tomorrow.”

Japanese: 双子たちの言う通り、道夫はこの翌日菅原亮を決闘することになっていた。
English: The twins were correct. Michio was scheduled to duel Ryo Sugawara the following day.

Japanese: 先日チームを譲り受けるという話をしたものの、やはり道夫はどうしても納得がいかない。リーダー同士皆の前で決着をつけた上でなければすっきりしないと、亮にしつこく粘ったのである。
English: Ryo had already agreed to hand over his team, yet Michio still could not accept the arrangement. He had pestered Ryo relentlessly, insisting he would never feel satisfied unless the two leaders settled matters before everyone.

Japanese: 亮とすれば別に道夫の縄張りが欲しいわけでもなく、負けて縄張りを失うことにもこだわりがなく、全く戦う理由がないと断り続けていたが、道夫が腰抜けだなんだと罵倒し続けていたら意外と短気なようで腹を立てて挑発に乗ってきた。
English: Ryo did not particularly want Michio’s territory and cared nothing about losing his own. With no reason whatsoever to fight, he repeatedly refused. But Michio continued calling him a coward until Ryo—who was apparently rather quick-tempered—became angry and took the bait.

Japanese: 「僕が勝ってもお前の縄張りはいらない。そのかわりに裸になって逆立ちで滑走路通りを往復してもらう」
English: “Even if I win, I don’t want your territory. Instead, you’ll strip naked, stand on your hands, and travel the length of Runway Street and back.”

Japanese: 亮が何かを手に入れるわけではなく、ただ道夫が恥をかくだけの条件に、やっぱりこいつは性格が悪いと確信しながら頷いた。
English: The condition offered Ryo nothing and merely ensured Michio’s humiliation. Convinced once again that Ryo had a rotten personality, Michio nevertheless agreed.

Japanese: ということで、明日の十三時にパラシュート通り裏の空き地でお互い武器も能力も一切使わずに一対一で戦うということが決まったのである。
English: The duel was thus set for one o’clock the next afternoon, in a vacant lot behind Parachute Street. They would fight one on one, using neither weapons nor abilities of any kind.

Japanese: 「思えば悪いことをしたかもしれないな。あいつは見るからに腕よりも頭を使うタイプなんだろう。それはわかっていたんだけど、おれもなんの理由もなく受け取ることなんか出来なかったんだ」
English: “Looking back, I may have done him wrong. He’s plainly the sort who uses his head more than his fists. I knew that, but I still couldn’t accept receiving something for no reason.”

Japanese: 道夫は頭に血が上って挑んでしまったことを少々後悔していた。
English: Michio had begun to regret issuing the challenge in the heat of the moment.

Japanese: 「それにきっと、おれが頑張ってることを馬鹿にされたような気にもなってたんだ。おれとしたことが大人げない……」
English: “And I think I felt as though he were making fun of everything I’ve been working for. How childish of me...”

Japanese: 道夫が溜息をつくと、双子はクスクスと笑った。
English: Michio sighed. The twins giggled.

Japanese: 「何がおかしいんだ？」
English: “What’s so funny?”

Japanese: 怪訝な顔で問いかえすと、
English: He frowned at them.

Japanese: 「油断してると、道夫負けるよ」
English: “If you’re not careful, Michio, you’ll lose.”

Japanese: 「あいつ、見かけによらず結構強いんだって」
English: “He’s a lot stronger than he looks.”

Japanese: 双子は予想外のことを言う。
English: The twins’ answer was entirely unexpected.

Japanese: 「何か知ってるのか？」
English: “Do you know something?”

Japanese: 「あいつ、馬世傑と一緒に何か習ってるんだよ」
English: “He’s learning something with Ma Sai-kit.”

Japanese: 「それで、練習相手になってるんだってさ」
English: “They say he’s Ma Sai-kit’s training partner.”

Japanese: 双子がヘドロ団地の年長の少年から聞いた話によると、夜に空き地で二人が拳法の道着を身につけてトレーニングをしているところを見かけたことがあるらしい。
English: According to a story the twins had heard from an older boy in the Sludge Housing Complex, the two had been seen training in a vacant lot at night, both dressed in martial-arts uniforms.

Japanese: 馬世傑と言えばYSの幹部にして武術の達人である馬明の息子として拳法の英才教育を受け、街の空手大会では少年でありながら敵知らずといわれた人物だ。大物ギャングの息子ということで街の不良少年たちとは一線を画し、混じって行動することがないが、もし街に出たら自分の勢力をもっていただろう。
English: Ma Sai-kit was the son of Ma Ming, a YS executive and martial-arts master. He had received an elite martial education and was considered unbeatable in the city’s karate tournaments despite his youth. As the son of an important gangster, he kept his distance from the city’s delinquent boys and never ran with them. Had he chosen to enter their world, however, he would surely have commanded a faction of his own.

Japanese: 双子に話をした少年も格闘技を習っていて、その世界の人間には興味があり、確かに見間違いではなかったと言う。
English: The boy who told the twins also practiced a martial art and took an interest in people from that world. He insisted that he could not have mistaken them.

Japanese: 「ああ、だから見覚えがあったのか」
English: “Oh. So that’s why I recognized him.”

Japanese: 空手大会の時にその姿を見たのかも知れない。
English: Perhaps Michio had seen Ryo at a karate tournament.

Japanese: 道夫は自分でそういったものに参加することはなかったが、街にどんな強い人間がいるのか見てやるつもりでよく見学に行った。馬世傑の優勝も目の当たりにしている。きっとそのとき見かけたのだろう。
English: Michio never participated in such events himself, but often attended to see who the strongest people in the city were. He had witnessed Ma Sai-kit’s victory. He had surely seen Ryo there as well.

Japanese: 「ま、まあ、でも練習相手だからって強いとは限らないさ……」
English: “W-well, being someone’s training partner doesn’t necessarily make him strong...”

Japanese: 道夫は腕組みをして強がってみせるが、動揺を隠しきれず双子に笑われてしまう。
English: Michio folded his arms and tried to sound confident, but failed to conceal his unease. The twins laughed at him.

Japanese: 「能力つかっちゃえばー？」
English: “Why don’t you use your power?”

Japanese: 「金色の目を使う？　それとも、右手の力でスパっと首を切り落としちゃう？」
English: “Will you use your golden eyes? Or slice his head right off with your hand?”

Japanese: 「ばか。そんなこと出来るわけないだろ」
English: “Idiots. Of course I can’t do that.”

Japanese: 道夫は苦い顔で否定してから、
English: Michio rejected the idea with a grimace, then continued.

Japanese: 「でも、腕が立つようならかえって良かったよ。勝つにしろ負けるにしろ、相手が強い方がいい。その方がすっきり戦えるからね」
English: “If he knows how to fight, so much the better. Win or lose, I’d rather face somebody strong. That way, we can have a clean fight.”

Japanese: 言葉どおり安堵したように溜息をついた。
English: Michio sighed, seeming genuinely relieved by his own conclusion.

Japanese: 「アハハ、へんなやつー」
English: “Ahaha! You’re so weird.”

Japanese: 「気持ちわるっ」
English: “Gross.”

Japanese: 「おれは真剣だぞ。おまえらはガキだし女だから、こういう気持ちがわからないんだ」
English: “I’m serious. You’re little kids and girls besides, so you can’t understand how this feels.”

Japanese: 道夫は顔を顰めた。
English: Michio frowned.

Japanese: 「まあ、なんでもいいよ」
English: “Whatever.”

Japanese: 「私たちも明日見に行くからね！」
English: “We’re coming to watch tomorrow!”

Japanese: 「くんなよ。男の真剣勝負なんだ」
English: “Don’t. It’s a serious contest between men.”

Japanese: 「いやだよ。見土道夫が負けるところ見るんだから」
English: “No. We’re coming to watch Michio Mido lose.”

Japanese: 「それで、裸で逆立ち歩きしてるところを写真に撮ってあげるね」
English: “And we’ll take pictures of you walking on your hands naked.”

Japanese: 双子はおかしそうに笑い、道夫は深く深く溜息をつくと、木片を一つ手に取ってようやく作業を再開した。
English: The twins laughed delightedly. Michio heaved a very deep sigh, picked up a piece of wood, and finally returned to his work.

Japanese: 翌日双子は朝から団地を出て、道夫と亮の決闘時間までを滑走路通りで遊んで過ごした。
English: The next morning, the twins left the housing complex and spent the hours before Michio and Ryo’s duel playing upon Runway Street.

Japanese: ヘドロ団地には彼女たちと同年代の子供も多く済み、彼らと遊ぶこともあったが最近は街に出てばかりいる。
English: Many children their age lived in the Sludge Housing Complex, and the twins sometimes played with them, but lately they had spent nearly all their time in the city.

Japanese: とにかく二人は毎日違うことをして、その日が少しでも変化のある、他の日とは違う一日になることを求めていたのだ。
English: More than anything, they wanted every day to bring something new, to become a day unlike all the others.

Japanese: ヘドロ団地はY地区の外にある小学校の学区であり、Y地区内にもいくつかの教育施設は存在する。双子も一応は小学生であったが、学校には一度か二度顔を出したきりだった。……もっとも、この辺りの事情は二人が特別だったわけではなく、この辺りの子供にとってはよくあることだ。子供の多くは親の仕事を手伝い、残りの時間は遊んでいる。
English: The Sludge Housing Complex fell within the catchment area of an elementary school outside Y District, and several educational facilities also existed inside Y District itself. The twins were nominally elementary-school pupils, yet they had attended school only once or twice. ...In this respect, however, they were not unusual. Such circumstances were common among the children of the area. Most helped with their parents’ work and spent the rest of their time playing.

Japanese: 物好きな大人が子供を集めて読み書きなどを教えており、そういった場所である程度知識を身につけることも出来たが、文字も読めない子供も多かった。
English: A few adults with the inclination gathered children and taught them reading, writing, and similar subjects. A child could acquire some knowledge at such places, but many remained unable even to read.

Japanese: だから平日の真っ昼間に彼女たちが歩いていてもおかしいということはないのだが、そっくり同じ容姿をもつ二人が並んでいると、人の多い滑走路通りでもよく目立ってしまう。
English: There was therefore nothing remarkable about the twins walking outside in the middle of a weekday. Yet two girls with identical faces stood out even amid the crowds of Runway Street.

Japanese: そして彼女たちに痛い目にあった経験がある路上の物売り者たちは、その姿を見るとしかめっ面になって売り物に覆いを掛けたり、目が合わぬように顔を背けたりするのだった。
English: Street vendors who had suffered at their hands grimaced when they saw them. Some covered their wares; others turned their faces away to avoid meeting the twins’ eyes.

Japanese: 双子はそういう反応をニヤニヤと眺めながら、スカートをひらめかせて通り過ぎてゆく。
English: The twins watched these reactions with grins, then passed by with their skirts fluttering.

Japanese: 滑走路通りには亮と揉めた周のグループも含めていくつかの不良少年のグループがあったが、そうした少年たちも双子には手を出さなかった。
English: Several groups of delinquent boys operated upon Runway Street, including Zhou’s group, which had clashed with Ryo. Even they left the twins alone.

Japanese: 以前はその傍若無人な態度に神経を逆なでされたものが表情をこわばらせて低い声で脅しにいったりもしたが、能力を使うことにまったく躊躇いのない双子に散々に弄ばれて恥をかくだけの結果に終わってしまうのだ。
English: In the past, boys angered by the twins’ insolence had sometimes approached with rigid expressions and threats delivered in low voices. But the twins felt no hesitation about using their abilities and merely toyed with them until they withdrew in humiliation.

Japanese: そうしたことが何度か繰り返された結果、双子の姿を見たほうがこそこそ姿を隠すような状態になった。
English: After this happened several times, the boys began hiding whenever they saw the twins instead.

Japanese: 双子はどこか特定のグループに入っているわけでもなかったし、ヘドロ団地の深沢が後見人であるということも徐々に知られはじめていたから、忌々しいながらも関わらないのが上策と判断されたのだった。
English: The twins belonged to no particular group, and word was gradually spreading that their guardian was Fukazawa, an important figure in the Sludge Housing Complex. However infuriating they might be, everyone concluded that avoiding them was the wiser course.

Japanese: 「あのクソ生意気なイカレたガキが……」
English: “Those fucking obnoxious little psychos...”

Japanese: と周少年などはよく口に出したが、彼もやはり実際に遭遇すると目をそらし、気づかぬふりをする。
English: Young Zhou often said this aloud. Yet when he actually encountered them, he too averted his eyes and pretended not to notice.

Japanese: これは双子にとってはまったく退屈な状況で、
English: The twins found this situation unbearably dull.

Japanese: 「ねえ、今日はあそばないの？」
English: “Hey, aren’t we playing today?”

Japanese: 「遊ぼうよ？」
English: “Come play with us.”

Japanese: 目の前に回り込んで挑発的に笑うのだが、周はことさらに仲間と大きな声で世間話を続けて視線を合わせないようにそれを避ける。
English: They stepped directly in front of Zhou and smiled provocatively. Zhou avoided their eyes by continuing an especially loud conversation with his friends.

Japanese: 「つまんないー！」
English: “Boring!”

Japanese: 「ばかー！」
English: “Idiot!”

Japanese: 双子は頬を膨らまし、その背中に小石を投げるのだった。
English: The twins puffed out their cheeks and threw pebbles at his back.

Japanese: そうしてどこへ行ってもすっかり腫れ物扱いをされている双子にも、優しく接するものはいた。
English: Yet even the twins, now treated everywhere as though they were dangerous to touch, had people who showed them kindness.

Japanese: 道夫もその一人ではあるが、滑走路通りの端でソフトクリームを売るメリッサというフィリピン人の若い女も、双子を見かけるたびに好きなソフトクリームを選ばせて二人を可愛がった。
English: Michio was one. Another was Melissa, a young Filipino woman who sold soft-serve ice cream at the end of Runway Street. Whenever she saw the twins, she let each choose her favorite flavor and treated them with affection.

Japanese: この頃は小さな販売車を使って一人で切り盛りしていた彼女だが、今は立派な店舗を構え十人もの従業員を抱える繁盛店のオーナーとなっている。
English: In those days, she operated alone from a small converted van. Today she owns a thriving shop with a proper storefront and ten employees.

Japanese: 「あの二人のことはねえ、本当に大好きだったんですよ」
English: “I truly loved those two girls.”

Japanese: メリッサは目のまわりに深い笑いジワが出来た優しげな表情の女性で、筆者が灰上姉妹について聞くために訪ねると、当時のアポイントメントにもかかわらず嫌な顔ひとつせずに対応してくれた。
English: Melissa was a gentle-looking woman with deep smile lines around her eyes. When the author visited to ask her about the Haigami sisters, she received him graciously despite the short notice.

Japanese: 「ご両親が亡くなって、暗い顔をしていたくないという気持ちが強かったんですよ。人を心配させたり、同情させると申し訳なくなるからいやだと言っていました。とても優しい子たちでした」
English: “After their parents died, they felt very strongly that they didn’t want to look unhappy. They said they hated making people worry about them or pity them because it made them feel guilty. They were very kind girls.”

Japanese: メリッサは当時を懐かしむような寂しさの入り交じった遠い笑顔を浮かべて双子のことを語る。
English: Melissa spoke of the twins with a distant smile that mingled nostalgia and sorrow.

Japanese: 話がコシチェイのことに及ぶと顔を僅かに暗くしたが、それでも双子のことを一言も悪くは言わなかった。
English: When the subject turned to Koschei, a slight shadow crossed her face. Even then, however, she did not say a single unkind word about the twins.

Japanese: 「とにかく、どんな相手にも公平で平等なんです。偏見がないというか……だから、そのような人が相手でも、何かひとつでも興味が持てるところがあれば、仲良くなってしまうんでしょうねえ。そんな人と関わればどうなるかというのは本人たちもよくわかっていたんでしょうけれど、そういう打算で行動するのを何よりも嫌う子たちでしたから……」
English: “More than anything, they were fair. They treated everyone equally, without prejudice... I suppose that was why, even with a person like that, if they found a single thing that interested them, they became friends. I’m sure they understood perfectly well what could happen if they associated with someone like that. But they hated acting from such calculations more than anything...”

Japanese: 彼女はそう言って深い溜息をついた。
English: With those words, Melissa sighed deeply.

Japanese: その日も双子はメリッサのワンボックスを改造した販売車の前で、客用に並べられた丸椅子に腰掛けて貰ったソフトクリームをなめて時間を過ごしていた。
English: That day, the twins sat upon the round stools arranged for customers before Melissa’s converted van, passing the time as they licked the soft-serve ice cream she had given them.

Japanese: 双子もメリッサには懐いており、その近くでは商売の邪魔になるような振る舞いをしない。悪いことをしなければ非常に愛くるしい二人の子供で、彼女のことを知らないものにとっては微笑ましく、あるいはいくらかの販促にもなっていただろう。
English: The twins were fond of Melissa and did nothing near her that might interfere with business. When they were not misbehaving, they were two exceedingly adorable children. To anyone unfamiliar with their reputation, they must have looked charming and might even have helped attract customers.

Japanese: 双子はそこでメリッサや他の客とおしゃべりを楽しむという、彼女たちにしては非常におとなしい時間の過ごし方をして、道夫たちの決闘が始まる少し前にその場を後にした。
English: They spent an unusually quiet interval chatting with Melissa and her other customers, then departed shortly before Michio and Ryo’s duel was to begin.

Japanese: 「どっちが勝つかなー？」
English: “Who do you think will win?”

Japanese: 「わからないけど、どっちかが負けそうになったら邪魔する？」
English: “I don’t know. Should we interfere if one of them starts losing?”

Japanese: 「おもしろそう。遠くから足とか引っ張って、転ばせちゃおっか？」
English: “That sounds fun. We could pull on his legs from far away and make him fall.”

Japanese: 「見土道夫はきっと真っ赤になって怒るよー」
English: “Michio Mido will turn bright red and get mad.”

Japanese: 二人がクスクスと笑い合いながら通行しているのは普通の路上ではなく、塀の上だった。彼女たちはあまり道を使わず、片方はサイキックの能力を借りて、もう片方はタイプBの脚力で、民家の屋根の上などを伝い、ぴょんぴょんと飛び跳ねて、猫でも使わないようなルートで移動する。
English: The twins giggled to each other as they traveled—not along an ordinary road, but atop a wall. They seldom used the streets. One relied upon psychic power while the other relied upon the legs of a Type B. They passed over the roofs of houses, hopping from place to place along routes that not even cats would use.

Japanese: そのため、どこにでも神出鬼没で現れ、そしていたずらをするものだから彼女のターゲットとなる人々にとっては厄介にもほどがあるだろう。
English: They consequently appeared anywhere without warning and played their pranks. For the people they targeted, there could hardly have been anything more troublesome.

Japanese: こうした移動方法も彼女たちなりの遊びで、ときおり見てはならないものを見てしまって危険なことに巻き込まれることもあるのだが、しかしこの日彼女たちが遭遇したものは今までのものとは全く性質が違った。
English: This way of traveling was another form of play for the twins. At times, they saw things they should not have seen and became entangled in danger. What they encountered this day, however, was unlike anything that had come before.

Japanese: タイプBの発作で叫び声がするボロ屋のトタン屋根を踏み越え、素人の手によって板を張り付けただけの雑な補修が目立つ古い木造アパートの裏にトンと着地をしたときだった。
English: They crossed the corrugated-metal roof of a shack from which someone screamed in the throes of a Type B episode, then landed lightly behind an old wooden apartment building whose crude repairs consisted of boards nailed on by amateur hands.

Japanese: 歩き出そうとしたところで地面に何か黒い影が見え、二人の頭上を大きなものがかすめ飛んでその長い髪をふわりと舞わせる。
English: They had just begun to move when a black shadow appeared upon the ground. Something large swept over their heads, lifting their long hair into the air.

Japanese: びっくりして足を止めた二人の目の前に、ストンと着地したのは見たことのない怪物だった。
English: The girls froze in surprise. An unknown monster landed lightly before them.

Japanese: 奇妙な姿をしたものが多数存在するこの街でも、これほどおかしな生き物を二人は見たことがない。
English: Even in this city of countless strange forms, the twins had never seen such a bizarre creature.

Japanese: 一見すると、巨大なクモやタカアシガニのようだった。くの字に折れ曲がる四本の足は長く細く、小さな二人が顎を上げて見上げるほどだ。そしてその足に、吊り下げられるように胴体が付いている。全身は茶色く短い毛に覆われ、頭には大きな複眼がひとつ、その下に窮屈に押し込められたように小さな口と鼻がついている。
English: At first glance, it resembled a gigantic spider or Japanese spider crab. Four long, slender legs bent at sharp angles and rose so high that the small girls had to tilt back their heads to see them. A torso appeared to hang suspended from those legs. Short brown hair covered the entire body. The head bore one enormous compound eye; beneath it, a tiny mouth and nose seemed to have been pressed into what little room remained.

Japanese: 身体にはズタボロになった白いシャツと、黒いズボン、そして胴体に斜めがけになっているのは革の黒カバンだった。
English: It wore a tattered white shirt and black trousers. A black leather bag hung diagonally across its torso.

Japanese: まったく怪物という他ない醜い姿だが、これも人間なのだろう。Y地区の外れのボーダーエリアには特質変異で醜く変わり果てたタイプAたちがかたまって住んでいるが、そこにもこれほど人間離れしたものはいない。
English: The hideous figure could only be called a monster, yet it was presumably human. Type As disfigured by trait mutations lived together in the border area at the edge of Y District, but even there, no one appeared so far removed from humanity.

Japanese: しかもその大きな複眼は金色に輝いている。
English: Moreover, the enormous compound eye shone gold.

Japanese: つまりこいつは、ただのタイプAではなく、タイプBの要素もかねあわせたハイブリッドなのだ。
English: In other words, this was not merely a Type A, but a hybrid who also possessed Type B qualities.

Japanese: 怪物はその金色の目で二人を見定めると、口を動かす。その表紙に、紫色の唇の端から唾液が糸を引いて垂れ落ちた。
English: The monster fixed its golden eye upon the twins and moved its mouth. At the motion, a thread of saliva stretched down from the corner of its purple lips.

Japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと、あなた何者？」
English: “W-who are you?”

Japanese: 「あっち行きなよ」
English: “Go away.”

Japanese: 二人は口では強がっているがさすがに顔は蒼白だった。
English: The twins spoke bravely, but their faces had gone pale.

Japanese: 「ほらっ！　石ぶつけるよ！」
English: “Stay back! We’ll throw stones at you!”

Japanese: 「近づかないで！」
English: “Don’t come any closer!”

Japanese: 片方は金色の目を光らせて石を握りしめ、もう片方は見えない力で浮かせる。
English: One girl’s eyes shone gold as she gripped a stone. The other raised one into the air with an invisible force.

Japanese: しかしその言葉は怪物に理解出来ないのか、それとも聞くつもりがないのか、口元でしゅるしゅると空気の抜ける音を立てながら近づいて来る。その長い手足の先には、土で茶色く汚れたかぎ爪がついていた。一本一本がちょっとした果物ナイフほどの大きさを持っている。
English: Perhaps the monster could not understand their words, or perhaps it had no intention of listening. It advanced with a hissing sound like air escaping through its mouth. Dirt-browned claws tipped its long limbs, each one the size of a small paring knife.

Japanese: 怪物が進む分だけ二人は後ずさる。準備した石は、攻撃によって相手の感情を逆なでしてしまうことを考えると簡単には投げつけることが出来ない。
English: The twins retreated with every step it took. They had readied their stones, but could not easily throw them for fear an attack would provoke the creature further.

Japanese: 「逃げよう！」
English: “Run!”

Japanese: 「うんっ」
English: “Okay!”

Japanese: 二人で頷きあうと、くるりと身体を反転してうしろに駆け出した。アパートの建物の横を通って路上に出れば、ゴミゴミした狭い裏路地になる。素早く小さい二人がここに逃げ込めば相手も姿を見失うはずだ。
English: They nodded to each other, turned in unison, and ran. Beyond the side of the apartment building lay a narrow, cluttered back street. If the quick, small girls could reach it, the creature ought to lose sight of them.

Japanese: しかし、数歩も進まないうちに、頭上でびゅんと何かが飛ぶ音がする。
English: Before they had taken more than a few steps, something sliced through the air above them.
“Eek!”

Japanese: 二人は足を止め首をすくめる。
English: The twins stopped and ducked their heads.

Japanese: その目の前に、ひとっ飛びで二人の頭を飛び越した怪物が土埃をあげて着地をした。
English: The monster had cleared both girls in a single leap. It landed before them in a cloud of dust.

Japanese: どうやらとても逃げられるような相手ではないようだ。
English: Evidently, this was not an opponent they could escape from.

Japanese: 「逃がしてくれないなら、痛い思いしてもらうよ」
English: “If you won’t let us go, you’re going to get hurt.”

Japanese: 「後悔しても遅いんだからね」
English: “It’ll be too late to regret it.”

Japanese: 緊張と恐怖で汗だくになりながら、二人は攻撃を開始する。
English: Drenched in sweat from tension and fear, the twins began their attack.

Japanese: まず一人がその念動力で石を飛ばす。空中で不規則に動きながら近づく石に、怪物の視線は釘付けになる。その隙に、もう一人がタイプBの力による大人顔負けの腕力で素早く強く石を投げつけるのだ。
English: First, one twin sent a stone flying with her psychokinesis. The monster’s gaze fixed upon the stone as it approached along an erratic path. While it was distracted, the other twin hurled her own stone swiftly and powerfully with Type B strength that rivaled an adult’s.

Japanese: これがこの二人の必勝パターンで、街の不良少年たちは幼い少女たちによる二種類の投石になすすべもない。
English: This was the twins’ infallible pattern. The delinquent boys of the city had no answer to such a two-pronged barrage from two young girls.

Japanese: 投石というのは危険なもので、当たり所や石の大きさや力の加減によって簡単に人が死ぬ。この幼い二人は見かけによらず冷静で普段はそれを心得ており、どんなときでも手加減していたが今回はそれをしなかった。
English: Throwing stones was dangerous. Depending upon the point of impact, the stone’s size, and the force employed, it could easily kill. The two young girls were calmer than their appearance suggested and ordinarily understood this. They always moderated their strength. This time, however, they did not.

Japanese: 全力で投げた石が、意識をとられた怪物の顔面に向かい風を切り裂く音を立てながら飛んで行く。
English: The stone thrown at full force screamed through the air toward the face of the distracted monster.

Japanese: ゴツッと鈍い音がする。
English: A dull thud followed.

Japanese: 「当たった？」
English: “Did it hit?”

Japanese: 「いや、ダメだ！」
English: “No! It’s no good!”

Japanese: 頭部を狙って投げつけた筈だが、僅かに外れて肩の辺りに飛んでしまったらしい。怪物は痛みで顔をしわだらけにして細かく震えたが、そうやって怯んでいるのも一瞬で、すぐに双子に向かって動き始める。
English: The throw had been aimed at the monster’s head, but apparently went slightly wide and struck near its shoulder. The creature’s face crumpled with pain, and it trembled rapidly. Yet it flinched for only a moment before beginning to move toward the twins once more.

Japanese: 四本の足をカサカサと動かす移動方法は、そのタイプBの力のせいか見かけによらず素早く、逃げ切ることが出来ない。
English: It scuttled upon its four legs, moving far more quickly than its appearance suggested—perhaps because of its Type B strength. They could not outrun it.

Japanese: もっと大きな石を探そうとしていたせいで判断が遅れた双子にそのかぎ爪のついた前足を伸ばす。
English: The twins lost precious time searching for a larger stone. The creature extended a clawed foreleg toward them.

Japanese: 「痛っ！」
English: “Ow!”

Japanese: 一人が肩を押さえ、血が空中に舞う。
English: One twin clutched her shoulder as blood flew through the air.

Japanese: 「くそっ！」
English: “Damn it!”

Japanese: もう一人が金色の目になって傷ついたもう一人の身体にしがみついた。そこに怪物の二振りめのかぎ爪が襲い掛かり、今度は助けようとした方の腕を切り裂く。
English: The other twin’s eyes turned gold, and she threw her arms around the wounded girl. The monster’s claws swept down a second time and slashed the arm of the twin attempting the rescue.

Japanese: 「うっ」
English: “Ngh!”

Japanese: 抱きかかえたまま地面を蹴って必死で距離を開けたが、地面に尻餅をついてしまう。
English: Still holding the other girl, she kicked desperately against the ground and put some distance between them and the monster. Then she landed hard upon her backside.

Japanese: この距離でこの体勢では、もう逃げることは出来ない。
English: At this distance and in this position, they could no longer escape.

Japanese: 二人は全身が凍り付くような恐怖と共に引きつった顔で相手を見たが、怪物はそこに立ち止まったまま動かない。
English: Their entire bodies seemed to freeze with fear. Faces rigid, they stared at their opponent. Yet the monster remained where it stood and did not move.

Japanese: 金色の目でこちらをみつめ、しゅるしゅると相変わらず口元で音を立てている。
English: Its golden eye watched them as the same hiss continued to issue from its mouth.

Japanese: 「早くっ！　石をっ！」
English: “Hurry! The stone!”

Japanese: 慌ててそのあたりに落ちているうちで一番大きそうなものをつかみ取ると、尻餅の姿勢のまま思い切り相手に投げつけた。
English: In a panic, one twin seized the largest object she could find nearby and hurled it with all her strength while still sitting upon the ground.

Japanese: 鈍い音と共に、怪物の頭の辺りで血がはじける。
English: With another dull sound, blood burst near the monster’s head.

Japanese: 今度は無事に頭部に命中したらしく、怪物は空気を切り裂くような甲高い悲鳴を上げて、全身を震わせた。
English: This time, the stone had apparently struck its target. The monster gave a shrill scream that tore through the air, and its entire body convulsed.

Japanese: そして双子はその間に立ち上がると恐怖に急かされ不十分な体勢のまま駆け出し、泳ぐようによろけながらその場を離れた。
English: While it recoiled, the twins stood. Driven by fear, they began running before they had regained their balance and staggered away as though swimming through the air.

Japanese: 亮と道夫は空き地の中央で向かい合っていた。
English: Ryo and Michio stood facing each other in the center of a vacant lot.

Japanese: その周囲をそれそれぞれの仲間が取り囲んでいる。これからこの二人の少年が彼らを代表して戦いをはじめる。取り囲む少年たちにとって二人は自分の運命を握るリーダーであると共に、闘鶏の鶏や闘犬の犬と同じ、見世物として戦う宿命を負った存在でもあった。
English: Their respective friends formed a ring around them. The two boys were about to begin fighting as their representatives. To the boys watching, they were leaders who held everyone’s fate in their hands. Yet they were also like roosters in a cockfight or dogs in a dogfight—creatures condemned to fight as a spectacle.

Japanese: 観衆の興奮と緊張が張り詰めたそのど真ん中で、二人はそれぞれ涼しい顔をしてお互いを見つめ合っている。こうして立つと道夫の方が頭半分くらい背が高かったが、亮には特に怯む様子もない。見ている方よりも、戦う側の方が落ち着いているようにさえ見えた。
English: At the very center of the spectators’ taut excitement and tension, the two boys regarded each other with equally calm expressions. Standing this way, Michio was about half a head taller, but Ryo showed no sign of intimidation. Indeed, the fighters themselves appeared calmer than the people watching.

Japanese: 二人の間に立っているのは立会人を買って出た西町のチャイという少年で、亮たちより二つ年上のタイ人だ。体格が良く腕っ節が強い上に温厚で人格も認められているために今回の件に引っ張り出された。
English: Between them stood the boy who had volunteered to referee: Chai of West Town, a Thai boy two years older than Ryo and Michio. He had been recruited because he possessed a strong build and powerful arms, yet was also mild-tempered and respected for his character.

Japanese: 「いいか、武器やミュータント能力は使おうとした時点で失格だ。気絶をしたらそれ以上攻撃をしてはいけない……」
English: “Listen carefully. The moment either of you attempts to use a weapon or mutant ability, you’re disqualified. If one of you loses consciousness, the other must not attack him again...”

Japanese: チャイはぎょろりとした丸い目で二人の顔を交互に見ながら説明を続ける。
English: Chai continued explaining, his large round eyes moving from one boy’s face to the other.

Japanese: 「決着がついたら、勝者と敗者は取り決め通りのものを交換する。道夫が勝った場合は縄張りを得て、亮が勝った場合は道夫の罰ゲームだ。いいな？」
English: “When the fight is decided, the winner and loser will honor the agreed terms. If Michio wins, he gets the territory. If Ryo wins, Michio performs the penalty. Understood?”

Japanese: 「ああ」
English: “Yes.”

Japanese: と返事をしたのは道夫。
English: Michio was the one who answered.

Japanese: 亮は無言でこくりと頷く。
English: Ryo silently gave a small nod.

Japanese: 「よし、じゃあ……」
English: “All right. Then—”

Japanese: そしてチャイが戦いの開始を告げようとしたときだった。
English: Chai was about to announce the beginning of the fight.

Japanese: 空き地に傷を負った二人の少女が真っ青な顔で入って来たのである。
English: At that moment, two wounded girls entered the vacant lot with faces drained of color.

Japanese: 普段勝ち気なその有名な双子がそんな顔をしているのも、腕からポタポタと血を流しているのも異常な光景だ。うしろの方にいた少年たちがその姿に気がつくとざわつきはじめ、これから戦おうとしている二人もその姿を見ることになった。
English: Seeing the famously headstrong twins wear such expressions was strange enough. Blood dripping from their arms made the sight stranger still. The boys at the back noticed them and began to murmur, drawing the attention of the two about to fight.

Japanese: 「……ちょっと、すまん」
English: “...Sorry. Give me a moment.”

Japanese: 道夫は亮にそう告げると、双子の近くに駈け寄った。
English: Michio said this to Ryo and ran over to the twins.

Japanese: 「おい、どうしたんだ。その怪我は……」
English: “Hey. What happened? Those injuries...”

Japanese: 「化け物が……」
English: “A monster...”

Japanese: 「クモみたいなやつに襲われて……」
