English: “Something like a spider attacked us...”

Japanese: 双子は今にも泣き出しそうに顔をしかめてそう言った。
English: The twins spoke with faces twisted upon the verge of tears.

Japanese: 「ごめん、決闘の邪魔をして」
English: “Sorry we interrupted the duel.”

Japanese: 「でも道夫しか頼れなかったんだ」
English: “But you were the only person we could rely on, Michio.”

Japanese: 「気にするな。それより、傷を見せてみろ」
English: “Forget about that. Let me see the wounds.”

Japanese: 道夫は双子の腕を掴むと、服ごと引き裂かれ、鮮血をしたたらせるその傷口を見た。
English: Michio took hold of the twins’ arms and examined the cuts beneath their torn clothes, dripping bright blood.

Japanese: 「安心しろ。血は流れているが切れているのはほんの表面だけだ。縫うほどの傷じゃない。だけれど、傷口の消毒はしたほうがいいな……おい、コンタ」
English: “Don’t worry. There’s blood, but the cuts are only superficial. You won’t need stitches. We should disinfect them, though... Hey, Konta.”

Japanese: 道夫は傍らで見ていた紺太を呼ぶと、決闘後のために用意していた消毒薬やガーゼで双子の傷の手当てをはじめる。
English: Michio called to Konta, who stood nearby, and began treating the twins with the disinfectant and gauze they had prepared for after the duel.

Japanese: 「化け物ってどういうことだ？」
English: “What do you mean by a monster?”

Japanese: いつの間にかそばまで来ていた亮が、道夫に腕を差し出し手当てをさせている双子にそう訊ねる。
English: Ryo had approached without their noticing. He put the question to the twins as they held out their arms for Michio’s treatment.

Japanese: そして双子は、悔しそうな顔で今さっきそこで起きたことを説明した。
English: With frustrated expressions, they explained what had happened only moments before.

Japanese: 正体不明の凶悪な怪物の出現に、その場の少年たちはざわめき出す。
English: The report of an unidentified and dangerous monster sent murmurs through the boys.

Japanese: 「クモみたいなやつか……聞いたことがないな。外からやって来たんだろうか……」
English: “Something like a spider... I’ve never heard of it. Could it have come from outside the city...?”

Japanese: 亮は難しい顔で首を捻った。
English: Ryo tilted his head with a troubled expression.

Japanese: 「もしかして、ボーダーから来たんじゃないか？」
English: “Maybe it came from the border area.”

Japanese: 手当を終えた道夫はそう言った。その顔には憤りを浮かべている。双子が傷つけられたことに怒っているのだ。
English: Having finished the treatment, Michio offered the suggestion. Indignation showed upon his face. He was angry that someone had hurt the twins.

Japanese: 「いやどうだろう。聞いたことがないな」
English: “I’m not sure. I’ve never heard of anything like it.”

Japanese: 「でもボーダーにはわけのわからないやつが沢山隠れてるぜ。……悪いが、決闘はまた今度にしてくれないか？」
English: “But all kinds of creatures nobody understands hide in the border area. ...I’m sorry, but can we hold the duel another time?”

Japanese: 「ああ。こちらとしても、自分のテリトリーにそんな怪物がいるんじゃゆっくり決闘なんかしている場合じゃない」
English: “Yes. If a monster like that is loose in my territory, this is hardly the time for a leisurely duel.”

Japanese: 「すまないな」
English: “Sorry.”

Japanese: 道夫は亮にそう謝り、また双子に向かった。
English: Michio apologized to Ryo, then turned back to the twins.

Japanese: 「とりあえず、今日はおまえたちは団地に戻るんだ。送ってやる。その化け物のことはおれたちに任せて休んだ方が良い」
English: “For now, you two are going back to the housing complex. I’ll escort you. Leave the monster to us and get some rest.”

Japanese: 「私たちだけ逃げられない」
English: “We can’t be the only ones who run away.”

Japanese: 双子は目を涙ぐませてはいるが、唇をぐっと噛み、負けん気をあらわにして言った。
English: Tears stood in the twins’ eyes. Nevertheless, they bit their lips and spoke with open defiance.

Japanese: 「見土、そいつらは好きにさせよう。今はとにかく、その怪物と遭遇したって現場に行った方がいいんじゃないか？　怪我をさせたなら、今がチャンスかもしれない」
English: “Mido, let them do as they like. For now, shouldn’t we go to the place where they encountered the monster? If they injured it, this may be our best opportunity.”

Japanese: 亮が言うと、道夫はその顔と双子の顔を交互に見てから、納得したように頷いた。
English: At Ryo’s words, Michio looked between Ryo and the twins, then nodded in acceptance.

Japanese: そしてすぐに二人は何人かの仲間を引き連れて双子が襲われたという場所へ急行した。
English: Michio and Ryo immediately gathered several companions and hurried to the place where the twins had been attacked.

Japanese: 「だ、誰もいないね」
English: “Th-there’s nobody here.”

Japanese: 両手に握った棒きれを構えている紺太は、怯えているわけではないがさすがに緊張してこめかみに汗をかいている。
English: Konta held a stick in each hand at the ready. He was not frightened, but the circumstances had understandably put him on edge, and sweat beaded at his temples.

Japanese: 一同が駆けつけたとき既にそこには誰の姿もなく、ただ土の上に血痕だけが残されていた。
English: By the time they arrived, no one remained. Only stains of blood upon the dirt marked the encounter.

Japanese: 「どこへ行ったんだろうな。人混みの方へ行ったんなら、騒ぎになっているはずだが」
English: “Where did it go? If it headed toward the crowds, there ought to be an uproar.”

Japanese: 道夫は周囲を見回すが、その化け物が逃げた方向の手がかりになりそうなものは見つからなかった。
English: Michio looked around but found nothing that might indicate the direction in which the monster had fled.

Japanese: 一方亮は連れてきた松子と共に血痕を取り囲んでしゃがみ込んでいる。
English: Ryo and Matsuko, whom he had brought along, crouched beside the bloodstains.

Japanese: 「何かにおいはするかい？」
English: “Can you smell anything?”

Japanese: 言われて松子は鼻をくんくんとさせてみるが、顔を顰めて首を横に振る。
English: At his request, Matsuko sniffed the air. She frowned and shook her head.

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: 亮は顎に手を当てて考え込み、するとそちらを見ている道夫と目が合った。
English: Ryo rested a hand upon his chin and sank into thought. Then he looked up and met Michio’s gaze.

Japanese: 「この子はタイプBの特性がとても強く出ていてね。嗅覚も犬並みとは言わないが、とても優れているんだ」
English: “Her Type B qualities manifest very strongly. I wouldn’t say her sense of smell rivals a dog’s, but it is still extremely acute.”

Japanese: 「発症しているのか？」
English: “Has she developed symptoms?”

Japanese: 「いや、そうじゃない。ちょっと変わってるんだ……」
English: “No, nothing like that. She’s simply a little unusual...”

Japanese: 亮は立ち上がると、
English: Ryo rose.

Japanese: 「それより、これだけの傷を負ってるなら、近くに血が落ちているかもしれない。手分けして探そう。……見土、見つけたら倒す自信はあるか？　それとも、大事をとってここで引き返すか？」
English: “More importantly, if the creature was injured this badly, it may have left blood nearby. Let’s split up and search. ...Mido, are you confident you can defeat it if you find it? Or should we put safety first and withdraw here?”

Japanese: 「菅原」
English: “Sugawara.”

Japanese: 道夫は不本意そうに唇をとがらせ、黒い腕をを突き出すと、
English: Michio thrust out his black arm, his lips pursed in displeasure.

Japanese: 「おれを侮ってもらっちゃ困る。お前らこそ、別れて大丈夫か？　全員でおれに付いてきた方がいいんじゃないか？」
English: “Don’t underestimate me. Are your people sure they’ll be all right split up? Wouldn’t you be better off staying together and following me?”

Japanese: 「大丈夫、こっちも負けやしないさ」
English: “We’ll be fine. We have no intention of losing either.”

Japanese: 「ふん、じゃあどちらが先に見つけてやっつけるか、勝負だな」
English: “Hmph. Then we’ll make it a contest to see who finds and defeats the thing first.”

Japanese: そして亮のパラシュート通り組と、道夫の暗闇通り組に別れて近くを探した。彼らは手に棒きれやバット、それからナイフなどを持っていて、通りがかった人は顔を顰めてそそくさと離れようとしたが、少年たちは気にしない。どころか、こちらから声をかけて「この辺りで怪物を見つけなかった」などと訊ねたりもした。
English: They divided into Ryo’s Parachute Street group and Michio’s Darkness Street group, then searched the vicinity. The boys carried sticks, bats, knives, and similar weapons. Passersby frowned and hurried to put distance between them, but the boys paid no attention. Indeed, they approached people themselves and asked, ‘Have you seen a monster around here?’

Japanese: 武器を持ち、殺気だった不良少年のグループにこんな質問をされる通行人は気の毒という他ない。
English: One could only pity the pedestrians confronted with such a question by a band of armed and murderous-looking delinquents.

Japanese: しかし、怪物は見つからず、追跡の手がかりになりそうなものも見つからなかった。
English: They found neither the monster nor any clue that might allow them to pursue it.

Japanese: 「相手が怪我をしているうちになんとかしたかったんだがな。……空き地に戻ってみんなと合流しよう」
English: “I wanted to do something while it was still injured... Let’s return to the vacant lot and rejoin the others.”

Japanese: 亮はそう言って溜息をついた。そして自分の仲間をまとめて引き返そうとする。
English: Ryo sighed, gathered his companions, and began to turn back.

Japanese: 「お、おい」
English: “H-hey.”

Japanese: そこで納得がいかないのは道夫だった。
English: Michio was not satisfied.

Japanese: 「さっきからなんでお前が全部指示出してるんだよ？」
English: “Why have you been giving all the orders?”

Japanese: 「……何か他の提案があるのか？　それなら聞くけど」
English: “...Do you have another proposal? If so, I’ll listen.”

Japanese: 亮が冷たい視線を浴びせかけると、道夫は肩をすくめ、
English: Ryo fixed him with a cold stare. Michio hunched his shoulders.

Japanese: 「い、いや、そういうわけじゃないけどさ」
English: “N-no, I don’t mean that exactly.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ行くぞ。時間がもったいない」
English: “Then let’s go. We’re wasting time.”

Japanese: 亮が無愛想に歩き出すと、道夫は渋いお茶でも飲んでしまったような顔をする。
English: Ryo strode off brusquely. Michio made a face as though he had swallowed bitter tea.

Japanese: 「あいつ生意気だな。あとでシメちゃおうよ？」
English: “He’s got some nerve. Want to rough him up later?”

Japanese: 紺太が隣で耳打ちするも、道夫は複雑な表情をするだけで何も答えず、
English: Konta whispered in his ear. Michio merely wore a complicated expression and gave no answer.

Japanese: 「おれたちも戻るぞ！」
English: “We’re going back too!”

Japanese: 仲間にそう呼びかけた。
English: He called out to his companions.

Japanese: 空き地に戻ると、双子が携帯を取り出し、皆でそれを覗き込んでいる。
English: When they returned to the vacant lot, the twins had taken out a mobile telephone, and everyone was peering at it together.

Japanese: 「どうした？」
English: “What’s wrong?”

Japanese: 道夫の呼びかけで双子は顔を上げる。二人の顔は、さっき別れるときに見せた強気な表情が消えて、怯えが勝っていた。
English: At Michio’s call, the twins looked up. The bold expressions they had worn when they parted were gone, replaced by fear.

Japanese: 「団地の友達からメールが来てた……」
English: “We got a message from a friend in the housing complex...”

Japanese: 「私の部屋から、あの怪物が出て来たんだって……」
English: “That monster came out of our room...”

Japanese: 団地の友人が遊びに誘おうと部屋の近くまで来たとき、開いたドアから手足の長い毛むくじゃらの怪物が飛び出してくるのを目撃したらしい。友人は怯えて腰を抜かしてしまい、怪物は確かにその姿を見たはずだが、一瞥するだけで去っていったと言う。
English: Their friend had approached their room to invite them to play and apparently saw a long-limbed, shaggy monster emerge through the open door. The sight terrified their friend so badly that they collapsed where they stood. The monster must have seen them, but reportedly gave them only a glance before departing.

Japanese: 「あいつ、私たちの部屋も知ってるんだ」
English: “It knows our room too.”

Japanese: 「どうして……」
English: “But how...?”

Japanese: 「メールが来たのはいつだ？」
English: “When did the message arrive?”

Japanese: 亮が道夫の後からそう訊ねる。
English: Ryo asked from behind Michio.

Japanese: 「大分前だよ」
English: “A long time ago.”

Japanese: 「メールが届いたの、今気づいたばかりなの」
English: “We only just noticed it.”

Japanese: 双子は亮にその画面を見せる。
English: The twins showed Ryo the screen.

Japanese: メールの送信時間からすると、双子が怪物と遭遇するより大分前の、彼女たちが団地を出た直後の時刻のようだ。
English: According to the timestamp, the message had been sent well before the twins encountered the monster—apparently just after they left the housing complex.

Japanese: 「出るのが遅れていたら、自分の部屋で対面することになってたわけか」
English: “If you’d left any later, you would have met it inside your own room.”

Japanese: 道夫は腕組みをしてそう呟く。
English: Michio folded his arms as he murmured the thought.

Japanese: 「しかし、これはまずいことになったね」
English: “This is becoming serious.”

Japanese: 亮は眉間にしわを寄せて言う。
English: Ryo spoke with a furrowed brow.

Japanese: 「時系列的には、まずきみらの部屋を訪ね、それから街に移動してきみらを襲ったわけだ。騒ぎになっていないところを見ると、大通りを避け、人目につかないところを移動していたんだろう。団地からあの辺りまで移動するなら、もっと騒ぎになってそうなものだけど、さっきネットで確認したところ、全然そんな話題は出てなかった」
English: “Chronologically, it visited your room first, then moved into the city and attacked you. Since there hasn’t been an uproar, it must have avoided the main streets and traveled through places where no one would see it. Something that conspicuous ought to have caused more of a disturbance moving from the housing complex to that neighborhood, but I checked online a moment ago, and nobody is discussing anything of the kind.”

Japanese: 「変なルートで移動してるから、やつと出会うことになったんだな」
English: “So they ran into it because they travel by such strange routes.”

Japanese: 道夫は納得したように頷く。
English: Michio nodded, apparently satisfied.

Japanese: 「それはそうかもしれないけど、それよりもっと大事なことがある」
English: “That may be true, but something else is far more important.”

Japanese: 「なんだ？」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 「まずひとつは、この怪物は明らかにこの二人を狙ってるってことだよ。他の誰でもなく、この二人だけをね。そしてもう一つは、話で聞く限りかなり目立つ姿だそうだが、それを隠して行動する程度の知性はあるってことだ」
English: “First, the monster is clearly targeting these two girls and no one else. Second, judging by their description, it has an extremely conspicuous appearance, yet possesses enough intelligence to conceal itself while moving.”

Japanese: 亮の言葉に、双子はビクリと肩をふるわせる。
English: At Ryo’s words, the twins’ shoulders jerked.

Japanese: 「何か心当たりはあるか？」
English: “Can you think of any reason?”

Japanese: 道夫が訊ねると、双子は完全に動きを同調させて、首をよこにぶんぶんと振る。
English: At Michio’s question, the twins shook their heads vigorously, every movement perfectly synchronized.

Japanese: 「よく思い出せ。何かあるはずだ」
English: “Think carefully. There must be something.”

Japanese: 道夫はさらに訊ねるが、双子は唇をわなわなと震わせて否定する。
English: Michio pressed them further, but the twins denied it with trembling lips.

Japanese: 「わ、わからないよっ！」
English: “W-we don’t know!”

Japanese: 「あんなの、絶対に見たことないわっ！」
English: “We’ve definitely never seen anything like that!”

Japanese: 「まあ、別に知らなくてもおかしくないよ」
English: “It wouldn’t be strange if you didn’t know it.”

Japanese: 亮は考えながら言葉を口にする。
English: Ryo gave voice to his thoughts as he considered the matter.

Japanese: 「怪物はきっと発症したハイブリッドのなれの果てなんだろうけど、だとしたら、妄想に取り憑かれて一方的な理由でこの双子につきまとっているのかもしれない。……ただ、妄想にしても全く接触がないとは考えにくい。どこかでちょっと見かけたとか、何かで写真を見たとか、そういうきっかけはあるかもしれない。近くに住んでるとか……知人の知人だとか……」
English: “The monster is probably what remains of a hybrid after onset. If so, it may be possessed by a delusion and pursuing the twins for reasons entirely its own. ...Still, even a delusion is unlikely to arise without any contact whatsoever. Perhaps it once glimpsed them somewhere or saw a photograph. Some small event like that may have set it off. It could live nearby... or be an acquaintance of an acquaintance...”

Japanese: 「それでも、全然思い当たらないよ」
English: “We still can’t think of anything.”

Japanese: 「あんな姿だったらもっとみんな知ってるはずなのに、聞いたことないってことは、遠い人だよきっと」
English: “If someone looked like that, everybody would know about it. If you’ve never heard of the creature, it must come from far away.”

Japanese: 「そうか。……まあとにかく、住まいが知られているのならこのまま団地に帰るのは危険だな。しかし、荒らされた団地の様子も確認しておきたいところだ」
English: “I see. ...In any event, if it knows where you live, returning to the housing complex would be dangerous. But we should also inspect what it did to your room.”

Japanese: 亮が考え込むと、周囲は自然と黙って彼の答えを待つ格好になる。普段から彼をリーダーと認めるパラシュート通りの仲間たちはもとより、さっきまで文句を言っていた道夫をはじめとする暗闇通りの子供たちも自然と亮に注目している。
English: Ryo fell into thought. The people around him naturally became silent and waited for his answer. This was true not only of his Parachute Street companions, who ordinarily recognized him as their leader, but even of Michio and the other Darkness Street children who had complained only moments before. Everyone’s attention settled upon Ryo.

Japanese: 菅原亮という少年にはまわりをそうさせる雰囲気があった。
English: There was something about Ryo Sugawara that made people behave this way.

Japanese: 「よし、双子は滑走路通りで喫茶店かどこかに入って待っていてくれ。怪物は人通りをさけているということだから、人目が多いところの方が安全かもしれない。補償はないけどね。……松子はそっちに行って一緒にいてくれるかい？」
English: “All right. Twins, go to a cafe or somewhere else upon Runway Street and wait there. The monster appears to avoid crowds, so a place with plenty of people may be safer. There’s no guarantee, of course. ...Matsuko, will you go with them and stay nearby?”

Japanese: 松子は黙ったまま頷くと、双子のそばに移動する。
English: Matsuko nodded without a word and moved beside the twins.

Japanese: 「そして、団地には僕と見土の二人だけで行って、様子を見てくる。残りの連中は解散だ。もし何かしたいなら、ネットで街の噂を調べたりして、怪物の目撃情報をあさっていてくれ。そして何かあったら僕に報告するんだ。間違っても自分たちで探そうとしたらいけない」
English: “Mido and I will go to the housing complex alone and inspect it. The rest of you should disperse. If you want to help, search the internet for rumors around the city and look for reports of the monster. Report anything you find to me. Whatever you do, do not try to search for it yourselves.”

Japanese: 「双子と一緒に行くのはその松子って子だけでいいのかい？」
English: “Is that girl Matsuko really enough to send with the twins?”

Japanese: そう質問したのは紺太だった。
English: Konta was the one who asked.

Japanese: 「こんな大人数でゾロゾロ動いていたら目立つだろう？　松子だけで十分だ。そいつは、普通のタイプBよりもよほど動ける。同じ理由で、団地も僕と見土だけの方が動きやすいだろう。……正直、僕らにとっては団地の方が怪物より厄介な気がするけどね」
English: “A group this large would stand out wherever it went, wouldn’t it? Matsuko is enough. She’s far more capable than an ordinary Type B. For the same reason, Mido and I will move more easily through the housing complex on our own. ...Honestly, I have a feeling that the housing complex will be more trouble for us than the monster.”

Japanese: 亮はそう言って苦笑する。
English: Ryo gave a wry smile.

Japanese: 「さて、僕の考えはこういったものだけれど、何か意見はあるか？」
English: “That’s my proposal. Does anyone have another opinion?”

Japanese: 亮がまっすぐ目を見つめて質問するのに、道夫は首を横に振る。
English: Ryo looked Michio directly in the eyes as he asked. Michio shook his head.

Japanese: 「ないね」
English: “No.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ、先に団地の方に行っていてくれないか。僕はちょっと家で物をとって来たらすぐに向かう」
English: “Then will you go ahead to the housing complex? I need to collect something from home. I’ll follow immediately.”

Japanese: そうして彼の提案したとおり、松子と双子は滑走路通りの方へ向かい、道夫はヘドロ団地へ行くことになった。亮は一旦家に帰ると、すぐに道夫のあとを追いかけて団地の手前で合流する。
English: They proceeded as Ryo had proposed. Matsuko and the twins headed toward Runway Street, while Michio set out for the Sludge Housing Complex. Ryo returned home briefly, then followed and joined Michio just before the complex.

Japanese: 目の前に広がる巨大な団地の群れの、壁の高い方はひび割れ蔦が生い茂り、手の届く部分にはペンキで卑猥な言葉や、妙に手慣れたイラストなど、好き放題落書きがされている。
English: The enormous mass of apartment blocks spread before them. The upper walls were cracked and overgrown with ivy. Every reachable surface had been covered freely in painted graffiti: obscene words, strangely accomplished illustrations, and more.

Japanese: ここから先はY地区の市街とはまた違ったルールに支配されている場所であることを、この二人の少年はよく理解していた。
English: Both boys understood well that beyond this point, rules unlike those of the streets of Y District held sway.

Japanese: 「おい、敷地に入ったらおれのそばを離れるなよ」
English: “Once we enter the grounds, don’t leave my side.”

Japanese: いよいよ団地に踏み入れる段になって、道夫は真顔でそう呟いた。
English: As they prepared to step into the complex at last, Michio murmured this with an entirely serious expression.

Japanese: 「なぜ？」
English: “Why?”

Japanese: 「お前みたいな女だかわからないようなガキは、いい獲物だからな。おれがこの金の目と腕の力で守ってやる」
English: “A kid like you, who nobody can even tell is a boy or a girl, makes easy prey. I’ll protect you with these golden eyes and the power of my arm.”

Japanese: 「随分親切だな。だけど、その必要はないよ」
English: “How kind. But that won’t be necessary.”

Japanese: 亮は無表情に言って、上着の胸元に手を突っ込むと、黒い物をチラリと道夫に見せる。
English: Ryo answered without expression. He slipped a hand inside his jacket and gave Michio a glimpse of something black.

Japanese: 見間違うはずもない。それはオートマチックピストルであった。彼が家に帰って持って来ると言ったものは、これあったのである。
English: There could be no mistake. It was an automatic pistol. This was the object Ryo had returned home to collect.

Japanese: 「……暴力は嫌いだと言ってた割りには、随分好戦的じゃないか」
English: “For someone who claims to hate violence, you’re remarkably eager for a fight.”

Japanese: 「暴力は嫌いだよ。争いはくだらない。目一杯長生きしたって百年も生きないような寿命の短い生物同士が、さらにその寿命を削り合うんだから、そんなのジョークとしか言いようがないと思わないか？　だから僕は、そのくだらないことに使う労力を減らすために、争いの時はなるべく効率的に、手短に済ませる手段をいつも使うことにしてるのさ」
English: “I do hate violence. Conflict is pointless. Creatures so short-lived that even if they live as long as possible they cannot survive a hundred years spend their time cutting one another’s lives shorter still. How can anyone call that anything but a joke? That’s why, whenever conflict arises, I use the most efficient method I can to end it quickly. It reduces the effort I waste upon something so pointless.”

Japanese: 「いい性格してやがる。だが、おれは全く正反対の考え方だな。どうせ短いんだから、長くしようなんてセコいことは考えず、情熱全部をこの瞬間にかけるぜっ」
English: “You’ve got a rotten way of thinking. Mine is the exact opposite. Life’s short anyway, so I won’t waste it on some pathetic attempt to stretch it out. I’ll stake every scrap of passion I have upon this moment!”

Japanese: 「そうか。でもお前の考え方は僕にとってはどうでもいい」
English: “I see. But what you think means nothing to me.”

Japanese: 平然と言う亮に、道夫はさすがに苦い表情をしつつ、
English: Ryo delivered the words with perfect calm. Even Michio could only make a bitter face before continuing.

Japanese: 「しかし、そんなに暴力がいやなら、おれと決闘するときはどうするつもりだったんだ？　ないか手短に済ませるインチキを考えていたのか？」
English: “If you hate violence so much, what were you planning to do in our duel? Had you devised some cheating way to end it quickly?”

Japanese: 「話してもいいけれど、それを聞くんなら決闘はしないよ」
English: “I can tell you, but if you hear the answer, there won’t be a duel.”

Japanese: 「言えよ。もうそんな気分じゃない。こんなやつ相手に男の真剣勝負なんか出来るか」
English: “Tell me. I’m not in the mood anymore. How am I supposed to have a serious contest between men with somebody like you?”

Japanese: 「適当に怪我をしないように殴られて、適当に負けるつもりだったよ。少し考えればわかるだろ？　僕には勝ちに行く理由がない。それとも本当に僕がお前の裸が見たいとでも思ったかい？」
English: “I planned to let you hit me without allowing you to cause any real injury, then lose when the time seemed right. You could work that out with a moment’s thought. I have no reason to try to win. Or did you genuinely think I wanted to see you naked?”

Japanese: 「……いやなやつだ」
English: “...You’re a bastard.”

Japanese: 道夫は舌打ちをして、亮はおかしそうに笑う。
English: Michio clicked his tongue. Ryo laughed with amusement.

Japanese: そして二人は団地に足を踏み入れた。
English: Then the two boys stepped into the housing complex.

Japanese: 双子の部屋がどこにあるかは聞いてある。そこに向かって歩く途中、何人かの住民とすれ違った。
English: They had been told where the twins lived. On the way there, they passed several residents.

Japanese: 明らかに薬物依存症としか思えない濃いくまを目の下に作った二人の男女。ボディビルダーのように黒光りする逞しい体躯をして、松葉杖を突く義足の男。玩具をもって走り回る子供たち。
English: There were a man and woman with such dark rings beneath their eyes that they looked unmistakably like drug addicts; a man on crutches with a prosthetic leg and a powerful, darkly gleaming physique like a bodybuilder’s; and children running about with toys.

Japanese: ジロジロと露骨に視線を送ってくるものもいれば、目の前に存在しないかのようにチラとも見ずに通り過ぎて行くものもいる。
English: Some stared at the boys openly. Others passed without so much as a glance, as though the visitors did not exist.

Japanese: 「聞いているほど大した場所じゃないな。これなら暗闇通りのほうがよっぽどヤバイぜ」
English: “This place isn’t nearly as bad as people say. Darkness Street is much more dangerous.”

Japanese: 道夫はそう強がったが、団地のあちこちからこちらを観察する視線を感じていた。
English: Michio spoke boldly, yet felt eyes observing them from all around the complex.

Japanese: 亮もそれを察していて何も言わない。ただいつ何が起きてもいいように、上に来ているパーカーのファスナーは降ろし、懐の銃はいつでも取り出せるようにしていた。その格好を見ればすぐに彼が銃を持っていることを悟られてしまうだろうが、それは本人も理解していた。
English: Ryo had noticed them too and said nothing. He kept his hoodie unzipped and the pistol inside ready to draw should anything happen. Anyone who saw the way he held himself would immediately realize he had a gun, but Ryo understood that as well.

Japanese: さて、口の中がカラカラに乾くほど緊張しながらも、二人は目的の建物に足を踏み入れ、ひんやりとする階段をのぼり、どうにか目的の部屋の前に辿り着いた。
English: Despite tension that left their mouths completely dry, the boys entered the building they sought, climbed its cool stairwell, and somehow reached the room.

Japanese: 聞いたとおりドアは破壊され外れており、真っ二つにされたそれが入り口の脇の壁に立てかけられている。
English: As they had been told, the door had been broken off. Split cleanly in two, it now leaned against the wall beside the entrance.

Japanese: 怪物のすさまじい腕力を感じさせるその痕跡の前に二人は無言のまま佇んでしまい、
English: The evidence of the monster’s tremendous strength left both boys standing speechless.

Japanese: 「入ろう」
English: “Let’s go inside.”

Japanese: と、見土が声をかけるまで彫像のようにかたまっていた。
English: Until Michio spoke, they had remained frozen like statues.

Japanese: 部屋のなかはまるで暴風が通り過ぎたようだった。玄関を入ると、まず天井から垂れ下がった少女の部屋らしいピンク色ののれんが切り裂かれたのが目に入り、そして、ドアというドアが全部開け放たれていずれも痛々しい爪痕で傷ついている。
English: The room looked as though a storm had passed through it. Immediately beyond the entrance, the pink curtain characteristic of a young girl’s room hung from the ceiling in tatters. Every door stood open, and cruel-looking claw marks scarred each one.

Japanese: 靴を脱ごうとする道夫の隣で亮は土足のまま無言で部屋にあがると、一番手前の部屋に顔を突っ込む。道夫も慌てて靴のまま上がり、同じように部屋を見た。そこは少女たちの寝室で、クローゼットのドアが開かれている。
English: Michio began to remove his shoes. Beside him, Ryo stepped wordlessly into the apartment without removing his own and peered into the nearest room. Michio hurriedly followed with his shoes still on and looked inside. It was the girls’ bedroom, and the closet door stood open.

Japanese: それを見て亮は眉間にしわをよせ、すぐに次の部屋を確認しに向かう。
English: Ryo frowned at the sight, then immediately went to inspect the next room.

Japanese: 道夫はそのあとを追いながら、重大な事実に気がついていた。
English: Following him, Michio became aware of a serious problem.

Japanese: （な、何を見ればいいんだ？）
English: What am I supposed to be looking for?

Japanese: 亮が言うまま危険をおかしてこの団地にやって来ていまさら驚くべき話だが、何を確認するためにここ来たのか全くわからなかったのである。
English: It was an astonishing realization to make only after following Ryo into this dangerous complex, but Michio had no idea what they had come to confirm.

Japanese: 確かに部屋には怪物がやって来て、散らかした痕跡があった。しかし、これがなんなのか。何を見ればあの双子をおびやかした怪物に対処するヒントが得られるのか。どうも彼にはピンと来ないのだが、亮は何か確信を持って部屋を見ている。ここで彼に聞けばいいのだが、さすがにそれはプライドが邪魔して聞けない。ここへ来て何をすればいいかなんて言ったらひどい恥なのである。
English: The monster had clearly entered the room and left signs of disorder. But what did that tell them? What could Michio look for that might help them deal with the creature threatening the twins? Nothing came to mind. Ryo, meanwhile, inspected the apartment with evident purpose. Michio could simply ask him, but his pride would not allow it. After coming all this way, admitting that he did not know what to do would be unbearably humiliating.

Japanese: 道夫が居心地悪いまま、二人でひとつひとつの部屋を確認し、一番奥のリビングに足を踏み入れた時だ。
English: Still uncomfortable, Michio helped inspect each room in turn. Then they entered the living room at the very back.

Japanese: 「ここもか……」
English: “Here too...”

Japanese: 亮は理解したようにそう呟くのだけれど、道夫には何がここもなのかわからない。
English: Ryo murmured as though he understood something, but Michio had no idea what ‘here too’ meant.

Japanese: 「あのさ菅原、おれたちはここで何をしたら……」
English: “Listen, Sugawara. What are we supposed to do here...?”

Japanese: 恥を忍んでついにそう声をかけたとき、亮はふと何かに気がついて、キッチンの方に歩いて行った。
English: Michio finally swallowed his shame and began to ask. Then Ryo noticed something and walked toward the kitchen.

Japanese: それを見て道夫も気がつく。
English: At the sight, Michio noticed it as well.

Japanese: キッチンも棚が開け放たれ、割れた食器が散乱した床の上に鼠の死体が落ちている。鼠は首の辺りに大きな傷が付き、そこから夥しい血液が流れ出しているのだが、普通ではあり得ない減少がそこに起きていた。
English: The kitchen cupboards also stood open, and broken dishes littered the floor. Amid them lay the corpse of a mouse. A large wound marked its neck, from which an enormous quantity of blood had flowed. Yet something impossible under ordinary circumstances had happened there.

Japanese: 血液の水たまりというものは通常楕円に似た形になるはずなのだが、その血液はどういうわけか、直線や矩形を組み合わせた複雑な形をしているのである。
English: A pool of blood would ordinarily form something like an oval. For some reason, however, this blood had taken a complex shape composed of straight lines and rectangles.
“A map...?”

Japanese: 道夫が思わず口にした通り、それは道路や建物を真上から見下ろしたようなかたちに見えた。
English: Just as Michio had blurted out, it resembled roads and buildings viewed from directly above.

Japanese: 「これもしかして、ここが滑走路通りでさ……」
English: “Could this be Runway Street here...?”

Japanese: 言いながらふと見た亮の顔が、さきほどまでとはうって変わって青ざめている。
English: As Michio spoke, he glanced at Ryo. The boy’s face, so calm until moments before, had turned pale.

Japanese: そして急いで携帯電話を取り出すと、どこかへ電話をかけた。
English: Ryo hurriedly took out his mobile telephone and called someone.

Japanese: 「怪物の狙いはほかの誰でもなく双子だ。すぐ二人を連れてそこを出てくれ。あいつは追跡能力を持っているから、出来るだけ移動し続けるんだ。僕もある程度そっちへ向かったらもう一度連絡するから、あとで合流しよう」
English: “The monster is after the twins and no one else. Take them and leave that place immediately. It has some kind of tracking ability, so keep moving as much as possible. I’ll call again once we’re closer, and then we’ll meet.”

Japanese: 亮は早口でそれだけ言うと、電話を切った。
English: Ryo delivered the instructions rapidly, then ended the call.

Japanese: 「見土、すぐに団地を出てあいつらと合流しよう。松子がいるから大丈夫だと思うけど、油断は出来ない」
English: “Mido, we need to leave the complex immediately and join them. Matsuko is there, so they should be safe, but we can’t let down our guard.”

Japanese: そして部屋を飛びだそうとした亮の服を、道夫は掴んだ。
English: Ryo began to rush from the room. Michio caught hold of his clothes.

Japanese: 「すまないが、わからないんだ。どういうことか説明してくれよ」
English: “Sorry, but I don’t understand. Explain what this means.”

Japanese: 「この部屋はあらゆるドアが開かれているが、人が隠れられそうなところばかりで部屋を物色した様子はない。つまり怪物は何か双子の持っているモノが欲しいんじゃなくて、双子自身に用があるんだ。そしてあの地図は怪物のサイキック能力だろう。あの裏路地で遭遇したのは偶然だと思っていたんだけれど、そうじゃなくてこれは……」
English: “Every door in this apartment has been opened, but it inspected only places where a person might hide. Nothing suggests it rummaged through anything. In other words, the monster doesn’t want some object the twins possess; it wants the twins themselves. And that map is probably the monster’s psychic ability. I thought their encounter in that back street was a coincidence, but it wasn’t. This is...”

Japanese: 彼がそこまで説明したところで口をつぐんだ。入り口の方で、物音がしたのである。
English: Ryo stopped speaking there. A noise had come from the entrance.

Japanese: あの怪物がここへ戻って来たのかと道夫は身を固くしたが、そうではなかった。
English: Michio stiffened, imagining that the monster had returned. It had not.

Japanese: 「うわー、こりゃひでえなあ」
English: “Whoa. This is awful.”

Japanese: 入り口の方から聞こえて来たのは、男の声である。
English: A man’s voice came from the entrance.

Japanese: 向こうは複数いて、入り口のそばで何か言葉を交わしている。はっきり言葉が聞き取れたわけではないが、切れ切れに聞こえる声のトーンや言葉の断片からすると、ボスが一人いて、比較的若い二人が何か報告しているようだった。
English: There were several people outside, exchanging words near the doorway. The boys could not hear them clearly. But from fragments of speech and the tones of the voices, it sounded as though one person was the leader and two relatively young companions were reporting to him.

Japanese: 「おれたちがここにいるって、知って来たのかな？」
English: “Do you think they knew we were here and came for us?”

Japanese: 道夫が小声で訊ねるが、亮は入り口の方を見たまま何か考えている。
English: Michio whispered the question. Ryo kept his gaze upon the entrance, thinking.

Japanese: （これはどうしたもんか）
English: What do we do now?

Japanese: 道夫は内心で焦るが答えが出ない。
English: Michio grew increasingly anxious but found no answer.

Japanese: やがてドアの外の連中は部屋のなかに足を踏み入れ、そしてリビングに立って様子をうかがっていた二人と対面するのであった。
English: At last, the people outside stepped into the apartment. They came face to face with the two boys watching from the living room.

Japanese: 「おい、なんだおまえたち」
English: “Hey. Who are you?”

Japanese: 入って来たのは三人組の男で、そのうち最も年長に見える小太りの男が言った。
English: Three men had entered. The speaker was a somewhat plump man who looked the oldest of them.

Japanese: 「お、おれたちは怪しいものじゃない」
English: “W-we’re not suspicious.”

Japanese: そう答えたのは道夫だった。
English: Michio was the one who answered.

Japanese: 「泥棒とかそういうのじゃない。おまえらこそ双子と何か関係あるのか？」
English: “We’re not thieves or anything like that. Are you connected to the twins?”

Japanese: 「おれは灰上姉妹の後見人の深沢だ。ドアが壊れていると話を聞いて慌ててここにやってきたんだが、どうなってるんだ？　そこに二人はいるのか？」
English: “I’m Fukazawa, guardian of the Haigami sisters. I heard the door had been broken and rushed here. What’s going on? Are the two girls inside?”

Japanese: 「ここにはいないが……」
English: “They’re not here, but...”

Japanese: 道夫は言いかけて、迷った。ここでなんと言うべきなのだろう？
English: Michio began to answer, then hesitated. What should he say?

Japanese: 相手は後見人と名乗っている。ということは、正直に話して協力を要請すべきなのか？　それとも、警戒が必要な相手なのか。
English: The man claimed to be their guardian. Did that mean they ought to tell him the truth and request his cooperation? Or was he someone they needed to treat with caution?

Japanese: 迷った挙げ句、亮を見た。
English: After a moment of indecision, Michio looked at Ryo.

Japanese: この状況で男たちと言葉で渡り合うのに自信がない。自分よりもきっと亮の方がうまくやるだろうと思ってのことである。
English: He was not confident that he could hold his own verbally against the men under these circumstances. Ryo would surely handle them better.

Japanese: その空気を察して亮は口を開く。
English: Understanding the silent request, Ryo opened his mouth.

Japanese: 「ぼ、僕たちは、本当に何にも知らないんですっ！」
English: “W-we really don’t know anything!”

Japanese: 亮は思ったよりも狼狽しており、声がうわずっていたので道夫の方が驚いてしまった。
English: Ryo appeared more flustered than Michio had expected, and his voice had risen sharply. Even Michio was surprised.

Japanese: これは、彼に任せないで自分が喋った方が良かったのかもしれない。
English: Perhaps he ought to have spoken for himself instead of leaving matters to Ryo.

Japanese: 「ただ、あの二人がサイキックに追われて逃げているって言うから、家の方を確認しに来ただけで……」
English: “We only came to inspect their home because they said they were running from a psychic...”

Japanese: 「サイキックに追われている？　あいつらがか？」
English: “A psychic is chasing them? Those two?”

Japanese: 深沢は目を丸くする。
English: Fukazawa’s eyes widened.

Japanese: 「そうなんです。クモみたいな怪物が相手だって……。地図を使って自分を追跡してくるから、かわりに見てくれって……」
English: “That’s right. They said it was some monster like a spider... They asked us to check their room because it was tracking them with a map...”

Japanese: 「本当か、確かにそういったのか？　地図を使うと？」
English: “Is that true? Did they definitely say it used a map?”

Japanese: 深沢は怪訝な顔をして繰り返す。すると、亮はすっと目を細め、
English: Fukazawa repeated the question with a puzzled expression. Ryo’s eyes suddenly narrowed.

Japanese: 「『確かにそういったのか』……と言ったね」
English: “You asked whether they ‘definitely said it.’”

Japanese: さっきまでの怯えた態度とは全く違う、冷たい表情で深沢を見つめた。
English: His cold expression bore no resemblance to the frightened face of moments before.

Japanese: 「双子が地図のことを知ってるのがおかしいような口ぶりだ。つまり、あんたは何か『知ってる』ってわけだ」
English: “You spoke as though it would be strange for the twins to know about the map. In other words, you know something.”

Japanese: 道夫は、この場面では男たちに全てを話して協力を頼むか、しらばっくれて通り過ぎるかしかないと思っていた。
English: Michio had believed they possessed only two choices: tell the men everything and request their help, or pretend ignorance and get past them.

Japanese: しかし、亮が選んだのは全く別の方法だった。
English: Ryo chose an entirely different method.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、洗いざらい喋って貰おうか」
English: “So you’re going to tell us everything you know.”

Japanese: 亮は懐から取り出した銃を、深沢に向かって構えた。
English: Ryo drew the gun from inside his jacket and leveled it at Fukazawa.

Japanese: 「おい！」
English: “Hey!”

Japanese: 「何をするんだ！」
English: “What do you think you’re doing?”

Japanese: 深沢の左右にいるラフな格好をした若い男たちがそう叫ぶ。
English: The young men in rough clothing on either side of Fukazawa shouted.

Japanese: 「黙ってて。今はごちゃごちゃ話している時間がないんだ」
English: “Be quiet. We don’t have time for everyone to talk at once.”

Japanese: 亮は冷たく言い放つ。
English: Ryo delivered the command coldly.

Japanese: 「おいおい、どういうつもりだ」
English: “Now, now. What exactly are you planning?”

Japanese: 深沢は驚きつつも、さすがヘドロ団地の大物だけあって口辺に笑みを浮かべたままそう答える。
English: Fukazawa was surprised. Yet he was an important figure in the Sludge Housing Complex and answered with the smile still upon his lips.

Japanese: 「クモの怪物は、こうしている間にも双子を追いかけているかもしれない。僕は彼女たちを守りたい。だから知っていることを全て話してくれ」
English: “The spider monster may be pursuing the twins even as we speak. I want to protect them. So tell me everything you know.”

Japanese: 「おい、どういうつもりだ」
English: “Hey. What exactly are you planning?”

Japanese: と訊ねたのは道夫だった。まさか亮がこんな暴挙に出るとは思ってもみなかったのである。
English: Michio was the one who asked this time. He had never imagined that Ryo would resort to anything so outrageous.

Japanese: 「何も知らなそうなら適当に誤魔化して通り過ぎるつもりだった。でも、知ってそうだから話を聞いてから向かおう」
English: “If they appeared to know nothing, I planned to bluff our way past. But they clearly know something, so we’ll hear it before we leave.”

Japanese: 「そうじゃなくて、その銃は……？」
English: “That’s not what I mean. What about the gun...?”

Japanese: 「ただの時間の短縮だ」
English: “It saves time.”

Japanese: 亮は短く答え、そして拳銃の撃鉄を親指でカチリと起こす。
English: Ryo answered briefly, then pulled back the pistol’s hammer with his thumb. It clicked into place.

Japanese: まったく道夫は呆れる他ない応えだが、こうなった以上は呆れてばかりもいられない。服の腕まくりをして黒い手を剥き出しにし、目をギラッと金色に輝かせて臨戦態勢を整える。
English: Michio was dumbfounded. But now that matters had gone this far, disbelief alone would not help. He rolled up his sleeve to expose his black hand, and his eyes flashed gold as he prepared to fight.

Japanese: 「深沢さん、さっさと喋りなよ。脅されてるからって恥じることはないよ。いまここで起きたことは誰にも喋らないと約束するから」
English: “Mr. Fukazawa, hurry up and talk. There’s no shame in yielding to a threat. I promise I won’t tell anyone what happened here.”

Japanese: 「そんなことをしなくたって、知りたけりゃ話してやるさ。おれだって姉妹に危険があったら困るんだからな。さあ、そんな物騒なものはしまえよ。この泣く子も黙るヘドロ団地のど真ん中で銃を振り回すお前さんの勇気に免じて、今すぐ謝ればなかったことにしてやる」
English: “You don’t need to do any of this. If you want to know, I’ll tell you. I’d be in trouble myself if the sisters were in danger. Now put away that nasty thing. We’re standing in the very heart of the infamous Sludge Housing Complex—the name alone could silence a crying child. In honor of your courage in waving a gun around here, apologize now and I’ll pretend this never happened.”

Japanese: 「謝るつもりはないし、銃を下げるつもりもない。人間は誰しも銃口の前では正直になるもんだからね」
English: “I don’t intend to apologize or lower the gun. Everyone becomes honest before the muzzle of a pistol.”

Japanese: 亮が挑発的に言うと、それまで余裕見せていた深沢の顔にはじめて鋭いものがあらわれる。
English: Ryo spoke provocatively. For the first time, Fukazawa’s composure gave way to a hard edge.

Japanese: 「おいガキ。優しくしている間に言うことを聞いたほうが身のためだぞ？」
English: “Listen, brat. For your own good, you’d better do as I say while I’m still being kind.”

Japanese: ドスをきかせたその声に、しかし亮は怯まない。
English: The menace in Fukazawa’s low voice failed to intimidate Ryo.

Japanese: 「文句があるならあとで言ってくれ。僕はパラシュート通りの菅原亮だ。逃げも隠れもしない。あらゆる情報に詳しいヘドロ団地の深沢さんならそれだけでわかるだろう？」
English: “Save your complaints for later. I’m Ryo Sugawara of Parachute Street. I’m not going to run or hide. For a man as well informed as Mr. Fukazawa of the Sludge Housing Complex, that name should be enough.”

Japanese: その言葉で深沢は顔色を変えた。
English: At those words, Fukazawa’s complexion changed.

Japanese: しかし道夫はその表情の変化には気づかず、
English: Michio failed to notice the reaction.

Japanese: （こんなところで名乗る馬鹿がいるか！）
English: What kind of idiot gives his name in a place like this?

Japanese: と、内心で冷や汗をかくのであった。
English: Michio broke into a cold sweat.

Japanese: 「私たちはヘドロ団地の灰上姉妹なのよ？」
English: “We’re the Haigami sisters of the Sludge Housing Complex.”

Japanese: 「こんなところでコソコソ隠れているなんてみっともない」
English: “It’s shameful to hide away in a place like this.”

Japanese: 亮たちの場面より数分前。場所は変わって滑走路通りの喫茶店の一席である。
English: This was several minutes earlier, at a table inside a cafe on Runway Street.

Japanese: 先ほどまで怯えていたはずの灰上姉妹はほっぺを膨らませて不満を口にしている。
English: The Haigami sisters, who ought to have been frightened only moments before, now puffed out their cheeks and complained.

Japanese: 「退避してるんだから、名前は言わないほうがいいと思う」
English: “We’re in hiding. I don’t think you should give your names.”

Japanese: 松子は表情のないすまし顔でそう言った。
English: Matsuko spoke with her usual composed, expressionless face.

Japanese: 「いいんだよ別に」
English: “It doesn’t matter.”

Japanese: 「見土道夫と菅原亮に好き勝手やらせるんじゃなかった！」
English: “We never should have let Michio Mido and Ryo Sugawara do whatever they wanted!”

Japanese: 「本当に情けない」
English: “It’s pathetic.”

Japanese: 「情けないわ」
English: “Completely pathetic.”

Japanese: 双子は交互に溜息をつく。
English: The twins sighed in alternation.

Japanese: 「真ん中に鏡があるみたいでおもしろいね」
English: “It’s funny. You look like there’s a mirror between you.”

Japanese: 松子はそう言ってから、自分の前に置かれたオレンジジュースをストローで飲んだ。
English: After making the observation, Matsuko drank the orange juice before her through its straw.

Japanese: その態度に双子は苛立ちを露わにして、
English: The twins displayed their irritation at her attitude.

Japanese: 「面白いなら楽しそうな顔しな？」
English: “If you think it’s funny, make a face like you’re having fun.”

Japanese: 「お面みたいな顔とにらめっこしてると、気が滅入っちゃう」
English: “Staring at a face like a mask is depressing.”

Japanese: 「面白いってどういう顔？」
English: “What does a face that’s having fun look like?”

Japanese: 松子は首をかしげる、
English: Matsuko tilted her head.

Japanese: 「こう！」
English: “Like this!”

Japanese: 「こうよ！」
English: “Like this.”

Japanese: 双子は二人そろって自分の頬の肉を両手で持ち上げるようにしながら、わざとらしい笑顔を作って見せた。
English: Both twins used their hands to push up their cheeks, showing Matsuko exaggerated smiles.

Japanese: 「こう？」
English: “Like this?”

Japanese: 言われて微笑んでみる松子を見て、双子は溜息をつく。
English: At their instruction, Matsuko attempted a smile. The twins sighed at the sight.

Japanese: 「なんだか気持ち悪い」
English: “That’s kind of creepy.”

Japanese: 「もうやめなよ」
English: “You should stop.”
“I see...”

Japanese: 松子は少し残念そうに顔を戻す。
English: Looking a little disappointed, Matsuko allowed her face to settle again.

Japanese: 「大体、あんたが残ってなんの意味があるわけ？」
English: “What good is having you stay with us, anyway?”

Japanese: 双子の一人がそう訊ねる。
English: One of the twins asked the question.

Japanese: 「何かあったら守るようリョウから言われた」
English: “Ryo told me to protect you if anything happened.”

Japanese: 「目がキンキラしてるけど、そんなに凄いタイプＢなの？」
English: “Your eyes are sparkling gold. Are you really such an impressive Type B?”

Japanese: もう一人がさらに訊ねる。
English: The other twin asked another question.

Japanese: 「私は動きが速くて、力が強くて、怪我がすぐ治る」
English: “I move quickly, I’m strong, and my injuries heal quickly.”

Japanese: 「たいした自信だね」
English: “You’re pretty confident.”

Japanese: 「じゃあ、ちょっと私と腕相撲をしようよ」
English: “Then arm wrestle me.”

Japanese: そして双子の片方が腕まくりをして、その白くて細い肘を乗せた。
English: One twin rolled up her sleeve and placed her slender white elbow upon the table.

Japanese: 「さあ、汐松子も手を出して」
English: “Come on, Matsuko Shio. Give me your hand.”

Japanese: そう挑発したその目は金色に色が変わる。それによって初めて、全く違いのない双子に違いが生まれた。
English: As she issued the challenge, the twin’s eyes turned gold. For the first time, a difference appeared between the otherwise identical sisters.

Japanese: 松子はオレンジジュースのグラスを脇によせ、同じように腕を乗せると相手の手を握る。すると、もう一人の双子がその握り合わさった手の上に自分の手のひらを乗せ、
English: Matsuko moved her glass of orange juice aside, placed her own elbow upon the table, and clasped the other girl’s hand. The remaining twin placed her palm over their joined hands.

Japanese: 「手を離したらスタートよ」
English: “We start when I let go.”

Japanese: と宣言し、二人が頷いたのを確認してから手を離す。
English: After making the declaration and confirming that both girls had nodded, the twin let go.

Japanese: その直後だった。天然木の分厚いテーブルが、ばんっ、と大きな音がして店内の人々の視線を集めてしまう。
English: The very next instant, the thick, solid-wood table gave a tremendous bang, drawing every eye in the cafe.

Japanese: 電光石火の早業で、松子が相手の手の甲をテーブルに叩きつけたのだった。
English: With lightning speed, Matsuko had slammed the back of her opponent’s hand against the table.

Japanese: 一瞬のことで、双子は凍り付いたまま動けない。
English: It happened so quickly that the twins remained frozen where they were.

Japanese: 「あ、ごめん」
English: “Oh. Sorry.”

Japanese: と松子が軽く言って手を離すと、
English: Matsuko spoke lightly and released her hand.

Japanese: 「いったあああああああい！」
English: “Owwwwww!”

Japanese: 双子の片方は真っ赤に晴れ上がった腕を押さえて飛び上がる。
English: One twin leaped up, clutching her reddened and rapidly swelling arm.

Japanese: 「あ、あんた、ゴリラ並の腕力なんだね……」
English: “Y-you have the strength of a gorilla...”

Japanese: 双子のもう片方は冷や汗をにじませながらそう言った。
English: The other twin spoke, beads of cold sweat gathering on her brow.

Japanese: 「いたあああい！　いたああああああいよう！」
English: “It hurts! It hurts so much!”

Japanese: 双子の片方な泣きじゃくりながらソファーの上を転げ回っている。もう片方はそれをなだめつつ、
English: One twin rolled back and forth upon the sofa, sobbing. The other tried to soothe her.

Japanese: 「ああもう、なんでこんなことに。こんな時にお兄ちゃんがいれば……」
English: “How did this happen? If only our brother were here at a time like this...”

Japanese: と嘆きの溜息をついた。
English: She gave a despairing sigh.

Japanese: 「お兄さんはそんなにすごいひとなの？」
English: “Is your brother really so impressive?”

Japanese: 松子が何気なく訊ねると、双子は鼻息あらく胸を張って、
English: Matsuko asked casually. The twins puffed out their chests and snorted.

Japanese: 「すごいんだよ！　国で特別な仕事をしているだから！」
English: “He’s amazing! He has a special job for the government!”

Japanese: 先ほどまで痛がってたのが嘘のように双子の片方が目を輝かせて言う。
English: One twin spoke with shining eyes, as though she had never been in pain at all.

Japanese: 「そうなんだ。どんな人？」
English: “I see. What kind of person is he?”

Japanese: 「背が高くて、きれいな黒髪で、眼鏡をかけてて……」
English: “He’s tall, with beautiful black hair, and he wears glasses...”

Japanese: 双子の片方がうっとりとした口調で語り出すと、
English: One twin began describing him dreamily.

Japanese: 「違うって言ってるでしょ？　ちょっと天然パーマで、色白で、眼鏡なんかしてないわ」
English: “I told you that’s wrong. His hair is a little naturally curly, his skin is pale, and he doesn’t wear glasses.”

Japanese: もう片方が否定する。
English: The other twin contradicted her.

Japanese: 「どういうこと？」
English: “What do you mean?”

Japanese: 話の食い違いに、松子は驚き目を丸くする。
English: Surprised by the inconsistency, Matsuko’s eyes widened.

Japanese: すると二人はばつが悪そうに俯き、
English: The twins lowered their heads awkwardly.

Japanese: 「……私たち、見たことないの」
English: “...We’ve never seen him.”

Japanese: 「……ちっちゃいときから、お兄ちゃんはずっと別のところで暮らしてたから……」
English: “...Our brother has always lived somewhere else, ever since we were little...”

Japanese: 「で、でも、遠くにいてもいつも私たちのこと大事にしてくれてるんだからっ！」
English: “B-but even far away, he’s always treasured us!”

Japanese: 「心が繋がってるんだからねっ！」
English: “Our hearts are connected!”

Japanese: 双子は大きな声で力説する。するとまた店内の客がこちらをふりかえる。
English: The twins made their case in loud voices. Once again, the other customers turned to look.

Japanese: 「そ、そうなんだ」
English: “I-I see.”

Japanese: 松子が面食らいながらそう答えると、すぐに店員がやって来て静かにするよう注意される。
English: Matsuko answered, taken aback. An employee immediately approached and warned them to be quiet.

Japanese: そして誰も一言も喋らなくなったところで、テーブルの上に置いてあった松子の電話が鳴ったのであった。
English: Once everyone had fallen completely silent, the telephone Matsuko had left on the table began to ring.

Japanese: それは亮からの危険を伝えるものだった。
English: It was Ryo, calling to warn them of danger.

Japanese: 電話を切ると、感情の薄い松子の表情にもわずかに緊張の色が浮かぶ。
English: When Matsuko ended the call, a trace of tension appeared even on her usually unreadable face.

Japanese: 「どうしたの？」
English: “What’s wrong?”

Japanese: 「リョウから。危険だからここをすぐ離れろって」
English: “It was Ryo. He says we’re in danger and have to leave immediately.”

Japanese: 「えっどういうこと？」
English: “What does that mean?”

Japanese: 「危険って」
English: “What danger?”

Japanese: 「わからないけど、あの怪物がおまえたちを追いかけているのは間違いないって。そして、これからやって来るかもしれないって」
English: “I don’t know, but he says there’s no doubt the monster is following you. And it may be coming here now.”

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: 「やっぱり？」
English: “We knew it...”

Japanese: 露骨に青ざめる双子の目の前で、松子は伝票を手に取り立ち上がる。
English: The twins visibly went pale. Matsuko picked up the bill in front of them and rose.

Japanese: そして、レジで会計を行っているときだった。
English: It happened while she was paying at the register.

Japanese: 表の滑走路通りでいくつかの悲鳴が聞こえた次の瞬間、背後でバシャンと大きな音がした。
English: Several screams came from Runway Street outside. A moment later, a tremendous crash sounded behind Matsuko.

Japanese: 振り返ると、喫茶店の大きなガラスを突き破って、茶色く長細い足をもった何かが店内に突入したところだった。
English: She turned. Something on long, spindly brown legs had smashed through the cafe’s great window and burst inside.

Japanese: 「あいつだ……」
English: “It’s the monster...”

Japanese: 「あれ、さっきのやつだよ……」
English: “That’s the one from before...”

Japanese: 双子が松子の袖を引き、彼女は小さく頷く。
English: The twins tugged at Matsuko’s sleeve. She gave a small nod.

Japanese: その怪物は先ほど双子がつけた傷によって頭が赤く血に塗れている。その下の大きな金色の複眼を動かして、店内をゆっくりと見回す。客や店員はあるいは悲鳴を上げ、あるいは恐怖で動けない。
English: Blood from the wound the twins had inflicted earlier covered the monster’s head. Beneath it, the enormous golden compound eye moved slowly across the cafe. Some customers and employees screamed; others were paralyzed with fear.

Japanese: （どうするか。このままじゃ他の客も危険かもしれない）
English: What should I do? The other customers may be in danger if this continues.

Japanese: 松子はレジの前に財布ごと置いてから、怪物の様子を観察した。
English: Matsuko left her wallet upon the counter and observed the monster.

Japanese: 怪物はテーブルの上を身軽に飛び跳ねながら何かを探している。亮の言葉が確かなら双子を探しているのだろうか。そして、怪物と視線があった赤ん坊が声をあげて泣く。
English: It bounded nimbly across the tables, searching for something. If Ryo was right, could it be looking for the twins? A baby whose eyes met the creature’s began to cry.

Japanese: 彼女が指示を受けているのは双子を守るということだけだ。そして、出会ってから僅かの間であるが、彼女自身もこの生意気だが愛嬌のある双子に好意を持っていた。亮と出歩くようになってから色々な人と出会ったが、この双子のような子供を見たことがない。松子の気持ちとしても、この双子を誰にも傷つけさせたくはなかった。
English: Matsuko had been instructed only to protect the twins. They had known one another for very little time, yet Matsuko herself had begun to like these insolent but charming girls. Since she had begun accompanying Ryo, she had met all sorts of people, but never children like them. Matsuko too wanted to keep anyone from hurting them.

Japanese: それを考えると今のうちに双子を連れて店の外に出るべきなのだが、ここで他の人間を見捨てていいものだろうか？
English: That suggested she should take the twins and leave now. But could she abandon everyone else inside?

Japanese: （きっと、リョウだったらみんなを守れって言うな……）
English: Ryo would surely tell me to protect everyone...

Japanese: そう思って怪物に一歩足をすすめたが、
English: With that thought, Matsuko took a step toward the monster.

Japanese: 「やめなさーい！」
English: “Stop right there!”

Japanese: 「私たちはこっちだよ！」
English: “We’re over here!”

Japanese: 双子がそれよりも先に前に出る。
English: The twins stepped forward before she could.

Japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっとおまえたち……」
English: “W-wait, you two...”

Japanese: 松子は引き留めようとするが二人は先ほどまでの怯えが嘘のように怪物の前に堂々と立ちはだかる。
English: Matsuko tried to stop them, but they stood boldly before the monster as though their earlier fear had never existed.

Japanese: 「そんなに遊びたいならもう一回遊んだげるわ！」
English: “If you want to play that badly, we’ll play with you again!”

Japanese: 「汐松子は、まわりのひとを守ってて！」
English: “Matsuko Shio, protect everyone around us!”

Japanese: すっかりおかしなスイッチが入ってしまったようで、そう告げると、二人はらんらんと目を輝かせて怪物を睨み付けた。
English: Some strange switch seemed to have flipped inside them. Having given Matsuko her orders, both girls glared at the monster with eyes blazing.

Japanese: こうなっては選択の余地はない。松子も腹をくくって観念するしかなかった。
English: There was no choice now. Matsuko could only accept the situation and steel herself.

Japanese: 床に散らばったガラスの破片がじゃらじゃらと音を立てて空中に舞い上がると、あられのように怪物に吹き付ける。怪物は顔を覆う様に腕を折り曲げた。その隙に、双子の片方が手元の花瓶などを投げつけている。
English: The shards of glass scattered across the floor rose into the air with a clatter, then blew against the monster like hail. The monster bent its arms over its face. In the opening, one twin hurled a vase and whatever else lay to hand.

Japanese: そうやって双子がモノをぶつけて怪物を飛び退かせている間に、松子は素早く走って行って、床の上で腰を抜かしていた泣きじゃくる子とそれを抱きかかえる母に手助けすると、
English: While the twins drove the monster back beneath their barrage, Matsuko raced over to help a sobbing child collapsed on the floor and the mother clutching the child.

Japanese: 「立って！　店を出て！」
English: “Stand! Get out of the cafe!”

Japanese: 大きな声で近くで怯える人々にそう指示する。
English: She shouted the instruction to the frightened people nearby.

Japanese: 恐怖に怯えて思考も身体も凍り付いてしまっている人間も、単純な指示を与えられると案外動けるものだ。
English: Even people whose thoughts and bodies have frozen in terror can move with surprising ease when given simple instructions.

Japanese: その声が引き金になって、何人かの客たちはバタバタと店を出て行った。
English: Her voice provided the trigger, and several customers rushed from the cafe.

Japanese: 路上には滑走路通りの人混みが混乱を作っていたが、
English: Outside, the crowd on Runway Street had descended into confusion.

Japanese: 「怪物だ！　化け物だ！」
English: “A monster! There’s a monster!”

Japanese: と、店から駆け出した客たちが叫ぶと、その大部分はクモの子を散らすように視界から離れて行く。その拍子に路上で物を売る者たちの商品を乗せた台がひっくり返り、ガチャガチャという騒音や、「ふざけんなよ！」というような怒号が聞こえる。
English: When the customers fleeing the cafe shouted this warning, most of the crowd scattered from sight like spiderlings. In the rush, tables bearing street vendors’ goods overturned. Crashes and clatters mixed with angry shouts of ‘What the hell?’

Japanese: 親子を退避させた松子がすぐに店内に戻ると、ほんの僅か離れていただけで、テーブルやら何やらがひっくり返ったりコーヒーカップやピッチャーの破片や氷の入ったドリンクがぶちまけられたりして、まるでミキサーか何かで確反した後のような状態になっていた。
English: After evacuating the mother and child, Matsuko immediately returned to the cafe. In the brief time she had been away, tables and other furniture had overturned, shards of coffee cups and pitchers lay everywhere, and drinks had spilled with ice strewn among them. The room looked as though it had been churned inside an enormous mixer.

Japanese: 双子は遠くからひたすら物を浴びせかけている。怪物はそれを長い腕で受けたり、横に飛んで交わしたりしながら双子に近づき、そのかぎ爪を伸ばす。双子は危うくそれをかわしてはいるが、どう見ても優勢とは言えない状況だった。
English: The twins continued pelting the monster with objects from a distance. It blocked some with its long arms and leaped sideways around others while closing in on the girls and reaching out with its claws. They narrowly avoided each strike, but plainly did not have the advantage.

Japanese: 二人は怯えてはいないにしろ顔は蒼白になっていて、極度の緊張が見て取れた。腕や、スカートから剥き出しになったふくらはぎなどに細かい切り傷が増えている。ぶつけた物はさほどダメージを与えられず、怪物の爪から逃げ回るので精一杯といった状況のようだ。
English: Though the twins showed no fear, their faces had gone pale and their extreme tension was plain to see. Small cuts multiplied across their arms and the calves exposed beneath their skirts. The objects they threw caused little damage; the girls seemed capable of little more than fleeing the monster’s claws.

Japanese: 松子が近づこうとすると、双子がまき散らすガラスの破片などが壁や天井ではじけて、彼女の行く手を阻む。
English: When Matsuko tried to approach, glass shards and other objects scattered by the twins burst against the walls and ceiling, blocking her way.

Japanese: 「もう大丈夫だから逃げて！　あとは私に任せて！」
English: “It’s safe now, so run! Leave the rest to me!”

Japanese: 「でも！」
English: “But!”

Japanese: 「私たちだって……」
English: “We can still—”

Japanese: 「邪魔なの！」
English: “You’re in the way!”

Japanese: 松子が表情を変えずに言うと、双子は下唇を噛み、涙をにじませながら後退して割れたガラスを踏み越え路上に退避した。
English: Matsuko spoke without changing her expression. The twins bit their lower lips and retreated with tears in their eyes, stepping across the broken glass and out into the street.

Japanese: それを追って路上に飛び出した怪物の前に松子が立ち塞がる。
English: The monster pursued them outside. Matsuko stepped into its path.

Japanese: 怪物は一瞬身を伏せると、跳躍してその頭上を飛び越そうとしたが、それより早く松子が足の一本にしがみつくと体勢を崩してアスファルトの上に土埃を上げて落ちる。その衝撃で松子の手も離れ、お互いはそれぞれの場所で倒れたが、それぞれが素早く立ち上がる。
English: The monster crouched for an instant, then leaped to clear her head. Matsuko moved first and clung to one of its legs. The creature lost its balance and crashed onto the asphalt in a cloud of dust. The impact tore her hands loose, and the two landed apart, but both were back on their feet at once.

Japanese: 怪物はそこで松子を睨み付けると、苛立たしげに四本の手足をばたつかせ、まるで犬のように低く吼えた。その方向は鼓膜をつんざくほどに大きく空気を震わせ、全身がビリビリとするようなその感覚に松子は顔を顰める。
English: The monster glared at Matsuko, thrashed its four limbs in irritation, and growled low like a dog. Its deafening roar shook the air. Matsuko frowned as the vibration ran through her entire body.

Japanese: そこで怪物は松子をはっきり敵と認めた。風を巻きながら突進し、右のかぎ爪を斜めに振り下ろす。
English: The monster now treated Matsuko unmistakably as an enemy. It charged in a swirl of air and swung its right claw down diagonally.

Japanese: それは目にもとまらぬ素早さであった。松子の想像を超えたもので、咄嗟には反応出来ない。全身を横に逃がしたが、それでは避けきれない。喉を切り裂かれる間一髪のところで右手を振り、どうにかかぎ爪を払いのけた。
English: The movement was too fast for the eye to follow and exceeded anything Matsuko had imagined. She could not react in time. She threw her whole body sideways but could not fully evade the strike. An instant before the claws tore open her throat, she flung up her right hand and somehow knocked them aside.

Japanese: 飛び退いてから松子は痛みを感じて右手を見ると、振り払った一差し指と中指と薬指の三本が切断されて断面から血がほとばしっていた。
English: Matsuko leaped back, then felt pain and looked at her right hand. The index, middle, and ring fingers that had struck the claw were gone. Blood spurted from the stumps.

Japanese: （思ったより早い……）
English: It’s faster than I thought...

Japanese: 松子は顔色一つ変えずに指が減った自分の手を確認してから、また視線を正面の怪物に戻す。
English: Without the slightest change of expression, Matsuko inspected the hand that had lost its fingers, then returned her gaze to the monster.

Japanese: 先ほど双子と対峙していたときより、怪物の動きは明らかに早く、その攻撃にも殺意があふれている。
English: The creature moved unmistakably faster than it had while confronting the twins. Its attacks now seemed filled with killing intent.

Japanese: （さっきは手を抜いていた？　……いや、違う）
English: Was it holding back before? ...No. That’s not it.

Japanese: 怪物はまた地面すれすれを飛ぶように突進してくると、横薙ぎにかぎ爪を払った。
English: The monster charged again, almost flying above the ground, and swept its claw horizontally.

Japanese: 松子は上体をそらしてそれをかわすが、避けきれずシャツの腹の辺りが切れ、うっすら血がにじむ。
English: Matsuko bent her upper body backward. The claw still caught the front of her shirt near the stomach, cutting the fabric and drawing a faint line of blood.

Japanese: （この人、双子とは戦う気がなかったんだ）
English: This person never wanted to fight the twins.

Japanese: そうとしか考えられない。
English: Matsuko could find no other explanation.

Japanese: 思えば、双子を傷つけてしまったのは、もしかしたらその爪の付いた手で触れようとしただけのようにも思える。とても、今松子を切り裂こうとしているような鋭い動きではなかった。実際、双子の傷は血液こそ流れているが表面の皮膚が少しひっかかれた程度のものでしかない。
English: Looking back, perhaps it had merely tried to touch the twins with its clawed hand when it hurt them. The motion had possessed none of the sharpness with which it now attempted to cut Matsuko apart. Indeed, although the twins’ wounds had bled, they amounted to little more than superficial scratches.

Japanese: （この人は何をしたいんだろう？）
English: What does this person want?

Japanese: そう考えながら見つめていると、相手はグルグルと低いうなり声を上げながら、また松子へと飛びかかる。
English: As Matsuko watched and considered the question, the monster growled low in its throat and leaped at her again.

Japanese: 右、左と交互に繰り出されるかぎ爪を、今度は傷つくことなく回避が出来た。
English: This time, Matsuko evaded the claws striking alternately from right and left without further injury.

Japanese: （さて、どうしようか）
English: Now, what should I do?

Japanese: 動きにはなんとかついていけているが、いかんせん腕の長さが違いすぎる。振り回す手足を掴もうとすれば早すぎて、先ほどのように指を失うだけだろう。素手のままでは相手に近づくことが出来ない。とすれば、双子がやっていたように何かを投げつけるか。
English: She could just manage to follow its movements, but the difference in their reach was far too great. Its limbs moved too quickly to seize; an attempt would merely cost her more fingers. Barehanded, she could not approach the monster. That left throwing something, as the twins had done.

Japanese: それにそもそも、そんなにむきになって攻撃すべき相手なのかという気がしている。もしかしたら、双子に対しなにか事情があるのかもしれない。
English: But she also wondered whether this was truly an opponent she should go all out to attack. The monster might have circumstances of its own involving the twins.

Japanese: （私にはわからないな。リョウがいれば……）
English: I don’t know. If Ryo were here...

Japanese: 手がジンジンと痛んで、切断面から血液が止めどもなく流れている。松子はそれを感じることが出来るが、自分の痛みに対して感情が動くことはない。目の前の怪物に対する恐怖もない。
English: Her hand throbbed, and blood poured without end from the severed surfaces. Matsuko could feel the pain, but her own injuries produced no movement of emotion within her. Nor did she fear the monster before her.

Japanese: ただ自分で何かを決定するのは得意ではなく、相手に何か事情がありそうなことを想像は出来たものの、それをどんな風に行動に結びつければいいのかわからない。
English: She was simply poor at deciding things for herself. She could imagine that the creature might have some reason for its behavior, but did not know how that thought should inform her actions.

Japanese: （普通の人ならこういうとき、心で決めるんだろう）
English: An ordinary person would decide with their heart at a time like this.

Japanese: 松子は、亮に連れて行かれた空き地でアリを棒で潰して殺した時のことを思い出し、背筋が冷たくなった。
English: Matsuko remembered crushing ants with a stick in the vacant lot Ryo had taken her to. A chill ran down her spine.

Japanese: 心と言えば、目の前のこの不可解な生き物も死なせたくはないというのが彼女の心だった。
English: If her heart was to decide, it said that she did not want this incomprehensible creature before her to die either.

Japanese: なんとか生かしたまま制圧する方法はないか。
English: Was there a way to subdue it without killing it?

Japanese: 「汐松子っ、下がって！」
English: “Matsuko Shio, get back!”

Japanese: 考えていると、背後から双子の叫ぶ声がする。
English: As she thought, the twins shouted behind her.

Japanese: 「えっ」
English: “What?”

Japanese: わけがわからないままも、松子は言われたとおり後ずさる。
English: Matsuko did not understand, but retreated as they instructed.

Japanese: すると、視界の上の方、怪物の頭上辺りで何かが動いたのが見えた。
English: Then, high in her field of vision, she saw something move above the monster’s head.

Japanese: 双子たちは怪物がその場所に来るのを待っていた。怪物が立っているのは、喫茶店の破れたガラスの前である。喫茶店は雑居ビルの一階部分を使って営業されていて、二階から上には様々なテナントが入っている。そして、それらのための看板がかかっていた。
English: The twins had been waiting for the monster to reach that place. It stood before the cafe’s shattered window. The cafe occupied the ground floor of a mixed-use building, with various tenants on the floors above and signs advertising their businesses.

Japanese: 双子は三階部分の消費者金融の看板に目をつけた。それは、ベランダの手すりにロープでくくりつけられている。双子は念動力でガラスの破片をそこまで動かし、ロープの一端を切った。そして怪物が下までやって来たところで、もう一端に切り目を入れたのだった。
English: The twins had selected the sign of a consumer lender on the third floor. It had been tied to the balcony railing with rope. Using psychokinesis, they moved a shard of glass up to the sign and cut one end of the rope. When the monster reached the ground below, they cut partway through the other end.

Japanese: 消費者金融『あおぞらローン』の『ロ』が書かれた正方形の看板が、手裏剣のように回転しながら落下する。
English: The square sign panel bearing the katakana RO from the consumer lender ‘Aozora Loans’ fell, spinning like a shuriken.

Japanese: 軌道は僅かにずれていたが、空中で見えない力によって修正され、怪物の背中に向かって舞い落ちた。
English: Its path was slightly off target, but an invisible force corrected it in midair, and it sailed toward the monster’s back.

Japanese: 怪物は直前に風を切る落下音に気がついてわずかに首を傾けたが、そのままの姿勢で、背中に看板の直撃を受けた。
English: At the last moment, the monster heard the sign slicing through the air and tilted its head slightly. Still in that position, it took the impact squarely in the back.

Japanese: 看板によって地面に胴体をはりつけにされる。グルルルルとうなり声を上げ、体をよじり、四肢を動かそうとするがかぎ爪は地面を捉えるほどの力がなく、胴体は持ち上がらない。
English: The sign pinned the monster’s torso to the ground. It growled, twisted its body, and tried to move its limbs, but the claws could not find enough purchase to lift it.

Japanese: ガラスが散らばるアスファルトの上に、真っ赤な血液が水たまりを広げて行く。
English: A pool of brilliant red blood spread across the glass-strewn asphalt.

Japanese: 「大丈夫っ！」
English: “Are you all right?”

Japanese: 「汐松子、指が……」
English: “Matsuko Shio, your fingers...”

Japanese: 双子は松子のそばに駆けつけ、その指を失った手を二人でいたわるように持ち上げた。
English: The twins ran to Matsuko and together lifted the hand that had lost its fingers as though cradling it.

Japanese: 「私は大丈夫」
English: “I’m all right.”

Japanese: 松子は言いながら、怪物の方を見ている。
English: Matsuko kept her eyes upon the monster as she spoke.

Japanese: 怪物はまだ死んではいない。荒い息を吐きながら、その手足を震わせている。そして首を何度もかしげるような仕草をしながら、こちらに視線を送っていた。
English: It was not yet dead. Its limbs trembled as it breathed harshly. Again and again, it seemed to cock its head, turning its gaze toward them.

Japanese: 「しぶといわね」
English: “It’s stubborn.”

Japanese: 「トドメをさそう」
English: “Let’s finish it.”

Japanese: 視線に気がついた双子が、怒りを露わにして怪物を睨み付けた。
English: Noticing the monster’s gaze, the twins glared back with open anger.

Japanese: 「ほっといても死ぬよ。それより……」
English: “It will die even if we leave it alone. More importantly...”

Japanese: 松子は双子を押しとどめて怪物に近づく。すると、そのぜえぜえと粘液がどこかでからまっているような呼吸音が耳に入る。看板が突き刺さった真っ赤な血の海のなかに、ぐちゃぐちゃになった肉と、脊椎の白が見える。
English: Matsuko stopped the twins and approached the monster. As she did, she heard its wheezing breaths, as though mucus had caught somewhere inside it. Amid the sea of bright blood around the embedded sign, mangled flesh and the white of its spine were visible.

Japanese: 松子の接近に、怪物は口元を噛みしめ敵意を剥き出しにしながら、また手足を地面に突き立てようとする。すると、その傍らに転がっていた握りこぶしほどの壁材のかけらがふわりと浮いた。松子は手を上げて背後の双子に合図をし、攻撃をやめさせる。
English: At Matsuko’s approach, the monster set its jaw and showed open hostility, trying again to drive its limbs into the ground. A fist-sized piece of wall rose lightly beside it. Matsuko raised one hand, signaling the twins behind her to stop their attack.

Japanese: 「もう終わった。私は何もしない。あなたが何者なのか知りたいだけ」
English: “It’s over. I won’t do anything. I only want to know who you are.”

Japanese: 松子は怪物の目をじっと見つめながらそう話しかけた。
English: Matsuko addressed the monster while looking steadily into its eye.

Japanese: 「あの子たちに用があるんだね？　ちょっと、荷物を見せて貰うから」
English: “You came because of those girls, didn’t you? I’m going to look through your belongings.”

Japanese: 松子は怪物が胴体に斜めにかけた革のショルダーバッグにまだ指がある左手を伸ばす。
English: Matsuko extended her left hand, which still had its fingers, toward the leather shoulder bag crossing the monster’s torso.

Japanese: 目を見つめながらゆっくり動くと、怪物は低いうなり声を上げ続けてはいたがそれ以上は何もしなかった。
English: She moved slowly and kept her gaze upon its eye. The monster continued its low growl but did nothing further.

Japanese: 掛け紐のフックを外して手元にたぐり寄せて膝の上に蚊抱え込むと、そのフラップを開く。
English: Matsuko unhooked the strap, drew the bag toward herself, cradled it upon her lap, and opened the flap.

Japanese: 開けた瞬間、ふわっと甘い腐臭が漂った。
English: The moment she opened it, a sweet odor of rot drifted out.

Japanese: カバンのなかから出て来たのはピンク色の包装紙で包まれ、赤いリボンのついた弁当箱ほどの箱だった。松子はそれを取り出して脇に置く。カバンには同じ箱が二つ入っていた。
English: Inside was a box about the size of a lunchbox, wrapped in pink paper and tied with a red ribbon. Matsuko removed it and placed it beside her. The bag contained two identical boxes.

Japanese: そして箱がなくなると、なにか茶色いものがカバンの側面に張り付くように折りたたまれている。松子はそれに触れる。
English: With the boxes gone, she saw something brown lying folded against the side of the bag. Matsuko touched it.

Japanese: ねちゃねちゃとしたものが指先に付着し、そして何か尖ったものがチクリと手に触れたので、思わず彼女は手を引っ込める。
English: Something sticky clung to her fingertip, and a sharp point pricked her. She instinctively pulled her hand back.

Japanese: 見ると指先に小さな赤い血の点が出来ていた。トゲのようなものに触れたのだ。次はより慎重に手を入れて、取り出す。
English: A tiny red bead of blood had formed on her finger. She had touched something like a thorn. Matsuko reached inside more carefully and removed the object.

Japanese: それは、一本の野バラだった。花の部分は完全に腐って持ち上げるとグズグズに壊れてしまったが、茎は比較的元の形を保っている。花の近くのトゲは少し残っていたが、下の方は綺麗に切り取られたあとがある。花屋で買ったのか、怪物がそうしたものなのか。
English: It was a single wild rose. The flower had rotted completely and fell apart when lifted, but the stem retained something of its original shape. A few thorns remained near the flower, while those lower down had been neatly removed. Had the monster bought it at a florist, or prepared it this way itself?

Japanese: 松子はそれも脇に置き、そして再度カバンのなかに手を入れて、別のポケットからパスケースのようなものを見つけて取り出した。
English: Matsuko set this aside as well. She reached into the bag once more and found something resembling a pass holder inside another pocket.

Japanese: 黒光りする使い込まれた表紙をめくると、怪物の顔写真がはりつけられた身分証のようなものがあらわれる。松子は知らなかったが、それは業務などでサイキック能力を使う者のために特別に発行されるライセンスであった。
English: She opened its well-used cover, polished black with age. Inside was something resembling identification, bearing a photograph of the monster’s face. Matsuko did not know it, but this was a license issued specially to people who used psychic abilities in their work.

Japanese: 松子はその名前の部分を読んで、絶句する。
English: Matsuko read the name and fell speechless.

Japanese: 「えっ、何これ……」
English: “What...? What’s this...?”

Japanese: 松子が振り返るといつのまにか双子がうしろに立って、肩越しに松子の手の中のものを見ていた。
English: Matsuko turned. At some point, the twins had come to stand behind her and were looking over her shoulder at the object in her hand.

Japanese: そのライセンスには『灰上彰』という名前がはっきりと書かれていた。
English: The license plainly bore the name ‘Akira Haigami.’

Japanese: 「うそっ、嘘だよ！」
English: “No! That’s a lie!”

Japanese: 双子の片方が、カバンから取り出した箱を取り出し、包装紙を破ってそのなかのものを確かめる。
English: One twin seized a box Matsuko had removed from the bag, tore away the wrapping paper, and checked the contents.

Japanese: 「これ、お兄ちゃんが私たちにプレゼントしてくれるって言ってたゲームだ……」
English: “This is the game our brother promised to give us...”

Japanese: 「こっちにあるのは、私たちの好きな薔薇の花……」
English: “And over here is our favorite flower, a rose...”

Japanese: 「嘘だよっ！　こんなの嘘だわっ！」
English: “It’s a lie! All of this is a lie!”

Japanese: 「こいつが、どこかでお兄ちゃんのカバンを盗んだんだよっ！　こいつっ！」
English: “This thing stole our brother’s bag somewhere! This monster did it!”

Japanese: 双子の片方が、目を金色に輝かせて傍らの瓦礫を持ち上げ怪物の頭に振り落とそうとするのを、松子が腕を掴んで押しとどめた。
English: One twin’s eyes shone gold as she raised a piece of rubble beside her and prepared to bring it down upon the monster’s head. Matsuko caught her arm and stopped her.

Japanese: すると遠くからエンジン音が聞こえてきて三人はそちらを振り向く。
English: Then the sound of an engine came from the distance, and all three girls turned toward it.

Japanese: 向こうからバイクに乗ってこちらへ近づいて来るのが見えた。
English: A motorcycle was approaching them from farther down the street.

Japanese: 「おいっ！　お前らっ！　そこにいるのか！」
English: “Hey! You three! Are you there?”

Japanese: 運転している道夫がそう叫ぶ。そのうしろには亮が座っている。
English: Michio shouted from the driver’s seat. Ryo sat behind him.

Japanese: 彼らは少女たちの目の前でバイクを止め、そしてこの光景で全てを悟った。
English: They stopped the motorcycle in front of the girls, took in the scene before them, and understood.

Japanese: 亮と道夫は深沢から全てを聞いていた。
English: Ryo and Michio had heard the complete account from Fukazawa.

Japanese: 灰上姉妹の兄である灰上彰は、生まれた時から重度の特質変異と強力なサイキック能力を持ち、とても社会で生活を営めないということで専用の施設で育てられた。
English: According to that account, Akira Haigami, elder brother of the Haigami sisters, had possessed a severe trait mutation and powerful psychic ability from birth. Because he was considered unable to live within society, he had been raised in a specialized facility.

Japanese: そして成人したあとは政府に採用され、そのサイキック能力を使った特殊な任務を請け負うことになる。
English: Upon reaching adulthood, he was reportedly employed by the government and assigned special missions that made use of his psychic ability.

Japanese: その能力は『配達』と呼ばれていたそうだ。
English: His ability was said to be called ‘Delivery.’

Japanese: 誰かに宛てて書かれた手紙やプレゼントを、確実に相手に届ける能力である。その手紙なりプレゼントなりを身につけた状態で血液をまき散らすと、そこに相手の居場所を示す地図が浮かび上がる。双子の部屋に見たあの血の地図は、そうして彼の能力によって作られたものだった。
English: According to the account, it allowed him to deliver a letter or gift reliably to its intended recipient. If he carried the item and scattered his blood, a map indicating the recipient’s location appeared. The map of blood found inside the twins’ room had been produced through this ability.

Japanese: 彼の能力は例えば爆弾を目的の相手に送り届けたり、単なる人探しだったり、使い方によっては様々な応用が出来るもので、政府では大層重宝されたという。
English: The ability could reportedly be applied in many ways, from delivering a bomb to a particular target to locating an ordinary missing person, and the government was said to value it highly.

Japanese: また、その人柄も評価されていた。
English: He was reportedly highly regarded for his character as well.

Japanese: 灰上彰は見かけこそ化け物のようだがひねくれたところがなく、性格は優しく真面目で、いつも周囲にきめこまやかな気配りの出来る青年だった。
English: Although Akira Haigami looked like a monster, the account described him as entirely without bitterness: a kind and earnest young man who always showed close consideration for the people around him.

Japanese: タイプBではあったが、精神に何か症状が出ているとは誰も思わなかった。
English: He was a Type B, but no one around him was reported to have seen any psychological symptoms.

Japanese: 大抵は兆候があるものだ。しかし、彼の場合はそれがなかった。
English: Ordinarily, there were signs. According to the account, he had shown none.

Japanese: 非番の日、妹たちに送るプレゼントを購入したあとに彼は『発症』し、行方不明になった。
English: Reportedly, on a day off after purchasing gifts for his sisters, he experienced ‘onset’ and disappeared.

Japanese: この失踪は世間には隠されたが、双子の保護者である深沢には連絡があった。
English: The disappearance was concealed from the public, but Fukazawa was informed because he was the twins’ guardian.

Japanese: 深沢は、灰上彰の正体を知らぬ双子にはこのことを伝えなかった。
English: Fukazawa did not tell the twins, who knew nothing of Akira’s real identity.

Japanese: 彰が失踪したのは遠く離れた場所であり、狂った頭でこんな場所までやって来ることは考えられなかったし、仮にそう思いついたとしても、どこかで警察の網に引っかかるだろうと考えていたからである。
English: Akira had disappeared in a distant place. Fukazawa had reportedly believed that, with his mind in that state, he could never travel this far and that, even if the idea occurred to him, the police would catch him somewhere along the way.

Japanese: そして彰が死んでから、当たり障りのないかたちで双子にその死を伝えようと考えていたのである。
English: Fukazawa said he had intended to wait until Akira died, then tell the twins of his death in terms unlikely to disturb them.

Japanese: それがまさか、本当にここまでやって来るとは。
English: He had never imagined, he said, that Akira would truly come this far.

Japanese: その道のりの困難さは、彰のボロボロになった服にもあらわれている。彼はこんな姿だが、いや、このような姿だからこそ、いつも身だしなみには気を遣い、新品と見間違うようなものを身につけていたのだ。
English: Akira’s ruined clothing testified to the difficulty of the journey. Despite his appearance—or perhaps precisely because of it—he had always reportedly taken great care with his grooming and wore clothes that could be mistaken for new.

Japanese: 彼がどうしても渡したかったプレゼントは、今こうして最愛の妹たちのもとに届いた。妹たちが大好きな薔薇はもう腐ってはいるが、ここに来る途中で彼が正気を喪いながらも手折ったものだ。――この様な状態でも届けることが出来たのだから、彼の『配達』の能力と、その仕事の熱心さはやはり評判通り優れていたのだろう。
English: The gifts he had so desperately wanted to deliver had now reached his beloved sisters. Their favorite rose had already rotted, but the account said he had plucked it along the way even as he lost his grip on reality. Since he succeeded in delivering everything even in this state, the narrator’s account concludes that both his ‘Delivery’ ability and his devotion to his work must indeed have been as exceptional as their reputation suggested.

Japanese: しかし、彼自身はその妹たちの手によって今まさに命を失おうとしていた。
English: Akira himself, however, was now about to lose his life by his sisters’ hands.

Japanese: 高い知性というものは、他人にとっても本人にとっても残酷な働きをする。双子は二人とも聰明で、感情がいくら否定したくても、その知性があまりにも理不尽な事実を彼女たちに突きつけた。双子は目をそらすことが出来ない。自分たちが兄を殺したのだ。
English: A powerful intellect can work cruelly upon both others and itself. The account presents both twins as clever enough that, however desperately their feelings denied it, their intelligence forced an unbearably cruel fact upon them. They could not look away from it: they had killed their brother.

Japanese: 顔を涙でぐしょぐしょにし、声をあげて泣いている。
English: Their faces were drenched in tears, and they wept aloud.

Japanese: 二人に出来ることはもはや、自分たちによって兄に訪れようとしている死を待つしかないように思われた。
English: It seemed that all they could do now was wait for the death they had brought upon him.

Japanese: そこで、亮が仲間たちの一歩前に出た。
English: Then Ryo stepped ahead of his companions.

Japanese: 何をするつもりかとみなに見守られるなか、彼は上着から拳銃を引き抜き、彰のこめかみに当てると躊躇なく引き金を引いた。
English: Everyone watched to see what he intended. Ryo drew the pistol from his jacket, pressed it to Akira’s temple, and pulled the trigger without hesitation.

Japanese: 彰は全身をビクリと震わせたが、そのあとはぐったりとしてもう二度と動かない。
English: Akira’s entire body jerked. Then it went limp and never moved again.

Japanese: 亮は双子を振り返り、
English: Ryo turned toward the twins.

Japanese: 「こいつを殺したのは僕だ。お前たちは何もしていない」
English: “I killed him. You did nothing.”

Japanese: と言った。
English: That was what he told them.

Japanese: これが菅原亮こと謝亮にとって生涯初めての殺人だった。
English: This was the first person Ryo Sugawara—Tse Leung—had killed in his life.

Japanese: この後、亮は自分のチームと縄張りを道夫に譲ることを提案したが、道夫はそれを頑なに断った。その代わりに道夫はお互いのチームを合同するという案を持ちかけた。
English: Afterward, Ryo proposed handing his team and territory to Michio, but Michio refused adamantly. In their place, he proposed that the two teams merge.

Japanese: 少年同士のいざこざから足を洗いたがっていた亮がそれを受け入れたのは、この件を通じて彼も道夫のことを評価したのだろう。奇しくも大人になって父クリス・ツェーに求められてYSに加入したように、謝亮という人物は自分の人生の大事な局面で他人の希望にこたえてしまうようだ。
English: Ryo had wanted to wash his hands of conflicts among boys. He probably accepted the proposal because this affair had given him some respect for Michio. Strangely, just as he would enter YS as an adult in response to the wishes of his father, Chris Tse, Tse Leung appears to have been a person who answered other people’s hopes at the decisive moments of his life.

Japanese: そして、見土道夫と菅原亮が手を組むことで生まれたこの少年たちのグループが、やがてY地区の少年史上に残る大きな集団となってゆくのである。
English: The group born when Michio Mido and Ryo Sugawara joined forces would eventually become one of the largest in the history of the boys of Y District.

Japanese: 汐健慈朗の家を出たあと、私たちは狭い裏路地を伝いながら移動する。背中のサーシェンカは人形のようにぐったりとしていて、毛布からはみ出た手足がぶらぶらと揺れている。
English: After leaving Kenjiro Shio’s house, we made our way through narrow back alleys. Sashenka hung limp as a doll upon our back, his arms and legs dangling from the blanket and swinging with every step.

Japanese: この状態で人目につく行動は避けたい。変に騒がれたら、殺さなくてはいけなくなる。
English: We wanted to avoid being seen in this condition. If anyone made a fuss, we would have to kill them.

Japanese: どこか休む場所が必要だ。コシチェイを連れている以上、この間まで隠れ家にしていたあの洋館には戻れない。ほかにどこか人気のない建物か、安く借りられる宿泊所がないかと考えたが、心あたりがない。
English: We needed somewhere to rest. As long as we had Koschei with us, we could not return to the Western-style mansion we had used as a hideout until recently. We tried to think of some other deserted building, or a cheap place to stay, but nothing came to mind.

Japanese: 落ち着く場所を求めてパラシュート通り裏の路地を彷徨っていると、また耳元で羽虫の音が聞こえてきた。この間よりもはっきりと。ぶううううん、ぶうううううううん。
English: As we wandered the alleys behind Parachute Street in search of somewhere to settle, we once again heard an insect buzzing beside our ear, clearer now than before. Bzzzzzz. Bzzzzzzzzzz.

Japanese: 発症の兆候だ。このまま何もしなければ、私たちの心は壊れるに違いない。
English: It was a sign of onset. If we did nothing, our mind would surely break.

Japanese: でも、ネオ・ローズで治療をすれば再生の力がなくなってしまう。YSや警察の追求をすり抜けて逃げなくてはいけないところを考えると、治療すべきかどうかは難しい。でも、この症状は耐えがたい。
English: But treatment with Neo Rose would take away our power of regeneration. We had to evade YS and the police, which made it difficult to decide whether to seek treatment. Yet the symptoms were unbearable.

Japanese: だんだん脂汗が出て来て、そのあたりの路地で座り込んで仕舞おうかと思った時、不動産屋の札がかかった売り出し中の建物を見つけて侵入した。
English: A clammy sweat gradually broke across our skin. Just as we thought we might sink down in one of those alleys, we found a building for sale with a real-estate sign outside and broke in.

Japanese: 喉が渇いている。水道の蛇口を捻ると水が出たので、それを直接口をつけて飲んだら顔がびしゃびしゃに濡れてしまった。
English: We were thirsty. Water came out when we turned the tap, so we put our mouth directly to it and drank, soaking our face.

Japanese: サーシェンカのところへ戻る。彼はうっすら目を開いている。
English: We returned to Sashenka. His eyes were faintly open.

Japanese: 「水を飲む？」
English: “Do you want some water?”

Japanese: 彼はもうろうとして目の前の空間をながめながら微かに頷く。
English: He gazed blearily into the empty space before him and gave the slightest nod.

Japanese: 「立てる？」
English: “Can you stand?”

Japanese: 彼はゆっくり首を横に振る。
English: Slowly, he shook his head.

Japanese: 「じゃあどうやるか……」
English: “Then how do we do this...?”

Japanese: コップのようなものはない。
English: There was nothing resembling a cup.

Japanese: 私たちはもう一度蛇口に口をつけると水を口の中に含む。
English: We put our mouth to the tap again and filled it with water.

Japanese: それを飲み込まないようにしながらサーシェンカのそばにしゃがみ込むと、その顎をあげ、唇をつけた。
English: Holding the water without swallowing, we crouched beside Sashenka, raised his chin, and pressed our lips to his.

Japanese: そしてゆっくりと彼の口に流し込む。喉がこくりとする。
English: Then we slowly poured the water into his mouth. His throat bobbed.

Japanese: 「もっと飲む？」
English: “Do you want more?”

Japanese: サーシェンカは頷く。
English: Sashenka nodded.

Japanese: 私たちはもう一度同じことをする。
English: We did the same thing once more.

Japanese: 「……ありがとう」
English: “...Thank you.”

Japanese: サーシェンカは少し笑って、また眠りにつく。
English: Sashenka smiled a little, then went back to sleep.

Japanese: 私たちも眠かった。そこで彼に寄り添うようにしながら横になると、すぐに眠りに落ちた。
English: We were sleepy too. We lay down close beside him and fell asleep at once.

Japanese: 多分三時間くらいしか寝ていないのに、目が覚めた。身体に疲れが残っているけれど、頭が緊張してもう一度眠りにつくことは出来そうになかった。耳鳴りはやんでいる。一時的なものかもしれないが、私たちはほっとして立ち上がった。
English: We woke after perhaps only three hours. Weariness remained in our body, but our mind was too tense to return to sleep. The ringing in our ears had stopped. It might only have been temporary, but we rose in relief.

Japanese: 食べるものも何もない。私たちはトイレに行ってから必要なものを調達するために家を出た。サーシェンカを置いていくのは心配だったけれど、買い物に彼を連れて行くわけにはいかない。
English: There was nothing to eat. After using the toilet, we left the house to obtain what we needed. We worried about leaving Sashenka behind, but could hardly take him shopping with us.

Japanese: このあたりは顔見知りも多い。私たちは髪で顔を隠すように俯いて歩き、日用品店で食糧と、身体拭きとサーシェンカのため、変身しても着られるようなゆったりとした衣服を買った。
English: Many people in the area knew our face. We walked with our head bowed, hiding it behind our hair, and bought food, body wipes, and loose clothing that Sashenka could wear even if he transformed.

Japanese: そして建物に戻ってくると、サーシェンカはその姿を消し、かわりに金髪の少女に変わっていた。瞬間移動の能力を持つ少女『マリア』だ。エフゲニ・イリイーチ・ヘスのお爺ちゃんの話によると、信心深い少女で、お爺ちゃんの指示の声を神の声だと信じ、それに従順に従っている。感情的になりやすいのが欠点だが、戦闘向きの能力と、その従順性から戦いの場面で呼び出されることが多い。殺人のための奴隷だ。
English: When we returned to the building, Sashenka had vanished. In his place was a blond girl: Maria, who possessed the power of teleportation. According to what old Yevgeny Ilyich Hess had told us, she was deeply religious and believed his instructions to be the voice of God, which she obeyed without question. Her tendency to become emotional was a fault, but her combat-oriented ability and obedience meant that she was often summoned for battle. In his telling, she was a slave used for murder.

Japanese: 人を殺しすぎて情緒がおかしくなっているとのことだった。
English: Hess had said that killing too many people had left her emotionally disturbed.

Japanese: マリアはいま全裸のまま毛布の上に立ち、うつろな表情をしている。その身体にはまだ傷跡が残っている。変身能力が戻っても、まだかつてのような再生能力は戻りきっていないんだろう。
English: Maria now stood naked upon the blanket, her expression vacant. Scars still covered her body. Even though her power of transformation had returned, her former regenerative ability probably had not yet recovered completely.

Japanese: 「どうしたの？」
English: “What’s wrong?”

Japanese: 「あなたダレ？」
English: “Who ARE you?”

Japanese: マリアはうろんな表情を向ける。
English: Maria gave us a suspicious look.

Japanese: 「会ったことあると思うけど」
English: “I think we’ve met before.”

Japanese: 「しらない……」
English: “Don’t know you...”

Japanese: 言って、マリアはぴょんとジャンプする。そして着地すると、悲しそうに顔をしかめた。
English: With that, Maria sprang into the air. When she landed, her face twisted with sorrow.

Japanese: 「チカラがなくなっちゃった。かみさまがきえちゃった……」
English: “My POWER is gone. God is gone...”

Japanese: 「薬によってサイキックの力が奪われてるだけ。昨日までカプセルに入れられてたでしょ。その時、そういう薬を使ってたんだって」
English: “The drugs only took your psychic power away. You were kept in a capsule until yesterday, remember? They used that kind of drug on you in there.”

Japanese: 「ちがう」
English: “No.”

Japanese: マリアは顔を横にぶんぶんと振る。
English: Maria shook her head violently from side to side.

Japanese: 「いいつけをまもれなかった、かみさまにすてられちゃったの……」
English: “I didn’t do what He told me. God threw me away...”

Japanese: マリアは涙をボロボロと流す。
English: Tears streamed down Maria’s face.

Japanese: 「どうしよう。……マリアシぬんだ。シんでジゴクにおちるんだ……。うう……」
English: “What do I do? ...Maria’s going to DIE. I’m going to DIE and go to HELL... Uuuh...”

Japanese: 「力は何日かで戻るって」
English: “Your power will come back in a few days.”

Japanese: 私たちの言葉にマリアは反応せず、泣き続ける。
