English: “You have to. There is no other way to preserve the Fernandes name. He will not say no. Deep down, he wants to help you. I know he does.”

Japanese: 「そんなことはないです……」
English: “That isn’t true...”

Japanese: 「彼がアタシに加勢するよう指示しなかったのは、あなたを見捨てたからじゃないわ」
English: “The fact that he didn’t order me to join the fight does not mean he abandoned you.”

Japanese: 「そ、それは関係ありません。そうじゃなくて……」
English: “Th-that has nothing to do with this. That isn’t why...”

Japanese: リタは顔を上げると視線を合わせて世傑のまなざしに応え、
English: Rita raised her face and met Sai-kit’s gaze.

Japanese: 「これは誇りの問題です。部下を殺され、家を荒らし尽くされて、自力で戦うことも出来ずにYSに頼るなんてフェルナンデス家の名折れです。そのような情けのないことをしたら、あの世で父に会わせる顔がありません。私たちの勢力が衰えたからといって離れるものがいるのならば、勝手に離れさせればいいのです。残ったもので戦います」
English: “This is a matter of pride. My subordinates have been killed, my home has been ravaged, and I am incapable of fighting by myself. To turn to YS now would disgrace the Fernandes name. If I behaved so shamefully, how could I face my father in the next world? If people wish to leave because our power has diminished, let them leave. Those who remain will fight.”

Japanese: 「死ぬ気？」
English: “Are you planning to die?”

Japanese: 「フェルナンデス家は、今までもこうした危機を乗り切って来ました。負けるつもりはありません」
English: “The Fernandes Family has survived crises like this before. I do not intend to lose.”
“I see...”

Japanese: 世傑は目を伏せ、自分のティーカップに手をつける。
English: Sai-kit lowered his eyes and picked up his teacup.

Japanese: 結局リタは一晩だけ彼のマンションで過ごし、翌朝すぐに親戚の家に向かうと決まった。
English: In the end, they agreed that Rita would spend only one night in his apartment and leave for her relatives’ home first thing the following morning.

Japanese: 深夜、ソファーで横になっていた世傑がトイレのために部屋を出ると、リタに貸し与えた寝室から物音がする。
English: Late that night, Sai-kit rose from the sofa to use the bathroom. As he left the living room, he heard a sound from the bedroom he had lent Rita.

Japanese: やはりまだ眠れないのだろう。彼女だって、この状況でなんの保護もなく帰ることに危険性は理解している。
English: She was probably still unable to sleep. She, too, had to understand the danger of returning without any protection under the circumstances.

Japanese: 恐ろしくないはずがない。しかも、彼女は今でこそフェルナンデス・ファミリーを背負っているが、ついこの間までは三人娘の末っ子という、家族のなかでは最もこのような役割から遠い位置にいたのだ。補佐があったとはいえ、ギャングの女ボスとして仲間を率いてゆくのは並大抵のことではなかったに違いない。
English: She could hardly be unafraid. Though the Fernandes Family now rested upon her shoulders, until very recently she had been merely the youngest of three daughters—the member of her family farthest removed from such a role. Even with advisers to help her, leading her people as a female gang boss could not have been easy.

Japanese: その結果、こうして仲間を殺してしまったことが彼女を追い詰めているのだろうか？
English: Had the deaths of her comrades, the result of her leadership, now driven her into a corner?

Japanese: 世傑はノックをしてドアを開けた。照明の落ちた部屋のなか、リタは横にならずにベッドに腰掛けたまま何か考え事をしている。
English: Sai-kit knocked and opened the door. In the darkened room, Rita sat on the edge of the bed rather than lying down, lost in thought.

Japanese: 「暗いところで考えても、前向きな考えは出ないわよ」
English: “You won’t find any positive thoughts brooding in the dark.”

Japanese: 世傑はそう言って部屋の照明をつけた。
English: Sai-kit switched on the light.

Japanese: リタは寝間着代わりに世傑が与えたぶかぶかの黒いトレーナーを着ている。彼を見上げる彼女の顔には泣いたあとがあり、目のまわりが赤く腫れ上がっていた。
English: Rita wore the oversized black sweatshirt he had given her for pajamas. When she looked up at him, her face showed signs of having cried, and her eyes were red and swollen.

Japanese: 世傑はそのことには触れず、リタも言い訳はしなかった。
English: Sai-kit did not mention it. Rita offered no excuse.

Japanese: 「お邪魔するわね」
English: “I’m coming in.”

Japanese: 世傑はそう断ってリタの隣に座ると、その手を握った。
English: After announcing himself, Sai-kit sat beside Rita and took her hand.

Japanese: 「こうすると、体温を感じるでしょう？」
English: “You can feel my body heat when I do this, can’t you?”

Japanese: 驚くリタに世傑は微笑み書けた。
English: Rita looked surprised. Sai-kit smiled at her.

Japanese: 「確かに、今アタシたちの身体は温かいわ。触れ合ってるところがぽかぽかとして春の日の日向みたい。それに、こうやって会話をして、意志の疎通も出来る。それは二人とも生きていて、心臓が動いていて、そしてその温かい身体のなかに心があるからなのよ」
English: “Our bodies really are warm right now. Where they touch, it feels as warm as a patch of sun on a spring day. We can talk like this, too. We can communicate what we mean. That’s because both of us are alive: our hearts are beating, and each of these warm bodies holds a human heart.”

Japanese: リタは相手がどういう話をしようとしているのかわからず、怪訝な表情をする。
English: Unable to tell what he was trying to say, Rita looked at him doubtfully.

Japanese: 世傑はかまわず続ける。
English: Sai-kit continued regardless.

Japanese: 「でも死んだら冷たくなって、もう会話も出来ない。今アタシを見ているあなたのキラキラした目も、灰色に濁ってしまう。市場で売ってる魚の目を見たことある？　人間も死んだらあんな目になっちゃうんだから。死んだ人間は悪臭がして、そうして少しずつ腐ってゆく……」
English: “But when you die, you grow cold, and you can’t speak anymore. Those bright eyes looking at me now will turn dull and gray. Have you ever seen the eyes of the fish at the market? Human eyes look like that when we die. Dead people stink, and then, little by little, they rot...”

Japanese: 世傑は鼻をつまんで、おどけてみせる。
English: Sai-kit pinched his nose and made a comic face.

Japanese: 「あなたは誇りのためなんて言うけれど、この世界には格好のいい死なんかないわ。色んな人の死を見てきたからわかる。誇り高く戦いに望んだギャングだって、負けて殺されれば衣服を剥ぎ取られ自分の逸物を口に突っ込まれる。美少女も美少年もナイフで一皮剥いただけでB級ホラーの怪物になるわ。それになにより、あんなに賑やかな部屋が、みんな死んでしまって静かになるというのはとても寂しいものよ。あの寂しさを感じたら、死というものがどれだけ価値がなく、くだらないものかわかるわ」
English: “You talk about pride, but there is no such thing as a beautiful death. I know because I have seen all kinds of people die. A gangster can go proudly into battle, but once he loses and is killed, they strip him and shove his own cock into his mouth. A beautiful girl or boy becomes a monster from a B movie after a knife peels off no more than one layer of skin. More than anything, though, it is terribly lonely when a room once full of noise falls silent because everyone in it has died. Once you feel that loneliness, you understand how worthless and stupid death really is.”

Japanese: 「……そこまで言うあなたは、なぜこの仕事を続けているんですか？」
English: “...If that is what you believe, why do you continue doing this work?”

Japanese: 世傑がどういう方向に話を持っていこうとしているのか理解したリタは、流されまいと意志を表情に出してそう訊ねた。
English: Rita had understood where Sai-kit meant to lead the conversation. Her expression hardened with her determination not to be swept along as she asked the question.

Japanese: 「……きっと、どこか狂ってるのね」
English: “...I suppose I’m mad in some way.”

Japanese: 世傑は肩をすくめる。
English: Sai-kit shrugged.

Japanese: 「アタシだけじゃないわ。小謝だってそう。あなたのお父さんだってきっとそうだったはず。この世界で、殺したり殺されたりする人間はみんな狂ってるのよ。だからそういう人間は最後はどこかでつじつまがあうようになってる。それがここのルール。でも、あなたはまだこの世界のルールに従う必要はないはずよ」
English: “It isn’t only me. Siu Tse is the same. I’m sure your father was, too. Everyone who kills and risks being killed in this world is mad. And for people like us, the accounts always balance somehow in the end. That’s the rule here. But you shouldn’t have to live by this world’s rules yet.”

Japanese: 「私だって、後戻りなんか出来ません」
English: “It is too late for me to turn back, too.”

Japanese: 「そうかしら。死ぬのはこわいでしょう？」
English: “Are you sure? You’re afraid to die, aren’t you?”

Japanese: リタは何か言いかけるが、それは言葉にならず、俯く。
English: Rita began to say something, but no words emerged. She lowered her head.

Japanese: その様子を見て世傑は苦笑し、
English: Sai-kit watched her and gave a rueful smile.

Japanese: 「ねえあなた、小謝のことが好きだったんでしょ？」
English: “Tell me, Rita. You were in love with Siu Tse, weren’t you?”

Japanese: 唐突にそう訊ねた。
English: The question came without warning.

Japanese: 「そ、そんな……」
English: “Th-that’s not...”

Japanese: リタは慌てて否定したが、その言葉とは裏腹に顔はみるみるうちに赤くなる。
English: Rita hurried to deny it, but in apparent contradiction of her words, her face rapidly turned red.

Japanese: 「だったら、小謝と今度こそ本当に結婚しなさいよ。アタシが仲介するわ」
English: “Then marry Siu Tse for real this time. I’ll arrange it.”

Japanese: 「む、無理です。それは……」
English: “I-I can’t. That would...”

Japanese: 「それはあなたのためじゃなくて、小謝のためにも。今の彼には支えが必要なの」
English: “And not just for your own sake. For Siu Tse’s, too. He needs someone to support him now.”

Japanese: 「……大丈夫ですよ。あの人は強い人です」
English: “...He will be all right. He is a strong man.”

Japanese: リタは首を横に振る。
English: Rita shook her head.

Japanese: 「アタシは色んな人を見たけど、本当に強い人なんか世界には一人もいないわ。みんなやせ我慢してるだけよ」
English: “I have seen all kinds of people, and there isn’t one truly strong person in this world. Everyone is only putting up a brave front.”

Japanese: 「そうかもしれませんが、私には無理です」
English: “Perhaps. But I cannot do this.”

Japanese: 「死んだお姉さんたちが反対していたから？」
English: “Because your dead sisters opposed it?”

Japanese: 「違います！」
English: “No!”

Japanese: リタは突然顔を上げて抗議をしたが、すぐに大声を恥じて元のように俯き、
English: Rita suddenly raised her head in protest. Almost at once, embarrassed by her own loud voice, she looked down again.

Japanese: 「確かに昔は好きだったかもしれません。でも、いまは違います。……私はあの人に認められたいんです。一人前の人間として。だから、もうこの話は終わりです」
English: “Perhaps I did like him once. But I don’t anymore. ...I want that man to acknowledge me—as an adult in my own right. So this conversation is over.”

Japanese: 「リタちゃん。それはね……」
English: “Rita. That is...”

Japanese: 言いかけた世傑の言葉を遮って、
English: Rita cut off whatever Sai-kit had been about to say.

Japanese: 「すみませんが、出て行ってください」
English: “I’m sorry, but please leave.”

Japanese: 「わかったわ」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: 世傑はなおも何か言いたそうだったが、リタの固い横顔を見て諦めたようだった。
English: Sai-kit still appeared to have something to say, but one look at Rita’s rigid profile made him give up.

Japanese: 相手の手を離し、立ち上がる。
English: He released her hand and rose.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、おやすみ」
English: “Good night, then.”

Japanese: パチリと照明を落として、ドアを閉めようとしたその時、
English: He switched off the light with a click and had begun closing the door when—

Japanese: 「世傑さん」
English: “Sai-kit.”

Japanese: とリタが呼びかけた。
English: Rita called out to him.

Japanese: 「私、自殺するつもりなんかありません。絶対に相手をやっつけて、生き延びるんですから。そうしたら、次のことを考えます。だからその時は、私に協力してくださいね」
English: “I have no intention of killing myself. I will defeat them, and I will survive. Then I will decide what comes next. So when that time comes, please help me.”

Japanese: その声は、最後は泣き声になっていた。
English: By the end, her voice had broken into a sob.

Japanese: 「わかったわ。その時は……」
English: “All right. When the time comes...”

Japanese: 言った世傑の声も震えている。
English: Sai-kit’s voice was trembling now, too.

Japanese: 「おやすみ」
English: “Good night.”

Japanese: 世傑は自分の表情を見せまいと、ドアを閉めた。そしてそのドアを背に目元を抑えた時、背後からリタのすすり泣く嗚咽が聞こえた。
English: Sai-kit closed the door so that Rita would not see his expression. With his back against it, he covered his eyes and heard Rita’s sobs from the other side.

Japanese: 翌朝すぐにリタ・フェルナンデスはマンションを出て行った。
English: Rita Fernandes left the apartment early the next morning.

Japanese: 親戚の家に到着したリタはその日のうちに自分の生存をインターネット上に表明し、そして八龍会を非難した。
English: After reaching her relatives’ home, she published a statement online that same day announcing her survival and condemning Hachiryukai.

Japanese: これによってフェルナンデス・ファミリーと八龍会が完全に対立するかたちとなったわけだが、しかし抗争が本格化する前にタイプBの青年二人の裏切りによってリタとその親戚は殺害される。裏切り者たちはリタの首を切り取り、それを手土産に解放軍に駆け込むと、解放軍はその加入を快く受け入れた。
English: The Fernandes Family and Hachiryukai were thereby placed in open opposition. Before the conflict could escalate in earnest, however, two young Type B men betrayed and killed Rita and her relatives. They cut off Rita’s head and carried it to the Liberation Army as a gift; the army gladly accepted them into its ranks.

Japanese: その後、かつてフェルナンデス家を襲撃した若者たちがされたように、リタと彼女を匿った人々の遺体は暗闇通りの路地に放置された。
English: Afterward, just as the bodies of the young people who had once attacked the Fernandes family had been, the bodies of Rita and those who sheltered her were abandoned in an alley on Darkness Street.

Japanese: 衣服を剥がれたそのいたましい遺体は通行人に撮影され、Y地区の暗部を示す一シーンとして週刊誌の一面を飾ることになる。このときリタ・フェルナンデスはわずか１９才だった。
English: Passersby photographed the pitiable bodies, stripped of their clothes. A photograph of them later appeared on the front page of a weekly magazine as one image of Y District’s dark underside. Rita Fernandes was only nineteen years old.

Japanese: YSの龍頭謝亮は報告を受けるとすぐに部下をその現場に派遣し、かつては盟友であった少女とその親族の遺体を回収すると、先に死んだ家族たちのそばに埋葬した。
English: Upon receiving the report, YS Longtou Ryo Sugawara immediately sent subordinates to the site. They recovered the bodies of the girl who had once been his ally and of her relatives, then buried them beside the members of her family who had died before them.

Japanese: こうして、Y地区で有数の勢力を持っていたフェルナンデス・ファミリーを完全な壊滅状態においやったことで、八龍会は名実ともにYSに対抗しうる存在として周知されることになった。
English: By reducing the Fernandes Family, once one of Y District’s most powerful forces, to complete ruin, Hachiryukai became known in both name and fact as an organization capable of standing against YS.
